## Start here (no group, above the tabs)

### Welcome

*Read this first: who you are, and where to go next.*

1. **Welcome, Demigod**: checkmark
   > You remember light pouring from your hands. Now there is only dirt under your nails.
   > What: Welcome to Warbucks Chemistry. You're a demigod who lost your power, and you win it back by mastering chemistry: taking matter apart into elements and building it up again.
   > How: the four signposts around this quest point to the pages that matter most. Read them, then take the road below to Getting Started.
   > Tip: the sleeping bag skips the night without moving your spawn point.
2. **The Demigod's Path**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > What: the Demigod's Path is the spine of the book: eight tiers, each opened by a chemistry milestone. Fire and bronze, then steel, hydrogen, electricity, acids, plastics, the atom and antimatter.
   > How: every other page hangs off it. Modern Industrialization's voltages (LV, MV, HV, EV) set the pace, and other mods open alongside.
   > Tip: if a recipe looks different from what you remember, it was changed on purpose. JEI always shows the real one.
3. **The Demigod's Market**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > What: most quests pay Demigod Tokens. The Market turns them into supplies and comforts, never into shortcuts past a tier.
   > How: open the Demigod's Market pages, or search Demigod Token in JEI and press U: every trade is a crafting recipe.
   > Tip: the Market sells more of what you have already made yourself, so finishing quests opens new stalls.
4. **Tips and Tricks**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > What: the Tips and Tricks page collects short lessons: JEI lookups, Jade, claiming land, Ultimine, waystones, perks and the pack's own changes.
   > How: R / U over an item for recipes and uses, M for the claim map, hold ` to vein mine. The page has the rest.
   > Tip: give the game about 8 to 10 GB of memory in your launcher's instance settings.
5. **Building Tips**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > What: the Building Tips pages are a catalogue of the pack's building tools and decoration: gadgets, chisels, framed blocks, stone, wood, glass, light, furniture and a proper laboratory.
   > How: everything there is optional. Dip in whenever your base needs a new look.
   > Tip: a construction stick and a stonecutter save more time than anything else on that page.
6. **Getting Started**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > The world is waiting to be taken apart and put back together.
   > How: open Getting Started and take your first step: wood, stone, food and a safe first night.
   > Tip: you can come back to this page any time from the top of the chapter list.
7. **Who You Were**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > Some things you still know without being taught: water is two parts hydrogen to one of oxygen, and fire is a reaction, not a spirit.
   > Chemistry: about 90 elements occur in nature. Rearrange their atoms and you change what a thing is. That's the whole game.
   > Tip: every chapter of this book returns one more piece of what you once were.
8. **The Periodic Table**: checkmark *(after: Welcome, Demigod)*
   > What: chemists know 118 elements. Each is defined by its number of protons, its atomic number.
   > Chemistry: Mendeleev ordered the table in 1869 by repeating properties and left gaps for elements nobody had found. Gallium and germanium later filled them almost exactly as he predicted.
   > Tip: the Periodic Table page tracks every element you collect, and whole groups grant permanent perks.

### The Demigod's Market

*Spend your Demigod Tokens: supplies and comforts, never shortcuts.*

1. **The Market**: checkmark *(after: The Demigod's Market)*
   > You remember offerings left at your altar. Now the world pays you in coins instead.
   > What: Demigod Tokens are the reward currency of this book. You trade them for supplies by crafting, with no shopkeeper and no server plugin.
   > How: every shop trade is a shapeless crafting recipe: put tokens in a crafting grid and the item appears.
   > How: the price list is JEI: search Demigod Token and press U (uses). Every trade shows as a crafting recipe. Do the same for the Greater Demigod Token.
   > Tip: the crafting shop sells raw supplies and comforts, never anything that skips a tier. Copies of machines you have already built are in the Machine Shop quests.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > What tokens never buy: the shop skips boring gathering (sand, gravel, string, torches), never learning. If a trade seems missing, it was left out on purpose.
   > Chemistry: a bag of raw ore is not a refinery. Raw tin still needs your crusher, raw titanium still needs your blast furnace.
2. **Where Tokens Come From**: `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: The Market)*
   > What: almost every quest pays tokens, scaled by tier: 1 per quest at the start, 2 in the steam and Nether chapters, 3 at LV and MV, 4 at HV, 5 at EV, 8 in space.
   > How: milestone quests (the big ones) pay double and also roll that tier's reward table. Optional side quests pay 1 or 2.
   > Tip: on a team, rewards go to each player who claims them, so everyone builds their own purse.
3. **The Price Bands**: checkmark *(after: Where Tokens Come From)*
   > What: the shop has three price bands. Small (1 to 3 tokens): cheap stacks of things you'd otherwise spend an afternoon gathering. Medium and large are on the next pages.
   > How: 1 token: 32 torches, 16 bread, 8 bottles o' enchanting, 32 bone meal, 64 sand, 64 gravel or 32 clay balls.
   > How: 2 tokens: 16 iron ingots, 16 coke, 16 rubber sheets, 16 fire clay dust, 32 salt dust, 16 string, 16 leather or a sleeping bag.
   > How: 3 tokens: 8 osmium ingots, 2 backpack upgrade bases, 16 gunpowder, 16 slime balls, 32 redstone or 16 lapis.
   > Tip: sand and gravel are the best early value: concrete, glass and silicon all start there.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Medium band (4 to 8 tokens): raw ores (you still process them yourself) and drops you would otherwise farm.
   > How: 4 tokens: a Warp Stone, 32 raw copper, 16 raw tin, 16 raw lead, 16 bauxite dust, 32 quartz or 32 glowstone dust.
   > How: 5: 16 raw nickel, 8 ender pearls, 4 phantom membranes, 16 amethyst. 6: 8 blaze rods, 4 ghast tears, 16 certus quartz, 8 source gems.
   > How: 7: 8 raw titanium or 2 name tags. 8: 8 raw tungsten or 32 prismarine shards.
   > Tip: raw ore bought here is worth up to 5x once your Mekanism line is running. Buy late, process well.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Large band (Greater Tokens): the big trades cost Greater Demigod Tokens, not regular ones.
   > How: 1 Greater: 4 golden apples, 4 diamonds, 16 emeralds or a saddle. 2: 2 shulker shells, a heart of the sea or a netherite scrap.
   > How: 3 Greater: a totem of undying or 4 echo shards. 4 Greater: an enchanted golden apple.
   > Tip: shulker shells mean shulker boxes. Many players find that the best trade in the shop.
4. **The Exchange**: `kubejs:greater_demigod_token` *(after: The Price Bands)*
   > What: a Greater Demigod Token is worth 9 Demigod Tokens, and the trade works both ways.
   > How: 9 tokens in a crafting grid make 1 Greater Token. 1 Greater Token alone in the grid gives the 9 back.
   > Tip: late-tier milestones and boss loot sometimes pay Greater Tokens directly.
5. **Market Day: Early**: 10x `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: The Price Bands, Iron)*
   > What: a reward for saving. Hold 10 Demigod Tokens at once and choose one comfort: a sleeping bag, a Warp Stone, backpack upgrade bases or a saddle.
   > How: the tokens are only checked, not taken. Spend them afterwards if you like.
   > Tip: the Warp Stone is the pick if you explore a lot.
6. **Market Day: Industrial**: 30x `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: Market Day: Early, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: hold 30 tokens and choose a stack of raw feedstock: tin, lead, nickel, bauxite or salt.
   > How: tokens are checked, not taken.
   > Tip: bauxite is the slow one to find, and aluminium is the gate to MV.
7. **Market Day: Divine**: 64x `kubejs:demigod_token` *(after: Market Day: Industrial, EV: Processing Units)*
   > You remember when worshippers brought you treasures. Now you just keep a full stack.
   > What: hold a full stack of 64 tokens and choose a treasure: a totem, shulker shells, a heart of the sea, an enchanted golden apple or 3 Greater Tokens.
   > How: tokens are checked, not taken. Exchange Greater Tokens back if you need 64 loose ones.
   > Tip: picking the Greater Tokens is the same as taking 27 regular tokens home.
8. **A Dragon's Hoard**: 9x `kubejs:greater_demigod_token` *(after: The Exchange)*
   > What: hold nine Greater Demigod Tokens at once. That's 81 tokens you chose not to spend.
   > Tip: the demigod approves of patience. The demigod also notes that totems exist.
9. **The Machine Shop**: checkmark *(after: The Market)*
   > You remember forges that worked while you slept. Once you know how a thing is made, its copies come cheap.
   > What: repeatable shop quests that sell copies of machines, boilers, tanks, hulls and cables.
   > How: a machine goes on sale only after you finish the quest where you build it yourself. Until then its entry is invisible.
   > How: hold the price and click Submit: the tokens are taken and the machine is yours. Buy again whenever you like.
   > Tip: counters run Steam, LV, MV, HV, EV. From MV up, prices are in Greater Demigod Tokens (9 tokens each). Multiblock controllers are never sold.

### Tips and Tricks

*Small lessons that save a demigod hours. All optional, read them in any order.*

1. **Tips and Tricks**: checkmark
   > You remember knowing every trick of your own world. These belong to this one.
   > What: each card below is one short tip about this pack: how to look things up, get around, and where it differs from other packs.
   > How: read any card and click its checkmark. Nothing here blocks the main path.
   > Tip: the top row is the most useful on your first day.
2. **Look It Up**: checkmark
   > What: JEI shows every recipe in the pack, including the ones changed for progression.
   > How: hover over any item and press R for how to make it or U for what it makes. Type @modname in the search bar to list one mod's items.
   > Tip: press A over an item to bookmark it, and use the + button in a recipe to fill your crafting grid.
3. **What Am I Looking At?**: checkmark
   > What: Jade shows a panel at the top of the screen for the block or mob under your crosshair: its name, its mod and its state.
   > How: look at a machine to see its progress, energy and fluids. Look at an ore to see which tool can mine it.
   > Tip: when a machine stalls, look at it first: Jade usually shows what's missing.
4. **Maps and Waypoints**: checkmark
   > What: JourneyMap keeps a minimap and a full world map of everywhere you've been.
   > How: press J for the full map and right-click a spot to set a waypoint.
   > Tip: it drops a waypoint where you die, which leads you straight back to your grave.
5. **Claim and Force-Load**: checkmark
   > What: claimed chunks are protected from other players. Force-loaded chunks keep running while you're away.
   > How: press M and drag over chunks to claim them. The same map force-loads a claimed chunk (its help text shows the clicks).
   > Tip: force-load your machine rooms and flight area, not your whole base: you have a limited number.
6. **One Swing, Whole Vein**: checkmark
   > What: Ultimine breaks every connected matching block at once: an ore vein, a tree, a strip of stone.
   > How: hold the ` key (left of 1) while you break a block. The Quality of Life page shows the shapes.
   > Tip: it costs hunger, so eat before you clear a big vein.
7. **Waystones**: 1x any of `or(item(waystones:waystone)item(waystones:mossy_waystone)item(waystones:sandy_waystone)item(waystones:deepslate_waystone)item(waystones:blackstone_waystone)item(waystones:end_stone_waystone))`
   > What: activate a waystone once and you can warp to it from any other waystone.
   > How: get any waystone: find one in a village or craft one (check JEI).
   > Tip: put one at your base, your mine and your Nether portal. A Warp Stone (Market or JEI) warps from anywhere.
8. **Sleep Anywhere**: 1x any of `or(item(comforts:sleeping_bag_white)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_orange)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_magenta)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_light_blue)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_yellow)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_lime)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_pink)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_gray)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_light_gray)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_cyan)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_purple)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_blue)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_brown)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_green)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_red)item(comforts:sleeping_bag_black)item(comforts:hammock_white)item(comforts:hammock_orange)item(comforts:hammock_magenta)item(comforts:hammock_light_blue)item(comforts:hammock_yellow)item(comforts:hammock_lime)item(comforts:hammock_pink)item(comforts:hammock_gray)item(comforts:hammock_light_gray)item(comforts:hammock_cyan)item(comforts:hammock_purple)item(comforts:hammock_blue)item(comforts:hammock_brown)item(comforts:hammock_green)item(comforts:hammock_red)item(comforts:hammock_black))`
   > What: a sleeping bag lets you sleep through the night wherever you are, without moving your spawn point.
   > How: get any sleeping bag (check JEI for the recipe). A hammock does the same for the day.
   > Tip: keep one in your backpack for long trips and deep mines.
9. **Carry More**: checkmark
   > What: Sophisticated Backpacks hold far more than your inventory and take upgrades: pickup, magnet, feeding, crafting and more.
   > How: get a backpack (leather, string and a chest, check JEI).
   > Tip: the Market sells upgrade bases, so tokens turn into upgrades early. The backpack quest itself is on the Storage page.
10. **Fewer Clicks**: checkmark
   > What: Utilitarian adds bulk wood recipes (two logs in a column make 16 sticks; chests and ladders straight from logs). Crafting on a Stick puts a crafting table, stonecutter or anvil in your hand.
   > How: press U on any log in JEI to see the shortcuts.
   > Tip: a Tool Belt keeps your spare tools one keypress away.
11. **Death Is Not the End**: checkmark
   > What: when you die, Corail Tombstone keeps your items in a grave where you fell.
   > How: type /back to return to the spot, or follow JourneyMap's death waypoint, then open the grave.
   > Tip: /sethome at your base and /home gets you back after a long trip.
12. **Play Together**: checkmark
   > What: FTB Teams puts players in a party that shares quest progress and claimed chunks.
   > How: open the Teams screen from your inventory (or use /ftbteams), create a party and invite your friends.
   > Tip: on a server, form the party early so claims and quest progress are shared from the start.
13. **Tokens and the Market**: checkmark
   > What: most quests pay Demigod Tokens; nine of them make one Greater Demigod Token.
   > How: the Demigod's Market pages trade tokens for supplies, and JEI shows every crafting trade (search Demigod Token, press U).
   > Tip: the Market sells more of what you've already made, never a way past a tier.
14. **Periodic Table Perks**: checkmark
   > What: the pack remembers every element you've held. Hold every element of a group once and you keep a bonus for good, even after death.
   > How: type /warbucks elements to see your progress. Aluminium, tin, lead and indium (the post-transition metals) give +2 armour toughness.
   > Tip: you only need to hold each element once; you can use it up afterwards.
15. **Quests Notice Everything**: checkmark
   > What: the book is flexible: an item quest completes as soon as you have the item, even if the quests before it aren't done yet.
   > How: just play. Craft a pickaxe early and its quest ticks off; claim the reward when you get there.
   > Tip: many quests take any variant (any wood, any colour), so check the task before you craft a specific one.
16. **The Fast Furnace**: checkmark
   > What: in this pack every furnace, smoker and blast furnace recipe cooks 4x faster, including modded smelting.
   > How: nothing to do: a stack of iron in a plain furnace is done in well under a minute.
   > Tip: machines from MI, Mekanism and Create keep their own speeds; only vanilla-style cooking is faster.
17. **Long Days, Little Rain**: checkmark
   > What: Overworld days last twice as long (about 20 minutes); nights are normal length.
   > How: dry spells are stretched and rain is cut short, so storms come less often.
   > Tip: a sleeping bag still skips the night, so you can stay in daylight almost all the time.
18. **Rich Deposits**: checkmark
   > What: loose ore is rarer here, but about one chunk in 16 to 30 hides a rich deposit of hundreds of ores, at a depth that depends on the metal.
   > How: explore caves, use Jade and Ultimine, and later the Spectrometer (LV): right-click it to read ore signals in the chunks around you.
   > Tip: a strong signal is usually a deposit. Walk towards it and scan again.
19. **The Mining Dimension**: checkmark
   > What: a Teleport Pad placed in the Overworld leads to the Mining dimension: flat layers rich in iron, gold, diamond, redstone, tin, lead, nickel, silver and bauxite.
   > How: craft the pad (ender pearl, allthemodium nuggets, MI steel plates, an analog circuit), stand on it with empty hands and sneak + right-click.
   > Tip: mobs spawn in the dark there, so light your tunnels.
20. **More Ore From Chemistry**: checkmark
   > What: before acids, every route caps at 2x per ore block. Mekanism's chemistry raises it: oxygen 3x, hydrogen chloride 4x, sulfuric acid 5x.
   > Chemistry: acids dissolve the ore into a solution, which can be purified far better than a crushed rock.
   > Tip: spin Mekanism's dirty dust in the MI Centrifuge for byproduct metals.
21. **Everything Is Made of Elements**: checkmark
   > What: Alchemistry's Dissolver breaks almost any block or item into its elements; the Combiner builds things back up.
   > Chemistry: atoms are rearranged, never created or destroyed, so what you take apart you can rebuild.
   > Tip: it's the only way to get some elements as items, like the hydrogen for your first flight.
22. **Read the Formula**: checkmark
   > What: chemistry items show their formula in the tooltip: ChemLib's elements and compounds, and many machine fluids and gases (H₂, Cl₂, D₂O and more).
   > How: hover over a compound or a fluid bucket in JEI or your inventory.
   > Tip: the Lab Notebook page explains the real chemistry behind each machine.
23. **Building Multiblocks**: checkmark
   > What: big machines are multiblocks. You never have to guess their shape.
   > How: press R on the controller in JEI for its layout, read the MI guidebook, and use Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks for Mekanism's.
   > Tip: MI multiblocks also need the right hatches for items, fluids and energy; the guidebook page for each one lists them.

### Building Tips

*A god's house should look like one.*

1. **Building Tips**: checkmark *(after: Planks and a Workbench)*
   > You remember raising cities with a gesture. For now, a few clever tools will do.
   > What: this page is a catalogue of the pack's building mods and decoration, one cluster per theme around this quest.
   > How: everything here is optional and cheap. Pick a cluster that suits your next build and work outward.
   > Tip: a stonecutter makes stairs, slabs, walls and patterns with no waste. Use it for every stone on this page.
2. **Construction Stick**: `constructionstick:wooden_stick` *(after: Building Tips)*
   > What: a Construction Stick places a whole row or face of blocks matching the one you click, from your inventory.
   > How: three sticks in a column (check JEI). Right-click the face of a wall to grow it by one layer.
   > Tip: the tooltip lists its modes, such as only extending in a straight line.
3. **Diamond Stick**: `constructionstick:diamond_stick` *(after: Construction Stick)*
   > What: better sticks place more blocks per click and last longer: copper, iron, diamond, then netherite.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon in a tight 3D lattice, which makes it the hardest natural material.
   > How: a diamond on two sticks (check JEI). Templates at a smithing table add tricks such as replacing blocks.
4. **Tool Extras**: `framedblocks:framing_saw`; `mcwwindows:hammer`; `constructionstick:template_angel` *(after: Diamond Stick)*
   > What: the Framing Saw crafts any framed shape from framed cubes; the Window Hammer reshapes a placed Macaw's window; the Angel template lets a stick place blocks in mid-air.
   > How: check JEI for each. Apply the template to a stick at a smithing table.
   > Tip: the angel template is a building aid, not flight. Flight in this pack is a chemistry milestone.
5. **Effortless Building**: `effortlessbuilding:randomizer_tool` *(after: Construction Stick)*
   > What: Effortless Building adds mirror, array and line modes for big symmetric builds.
   > How: open its menu (check Controls) and pick a mode. The randomizer places a random mix of the blocks you load into it.
   > Tip: load the randomizer with stone, andesite and cobblestone for natural-looking walls.
6. **Scaffolding**: 16x `minecraft:scaffolding` *(after: Construction Stick)*
   > What: scaffolding stacks upward and outward, you climb it like a ladder, and breaking the bottom brings the whole tower down.
   > Chemistry: bamboo is a grass whose stems are stiffened with lignin and silica, which is why real scaffolds have used it for centuries.
   > How: six bamboo and a string make six scaffolding (check JEI). Sneak to climb down.
7. **Building Gadgets**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_building` *(after: Construction Stick, LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: FE-powered gadgets that place, swap, copy and remove blocks in bulk.
   > How: iron, redstone, lapis and a diamond (check JEI). Charge it in any energy storage block.
   > Tip: link the gadget to a chest or backpack so it pulls blocks from storage.
8. **Copy and Paste**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_copy_paste`; `buildinggadgets2:template_manager` *(after: Building Gadgets)*
   > What: copy an area and paste it elsewhere; the Template Manager saves copies to share.
   > How: check JEI. Great for repeating a row of furnaces or a decorated wall.
   > Tip: templates can be shared with friends on the server.
9. **Exchanging Gadget**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_exchanging` *(after: Building Gadgets)*
   > What: replaces blocks in an area with another block, keeping the shape.
   > How: check JEI. Perfect for turning a cobblestone shell into something pretty.
   > Tip: it uses the blocks in your inventory, so carry enough.
10. **Destruction Gadget**: `buildinggadgets2:gadget_destruction` *(after: Building Gadgets)*
   > What: removes a box of blocks in front of you, sized however you like. It can undo its last action.
   > How: check JEI. Set the depth, width and height in its menu.
   > Tip: perfect for hollowing out a hillside for a new factory floor.
11. **Rechiseled**: `rechiseled:chisel` *(after: Building Tips, Iron)*
   > What: Rechiseled's chisel turns stone, planks, metal blocks and more into patterns: bricks, tiles, pillars, gears.
   > How: an iron ingot on a stick (check JEI). Right-click to open it, put blocks in and pick a pattern.
   > Tip: iron and copper block patterns make a machine room look deliberate.

   > What: every Rechiseled pattern has a connecting version whose texture joins up with the same block next to it, so a wall reads as one panel.

13. **Framed Blocks**: 8x `framedblocks:framed_cube`; `framedblocks:framed_hammer` *(after: Rechiseled)*
   > What: FramedBlocks are wooden frames that take the look of any block you right-click into them, in dozens of shapes.
   > How: framed cubes are planks and sticks (check JEI). Right-click one with a full block to apply it; the Framed Hammer takes it off.

14. **Slopes and Panels**: 6x any of `or(item(framedblocks:framed_slope)item(framedblocks:framed_corner_slope)item(framedblocks:framed_stairs)item(framedblocks:framed_slab)item(framedblocks:framed_panel)item(framedblocks:framed_pillar)item(framedblocks:framed_prism))` *(after: Framed Blocks)*
   > What: any six framed slopes, corner slopes, stairs, slabs, panels, pillars or prisms.
   > How: each shape is made from framed cubes (check JEI). Most come several at a time.
   > Tip: framed slopes camouflaged as stone make roofs and ramps that look hand-carved.
15. **Secret Storage**: `framedblocks:framed_secret_storage` *(after: Slopes and Panels)*
   > What: a full-block chest that wears any block's texture, so it disappears into a wall.
   > How: a framed chest surrounded by framed cubes (check JEI), then camouflage it.
   > Tip: hide your rarest elements in one. Nobody suspects the third stone brick from the left.
16. **Copycats**: 2x `copycats:copycat_block`; 4x any of `or(item(copycats:copycat_slope)item(copycats:copycat_stairs)item(copycats:copycat_board)item(copycats:copycat_beam)item(copycats:copycat_slice)item(copycats:copycat_vertical_slope))` *(after: Rechiseled, Andesite Casing)*
   > What: Copycats+ adds many more Create copycat shapes: slopes, boards, beams, slices. Each takes the look of the block you apply.
   > How: cut zinc ingots in a stonecutter (check JEI), then right-click a placed copycat with a block.
   > Tip: copycat boards cover pipes and shafts while leaving them working.
17. **Know Your Rocks**: 64x any of `or(item(minecraft:stone)item(minecraft:deepslate)item(minecraft:andesite)item(minecraft:diorite)item(minecraft:granite)item(minecraft:tuff)item(minecraft:calcite))` *(after: Building Tips, Stone Age)*
   > What: stone, deepslate, andesite, diorite, granite, tuff or calcite, mixed as you like. Each has polished and brick forms.
   > Chemistry: granite cooled slowly deep underground, so its quartz and feldspar crystals grew large. Tuff is welded volcanic ash, and calcite is CaCO₃.
   > Tip: the Trowel (Quality of Life page) mixes them into a natural-looking wall.
18. **Masonry**: 16x `minecraft:clay_ball`; 16x `minecraft:brick`; 4x `minecraft:chiseled_stone_bricks`; 8x `minecraft:cobblestone_wall` *(after: Know Your Rocks, Fire)*
   > What: clay fires into bricks; stone bricks chisel into patterns; walls make fences mobs can't jump.
   > Chemistry: clay is mostly kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄. Fired above about 900 °C it loses its water and sinters into hard, waterproof ceramic.
   > How: dig clay from riverbeds and lush caves and smelt it. Chiseled stone bricks and walls come from the stonecutter.
19. **Mud Bricks**: 8x `minecraft:packed_mud`; 8x `minecraft:mud_bricks` *(after: Masonry)*
   > What: mud packs with wheat into packed mud, which cuts into warm brown mud bricks.
   > Chemistry: sun-dried mud brick (adobe) binds clay particles with straw fibres; it hardens by drying, not by firing, so it needs a roof to stay dry.
   > How: use a water bottle on dirt to make mud, craft it with wheat into packed mud, then four packed mud make mud bricks.
20. **Deep Stone**: 32x any of `or(item(minecraft:deepslate_tiles)item(minecraft:deepslate_bricks)item(minecraft:polished_deepslate)item(minecraft:tuff_bricks)item(minecraft:polished_tuff)item(minecraft:chiseled_tuff))` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: deepslate tiles and bricks, and tuff bricks from the trial chambers' palette: dark, heavy-looking stone for foundations.
   > Chemistry: deepslate is a metamorphic rock: older stone squeezed and heated far underground until its minerals lined up in layers.
   > How: any 32 of them, cut from cobbled deepslate or tuff in a stonecutter.
21. **Coloured Sandstone**: 32x any of `or(item(biomesoplenty:white_sandstone)item(biomesoplenty:orange_sandstone)item(biomesoplenty:black_sandstone)item(biomesoplenty:smooth_white_sandstone)item(biomesoplenty:smooth_orange_sandstone)item(biomesoplenty:smooth_black_sandstone)item(minecraft:sandstone)item(minecraft:red_sandstone))` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: Biomes O' Plenty adds white, orange and black sands; each makes its own sandstone.
   > Chemistry: white sand is nearly pure quartz (SiO₂), orange and red sand are stained by iron oxides, and black sand is ground volcanic rock rich in magnetite.
   > How: any 32 sandstone blocks of any colour. Four sand make one sandstone.
22. **Rocks of Other Biomes**: 16x `regions_unexplored:chalk`; 16x `regions_unexplored:argillite`; 8x `regions_unexplored:mossy_stone` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: three building stones from Regions Unexplored biomes: white chalk, dark red argillite and mossy stone.
   > Chemistry: chalk is CaCO₃ made of the tiny plates of ancient sea algae. Argillite is clay squeezed into hard rock.
   > How: find the biomes with Nature's Compass (Quality of Life page) and mine the stone.
23. **Dripstone**: 8x `minecraft:pointed_dripstone`; 8x `minecraft:dripstone_block` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: pointed dripstone grows in dripstone caves; hanging under a water source, it slowly fills a cauldron below.
   > Chemistry: dripping water loses CO₂ and leaves calcite behind: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. A real stalactite grows about a centimetre a century.
   > How: mine both in a dripstone cave (Nature's Compass finds one).
24. **Amethyst**: 8x `minecraft:amethyst_shard`; 2x `minecraft:amethyst_block` *(after: Know Your Rocks, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: amethyst grows on budding amethyst inside underground geodes. Shards make spyglasses, tinted glass and blocks that chime.
   > Chemistry: amethyst is quartz, SiO₂, coloured violet by traces of iron that natural radiation has turned into colour centres.
   > Tip: never break the budding amethyst: it can't be moved and it's the only thing that grows more.
25. **Building with Ice**: 8x `minecraft:snow_block`; 8x `minecraft:packed_ice`; 2x `minecraft:blue_ice` *(after: Know Your Rocks)*
   > What: snow blocks, packed ice (it doesn't melt) and blue ice, the slipperiest block in the game.
   > Chemistry: ice floats because hydrogen bonds lock water into an open hexagonal lattice, about 9% less dense than liquid water.
   > How: 4 snowballs make a snow block; 9 ice make packed ice, 9 packed ice make blue ice. Icebergs have both.
26. **Nether Masonry**: 16x `minecraft:polished_blackstone`; `minecraft:gilded_blackstone`; 4x `minecraft:chain` *(after: Building Tips, Blackstone)*
   > What: polished blackstone makes dark, gothic builds; gilded blackstone sparkles with gold; chains hang lanterns.
   > Chemistry: gold in dark rock is how real gold is often found: hot water carries dissolved gold through cracks and drops it as it cools.
   > How: polish blackstone in a stonecutter. Gilded blackstone is found in bastions. Chain: an iron ingot between two iron nuggets.
27. **Brimstone**: 16x `biomesoplenty:brimstone`; 8x `biomesoplenty:brimstone_bricks` *(after: Nether Masonry)*
   > What: Biomes O' Plenty's brimstone covers volcanic Nether biomes, around fumaroles that puff smoke.
   > Chemistry: "brimstone" is the old name for sulfur. Real volcanic vents deposit yellow sulfur crystals as hot H₂S and SO₂ gases cool and react.
   > How: mine brimstone in the Nether (Nature's Compass finds the biome) and craft or cut it into bricks.
28. **End Stone**: 16x `minecraft:end_stone`; 8x `minecraft:end_stone_bricks` *(after: Nether Masonry, The End)*
   > What: end stone and its bricks: pale yellow and very blast-resistant. Chorus plants grow only on it.
   > How: mine end stone on any End island; 4 end stone make 4 end stone bricks.
   > Tip: end stone resists explosions far better than cobblestone, so wall in anything that might blow.
29. **Purpur**: 8x `minecraft:purpur_block`; 4x `minecraft:purpur_pillar` *(after: End Stone)*
   > What: purpur blocks and pillars are what End cities are built from.
   > How: pop chorus fruit in a furnace, then four popped fruit make four purpur blocks; pillars come from the stonecutter.
   > Tip: chorus plants regrow from their flowers on end stone, so you can farm purpur at home.
30. **Prismarine**: 8x `minecraft:prismarine_bricks`; 8x `minecraft:dark_prismarine` *(after: Nether Masonry, Guardian Hunter)*
   > What: prismarine bricks and dark prismarine, the stone of ocean monuments, made from guardians' shards.
   > Chemistry: real sea creatures build shells from calcium carbonate and silica drawn out of seawater, which is where reef stone comes from.
   > How: 9 prismarine shards make prismarine bricks; 8 shards around a black dye make dark prismarine.

   > What: the Undergarden's stones cut into bricks and tiles: grey depthrock, icy shiverstone and cracked tremblecrust.

   > Tip: depthrock bricks make a fine floor for a room that should feel underground.

   > What: the clock block shows the time on a wall; the hourglass is a timer you fill with sand or other powders.
   > Chemistry: a real hourglass works because dry sand flows at a steady rate no matter how full the glass is, unlike water.
   > How: check JEI for both. Days here are twice as long, so the clock moves slowly in daylight.

   > What: flags that flutter in the wind and strings of bunting for a festival look.
