   > What: Leather armour is weak, but it's the first protection you can make, and it's dyeable.
   > Chemistry: Leather is animal skin that's been tanned: tannins or chromium salts cross-link the collagen proteins so the hide stops rotting and stays flexible.
   > How: Cows drop leather. A tunic takes 8 leather and boots take 4.
   > Tip: Save spare leather: your first backpack needs some (on the Storage and Logistics page).
24. **Iron**: 8x `minecraft:iron_ingot` *(after: Leather Armour)*
   > The ore gives up its metal in the fire. Once, you did this with a thought.
   > What: Iron is the metal of your first real tools, buckets and armour, and the key to most of the other pages in this book.
   > Chemistry: Iron ore is iron oxide. In the furnace, carbon pulls the oxygen away: Fe₂O₃ + 3C → 2Fe + 3CO. That's reduction.
   > How: Mine iron ore with a stone pickaxe (it's common around Y 16 and in mountains) and smelt the raw iron.
   > Tip: Iron Furnaces (on the Storage and Logistics page) smelt faster once you have spare iron.
25. **Shield**: `minecraft:shield` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: A shield blocks arrows, melee hits and creeper blasts while you hold right-click.
   > How: 1 iron ingot and 6 planks (check JEI for the shape).
   > Tip: Hold it in your off-hand so you can block and swing at the same time. The Monster Hunting page opens from here.
26. **Shearing Season**: `minecraft:shears`; 16x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wool)` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Shears take 1 to 3 wool from a sheep without hurting it, and the wool grows back after the sheep eats grass.
   > Chemistry: Raw wool is coated in lanolin, a waxy mix of esters that keeps the sheep dry. It's the base of many skin creams.
   > How: 2 iron ingots placed diagonally make shears. Right-click a sheep.
   > Tip: Dye a sheep before you shear it to get coloured wool every time it regrows.
27. **Iron Pickaxe**: `minecraft:iron_pickaxe` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Needed for diamonds, redstone and gold, and to start the journey to the Nether.
   > Chemistry: Iron is harder than stone because its atoms sit in a regular metal lattice held by metallic bonds, which bend rather than shatter.
   > How: 3 iron ingots and 2 sticks.
28. **Redstone**: 8x `minecraft:redstone` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: Redstone powers doors, lamps and contraptions now, and goes into circuits and machines all through the book.
   > Chemistry: Redstone has no real-world twin, but its ore looks a lot like cinnabar, mercury sulfide (HgS): the red mineral people once ground into vermilion paint.
   > How: Redstone ore sits deep, mostly below Y 16, and needs an iron pickaxe. Each block drops several dust.
   > Tip: Levers, repeaters and the rest are on the Quality of Life page (Redstone Basics).
29. **All That Glitters**: 1x any of `or(item(minecraft:golden_helmet)item(minecraft:golden_chestplate)item(minecraft:golden_leggings)item(minecraft:golden_boots))` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: Gold armour is weaker than iron and wears out fast, but in the Nether piglins leave you alone while you wear one piece.
   > Chemistry: Gold is a noble metal: it hardly reacts with oxygen or water, so it never tarnishes. That's why ancient gold still shines.
   > How: Mine gold ore with an iron pickaxe and smelt it. Any one piece of gold armour counts.
30. **Carbon Under Pressure**: `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: Diamonds make the toughest vanilla tools, and a diamond pickaxe is the only early way to mine obsidian.
   > Chemistry: A diamond is the same element as coal: carbon. Here every atom is bonded to four others in a rigid 3D lattice, formed about 150 km underground under enormous pressure.
   > How: Diamond ore sits in the deepslate layers, most of it near the bottom of the world. Mine it with an iron pickaxe.
   > Tip: Obsidian is the frame of the Nether portal in Chapter III. Keep your first diamonds for a pickaxe.
31. **Iron Tools**: `minecraft:iron_sword`; `minecraft:iron_axe`; `minecraft:iron_shovel` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: Iron tools are faster and last far longer than stone, and an iron sword handles anything the early nights throw at you.
   > How: Same shapes as the stone tools, with iron ingots in place of cobblestone.
   > Tip: Your iron pickaxe, axe and shovel combine into one paxel: that quest is on the Gear and Comfort page.
32. **Iron Armour**: `minecraft:iron_helmet`; `minecraft:iron_chestplate`; `minecraft:iron_leggings`; `minecraft:iron_boots` *(after: Iron Tools)*
   > What: A full set of iron armour makes caves and the night survivable.
   > How: Helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots take 24 iron ingots in total.
   > Tip: Ultimine through an iron vein and you'll have this set in minutes.
33. **Chainmail**: 1x any of `or(item(minecraft:chainmail_helmet)item(minecraft:chainmail_chestplate)item(minecraft:chainmail_leggings)item(minecraft:chainmail_boots))` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Chainmail sits between leather and iron. It isn't craftable in vanilla, but you can trade an armourer villager for it or take it from a mob that spawned wearing it.
   > Chemistry: Interlocked rings spread the force of a blow across many links, so no single point takes the whole hit.
   > How: Modern Industrialization adds a recipe from Iron Rings once you have its tools (check JEI for both). Any one piece counts.
34. **Water**: `minecraft:water_bucket` *(after: Iron Armour)*
   > What: Water is the most important chemical in this pack: steam, electrolysis and acids all start with it.
   > Chemistry: H₂O is a small, polar molecule. That polarity lets it dissolve salts and acids, which is why chemists call it the universal solvent.
   > How: 3 iron ingots in a V make a bucket. Fill it at any water source.
   > Tip: Two water sources in a 2x2 hole make an infinite spring. Carry a water bucket while mining: it puts out fire and breaks falls.
35. **A Taste of Everything**: checkmark *(after: Iron Armour)*
   > Your memories come back in pieces, and not in order. Gears, spirits, strange seeds: you knew all of it once.
   > What: The Demigod's Path is the main road, but every category in the sidebar is a mod with its own chapters. The quests here are one small step into a few of them, and each says where to go next.
   > How: Click the checkmark, then try whichever look fun. Most of these are optional.
   > Tip: None of these block Chapter I. Claim Your Land and Tools from Parts are worth doing early; the rest can wait for a quiet evening.
36. **Tools from Parts**: `silentgear:blueprint_paper`; `silentgear:pickaxe` *(after: A Taste of Everything)*
   > What: Silent Gear builds tools from parts. Each part's stats come from its material, so better chemistry means better tools.
   > How: Make Blueprint Paper, craft a Pickaxe Blueprint, then craft a pickaxe head and rod (check JEI). An iron head is a good start.
   > Tip: Repair kits, better materials and the paxels are on the Gear and Comfort page.
37. **Clockwork**: 2x `create:andesite_alloy` *(after: A Taste of Everything)*
   > What: Create is the pack's early mechanical tier: shafts, water wheels, presses and mixers that turn by rotation, before you have electricity.
   > Chemistry: Andesite is a grey volcanic rock, rich in feldspar. Bound with metal it makes a cheap, sturdy frame material, which is all Create needs from it.
   > How: Andesite and iron nuggets in a 2x2 grid (check JEI). Andesite is the speckled grey stone common in hills and caves.
   > Tip: The Mechanical Age category picks up from here. Create feeds Modern Industrialization later; it doesn't replace it.
38. **Kitchen Chemistry**: `farmersdelight:cooking_pot`; `farmersdelight:beef_stew` *(after: A Taste of Everything)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight meals restore more hunger and give the Nourishment and Comfort effects.
   > Chemistry: Stewing denatures proteins: heat unfolds them, which is why meat turns firm and tender.
   > How: Craft a Cooking Pot (iron, bricks, a water bucket and a wooden shovel), set it over a campfire or stove, and cook raw beef, a carrot and a potato.
   > Tip: The Farming and Food category has knives, crops, feasts and more.
39. **Seeds of Plenty**: 4x `mysticalagriculture:inferium_essence` *(after: A Taste of Everything)*
   > What: Inferium essence is the base of Mystical Agriculture, whose crops grow resources instead of food.
   > How: Inferium ore is green-flecked stone found underground; mine it with any pickaxe. Mobs drop a little essence too.
   > Tip: The Mystical Agriculture category starts with the Infusion Altar. Higher seed tiers need MI circuits, and the chemistry milestones can't be grown at all.
40. **Strange Seeds**: `occultism:datura_seeds` *(after: A Taste of Everything)*
   > What: Demon's Dream seeds are the first step into Occultism, the pack's spirit magic.
   > Chemistry: Real datura plants are full of tropane alkaloids such as scopolamine and atropine. They're poisonous, and they cause vivid hallucinations. Never eat the real thing.
   > How: Break grass: the seeds drop now and then.
   > Tip: The Occultism category shows what the fruit does and what the spirits can do for you.
41. **Claim Your Land**: checkmark *(after: A Taste of Everything)*
   > What: FTB Chunks protects your base and can keep it loaded while you're away.
   > How: Press M to open the map, then drag over chunks to claim them. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: Right-click a claimed chunk to force-load it. You'll need that for the flight pylon later. More conveniences like this are on the Quality of Life page.
42. **A First Mining Trip**: 16x `minecraft:raw_copper`; 16x `minecraft:raw_iron` *(after: Water)*
   > What: Chapter I needs copper and plenty of iron. Time for a proper trip underground.
   > Chemistry: Below about Y 0, stone gives way to deepslate: older, denser rock formed under more heat and pressure. Ores near the surface are often oxidised by air and water, which is why copper ore has green streaks.
   > How: Pack torches, food, a water bucket and spare tools. Dig a staircase down (never straight down) or explore a cave, and bring back raw copper and raw iron.
   > Tip: Utilitarian turns 7 logs (in the ladder shape) into 24 ladders. Place a ladder line in your shaft so you can always climb out.
43. **Rock Collector**: `minecraft:coal`; `minecraft:raw_iron`; `minecraft:raw_copper`; `minecraft:raw_gold`; `minecraft:redstone`; `minecraft:lapis_lazuli`; `minecraft:diamond`; `minecraft:emerald` *(after: A First Mining Trip)*
   > What: Collect one drop from every vanilla ore. Emeralds only generate in mountain biomes.
   > Chemistry: Real ores are minerals: iron comes from oxides like hematite (Fe₂O₃), copper often from sulfides like chalcopyrite (CuFeS₂), and diamond is pure carbon.
   > Tip: Every one of these can go into the Dissolver later. Keep spares.
44. **A Closer Look**: `minecraft:spyglass` *(after: A First Mining Trip)*
   > What: A spyglass lets you scout terrain and spot ore in cliff faces from far away.
   > Chemistry: Amethyst is quartz (SiO₂). Its purple colour comes from traces of iron in the crystal.
   > How: 2 copper ingots and 1 amethyst shard. Amethyst geodes sit underground, ringed with smooth basalt.
45. **Ready for Chemistry**: checkmark *(after: A First Mining Trip)*
   > Fed, armed, sheltered: a good day, by mortal standards. Now the real work begins, the long road back to what you were.
   > What: Chapter I, Fire and Bronze, starts the Demigod's Path proper: charcoal, your first alloy and steam power.
   > How: Click to open Chapter I. The copper and tin in the reward are a head start on bronze.
   > Tip: Bring spare coal and iron. Chapter I eats both.

### I. Fire and Bronze

*Heat drives chemistry: reduce ore with carbon, mix metals into alloys, and let steam do the work.*

1. **Pyrolysis**: 8x `minecraft:charcoal` *(after: Ready for Chemistry)*
   > You remember the first fire you ever tamed. It was smaller than this, and it frightened you more.
   > What: Charcoal is almost pure carbon: fuel, and the reducing agent that turns ore into metal.
   > Chemistry: Heat wood without enough oxygen to burn and the volatile compounds escape as smoke, tar, methanol and acetic acid. What's left is carbon. This is pyrolysis.
   > How: Smelt logs in a furnace.
   > Tip: A tree farm now saves hours later. Charcoal fuels everything until you have coke.
2. **Copper**: 16x `minecraft:copper_ingot` *(after: Ready for Chemistry)*
   > What: Copper is three quarters of bronze, and MI uses it for rotors, gears and wires.
   > Chemistry: Smelting is reduction: carbon pulls oxygen away from the metal oxide and leaves metal behind, CuO + C → Cu + CO.
   > How: Copper ore is common near the surface, especially in dripstone caves. Smelt the raw copper.
   > Tip: You'll need far more than sixteen: this chapter's pipes, rotors and gears are mostly copper.
3. **Tin**: 4x `modern_industrialization:raw_tin`; 4x `modern_industrialization:tin_ingot` *(after: Copper)*
   > What: Tin is soft on its own, but a little of it makes copper much harder.
   > Chemistry: Real tin comes from cassiterite, SnO₂. Carbon reduces it the same way: SnO₂ + 2C → Sn + 2CO.
   > How: Tin ore here comes from Modern Industrialization (MI). It's grey with pale specks and fairly common underground. Mine it and smelt the raw tin.
4. **The MI Guidebook**: `modern_industrialization:guidebook` *(after: Ready for Chemistry)*
   > What: Modern Industrialization's own manual. It explains each machine and shows multiblock layouts.
   > How: 8 copper nuggets around a book. Break a copper ingot into nuggets first.
   > Tip: JEI (R/U) also shows multiblock shapes in 3D.
5. **Heavy Iron Plates**: 3x `minecraft:heavy_weighted_pressure_plate` *(after: Ready for Chemistry)*
   > What: The Forge Hammer's head is three heavy weighted pressure plates.
   > Chemistry: Iron is dense (7.9 g/cm³), so a slab of it carries a lot of momentum into each blow. That's all a hammer is.
   > How: 2 iron ingots side by side make 1 heavy weighted pressure plate. You need 3, plus 4 more ingots for the base.
6. **The Forge Hammer**: `modern_industrialization:forge_hammer` *(after: Pyrolysis, Heavy Iron Plates)*
   > What: MI's first workstation. It crushes ore and ingots into dust and hammers ingots into plates, rods and bolts.
   > How: 3 heavy weighted pressure plates over 4 iron ingots. Place it and right-click to use.
   > Tip: Ores give at most 2x here. Bigger yields come later from acids, not bigger hammers. Make a spare: the Steam Compressor uses one up.
7. **Metal Dust**: 3x `modern_industrialization:copper_dust`; `modern_industrialization:tin_dust` *(after: The Forge Hammer, Tin)*
   > What: Solid ingots can't blend. Powders can.
   > Chemistry: Grinding a metal to powder gives it a huge surface area, so the two metals mix evenly when they melt together.
   > How: Put copper and tin ingots in the Forge Hammer: 1 ingot makes 1 dust.
8. **Mixing Bronze**: 3x `modern_industrialization:bronze_dust` *(after: Metal Dust)*
   > What: Bronze dust is the blended alloy, ready to melt into ingots.
   > Chemistry: Traditional bronze is about 88% copper and 12% tin by mass. Tin atoms jam the copper crystal so its layers can't slide, which makes it harder.
   > How: Craft 3 copper dust with 1 tin dust to get 3 bronze dust.
   > Tip: The Steam Mixer later turns the same inputs into 4 bronze dust instead of 3.
9. **The First Alloy**: 8x `modern_industrialization:bronze_ingot` *(after: Mixing Bronze)*
   > Metal that never existed until a mind decided it should. The feeling is an old friend.
   > What: Bronze is harder than either copper or tin alone, and it's the frame of your whole steam age.
   > Chemistry: An alloy is a mixture of metals. Its properties can beat its ingredients because the mixed atoms resist being pushed out of line.
   > How: Smelt bronze dust in any furnace.
   > Tip: The boiler, casings and machines ahead eat about sixty ingots. Keep the copper and tin coming.
10. **Bronze Age Hoard**: 4x `modern_industrialization:bronze_block` *(after: The First Alloy)*
   > What: 36 ingots of bronze, stored as blocks.
   > Chemistry: Bronze resists corrosion: its surface forms a thin layer of copper compounds that protects the metal underneath. Bronze statues can last thousands of years.
   > How: 9 bronze ingots make 1 block.
11. **Bronze Paxel**: `mekanismtools:bronze_paxel` *(after: The First Alloy)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools makes paxels from bronze too.
   > Chemistry: Ancient bronze tools replaced stone ones because bronze can be cast, sharpened and repaired. Stone can only be chipped.
   > How: Craft a bronze pickaxe, axe and shovel, then combine them with 2 sticks.
12. **Bronze Armour**: `mekanismtools:bronze_helmet`; `mekanismtools:bronze_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:bronze_leggings`; `mekanismtools:bronze_boots` *(after: The First Alloy)*
   > What: A full set of Mekanism Tools bronze armour: a little tougher than iron.
   > Chemistry: Bronze Age armies wore bronze plate and scale. It was heavy, but a cast and hammered tin-bronze plate turned blades that would cut leather.
   > How: The usual armour shapes, in bronze ingots: 24 ingots for the set.
13. **Bronze Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:bronze_plate` *(after: The First Alloy)*
   > What: Almost every steam machine is built from plates.
   > How: Hammer bronze ingots in the Forge Hammer. Without a hammer tool, 2 ingots make 1 plate.
   > Tip: With an Iron Hammer in the tool slot it's 1 ingot per plate, and the Steam Compressor later does it 1:1 for free.
14. **Rods, Bolts and Rings**: 2x `modern_industrialization:bronze_rod`; 4x `modern_industrialization:bronze_bolt`; `modern_industrialization:bronze_ring` *(after: Bronze Plates)*
   > What: Gears need bolts and a ring; rings need rods and bolts.
   > How: In the Forge Hammer, 1 bronze ingot makes 1 rod, 2 bolts or 1 ring. By hand, 4 rods and 4 bolts make 2 rings (check JEI).
   > Tip: Make a few extra of each. Every gear takes 4 bolts and a ring.
15. **Bronze Gears**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_gear` *(after: Rods, Bolts and Rings)*
   > What: Each machine casing needs a gear at its centre.
   > How: 4 bronze plates, 4 bolts and 1 ring (check JEI for the shape).
   > Tip: Make extra rings and bolts while you're at it. You'll need several casings.
16. **Bronze Machine Casing**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_machine_casing` *(after: Bronze Gears)*
   > What: The core of every steam machine. You'll also need one for the Dissolver in Chapter II.
   > How: 8 bronze plates around 1 bronze gear.
   > Tip: The macerator, compressor, mixer, cutter and water pump each take one, and so does every multiblock hatch. Make a few.
17. **Glass**: 8x `minecraft:glass`; 2x `minecraft:glass_pane` *(after: Pyrolysis)*
   > What: Tanks have a glass core, every batch of fluid pipes needs a pane, and the mixer and cutter have glass windows.
   > Chemistry: Sand is mostly silica, SiO₂. Melt it and cool it quickly and the atoms freeze in a jumble instead of a crystal: that's glass, a solid with the structure of a liquid.
   > How: Smelt sand. 6 glass blocks make 16 panes.
18. **Bronze Tank**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_tank` *(after: Bronze Plates, Glass)*
   > What: A bronze tank stores 4 buckets of fluid, and the boiler and water pump each need one.
   > Chemistry: Bronze resists corrosion from water, which is why it was used for ship fittings for centuries.
   > How: 8 bronze plates around 1 glass block.
19. **The Wrench**: `modern_industrialization:wrench` *(after: Bronze Plates)*
   > What: MI's wrench rotates MI machines, sets which face they output from, and picks them up quickly.
   > How: 5 bronze plates in a wrench shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: Handy when you rearrange your steam setup for the Coke Oven in Chapter II. Held near a multiblock controller, it also highlights where hatches can go.
20. **Bronze Barrel**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_barrel` *(after: Bronze Plates)*
   > What: A barrel that holds 32 stacks of a single item and keeps them when broken.
   > How: 8 bronze plates around a wooden barrel. Right-click to put a stack in, left-click to take one out.
   > Tip: One barrel of cobblestone or charcoal clears a lot of chest space.
21. **Iron Plates**: 8x `modern_industrialization:iron_plate` *(after: The Forge Hammer)*
   > What: Iron plates are the first step to the Iron Hammer, the tool that unlocks brick dust.
   > Chemistry: Hammering metal flat squeezes its crystal grains and tangles their defects, so the plate ends up harder than the ingot. Smiths call it work hardening.
   > How: In the Forge Hammer, 2 iron ingots make 1 plate (1:1 once you have the Iron Hammer).
22. **Large Iron Plates**: 5x `modern_industrialization:iron_large_plate` *(after: Iron Plates)*
   > What: The head of the Iron Hammer is made of large plates.
   > How: Craft 4 iron plates in a 2x2 into 1 large plate. That's about 40 iron in total.
   > Tip: Ultimine an iron vein first. This is the hungriest step of the chapter.
23. **The Iron Hammer**: `modern_industrialization:iron_hammer` *(after: Large Iron Plates)*
   > What: Put it in the Forge Hammer's tool slot to unlock better recipes: 1 ingot per plate, and crushing bricks into dust.
   > How: 5 large iron plates and 2 sticks (check JEI). The tool loses durability with each use.
   > Tip: Only use the tool slot when you need it. Plain recipes don't wear it down.
24. **Clay**: 16x `minecraft:clay_ball` *(after: Ready for Chemistry)*
   > What: Clay goes into bricks twice: once as bricks to crush, and again raw in the fire clay mix.
   > Chemistry: Clay is weathered rock: tiny flakes of aluminosilicate minerals such as kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄. Water between the flakes is what makes it mouldable.
   > How: Dig clay blocks from riverbeds, lakes and swamps. Each block breaks into 4 balls.
   > Tip: The boiler alone needs 12 clay balls and the Steam Blast Furnace in Chapter II far more. Take a whole clay patch.
25. **Bricks**: 8x `minecraft:brick` *(after: Clay)*
   > What: Single bricks, the half of fire clay you crush.
   > Chemistry: Around 600 °C, clay minerals lose the water locked inside their crystals; hotter still, the grains fuse. The result is ceramic, and it can't turn back into clay.
   > How: Smelt clay balls in a furnace.
26. **Brick Dust**: 4x `modern_industrialization:brick_dust` *(after: The Iron Hammer, Bricks)*
   > What: Brick dust is half of fire clay.
   > Chemistry: Potters call crushed fired clay grog. It has already shrunk in the kiln, so mixing it into raw clay stops the new brick cracking when heated.
   > How: Hammer bricks in the Forge Hammer with the Iron Hammer in the tool slot: 1 brick makes 1 dust.
27. **Fire Clay**: 6x `modern_industrialization:fire_clay_dust` *(after: Brick Dust)*
   > What: Fire clay is a refractory: a material that stays solid at temperatures that would ruin ordinary brick.
   > Chemistry: Refractory clays are rich in alumina (Al₂O₃) and silica (SiO₂), which melt far above a fire's temperature.
   > How: Craft 2 clay balls with 2 brick dust to make 3 fire clay dust.
28. **Fire Clay Bricks**: 4x `modern_industrialization:fire_clay_brick` *(after: Fire Clay)*
   > What: Single fire bricks, ready to stack into blocks.
   > Chemistry: Firing drives the bound water out of clay minerals and fuses the grains together. That change can't be undone.
   > How: Smelt fire clay dust in a furnace.
29. **Firebrick Blocks**: 3x `modern_industrialization:fire_clay_bricks` *(after: Fire Clay Bricks)*
   > What: The bronze boiler sits on a row of 3 fire clay brick blocks, and the Steam Furnace on 3 more.
   > How: 4 fire clay bricks in a 2x2 make 1 block.
   > Tip: Chapter II's Steam Blast Furnace is built from dozens of these. Start stockpiling clay.
30. **The Diamond Hammer**: `modern_industrialization:diamond_hammer` *(after: The Iron Hammer, Steam Compressor)*
   > What: A more durable hammer for the Forge Hammer's tool slot. It does the same jobs as the Iron Hammer and wears out far more slowly.
   > Chemistry: Diamond is carbon locked into a rigid 3D lattice, which makes it the hardest natural material. Iron bends; diamond doesn't.
   > How: The Steam Compressor presses 1 diamond into 1 diamond plate; 4 plates make a large plate. Then 5 large plates and 2 sticks, in the Iron Hammer's shape.
   > Tip: That's 20 diamonds. Ore yields stay capped at 2x either way, so build it only if you're tired of crafting Iron Hammers.
31. **Fire Clay in Bulk**: 32x `modern_industrialization:fire_clay_dust` *(after: Steam Mixer, Fire Clay)*
   > What: Stockpile fire clay for the Steam Blast Furnace in Chapter II.
   > Chemistry: The same 2 clay + 2 brick dust gives 4 fire clay in the Steam Mixer instead of 3 by hand. Better mixing, better yield.
   > Tip: The Steam Macerator grinds bricks and brick blocks into dust too (4 dust per block), so the Iron Hammer can rest.
32. **Copper Plates**: 6x `modern_industrialization:copper_plate` *(after: The Forge Hammer, Copper)*
   > What: Copper gears and curved plates start as flat plates.
   > Chemistry: Copper is one of the most malleable metals: its atoms sit in a close-packed lattice whose layers slide over each other without breaking apart.
   > How: In the Forge Hammer, 2 copper ingots make 1 plate (1:1 with the Iron Hammer in the tool slot).
33. **Curved Copper**: 4x `modern_industrialization:copper_curved_plate` *(after: Copper Plates)*
   > What: Rotor blades are curved copper plates on a copper rod.
   > How: Hammer 2 copper ingots into 1 curved plate, or 1 plate into 1 curved plate with the Iron Hammer in the tool slot.
   > Tip: Two rotors need 8 blades, and 2 curved plates and a rod make 4 blades.
34. **Copper Rods and Bolts**: 4x `modern_industrialization:copper_rod`; 8x `modern_industrialization:copper_bolt` *(after: The Forge Hammer, Copper)*
   > What: Rods hold blades, bolts hold rotors and gears together, and the Steam Compressor needs 2 rods of its own.
   > How: In the Forge Hammer, 1 copper ingot makes 1 rod or 2 bolts.
   > Tip: The Steam Cutting Machine later doubles both. Until then, the hammer will do.
35. **Copper Blades**: 8x `modern_industrialization:copper_blade` *(after: Curved Copper, Copper Rods and Bolts)*
   > What: The vanes of a rotor: they push water and steam through a pipe when the rotor turns.
   > How: 2 curved copper plates stacked on a copper rod make 4 blades.
36. **Copper Rings**: 4x `modern_industrialization:copper_ring` *(after: Copper Rods and Bolts)*
   > What: Every rotor and every gear is built around a ring.
   > How: 4 copper rods and 4 copper bolts make 2 rings, or the Forge Hammer makes 1 ring from 1 ingot.
37. **Copper Gears**: 4x `modern_industrialization:copper_gear` *(after: Copper Plates, Copper Rings)*
   > What: The macerator, compressor, cutter and water pump each take 2 copper gears, the mixer 1.
   > How: 4 copper plates, 4 copper bolts and 1 copper ring, the same shape as the bronze gear.
   > Tip: That's 9 gears for the full set of machines. Build them as you need them.
38. **Copper Rotors**: 2x `modern_industrialization:copper_rotor` *(after: Copper Blades, Copper Rings)*
   > What: Rotors push fluid through pipes and pumps.
   > How: 4 copper blades, 1 copper ring and 4 copper bolts (check JEI).
   > Tip: Fluid pipes take 2 per batch, the mixer 2 and the water pump 2. Make six.
39. **Copper Drill Head**: `modern_industrialization:copper_drill_head` *(after: Copper Gears, Curved Copper)*
   > What: The tip of the Steam Mining Drill.
   > How: A copper plate, 2 curved plates, a rod, 2 copper gears and 3 bolts (check JEI).
   > Tip: Copper is soft for a drill bit, but this one only has to turn. The drill's own power does the work.
40. **Steam Mining Drill**: `modern_industrialization:steam_mining_drill` *(after: Copper Drill Head)*
   > What: A fuel-burning mining tool that digs a 3x3 area and can give an easy Silk Touch.
   > How: Furnaces, diamonds, large iron plates, the copper drill head and a bucket (check JEI). Fill it from a water source and feed it solid fuel.
   > Tip: Silk-touched ore goes into the Forge Hammer for 2 raw ore each.
41. **Ore, Whole**: 8x any of `or(item(modern_industrialization:tin_ore)item(modern_industrialization:deepslate_tin_ore))` *(after: Steam Mining Drill)*
   > What: Mine 8 tin ore blocks whole with the drill's Silk Touch mode.
   > Chemistry: An ore block is mostly worthless rock (gangue) around a little mineral. Crushing it first frees more of the mineral grains, which is why the Forge Hammer gets 2 raw ore from a block.
   > How: Switch the Steam Mining Drill to Silk Touch (see its tooltip), mine tin ore, and hammer each block into 2 raw tin.
42. **Steam Power**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_boiler` *(after: Bronze Tank, Firebrick Blocks, Bronze Machine Casing)*
   > The engines remember you even if the world doesn't. Pressure, heat, motion: old friends.
   > What: Burn fuel, boil water, and the expanding steam does work. Welcome to the industrial revolution.
   > Chemistry: Water expands more than 1,600 times in volume when it boils into steam. That pressure is what drives the machines.
   > How: 4 bronze plates, a bronze tank, a furnace and 3 fire clay brick blocks. Give it water and fuel (coal or charcoal), and place steam machines next to it.
   > Tip: A hot boiler makes 8 mB of steam a tick, enough for four bronze machines at once.
43. **Steam Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_furnace` *(after: Steam Power)*
   > What: Smelts with steam instead of fuel. Your first automated machine, and the only one that needs no pipes.
   > How: 5 bronze plates, a furnace and 3 fire clay brick blocks. Place it touching the boiler.
   > Tip: It's as slow as a vanilla furnace, but steam carries heat so well that it costs about a tenth of the fuel.
44. **Curved Plates**: 6x `modern_industrialization:bronze_curved_plate` *(after: Bronze Plates)*
   > What: Pipes are made from curved bronze plates.
   > How: Hammer 2 bronze ingots into 1 curved plate in the Forge Hammer. Later the Steam Compressor bends plates into curved plates 1:1.
   > Tip: You need 6 per batch of 16 pipes. Make 12 to have pipes to spare.
45. **Fluid Pipes**: 8x `modern_industrialization:fluid_pipe` *(after: Curved Plates, Copper Rotors, Glass)*
   > Water that goes where you tell it. You used to do that with rivers.
   > What: MI fluid pipes carry water, steam and later every chemical in the pack. Four of the five steam machines are built with them.
   > How: 6 bronze curved plates, 2 copper rotors and a glass pane make 16 pipes.
   > Tip: A pipe holds one fluid at a time. Right-click a pipe with a wrench to change its connection; item pipes need steel gears, so they wait for Chapter II.
46. **Coal by the Block**: 4x `minecraft:coal_block` *(after: Steam Power)*
   > What: A block of coal holds 9 coal and burns as long as all nine, so one block keeps a boiler going far longer between refills.
   > Chemistry: The energy is in the carbon, not the shape: packing coal tighter doesn't add heat, it just stores more of it in one slot.
   > How: 9 coal in a crafting grid make 1 block.
   > Tip: Feed boilers coal blocks through a hopper and you can leave them alone for a long time.
47. **Steam in a Bucket**: `modern_industrialization:steam_bucket` *(after: Steam Power)*
   > What: Smelt a water bucket in any furnace and you get a bucket of steam: portable power for a machine far from the boiler.
   > Chemistry: Boiling doesn't change water chemically; H₂O stays H₂O. It only gives the molecules enough energy to escape the liquid, about 2,260 joules per gram.
   > Tip: Handy for testing a machine before you've run a pipe to it.
48. **Diamonds for Grinding**: 3x `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Ready for Chemistry)*
   > What: The Steam Macerator grinds with 2 diamonds and the Steam Cutting Machine cuts with 1.
   > Chemistry: Diamond is the hardest natural material, so it grinds and cuts everything softer than itself. Real industrial saws and grinders are tipped with diamond grit for the same reason.
   > How: Diamond ore is most common near the bottom of the world, around Y -59. An iron pickaxe mines it.
   > Tip: A Fortune pickaxe helps a lot here.
49. **Steam Macerator**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_macerator` *(after: Fluid Pipes, Copper Gears, Diamonds for Grinding)*
   > What: Grinds ore and items into dust without wearing out a tool.
   > How: 2 diamonds, 2 copper gears, a bronze machine casing and 3 fluid pipes. Ores give at most 2x until acids.
   > Tip: It also grinds bricks into brick dust, so your Iron Hammer can rest.
50. **Steam Compressor**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_compressor` *(after: Fluid Pipes, Copper Gears)*
   > What: Presses ingots into plates 1:1, and plates into curved plates.
   > How: A Forge Hammer, 2 copper rods, 2 copper gears, a bronze machine casing and 3 fluid pipes. The Forge Hammer goes into the recipe, so craft a second one.
   > Tip: Machines need lots of plates. Keep this one fed.
51. **Steam Mixer**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_mixer` *(after: Fluid Pipes, Copper Gears)*
   > What: Mixes dusts (like copper and tin into bronze) and fluids.
   > Chemistry: Same copper and tin, less loss: a good process wastes less of its inputs. That's called yield.
   > How: 2 glass, a copper gear, 2 copper rotors, a bronze machine casing and 3 fluid pipes. Here 3 copper dust + 1 tin dust makes 4 bronze dust, one more than by hand.
52. **Steam Cutting Machine**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_cutting_machine` *(after: Fluid Pipes, Copper Gears, Diamonds for Grinding)*
   > What: Cuts ingots into 2 rods, rods into bolts, and logs into 6 planks.
   > How: A diamond, 2 glass, 2 copper gears, a casing and pipes. It needs lubricant as a cutting fluid. You'll make lubricant from creosote and redstone in Chapter II, so build it now and run it then.
   > Tip: Until then, the Forge Hammer makes rods and bolts.
53. **Endless Water**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_water_pump` *(after: Fluid Pipes, Copper Gears, Bronze Tank)*
   > Fire, water, metal, motion. The pieces of a world are coming back to you.
   > What: A steam-powered pump that pulls water from the ground, so your boiler never runs dry.
   > How: 2 copper rotors, 2 copper gears, a bronze tank, a machine casing and 3 fluid pipes. Place it next to the boiler, or pipe its water into it.
   > Tip: The Coke Oven in Chapter II runs on steam, so a boiler that never runs dry comes first. Next stop: coke and steel.
54. **Efficient Alloying**: 32x `modern_industrialization:bronze_dust` *(after: Steam Mixer)*
   > What: Mix 32 bronze dust in the Steam Mixer.
   > Chemistry: In real metallurgy, alloy ratios are measured by mass or by number of atoms. Getting the ratio right matters more than the amount.
   > Tip: Pipe the macerator's dust straight into the mixer and you'll never mix by hand again.
55. **Plates at Scale**: 64x `modern_industrialization:bronze_plate` *(after: Steam Compressor)*
   > What: Press a full stack of bronze plates in the Steam Compressor.
   > How: The compressor gives 1 plate per ingot, where the bare Forge Hammer gives 1 per 2.
   > Tip: Chapter II's hatches, tanks and steel upgrades are mostly plates. A stack in a barrel saves trips.

### II. Steam and Steel

*Destructive distillation turns coal into coke, and coke turns iron into steel. At the end of this chapter, matter itself opens up to you.*

1. **A Kiln's Worth of Bricks**: 16x `minecraft:bricks` *(after: Endless Water)*
   > Smoke rising from a hill of earth, and what came out of it burning hotter than anything before. That memory is older than any city.
   > What: The Coke Oven is built from ordinary brick blocks: 8 for the controller and 21 more for its walls.
   > Chemistry: Firing clay drives out the water bound in its minerals and fuses the grains, turning soft mud into ceramic.
   > How: Smelt clay balls into bricks, then craft 4 bricks into a brick block.
   > Tip: Rivers and swamps are full of clay. Ultimine a clay patch.
2. **Coal for Coking**: 32x `minecraft:coal` *(after: Endless Water)*
   > What: The Coke Oven bakes coal, not charcoal, and it's hungry: one coal becomes one coke.
   > Chemistry: Coal is ancient plant matter, pressed and heated underground for millions of years. It's mostly carbon, plus hydrogen, sulfur and tars that coking will drive off.
   > How: Coal ore is common in exposed stone and mountains. Ultimine a vein.
   > Tip: Coal dust works too (it cokes into coke dust), and the Steam Macerator grinds coal 1:1.
3. **The Coke Oven**: `modern_industrialization:coke_oven` *(after: A Kiln's Worth of Bricks)*
   > What: The controller of a small multiblock that bakes coal into coke.
   > Chemistry: Coal is carbon mixed with many other compounds. Bake it without air and those volatiles are driven off. This is destructive distillation.
   > How: 8 brick blocks around a furnace.
4. **Hatches**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_item_input_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:bronze_item_output_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:bronze_fluid_input_hatch` *(after: The Coke Oven)*
   > What: MI multiblocks have no inventory of their own. Hatches built into the walls take items and steam in and push products out.
   > How: An item hatch is a hopper on a bronze machine casing; a fluid hatch is a bronze tank on a casing (check JEI for the output versions).
   > Tip: Hold a hatch or a wrench near the controller to see where hatches can go and what's missing.
5. **A Way Out for Tar**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_fluid_output_hatch` *(after: Hatches)*
   > What: Coking coal also drives out a liquid. Without a fluid output hatch it has nowhere to go and is lost.
   > Chemistry: The volatile part of coal leaves as gas and condenses into tar as it cools. Real coke works collect it, because coal tar is a feedstock, not waste.
   > How: A bronze machine casing on top of a bronze tank. Swap one wall brick of the Coke Oven for it.
   > Tip: Pipe it straight into a tank so it never fills up.
6. **Build the Coke Oven**: checkmark *(after: Hatches)*
   > What: Put the shell together and the controller comes to life.
   > How: Press R on the Coke Oven in JEI or open the MI guidebook to see the 3D layout: a 3x3x3 cube of brick blocks with the controller in one face. Swap wall bricks for hatches: item in, item out, steam in, and a fluid output for creosote.
   > Tip: Pipe steam from your boiler into the fluid input hatch. Click the checkmark once the controller shows it's formed.
7. **Coke**: 16x `modern_industrialization:coke` *(after: Build the Coke Oven, Coal for Coking)*
   > Carbon with everything weak burned out of it. You used to build with something like this. Mountains, mostly.
   > What: Coke is exactly what a blast furnace needs: strong, porous, nearly pure carbon. It also burns four times as long as coal.
   > Chemistry: With the hydrogen, sulfur and tars baked out, what's left is a carbon skeleton that burns hot and clean.
   > How: Feed coal into the item input hatch. Each coal becomes 1 coke in 30 seconds.
8. **Fuel Reserve**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coke_block` *(after: Coke)*
   > What: A stockpile of coke for boilers, generators and future steel.
   > Chemistry: Coke is porous. Air flows through it, which is why it burns so hot and steadily in a furnace.
   > Tip: A full Coke Oven running overnight fills these quickly.
9. **Byproduct: Creosote**: `modern_industrialization:creosote_bucket` *(after: Build the Coke Oven, A Way Out for Tar)*
   > What: Half the time, coking a coal also yields 500 mB of creosote. Nothing is wasted in chemistry: creosote becomes lubricant now and generator fuel later.
   > Chemistry: Coal-tar creosote is a mix of phenols, cresols and ring-shaped hydrocarbons, the same family of compounds that makes tar smell the way it does.
   > How: Pipe it out of the fluid output hatch into a tank and fill a bucket from the tank.
10. **Lubricant**: `modern_industrialization:lubricant_bucket` *(after: Byproduct: Creosote)*
   > What: The Steam Cutting Machine needs lubricant as cutting fluid. Now you can finally run it.
   > How: In the Steam Mixer, 500 mB of creosote and 1 redstone make 500 mB of lubricant.
   > Tip: Each cut uses only 1 mB, so one bucket lasts a very long time. The Cutting Machine now makes your steel rods and bolts at 2 per ingot.
11. **Coke Dust**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coke_dust` *(after: Coke)*
   > What: Steel is mixed as dust, so the carbon has to be a powder too.
   > Chemistry: Coke is the reducing agent in a real blast furnace: it pulls oxygen out of iron ore and supplies the carbon that becomes steel.
   > How: Grind coke in the Steam Macerator, or coke coal dust directly in the Coke Oven.
12. **Iron Dust**: 7x `modern_industrialization:iron_dust` *(after: Coke Dust)*
   > What: The other ingredient of steel.
   > How: Grind iron ingots in the Steam Macerator or the Forge Hammer (1 ingot makes 1 dust).
   > Tip: Macerating iron ore gives 2 raw iron per ore, which smelts into more ingots than mining alone.
13. **Uncooked Steel**: 7x `modern_industrialization:uncooked_steel_dust` *(after: Iron Dust)*
   > What: A blend of iron and carbon, ready for the blast furnace.
   > Chemistry: Real steel holds far less carbon than this mix suggests, but the idea is right: carbon is the ingredient that turns soft iron into steel.
   > How: Craft 7 iron dust with 2 coke dust to get 7 uncooked steel dust.
14. **Steel by the Batch**: 27x `modern_industrialization:uncooked_steel_dust` *(after: Uncooked Steel)*
   > What: The Steam Mixer turns the same 7 iron dust and 2 coke dust into 9 uncooked steel instead of 7.
   > Chemistry: Hand-mixing powders always leaves pockets of unmixed metal. Stirring blends them evenly, so less of the batch is wasted.
   > Tip: Pipe the macerator into the mixer and the mixer into the blast furnace's input hatch.
15. **Blast Furnace Materials**: 16x `modern_industrialization:fire_clay_bricks`; `minecraft:blast_furnace` *(after: Coke)*
   > What: The Steam Blast Furnace is a tower of fire clay bricks: 8 around its controller and 29 more for the walls.
   > How: Make fire clay bricks as in Chapter I (the Steam Macerator grinds bricks into brick dust now). A vanilla blast furnace is 5 iron, a furnace and 3 smooth stone.
   > Tip: Automate it: macerator → mixer → steam furnace. You'll want a lot of these.
16. **The Steam Blast Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:steam_blast_furnace` *(after: Blast Furnace Materials)*
   > What: A multiblock that gets hot enough to melt iron and dissolve carbon into it.
   > How: Craft the controller from 8 fire clay brick blocks around a blast furnace. Check the structure in JEI: the Coke Oven's shape in fire clay bricks with one extra hollow layer on top, and the same three hatches.
   > Tip: Some later recipes in this furnace need a steel hatch. Steel itself only needs bronze ones.
17. **Steel**: 8x `modern_industrialization:steel_ingot` *(after: The Steam Blast Furnace, Uncooked Steel)*
   > Iron that bends without breaking. You once forged weapons for gods out of something very like this.
   > What: Iron with a small, controlled amount of carbon (about 0.2-2%) is steel: strong, tough, and the backbone of every machine to come.
   > Chemistry: Carbon atoms sit in the gaps between iron atoms and stop the layers sliding. Too much carbon and you get brittle cast iron. Chemistry is about the right ratio.
   > How: Put uncooked steel dust in the blast furnace's item input hatch. Each dust becomes 1 steel ingot in 30 seconds.
18. **Steel Paxel**: `mekanismtools:steel_paxel` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Mekanism's steel tools are diamond tier: a steel paxel mines obsidian, which the Combiner needs, and lasts far longer than iron.
   > Chemistry: A little carbon in iron makes it much harder: carbon atoms in the gaps of the iron lattice pin it so the layers can't slip.
   > How: A steel pickaxe, axe and shovel with 2 sticks (check JEI).
   > Tip: No diamonds needed for obsidian now. Save your diamonds for the Combiner itself.
19. **Steel Plates**: 8x `modern_industrialization:steel_plate` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: The Dissolver and Combiner are framed in steel plates, and steel gears need them too.
   > How: The Steam Compressor presses 1 steel ingot into 1 plate.
   > Tip: You need at least 8 for the Dissolver and Combiner, plus more for gears and casings. Keep the compressor busy.
20. **Steel Rods, Bolts and Rings**: 4x `modern_industrialization:steel_rod`; 8x `modern_industrialization:steel_bolt`; 2x `modern_industrialization:steel_ring` *(after: Steel, Lubricant)*
   > What: Steel gears need steel bolts and rings, and the LV motors of Chapter IV are built on steel rods.
   > How: The Steam Cutting Machine cuts 1 steel ingot into 2 rods and 1 rod into 2 bolts, using a drop of lubricant each time. The Forge Hammer works too, at worse ratios.
   > Tip: 4 rods and 4 bolts craft into 2 rings, or the Steam Compressor bends 1 rod into 1 ring.
21. **Steel Gears**: 2x `modern_industrialization:steel_gear` *(after: Steel Plates, Steel Rods, Bolts and Rings)*
   > What: Steel machine casings (the core of every LV machine in Chapter IV) and item pipes need steel gears.
   > How: Same pattern as bronze: 4 steel plates, 4 steel bolts and 1 steel ring (check JEI).
22. **Steel Machine Casing**: `modern_industrialization:steel_machine_casing` *(after: Steel Gears)*
   > What: The steel version of the bronze casing. Steel hatches, steel upgrades, the Packer and every LV machine hull are built around one.
   > How: 8 steel plates around a steel gear.
   > Tip: That's 12 steel ingots per casing. Chapter IV wants several, so keep the blast furnace running.
23. **Item Pipes**: 16x `modern_industrialization:item_pipe` *(after: Steel Gears)*
   > What: MI item pipes move items between machines, so dust, ingots and coke flow on their own.
   > How: 6 bronze curved plates and 2 steel gears make 16 pipes.
   > Tip: Item pipes are on whitelist by default: right-click a connection and either add the items to move or switch it to blacklist. Configure both ends.
24. **Steel Hatches**: `modern_industrialization:steel_item_input_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:steel_item_output_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:steel_fluid_input_hatch` *(after: Steel Machine Casing)*
   > What: Steel hatches hold more than bronze ones, and a steam multiblock with at least one steel hatch is upgraded to steel tier: twice as fast, as long as the recipe stays within 4 EU/t.
   > How: Each is a steel machine casing with a hopper or a steel tank on top (check JEI for the output versions).
   > Tip: Swap one hatch on your Coke Oven and Steam Blast Furnace and both run at double speed.
25. **Packer and Unpacker**: `modern_industrialization:steel_packer`; `modern_industrialization:steel_unpacker` *(after: Item Pipes, Steel Machine Casing)*
   > What: The Packer does small crafts on its own: blocks, double ingots and pipes. The Unpacker takes blocks back apart. Both exist only in steel.
   > How: A steel machine casing with bronze gears, fluid pipes and item pipes (check JEI; the Unpacker also needs bronze rods).
   > Tip: Pipe ingots into the Packer and store your metal as blocks: nine times fewer slots.
26. **Nickel**: 8x `modern_industrialization:nickel_ingot` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Nickel goes into two alloys you'll lean on: invar now, and cupronickel heating coils in Chapter IV.
   > Chemistry: Nickel (Ni, element 28) sits right next to iron and cobalt and shares their magnetism. Most of Earth's nickel is thought to be in its iron core.
   > How: MI nickel ore is fairly rare scattered, but rich deposits sit around Y -32 to 8. Smelt the raw nickel, or macerate it first for 2x.
27. **Invar Dust**: 6x `modern_industrialization:invar_dust` *(after: Nickel)*
   > What: The mixed powder of iron and nickel, ready to smelt.
   > How: In the Steam Mixer, 2 iron dust and 1 nickel dust make 3 invar dust. Grind nickel ingots in the macerator first.
28. **Invar**: 6x `modern_industrialization:invar_ingot` *(after: Invar Dust)*
   > What: Invar is iron with about a third nickel. MI builds rotary blades, heatproof casings and the alloy smelter from it.
   > Chemistry: Almost every metal expands as it warms. Invar (64% Fe, 36% Ni) barely does: its magnetic order cancels the thermal expansion. Its discovery won Charles-Édouard Guillaume the 1920 Nobel Prize in Physics.
   > How: Smelt invar dust in any furnace.
29. **Invar Plates and Gears**: 4x `modern_industrialization:invar_plate`; `modern_industrialization:invar_gear` *(after: Invar)*
   > What: An invar gear is the hub of the rotary blade. Later, invar plates and gears make the heatproof casings of the Electric Blast Furnace.
   > How: The Steam Compressor presses invar ingots into plates 1:1. A gear is 4 plates, 4 invar bolts and an invar ring, the same shape as before.
30. **Diamond Dust**: 4x `modern_industrialization:diamond_dust` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Diamond dust is the cutting edge of the invar rotary blade.
   > Chemistry: Industrial abrasives are mostly diamond grit, and most of that is synthetic, made by squeezing graphite at around 5 GPa and 1,500 °C.
   > How: The Steam Macerator grinds 1 diamond into 1 dust. It's slow (40 seconds each), so leave it running.
31. **Invar Rotary Blade**: `modern_industrialization:invar_rotary_blade` *(after: Invar Plates and Gears, Diamond Dust)*
   > What: The grinding wheel of the Steam Quarry, the Electric Macerator and the Electric Cutting Machine.
   > How: 1 invar gear with 4 diamond dust around it.
   > Tip: Each blade costs 4 diamonds. Chapter IV's macerator and cutter each take one, so plan for two more.
32. **Steel Alloy Smelter**: `extended_industrialization:steel_alloy_smelter` *(after: Invar Plates and Gears, Bronze Rotors, Steel Machine Casing)*
   > What: An Extended Industrialization machine that melts metals together and pours alloy ingots directly: bronze, invar, cupronickel, electrum, battery alloy, brass and more.
   > Chemistry: Alloying in the melt is how bronze was really made: liquid copper and tin mix atom by atom, then freeze together.
   > How: Invar plates, a bronze rotor, fluid pipes and a steel machine casing (check JEI). Feed it ingots, dusts or nuggets.
   > Tip: 27 copper and 9 tin nuggets make 4 bronze ingots: the same 3:1 ratio as the dust, with no mixing step.
33. **Drill Parts**: `modern_industrialization:bronze_drill_head`; 2x `modern_industrialization:iron_gear` *(after: Item Pipes)*
   > What: Bronze drills are the quarry's consumable. Each batch of 4 needs a bronze drill head, 2 iron gears, an item pipe and a fluid pipe.
   > How: The drill head is a bronze plate, 2 curved plates, a rod, 2 bronze gears and bolts. Iron gears are 4 iron plates, iron bolts and an iron ring (check JEI).
34. **The Steam Quarry**: `modern_industrialization:steam_quarry`; 4x `modern_industrialization:bronze_drill` *(after: Drill Parts, Invar Rotary Blade)*
   > What: A steam multiblock that wears out bronze drills to bring up ore from deeper than bedrock. Slow, but you never have to dig.
   > How: The controller takes steel large plates, steel gears, item pipes, an invar rotary blade and a steel machine casing (check JEI for the shape and its ore table).
   > Tip: It eats a lot of steel, so build it once your Steam Blast Furnace runs on its own. Quarry ore still obeys the 2x cap until acids.
35. **Bronze Blades**: 8x `modern_industrialization:bronze_blade` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: The vanes of a bronze rotor. Steel upgrades and the Steel Wiremill of Chapter IV both need bronze rotors.
   > How: 2 bronze curved plates on a bronze rod make 4 blades, just like the copper ones.
36. **Bronze Rotors**: 3x `modern_industrialization:bronze_rotor` *(after: Bronze Blades)*
   > What: A rotor that holds its shape under steel-tier loads.
   > How: 4 bronze blades, 1 bronze ring and 4 bronze bolts (check JEI).
   > Tip: The Steel Wiremill takes 2 and each pair of Steel Upgrades takes 1.
37. **Steel Upgrades**: `modern_industrialization:steel_upgrade`; `modern_industrialization:steel_macerator` *(after: Bronze Rotors, Steel Machine Casing)*
   > What: A Steel Upgrade turns a bronze steam machine into its steel version: twice as fast for recipes up to 4 EU/t.
   > How: Bronze rods, a bronze rotor, 2 bronze gears, a steel machine casing, fluid pipes and fire clay bricks make 2 upgrades (check JEI). Combine one with the Bronze Macerator.
   > Tip: Upgrade the machines that bottleneck you first, usually the macerator.
38. **Steel Tank**: `modern_industrialization:steel_tank` *(after: Steel Plates)*
   > What: A tank that holds 16 buckets, four times a bronze one. The steel boiler is built around it.
   > How: 8 steel plates around a glass block.
   > Tip: A steel tank under the Coke Oven's creosote output means you rarely have to empty it.
39. **Steel Boiler**: `modern_industrialization:steel_boiler` *(after: Steel Tank)*
   > What: Twice the steam of the bronze boiler, up to 16 mB a tick.
   > How: Steel plates, a steel tank, a furnace and 3 fire clay brick blocks, or a bronze boiler with a Steel Upgrade (check JEI).
   > Tip: A steel water pump doubles the water too, up to 2 buckets every 5 seconds.
40. **Large Steel Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:steel_large_plate` *(after: Steel Plates)*
   > What: Large steel plates go into the Steam Quarry and the Steel Hammer.
   > How: 4 steel plates in a 2x2 make 1 large plate.
41. **The Steel Hammer**: `modern_industrialization:steel_hammer` *(after: Large Steel Plates)*
   > What: The steel version of the Iron Hammer: same recipes in the Forge Hammer, many more uses before it breaks.
   > Chemistry: Carbon steel is far harder than wrought iron, so the striking face deforms less with every blow.
   > How: 5 large steel plates and 2 sticks, in the Iron Hammer's shape.
42. **Automatic Trash Can**: `modern_industrialization:trash_can` *(after: Steel Plates)*
   > What: Destroys any item or fluid piped into it. Hold it over a machine's fluid tank and click to dump that tank.
   > How: 8 steel plates around a lava bucket.
   > Tip: A full output slot stops a machine. A trash can on the end of an overflow pipe keeps cobblestone and spare creosote from jamming things.
43. **Blocks of Redstone**: `minecraft:redstone_block` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: The Copper Generator and its Iron upgrade each have a block of redstone in their recipe, so you'll need two in all.
   > How: 9 redstone dust make 1 block. Redstone ore sits deep, mostly below Y 16, and needs an iron pickaxe.
   > Tip: Ultimine a redstone vein: one gives plenty, and lubricant needs dust too.
44. **A Simple Generator**: `generatorgalore:copper_generator` *(after: Blocks of Redstone)*
   > What: Generator Galore's Copper Generator burns solid fuel into FE (Forge Energy) and pushes it into machines it touches.
   > Chemistry: Burning releases the chemical energy stored in carbon bonds as heat; the generator turns that heat into electricity.
   > How: 7 copper ingots around a furnace, with a block of redstone.
45. **Forge Energy**: `generatorgalore:iron_generator` *(after: A Simple Generator)*
   > What: Some machines run on FE instead of steam. You'll need it for the Dissolver.
   > How: Upgrade the Copper Generator: surround it with 7 iron ingots and a block of redstone to make the Iron Generator.
   > Tip: A Mekanism Heat Generator or Powah Furnator also works. Burn coke for long runs.
46. **Heat and Pressure**: 2x `minecraft:magma_block`; 2x `minecraft:piston` *(after: Steel Plates)*
   > What: Besides 4 steel plates and a bronze machine casing, the Dissolver needs 2 magma blocks and 2 pistons.
   > Chemistry: Magma blocks are rock hot enough to glow, a fitting heat source for a machine that tears compounds apart.
   > How: Magma blocks generate in underwater ravines and caves, or can be crafted from 4 magma cream. Pistons need iron, redstone, cobblestone and planks.
47. **Pressure and Precision**: `minecraft:diamond`; 2x `minecraft:obsidian` *(after: Steel Plates, Steel Paxel)*
   > What: The Combiner needs a diamond, 2 obsidian and a piston, plus 4 steel plates and a casing.
   > Chemistry: Obsidian is volcanic glass: lava that cooled too fast for crystals to form.
   > How: Pour water onto a lava source to make obsidian. Your steel paxel is diamond tier, so it mines obsidian; no diamond pickaxe needed. Diamonds are most common near the bottom of the world.
48. **The Dissolver**: `alchemistry:dissolver` *(after: Heat and Pressure, Forge Energy)*
   > Your first gift returns: look at anything and know what it's made of.
   > What: The Dissolver breaks any item into the elements and compounds it's made of.
   > How: 4 steel plates, 2 pistons, 2 magma blocks and a Bronze Machine Casing. Power it with FE, insert anything, and collect the elements.
   > Tip: Some things dissolve into compounds first. Put those back in to break them down further.
49. **The Combiner**: `alchemistry:combiner` *(after: Pressure and Precision, Forge Energy)*
   > And the other half of the gift: what you can take apart, you can put back together.
   > What: The reverse: arrange elements and the Combiner builds them back into items and blocks.
   > How: 4 steel plates, a diamond, 2 obsidian, a piston and a Bronze Machine Casing. It runs on FE too.
   > Tip: Its first real job comes in Chapter IV: sulfuric acid for the lead-acid redstone battery. Taking the world apart and rebuilding it is what this pack is about.
50. **Wood, Undone**: 4x `chemlib:cellulose` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: Your first compound out of the Dissolver.
   > Chemistry: Cellulose is a chain of glucose units, (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ. It's the most common organic compound on Earth and gives wood its strength.
   > How: Dissolve logs: each log gives 1 cellulose. Dissolve the cellulose again to get 6 carbon, 10 hydrogen and 5 oxygen.
51. **Graphite**: 4x `chemlib:graphite` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: Coal and charcoal dissolve into graphite, a pure form of carbon.
   > Chemistry: In graphite, carbon atoms form flat sheets of hexagons that slide over each other. That's why pencil 'lead' leaves a mark.
   > How: Dissolve coal or charcoal: each gives 2 graphite. Each graphite dissolves into 4 carbon.
52. **First Entries in the Periodic Table**: 16x `chemlib:hydrogen`; 16x `chemlib:carbon`; 16x `chemlib:oxygen`; 16x `chemlib:iron` *(after: Wood, Undone, Graphite, The Combiner)*
   > What: Dissolve whatever you have lying around and collect your first elements: H (1), C (6), O (8), Fe (26).
   > Chemistry: The number is the atomic number: how many protons are in the nucleus. Change it and you have a different element.
   > How: Cellulose gives carbon, hydrogen and oxygen; graphite gives carbon. Each iron ingot gives 16 iron.
   > Tip: The Periodic Table chapter tracks every element from here on.
53. **Your First Synthesis**: 4x `chemlib:water` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > Two hydrogen, one oxygen. You once filled oceans with this; today it's a few drops. It's a start, and it's yours.
   > What: Build water from its elements in the Combiner. It's a trivial compound, but you made it from scratch. That's the point.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Hydrogen and oxygen share electrons in covalent bonds, and the bent shape of the molecule makes it polar.
   > How: Pick water as the target in the Combiner's GUI, then supply 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen per water.
54. **Proof of Composition**: 16x `chemlib:copper`; 16x `chemlib:tin` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > What: Dissolve a copper ingot and a tin ingot to see the two elements that make bronze.
   > Chemistry: Copper is element 29 and tin is element 50. Every bronze ingot you made in Chapter I was these two, mixed.
   > How: Each copper or tin ingot dissolves into 16 of its element.
55. **Sweet Chemistry**: `chemlib:sucrose` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > What: Dissolve sugar into sucrose, then sucrose into its elements.
   > Chemistry: Sucrose is glucose and fructose joined together. Dissolved, it gives 12 carbon, 22 hydrogen and 11 oxygen.
   > How: Sugar cane makes sugar; the Dissolver turns 1 sugar into 1 sucrose.
56. **Carbon Is Carbon**: 128x `chemlib:graphite` *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > What: A diamond dissolves into 128 graphite. Expensive, but it proves a point.
   > Chemistry: Diamond and graphite are both pure carbon, called allotropes. In diamond every atom bonds to four neighbours in 3D; in graphite, to three in flat sheets.
   > Tip: Don't dissolve your last diamond. You'll need them for machines.
57. **The Atomizer**: `alchemistry:atomizer` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: An Alchemistry machine that turns a fluid into its compound as items. Its best trick: 500 mB of water becomes 8 ChemLib water.
   > Chemistry: Each ChemLib water dissolves into 2 hydrogen and 1 oxygen, so one bucket of water is 32 hydrogen. That's the easiest hydrogen you'll find for the flight pylon in Chapter III.
   > How: 4 iron ingots, 2 pistons, 2 cauldrons and redstone. Pipe in water from your pump and give it FE.
   > Tip: Chain it: water pump → Atomizer → Dissolver, and hydrogen and oxygen pile up on their own.
58. **The Liquifier**: `alchemistry:liquifier` *(after: The Atomizer)*
   > What: The Atomizer in reverse: 8 compound items become 500 mB of their fluid, ready to pipe.
   > Chemistry: A real chemical plant moves almost everything as liquids and gases, because fluids flow through pipes. Solids have to be carried.
   > How: 4 iron ingots, a piston, 2 stone pressure plates, redstone and a cauldron.
59. **The Compactor**: `alchemistry:compactor` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: Presses piles of elements back into usable dust: 16 iron atoms into an MI iron dust, 4 carbon into a graphite, 8 of many compounds into their dust.
   > How: 4 iron ingots, 2 pistons, 2 stone pressure plates and redstone.
   > Tip: Elements you dissolved out of junk become real metal again, so nothing is lost.
60. **The Breath of Fire**: 4x `chemlib:carbon_dioxide` *(after: Your First Synthesis)*
   > What: Build carbon dioxide in the Combiner from 1 carbon and 2 oxygen.
   > Chemistry: Every fire you've lit made this: C + O₂ → CO₂. It's also what you breathe out, and what plants turn back into cellulose with sunlight.
   > How: Pick carbon dioxide in the Combiner's GUI and supply the elements.
61. **The Simplest Fuel**: 4x `chemlib:methane` *(after: Your First Synthesis)*
   > What: Build methane, the main part of natural gas, from 1 carbon and 4 hydrogen.
   > Chemistry: Carbon makes four bonds, so the smallest hydrocarbon is one carbon with four hydrogens arranged as a tetrahedron. Every fuel in the oil age is a longer chain of the same idea.
   > How: Pick methane in the Combiner's GUI and supply the elements.
62. **Sand, Undone**: 16x `chemlib:silicon_dioxide` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: Dissolve sand: each block gives 4 silicon dioxide, and once in a while a speck of gold.
   > Chemistry: Silica is the most common compound in Earth's crust. Glass is silica, quartz is silica, and in Chapter V carbon will strip its oxygen away to give you silicon for circuits.
   > Tip: Placer gold is real: rivers concentrate heavy gold grains in their sand, which is why prospectors panned for it.

### III. Divine Ascent

*Walk through fire, brew in the dark, and take back the sky. Flight needs the Nether and your first Alchemistry machine: fire and chemistry together.*

1. **A Door of Fire**: 10x `minecraft:obsidian`; `minecraft:flint_and_steel` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > You remember the sky. Not looking up at it: standing in it.
   > What: a Nether portal is a 4x5 frame of obsidian (corners optional), lit with flint and steel.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass. Lava cooled so fast its atoms never had time to form crystals.
   > How: mine obsidian with a diamond pickaxe (or a steel paxel, which is diamond tier), or pour water over still lava to make it in place.
   > Tip: a bucket of water and a bucket of lava let you cast the frame block by block.
2. **Into the Fire**: visit `minecraft:the_nether` *(after: A Door of Fire)*
   > What: the Nether is a chemistry lab: quartz (SiO₂), blaze powder, glowstone and nether wart all come from here.
   > How: bring food, armour, blocks and a way home. NetherPortalFix keeps portals linked properly.
   > Tip: water evaporates instantly here and beds explode. Bring a respawn plan, not a bed.
3. **Fortress Found**: 32x `minecraft:nether_brick` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: Nether Fortresses hold blazes, wither skeletons and nether wart.
   > How: Explorer's Compass points to structures. Mine nether bricks from the fortress walls.
   > Tip: build a small portal near the fortress and your next trip is much shorter.
4. **A Bastion of Gold**: find structure `minecraft:bastion_remnant` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: Bastion remnants are huge blackstone ruins full of piglins and gold. Stand inside one.
   > How: Explorer's Compass finds them. Wear at least one piece of gold armour so the piglins stay calm, and never open their chests in front of them.
   > Tip: the walls are polished blackstone already: a free start on the pylon's frame.
5. **The Basalt Deltas**: find biome `minecraft:basalt_deltas` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Nether's volcanic badlands: basalt columns, blackstone, magma cubes and falling ash.
   > Chemistry: basalt is the most common rock on Earth's ocean floors: lava rich in iron and magnesium that cooled slowly enough to form small crystals, unlike obsidian.
   > Tip: magma cubes here drop magma cream for Fire Resistance and the Dissolver's magma blocks.
6. **Nether Gold**: 36x `minecraft:gold_nugget` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: nether gold ore drops gold nuggets: four ingots' worth fills this quest.
   > Chemistry: gold is so unreactive that it occurs as the native metal, not as a compound. That's why it was the first metal people ever found.
   > How: mine the yellow-flecked netherrack with any pickaxe. Fortune helps.
7. **Ghast Tears**: 2x `minecraft:ghast_tear` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: ghast tears brew Regeneration and drop rarely, since the ghast must die over solid ground.
   > How: reflect a fireball back with a punch or arrow, then catch the tear before it burns in lava.
   > Tip: a bow and patience beat chasing ghasts across lava lakes.
8. **Ancient Debris**: 2x `minecraft:ancient_debris` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: ancient debris smelts into netherite scrap, the base of netherite gear.
   > How: it hides deep in the Nether (around Y 8-22) and resists explosions, so bed or TNT mining works.
   > Tip: try the Dissolver on a scrap later and see what this 'element' really is.
9. **Netherite**: checkmark *(after: Ancient Debris)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Netherite Ingot" on the Armour and Harvest Tiers page. Click to dismiss.
10. **A Grim Trophy**: `minecraft:wither_skeleton_skull` *(after: Fortress Found)*
   > What: wither skeletons drop their skull only now and then. Three of them summon the Wither, much later.
   > How: fight wither skeletons in fortress corridors with a Looting sword. Their hits cause Wither, so bring milk or a stack of food.
   > Tip: no rush: nothing in this chapter needs it. Put it on a shelf and admire it.
11. **Nether Quartz**: 16x `minecraft:quartz` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: Nether quartz ore is everywhere in Nether netherrack. The Infusion Pylon is capped with quartz.
   > Chemistry: quartz is silicon dioxide, SiO₂. Much later you'll reduce it with carbon to get pure silicon for circuits.
   > Tip: keep a spare stack. Quartz dust plus coke becomes silicon in Chapter V.
12. **Blackstone**: 16x `minecraft:blackstone` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Infusion Pylon stands on polished blackstone.
   > Chemistry: blackstone is a basalt-like volcanic rock, rich in dark iron and magnesium minerals.
   > How: it fills basalt deltas and bastion remnants. Any pickaxe mines it.
13. **Glowstone**: 16x `minecraft:glowstone_dust` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: glowstone clusters hang from the Nether's ceilings. The dust strengthens potions (Level II) at the cost of duration.
   > How: break glowstone blocks (they drop 2 to 4 dust) or kill witches. A Silk Touch tool gives the whole block.
   > Tip: a strengthened potion can't also be extended with redstone, so keep glowstone away from the potions you want to last.
14. **The Light-Bearer**: 16x `chemlib:phosphorus` *(after: Glowstone, The Dissolver)*
   > What: every glowstone dust dissolves into 4 phosphorus.
   > Chemistry: phosphorus means 'light-bearer' in Greek. White phosphorus glows in the dark as it slowly reacts with the oxygen in air. Hennig Brand found it in 1669 by boiling down urine.
   > How: put glowstone dust in the Dissolver.
15. **Quartz, Undone**: 16x `chemlib:barium` *(after: Nether Quartz, The Dissolver)*
   > What: Nether quartz dissolves into 32 silicon dioxide and 16 barium.
   > Chemistry: pure quartz is only SiO₂, but real quartz veins often carry barite (barium sulfate, BaSO₄). Barium salts burn green, which is how fireworks get that colour.
   > How: put Nether quartz in the Dissolver.
16. **Blaze Powder, Undone**: 8x `chemlib:germanium` *(after: Blaze Powder, The Dissolver)*
   > What: Alchemistry reads blaze powder as 8 germanium, 2 graphite and 8 sulfur.
   > Chemistry: germanium (Ge, 32) is a semiconductor. The first transistor, built at Bell Labs in 1947, was a sliver of germanium.
   > Tip: the sulfur is handy: Chapter IV's battery acid needs sulfur too.
17. **Soul Sand**: 16x `minecraft:soul_sand` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: nether wart only grows on soul sand. Bring some home and plant a wart farm.
   > How: soul sand valleys are full of it, and fortress stairwells have small patches. A shovel digs it fast.
   > Tip: soul sand under water makes a bubble column that pushes you up.
18. **Blaze Rods**: 4x `minecraft:blaze_rod` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: blaze rods craft the brewing stand, and blaze powder fuels it.
   > How: blazes spawn around spawners in Nether Fortresses. Explorer's Compass can point you to one.
   > Tip: snowballs hurt blazes, and fire resistance makes the fight easy.
19. **Blaze Powder**: 8x `minecraft:blaze_powder` *(after: Blaze Rods)*
   > What: blaze powder fuels the brewing stand: one powder lasts 20 brews.
   > How: 1 blaze rod makes 2 powder by hand. The Steam Macerator gets 4 per rod.
   > Tip: keep one rod back for the stand itself.
20. **Nether Wart**: 8x `minecraft:nether_wart` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the base reagent for almost every potion.
   > How: it grows on soul sand in fortress stairwells. Bring some soul sand home and replant it; it grows in the Overworld too.
   > Tip: one stack of wart grown at home covers every brew in this chapter.
21. **The Brewer's Art**: `minecraft:brewing_stand` *(after: Blaze Powder, Nether Wart)*
   > Tinctures and draughts: the first chemistry was done by people trying to bottle a little divinity. You can relate.
   > What: a brewing stand turns water bottles into potions, one ingredient at a time.
   > Chemistry: brewing is extraction and reaction: each ingredient changes what's dissolved in the bottle.
   > How: 1 blaze rod + 3 cobblestone. Blaze powder in the top-left slot fuels 20 brews.
   > Tip: look up Potion of Flying in JEI (from Apothic Attributes). The next quests walk the whole chain.
22. **Glass Bottles**: 6x `minecraft:glass_bottle` *(after: The Brewer's Art)*
   > What: every potion lives in a bottle. The stand brews three at a time.
   > How: 3 glass in a V shape make 3 bottles. The Steam Compressor presses 1 glass block into 2.
   > Tip: make plenty: the flight chain takes several rounds of three.
23. **Bottled Water**: 3x `minecraft:potion` *(after: Glass Bottles)*
   > What: fill three bottles from any water source. Then brew nether wart into them to get Awkward Potions, the base of almost every recipe.
   > Chemistry: water is the universal solvent: its polar molecules pull apart salts and sugars, so whatever you add to the bottle ends up dissolved in it.
   > How: right-click water with empty bottles. Any potion counts for this quest.
24. **Fire Resistance**: 4x `minecraft:magma_cream` *(after: The Brewer's Art)*
   > What: Fire Resistance makes lava and blaze fire harmless. Swimming in lava becomes a shortcut.
   > How: magma cubes drop magma cream in basalt deltas, or craft it from blaze powder + slimeball. Brew it into an Awkward Potion.
   > Tip: add redstone for an 8-minute version before any lava-heavy trip.
25. **Slow Falling**: 2x `minecraft:phantom_membrane` *(after: Bottled Water)*
   > What: step 1 toward flight. Awkward Potion + phantom membrane = Potion of Slow Falling.
   > How: phantoms appear at night when someone in the world hasn't slept for three or more days. Fight them on a roof.
   > Tip: one membrane brews three bottles, so two membranes go a long way.
26. **Fermenting Supplies**: 2x `minecraft:spider_eye`; 2x `minecraft:sugar`; 2x `minecraft:brown_mushroom` *(after: The Brewer's Art)*
   > What: the three ingredients of a fermented spider eye, the reagent that turns an effect into its opposite.
   > Chemistry: fermentation needs a sugar to feed on and a living culture to do the work. Here the mushroom plays the yeast and the sugar is its food.
   > How: spiders and cave spiders drop eyes, sugar comes from sugar cane, and brown mushrooms grow in dark places.
27. **Levitation**: `minecraft:fermented_spider_eye` *(after: Slow Falling, Fermenting Supplies)*
   > What: step 2. Slow Falling + fermented spider eye = Potion of Levitation (Apothic Attributes).
   > Chemistry: fermentation is yeast turning sugar into alcohol and acids. Here it 'corrupts' the effect into its opposite.
   > How: fermented spider eye = spider eye + sugar + brown mushroom (shapeless). The Steam Mixer can make them too.
28. **Lifting Gas**: 2x `chemlib:hydrogen` *(after: Levitation, Lighter than Air)*
   > What: step 3. In this pack, Flying is made with hydrogen instead of End chorus fruit, so you can fly before the End.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen (H₂) is the lightest gas there is, about 14 times lighter than air. It lifted the first passenger balloons in 1783.
   > How: in a crafting grid, 1 Potion of Levitation + 2 hydrogen make a Potion of Flying: 8 minutes of creative-style flight (check JEI).
   > Tip: don't drink it yet; the next step makes it last longer. The brewing-stand route (popped chorus fruit) also works once you reach the End.
29. **Extended Flight**: 8x `minecraft:redstone` *(after: Lifting Gas)*
   > What: redstone stretches a potion's duration. Flying + redstone = Long Flying (15 min). Add redstone again for Extra Long Flying (30 min).
   > How: brew redstone into your Flying potions, then into the Long ones.
   > Tip: a Potion Filter needs a full hour, which is just two Extra Long potions. Brew at least two.
30. **Lighter than Air**: 8x `chemlib:hydrogen` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: your flight potion and the pylon itself need hydrogen, and only the Dissolver can pull it out of matter as an item.
   > Chemistry: H is element 1: one proton, one electron. It makes up about three quarters of the ordinary matter in the universe.
   > How: dissolve logs (cellulose) or sugar (sucrose), or let the Atomizer turn piped water into ChemLib water and dissolve that: 2 hydrogen each.
   > Tip: feed the Dissolver from a hopper and it runs while you're in the Nether.
31. **A Block of Emerald**: `minecraft:emerald_block` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: the Infusion Pylon is built around a block of emerald, and the Potion Filter needs one more emerald.
   > Chemistry: emerald is the mineral beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, coloured green by a trace of chromium. Without the chromium the same crystal is colourless.
   > How: emerald ore hides in mountain biomes. Trading with villagers is the steadier way: most professions pay emeralds for simple goods.
   > Tip: a farmer villager buys wheat, potatoes and carrots. Your field from the first day pays for this.
32. **Coloured Clay**: 2x `minecraft:cyan_terracotta`; `minecraft:green_dye` *(after: Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: the Potion Filter is framed in cyan terracotta with a green dye at its centre.
   > Chemistry: smelt cactus and its green pigment survives as dye. Mix it with lapis blue for cyan. Alchemistry agrees: 4 copper chloride compact into cyan dye, the colour of copper salts.
   > How: smelt clay blocks into terracotta, then 8 terracotta around 1 cyan dye make 8 cyan terracotta.
33. **Potion Filter**: `pylons:potion_filter` *(after: Extended Flight, A Block of Emerald, Coloured Clay)*
   > An hour of flight, folded into a pane of glass. Close enough to a feather from your old wings.
   > What: a Potion Filter holds a potion effect for the Infusion Pylon.
   > How: 2 cyan terracotta, green dye, an emerald and 5 glass. Drink a potion, then right-click the filter to store the effect. It activates once it holds 1 hour of Flying: two Extra Long (30 min each), four Long (15 min) or about eight regular potions.
   > Tip: drink and load one potion at a time so none of the effect runs out first. Two filters with the same effect combine: hold one in each hand and right-click.
34. **Quartz Slabs**: 2x `minecraft:quartz_slab` *(after: Nether Quartz)*
   > What: the pylon is topped with two quartz slabs.
   > How: 4 Nether quartz make a block of quartz; 3 blocks in a row make 6 slabs.
35. **The Pylon's Frame**: 3x `minecraft:polished_blackstone`; 2x `minecraft:iron_bars` *(after: Blackstone)*
   > What: the pylon stands on 3 polished blackstone with 2 iron bars at its sides.
   > How: 4 blackstone in a 2x2 make 4 polished blackstone. 6 iron ingots make 16 iron bars.
36. **Wings of a God**: `pylons:infusion_pylon` *(after: Potion Filter, Quartz Slabs, The Pylon's Frame)*
   > Your second gift returns, and the sky is yours again. You had forgotten how small the world looks from here.
   > What: the Infusion Pylon applies a filter's effect to you anywhere. With a Flying filter, that's creative-style flight.
   > How: 2 quartz slabs, 2 iron bars, a block of emerald, 3 polished blackstone and 1 hydrogen from your Dissolver (see JEI). Place it and put the full (one-hour) filter inside.
   > Tip: the pylon only works while its chunk is loaded. Force-load it (see the next quest).
37. **Keep It Running**: checkmark *(after: Wings of a God)*
   > What: if the pylon's chunk unloads, your flight stops. Over a long trip that means a long fall.
   > How: open the FTB Chunks map (press M), claim the chunk with the pylon, then right-click it again to force-load it.
   > Tip: force-load your Dissolver and brewing setup too, so they keep working while you travel.
38. **Eyes of Ender**: 4x `minecraft:ender_pearl`; 2x `minecraft:ender_eye` *(after: Blaze Powder)*
   > What: An Eye of Ender, thrown, flies towards the nearest stronghold, and twelve of them open the way to the End.
   > How: Endermen drop ender pearls; they spawn in every dimension but crowd the Nether's warped forests. Craft 1 pearl with 1 blaze powder (shapeless) for an eye.
   > Tip: No rush. Flight here runs on hydrogen, so the End can wait until you want its chorus fruit.
39. **Whispers of Magic**: `ars_nouveau:worn_notebook`; 4x `ars_nouveau:source_gem` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Worn Notebook teaches Ars Nouveau spellcrafting. Source gems are its basic magical material.
   > How: the notebook is a book + lapis lazuli (shapeless). Source gems come from the Imbuement Chamber (lapis or amethyst + Source).
