   > Tip: its Ritual of Flight is a second way to fly near your base. See the Ars Nouveau page (Magic and Relics).
40. **Fire into Source**: checkmark *(after: Whispers of Magic)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Volcanic Sourcelink" on the Ars Nouveau page. Click to dismiss.
41. **Archwood**: 8x any of `item_tag(c:logs/archwood)` *(after: Whispers of Magic)*
   > What: archwood is Ars Nouveau's magic wood, used for its jars, tables and rituals.
   > How: look for brightly coloured trees in archwood forests; any colour of archwood log counts.
   > Tip: archwood saplings grow at home, so a few logs become a farm.

### IV. The Electric Age

*Electricity is the tool that splits compounds apart. First you have to make it, and build the circuits that use it.*

1. **Oil from Coal**: `modern_industrialization:raw_synthetic_oil_bucket` *(after: Steel)*
   > Lightning used to come when you called it. Now you'll have to build it a road, and the road starts in a coal pit.
   > What: Raw synthetic oil is the first step to rubber, and rubber is what keeps electricity in its wires.
   > Chemistry: Hot carbon and steam react into syngas, C + H₂O → CO + H₂, and the Fischer-Tropsch process builds that up into longer hydrocarbon chains. Coal-to-oil really was done this way.
   > How: In the Steam Mixer, 1 coke dust and 100 mB of water make 200 mB of raw synthetic oil. Fill a bucket from the mixer's output.
   > Tip: Grind coke in the Steam Macerator for the dust. One coke dust is a fifth of a bucket of oil.
2. **Synthetic Oil**: `modern_industrialization:synthetic_oil_bucket` *(after: Oil from Coal)*
   > What: Raw oil is a messy mixture. Heat refines it into synthetic oil, the input for rubber.
   > Chemistry: Heating a crude hydrocarbon mix breaks up the unstable pieces and drives off the light ones, leaving a cleaner, more uniform oil.
   > How: Pipe raw synthetic oil into a fluid input hatch on your Steam Blast Furnace: 100 mB in, 100 mB out. It needs a fluid output hatch too.
   > Tip: A tank between mixer and furnace keeps both busy.
3. **Paper**: 16x `minecraft:paper` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Rubber sheets are cast on paper, and resistors are wrapped in it.
   > Chemistry: Paper is a mat of cellulose fibres held together by hydrogen bonds between the chains. Wet it and the water breaks those bonds, which is why wet paper tears.
   > How: 3 sugar cane make 3 paper.
   > Tip: A sugar cane farm next to water keeps this coming. Every rubber sheet batch eats one paper.
4. **Rubber**: 8x `modern_industrialization:rubber_sheet` *(after: Synthetic Oil, Paper)*
   > A wire is only useful if the current stays inside it. You used to just tell lightning where to go.
   > What: rubber sheets insulate cables and form circuit boards. Here rubber is synthetic, made from coal, not tree sap.
   > Chemistry: rubber is a polymer: long, tangled hydrocarbon chains. Cross-linked with sulfur (vulcanisation), the chains become a tough, flexible insulator.
   > How: Mixer: 100 mB synthetic oil + 1 paper → 2 rubber sheets. Or vulcanise 1000 mB of oil with sulfur dust into synthetic rubber fluid first: then 1 paper and 100 mB give 12 sheets.
   > Tip: the sulfur route gives six times more sheets per oil, but it needs a steel or electric mixer (4 EU/t).
5. **Casings for the LV Line**: 4x `modern_industrialization:steel_machine_casing` *(after: Steel Machine Casing)*
   > What: the Steel Wiremill takes one casing and every LV machine hull takes another. Build a few ahead.
   > How: 8 steel plates around a steel gear, the same shape as the bronze one.
   > Tip: the Assembler later makes them for you. Until then, keep the blast furnace running.
6. **Steel Wiremill**: `modern_industrialization:steel_wiremill` *(after: Casings for the LV Line, Bronze Rotors)*
   > What: Copper wire can't be crafted by hand. The Wiremill draws plates into wire, and wire into fine wire.
   > Chemistry: Metals are ductile: their atoms slide past each other without the bonds breaking, so a plate can be pulled through a die into a thin wire.
   > How: A steel machine casing, 4 bronze gears, 2 bronze rotors and 2 fluid pipes. It runs on steam like your other machines.
   > Tip: 1 copper plate makes 2 wire. Keep it fed from your Steam Compressor.
7. **Tin Wire**: 8x `modern_industrialization:tin_wire` *(after: Steel Wiremill)*
   > What: Tin cable, the wire that carries LV power, has tin wire at its core. The Polarizer needs bare tin wire too.
   > Chemistry: tin conducts about a seventh as well as copper. That's plenty for low voltage, and tin was cheap and resisted corrosion.
   > How: Press tin ingots into plates, then draw each plate into 2 tin wire in the Wiremill.
8. **Wires and Cables**: 8x `modern_industrialization:copper_wire`; 8x `modern_industrialization:tin_cable` *(after: Tin Wire, Rubber)*
   > What: copper wire goes into every component. Tin cable carries LV power between machines.
   > Chemistry: copper's single outer electron moves freely between atoms, which is why it conducts so well.
   > How: the Wiremill pulls copper plates into wire. 3 tin wire between 6 rubber sheets make 3 tin cable.
   > Tip: tin cable is rated for LV (32 EU/t). Higher tiers need better cable.
9. **Fine Copper Wire**: 8x `modern_industrialization:copper_fine_wire` *(after: Wires and Cables)*
   > What: Thinner wire for small components. Resistors need it first.
   > Chemistry: A thinner wire has more resistance: current has less metal to flow through. Useful when you want to limit current, not carry it.
   > How: Put copper wire back into the Wiremill: 1 wire makes 4 fine wire.
10. **Analog Circuit Board**: 2x `modern_industrialization:analog_circuit_board` *(after: Rubber)*
   > What: the base every analog circuit is soldered onto.
   > How: rubber sheet, copper plate, rubber sheet stacked in a column.
   > Tip: once you have an Assembler, it makes these automatically.
11. **Coal Dust**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coal_dust` *(after: Fine Copper Wire)*
   > What: the resistive filling of a carbon resistor.
   > How: the Steam Macerator grinds 1 coal into 1 coal dust. Coal, not charcoal: the recipe wants coal dust specifically.
   > Tip: one coal dust makes three resistors by hand, twelve in the Assembler.
12. **Resistor**: 3x `modern_industrialization:resistor` *(after: Coal Dust)*
   > What: resistors limit current so the rest of the circuit doesn't burn out.
   > Chemistry: carbon conducts, but poorly. A pinch of coal dust between fine copper wires makes a carbon resistor.
   > How: 2 paper, 2 copper fine wire and 1 coal dust. One craft gives three.
13. **Gold Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:gold_plate` *(after: Wires and Cables)*
   > What: every capacitor holds two gold plates.
   > Chemistry: gold doesn't oxidise, so its surface stays clean and conductive forever. Real electronics plate their contacts with a thin layer of it.
   > How: the Steam Compressor presses 1 gold ingot into 1 plate.
   > Tip: the Nether's gold ore and piglin trades are an easy source.
14. **Capacitor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:capacitor` *(after: Gold Plates)*
   > What: capacitors store a small charge and smooth out the current.
   > Chemistry: two conductors (gold plates) separated by an insulator (rubber): charge builds up on each side.
   > How: 2 gold plates, 2 copper wire and a rubber sheet.
15. **Inductor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:inductor` *(after: Wires and Cables)*
   > What: inductors resist sudden changes in current. The Polarizer also needs them.
   > Chemistry: current through a coil makes a magnetic field; changing the current fights that field.
   > How: 8 copper wire wound around a steel rod.
16. **Analog Circuit**: 2x `modern_industrialization:analog_circuit` *(after: Analog Circuit Board, Capacitor, Resistor, Inductor)*
   > What: the LV circuit. Mekanism's Basic Control Circuit also needs one, so MI and Mekanism advance together.
   > How: 2 resistors, 1 inductor, 2 capacitors, the board, and 3 copper wire (see JEI for the layout).
   > Tip: make four or five now. The hull, turbine and each machine all eat them.
17. **The Spectrometer**: `warbuckscore:spectrometer` *(after: Analog Circuit)*
   > Once you could see the colours inside things, the light every element gives off. This is a fair copy.
   > What: a hand-held scanner (Warbucks Core, made for this pack). Right-click to read the ore signal in the loaded chunks around you.
   > Chemistry: heated atoms give off light only at certain wavelengths, an emission spectrum unique to each element. That's how helium was found in the Sun before anyone found it on Earth.
   > How: amethyst prism, steel plates, copper wire and an analog circuit (check JEI). It lists each element with its strength, direction, distance and depth.
   > Tip: a "strong" signal is usually a rich deposit. Walk towards it and scan again.
18. **Redstone Control Module**: `modern_industrialization:redstone_control_module` *(after: Analog Circuit)*
   > What: slot it into an electric machine or multiblock and a redstone signal decides when it runs.
   > How: redstone, a redstone torch, a capacitor, 2 resistors, 2 inductors and an analog circuit board (check JEI). Configure it in your hand first.
   > Tip: wire it to a comparator on a tank and a machine stops before its output overflows.
19. **Lead**: 8x `modern_industrialization:lead_ingot` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: lead is most of the battery alloy in every redstone battery.
   > Chemistry: most lead comes from galena, lead sulfide (PbS). Roasting drives the sulfur off as SO₂ and carbon reduces the oxide that's left: PbO + C → Pb + CO.
   > How: MI lead ore is common, and rich deposits sit around Y -24 to 16. Smelt the raw lead.
20. **A Rich Lead Deposit**: 64x `modern_industrialization:raw_lead` *(after: Lead)*
   > What: rich ore deposits hold hundreds of ores in one chunk, at a metal-specific depth. Lead's sits around Y -24 to 16.
   > How: strip-mine at that depth and check ore with Jade. FTB Ultimine clears a vein in one go.
   > Tip: galena (lead sulfide, PbS) is the world's main lead ore, and it often carries silver.
21. **Antimony**: 4x `modern_industrialization:antimony_ingot` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: a brittle, silvery metalloid. A little of it makes soft lead stiff enough to hold its shape in a battery.
   > Chemistry: antimony's main ore is stibnite, Sb₂S₃. Ancient Egyptians ground it into kohl, the black eyeliner.
   > How: MI antimony ore sits around Y -24 to 16 in rich deposits. Smelt the raw antimony.
22. **Battery Alloy Dust**: 4x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_dust` *(after: Lead, Antimony)*
   > What: the mixed powder of lead and antimony.
   > How: grind the ingots in the macerator, then mix 1 lead dust and 1 antimony dust into 2 battery alloy dust in the Steam Mixer.
23. **Battery Alloy**: 4x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_ingot` *(after: Battery Alloy Dust)*
   > What: battery alloy makes the casing and grids of redstone batteries.
   > Chemistry: lead hardened with antimony is the grid metal of real lead-acid batteries. Pure lead is too soft.
   > How: smelt battery alloy dust in any furnace.
24. **Battery Plates**: 2x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_plate`; 8x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_curved_plate` *(after: Battery Alloy)*
   > What: each redstone battery is a flat battery alloy plate on top of four curved ones.
   > Chemistry: in a real lead-acid cell the plates are grids, so the acid can reach as much lead surface as possible. More surface, more current.
   > How: the Steam Compressor presses ingots into plates and plates into curved plates, 1:1.
25. **Sulfur from Gunpowder**: 8x `chemlib:sulfur` *(after: The Dissolver)*
   > What: the S in H₂SO₄. Battery acid needs it, and the Dissolver can pull it out of gunpowder.
   > Chemistry: gunpowder is saltpetre (KNO₃), sulfur and charcoal. One gunpowder dissolves into 2 potassium nitrate, 8 sulfur and 2 graphite.
   > How: creepers drop gunpowder. Blaze powder dissolves into 8 sulfur too.
26. **Battery Acid**: 2x `chemlib:sulfuric_acid` *(after: The Combiner, Sulfur from Gunpowder)*
   > What: the redstone battery is a real lead-acid battery, and its electrolyte is sulfuric acid. The Combiner from Chapter II makes it from elements.
   > Chemistry: H₂SO₄ is the most-produced chemical in the world. In a car battery it reacts with the lead plates (Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O) and releases electrons; charging runs the reaction backwards.
   > How: pick sulfuric acid in the Combiner and supply 2 hydrogen, 1 sulfur and 4 oxygen. Water or cellulose give the hydrogen and oxygen.
   > Tip: every LV hull needs two batteries, so keep a stack of acid ready.
27. **Redstone Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:redstone_battery` *(after: Battery Plates, Wires and Cables, Battery Acid)*
   > What: a rechargeable lead-acid battery. Every LV hull holds two.
   > Chemistry: lead-antimony grids, sulfuric acid electrolyte: the same chemistry as the battery under a car's bonnet.
   > How: 1 battery alloy plate, 4 curved plates, 2 tin cable, 1 redstone and 1 sulfuric acid from the Combiner.
   > Tip: the LV Storage Unit is built from six of these, so make spares.
28. **LV Storage Unit**: checkmark *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > Moved: this step is now "EU Storage" on the Power page. Click to dismiss.
29. **LV Machine Hull**: `modern_industrialization:basic_machine_hull` *(after: Analog Circuit, Redstone Battery)*
   > Your hands remember wiring this. Your mind is still catching up.
   > What: LV (Low Voltage) is the first electric tier. Every LV machine is built on this hull.
   > How: steel machine casing + analog circuit + 2 redstone batteries + 3 tin cable.
30. **Magnetic Steel Rod**: 2x `modern_industrialization:steel_rod_magnetic` *(after: Steel Rods, Bolts and Rings)*
   > What: the core of an electric motor.
   > Chemistry: iron-based alloys hold magnetism because their electron spins line up in domains.
   > How: a steel rod ringed by 6 redstone. Later the Polarizer magnetises rods with electricity.
31. **Electric Motor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:motor` *(after: Magnetic Steel Rod, Wires and Cables)*
   > What: motors drive turbines, pistons, conveyors and robot arms. Nearly every LV machine needs one.
   > Chemistry: current in a coil next to a magnet creates a force; that's the motor effect. Run it backwards and it's a generator.
   > How: a magnetic steel rod, 2 steel rods, 4 copper wire and 2 tin cable.
32. **Tin Blades, Rings and Bolts**: 8x `modern_industrialization:tin_blade`; 2x `modern_industrialization:tin_ring`; 8x `modern_industrialization:tin_bolt` *(after: Tin Wire)*
   > What: electric machines push fluids with tin rotors, not copper ones.
   > How: the same parts as before: 2 tin curved plates on a tin rod make 4 blades; the Forge Hammer and Cutting Machine make rods, bolts and rings.
   > Tip: the turbine and the mixer need 2 rotors each and a pump 3. Every rotor is 4 blades.
33. **Tin Rotors**: 4x `modern_industrialization:tin_rotor` *(after: Tin Blades, Rings and Bolts)*
   > What: the spinning heart of the steam turbine, and the stirrer of the electric mixer.
   > How: 4 tin blades, a tin ring and 4 tin bolts.
34. **Steam to Electricity**: `modern_industrialization:lv_steam_turbine` *(after: LV Machine Hull, Electric Motor, Tin Rotors)*
   > What: a turbine turns your boiler's steam into EU, MI's electricity: 1 mB of steam is 1 EU, up to 32 EU/t.
   > How: an LV hull, an analog circuit, 2 tin rotors, 2 motors, 2 fluid pipes and tin cable. Pipe steam in and run tin cable from its output side to your machines.
   > Tip: one turbine at full speed eats the steam of two steel boilers. If machines stall, add boilers before adding turbines.
35. **LV Energy Input Hatch**: `modern_industrialization:lv_energy_input_hatch` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: electric multiblocks take power through energy hatches. The Electric Blast Furnace needs at least one.
   > How: a tin cable on top of an LV machine hull.
   > Tip: an LV hatch only connects to LV cables. Two hatches double the power a multiblock can draw.
36. **Pipe Config Card**: `modern_industrialization:config_card` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: saves an item or fluid pipe connection's settings and pastes them onto other connections.
   > How: sneak + use on a configured pipe connection to save; use on another connection to apply. Sneak + use on air clears it.
   > Tip: it can also camouflage pipes as any block. The card's tooltip explains how.
37. **Pump**: 2x `modern_industrialization:pump` *(after: Electric Motor, Tin Rotors)*
   > What: MI's pump component: the Electric Water Pump and the Diesel Generator are built around it.
   > How: 3 fluid pipes, a motor, 3 tin rotors and 2 tin bolts (check JEI).
38. **Electric Water Pump**: `modern_industrialization:electric_water_pump` *(after: Steam to Electricity, Pump)*
   > What: pumps water from nothing but power, for boilers and (soon) electrolysis.
   > How: an LV hull with 2 pumps, a tin rotor, fluid pipes, tin cable and an analog circuit.
   > Tip: next chapter, water becomes hydrogen and oxygen. You'll want lots of it.
39. **Burning Creosote**: `modern_industrialization:lv_diesel_generator` *(after: Pump, Byproduct: Creosote)*
   > What: the Diesel Generator burns liquid fuels into EU. Right now that means creosote from the Coke Oven, a waste product turned into power.
   > Chemistry: creosote is a mix of aromatic hydrocarbons and phenols. Burning them releases the energy in their C-H and C-C bonds as heat, just like coal, but it flows through a pipe.
   > How: an LV hull, 2 pumps, 2 tin gears, an analog circuit and 3 tin cable. Check JEI for every fuel it accepts.
   > Tip: later fuels from the distillation tower burn far longer per bucket.
40. **Piston**: 2x `modern_industrialization:piston` *(after: Electric Motor)*
   > What: MI's piston component, used in the macerator, compressor and robot arm.
   > How: 3 steel plates, 2 steel rods, a steel gear, 2 tin cable and a motor.
   > Tip: the Electric Macerator needs 2 pistons and the Electric Compressor 4, so make plenty.
41. **Conveyor**: 2x `modern_industrialization:conveyor` *(after: Electric Motor)*
   > What: conveyors move items inside machines. The Assembler, Packer and Cutting Machine need them.
   > How: 6 rubber sheets, 2 motors and a tin cable.
   > Tip: motors are the bottleneck here. Keep a few spare.
42. **Robot Arm**: 2x `modern_industrialization:robot_arm` *(after: Piston)*
   > What: robot arms move parts inside the Assembler and Packer.
   > How: two motors, a piston, steel rods, tin cable and an analog circuit.
   > Tip: the Assembler takes four and the Packer two.
43. **Electric Compressor**: `modern_industrialization:electric_compressor` *(after: Steam to Electricity, Piston)*
   > What: plates, curved plates and rings for every part you'll build next.
   > How: LV hull, four pistons, two analog circuits and two tin cable.
   > Tip: it doubles as a second plate source while the steam compressor keeps running.
44. **Electric Wiremill**: `modern_industrialization:electric_wiremill` *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: copper wire and fine wire in bulk. Circuits and coils use a lot of it.
   > How: LV hull, 4 motors, 2 analog circuits and 2 tin cable.
   > Tip: feed it from your compressor's plate output.
45. **Polarizer**: `modern_industrialization:polarizer` *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: magnetic steel rods for motors, and magnetic cupronickel wire for heating coils.
   > Chemistry: a strong field lines up the magnetic domains in the metal, and they stay lined up.
   > How: LV hull, 2 inductors, 4 tin wire and 2 tin cable.
46. **Electric Mixer**: `modern_industrialization:electric_mixer` *(after: Steam to Electricity)*
   > What: mixing dusts into alloys (bronze, invar, cupronickel, battery alloy) and fluids into mixtures, faster than steam and up to 32 EU/t.
   > How: LV hull, a motor, 2 tin rotors, 2 glass, a fluid pipe and 2 analog circuits.
   > Tip: recipes that need more than 4 EU/t, like vulcanised synthetic rubber, run here and not in the steam mixer.
47. **Electric Macerator**: `modern_industrialization:electric_macerator` *(after: Piston, Steam to Electricity, Invar Rotary Blade)*
   > What: ore to crushed dust, ingots back to dust. Still capped at 2x per ore until acids.
   > How: an LV hull, an invar rotary blade, 2 pistons, 2 motors, 2 analog circuits and tin cable.
   > Tip: the hull quest reward included one. Build a second for throughput.
48. **Cutting Machine**: `modern_industrialization:electric_cutting_machine` *(after: Conveyor, Steam to Electricity, Invar Rotary Blade)*
   > What: cutting ingots into rods and bolts, and logs into more planks.
   > How: an LV hull, an invar rotary blade, 2 motors, a conveyor, 2 glass and 2 analog circuits. Its cuts use a little lubricant, the creosote + redstone mix from Chapter II.
   > Tip: logs give six planks here instead of four.
49. **Assembler**: `modern_industrialization:assembler` *(after: Robot Arm, Conveyor)*
   > What: circuits and machine parts, automatically, from a stocked input.
   > How: LV hull, four robot arms, two conveyors and two analog circuits.
   > Tip: automate hulls, circuits, motors, pistons, robot arms and conveyors first. With slot locking, one Assembler can hold up to three recipes.
50. **Packer**: `modern_industrialization:electric_packer` *(after: Robot Arm, Conveyor)*
   > What: compacting ingots into blocks and double ingots, and assembling a few parts. You'll want bauxite blocks next chapter.
   > How: 2 robot arms, 2 conveyors, 3 analog circuits and 2 tin cable on an LV hull.
   > Tip: unpacking is a separate machine, the Unpacker. Build one if you store metal as blocks.
51. **Configurable Chest**: `modern_industrialization:configurable_chest` *(after: Analog Circuit, Electric Motor)*
   > What: a chest with lockable slots and auto-eject: a buffer between machines that keeps exactly what you tell it to.
   > How: a steel machine casing, 2 motors, 2 hoppers and 4 analog circuits make 4 chests.
   > Tip: lock its slots to the parts of a recipe and it becomes a tidy input buffer for an Assembler.
52. **Steel Drills**: 4x `modern_industrialization:steel_drill` *(after: The Steam Quarry, Electric Motor, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: the steel tier of quarry drill. The Steam Quarry digs a different ore table with them (check JEI).
   > How: a steel drill head, 2 iron gears, 2 item pipes, 2 motors, a tin cable and an analog circuit make 4 drills.
53. **Cupronickel Dust**: 8x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_dust` *(after: Nickel)*
   > What: the mixed powder for MI's first heating wire.
   > How: in a mixer, 1 copper dust and 1 nickel dust make 2 cupronickel dust. The Steam Mixer can do it.
   > Tip: the furnace's coils alone take 64 cupronickel ingots. Find a nickel deposit (Y -32 to 8) before you start.
54. **Cupronickel Ingots and Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_ingot`; 8x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_plate` *(after: Cupronickel Dust)*
   > What: cupronickel is drawn into wire from plates, just like copper.
   > Chemistry: copper and nickel dissolve into each other in any ratio: a true solid solution, one crystal lattice with both atoms mixed at random.
   > How: smelt the dust into ingots, then press ingots into plates in a compressor.
55. **Cupronickel Wire**: 16x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_wire` *(after: Cupronickel Ingots and Plates, Steel Wiremill)*
   > What: bare cupronickel wire, the start of both coils and heating elements.
   > How: the Wiremill draws 1 cupronickel plate into 2 wire.
56. **Magnetic Cupronickel Wire**: 8x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_wire_magnetic` *(after: Cupronickel Wire, Polarizer)*
   > A wire that turns current into heat on command. Fire, tamed one more time.
   > What: the heating wire for the Electric Furnace (4) and the Electric Blast Furnace controller (7).
   > Chemistry: cupronickel (copper + nickel) resists current more than copper and survives heat. Coins and ship pipes use it too.
   > How: magnetise cupronickel wire in the Polarizer, 1:1.
57. **Electric Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:electric_furnace` *(after: Magnetic Cupronickel Wire)*
   > What: fast, fuel-free smelting.
   > Chemistry: current through a resistive wire turns into heat (Joule heating), the same idea as a toaster.
   > How: LV hull wrapped in 4 magnetic cupronickel wire, with 2 analog circuits and tin cable.
58. **Cupronickel Cable**: 24x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_cable` *(after: Cupronickel Wire, Rubber)*
   > What: coils are wound from insulated cupronickel cable. Cupronickel cable is also MV-rated if you ever need it for power.
   > How: 3 cupronickel wire between 6 rubber sheets make 3 cable. The Assembler does it with synthetic rubber fluid and no sheets.
   > Tip: 16 coils need 128 cable. This is where an Assembler and a rubber line pay off.
59. **Cupronickel Coils**: 16x `modern_industrialization:cupronickel_coil` *(after: Cupronickel Cable)*
   > What: the heating jacket of the Electric Blast Furnace: two hollow 3x3 rings of 8 coils each.
   > Chemistry: a coil packs a long wire into a small space, so a lot of resistive heating happens in one block. Kilns and toasters use the same trick.
   > How: 8 cupronickel cable in a ring make 1 coil.
   > Tip: cupronickel coils run EBF recipes up to 32 EU/t, which covers aluminium and silicon.
60. **A Stack of Invar Plates**: 32x `modern_industrialization:invar_plate` *(after: Invar)*
   > What: heatproof casings are 8 invar plates around an invar gear each. The furnace needs a dozen or more.
   > How: mix iron and nickel dust 2:1 into invar dust, smelt, and press the ingots into plates.
   > Tip: that's well over a hundred plates in all. Run the mixer, a furnace and the compressor in a line.
61. **Heatproof Machine Casings**: 12x `modern_industrialization:heatproof_machine_casing` *(after: A Stack of Invar Plates, Invar Plates and Gears)*
   > What: the Electric Blast Furnace's bottom and top layers are heatproof casings, with the controller and hatches set into them.
   > Chemistry: a furnace wall that expands as it heats cracks at the joints. Invar barely expands, so a casing made of it holds its shape at any temperature the coils reach.
   > How: 8 invar plates around an invar gear. You need up to 14: 18 blocks in the two layers, minus the controller and each hatch.
62. **Electric Blast Furnace**: `modern_industrialization:electric_blast_furnace` *(after: Magnetic Cupronickel Wire, Cupronickel Coils, Heatproof Machine Casings, LV Energy Input Hatch)*
   > Fire you can measure in volts. You used to do this without the volts.
   > What: MI's big furnace multiblock. With cupronickel coils it reaches the heat for aluminum and silicon.
   > How: the controller is an LV hull, 7 magnetic cupronickel wire and a blast furnace. Build a layer of heatproof casings (controller in it), two hollow rings of cupronickel coils, and another heatproof layer. Hatches go in the top or bottom layer: an LV energy input hatch and item hatches.
   > Tip: hold a hatch or wrench near the controller to see the valid positions highlighted. JEI shows the whole shape in 3D.
63. **Osmium**: 8x `mekanism:raw_osmium` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Mekanism builds almost everything from osmium: its infuser, casings and circuits.
   > Chemistry: real osmium is the densest natural element, 22.6 g/cm³. A litre of it weighs about as much as a big dog.
   > How: osmium ore is common in small veins underground. Mine it with an iron pickaxe or better.
64. **Osmium Ingots**: 8x `mekanism:ingot_osmium` *(after: Osmium)*
   > What: the Metallurgic Infuser, the Steel Casing and every Basic Control Circuit each take an osmium ingot.
   > Chemistry: osmium is named for its smell: the Greek osme. Powdered osmium slowly oxidises in air to OsO₄, a volatile and very toxic oxide with a sharp odour.
   > How: smelt raw osmium in any furnace.
65. **Osmium Hoard**: 32x `mekanism:ingot_osmium` *(after: Osmium Ingots)*
   > What: every Mekanism machine, casing and circuit costs osmium. A stockpile saves trips.
   > How: smelt or enrich raw osmium into ingots.
   > Tip: the Enrichment Chamber doubles osmium ore, so process it there once it's built.
66. **Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser**: `mekanism:metallurgic_infuser` *(after: Osmium Ingots)*
   > What: Mekanism's entry machine. It infuses metals with other materials.
   > How: 4 iron ingots, 2 redstone, an osmium ingot and 2 furnaces.
   > Tip: it runs on FE. Your Chapter II generator works, or a Mekanism Heat Generator (Power chapter).
67. **Infused Alloy**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_infused` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: Mekanism's basic alloy. The Enrichment Chamber and many basic machines need it.
   > Chemistry: a real alloy mixes metals at the atomic level. Here redstone plays the part of the second element.
   > How: put redstone in the infuser's left slot (it becomes an infusion buffer), then feed copper ingots.
68. **Mekanism Circuits**: 2x `mekanism:basic_control_circuit`; `mekanism:steel_casing` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: in this pack, a Basic Control Circuit is MI Analog Circuit + osmium ingot (shapeless). Each Mekanism circuit tier needs the matching MI circuit.
   > How: the Steel Casing (4 steel, 4 glass and an osmium ingot) is the frame for most Mekanism machines.
   > Tip: make several casings at once. Every Mekanism machine in the next chapter needs one.
69. **Enrichment Chamber**: `mekanism:enrichment_chamber` *(after: Mekanism Circuits, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: ore → 2 dust. It also turns dirty dust into clean dust in the higher-tier lines.
   > How: steel casing, 4 infused alloy, 2 iron and 2 basic control circuits.
   > Tip: 3x, 4x and 5x need gases and acids: that's the next chapter.
70. **Crusher**: `mekanism:crusher` *(after: Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: crushes ingots to dust and, later, ore clumps into dirty dust in the 3x+ lines.
   > How: steel casing, 2 basic control circuits, 4 redstone and 2 lava buckets.
   > Tip: it also turns ingots back into dust, handy for alloy recipes.

### V. Electrochemistry and Acids

*Electricity splits compounds into elements. Acids dissolve what fire can't. Ore processing becomes chemistry.*

1. **Mekanism Gases**: `mekanism:electrolytic_separator` *(after: The Electrolytic Core)*
   > Once a word was enough to pull water apart. Now it takes a machine and a cable, and that will have to do.
   > What: the Electrolytic Separator makes hydrogen and oxygen as gases you can pipe and store.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. Current drives the reaction backwards from burning hydrogen.
   > How: feed it water and FE. Gases leave from the coloured sides (configure them with the Configurator).
2. **Pressurized Tubes**: 16x `mekanism:basic_pressurized_tube` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: gases need sealed tubes. Item pipes and fluid pipes won't carry them.
   > How: craft basic pressurized tubes (see JEI) and run them from the separator's outputs.
   > Tip: vent what you don't need yet. A full output tank stops the whole separator.
3. **A Source of Sulfur**: 8x `modern_industrialization:sulfur_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: sulfur is where sulfuric acid starts.
   > Chemistry: S is element 16. Volcanoes and fossil fuels are full of it; most industrial sulfur is stripped out of oil and gas.
   > How: macerate crushed lignite coal (about half the time you get sulfur dust), or centrifuge lava later. Press U on Sulfur Dust in JEI for all sources.
4. **Contact Process 1: SO₂**: `mekanism:chemical_oxidizer` *(after: Pressurized Tubes, A Source of Sulfur, Dynamic Tanks)*
   > What: the Chemical Oxidizer turns a solid into a gas. Sulfur dust becomes sulfur dioxide.
   > Chemistry: S + O₂ → SO₂. It's the sharp smell of a struck match.
   > How: one sulfur dust gives 100 mB of SO₂. Pipe it out with pressurized tubes.
5. **Contact Process 2: SO₃**: `mekanism:chemical_infuser` *(after: Contact Process 1: SO₂)*
   > What: the Chemical Infuser combines two gases. SO₂ plus oxygen from your separator gives sulfur trioxide.
   > Chemistry: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. Real plants pass the gases over a vanadium oxide (V₂O₅) catalyst at about 450 °C: the 'contact' in the name.
   > How: SO₂ in one side, O₂ in the other.
6. **Water Vapor**: `mekanism:rotary_condensentrator` *(after: Contact Process 2: SO₃, Energy Tablet)*
   > What: the Rotary Condensentrator converts fluids to gases and back. It turns water into water vapor.
   > How: set it to gas mode (the toggle in its GUI), pipe water in and pressurized tube out.
   > Tip: it also turns Mekanism gases into buckets, which is handy for storage and trading.
7. **Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄**: checkmark *(after: Water Vapor)*
   > What: a second Chemical Infuser combines SO₃ with water vapor into sulfuric acid gas. Tick this when acid is flowing.
   > Chemistry: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄. Real plants dissolve SO₃ in existing acid first (oleum), because SO₃ and water alone make a corrosive mist.
   > Tip: store the acid in a chemical tank. The 5x ore line drinks it.
8. **Salt**: 16x `modern_industrialization:salt_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: salt is the start of the chlor-alkali industry: chlorine, sodium and everything made from them.
   > Chemistry: NaCl is an ionic crystal: Na⁺ and Cl⁻ held together by charge. Split it and you get a soft, reactive metal and a toxic green gas.
   > How: MI salt ore is found underground and drops salt dust.
9. **Brine**: checkmark *(after: Salt, Contact Process 1: SO₂)*
   > What: brine is salty water, and Mekanism splits it into chlorine. Tick this when you have brine.
   > How: put salt dust in a Chemical Oxidizer (15 mB brine per dust), or build a Thermal Evaporation Plant (see the side quest).
   > Tip: a second oxidizer just for salt saves you from swapping inputs.
10. **Chlorine**: checkmark *(after: Brine)*
   > What: the Electrolytic Separator also takes brine. Out come chlorine and sodium. Tick this when chlorine is flowing.
   > Chemistry: real brine electrolysis gives Cl₂ at one electrode and H₂ + NaOH at the other. Mekanism simplifies it to sodium + chlorine.
   > Tip: use a second separator so your hydrogen and oxygen line keeps running.
11. **Hydrogen Chloride**: checkmark *(after: Chlorine, Contact Process 2: SO₃)*
   > What: hydrogen chloride drives the 4x ore line. Tick this when HCl is flowing.
   > Chemistry: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. Dissolved in water it's hydrochloric acid, the same acid in your stomach.
   > How: hydrogen in one side of a Chemical Infuser, chlorine in the other.
12. **3x Ore: Oxygen**: `mekanism:purification_chamber` *(after: Mekanism Gases, Enrichment Chamber, Advanced Control Circuits)*
   > What: before acids, every route caps at 2x per ore. Purifying ore with oxygen gives 3x. The chamber needs advanced control circuits, which are built on MI's electronic circuit.
   > How: ore + O₂ → 3 clumps. Crusher: clumps → dirty dust. Enrichment Chamber: dirty dust → dust.
   > Tip: Mekanism shows each step in JEI. Chain them with pipes and side configuration.
13. **4x Ore: Hydrogen Chloride**: `mekanism:chemical_injection_chamber` *(after: Hydrogen Chloride, Reinforced Alloy)*
   > What: injecting hydrogen chloride splits ore into shards: 4x.
   > How: ore + HCl → 4 shards. Purification Chamber: shards → clumps, then on through your 3x line.
   > Tip: your 3x machines are now the back half of the 4x line. Nothing is wasted.
14. **Dissolving Ore**: `mekanism:chemical_dissolution_chamber` *(after: 4x Ore: Hydrogen Chloride, Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄, Refined Obsidian)*
   > What: the Dissolution Chamber dissolves ore in sulfuric acid, giving a dirty slurry.
   > Chemistry: acid leaching: H₂SO₄ turns metal minerals into soluble sulfates, leaving the rock behind.
   > How: feed it ore and sulfuric acid gas. The slurry comes out as a chemical.
15. **Washing Slurry**: `mekanism:chemical_washer` *(after: Dissolving Ore)*
   > What: the Chemical Washer rinses impurities out of the slurry.
   > Chemistry: washing removes the dissolved gangue (waste rock) so only the metal salt is left to crystallise.
   > How: slurry in, water in, clean slurry out. An MI electric water pump keeps the water coming.
16. **5x Ore: Dissolution**: `mekanism:chemical_crystallizer` *(after: Washing Slurry, Fluorite)*
   > Five from one. You used to call that a small miracle. Now you call it hydrometallurgy.
   > What: the Chemical Crystallizer turns clean slurry into crystals: 5x per ore.
   > Chemistry: this is hydrometallurgy, the way most of the world's copper is really refined.
   > How: crystals → Injection Chamber (shards) → Purification Chamber (clumps) → Crusher → Enrichment Chamber.
   > Tip: the Crystallizer itself needs fluorite gems: Mekanism's fluorite ore sits deep underground (check JEI for the recipe).
17. **Ore Byproducts**: 4x `modern_industrialization:silver_dust` *(after: 5x Ore: Dissolution, The Centrifuge)*
   > What: real ores are never pure. Send Mekanism's dirty dust through MI's Centrifuge instead of the Enrichment Chamber for the same dust plus a chance at a bonus metal.
   > Chemistry: iron → nickel, copper → gold, gold → silver, lead → silver (galena), tin → tungsten, osmium → iridium, uranium → lead (decay).
   > How: route dirty dust to your Centrifuge instead of the Enrichment Chamber. Silver from lead (or gold) dirty dust ticks this quest.
18. **Bauxite**: 16x `modern_industrialization:bauxite_dust` *(after: Electric Blast Furnace)*
   > An emperor once served his finest guests on this metal. You knew even then it was never rare, only stubborn.
   > What: bauxite is the only practical aluminum ore. MI bauxite ore drops bauxite dust.
   > Chemistry: bauxite is mostly aluminium hydroxides, Al(OH)₃ and AlO(OH), stained red by iron oxide.
   > How: rich bauxite deposits sit around Y -16 to 24. No furnace will free the metal: it goes through the Bayer process first.
19. **Lye for the Digester**: `modern_industrialization:sodium_hydroxide_bucket` *(after: Electric Mixer, The Combiner)*
   > What: the Bayer process dissolves bauxite in hot lye, so you need sodium hydroxide solution first.
   > Chemistry: NaOH is a strong base: it fully splits into Na⁺ and OH⁻ in water, and OH⁻ is what pulls aluminium into solution.
   > How: combine Na + O + H in the Alchemistry Combiner (check JEI on Sodium Hydroxide), then Mixer: 1 crystal + 250 mB water → 250 mB lye.
   > Tip: the digester gives most of the lye back, so a few crystals go a long way. Later the Chemical Reactor makes it in bulk.
20. **Bayer Digestion**: `modern_industrialization:sodium_aluminate_solution_bucket` *(after: Bauxite, Lye for the Digester)*
   > What: the first step of every aluminium refinery since 1888: hot lye dissolves the aluminium out of bauxite.
   > Chemistry: Al(OH)₃ + NaOH → NaAl(OH)₄ (sodium aluminate). Iron and titanium oxides don't dissolve; they settle out as 'red mud'.
   > How: Mixer: 4 bauxite dust + 1000 mB lye → 1000 mB sodium aluminate solution + 2 tiny iron dust + 1 tiny titanium dust.
   > Tip: pipe the solution straight into the next Mixer; a bucket is only needed for this quest.
21. **Precipitation**: 8x `chemlib:aluminum_hydroxide_dust` *(after: Bayer Digestion)*
   > What: pure aluminium hydroxide, crystallised back out of the solution, with the lye recovered.
   > Chemistry: NaAl(OH)₄ → Al(OH)₃ + NaOH. Diluting the liquor makes the reaction run backwards; the impurities stayed behind in the red mud.
   > How: Mixer: 1000 mB sodium aluminate + 1000 mB water → 4 aluminium hydroxide dust + 900 mB lye.
   > Tip: loop the 900 mB of lye back into the digester. That loop is why the Bayer process is cheap.
22. **Alumina**: 4x `chemlib:aluminum_oxide_dust` *(after: Precipitation)*
   > What: alumina (aluminium oxide) is the white powder that actually goes into the smelter.
   > Chemistry: calcination: 2Al(OH)₃ → Al₂O₃ + 3H₂O at around 1000 °C. Alumina also makes sapphire and ruby, coloured by traces of iron, titanium or chromium.
   > How: Electric Blast Furnace: 2 aluminium hydroxide dust → 1 alumina dust.
23. **The Hall-Héroult Cell**: `modern_industrialization:hall_heroult_cell` *(after: Alumina, Steel Large Plates)*
   > What: a multiblock smelter that splits alumina with electricity. It's built from steel and LV parts, because it's what makes your first aluminium.
   > Chemistry: alumina melts at 2072 °C, far too hot. Dissolved in molten cryolite it melts near 950 °C. Current then splits it: 2Al₂O₃ + 3C → 4Al + 3CO₂, burning the carbon anode away.
   > How: controller from steel large plates, analog circuits, cupronickel coils and an LV hull. Check JEI (press U on the controller) for the 3x3x3 shape: steel casings top and bottom, a ring of cupronickel coils with the controller in the middle layer.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > History: Charles Martin Hall (USA) and Paul Héroult (France) found the process independently in 1886, both in their early twenties. Within about ten years the price of aluminium fell by more than 90%.
   > Note: every primary aluminium smelter on Earth still uses it, and the cells draw a few percent of the world's electricity.
24. **Aluminum**: 8x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_ingot` *(after: The Hall-Héroult Cell)*
   > The metal comes away bright and light in your hand. Some part of you is pleased it still had to work for it.
   > What: aluminum is the metal of the MV tier: boards, rotors, casings, the Chemical Reactor and the Electrolyzer.
   > Chemistry: aluminium is the most common metal in the crust but clings to oxygen, so only electricity can pull it free.
   > How: Hall-Héroult Cell (LV power): 1 alumina dust + coke dust (the anode, used half the time) + a pinch of fluorite flux → 1 aluminum ingot.
   > Tip: 4 bauxite dust becomes 2 ingots. The cell only takes refined alumina dust, and no furnace will smelt aluminium dust: the Bayer line is the way in.
25. **Fun Fact: No Shortcut**: checkmark *(after: Alumina)*
   > What: for decades aluminium cost more than silver, because nobody could pull it off its oxygen cheaply. Tick this once you've read why.
   > Chemistry: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃ releases so much energy that thermite (Al + iron oxide) burns white-hot. Carbon grabs oxygen far less strongly, so coke in a furnace can't take it back from alumina.
   > How: that's why this pack has no furnace route for aluminium: the Hall-Héroult cell feeds in electricity instead, and it only accepts refined alumina dust from your Bayer line.
   > Tip: Napoleon III reportedly served his most honoured guests on aluminium plates. Everyone else made do with gold.
26. **Electrum**: 4x `modern_industrialization:electrum_ingot` *(after: Electric Mixer)*
   > What: electrum cable and fine wire go into every MV component.
   > Chemistry: electrum is a natural gold-silver alloy. The first coins, in Lydia around 600 BC, were struck from it.
   > How: mix gold and silver dust, then smelt. Check JEI (press R on Silver Dust) for silver ore in this pack.
27. **Silicon**: 4x `modern_industrialization:silicon_ingot` *(after: Electric Blast Furnace, Quartz Dust)*
   > What: silicon is the semiconductor every transistor and diode is built on.
   > Chemistry: SiO₂ + 2C → Si + 2CO. Carbon pulls the oxygen off quartz at furnace heat: carbothermic reduction.
   > How: macerate quartz into dust, then EBF: quartz dust + coke dust → silicon dust. Smelt it into ingots.
   > Tip: this is the only source of silicon in the pack. AE2's certus smelting and Mekanism's sand crushing are removed, so AE2 runs on this silicon too.
28. **Electronic Circuit Board**: `modern_industrialization:electronic_circuit_board` *(after: Aluminum Plates, Electrum Cable)*
   > What: the base for MV circuits.
   > How: an analog circuit board with aluminum plates, electrum cable and a redstone battery (see JEI).
   > Tip: the Assembler can make these too, once you stock it.
29. **Transistors and Diodes**: 2x `modern_industrialization:transistor`; 2x `modern_industrialization:diode` *(after: Silicon Plates, Electrum Fine Wire)*
   > What: diodes let current flow one way; transistors are switches controlled by current.
   > Chemistry: a pure silicon crystal barely conducts. Tiny amounts of other elements ('doping') make it conduct in controllable ways.
   > How: silicon plates, steel plates and electrum fine wire (diodes add glass).
30. **Electronic Circuit**: 2x `modern_industrialization:electronic_circuit` *(after: Electronic Circuit Board, Transistors and Diodes)*
   > What: the MV circuit. The Electrolyzer, Chemical Reactor and Centrifuge all need it, even though they sit on an LV hull.
   > How: electronic circuit board, 4 analog circuits, 2 diodes and 2 transistors.
   > Tip: set an Assembler to make these. You'll need dozens.
31. **Electrolysis**: `modern_industrialization:electrolyzer` *(after: Pumps, Large and Small)*
   > What: pass current through a compound and it splits. This is electrochemistry.
   > Chemistry: water → H₂ + O₂ (3000 mB water → 2000 mB H₂ + 1000 mB O₂). Salt → sodium + chlorine.
   > How: magnetic cupronickel wire, aluminum rods, an LV hull, an electronic circuit and a large pump.
32. **The Chemical Reactor**: `modern_industrialization:chemical_reactor` *(after: Pumps, Large and Small)*
   > What: combines items and fluids into new compounds. You'll use it constantly from here to the end.
   > How: glass, a large pump, aluminum rotors, an LV hull, electronic circuits and electrum cable.
   > Tip: MI fluids go in through pipes. A Configurable Tank holds spare H₂ and O₂.
33. **Sodium**: 4x `modern_industrialization:sodium_dust` *(after: Electrolysis, Salt)*
   > What: sodium goes into the HV tier's sodium battery. The chlorine is a bonus.
   > Chemistry: 2NaCl → 2Na + Cl₂. Real sodium is made this way from molten salt (the Downs cell). It reacts violently with water.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 2 salt dust → 1 sodium dust + 125 mB chlorine.
34. **Sulfuric Acid**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_acid_bucket` *(after: The Chemical Reactor, A Source of Sulfur)*
   > Acid opens what fire cannot. You learned that once, the hard way, and the lesson has come back intact.
   > What: sulfuric acid, as an MI fluid you can bucket. The Undergarden portal and many MI recipes need it.
   > Chemistry: S + O₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₄, the whole contact process in one vessel. Industry makes more of it than any other chemical.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 sulfur dust + 200 mB O₂ + 200 mB water → 500 mB sulfuric acid.
35. **Silicon Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:silicon_battery` *(after: Battery Plates, Electrum Cable, Silicon)*
   > What: the MV battery. Every MV hull holds two.
   > How: battery alloy plates, electrum cable and silicon dust.
   > Tip: make four. The Advanced (MV) hull uses two, and you'll want a second hull soon.
36. **MV: Aluminum**: `modern_industrialization:electronic_circuit`; `modern_industrialization:advanced_machine_hull` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Silicon Battery, Advanced Machine Casing)*
   > The circuits are getting smaller and the power larger. So are you.
   > What: the MV hull is the base for every MV machine, and Powah, Hostile Neural Networks and Extended Crafting all want MV circuits.
   > How: advanced machine casing (an LV hull wrapped in aluminum plates) + electronic circuit + 2 silicon batteries + electrum cable.
37. **Uranium**: 4x `modern_industrialization:uranium_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: uranium is the fuel of Powah's reactors and, much later, fission.
   > Chemistry: U is element 92, the heaviest element found in quantity in nature. It slowly decays into lead.
   > How: rich uranium deposits sit deep, around Y -56 to -24. Macerate the ore into dust.
38. **Uranium Dioxide**: `powah:energizing_orb`; 4x `powah:uraninite` *(after: MV: Aluminum, The Chemical Reactor, Uranium)*
   > What: uraninite fuels Powah's reactors. Powah's Energizing Orb needs an MV circuit.
   > Chemistry: uraninite is UO₂, the main ore of uranium in nature. Here you make it: U + O₂ → UO₂.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: uranium dust + 500 mB oxygen → uraninite. Powah's own uraninite ore is turned off.
39. **The Undergarden**: `undergarden:catalyst`; visit `undergarden:undergarden` *(after: Sulfuric Acid, Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄)*
   > A world beneath the world, and the key to its door is a bottle of acid. You are trusted with more every day.
   > What: a strange underground dimension. Its portal catalyst needs a bucket of sulfuric acid: MI's, Mekanism's or ChemLib's all work.
   > How: the quickest bucket is your Mekanism contact process: a Rotary Condensentrator in liquid mode turns the acid gas into fluid you can bucket. MI's Chemical Reactor acid works too. Then build a stone-brick portal frame and right-click it with the catalyst.
   > Tip: bring torches and food. It is dark down there.
40. **Thermal Evaporation**: `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_controller`; `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_valve`; 16x `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_block` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: a tall multiblock that boils water down into brine, and brine down into lithium.
   > Chemistry: evaporation concentrates dissolved salts. Salt flats and lithium ponds in Chile work the same way.
   > How: see Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI for the layout. Taller towers run faster; heat speeds it up.
41. **Bottled Gases**: 3x `mekanism:basic_chemical_tank` *(after: A Tank for Gas)*
   > What: chemical tanks store gases and keep them when broken, so you can carry them around.
   > How: fill one tank each with hydrogen, oxygen and chlorine.
   > Tip: a tank of hydrogen also fuels the Gas-Burning Generator (Power chapter).
42. **Fun Fact: Oleum**: checkmark *(after: Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄)*
   > What: SO₃ hitting water directly forms a fine acid mist that's hard to capture.
   > Chemistry: plants absorb SO₃ into concentrated H₂SO₄ to make oleum (H₂S₂O₇), then dilute: H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄.
   > Tip: you've now run, in miniature, a process that makes over 250 million tonnes a year.
43. **Five for Everything**: checkmark *(after: 5x Ore: Dissolution)*
   > What: a challenge: put at least five different ores through the full 5x line.
   > How: one Dissolution Chamber handles every metal, but each slurry needs its own washer and crystallizer pass. Tick this when five ores are done.
   > Tip: Mekanism factories (upgraded machines) run several ores at once.
44. **A Red Mountain**: 128x `modern_industrialization:bauxite_dust` *(after: Bauxite)*
   > What: rich deposits hold hundreds of ores in one chunk. Find bauxite's and the MV tier stops feeling slow.
   > How: strip-mine around Y -16 to 24 and look for red ore with Jade. FTB Ultimine helps a lot.
   > Tip: Fortune works on bauxite ore, since it drops dust.
45. **A Hint of Titanium**: 9x `modern_industrialization:titanium_tiny_dust` *(after: Bayer Digestion)*
   > What: Bayer digestion leaves a little titanium behind with the iron. Save it for much later.
   > Chemistry: bauxite carries titanium dioxide (TiO₂) as an impurity. It doesn't dissolve in lye, so it ends up in the 'red mud'.
   > How: every Bayer digestion (4 bauxite dust) gives 1 tiny titanium dust. Nine of them pack into a full dust.
46. **Hydrochloric Acid, MI Style**: `modern_industrialization:hydrochloric_acid_bucket` *(after: Hydrogen and Oxygen, MI Style, Chlorine, MI Style)*
   > What: MI makes hydrochloric acid as a fluid, the MI twin of Mekanism's HCl gas. Chromium leaching and PVC both need it later.
   > Chemistry: H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl. 1000 mB of each gas gives 2000 mB of acid.
   > How: chlorine from salt electrolysis, hydrogen from water electrolysis, both into the Chemical Reactor.
47. **Lye**: `modern_industrialization:sodium_hydroxide_bucket` *(after: The Chemical Reactor, Sodium, Hydrogen and Oxygen, MI Style)*
   > What: sodium hydroxide (NaOH, lye) is the strong base to sulfuric acid's strong acid. Soap is made with it.
   > Chemistry: acid + base → salt + water. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: sodium dust + 1000 mB oxygen + 1000 mB hydrogen → 2000 mB sodium hydroxide.
   > Tip: this is the bulk lye supply for the Bayer digester, so you can stop feeding it Combiner crystals.
48. **Pumps, Large and Small**: 3x `modern_industrialization:pump`; `modern_industrialization:large_pump` *(after: Large Motor, Aluminum Rotors)*
   > What: the Electrolyzer and the Chemical Reactor each need a Large Pump, and a Large Pump is three small pumps driven by a Large Motor.
   > How: Large Pump: 2 electronic circuits, 3 aluminum rotors, a Large Motor and 3 pumps (Assembler or crafting table; check JEI).
   > Tip: pumps are the part you'll run short of. Keep an Assembler stocked with motors and rotors.
49. **Doping Silicon**: `modern_industrialization:silicon_n_doped_plate`; `modern_industrialization:silicon_p_doped_plate` *(after: The Chemical Reactor)*
   > What: silicon plates with a trace of another element, used in cheaper recipes for transistors and diodes.
   > Chemistry: silicon has four outer electrons. Antimony has five, so it adds a spare electron (n-type); aluminium has three, so it leaves a 'hole' (p-type). Where n meets p, current flows one way only: a diode.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 silicon plate + 1 tiny antimony dust → n-doped plate; 1 silicon plate + 1 tiny aluminum dust → p-doped plate. JEI shows the doped transistor and diode recipes.
50. **Machine Upgrades**: 4x `modern_industrialization:basic_upgrade`; `modern_industrialization:overdrive_module` *(after: Electronic Circuit Board)*
   > What: Upgrades go in a machine's upgrade slot and raise how much EU/t it may draw, so it overclocks harder. The Overdrive Module keeps a machine's efficiency up while it waits for input.
   > How: Assembler: 2 conveyors, 4 motors, 2 robot arms and an analog circuit board → 4 basic upgrades. Overdrive Module: 2 diodes, 2 transistors, 4 electrum fine wire and an electronic circuit board.
   > Tip: hover over an upgrade for its exact bonus. Some late recipes ask for more EU/t than a plain machine allows; upgrades are the answer.
51. **Electric Helpers**: `extended_industrialization:electric_alloy_smelter`; `modern_industrialization:electric_unpacker` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: the electric versions of two steam-age helpers: the Electric Alloy Smelter (Extended Industrialization) pours alloys from nuggets, the Electric Unpacker breaks blocks and double ingots back down.
   > How: both sit on an LV machine hull with analog circuits. The Alloy Smelter adds a tin rotor and magnetic cupronickel wire, the Unpacker motors and conveyors (check JEI).
   > Tip: they run on the same LV cable as everything else, so your steam boilers can finally rest.
52. **The Electrolytic Core**: `mekanism:electrolytic_core` *(after: Mekanism Circuits, Infused Alloy)*
   > You remember a time when you split water by asking it to. The memory comes back as a wiring diagram.
   > What: the core of Mekanism's Electrolytic Separator: the part that actually carries current through the water.
   > Chemistry: an electrolysis cell needs electrodes that conduct and don't dissolve. Real alkaline cells use nickel; Mekanism uses osmium, iron and gold.
   > How: infused alloy, osmium dust, iron dust and gold dust on a crafting table (check JEI for the pattern).
53. **A Tank for Gas**: 2x `mekanism:basic_chemical_tank` *(after: Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: a basic chemical tank stores one gas. Most Mekanism chemistry machines have one built in.
   > How: basic alloy and osmium ingots (check JEI). The Oxidizer, Infuser, Condensentrator, Washer and Dissolution Chamber all take one.
   > Tip: a broken tank keeps its contents, so you can carry a tank of oxygen across the base.
54. **Energy Tablet**: `mekanism:energy_tablet` *(after: Infused Alloy)*
   > What: a portable energy store. The Rotary Condensentrator and the laser are built around one.
   > How: gold ingots, infused alloy and redstone dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also charges Mekanism tools from your inventory.
55. **Dynamic Tanks**: 4x `mekanism:dynamic_tank` *(after: A Tank for Gas)*
   > What: dynamic tank blocks. One goes into the Chemical Oxidizer; a ring of them makes Mekanism's big multiblock fluid tank.
   > How: 4 steel ingots around a bucket → 4 dynamic tanks.
   > Tip: a small dynamic tank multiblock is a cheap place to keep thousands of buckets of water or brine.
56. **Acid by the Bucket**: `mekanism:sulfuric_acid_bucket` *(after: Contact Process 3: H₂SO₄)*
   > What: a bucket of Mekanism sulfuric acid. It opens the Undergarden and counts for the Seed's eight acid buckets.
   > Chemistry: pure H₂SO₄ boils near 337 °C, so at room temperature it is an oily liquid. Mekanism keeps it as a gas only for piping.
   > How: switch a Rotary Condensentrator to liquid mode, pipe the acid gas in and take the fluid out in a bucket.
57. **Advanced Control Circuits**: 2x `mekanism:advanced_control_circuit` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: every Mekanism chamber past the Enrichment Chamber needs advanced control circuits.
   > How: 1 MI electronic circuit, 2 infused alloy and 1 basic control circuit. Mekanism's own infuser shortcut is removed in this pack.
   > Tip: make six: the Purification, Injection, Dissolution, Washer and Crystallizer recipes all want two.
58. **Clumps**: 6x any of `item_tag(mekanism:clumps)` *(after: 3x Ore: Oxygen)*
   > What: any 6 Mekanism clumps: the first product of the 3x line.
   > Chemistry: oxygen burns off sulfur and other volatile impurities (roasting), leaving a cleaner metal oxide behind.
   > How: Purification Chamber: 1 ore + a little oxygen → 3 clumps (2 from raw ore).
59. **Dirty Dust**: 6x any of `item_tag(mekanism:dirty_dusts)` *(after: Clumps, Crusher)*
   > What: any 6 dirty dusts. One more Enrichment Chamber pass turns each into clean dust.
   > How: Crusher: 1 clump → 1 dirty dust. Enrichment Chamber: dirty dust → dust.
   > Tip: dirty dust is also what MI's Centrifuge wants for ore byproducts (silver from lead, nickel from iron).
60. **Reinforced Alloy**: 2x `mekanism:enriched_diamond`; 4x `mekanism:alloy_reinforced` *(after: 3x Ore: Oxygen)*
   > What: the second Mekanism alloy. The Injection Chamber, the laser and elite circuits all need it.
   > How: Enrichment Chamber: diamond → enriched diamond. Metallurgic Infuser: infused alloy + diamond infusion → reinforced alloy.
   > Tip: one enriched diamond is a lot of infusion. Don't waste whole diamonds on it.
61. **Shards**: 8x any of `item_tag(mekanism:shards)` *(after: 4x Ore: Hydrogen Chloride)*
   > What: any 8 Mekanism shards, the first product of the 4x line.
   > Chemistry: hydrochloric acid attacks the minerals around the metal (carbonates, oxides) and breaks the ore into fragments. Real hydrometallurgy leaches with HCl the same way.
   > How: Chemical Injection Chamber: 1 ore + HCl → 4 shards. Shards go into the Purification Chamber as if they were ore.
62. **Refined Obsidian**: 12x `mekanism:ingot_refined_obsidian` *(after: Reinforced Alloy)*
   > What: the casing metal of the 5x line: the Washer, Dissolution Chamber and Crystallizer each take 4 ingots.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass, mostly SiO₂, cooled too fast to crystallise. That's why it shatters into razor edges.
   > How: Crusher: obsidian → 4 obsidian dust. Metallurgic Infuser with diamond → refined obsidian dust. Osmium Compressor with osmium → ingot (check JEI).
63. **Fluorite**: 4x `mekanism:fluorite_gem` *(after: Dissolving Ore)*
   > What: fluorite gems. The Chemical Crystallizer needs two, and later fluorite becomes hydrofluoric acid.
   > Chemistry: fluorite is calcium fluoride, CaF₂. Some samples glow under ultraviolet light, which is where the word fluorescence comes from.
   > How: Mekanism fluorite ore sits deep underground. It drops dust; the Enrichment Chamber turns dust into gems. No farm or spirit can make it in this pack.
64. **Crystals**: 8x any of `item_tag(mekanism:crystals)` *(after: 5x Ore: Dissolution)*
   > What: any 8 Mekanism crystals, the first product of the 5x line.
   > Chemistry: crystallisation pulls a pure salt out of solution and leaves the impurities dissolved. It's one of the oldest purification tricks in chemistry.
   > How: Chemical Crystallizer: 200 mB clean slurry → 1 crystal. Then Injection Chamber → shards → Purification Chamber → and on down the line.
65. **Steel Large Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:steel_large_plate` *(after: Steel Plates)*
   > What: the Hall-Héroult Cell and, later, the Oil Drilling Rig are both framed in steel large plates.
   > How: 4 steel plates in a square on a crafting table, or the Packer.
66. **Aluminum Plates**: 16x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_plate` *(after: Aluminum)*
   > What: MV parts are wrapped in aluminum: 3 per electronic circuit board, 8 per advanced machine casing.
   > Chemistry: a fresh aluminium surface grows an oxide skin a few nanometres thick within seconds. It's why aluminium doesn't rust away, even though it reacts with oxygen far more eagerly than iron.
   > How: Compressor: 1 aluminum ingot → 1 plate.
67. **Aluminum Rods**: 6x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_rod` *(after: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Electrolyzer and the Large Motor each take two; rotors and rings need more.
   > How: Cutting Machine with a little lubricant: 1 ingot → 2 rods.
68. **Curved Aluminum**: 4x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_curved_plate` *(after: Aluminum Plates)*
   > What: curved plates become rotor blades now and drill heads in the next chapter.
   > How: Compressor: 1 aluminum plate → 1 curved plate (or Extended Industrialization's Bending Machine).
69. **Aluminum Rotors**: 3x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_rotor` *(after: Curved Aluminum, Aluminum Rods)*
   > What: every Large Pump spins three aluminum rotors, and the Chemical Reactor stirs with two more.
   > How: blades: 2 curved plates + 1 rod → 4 blades. Ring: Compressor, 1 rod → 1 ring. Rotor: 4 blades, 4 bolts and a ring on a crafting table.
   > Tip: the Assembler also makes rotors, but its recipe uses soldering alloy, which comes much later. Craft these by hand.
70. **Electrum Wire**: 2x `modern_industrialization:electrum_plate`; 8x `modern_industrialization:electrum_wire` *(after: Electrum)*
   > What: electrum wire is the conductor of the MV tier.
   > Chemistry: silver is the best electrical conductor of all metals, and gold never tarnishes. Their alloy keeps a little of both virtues.
   > How: Compressor: ingot → plate. Wiremill: 1 plate → 2 wire.
71. **Electrum Cable**: 12x `modern_industrialization:electrum_cable` *(after: Electrum Wire, Rubber)*
   > What: the MV cable. Circuit boards take 4, hulls 3, batteries 2, and it carries MV power between machines.
   > Chemistry: rubber is a polymer with no free electrons, so it can't carry current. A thin sleeve of it keeps the current inside the wire.
   > How: 3 electrum wire between 6 rubber sheets → 3 cables (crafting table or Packer).
72. **Electrum Fine Wire**: 8x `modern_industrialization:electrum_fine_wire` *(after: Electrum Wire)*
   > What: the leads inside transistors (1 each) and diodes (3 each).
   > How: Wiremill: 1 electrum wire → 4 fine wire.
73. **Quartz Dust**: 8x `modern_industrialization:quartz_dust` *(after: Nether Quartz, Electric Macerator)*
   > What: the raw material for silicon.
   > Chemistry: quartz is SiO₂: every silicon atom bonded to four oxygens in a rigid network. That's why it's so hard and melts at about 1700 °C.
   > How: Macerator: 1 Nether quartz → 1 quartz dust. Centrifuging redstone also gives a little.
74. **Silicon Plates**: 6x `modern_industrialization:silicon_plate` *(after: Silicon)*
   > What: transistors take 3 silicon plates, diodes 1.
   > How: Compressor: 1 silicon ingot → 1 plate.
75. **Battery Plates**: 2x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_plate`; 8x `modern_industrialization:battery_alloy_curved_plate` *(after: Battery Alloy)*
   > What: each battery from here to the quantum tier is 1 battery alloy plate and 4 curved plates around its chemistry.
   > Chemistry: battery alloy is lead and antimony, the same grid metal used in car batteries since the 1880s. Antimony makes soft lead stiff enough to hold its shape.
   > How: Compressor: ingot → plate; Compressor again: plate → curved plate.
76. **Large Motor**: `modern_industrialization:large_motor` *(after: Electronic Circuit, Aluminum Rods)*
   > What: the drive of the Large Pump, the Centrifuge and the Electric Quarry.
   > How: an electronic circuit, 2 aluminum rods and 6 motors (crafting table or Assembler).
   > Tip: the Centrifuge alone eats four. Keep an Assembler on motors.
77. **The Centrifuge**: `modern_industrialization:centrifuge` *(after: Pumps, Large and Small)*
   > What: MI's Centrifuge spins mixtures apart. Ore byproducts, ruby and chromium, liquid air and monazite all go through it later.
   > Chemistry: spinning multiplies gravity thousands of times, so heavier particles and molecules move outward faster than light ones.
   > How: 4 large motors, a large pump, an electronic circuit, 2 electrum cable and an LV hull.
78. **Advanced Machine Casing**: `modern_industrialization:advanced_machine_casing` *(after: Aluminum Plates, LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: the shell of the MV hull.
   > How: 8 aluminum plates around a basic (LV) machine hull.
79. **Hydrogen and Oxygen, MI Style**: `modern_industrialization:hydrogen_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:oxygen_bucket` *(after: Electrolysis)*
   > What: MI's own hydrogen and oxygen. The Chemical Reactor takes them by pipe, not Mekanism's gases.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂: two volumes of hydrogen for every one of oxygen, as the recipe shows.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 3000 mB water → 2000 mB hydrogen + 1000 mB oxygen. Fill a bucket of each from the output.
80. **Chlorine, MI Style**: `modern_industrialization:chlorine_bucket` *(after: Sodium)*
   > What: MI chlorine, the other half of salt electrolysis. It makes hydrochloric acid and, much later, PVC.
   > Chemistry: Cl₂ is a yellow-green gas, heavier than air. Its name comes from the Greek for pale green.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 2 salt dust → 1 sodium dust + 125 mB chlorine. Eight runs fill a bucket.
81. **An MV Grid**: `modern_industrialization:lv_mv_transformer`; `modern_industrialization:mv_storage_unit` *(after: MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: a transformer joins your LV and MV cables; the MV storage unit buffers a lot more energy than the LV one.
   > How: transformer: an LV hull, 4 tin cable and 1 electrum cable. Storage unit: an MV hull, 6 silicon batteries and 2 battery alloy plates.
   > Tip: multiblocks draw from energy hatches, so a big buffer next to them keeps recipes from stalling.

### VI. Petrochemistry

*Crude oil is a mixture. Separate it by boiling point, then build polymers from the pieces.*

1. **Black Gold**: `modern_industrialization:oil_drilling_rig`; `modern_industrialization:crude_oil_bucket` *(after: MV: Aluminum, Aluminum Drills, Steel Large Plates, Pipe Casings, Rig Hatches)*
   > Before there were people, you watched forests grow, fall and sink, and the ages press them into oil. Time to take some of that sunlight back.
   > What: crude oil is a soup of hydrocarbons, from tiny gas molecules to long waxy chains.
   > Chemistry: hydrocarbons are just carbon and hydrogen (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and friends). Chain length decides whether one is a gas, a fuel or a tar.
   > How: the Oil Drilling Rig is a multiblock (layout in JEI and the MI guidebook). Controller: 4 steel large plates, 2 large pumps, an electronic circuit, a fluid pipe and an MV hull. Walls of steel casings and steel pipe casings, with chains. Feed it aluminum drills and power; each cycle pumps 500 mB of crude and has a small chance to wear a drill out.
   > Tip: pipe the crude straight into a tank. You'll need a lot of it.
2. **Sour Fractions**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_light_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_heavy_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_naphtha_bucket` *(after: Sour Light Fuel, Sour Heavy Fuel, Sour Naphtha)*
   > What: 1000 mB of crude gives 500 light fuel, 200 heavy fuel and 300 naphtha, but all three are 'sour'.
   > Chemistry: natural oil carries sulfur compounds. Burn them and you get SO₂, the gas behind acid rain.
   > How: a bucket of each, from the Distillery's three crude-oil recipes. Later the Distillation Tower makes all three at once.
3. **Sweetening the Oil**: `modern_industrialization:light_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:heavy_fuel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:naphtha_bucket` *(after: Sour Fractions, Hydrogen and Oxygen, MI Style)*
   > What: hydrotreating removes the sulfur and gives clean light fuel, heavy fuel and naphtha.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen reacts with sulfur compounds to form H₂S. Real refineries turn that into sulfur and then acid; MI hands you sulfuric acid directly.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 12 B of a sour fraction + 2 B hydrogen → 12 B clean fraction + 2 B H₂SO₄.
   > Tip: feed the acid back into your ore line. Nothing is wasted.
4. **Diesel Power**: `modern_industrialization:diesel_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:lv_diesel_generator` *(after: Sweetening the Oil)*
   > What: diesel runs MI generators, tools and, later, your rockets (Ad Astra burns MI diesel).
   > Chemistry: diesel is a blend of C₁₀ to C₂₀ hydrocarbons: mostly light fuel, with heavy fuel for energy density.
   > How: Mixer: 5 B light fuel + 1 B heavy fuel → 6 B diesel.
   > Tip: a Large Diesel Generator is far more efficient than a row of small ones.
5. **Steam Cracking**: `modern_industrialization:steam_cracked_naphtha_bucket` *(after: Sweetening the Oil)*
   > What: naphtha is too big to make plastic from. Cracking breaks it into the small building blocks chemists actually want.
   > Chemistry: at high temperature with steam, long chains snap apart into short, reactive molecules with double bonds (alkenes).
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1000 mB naphtha + 100 mB steam → 1000 mB steam-cracked naphtha.
6. **Ethylene**: `modern_industrialization:ethylene_bucket` *(after: Steam Cracking)*
   > What: distilling cracked naphtha gives eight products: methane, acetylene, ethylene, propene, butadiene, benzene, toluene and ethylbenzene.
   > Chemistry: ethylene's C=C double bond can open up and link to its neighbours. That is how plastics are born.
   > How: Distillery: 1000 mB steam-cracked naphtha → 250 mB ethylene. Cracked light fuel gives 300 mB. The Distillation Tower (EV) later splits out all eight at once.
   > Tip: store every fraction. Each one has a use later in this chapter.
7. **Polymerisation**: `modern_industrialization:polyethylene_bucket` *(after: A Pinch of Catalyst)*
   > What: polyethylene, (C₂H₄)ₙ, is the plastic in bags and bottles, and the laminate on HV circuit boards.
   > Chemistry: a metal catalyst opens each double bond so the molecules join head to tail. Real plants use chromium (Phillips) or titanium catalysts.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 500 mB ethylene + 4 tiny lead or chromium dust → 300 mB polyethylene.
8. **HDPE**: 8x `mekanism:hdpe_pellet` *(after: Polymerisation, Pressurized Reaction Chamber)*
   > What: high-density polyethylene pellets become Mekanism's plastic sheets, rods and later the MekaSuit.
   > Chemistry: HDPE has straight chains that pack tightly, so it's stiffer than ordinary polyethylene.
   > How: Pressurized Reaction Chamber with ethylene, water and substrate (check JEI).
9. **Chromium and Manganese**: 4x `modern_industrialization:chromium_dust`; 4x `modern_industrialization:manganese_dust` *(after: Chromium Leach, Manganese Leach)*
   > What: stainless steel needs chromium, nickel and manganese on top of iron.
   > Chemistry: chromium is leached with acid: crushed chromium + HCl → chromium chloride solution, then electrolysis splits out the metal plus H₂ and Cl₂.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 1000 mB chromium solution → 3 tiny chromium dust (plus H₂ and Cl₂ back); 1000 mB manganese solution → 3 tiny manganese dust (plus most of the acid back). Nine tiny dusts make one dust.
10. **Stainless Steel Dust**: 9x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_dust` *(after: Chromium and Manganese, Nickel)*
   > What: the mixed powder that becomes stainless steel.
   > Chemistry: at 10.5% chromium or more, the surface forms an invisible Cr₂O₃ film that stops rust spreading.
   > How: Mixer: 6 iron dust + 1 chromium + 1 nickel + 1 manganese → 9 stainless steel dust.
11. **Hot Ingots**: `modern_industrialization:vacuum_freezer`; `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_hot_ingot` *(after: Stainless Steel Dust, Aluminum Large Plates)*
   > What: the Electric Blast Furnace melts the dust into a hot ingot that must be cooled before use.
   > How: EBF turns 1 stainless steel dust into 1 hot ingot. Build the Vacuum Freezer multiblock (layout in JEI) to cool it.
   > Tip: later, the Heat Exchanger cools hot ingots too and gives argon and helium back.
12. **Stainless Steel**: 8x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_ingot` *(after: Hot Ingots, Electric Blast Furnace)*
   > What: stainless steel resists corrosion, so it can hold acids and hot fluids.
   > Chemistry: if the surface is scratched, chromium re-forms the oxide film at once. The steel heals itself.
   > How: cool hot ingots in the Vacuum Freezer. HV circuit boards need 4 stainless plates each.
   > Tip: automate the whole line: mixer → EBF → freezer → compressor.
13. **Digital Circuit Board**: `modern_industrialization:digital_circuit_board` *(after: Polymerisation, Stainless Plates, Aluminum Cable, Silicon Battery)*
   > What: the base of every HV circuit.
   > Chemistry: polyethylene is an excellent insulator, so it separates the copper layers of the board.
   > How: Assembler: electronic circuit board + 4 stainless steel plates + silicon battery + 6 aluminum cable + 750 mB polyethylene.
14. **Sodium Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:sodium_battery` *(after: Sodium, Aluminum Cable, Battery Plates)*
   > What: the HV hull needs two sodium batteries.
   > Chemistry: sodium metal gives up its one outer electron very easily (it fizzes in water), which is what makes it a good battery material.
   > How: sodium dust from the Electrolyzer (2 salt dust → 1 sodium dust + chlorine), as in Electrochemistry. Then craft the battery (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep the chlorine. It's needed for HCl and, next chapter, PVC.
15. **HV: Digital Circuits**: `modern_industrialization:digital_circuit`; `modern_industrialization:turbo_machine_hull` *(after: Digital Circuit Board, Sodium Battery, Logic Gates, Turbo Machine Casing)*
   > Logic gates, clicking into place. You used to think this fast.
   > What: digital circuits unlock HV machines, AE2, the Angel Ring and elite jetpack coils.
   > How: Assembler: digital circuit board + 4 electronic circuits + AND, OR and NOT gates. The Turbo hull adds 2 sodium batteries and aluminum cable.
   > Tip: set up a dedicated assembler for circuits. You'll make hundreds.
16. **Fallen Stars**: `ae2:meteorite_compass`; `ae2:engineering_processor_press`; `ae2:silicon_press` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: AE2's inscriber presses are only found in the core of meteorites.
   > How: charge an ordinary compass in AE2's Charger to get a Meteorite Compass, follow it, and dig to the centre of the sky stone crater. Each meteorite's mysterious cube holds one press.
   > Tip: once you have one press, the Inscriber can copy it with an iron block.
17. **Fluix**: `ae2:charger`; 8x `ae2:fluix_crystal` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: fluix crystals carry the ME network's signal. The ME Controller needs them.
   > How: charge certus quartz in the Charger, then drop charged certus, redstone and Nether quartz in water together (check JEI).
   > Tip: budding certus quartz grows new crystals, so certus is renewable once you find some.
18. **The Inscriber**: `ae2:inscriber`; 2x `ae2:engineering_processor` *(after: Fallen Stars)*
   > What: every AE2 processor is printed in the Inscriber. In this pack it's built on a Turbo hull.
   > Chemistry: engineering processors print a circuit onto silicon, the same element your HV boards depend on.
   > How: press a diamond into a printed engineering circuit, silicon into printed silicon, then combine them with redstone.
   > Tip: the silicon is your MI silicon from the EBF. AE2's certus-to-silicon smelting is removed in this pack.
19. **The God's Archive**: `ae2:controller` *(after: Processors, Sky Stone, Fluix Cable)*
   > Everything you own, known at once and found in an instant. Your memory used to work like this; now it lives in a network you built.
   > What: Applied Energistics 2 stores items as data and crafts on demand.
   > How: the ME Controller needs a digital circuit, an engineering processor, fluix and smooth sky stone.
   > Tip: Tom's Simple Storage was your early network. AE2 takes over from here (see the Applied Energistics page in Engineering).
20. **First Storage Cells**: 2x `ae2:item_storage_cell_1k`; `ae2:fluid_storage_cell_1k` *(after: The God's Archive)*
   > What: storage cells go into an ME Drive. Fluid cells hold your acids and fuels as data too.
   > How: a 1k cell component needs a logic processor (gold + logic press). Check JEI for the housing.
   > Tip: a few fluid cells beat a wall of tanks for small stocks of rare chemicals.
21. **The Twilight Forest**: visit `twilightforest:twilight_forest` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > A forest held forever at dusk. Even a god can get lost here, which is half the fun.
   > What: a dimension of bosses, strange woods and unique metals (see the Twilight Forest page in Exploration).
   > How: dig a 2x2 pool of water ringed with flowers, stand in it, and throw in a diamond.
   > Tip: set a waystone near the portal before you explore.
22. **Benzene Rings**: `modern_industrialization:benzene_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:toluene_bucket` *(after: Steam Cracking)*
   > What: benzene (C₆H₆) and toluene (C₇H₈) come out of the cracked-naphtha distillation.
   > Chemistry: benzene is a flat ring of six carbons whose electrons are shared around the whole ring. That makes it unusually stable.
   > How: collect them from the Distillation Tower's benzene and toluene outputs.
   > Tip: keep the toluene: Industrial TNT needs it in the next chapter. Benzene also makes nylon (side quest).
23. **Styrene**: `modern_industrialization:ethylbenzene_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:styrene_bucket` *(after: Benzene Rings)*
   > Chemistry: benzene + ethylene → ethylbenzene (acid catalyst). Steam over iron then pulls off H₂ to give styrene, C₈H₈, exactly as in real plants.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: benzene + ethylene + a little HCl → ethylbenzene. Then ethylbenzene + steam + iron dust → styrene + hydrogen.
   > Tip: the hydrogen by-product can go straight back into hydrotreating.
24. **Synthetic Rubber**: `modern_industrialization:styrene_butadiene_rubber_bucket` *(after: Butadiene)*
   > What: styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) is the rubber in most tyres. Here it makes rubber sheets by the stack.
   > Chemistry: styrene and butadiene polymerise together into one chain (a copolymer): stiff styrene parts, springy butadiene parts.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: styrene + butadiene → styrene-butadiene, then polymerise with tiny lead or chromium dust. The Vacuum Freezer turns 200 mB into 64 rubber sheets.
   > Tip: keep a tank of liquid SBR: the RAM chips of the next chapter are printed with 500 mB each, and it makes cable far cheaper than rubber sheets.
25. **Diesel Toys**: `modern_industrialization:diesel_mining_drill`; `modern_industrialization:diesel_jetpack` *(after: Diesel Power)*
