   > What: MI's diesel drill and jetpack run on the fuel you just learned to blend.
   > How: check JEI for both recipes, then fill them from a tank.
   > Tip: the jetpack is loud and thirsty, but it flies. Real flight comes later.
26. **Fuel from Plants**: `modern_industrialization:biodiesel_bucket` *(after: Diesel Power)*
   > Chemistry: transesterification: plant oil + ethanol, with NaOH as catalyst, swaps the oil's glycerol backbone for ethyl groups. The result burns like diesel.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: plant oil + ethanol + sodium hydroxide → raw biodiesel, then wash it with steam (check JEI for plant oil).
   > Tip: Ad Astra rockets accept biodiesel too.
27. **Acrylic Glue**: `modern_industrialization:acrylic_acid_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:acrylic_glue_bucket` *(after: Propene)*
   > Chemistry: propene + oxygen → acrylic acid + water. Polymerised, it becomes a sticky acrylic: the same family as superabsorbent polymers.
   > How: Chemical Reactor for the acid, then polymerise with tiny lead or chromium dust.
   > Tip: the Chemical Reactor can turn acrylic glue into slime balls. No more slime farms.
28. **Nylon**: `modern_industrialization:caprolactam_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:nylon_bucket` *(after: Benzene Rings)*
   > Chemistry: benzene + hydrogen over nickel leads to caprolactam, a ring that opens up and polymerises into nylon-6.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: benzene + hydrogen + tiny nickel dust → caprolactam, then polymerise it.
   > Tip: 20 mB of nylon makes one string in the Chemical Reactor.
29. **A Mountain of Rubber**: 256x `modern_industrialization:rubber_sheet` *(after: Synthetic Rubber)*
   > How: keep the SBR line and Vacuum Freezer running until you have 256 sheets.
   > What: four full stacks of rubber sheets, made the modern way.
   > Tip: one bucket of SBR is five freezer runs, so a single bucket gets you there.
30. **Logic Gates**: 2x `modern_industrialization:op_amp`; `modern_industrialization:and_gate`; `modern_industrialization:or_gate`; `modern_industrialization:not_gate` *(after: Operational Amplifiers, Aluminum Cable)*
   > What: every digital circuit needs one AND, one OR and one NOT gate, and every gate starts with an operational amplifier.
   > Chemistry: a transistor is a switch with no moving parts. Wire a few together and they answer yes-or-no questions; wire millions and you have a computer.
   > How: Assembler. Op amp: 4 resistors, 4 transistors, 1 diode. AND: 2 resistors, 1 op amp, 4 aluminum wire. OR: 2 op amps, 2 aluminum wire, 1 diode. NOT: 1 resistor, 1 op amp, 1 aluminum wire.
   > Tip: set one Assembler per gate type. Digital circuits eat them by the dozen.
31. **The Distillery**: `modern_industrialization:distillery` *(after: Black Gold, Pumps, Large and Small)*
   > What: a single-block still that pulls one fraction out of a fluid per recipe. It's the refinery of this chapter; the full Distillation Tower needs EV parts.
   > Chemistry: a pot still works by boiling point too, but with only one stage it can't separate everything at once.
   > How: LV machine hull, 2 large pumps, 2 electronic circuits, glass, a fluid pipe and electrum cable.
   > Tip: JEI lists one Distillery recipe per fraction. Several Distilleries side by side, one per product, make a fine first refinery.
32. **Chromium and Manganese Ores**: 2x `modern_industrialization:chromium_crushed_dust`; 2x `modern_industrialization:manganese_crushed_dust` *(after: Ruby Dust, The Centrifuge)*
   > What: the raw material for the chromium and manganese leaching lines.
   > Chemistry: ruby is aluminium oxide coloured red by chromium, so it hides chromium. Iron ores usually carry a little manganese.
   > How: Centrifuge: 6 ruby dust → 1 chromium crushed dust + 2 aluminum dust (ruby dust comes from centrifuging redstone). Centrifuge: 6 raw iron → 8 iron dust + 1 manganese crushed dust.
33. **Hot and Cold Casings**: 4x `modern_industrialization:heatproof_machine_casing`; 4x `modern_industrialization:frostproof_machine_casing` *(after: Hot Ingots)*
   > What: heatproof casings wall in your Blast Furnace; frostproof casings wall in the Vacuum Freezer. The Heat Exchanger needs both.
   > Chemistry: invar (iron with 36% nickel) barely expands when heated. Aluminium stays tough in the cold, where steel turns brittle.
   > How: 8 invar plates + an invar gear, or 8 aluminum plates + an aluminum gear (Assembler or crafting table).
34. **Advanced Upgrades**: 4x `modern_industrialization:advanced_upgrade` *(after: Polymerisation)*
   > What: a bigger EU/t boost per slot than basic upgrades.
   > How: Assembler: 4 basic upgrades, 2 large motors, a large pump, an electronic circuit board and 1000 mB polyethylene → 4 advanced upgrades.
35. **Cracking Light Fuel**: `modern_industrialization:steam_cracked_light_fuel_bucket` *(after: Steam Cracking)*
   > What: light fuel can be steam-cracked too, and the cracked fuel distils into another mix of small molecules.
   > Chemistry: cracking breaks long chains into short ones. Refineries crack whatever fraction the market wants less of into what it wants more of.
   > How: steam + light fuel in the cracker (check JEI), then send it through the Distillation Tower.
36. **Butadiene**: `modern_industrialization:butadiene_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:styrene_butadiene_bucket` *(after: Styrene)*
   > What: butadiene (C₄H₆) is the second monomer of SBR rubber.
   > Chemistry: two double bonds make it springy once polymerised. Before oil, Soviet plants made it from ethanol (the Lebedev process); MI can too.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 750 mB ethanol + a tiny aluminum dust, or distil it out of cracked naphtha or cracked fuels (check JEI). Then styrene + butadiene → styrene-butadiene.
37. **Shale Oil**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_crude_oil_bucket` *(after: Sweetening the Oil, Stainless Steel)*
   > What: the Oil Drilling Rig, fed stainless steel drills instead of aluminum ones, brings up shale oil. Distilled, it gives sour (sulfuric) crude, sulfuric naphtha and a little helium.
   > Chemistry: sour crude is full of sulfur compounds. Hydrotreating strips them out with hydrogen, the same way your fuels are cleaned: 12 B sour crude + 2 B H₂ → 12 B crude oil + 2 B sulfuric acid.
   > Tip: real helium is mined from natural gas wells, where it collects from uranium decay. Keep this helium; you'll want it later.
38. **Processing Array**: `extended_industrialization:processing_array`; 2x `modern_industrialization:clean_stainless_steel_machine_casing` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: an Extended Industrialization multiblock that holds a stack of identical machines and runs them as one.
   > How: an Assembler, 4 robot arms, 2 digital circuits and 2 clean stainless steel casings (8 stainless plates + a stainless gear each). Check JEI for the layout and what it accepts.
   > Tip: one array of 16 macerators beats 16 macerators on cables.
39. **Aluminum Drills**: `modern_industrialization:aluminum_drill_head`; 4x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_drill` *(after: Pumps, Large and Small, Curved Aluminum)*
   > What: the Oil Drilling Rig wears through aluminum drills as it pumps.
   > How: drill head: an aluminum plate, 2 curved plates, a rod, 2 aluminum gears and bolts. Drill: the head, 2 iron gears, 2 fluid pipes, 2 pumps, an electrum cable and an electronic circuit → 4 drills.
   > Tip: each pumping cycle has only a small chance to break a drill, so four last a long time.
40. **Sour Light Fuel**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_light_fuel_bucket` *(after: The Distillery)*
   > What: the lightest liquid cut of crude, still carrying its sulfur.
   > Chemistry: light fuel is roughly C₅ to C₁₂: petrol and kerosene. Small molecules have weak forces between them, so they boil first.
   > How: Distillery: 1000 mB crude oil → 500 mB sulfuric light fuel.
41. **Sour Heavy Fuel**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_heavy_fuel_bucket` *(after: The Distillery)*
   > What: the heaviest cut: long chains that boil last.
   > Chemistry: long molecules tangle and attract each other more, so they need more heat to escape as vapour. That's why heavy fuel is thick and oily.
   > How: Distillery: 1000 mB crude oil → 200 mB sulfuric heavy fuel.
42. **Sour Naphtha**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_naphtha_bucket` *(after: The Distillery)*
   > What: naphtha is the feedstock of the whole plastics industry.
   > Chemistry: a mix of mid-sized alkanes and rings. Too big for gas, too small for diesel, just right to crack into ethylene.
   > How: Distillery: 1000 mB crude oil → 300 mB sulfuric naphtha.
43. **Tanks for Every Fraction**: 3x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_tank` *(after: The Distillery)*
   > What: aluminum tanks hold far more than bronze or steel ones.
   > How: check JEI. Put one on each Distillery output so a full tank never stalls the line.
   > Tip: label them. By the end of this chapter you'll have a dozen fluids.
44. **Methane**: `modern_industrialization:methane_bucket` *(after: Steam Cracking)*
   > What: natural gas. Next chapter it becomes acetylene, and acetylene becomes PVC.
   > Chemistry: one carbon, four hydrogens, arranged as a tetrahedron. It burns cleanly to CO₂ and water.
   > How: Distillery: 1000 mB steam-cracked naphtha → 150 mB methane. Store it; you'll want a few buckets.
45. **Propene**: `modern_industrialization:propene_bucket` *(after: Steam Cracking)*
   > What: propene (propylene, C₃H₆) is the second most important plastics monomer in the real world.
   > Chemistry: one more carbon than ethylene, with the same C=C double bond. Polymerised, it becomes polypropylene.
   > How: Distillery: 1000 mB steam-cracked naphtha → 75 mB propene.
46. **A Pinch of Catalyst**: 8x any of `or(item(modern_industrialization:lead_tiny_dust)item(modern_industrialization:chromium_tiny_dust))` *(after: Ethylene)*
   > What: MI polymerises with a tiny dust of metal: 4 tiny lead dust or 1 tiny chromium dust per 500 mB of monomer.
   > Chemistry: a catalyst speeds a reaction without being used up overall. Real polyethylene plants use chromium (Phillips) or titanium (Ziegler-Natta) catalysts.
   > How: craft 1 lead dust into 9 tiny dusts. Chromium gives more plastic per pinch once your stainless line runs.
47. **Pressurized Reaction Chamber**: `mekanism:pressurized_reaction_chamber` *(after: Dynamic Tanks, A Tank for Gas)*
   > What: the PRC reacts an item, a fluid and a gas together under pressure. It makes HDPE, substrate and, later, nuclear pellets.
   > How: an Enrichment Chamber, 2 basic control circuits, steel, infused alloy, 2 basic chemical tanks and a dynamic tank (check JEI).
   > Tip: MI ethylene counts as Mekanism ethene in this pack, so your Distillery feeds it directly.
48. **Ruby Dust**: 6x `modern_industrialization:ruby_dust` *(after: The Centrifuge)*
   > What: ruby dust is MI's chromium ore.
   > Chemistry: ruby is aluminium oxide with a trace of chromium. Cr³⁺ ions absorb green light, which is why the crystal looks red.
   > How: Centrifuge: 10 redstone → 5 iron dust, 1 ruby dust, 1 quartz dust and sometimes a tiny neodymium dust.
49. **Chromium Leach**: `modern_industrialization:chromium_hydrochloric_solution_bucket` *(after: Chromium and Manganese Ores, Hydrochloric Acid, MI Style)*
   > What: chromium chloride solution, ready for the Electrolyzer.
   > Chemistry: HCl dissolves the metal as chloride ions, leaving the rock behind. Electrolysis then plates the metal back out.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 chromium crushed dust + 9000 mB hydrochloric acid → 9000 mB solution.
50. **Manganese Leach**: `modern_industrialization:manganese_sulfuric_solution_bucket` *(after: Chromium and Manganese Ores, Sulfuric Acid)*
   > What: manganese sulfate solution. Most of the world's pure manganese is made by electrolysing exactly this.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 manganese crushed dust + 9000 mB sulfuric acid → 9000 mB solution.
   > Tip: the Electrolyzer gives most of the acid back, so the loop barely costs you any.
51. **Nickel**: 4x `modern_industrialization:nickel_dust` *(after: Electric Macerator)*
   > What: one of the four dusts in stainless steel, and the anode metal of the platinum line later.
   > Chemistry: nickel keeps stainless steel in its austenite structure at room temperature: tough, non-magnetic and easy to shape.
   > How: mine MI nickel ore and macerate the raw nickel.
52. **Aluminum Large Plates**: 2x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_large_plate` *(after: Aluminum Plates)*
   > What: the Vacuum Freezer takes two.
   > How: 4 aluminum plates in a square (crafting table or Packer).
53. **Stainless Plates**: 16x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_plate` *(after: Stainless Steel)*
   > What: digital circuit boards take 4, the Turbo casing 8, and air intakes, gears and rotors more.
   > How: Compressor: 1 stainless steel ingot → 1 plate.
54. **Aluminum Cable**: 6x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_wire`; 9x `modern_industrialization:aluminum_cable` *(after: Aluminum Plates, Rubber)*
   > What: aluminum cable carries HV power and goes into the digital circuit board, the sodium battery and the Turbo hull. Logic gates use bare aluminum wire.
   > Chemistry: aluminium conducts about 60% as well as copper but weighs a third as much. Real overhead power lines are aluminium for that reason.
   > How: Wiremill: 1 aluminum plate → 2 wire. 3 wire between 6 rubber sheets → 3 cable (or liquid SBR in the Assembler).
55. **Operational Amplifiers**: 4x `modern_industrialization:op_amp` *(after: Transistors and Diodes)*
   > What: every logic gate starts with an op amp.
   > Chemistry: an op amp multiplies the difference between two voltages enormously. Feed some of its output back and it can add, compare or switch.
   > How: 4 resistors, 4 transistors and 1 diode (crafting table or Assembler).
56. **Turbo Machine Casing**: `modern_industrialization:turbo_machine_casing` *(after: Stainless Plates, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the shell of the HV (Turbo) hull.
   > How: 8 stainless steel plates around an MV (advanced) machine hull.
57. **An HV Grid**: `modern_industrialization:mv_hv_transformer`; `modern_industrialization:hv_storage_unit` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: an MV-to-HV transformer and an HV storage unit.
   > How: check JEI for both. The storage unit is built on a Turbo hull with sodium batteries.
   > Tip: the Electric Blast Furnace and Vacuum Freezer pull a lot; give them an HV buffer.
58. **Certus Quartz**: 16x `ae2:certus_quartz_crystal` *(after: Fallen Stars)*
   > What: certus quartz becomes fluix, AE2's network crystal.
   > How: meteorites carry budding certus. Mine around it (not the budding block itself) and harvest the crystals that grow.
   > Tip: a Growth Accelerator next to budding certus speeds it up a lot (check JEI).
59. **Sky Stone**: 4x `ae2:smooth_sky_stone_block` *(after: Fallen Stars)*
   > What: the ME Controller is framed in 4 smooth sky stone blocks.
   > How: mine sky stone from the meteorite and smelt it.
60. **Processors**: 2x `ae2:logic_processor`; 2x `ae2:calculation_processor`; 2x `ae2:engineering_processor` *(after: The Inscriber)*
   > What: AE2's three processors. Storage cells use logic, crafting uses calculation, the controller and drives use engineering.
   > How: Inscriber: gold → printed logic circuit, certus → printed calculation circuit, diamond → printed engineering circuit, silicon → printed silicon. Then circuit + redstone + printed silicon → processor.
   > Tip: MI's Packer can also print silicon with a silicon press.
61. **Fluix Cable**: 16x `ae2:fluix_glass_cable` *(after: Fluix)*
   > What: ME cable joins the controller, drives and terminals into one network.
   > How: quartz fiber + 2 fluix → 4 glass cables (check JEI for quartz fiber).
62. **Pipe Casings**: 4x `modern_industrialization:steel_machine_casing_pipe` *(after: Casings for the LV Line)*
   > What: steel pipe machine casings form the shaft of the Oil Drilling Rig, around the drill string.
   > How: a steel machine casing wrapped in 6 steel curved plates gives 2 pipe casings (crafting table or Assembler).
   > Tip: place the rig's controller and hold a wrench: MI previews the whole structure in the world.
63. **Rig Hatches**: `modern_industrialization:steel_item_input_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:steel_fluid_output_hatch`; 1x any of `or(item(modern_industrialization:lv_energy_input_hatch)item(modern_industrialization:mv_energy_input_hatch))` *(after: MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: a multiblock talks to the world through hatches. The rig needs an item input (drills), a fluid output (crude) and an energy input.
   > How: steel hatches are a steel casing plus a chest or tank (check JEI). An energy input hatch is a machine hull plus a cable of its tier.
   > Tip: any casing slot of the structure can hold a hatch, so put them where your pipes already run.

### VII. Materials and Nuclear

*Purity and precision: semiconductors, PVC, isotopes. Then transmutation: any element from any other.*

1. **Argon from Air**: `modern_industrialization:argon_bucket` *(after: Liquid Air, The Centrifuge)*
   > You once stirred the sky. Now you pour it, liquid, into a tank.
   > What: argon is an inert blanket gas. Growing a silicon crystal in air would ruin it.
   > Chemistry: air is 78% N₂, 21% O₂ and about 0.9% argon. Cool it until it liquefies, then separate the parts.
   > How: the Vacuum Freezer (or Pressurizer) with an Air Intake makes liquid air. The Centrifuge splits it into oxygen, nitrogen and a little argon.
   > Tip: the Heat Exchanger gives far more argon while it cools hot ingots.
2. **Semiconductor Silicon**: 8x `modern_industrialization:silicon_wafer` *(after: A Perfect Crystal)*
   > What: computer chips need silicon purer than 99.9999999%, grown as one single crystal.
   > Chemistry: a seed crystal is pulled slowly out of molten silicon (the Czochralski process). Every atom lines up with the one below it.
   > How: Cutting Machine: 1 monocrystalline silicon + 500 mB lubricant → 32 wafers.
   > Tip: one boule is 32 wafers: enough for a long run of RAM and MMUs.
3. **Chips**: 2x `modern_industrialization:random_access_memory`; `modern_industrialization:arithmetic_logic_unit`; `modern_industrialization:memory_management_unit` *(after: RAM, Arithmetic Logic Unit, Memory Management Unit)*
   > What: a processing unit needs RAM, an ALU and an MMU.
   > Chemistry: a pinch of aluminum (p-type) or phosphorus (n-type) in silicon changes how it carries current. That's 'doping', the basis of every transistor.
   > How: one of each, made in the quests around this one. The processing unit takes 2 RAM, 1 ALU and 1 MMU.
4. **Acetylene**: `modern_industrialization:acetylene_bucket` *(after: Methane, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: acetylene (C₂H₂) has a triple bond, which makes it very reactive.
   > Chemistry: heat methane hard enough and pairs of molecules lose hydrogen and join: 2CH₄ → C₂H₂ + 3H₂.
   > How: Electric Blast Furnace: 200 mB methane → 200 mB acetylene. Cracked naphtha also gives a little.
5. **Vinyl Chloride**: `modern_industrialization:vinyl_chloride_bucket` *(after: Acetylene, Hydrochloric Acid, MI Style)*
   > Chemistry: C₂H₂ + HCl → C₂H₃Cl. HCl adds across the triple bond. This was the original industrial route to PVC.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 B acetylene + 1 B hydrochloric acid → 1 B vinyl chloride.
   > Tip: your salt line's chlorine and hydrogen make the HCl.
6. **PVC**: `modern_industrialization:polyvinyl_chloride_bucket` *(after: Vinyl Chloride, A Pinch of Catalyst)*
   > What: polyvinyl chloride, (C₂H₃Cl)ₙ, is tough, fire-resistant and insulates EV circuit boards.
   > Chemistry: just like polyethylene, but every other carbon carries a chlorine atom. That's why PVC doesn't burn easily.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 500 mB vinyl chloride + 4 tiny lead or chromium dust → 300 mB PVC.
7. **Cadmium Battery**: 4x `modern_industrialization:cadmium_dust`; 2x `modern_industrialization:cadmium_battery` *(after: Monazite, Annealed Copper Cable)*
   > What: the EV hull and processing unit board each need 2 cadmium batteries.
   > Chemistry: a NiCd cell runs Cd + 2NiO(OH) + 2H₂O → Cd(OH)₂ + 2Ni(OH)₂, and it can be recharged by running it backwards.
   > How: Centrifuge: 9 monazite dust → 3 cadmium dust (plus neodymium, yttrium and helium). Battery: 2 cadmium dust, a battery alloy plate, 4 curved plates and 2 annealed copper cable. In reality cadmium is mostly a by-product of zinc refining.
   > Tip: cadmium is toxic in real life. Here it just needs a lot of monazite.
8. **Processing Unit Board**: `modern_industrialization:processing_unit_board` *(after: PVC, Cadmium Battery, Platinum Plates)*
   > How: Assembler: digital circuit board + 4 platinum plates + 2 cadmium batteries + 8 annealed copper cable + 1500 mB PVC.
   > Chemistry: platinum never corrodes, so it makes contacts that last forever.
   > Tip: platinum comes from MI's ore processing or the Platinum Line below (check JEI).
9. **EV: Processing Units**: `modern_industrialization:processing_unit`; `modern_industrialization:highly_advanced_machine_hull` *(after: Processing Unit Board, Chips, Highly Advanced Casing)*
   > A mind of silicon, insulated in salt and oil. It thinks the way you used to.
   > What: processing units unlock EV machines, the NASA Workbench, Flux Networks and Alchemistry's chambers.
   > How: Assembler: processing unit board + 4 digital circuits + 2 RAM + ALU + MMU. The EV hull is a highly advanced casing + a processing unit + 2 cadmium batteries + 3 annealed copper cable.
10. **Yellowcake**: 4x `mekanism:yellow_cake_uranium` *(after: EV: Processing Units, Uranium Ingots)*
   > What: yellowcake is concentrated uranium oxide powder, the raw material of nuclear fuel.
   > Chemistry: natural uranium is only 0.72% U-235, the isotope that splits. The rest is U-238.
   > How: Enrichment Chamber: 1 uranium ingot → 2 yellowcake. Then the Chemical Oxidizer turns it into uranium oxide gas.
   > Tip: a Geiger counter tells you when you're standing too close to anything radioactive.
11. **Hydrofluoric Acid**: 16x `mekanism:fluorite_gem` *(after: EV: Processing Units, Fluorite)*
   > Chemistry: CaF₂ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + 2HF. Hydrogen fluoride dissolves glass and is one of the most dangerous acids there is.
   > How: Chemical Dissolution Chamber: fluorite + sulfuric acid → hydrofluoric acid gas.
   > Tip: fluorite ore sits deep. Mystical Agriculture and Occultism can't make it in this pack. Keep extra HF: the Seed of a New World needs 4 buckets (a Rotary Condensentrator in liquid mode turns the gas into fluid).
12. **Uranium Hexafluoride**: `mekanism:chemical_infuser`; `mekanism:chemical_oxidizer` *(after: Yellowcake, Hydrofluoric Acid)*
   > What: UF₆ is the only uranium compound that becomes a gas at low temperature (it sublimes at 56 °C), so it can be spun.
   > Chemistry: real plants go UO₂ → UF₄ → UF₆ with HF and then fluorine. Mekanism combines the steps.
   > How: Chemical Infuser: uranium oxide + hydrofluoric acid → uranium hexafluoride.
13. **Isotope Separation**: `mekanism:isotopic_centrifuge` *(after: Uranium Hexafluoride, Ultimate Control Circuits)*
   > What: the two isotopes behave identically in every reaction, so chemistry can't separate them.
   > Chemistry: U-235 is about 1% lighter. Spin UF₆ fast enough and the heavier molecules drift outward.
   > How: Isotopic Centrifuge (6 lead ingots, 2 ultimate control circuits, a chemical tank): uranium hexafluoride → fissile fuel.
14. **Reactor Parts**: 4x `mekanismgenerators:fission_fuel_assembly`; `mekanismgenerators:control_rod_assembly`; 4x `mekanismgenerators:fission_reactor_port` *(after: Isotope Separation)*
   > What: fuel assemblies hold the fuel, control rods absorb neutrons, and ports move fuel, coolant and waste.
   > Chemistry: each split releases 2 to 3 neutrons. Absorb too few and the chain reaction runs away.
   > How: check JEI for each part. Plan for water or sodium coolant and somewhere for the steam to go.
15. **Fission**: 16x `mekanismgenerators:fission_reactor_casing` *(after: Reactor Parts)*
   > What: split heavy nuclei and release enormous energy. Mind the temperature, and the waste.
   > Chemistry: U-235 + n → two lighter nuclei + 2-3 n + about 200 MeV, millions of times more than any chemical bond.
   > How: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks shows the layout in JEI. Pair it with a turbine (see Power).
   > Tip: wire a Logic Adapter to SCRAM the reactor if it overheats.
16. **Plutonium**: `mekanism:pellet_plutonium` *(after: Fission, Fluorite Dust)*
   > Chemistry: U-238 captures a neutron and beta-decays twice into Pu-239, which is itself fissile.
   > How: Isotopic Centrifuge: 10 nuclear waste → 1 plutonium. Pressurized Reaction Chamber: plutonium + fluorite dust + water → pellet.
   > Tip: the pellet reaction also gives spent nuclear waste. Store it in a Radioactive Waste Barrel.
17. **Polonium**: `mekanism:pellet_polonium` *(after: Fission, Solar Neutron Activator, Fluorite Dust)*
   > Chemistry: polonium-210 is made by neutron capture; it is intensely radioactive and gives off heat on its own.
   > How: Solar Neutron Activator (open sky, daylight): 10 nuclear waste → 1 polonium. Pellets come from the Pressurized Reaction Chamber, as with plutonium.
   > Tip: polonium is the input for the SPS and for Energy Cores.
18. **Transmutation by Neutron**: `mekanism:pellet_plutonium`; `mekanism:pellet_polonium` *(after: Plutonium, Polonium)*
   > The old alchemists wanted to change one element into another. You do it before breakfast.
   > What: reprocessing nuclear waste gives plutonium and polonium, two elements that barely exist in nature.
   > How: keep both pellet lines running. Plutonium feeds the quantum tier; polonium feeds antimatter.
   > Tip: spent waste still goes in a Radioactive Waste Barrel. Never dump it.
19. **Chamber Frame**: 16x `alchemistry:reactor_casing`; `alchemistry:reactor_energy`; `alchemistry:reactor_input`; `alchemistry:reactor_output` *(after: EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: Alchemistry's fission and fusion chambers share the same casing, energy, input and output blocks.
   > How: craft the frame blocks (check JEI) and build the chamber around its controller. The controllers themselves are crafted with a reactor casing.
   > Tip: build both chambers side by side so one can feed the other.
20. **Element Transmutation**: `alchemistry:fission_chamber_controller`; `alchemistry:fusion_chamber_controller` *(after: A Nether Star)*
   > What: the fission chamber splits one element into two lighter ones; the fusion chamber merges two into a heavier one.
   > Chemistry: atomic numbers simply add or divide: fuse sodium (11) with chlorine (17) and you get nickel (28).
   > How: both controllers need a processing unit; fusion also needs a Nether Star.
   > Tip: with both, every element is within reach.
21. **The Complete Periodic Table**: 16x `chemlib:uranium`; `chemlib:oganesson` *(after: Element Transmutation)*
   > Oganesson. It barely exists in reality, but you made one.
   > What: the heaviest element on the table, made by fusing lighter ones.
   > Chemistry: real oganesson has been made only a handful of times, and each atom lasted under a millisecond.
   > How: fuse your way up in the Fusion Chamber (check JEI for which pairs reach 118).
   > Every block in this world can now be built from chemicals. You're close to what you once were.
22. **Wireless Power**: `fluxnetworks:flux_core` *(after: EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: Flux Networks moves energy anywhere in a dimension, or across them.
   > How: the Flux Core needs a processing unit in this pack. Add plugs at sources and points at machines.
   > Tip: set a password on your network if you share a server.
23. **Haber-Bosch**: `chemlib:ammonia_bucket` *(after: The Rest of the Air, Hydrogen and Oxygen, MI Style)*
   > Feeding a world used to take a harvest god. Now it takes a reactor and some hydrogen.
   > What: ammonia is the root of fertiliser, nitric acid and ammonium salts.
   > Chemistry: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. Breaking nitrogen's triple bond is hard; this process feeds about half the world through fertiliser.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 B nitrogen + 3 B hydrogen → 2 B ammonia. Fill a bucket from the output tank.
24. **Ostwald Process**: `chemlib:nitric_acid_bucket` *(after: Haber-Bosch)*
   > Chemistry: NH₃ + 2O₂ → HNO₃ + H₂O. Real plants burn ammonia over a platinum gauze, the very metal you're about to extract with it.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 B ammonia + 2 B oxygen → 1 B nitric acid + 1 B water.
   > Tip: the water by-product can go back into your electrolysis line.
25. **Anode Sludge**: 4x `kubejs:pgm_sludge` *(after: Ostwald Process)*
   > What: refining nickel and copper electrically leaves a sludge rich in platinum-group metals.
   > Chemistry: noble metals don't dissolve at the anode, so they fall to the bottom of the cell.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 4 nickel or copper dust → 4 dust back + PGM sludge (25% chance).
   > Tip: it costs you nothing but power. Leave it running.
26. **Ammonium Chloride**: 4x `chemlib:ammonium_chloride_dust` *(after: Haber-Bosch)*
   > Chemistry: NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl. Open bottles of each near one another and a white smoke of this salt forms in the air.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 B ammonia + 1 B hydrochloric acid → 1 ammonium chloride.
   > Tip: you need 2 per precipitation, so make plenty.
27. **Aqua Regia**: 2x `kubejs:chloroplatinic_acid`; `kubejs:pgm_residue` *(after: Anode Sludge)*
   > Chemistry: 3 HCl : 1 HNO₃. Nitric acid oxidises the platinum and chloride grabs the ions, forming chloroplatinic acid, H₂PtCl₆.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 4 PGM sludge + 3 B HCl + 1 B nitric acid → 2 chloroplatinic acid + 1 PGM residue.
   > Tip: iridium, osmium, rhodium and ruthenium don't dissolve. Keep the residue.
28. **Precipitation**: 2x `kubejs:ammonium_hexachloroplatinate` *(after: Aqua Regia, Ammonium Chloride)*
   > Chemistry: ammonium chloride makes the platinum fall out as yellow ammonium hexachloroplatinate, (NH₄)₂PtCl₆.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 chloroplatinic acid + 2 ammonium chloride → 1 ammonium hexachloroplatinate.
   > Tip: this step is why real platinum refining needs both the Haber-Bosch and Ostwald plants.
29. **The Platinum Line**: 4x `modern_industrialization:platinum_dust` *(after: Precipitation)*
   > Metals that never tarnish. You used to think it was pride; now you know they simply refuse to react.
   > Chemistry: heating (calcining) drives off ammonia and HCl and leaves pure platinum metal.
   > How: Electric Blast Furnace: 2 ammonium hexachloroplatinate → 1 platinum dust.
   > Tip: processing unit boards need 4 platinum plates each. Automate this line.
30. **The Rare Four**: `modern_industrialization:iridium_dust`; `mekanism:dust_osmium`; `chemlib:rhodium_dust`; `chemlib:ruthenium_dust` *(after: The Platinum Line)*
   > What: the insoluble residue holds the rarest metals on Earth.
   > Chemistry: osmium is the densest element known, and iridium the most corrosion-resistant metal.
   > How: Centrifuge the PGM residue. Each output is a chance, so run plenty.
   > Tip: iridium is needed for monocrystalline silicon and, later, quantum circuit boards.
31. **Dress for the Job**: `mekanism:hazmat_mask`; `mekanism:hazmat_gown`; `mekanism:hazmat_pants`; `mekanism:hazmat_boots`; `mekanism:geiger_counter` *(after: Isotope Separation)*
   > How: check JEI for each piece.
   > What: a full hazmat suit blocks radiation; the Geiger counter shows how much is around you.
   > Tip: a leaking waste pipe can make an area dangerous for a long time. Check before you build.
32. **Closing the Fuel Cycle**: 4x `mekanism:reprocessed_fissile_fragment` *(after: Plutonium)*
   > Chemistry: plutonium-239 is fissile, so spent fuel can be recycled into new fuel, as some real reactors do.
   > How: Chemical Injection Chamber: plutonium pellet + hydrogen chloride → 4 fragments. Oxidize them into fissile fuel.
   > Tip: it means less waste and more fuel from every uranium ingot.
33. **The Unstable Ones**: `chemlib:technetium`; `chemlib:promethium`; `chemlib:astatine`; `chemlib:francium` *(after: Element Transmutation)*
   > What: four elements that real chemists almost never get to hold.
   > Chemistry: technetium (43) and promethium (61) are the only light elements with no stable isotope. Astatine and francium are the rarest natural elements: grams exist in the whole crust.
   > How: fuse or split your way to each atomic number (check JEI).
34. **Platinum Reserve**: 32x `modern_industrialization:platinum_ingot` *(after: The Platinum Line)*
   > How: keep the Platinum Line running, then smelt the dust.
   > What: half a stack of platinum ingots, all pulled out of sludge.
   > Tip: every processing unit board eats 4 platinum plates. You'll be glad of the reserve.
35. **Kanthal**: 3x `modern_industrialization:kanthal_dust`; `modern_industrialization:kanthal_hot_ingot`; 4x `modern_industrialization:kanthal_ingot` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: Kanthal is the wire inside toasters and kilns. Coiled around your Blast Furnace it reaches recipes cupronickel can't.
   > Chemistry: FeCrAl alloy. When hot, its aluminium forms a thin skin of alumina (Al₂O₃) that stops the wire burning away, even near 1400 °C.
   > How: Mixer: 1 stainless steel + 1 chromium + 1 aluminum dust → 3 Kanthal dust. EBF → hot ingot, then the Vacuum Freezer.
36. **A Hotter Furnace**: 16x `modern_industrialization:kanthal_coil` *(after: Kanthal Cable)*
   > What: an Electric Blast Furnace built with Kanthal coils unlocks a new set of recipes. JEI lists them under 'EBF (Kanthal Tier)'.
   > How: each coil is 8 Kanthal cables (crafting table or Assembler). The EBF's two coil rings take 16.
   > Tip: keep your old cupronickel furnace running too: cheap recipes don't need the upgrade.
37. **Annealed Copper**: 8x `modern_industrialization:annealed_copper_ingot` *(after: A Hotter Furnace)*
   > What: annealed copper cable goes into cadmium batteries, the processing unit board and every stainless motor.
   > Chemistry: annealing heats a metal and lets it cool slowly, so its crystals regrow without strain. Soft, fully annealed copper conducts best of all and is the standard (100% IACS) that other conductors are measured against.
   > How: Kanthal-tier EBF: copper dust + 250 mB oxygen → annealed copper hot ingot, then the Vacuum Freezer.
38. **Titanium**: `modern_industrialization:titanium_hot_ingot`; 8x `modern_industrialization:titanium_ingot` *(after: A Hotter Furnace)*
   > What: titanium builds the toughest MI machines: the Implosion Compressor, the Pressurizer and their casings.
   > Chemistry: titanium grabs oxygen and nitrogen when hot, so real plants reduce TiCl₄ with molten magnesium under argon (the Kroll process). Here the EBF does it in one step.
   > How: MI titanium ore needs an iron pick; macerate it to dust (bauxite digestion leaves tiny titanium too). Kanthal-tier EBF → hot ingot → Vacuum Freezer.
39. **The Rest of the Air**: `modern_industrialization:nitrogen_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:oxygen_bucket` *(after: Liquid Air, The Centrifuge)*
   > What: the liquid air you split for argon is mostly nitrogen and oxygen. Nitrogen goes into explosives; oxygen into almost everything.
   > Chemistry: nitrogen boils at −196 °C, oxygen at −183 °C and argon in between. Real air-separation plants distil liquid air exactly along those steps.
   > How: Centrifuge: 3000 mB liquid air → 2315 nitrogen + 650 oxygen + 35 argon.
40. **Industrial TNT**: 8x `modern_industrialization:industrial_tnt` *(after: The Rest of the Air, Benzene Rings)*
   > What: Industrial TNT drives the Implosion Compressor, the only way to press the hardest alloys.
   > Chemistry: real TNT is 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene: toluene with three nitro groups, made with nitric and sulfuric acid. It's stable enough to melt and cast, which is why it was used so widely.
   > How: Mixer: 4 sand + 3 flint + 250 mB toluene (from cracked naphtha) + 1000 mB nitrogen → 4 Industrial TNT.
41. **Tungsten**: 9x `modern_industrialization:tungsten_tiny_dust`; 9x `modern_industrialization:tungsten_nugget`; `modern_industrialization:tungsten_ingot` *(after: Kanthal)*
   > What: tungsten goes into blastproof alloy and, much later, the ultradense metal ball.
   > Chemistry: tungsten melts at 3422 °C, so no furnace casts it. Real tungsten parts are pressed from powder and sintered: powder metallurgy.
   > How: tungsten ore (iron pick, deep) → dust → tiny dust. Compressor: 1 tiny dust → 1 nugget (slow). Once you have an Implosion Compressor: 9 tiny dust + a stainless nugget + Industrial TNT → 1 ingot.
42. **Stainless Motors**: 2x `modern_industrialization:advanced_motor`; `modern_industrialization:advanced_pump` *(after: Annealed Copper Cable, Magnetic Stainless Rods, Stainless Rotors, Aluminum Cable)*
   > What: advanced motors and pumps run the Implosion Compressor, the heat exchangers and the best upgrades.
   > How: advanced motor: a magnetic stainless rod, 2 stainless rods, 2 aluminum cable, 4 annealed copper wire. Advanced pump: advanced motor, 2 stainless rotors, fluid pipes and stainless bolts.
   > Tip: advanced pumps also build the Distillation Tower, the EV refinery.
43. **Blastproof Alloy**: 2x `modern_industrialization:mixed_ingot_blastproof`; 4x `modern_industrialization:blastproof_alloy_plate` *(after: Titanium, Tungsten)*
   > What: the armour of the Implosion Compressor and every nuclear fuel rod.
   > Chemistry: tungsten for heat, titanium for lightness, stainless for toughness: a composite does what no single metal can.
   > How: Packer: 1 tungsten + 1 titanium + 1 stainless steel ingot → mixed blastproof ingot. Compressor: 2 mixed ingots → 1 plate (slow). With an Implosion Compressor: 1 mixed ingot + TNT → 3 ingots.
   > Tip: the Compressor route is only for your first compressor's 16 plates. After that, use the bang.
44. **The Implosion Compressor**: `modern_industrialization:implosion_compressor`; 4x `modern_industrialization:blastproof_casing` *(after: Blastproof Alloy, Stainless Motors, Industrial TNT, Titanium Plates)*
   > What: a multiblock that uses Industrial TNT to press tungsten, blastproof alloy, beryllium and nuclear alloy.
   > Chemistry: explosive compaction is real: a shockwave can squeeze powder past what any press reaches. Explosions even make tiny diamonds from graphite.
   > How: controller: 2 advanced motors, 2 titanium large plates, an HV hull and 4 blastproof large plates. Blastproof casings (8 plates each) form the walls; layout in JEI and the MI guidebook.
45. **Beryllium**: 3x `modern_industrialization:beryllium_dust`; 2x `modern_industrialization:beryllium_plate` *(after: The Implosion Compressor)*
   > What: beryllium is one third of nuclear alloy.
   > Chemistry: emerald is the mineral beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈. Beryllium is light, stiff and reflects neutrons back into a reactor core.
   > How: Electrolyzer: 23 emerald dust → 3 beryllium + 2 aluminum + 6 silicon dust + oxygen. Implosion Compressor: 9 tiny beryllium dust + a stainless nugget + TNT → 1 ingot. Compress it into plates.
46. **Rare Earths and Helium**: 3x `modern_industrialization:neodymium_dust`; 3x `modern_industrialization:yttrium_dust`; `modern_industrialization:helium_bucket` *(after: Monazite)*
   > What: the same centrifuge run that gives cadmium also gives neodymium, yttrium and sometimes helium. You'll need all three for superconductors and fuel rods.
   > Chemistry: monazite is a rare-earth phosphate, (Ce,La,Nd,Th)PO₄. Its thorium slowly decays and the alpha particles it fires become helium atoms trapped in the crystal.
   > How: Centrifuge: 9 monazite dust → 3 neodymium + 3 yttrium + 3 cadmium dust, plus 300 mB helium half the time.
   > Tip: helium also comes from centrifuging uranium, distilling shale oil, and cooling hot ingots in the Heat Exchanger.
47. **Soldering Alloy**: 8x `modern_industrialization:soldering_alloy_dust` *(after: Kanthal)*
   > What: molten solder seals every MI fuel rod and control rod.
   > Chemistry: tin and lead together melt lower than either alone (a eutectic, about 183 °C), so solder flows into joints without melting the parts.
   > How: Mixer: 1 tin dust + 1 lead dust → 2 solder dust. The EBF melts 1 dust into 90 mB of liquid solder.
48. **Nuclear Alloy**: `modern_industrialization:mixed_plate_nuclear`; 6x `modern_industrialization:nuclear_alloy_plate`; `modern_industrialization:nuclear_alloy_large_plate` *(after: Beryllium, Cadmium Battery)*
   > What: the metal the MI Nuclear Reactor is built from.
   > Chemistry: a reactor wall must survive heat and handle neutrons: beryllium reflects them, cadmium absorbs them, blastproof alloy holds it all together.
   > How: Packer: blastproof plate + beryllium plate + cadmium plate → mixed nuclear plate. Implosion Compressor with TNT → 3 nuclear alloy plates. Four plates make a large plate.
49. **Control Rods**: 2x `modern_industrialization:cadmium_control_rod` *(after: Blastproof Alloy, Soldering Alloy, Rare Earths and Helium, Cadmium Rods)*
   > What: cadmium control rods soak up neutrons. The reactor controller needs two, and they tame a hot core.
   > Chemistry: cadmium-113 swallows slow neutrons more readily than almost any other nucleus, so a little cadmium stops a chain reaction from running away.
   > How: Assembler: 18 cadmium rods, 2 blastproof curved plates, a large motor, 2 robot arms, 500 mB solder and 100 mB helium.
50. **Reactor Shell**: 4x `modern_industrialization:nuclear_casing`; `modern_industrialization:nuclear_item_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:nuclear_fluid_hatch`; `modern_industrialization:nuclear_alloy_machine_casing_pipe` *(after: Nuclear Alloy, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: the walls and the top grid of the reactor. Item hatches hold fuel and rods; fluid hatches hold water to boil into steam.
   > How: nuclear casing: 8 nuclear alloy plates around an HV hull. Hatches: 8 plates around an EV item or fluid input hatch. Check JEI for the pipe casing.
   > Tip: the reactor comes in several sizes. Start small; the MI guidebook shows them all.
51. **Fuel Rods**: 2x `modern_industrialization:uranium_fuel_rod`; `modern_industrialization:uranium_fuel_rod_double` *(after: Soldering Alloy, Nuclear Alloy, Uranium Rods)*
   > What: plain uranium fuel rods need no enrichment. They burn slowly, and that slowness breeds plutonium.
   > Chemistry: natural uranium is 99.3% U-238 and 0.7% fissile U-235. U-238 catches a neutron and decays twice: ²³⁸U → ²³⁹U → ²³⁹Np → ²³⁹Pu.
   > How: 18 uranium rods (see Uranium Rods). Assembler: 18 uranium rods, 2 blastproof curved plates, a large motor, 2 robot arms, 500 mB solder, 100 mB helium. Packer: 2 rods + a nuclear alloy plate → double rod.
52. **The Nuclear Reactor**: `modern_industrialization:nuclear_reactor` *(after: Reactor Shell, Control Rods)*
   > What: a big power source, and the only place in the pack that makes MI plutonium. Quantum circuits need it.
   > How: Assembler: 4 nuclear alloy large plates, an EV hull, 2 processing units, 2 cadmium control rods. Put water in fluid hatches and fuel in item hatches; JEI shows each part's heat and neutron numbers.
   > Tip: it can't explode or irradiate anything. Too much heat only destroys what's inside the hatches. Experiment freely.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: fast and slow neutrons
   > Fission releases fast neutrons. Fuel catches slow ones far better, so reactors use a moderator (water, heavy water, graphite) to slow them down by collisions.
   > MI models both kinds. Neutrons that escape the edge are lost; ones that hit a hatch can scatter, slow down, or be absorbed. Read the reactor's GUI as a map of where neutrons go.
53. **Bred Plutonium**: `modern_industrialization:uranium_fuel_rod_depleted`; 9x `modern_industrialization:plutonium_tiny_dust`; 2x `modern_industrialization:plutonium_dust` *(after: The Nuclear Reactor, Fuel Rods)*
   > Uranium in, plutonium out. You are keeping a forge for elements now.
   > What: MI plutonium dust, the heart of the plutonium battery and so of every quantum circuit.
   > How: burn uranium fuel rods until they're depleted. Centrifuge one depleted rod → 53 tiny U-238 dust + 27 tiny plutonium dust (3 full dusts) and sometimes a tiny U-235.
   > Tip: this is MI plutonium, not Mekanism's pellets. You need both: pellets for the Seed, dust for quantum circuits.
54. **Small Heat Exchanger**: 2x `modern_industrialization:small_heat_exchanger` *(after: Stainless Motors)*
   > What: a component for cooling cells (quantum circuits need them) and for the Heat Exchanger multiblock.
   > Chemistry: a heat exchanger lets a hot fluid warm a cold one through a thin wall. Every power station and refrigerator relies on one.
   > How: Assembler: 4 invar plates, a stainless large plate and 4 advanced pumps.
55. **Titanium Casings**: 4x `modern_industrialization:solid_titanium_machine_casing`; 2x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_machine_casing_pipe` *(after: Titanium)*
   > What: solid titanium casings wall in the Pressurizer and the high-pressure boilers; stainless pipe casings carry fluids through the Heat Exchanger.
   > How: 8 titanium plates + a titanium gear per casing (Assembler). Check JEI (press U on a casing) for the multiblocks that use each.
56. **The Heat Exchanger**: `modern_industrialization:heat_exchanger` *(after: Small Heat Exchanger, Titanium Casings)*
   > What: a multiblock that cools hot ingots with cryofluid (giving back argon and helium) and recycles high-pressure water and steam.
   > How: Assembler: 2 small heat exchangers, an HV hull, 2 stainless pipe casings, 2 frostproof and 2 heatproof casings. Layout in JEI.
   > Tip: each ingot cooled this way returns 13 mB argon and 5 mB helium. It adds up.
57. **Heavy Water**: `modern_industrialization:deuterium_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:heavy_water_bucket` *(after: The Nuclear Reactor)*
   > What: deuterium is hydrogen with one extra neutron; heavy water is D₂O. Both feed fusion, and heavy water is a reactor coolant.
   > Chemistry: about 1 hydrogen atom in 6400 is deuterium. Heavy water is 11% denser than normal water, and ice made from it sinks.
   > How: Centrifuge: 1000 mB hydrogen → 20 mB deuterium + 1 mB tritium, or 1000 mB water → 20 mB heavy water. Chemical Reactor: 2000 deuterium + 1000 oxygen → 3000 heavy water.
58. **Uranium Isotopes**: `modern_industrialization:uranium_235_tiny_dust`; 16x `modern_industrialization:uranium_238_tiny_dust` *(after: The Nuclear Reactor)*
   > What: MI's own isotope split, for enriched fuel.
   > Chemistry: U-235 and U-238 differ by three neutrons, about 1% in mass. Spinning them hard is still how most enrichment is done.
   > How: Centrifuge: 9 uranium dust → 1 tiny U-235 + 80 tiny U-238 (and sometimes helium). Very slow; depleted rods give more.
59. **Enriched Uranium**: `modern_industrialization:le_uranium_dust`; `modern_industrialization:he_uranium_dust` *(after: Uranium Isotopes)*
   > What: enriched fuel burns hotter and makes more neutrons than natural uranium.
   > How: Mixer: 8 U-238 + 1 U-235 dust → 9 LE uranium dust; 6 U-238 + 3 U-235 → 9 HE uranium dust. Then rods and fuel rods as before.
   > Tip: more neutrons also means more heat. Add control rods before you add HE fuel.
60. **MOX Fuel**: `modern_industrialization:le_mox_dust`; `modern_industrialization:he_mox_dust` *(after: Enriched Uranium, Bred Plutonium)*
   > What: mixed-oxide fuel uses plutonium in place of U-235.
   > Chemistry: real MOX mixes PuO₂ into UO₂. France recycles spent fuel into MOX, getting more energy from the same mined uranium.
   > How: Mixer: 8 U-238 + 1 plutonium dust → 9 LE MOX; 6 U-238 + 3 plutonium → 9 HE MOX.
61. **Better Fuel Rods**: 1x any of `or(item(modern_industrialization:le_uranium_fuel_rod_double)item(modern_industrialization:he_uranium_fuel_rod_double)item(modern_industrialization:le_mox_fuel_rod_double)item(modern_industrialization:he_mox_fuel_rod_double))` *(after: Enriched Uranium)*
   > What: any double fuel rod made from LE or HE uranium, or from LE or HE MOX.
   > How: the same Assembler recipe as plain fuel rods, with the enriched rods instead. Packer: 2 rods + a nuclear alloy plate → double.
62. **Spent Fuel**: 1x any of `or(item(modern_industrialization:le_uranium_fuel_rod_depleted)item(modern_industrialization:he_uranium_fuel_rod_depleted)item(modern_industrialization:le_mox_fuel_rod_depleted)item(modern_industrialization:he_mox_fuel_rod_depleted))` *(after: Better Fuel Rods)*
   > What: a depleted enriched or MOX rod, ready for the Centrifuge.
   > How: centrifuging it returns U-238 and plutonium (and U-235 from uranium fuel). HE MOX gives the most plutonium back.
   > Tip: this closes the loop: uranium in, plutonium out, plutonium back in as MOX.
63. **Turbo Upgrades**: 4x `modern_industrialization:turbo_upgrade` *(after: Stainless Motors, PVC)*
   > How: Assembler: 16 advanced motors, 2 advanced pumps, 4 advanced upgrades, a digital circuit board and 1000 mB PVC → 4 turbo upgrades.
   > Tip: one turbo upgrade in a multiblock lets the hungriest recipes run.
64. **Large Advanced Motors**: `modern_industrialization:large_advanced_motor`; `modern_industrialization:large_advanced_pump` *(after: Stainless Motors, EV: Processing Units)*
   > How: large advanced motor: a processing unit, 2 titanium rods, 6 advanced motors. Large advanced pump: 2 processing units, 3 titanium rotors, a large advanced motor and 3 advanced pumps.
   > Tip: they go into highly advanced upgrades and the biggest pumps and machines.
65. **Highly Advanced Upgrades**: 4x `modern_industrialization:highly_advanced_upgrade` *(after: Turbo Upgrades, Large Advanced Motors)*
   > How: Assembler: 8 large advanced motors, 4 large advanced pumps, 4 turbo upgrades, a processing unit board and 2500 mB PVC → 4.
   > Tip: the Quantum Upgrade, after the Seed, needs 32 of these.
66. **Fractional Distillation**: `modern_industrialization:distillation_tower` *(after: Stainless Motors, The Distillery)*
   > What: the Distillation Tower is a multiblock that splits one fluid into several fractions at once.
   > Chemistry: heat the crude and each fraction boils off at its own temperature. Light molecules rise to the top, heavy ones stay low.
   > How: controller: 4 advanced pumps, 2 Distilleries, 2 digital circuits and a Turbo hull. The layout is in JEI. Each extra layer adds one more output, up to eight.
   > Tip: one tower replaces a whole row of Distilleries: steam-cracked naphtha gives methane, acetylene, ethylene, propene, butadiene, benzene, toluene and ethylbenzene in one pass.
67. **Stainless Rotors**: 3x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_rotor` *(after: Stainless Plates)*
   > What: the air intake spins one; every advanced pump spins three.
   > How: blades: 2 stainless curved plates + 1 stainless rod → 4 blades. Ring: Compressor, 1 rod → 1 ring. Rotor: 4 blades, 4 bolts and a ring on a crafting table.
   > Tip: the Assembler recipe needs soldering alloy; craft by hand until your solder line runs.
68. **Air Intake**: `modern_industrialization:air_intake` *(after: Stainless Rotors)*
   > What: the Air Intake sits in the Vacuum Freezer or Pressurizer and lets it pull in air to liquefy. It isn't used up.
   > How: 4 stainless plates, 4 aluminum plates and a stainless rotor.
69. **Liquid Air**: `modern_industrialization:liquid_air_bucket` *(after: Air Intake, Hot Ingots)*
   > What: air cold enough to be a liquid: the raw material for nitrogen, oxygen and argon.
   > Chemistry: air liquefies below about −194 °C. Carl von Linde did it industrially in 1895 by compressing air, cooling it, and letting it expand again and again.
   > How: Vacuum Freezer with an Air Intake inside: 1000 mB liquid air per run.
70. **A Perfect Crystal**: `modern_industrialization:monocrystalline_silicon` *(after: Argon from Air, The Rare Four)*
   > What: a monocrystalline silicon boule, the start of every chip.
   > Chemistry: in the Czochralski process a seed crystal is drawn slowly out of molten silicon, and every atom lines up with the one below. Argon keeps oxygen and nitrogen out of the melt.
   > How: Electric Blast Furnace: 32 silicon dust + 1 tiny iridium dust + 1250 mB argon → 1 monocrystalline silicon.
   > Tip: the tiny iridium is from the Platinum Line's residue. Keep a few.
71. **RAM**: 2x `modern_industrialization:random_access_memory` *(after: Semiconductor Silicon, Synthetic Rubber)*
   > What: random access memory; each processing unit takes 2.
   > Chemistry: a DRAM cell is one transistor and one tiny capacitor. The capacitor's charge is the bit, and it leaks away, so the chip refreshes itself thousands of times a second.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 silicon wafer + 1 antimony dust + 1 aluminum dust + 250 mB argon + 500 mB styrene-butadiene rubber → 2 RAM.
72. **Diamond Plates**: 2x `modern_industrialization:diamond_plate` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: each ALU is built on a diamond plate.
   > Chemistry: diamond conducts heat better than any metal while insulating electrically: ideal for a chip that runs hot.
   > How: Compressor: 1 diamond → 1 diamond plate (slow).
73. **Arithmetic Logic Unit**: `modern_industrialization:arithmetic_logic_unit` *(after: Diamond Plates, Logic Gates)*
   > What: the part of a processor that adds, compares and decides. Qubits need two each later.
   > Chemistry: binary addition is just XOR and AND: a half adder is two gates. Chain them and you can add numbers of any size.
   > How: 1 diamond plate, 2 AND gates, 2 OR gates and 4 NOT gates.
74. **Emerald Plates**: 2x `modern_industrialization:emerald_plate` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the MMU sits on an emerald plate.
   > How: Compressor: 1 emerald → 1 emerald plate (slow).
75. **Platinum Plates**: 8x `modern_industrialization:platinum_plate` *(after: The Platinum Line)*
   > What: every processing unit board takes 4 platinum plates; wire for the MMU comes from them too.
   > How: smelt platinum dust into ingots, then Compressor: 1 ingot → 1 plate.
76. **Platinum Fine Wire**: 6x `modern_industrialization:platinum_fine_wire` *(after: Platinum Plates)*
   > What: each MMU takes 6.
   > How: Wiremill: plate → 2 platinum wire; wire → 4 fine wire.
77. **Memory Management Unit**: `modern_industrialization:memory_management_unit` *(after: Semiconductor Silicon, Emerald Plates, Platinum Fine Wire)*
   > What: the MMU translates the addresses a program asks for into real places in RAM.
   > How: 1 emerald plate, 2 silicon wafers and 6 platinum fine wire.
78. **Monazite**: 9x `modern_industrialization:monazite_dust` *(after: The Centrifuge)*
   > What: monazite is the pack's source of cadmium, neodymium, yttrium and helium, all from one centrifuge run.
   > Chemistry: (Ce,La,Nd,Th)PO₄: a phosphate of rare earths with a little thorium, which makes it faintly radioactive.
   > How: mine MI monazite ore and macerate it. A stainless steel drill in a quarry also brings some up.
79. **Annealed Copper Cable**: 8x `modern_industrialization:annealed_copper_wire`; 8x `modern_industrialization:annealed_copper_cable` *(after: Annealed Copper)*
   > What: annealed copper cable carries EV power and goes into cadmium batteries, the processing unit board and the EV hull. Advanced motors use the bare wire.
   > How: Compressor: ingot → plate. Wiremill: plate → 2 wire. 3 wire + rubber (sheets or liquid SBR) → 3 cable.
80. **Chromium Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:chromium_ingot`; 4x `modern_industrialization:chromium_plate` *(after: Chromium and Manganese, Hot Ingots)*
   > What: the highly advanced casing is half chromium plates.
   > Chemistry: chromium is the hardest pure metal and the reason chrome plating shines: its oxide film is clear and self-healing.
   > How: EBF: chromium dust → hot ingot. Vacuum Freezer → ingot. Compressor → plate.
81. **Titanium Plates**: 8x `modern_industrialization:titanium_plate`; 2x `modern_industrialization:titanium_large_plate` *(after: Titanium)*
   > What: the highly advanced casing takes 4 titanium plates; the Implosion Compressor takes 2 large plates.
   > How: Compressor: ingot → plate. 4 plates → 1 large plate (crafting table or Packer).
82. **Highly Advanced Casing**: `modern_industrialization:highly_advanced_machine_casing` *(after: Titanium Plates, Chromium Plates, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the shell of the EV hull.
   > How: 4 titanium plates and 4 chromium plates around a Turbo (HV) machine hull.
83. **An EV Grid**: `modern_industrialization:hv_ev_transformer`; `modern_industrialization:ev_storage_unit` *(after: EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: an HV-to-EV transformer and an EV storage unit.
   > How: transformer: a Turbo hull, 4 aluminum cable, 1 annealed copper cable. Storage: an EV hull, 6 cadmium batteries, 2 battery alloy plates.
84. **Kanthal Cable**: 6x `modern_industrialization:kanthal_wire`; 16x `modern_industrialization:kanthal_cable` *(after: Kanthal)*
   > What: Kanthal coils are wound from Kanthal cable, 8 per coil.
   > How: Compressor: ingot → plate. Wiremill: plate → 2 wire. 3 wire + rubber → 3 cable.
   > Tip: a full furnace needs 16 coils, so 128 cables. Set the Wiremill and Packer running early.
85. **Magnetic Stainless Rods**: 2x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_rod_magnetic` *(after: Rare Earths and Helium, Stainless Steel)*
   > What: the rotor core of every advanced motor.
   > Chemistry: neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest permanent magnets made. Every wind turbine and electric car motor has them.
   > How: Polarizer: 1 stainless steel rod + 1 neodymium dust → 1 magnetic stainless rod.
86. **Elite Control Circuits**: 4x `mekanism:elite_control_circuit` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits, Reinforced Alloy)*
   > What: fission ports, control rods and the Solar Neutron Activator all need elite circuits.
   > How: 1 MI digital circuit, 2 reinforced alloy and 1 advanced control circuit.
87. **Ultimate Control Circuits**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_atomic`; 2x `mekanism:ultimate_control_circuit` *(after: EV: Processing Units, Elite Control Circuits)*
   > What: the Isotopic Centrifuge and the SPS run on ultimate circuits.
   > How: atomic alloy: Metallurgic Infuser, reinforced alloy + refined obsidian. Circuit: 1 MI processing unit, 2 atomic alloy and 1 elite circuit.
88. **Uranium Ingots**: 4x `modern_industrialization:uranium_ingot` *(after: Uranium)*
   > What: Mekanism's enrichment starts from ingots, and MI's fuel rods are cut from them.
   > Chemistry: uranium metal is dense (19 g/cm³, about as heavy as gold) and burns in air when finely divided.
   > How: smelt raw uranium in any furnace, or melt uranium dust in a Kanthal-tier Electric Blast Furnace.
89. **Fluorite Dust**: 8x `mekanism:dust_fluorite` *(after: Fluorite)*
   > What: each plutonium or polonium pellet takes 1 fluorite dust.
   > How: Crusher: 1 fluorite gem → 1 dust. Fluorite ore crushed in Occultism gives more.
90. **HF in a Bucket**: `mekanism:hydrofluoric_acid_bucket` *(after: Hydrofluoric Acid)*
   > What: hydrofluoric acid as a liquid. The Seed of a New World takes 4 buckets.
   > Chemistry: HF boils at 19.5 °C, so on a warm day it's barely a liquid. Real plants keep it cooled under pressure in steel, never glass.
   > How: Rotary Condensentrator in liquid mode, HF gas in, fluid out.
91. **Solar Neutron Activator**: `mekanism:solar_neutron_activator` *(after: Elite Control Circuits, HDPE)*
   > What: the machine that turns nuclear waste into polonium.
   > How: reinforced alloy, an HDPE sheet, 2 elite circuits, a steel casing and bronze ingots (check JEI). It needs a clear view of the sky and works only in daylight.
92. **Waste Barrels**: 2x `mekanism:radioactive_waste_barrel` *(after: Fission)*
   > What: radioactive waste barrels hold spent waste and let it decay slowly instead of leaking.
   > Chemistry: every radioactive isotope halves on its own schedule. Real spent fuel is kept cool for years before it is moved anywhere.
   > How: 4 steel and 4 lead ingots.
93. **Reactor Logic**: checkmark *(after: Fission)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Fission Logic Adapter" on the Mekanism: Power page. Click to dismiss.
94. **A Nether Star**: `minecraft:nether_star` *(after: Chamber Frame)*
   > What: the Fusion Chamber controller needs a Nether Star.
   > How: defeat a Wither (soul sand T, three wither skeleton skulls). Fight it in a sealed room, deep underground.
   > Tip: save the skulls you find from now on: the Seed of a New World needs four more stars.
95. **Cadmium Rods**: 2x `modern_industrialization:cadmium_ingot`; 18x `modern_industrialization:cadmium_rod` *(after: Cadmium Battery)*
   > What: each cadmium control rod is 18 of these.
   > How: smelt cadmium dust into ingots. Cutting Machine with lubricant: 1 ingot → 2 rods.
96. **Uranium Rods**: 18x `modern_industrialization:uranium_rod` *(after: Uranium Ingots)*
   > What: each MI uranium fuel rod is 18 of these.
   > How: Cutting Machine with lubricant: 1 uranium ingot → 2 rods.
97. **Large Diesel Generator**: checkmark *(after: Stainless Motors, Diesel Power)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Large Diesel Generator" on the Power page. Click to dismiss.

### VIII. Beyond the Sky

*Leave the cradle. Make matter from energy. Seed a new world.*

1. **Leaving the Cradle**: `ad_astra:nasa_workbench` *(after: EV: Processing Units)*
   > The stars were close once, close enough to touch. Time to stop looking at them from the ground.
   > What: the NASA Workbench assembles every Ad Astra rocket.
   > How: iron rods, steel plates, redstone torches and a steel block around an EV (highly advanced) hull, so processing units come first.
2. **Rocket Parts**: `ad_astra:rocket_nose_cone`; 4x `ad_astra:rocket_fin`; 2x `ad_astra:steel_tank`; `ad_astra:steel_engine` *(after: Nose Cone, Fins, Fuel Tanks, Steel Engine)*
   > What: a Tier 1 rocket needs a nose cone, 4 fins, 2 steel tanks, a steel engine and 6 steel blocks.
   > Chemistry: real rockets carry their own oxidiser (often liquid oxygen) as well as fuel, because there's no air to burn in once you're up. Ad Astra simplifies this: its tanks take fuel only (MI diesel, biodiesel or cryo fuel; see Rocket Fuel).
   > How: all parts are crafted from steel plates and rods (check JEI). The nose cone uses a lightning rod.
3. **Breathe**: `ad_astra:space_helmet`; `ad_astra:oxygen_loader` *(after: Gas Tanks, Fans)*
   > What: the Oxygen Loader fills your space suit's tank.
   > Chemistry: it accepts plain water, but 100 mB of water gives only 4 mB of oxygen. Pure O₂ from your electrolysis line (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂) goes in 1:1.
   > How: helmet: 5 steel plates and a glass pane. Loader: steel plates, a fan, 2 gas tanks, a lightning rod and a redstone block. Pipe MI or Mekanism oxygen in, power it, and put the suit in the slot.
4. **The Full Suit**: `ad_astra:space_suit`; `ad_astra:space_pants`; `ad_astra:space_boots` *(after: Breathe, Oxygen Gear)*
   > What: the full set keeps you alive in vacuum and in the cold of the Moon.
   > How: check JEI for each piece. Wear all four before launch.
   > Tip: the chest piece holds the oxygen. Watch the gauge on your HUD.
5. **Launch Pad**: `ad_astra:launch_pad` *(after: Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: rockets are placed on a launch pad, not on the bare ground.
   > How: 5 steel plates and 4 steel rods. Place it in the open, with clear sky above.
   > Tip: build a pad on each world you visit so you always have somewhere to land and relaunch.
6. **Rocket Fuel**: 3x `modern_industrialization:diesel_bucket` *(after: Leaving the Cradle, Diesel Power)*
   > What: in this pack rockets burn anything in the Ad Astra fuel tag: MI diesel or biodiesel, or Ad Astra's cryo fuel. Ad Astra's own oil refining is removed.
   > Chemistry: a kilogram of diesel releases about 45 MJ when it burns: more than ten times a good battery.
   > How: fill the rocket from buckets or pipes (check its GUI for how much it holds). Cryo fuel comes from Ad Astra's Cryo Freezer (check JEI).
   > Tip: bring spare fuel for the trip home.
7. **One Small Step**: `ad_astra:tier_1_rocket`; visit `ad_astra:moon` *(after: Launch Pad, Rocket Fuel, The Full Suit)*
   > The Moon looks smaller than you remember. Or perhaps you were larger.
   > How: build the rocket in the NASA Workbench, place it on the pad, fuel it, climb in and launch. Pick the Moon on the planet screen.
   > Tip: place a bed or waystone near your landing site before exploring.
8. **Desh**: 8x `ad_astra:raw_desh`; 4x `ad_astra:desh_plate` *(after: One Small Step)*
   > What: desh is Ad Astra's lunar metal, needed for the Tier 2 rocket and oxygen equipment.
   > How: mine desh ore on the Moon, smelt it, and press the ingots into plates in Ad Astra's Compressor.
   > Tip: the Moon also has cheese ore. Really.
9. **A Breathable Room**: checkmark *(after: Desh)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Breathable Bases" on the Space page. Click to dismiss.
10. **Supercritical Phase Shifter**: 2x `mekanism:sps_port`; `mekanism:supercharged_coil` *(after: SPS Casing, Laser, Ultimate Control Circuits)*
   > What: the SPS is Mekanism's largest machine. It needs huge amounts of power.
   > How: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks shows the full layout in JEI. Ports (4 casings + an ultimate circuit) feed polonium in; the supercharged coil (copper, 2 ultimate circuits, a laser and polonium pellets) takes the power.
   > Tip: feed it from a fission reactor and turbine, or several Flux Networks plugs.
11. **Bottling Antimatter**: `mekanism:chemical_crystallizer` *(after: Supercritical Phase Shifter)*
   > What: the SPS outputs antimatter as a gas. The Chemical Crystallizer packs 1000 mB of it into one pellet.
   > How: pipe antimatter from the SPS output port into the crystallizer.
   > Tip: pipe the SPS straight into the crystallizer so the antimatter never sits in a tank.
12. **Antimatter**: 4x `mekanism:sps_casing`; `mekanism:pellet_antimatter` *(after: One Small Step, Bottling Antimatter)*
   > Matter from nothing but energy. Even the oldest part of you is impressed.
   > Chemistry: when matter meets antimatter both vanish into pure energy, E = mc². One gram of each releases about 1.8 × 10¹⁴ J.
   > How: SPS → antimatter gas → Chemical Crystallizer → antimatter pellet.
   > Tip: it's the most energy-dense substance there is. Antimatter Cores need four pellets each.
13. **Empty Energy Core**: `kubejs:energy_core_empty` *(after: Transmutation by Neutron)*
   > What: the vessel for the most concentrated energy you can hold.
   > Chemistry: polonium gives off so much heat by decay that a gram of it glows. Here it seeds the core.
   > How: craft: 4 stainless steel plates + 4 polonium pellets + a processing unit in the centre.
   > Tip: the Complete Periodic Table quest rewards one empty core.
14. **Charge the Core**: `kubejs:energy_core` *(after: Empty Energy Core)*
   > What: an empty core holds nothing until you charge it with raw electrical energy.
   > How: MI Assembler at 512 EU/t for 6000 ticks: about 3 million EU per core.
   > Tip: give it its own power line. A charging core will starve every other machine on the network.
15. **Antimatter Core**: `kubejs:antimatter_core` *(after: Charge the Core, Antimatter, Quantum Circuit)*
   > It hums in your hand like a small sun. You were this, once.
   > What: a charged core, upgraded with antimatter and a quantum circuit.
   > How: MI Assembler at 2048 EU/t for 6000 ticks: charged Energy Core + 4 antimatter pellets + 1 quantum circuit.
   > Tip: the Seed needs eight. Start a production line, not a one-off.
16. **Made of Cheese**: checkmark *(after: One Small Step)*
   > Moved: this step is now "The Moon Is Cheese" on the Space page. Click to dismiss.
17. **Low Earth Orbit**: visit `ad_astra:earth_orbit` *(after: One Small Step)*
   > What: every planet has an orbit dimension above it, a good place for a space station.
   > How: pick Earth Orbit on the rocket's planet screen.
   > Tip: bring building blocks and a way home.
18. **Grand Tour**: visit `ad_astra:moon`; visit `ad_astra:mars`; visit `ad_astra:venus`; visit `ad_astra:mercury`; visit `ad_astra:glacio` *(after: One Small Step)*
   > What: the Moon (Tier 1 rocket), Mars (Tier 2), Venus and Mercury (Tier 3) and Glacio (Tier 4).
   > How: a dimension task completes on arrival. Plan fuel and oxygen for each trip.
   > Tip: Venus and Mercury are hot enough to cook an ordinary space suit. Bring the netherite one.
19. **Heat-Proof Suit**: `ad_astra:netherite_space_helmet`; `ad_astra:netherite_space_suit` *(after: The Full Suit, Mars)*
   > What: the netherite space suit survives the heat of Venus and Mercury.
   > How: the chest piece is a netherite chestplate with ostrum plates (from Mars), gas tanks and an oxygen gear. Check JEI for the rest.
20. **Glacio**: `ad_astra:tier_4_rocket`; visit `ad_astra:glacio` *(after: Venus)*
   > What: Glacio orbits another star and needs a Tier 4 rocket built from calorite.
   > How: calorite comes from Venus. The tanks, engine and blocks are all calorite (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's the only planet outside our solar system. Take a look at the sky.
21. **Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer**: checkmark *(after: Antimatter)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer" on the Mekanism: Power page. Click to dismiss.
22. **Cryofluid**: `modern_industrialization:cryofluid_bucket` *(after: The Rest of the Air, Rare Earths and Helium)*
   > What: cryofluid fills cooling cells and qubits. Superconductors only work this cold.
   > Chemistry: liquid helium boils at −269 °C, four degrees above absolute zero. Nothing else stays liquid that cold.
   > How: Vacuum Freezer: 140 mB argon + 60 mB helium → 200 mB cryofluid.
   > Tip: the recipe draws 256 EU/t, more than a plain freezer allows. Put machine upgrades in it (Electrochemistry and Petrochemistry side quests).
23. **Cooling Cells**: 4x `modern_industrialization:cooling_cell` *(after: Cryofluid, Small Heat Exchanger)*
   > What: cooling cells keep superconductor cable and quantum circuits below their critical temperature.
   > How: Assembler: 3 fluid pipes, 2 small heat exchangers, 6 tin plates and 1000 mB cryofluid.
   > Tip: every quantum circuit uses 2 directly, plus more inside its cable. Make a stack.
24. **Superconductor Cable**: 6x `modern_industrialization:superconductor_wire`; 6x `modern_industrialization:superconductor_cable` *(after: Superconductor Plates, Cooling Cells)*
   > What: the cable of the quantum tier.
   > Chemistry: below its critical temperature a superconductor carries current with no loss at all and pushes magnetic fields out (the Meissner effect).
   > How: Wiremill: 1 superconductor plate → 2 wire. Assembler: 3 wire + 2 cooling cells + 1000 mB PVC → 6 cable.
25. **Pure Carbon**: 2x `modern_industrialization:carbon_dust`; 2x `modern_industrialization:carbon_plate` *(after: Leaving the Cradle)*
   > What: carbon plates hold each qubit.
   > Chemistry: coal is carbon plus hydrogen, sulfur and ash. The Centrifuge spins the rest away.
   > How: Centrifuge: 1 coal dust → 1 carbon dust. Compressor: carbon dust → carbon plate.
26. **Tritium**: `modern_industrialization:tritium_bucket` *(after: The Nuclear Reactor)*
   > What: every qubit needs 50 mB of tritium.
   > Chemistry: tritium (³H) is radioactive, with a half-life of about 12 years. Real tritium is bred in reactors by hitting lithium or deuterium with neutrons.
   > How: Centrifuge: 1000 mB hydrogen → 20 mB deuterium + 1 mB tritium. That's slow; the Nuclear Reactor turns fluids in its fluid hatches into heavier isotopes much faster (check JEI under the reactor).
27. **Qubits**: 2x `modern_industrialization:qubit` *(after: Superconductor Cable, Pure Carbon, Tritium, Arithmetic Logic Unit)*
   > What: the core of a quantum circuit.
   > Chemistry: a qubit holds a superposition of 0 and 1. Real ones are superconducting loops kept a hair above absolute zero, which is why yours needs cryofluid.
   > How: Assembler: 2 arithmetic logic units, 2 carbon plates, 2 glass panes, 6 superconductor wire, 250 mB cryofluid and 50 mB tritium.
28. **Plutonium Battery**: 2x `modern_industrialization:plutonium_battery` *(after: Superconductor Cable, Bred Plutonium)*
   > What: the quantum tier's battery: the circuit board and the quantum hull each take two.
   > Chemistry: radioisotope generators turn decay heat into electricity. The Voyager probes still run on plutonium-238, launched in 1977.
   > How: Assembler: a battery alloy plate, 4 battery alloy curved plates, 2 superconductor cable and 2 MI plutonium dust.
29. **Helium-3**: `modern_industrialization:helium_3_bucket` *(after: Rare Earths and Helium)*
   > What: every quantum circuit board needs 50 mB of helium-3.
   > Chemistry: helium-3 has one neutron instead of two. Earth has almost none; the Moon's soil holds more, implanted by the solar wind.
   > How: Centrifuge: 1000 mB helium → 5 mB helium-3. That's 10 buckets of helium per board, so tap every helium source you have.
30. **Quantum Circuit Board**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_circuit_board` *(after: Plutonium Battery, Helium-3, Iridium Plates)*
   > How: Assembler: a processing unit board, 12 superconductor cable, 2 plutonium batteries, 6 iridium plates and 50 mB helium-3.
   > Tip: the iridium plates are the slow part: each one is an implosion. Plan for 6 per board.
31. **Quantum Circuit**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_circuit` *(after: Quantum Circuit Board, Qubits)*
   > A thought that holds every answer until it is asked. This one you didn't remember. You built it.
   > What: the top MI circuit. Each Antimatter Core needs one, so the Seed needs eight.
   > How: Assembler: 4 processing units, 2 cooling cells, 2 qubits and a quantum circuit board.
   > Tip: automate the whole line before you need eight. Cooling cells and helium-3 are the slow parts.
32. **Quantum Hull**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_machine_hull` *(after: Quantum Circuit, Quantum Casing)*
   > What: the base of MI's fusion reactor, replicator and quantum machines (Creation chapter).
   > How: Assembler: a quantum machine casing, a quantum circuit, 2 plutonium batteries and 3 superconductor cable.
33. **Steel for the Ship**: 32x any of `item_tag(ad_astra:steel_plates)`; 7x any of `item_tag(ad_astra:steel_blocks)` *(after: Leaving the Cradle)*
   > What: a Tier 1 rocket is mostly steel: 6 steel blocks in the body plus plates for every part around them.
   > How: MI steel plates count as Ad Astra steel plates, and MI or Mekanism steel blocks as Ad Astra steel blocks. Your steel line already makes them.
   > Tip: one more block and a few plates go into the NASA Workbench itself.
34. **Nose Cone**: `ad_astra:rocket_nose_cone` *(after: Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: the tip of the rocket.
   > Chemistry: a rocket's nose takes the worst of the air's friction on the way up. Real cones are shaped to push the shock wave away from the body.
   > How: a lightning rod on top of 4 steel plates.
35. **Fins**: 4x `ad_astra:rocket_fin` *(after: Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: fins keep the rocket pointed nose-first while it's still in the air.
   > How: 6 steel plates → 4 fins.
36. **Gas Tanks**: 6x `ad_astra:gas_tank` *(after: Leaving the Cradle)*
   > What: the steel tanks, the space suit and the Oxygen Loader each take two.
   > How: an iron rod and 4 iron plates (MI iron plates work).
37. **Fuel Tanks**: 2x `ad_astra:steel_tank` *(after: Gas Tanks, Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: the rocket carries its fuel in two steel tanks.
   > How: a gas tank, a steel rod and 5 steel plates each.
38. **Fans**: 2x `ad_astra:fan` *(after: Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: the engine and the Oxygen Loader each need a fan.
   > How: 4 steel plates around a steel rod.
39. **Engine Frame**: `ad_astra:engine_frame` *(after: Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: the skeleton of the rocket engine.
   > How: 8 steel rods around a steel plate.
40. **Steel Engine**: `ad_astra:steel_engine` *(after: Engine Frame, Fans)*
   > What: the engine that lifts a Tier 1 rocket.
   > Chemistry: a rocket works by Newton's third law: hot gas thrown down fast pushes the rocket up. It needs nothing to push against, which is why it works in vacuum.
   > How: an engine frame, a fan and 5 steel plates.
41. **Oxygen Gear**: `ad_astra:oxygen_gear` *(after: Steel for the Ship)*
   > What: the valve that feeds the suit's air to your helmet. The space suit and the Oxygen Distributor use one.
   > How: 3 steel rods and 4 steel plates.
42. **HDPE Sheets**: 16x `mekanism:hdpe_sheet` *(after: HDPE)*
   > What: every SPS casing is 4 HDPE sheets around polonium and plutonium.
   > How: Enrichment Chamber: 3 HDPE pellets → 1 sheet.
43. **SPS Casing**: 4x `mekanism:sps_casing` *(after: HDPE Sheets, Transmutation by Neutron)*
   > What: the walls of the Supercritical Phase Shifter.
   > How: 4 HDPE sheets, 4 polonium pellets and 1 plutonium pellet per casing.
   > Tip: the whole shell needs many more than four. Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI gives the exact count; start your pellet lines early.
44. **Laser**: `mekanism:laser` *(after: Reinforced Alloy, Energy Tablet)*
   > What: the SPS's supercharged coil is built around a Mekanism laser.
   > Chemistry: laser stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation: excited atoms are triggered to release identical photons, all in step.
   > How: 3 reinforced alloy, 2 energy tablets, a steel casing and a diamond.
45. **Superconductor Dust**: 9x `modern_industrialization:superconductor_dust` *(after: The Rare Four, Annealed Copper, Rare Earths and Helium)*
   > What: the mixed powder that becomes superconductor.
   > Chemistry: real high-temperature superconductors are copper oxides layered with yttrium and rare earths, like YBa₂Cu₃O₇. MI's mix borrows the idea: copper, yttrium and neodymium.
   > How: Mixer: 1 iridium + 3 annealed copper + 3 yttrium + 2 neodymium dust → 9 superconductor dust.
46. **Superconductor Ingots**: 4x `modern_industrialization:superconductor_ingot` *(after: Superconductor Dust, A Hotter Furnace)*
   > What: superconductor as metal.
   > How: Kanthal-tier Electric Blast Furnace → hot ingot → Vacuum Freezer (or the Heat Exchanger, which gives argon and helium back).
47. **Superconductor Plates**: 4x `modern_industrialization:superconductor_plate` *(after: Superconductor Ingots)*
   > What: plates become superconductor wire.
   > How: Compressor: 1 ingot → 1 plate.
48. **Iridium Plates**: 6x `modern_industrialization:iridium_plate` *(after: The Implosion Compressor, The Rare Four)*
   > What: each quantum circuit board takes 6 iridium plates.
   > Chemistry: iridium is the most corrosion-resistant metal known. A thin layer of it marks the 66-million-year-old boundary left by the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs.
   > How: Packer: 2 blastproof alloy ingots + 1 iridium ingot → mixed iridium ingot. Implosion Compressor: mixed ingot + Industrial TNT → 1 iridium plate.
49. **Quantum Casing**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_machine_casing` *(after: Iridium Plates)*
   > What: the shell of the quantum (IV) hull, which the Creation chapter's machines are built on.
   > How: 8 iridium plates around a highly advanced (EV) machine hull.

### The Seed of a New World

*Every tier in one 9x9 grid. The act of making a world.*

1. **The Last Recipe**: checkmark *(after: Leaving the Cradle)*
   > Now it comes back, what all of this was for. Not machines. A world.
   > What: the Seed of a New World is the pack's final craft: a 9x9 Ultimate Table recipe that uses something from every tier you've climbed.
   > How: every ingredient has its own branch, from raw material to finished part, and each branch ends in a checklist quest with the exact count. Finish all eight checklists and the Ultimate Table, and the Seed opens.
   > Tip: you can start the cheap lines (coke, water, acids, plastic) right away. The Antimatter Cores at the bottom take the longest.
   > {@pagebreak}
