   > The full recipe: 4 coke, 8 ChemLib water, 4 hydrogen, 4 hydrofluoric acid buckets, 8 sulfuric acid buckets, 12 polyethylene buckets, 8 processing units, 4 stainless steel plates, 8 oganesson, 4 plutonium pellets, 4 polonium pellets, 4 Nether Stars, 8 Antimatter Cores and 1 Dragon Egg. 81 slots, every one filled.
   > Why these: read them in order and they retell the climb: fire (coke), the elements (synthesized water), the Acid Age (sulfuric and hydrofluoric acid), the Oil Age, the machine ages, the atomic age, and the energy you learned to bottle at the end.
   > Where: the Extended Crafting Ultimate Table (9x9). JEI shows the layout; press U on the Seed.
2. **Coke**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coke` *(after: The Last Recipe)*
   > What: the four corners of the Seed are coke, the first thing your coke oven ever made.
   > Chemistry: coke is coal baked without air. Heat drives off water, tar and coal gas, leaving a hard, porous lump that is mostly carbon.
   > How: any coke oven or MI Coke Oven. Four pieces.
   > Tip: it's fitting that the last recipe starts with the first fuel.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why coke, not coal?
   > Raw coal is full of volatile hydrocarbons and sulfur. In a blast furnace they would boil off, foul the iron and choke the burden.
   > Coking (about 1000 °C, no oxygen) cooks them out. What's left is strong enough to carry the weight of ore above it and burns hot and clean.
   > In the furnace, coke does two jobs: it burns for heat, and its carbon monoxide strips oxygen from iron oxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
3. **Hydrogen, Element 1**: 12x `chemlib:hydrogen` *(after: The Last Recipe)*
   > What: the Seed takes 4 hydrogen itself, and its 8 synthesized water need 16 more to build. Start with a dozen and keep the Dissolver running.
   > Chemistry: one proton and one electron. Hydrogen makes up about three quarters of all the ordinary matter in the universe by mass.
   > How: the Alchemistry Dissolver breaks ChemLib water into 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen. Other compounds give hydrogen too (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's the same element you used for the Potion of Flying back in Chapter II.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: the first element
   > Almost all the hydrogen in existence was made in the first few minutes after the Big Bang. Every other element was built from it later, inside stars.
   > Stars fuse hydrogen into helium. Bigger stars go on to carbon, oxygen and up to iron. Heavier elements need supernovae and neutron-star collisions.
   > So hydrogen is the right place to start a new world: it's where the old one started too.
4. **Synthesized Water**: 8x `chemlib:water` *(after: Hydrogen, Element 1, Oxygen, Element 8)*
   > What: 8 ChemLib water, made from elements rather than scooped from a lake.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. The reaction releases a lot of energy: it's what powers a hydrogen fuel cell.
   > How: Alchemistry Combiner: 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen → 1 water.
   > Tip: the Dissolver gives you the oxygen along with the hydrogen, so nothing is wasted.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why build water at all?
   > You could pour a bucket. The point of the Seed is that every part of a world can be made from its elements, and water is the most important compound of all.
   > Water's bent shape (104.5° between the two O-H bonds) makes it polar. That polarity is why it dissolves salts, why ice floats, and why it holds so much heat.
   > No water, no life. It's on the Seed eight times.
5. **Sulfur**: 16x `modern_industrialization:sulfur_dust` *(after: The Last Recipe)*
   > What: eight buckets of acid need 16 sulfur dust.
   > Chemistry: sulfur is a yellow non-metal. Most of the world's supply comes from scrubbing it out of oil and gas, much as you do in petrochemistry.
   > How: sulfuric purification of crude oil and fuels in the MI Chemical Reactor, or from ore processing byproducts (check JEI).
6. **The King of Chemicals**: `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_acid_bucket` *(after: Sulfur, Oxygen for the Reactor)*
   > What: the acid that unlocked 5x ore processing. The Seed needs eight buckets.
   > Chemistry: S + O₂ → SO₂, then 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃, then SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄. MI's Chemical Reactor does it in one step from sulfur, oxygen and water.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 1 sulfur dust + 200 mB oxygen + 200 mB water → 500 mB sulfuric acid.
   > Tip: one reactor makes the full 8000 mB in a few minutes.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: the Contact Process
   > Industry makes sulfuric acid by the contact process. Burning sulfur gives SO₂; a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst at about 450 °C turns it into SO₃.
   > SO₃ isn't simply added to water: the reaction is so violent it makes a mist of acid. It's absorbed into concentrated acid first (making oleum, H₂S₂O₇), then diluted.
   > More sulfuric acid is made than any other chemical. A country's output of it was once used as a measure of its industrial strength.
7. **Ethylene**: `modern_industrialization:ethylene_bucket` *(after: Cracked Naphtha)*
   > What: the feedstock for polyethylene. 12 buckets of plastic need about 8.6 buckets of ethylene.
   > Chemistry: ethylene has a carbon-carbon double bond. That bond is what lets thousands of molecules link into a chain.
   > How: steam-crack naphtha or light fuel and distil the result, or dehydrate ethanol in the Chemical Reactor (check JEI).
8. **Polymerise**: `modern_industrialization:polyethylene_bucket` *(after: Ethylene, Chromium Catalyst)*
   > What: the Seed uses 12 buckets of polyethylene, more than any other ingredient.
   > Chemistry: n C₂H₄ → (–CH₂–CH₂–)ₙ. The double bond opens and each monomer joins the next.
   > How: Chemical Reactor: 500 mB ethylene + a tiny pile of chromium (or lead) dust → 700 mB polyethylene.
   > Tip: the chromium is a catalyst in real life too (see the next page).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: catalysts that make plastic
   > Most of the world's high-density polyethylene is made with chromium catalysts (the Phillips process) or titanium-aluminium ones (Ziegler-Natta).
   > The metal centre grabs an ethylene molecule and slots it into the growing chain, again and again. The result is a long, straight chain that packs tightly: strong, stiff plastic.
   > Without a catalyst you need huge pressures and get a branched, softer plastic (LDPE). Same formula, different shape, different material.
9. **Eight Processing Units**: 8x `modern_industrialization:processing_unit` *(after: Processing Unit Boards, Chips by the Batch, Digital Circuits)*
   > What: processing units are MI's EV circuits. The Seed takes eight, and each Energy Core needs one more.
   > Chemistry: they're built on PVC boards. PVC is polyethylene with a chlorine atom on every other carbon, which makes it harder and flame-resistant.
   > How: MI Assembler (check JEI). Queue sixteen: eight for the Seed and eight for the cores.
   > Tip: processing units are slow. Start them first and let them run while you do the other lines.
10. **Stainless Steel**: 36x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_plate` *(after: Stainless Ingots)*
   > What: 4 plates for the Seed itself and 4 for each of the 8 Energy Core shells: 36 in all.
   > Chemistry: stainless steel is iron with at least 10.5% chromium, often with nickel. The chromium forms a thin Cr₂O₃ film that heals itself when scratched.
   > How: plates from stainless steel ingots in the Compressor. Ingots from the Electric Blast Furnace (check JEI).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: passivation
   > Ordinary iron rusts because its oxide flakes off and exposes fresh metal. Chromium oxide does the opposite: it's a dense layer a few nanometres thick that sticks.
   > Scratch it and the exposed chromium reacts with oxygen in the air and seals the gap within moments. That's why stainless steel stays shiny.
   > Nickel keeps the steel in its austenite form at room temperature: tough, non-magnetic and easy to work.
11. **Oganesson ×8**: 8x `chemlib:oganesson` *(after: The Last Recipe, The Complete Periodic Table)*
   > What: the last element on the periodic table. You made one to finish the table; the Seed wants eight.
   > Chemistry: oganesson-294 has a half-life of under a millisecond. Only a handful of atoms have ever been made.
   > How: Alchemistry Fusion Chamber: fuse two elements whose atomic numbers add up to 118 (check JEI for the pairs).
   > Tip: automate the inputs. Eight by hand is a long afternoon.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: making element 118
   > In 2002 a team in Dubna, Russia fired calcium-48 ions (20 protons) at a californium-249 target (98 protons). 20 + 98 = 118.
   > Over months of beam time they saw about three atoms. Each decayed by alpha emission within a millisecond, into livermorium (116).
   > It sits in the noble gas column, but it may not behave like one: its electrons move so fast that relativity smears out its shells. Your Fusion Chamber does the same addition, rather more reliably.
12. **Plutonium Pellets**: 4x `mekanism:pellet_plutonium` *(after: Fluorite for the Pellets)*
   > What: four plutonium pellets for the Seed.
   > Chemistry: uranium-238 in a reactor captures a neutron and decays twice: U-238 → U-239 → Np-239 → Pu-239.
   > How: Mekanism: nuclear waste → Isotopic Centrifuge → plutonium → Chemical Crystallizer → pellet.
   > Tip: a running fission reactor makes waste whether you want it or not. This is a good use for it.
13. **Polonium Pellets**: 36x `mekanism:pellet_polonium` *(after: Fluorite for the Pellets)*
   > What: 4 pellets for the Seed and 4 for each of the 8 Energy Core shells: 36 in all. Polonium also feeds the SPS that makes antimatter.
   > Chemistry: Marie and Pierre Curie found polonium in 1898 and named it after Poland. Po-210 is so radioactive that a gram of it glows from its own heat.
   > How: Mekanism: nuclear waste → Solar Neutron Activator → polonium → Chemical Crystallizer → pellet.
   > Tip: activators only work in daylight. Build a row of them, not one.
14. **The Wither**: kill 1x `minecraft:wither` *(after: Skulls and Soul Sand)*
   > What: every Nether Star comes from a Wither. The Seed needs four.
   > How: soul sand T-shape, three wither skeleton skulls on top. Fight it somewhere you don't mind losing.
   > Tip: fight it underground or in a sealed box so it can't fly off, and bring milk for the wither effect.
15. **The Dragon**: kill 1x `minecraft:ender_dragon` *(after: The End)*
   > What: the Dragon Egg is the Seed's centre slot.
   > How: kill the Ender Dragon. The egg appears on top of the exit portal. Push it off with a piston or knock it onto a torch; clicking it makes it teleport.
   > Tip: if someone on the server already took the egg, there's another way. Look into the Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer.
16. **Thirty-Two Antimatter Pellets**: 32x `mekanism:pellet_antimatter` *(after: Eight Pellets)*
   > What: each Antimatter Core takes 4 antimatter pellets, so eight cores need 32.
   > Chemistry: an antiproton has the proton's mass and the opposite charge. When one meets a proton both vanish into energy (and a spray of lighter particles).
   > How: SPS → antimatter gas → Chemical Crystallizer. Keep both running non-stop.
   > Tip: a second SPS halves the wait, if you can feed it the polonium and the power.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: how much energy?
   > E = mc². Annihilating 1 gram of antimatter with 1 gram of matter releases about 1.8 × 10¹⁴ J, roughly the energy of a 43-kiloton explosion.
   > Real labs (CERN's Antiproton Decelerator) have made only nanograms in decades, and keep them for minutes at most in magnetic traps.
   > Your SPS is far kinder than physics, but it still asks for a lot of power. That's the price of reversing every charge in an atom.
17. **Eight Quantum Circuits**: 8x `modern_industrialization:quantum_circuit` *(after: Boards and Qubits)*
   > What: MI's top circuit. Each Antimatter Core needs one.
   > How: MI Assembler (check JEI). Quantum circuit boards come first.
   > Tip: quantum circuits also build the fusion reactor and the quantum armour in the Creation chapter. Make spares.
18. **Two Cores**: 2x `kubejs:antimatter_core` *(after: Antimatter Core, Charged Cores, Thirty-Two Antimatter Pellets, Eight Quantum Circuits)*
   > What: you've made one Antimatter Core. Make it two.
   > How: Empty Energy Core (4 stainless plates, 4 polonium pellets, 1 processing unit) → MI Assembler at 512 EU/t to charge it → MI Assembler at 2048 EU/t with 4 antimatter pellets and 1 quantum circuit.
   > Tip: two assemblers, one for each step, let the cores flow without you.
19. **Four Cores**: 4x `kubejs:antimatter_core` *(after: Two Cores)*
   > What: four Antimatter Cores. The Seed's diamond of power is half built.
   > How: keep the line running. Each core is about 3 million EU to charge and 12 million more to upgrade.
   > Tip: if your network sags while the assemblers run, give them their own generator.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: the energy budget
   > Charging: 512 EU/t × 6000 ticks = about 3.1 million EU. Upgrading: 2048 EU/t × 6000 ticks = about 12.3 million EU.
   > That's about 15 million EU per core, or about 123 million EU for all eight, before counting the SPS that makes the antimatter.
   > A fission reactor with a turbine, or a Mekanism fusion reactor, makes this a matter of hours. A wall of solar panels makes it a matter of weeks.
20. **Fire, Water and Hydrogen**: 4x `modern_industrialization:coke`; 8x `chemlib:water`; 4x `chemlib:hydrogen` *(after: Coke, Synthesized Water)*
   > What: the Seed's corners and outer ring hold the first things you learned: coke from your coke oven, and water synthesized from its elements.
   > How: 4 coke, 8 ChemLib water (Combiner: 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen each) and 4 hydrogen, all held at once.
   > Tip: both are cheap now. Make spares.
21. **Eight Buckets of Acid**: 8x any of `item_tag(warbucks:sulfuric_acid_buckets)` *(after: The King of Chemicals)*
   > What: 8 buckets of sulfuric acid, the chemical that unlocked 5x ore processing.
   > How: fill buckets from your sulfuric acid tanks. MI, Mekanism and ChemLib acid buckets all count, in any mix.
   > Tip: buckets don't stack. Clear inventory space first, or keep them in a backpack.
22. **Four Buckets of HF**: 4x `mekanism:hydrofluoric_acid_bucket` *(after: Hydrofluoric Acid, Hydrofluoric Acid)*
   > What: 4 buckets of hydrofluoric acid, the acid that opened the road to nuclear fuel.
   > Chemistry: CaF₂ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + 2HF. HF is a weak acid by strength, yet it etches glass and soaks through skin: fluoride grabs silicon and calcium.
   > How: Chemical Dissolution Chamber: fluorite + sulfuric acid → HF gas. A Rotary Condensentrator in liquid mode turns the gas into fluid; fill buckets from it.
   > Tip: never store HF in glass, in real life. In game, a Mekanism fluid tank is fine.
23. **Twelve Buckets of Plastic**: 12x `modern_industrialization:polyethylene_bucket` *(after: Polymerise)*
   > What: 12 buckets of polyethylene, the most of any ingredient.
   > How: polymerise ethylene in the Chemical Reactor, as in Petrochemistry.
   > Tip: fill them straight from your polymerisation reactor's output.
24. **Circuits and Steel**: 8x `modern_industrialization:processing_unit`; 4x `modern_industrialization:stainless_steel_plate` *(after: Eight Processing Units, Stainless Steel)*
   > What: 8 processing units and 4 stainless steel plates.
   > How: both come from lines you already run. Keep these apart from the ones meant for Energy Cores.
   > Tip: processing units are slow to make, so start these early.
25. **Heavy Elements**: 8x `chemlib:oganesson`; 4x `mekanism:pellet_plutonium`; 4x `mekanism:pellet_polonium` *(after: Oganesson ×8, Plutonium Pellets, Polonium Pellets)*
   > What: 8 oganesson, 4 plutonium pellets and 4 polonium pellets.
   > How: oganesson from the Fusion Chamber; pellets from your reactor's waste.
   > Tip: keep 4 polonium pellets aside. The core shells will happily eat them all.

### Creation

*The Seed is planted. Now shape what grows.*

1. **A New World**: checkmark *(after: Seed of a New World)*
   > You took the world apart, element by element, and learned to build it again.
   > Fire, steel, acid, oil, silicon, the atom, antimatter. Every tier was a lesson in chemistry, and you mastered them all.
   > The worlds out there are blank canvases now. Go make them yours.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > What now: this chapter is for after the Seed. Nothing here gates anything; it's what a demigod does with full power.
   > To the right: making matter. Rewrite nuclei with antimatter, compress a singularity, build armour from a collapsed star.
   > To the left: walking the worlds you can now reach, and holding the rarest parts of the periodic table in your hand.
2. **A Sample of Somewhere**: `warbuckscore:biome_capsule` *(after: A New World)*
   > Every world you have walked through, you can carry with you.
   > What: a Biome Capsule records the biome you stand in (sneak + right-click). It tells the Terraformer what to grow.
   > How: glass bottle, rubber sheet and any sapling. Travel to the biome you want, then record it.
   > Tip: capsules stack until filled; each one holds one biome.
3. **The Terraformer**: `warbuckscore:terraformer` *(after: A Sample of Somewhere, Two Charged Cores)*
   > The Seed was never meant to stay in your pocket.
   > What: the Terraformer (Warbucks Core) rewrites the biome around it, nearest chunks first, out to a 9x9 chunk area.
   > How: craft it from the Seed of a New World, processing units, stainless plates and energy cores. Right-click it with a filled Biome Capsule, then with Charged Energy Cores (each powers 9 chunks; sneak to insert a stack). Right-click empty-handed for status.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > What changes: grass and leaf colours, weather (rain or snow), and which mobs spawn, just like vanilla /fillbiome. Blocks you placed stay as they are.
   > Tip: you can change it again later: a new capsule restarts the spread with the new biome.
4. **A World You Chose**: checkmark *(after: The Terraformer)*
   > This is what the power was for.
   > What: let a Terraformer finish its whole area (status shows 81 / 81), then tick this off.
   > Tip: 9 Charged Energy Cores finish one Terraformer.
5. **Nucleosynthesis**: `mekanism:antiprotonic_nucleosynthesizer` *(after: A New World)*
   > Making something out of nothing was once your trade. This is close.
   > What: Mekanism's Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer feeds a few millibuckets of antimatter into an item and rebuilds it as something rarer.
   > Chemistry: nucleosynthesis is how stars make elements: lighter nuclei fuse into heavier ones. This machine borrows the idea.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe and the full list of transmutations. Pipe antimatter in from your SPS.
   > Tip: it works slowly. Give it its own antimatter tank.
6. **Hearts of the Sea**: 4x `minecraft:heart_of_the_sea` *(after: Nucleosynthesis)*
   > What: four Hearts of the Sea, each nucleosynthesized from a Nether Star with 5 mB of antimatter.
   > How: Nether Star in, antimatter in, wait about a minute.
   > Tip: a Heart of the Sea plus nautilus shells makes a Conduit: permanent water breathing and night vision around an ocean base.
7. **Skulls on Demand**: 6x `minecraft:wither_skeleton_skull` *(after: Hearts of the Sea)*
   > What: six wither skeleton skulls, made from ordinary skeleton skulls with 5 mB of antimatter each.
   > How: skeleton skulls drop when a charged creeper kills a skeleton, or from other sources (check JEI). Feed them to the Nucleosynthesizer.
   > Tip: that's enough for two more Withers, and two more Nether Stars for a second Seed.
8. **Echoes**: 32x `minecraft:echo_shard` *(after: Skulls on Demand)*
   > What: 32 echo shards, rebuilt from amethyst shards with 2 mB of antimatter each.
   > Chemistry: real amethyst is quartz (SiO₂) coloured purple by traces of iron and natural radiation. Here it becomes something no chemist could make.
   > How: amethyst shards from geodes or a budding amethyst farm. Nucleosynthesizer, 2 mB antimatter each.
   > Tip: echo shards make Recovery Compasses, which point to where you last died.
9. **Sixty-Four Nukes**: 64x `modern_industrialization:nuke` *(after: The First Two)*
   > What: MI's Nuke block. Sixty-four of them are crushed together to make a singularity.
   > Chemistry: a nuke combines fission (plutonium) and fusion fuel (deuterium and tritium, the heavy isotopes of hydrogen) around industrial TNT.
   > How: MI Assembler: 6 industrial TNT, 4 plutonium ingots, 2 processing units, 4 nuclear alloy plates, 100 mB deuterium, 50 mB tritium → 2 nukes.
   > Tip: that's 32 crafts, 64 processing units and 128 plutonium ingots. Automate it.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: two kinds of nuclear energy
   > Fission splits heavy nuclei like Pu-239 into lighter ones. Fusion joins light nuclei like deuterium (²H) and tritium (³H) into helium.
   > Both release energy because the products are more tightly bound than the inputs. Iron-56 sits at the bottom of that curve: nothing is gained by splitting it or fusing it.
   > Real thermonuclear weapons use a fission stage to compress and heat a fusion stage. MI's recipe follows the same idea.
10. **A Singularity**: `modern_industrialization:singularity` *(after: Sixty-Four Nukes, Ultradense Metal Ball)*
   > What: MI's Singularity: an ultradense metal ball collapsed by 64 nukes in the Implosion Compressor.
   > How: ultradense metal ball (tungsten large plates, lead plates and an iridium plate, check JEI) + 64 nukes → Implosion Compressor.
   > Tip: it's never used up in the Electrolyzer: it slowly bleeds out UU-matter, 1 mB every 2500 ticks. Build several Electrolyzers and several singularities.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: collapse
   > A real singularity is the centre of a black hole, where matter is crushed past every limit we know. Stars more than about 20 times the Sun's mass end this way.
   > Before that, there's neutron-star matter: electrons are pushed into protons until only neutrons remain. A teaspoon would weigh about a billion tonnes.
   > MI's singularity is a game item, not physics. But the idea, matter compressed until it becomes a source of something new, fits a demigod well.
11. **Quantum Upgrade**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_upgrade` *(after: A Singularity, Thirty-Two Upgrades, Eight More Quantum Circuits)*
   > What: the part that turns netherite armour into MI quantum armour.
   > How: MI Assembler: 32 highly advanced upgrades, 8 quantum circuits, 1 singularity, 1 quantum circuit board, 50 mB UU-matter.
   > Tip: 50 mB of UU-matter takes one Electrolyzer and singularity about 1.7 hours (1 mB per 2500 ticks). More singularities, more Electrolyzers.
12. **Quantum Armour**: `modern_industrialization:quantum_helmet`; `modern_industrialization:quantum_chestplate`; `modern_industrialization:quantum_leggings`; `modern_industrialization:quantum_boots` *(after: Quantum Upgrade, Netherite Set)*
   > Once you needed no armour at all. This is the next best thing.
   > What: MI's quantum armour: a full set, each piece a netherite piece plus a quantum upgrade.
   > How: MI Packer: netherite armour piece + 1 quantum upgrade, 200 ticks at 1,000,000 EU/t. Four upgrades for four pieces.
   > Tip: that draw is far above a plain Packer's limit. Check JEI and the MI guidebook for how machine upgrades raise it.
13. **Replicator**: `modern_industrialization:replicator` *(after: Quantum Upgrade)*
   > What: MI's Replicator copies items using UU-matter.
   > How: MI Assembler: quantum machine hull, 2 quantum upgrades, 4 quantum circuits, 500 mB UU-matter. Check JEI for what it can copy.
   > Tip: 500 mB is about 17 hours for one Electrolyzer. A long-term goal for a server, not a weekend.
14. **A Star in a Box**: `modern_industrialization:fusion_reactor`; `modern_industrialization:plasma_turbine` *(after: Six Fusion Chambers, Quantum Hulls)*
   > What: MI's fusion reactor makes helium plasma; the plasma turbine turns it into a flood of EU.
   > Chemistry: D + T → ⁴He + n. MI's reactor turns 1000 mB each of deuterium and tritium into helium plasma and hydrogen.
   > How: fusion reactor: 6 fusion chambers, a quantum machine hull and 2 quantum circuits. Plasma turbine: 4 superconductor coils, 2 quantum circuits, 2 titanium rotors and a quantum hull. The multiblock layout is in JEI and the MI guidebook.
   > Tip: deuterium-deuterium and helium-3 routes exist too (check JEI under the fusion reactor).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why fusion is hard
   > Nuclei are positively charged and repel each other. To fuse, they need temperatures over 100 million °C, hotter than the Sun's core.
   > The Sun manages at 15 million °C only because of its crushing gravity and its sheer size. On Earth we use magnetic bottles (tokamaks) or lasers instead.
   > In 2022 the US National Ignition Facility got more energy out of a fusion shot than its lasers put in, for the first time.
15. **Sixty-Four Superconductors**: 64x `modern_industrialization:superconductor_ingot` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: a stack of MI superconductor ingots, the material of MI's best cables and coils.
   > Chemistry: below a critical temperature, a superconductor carries current with zero resistance. Real high-temperature ones, like YBa₂Cu₃O₇, are copper oxides with yttrium and rare earths.
   > How: Mixer: iridium, annealed copper, yttrium and neodymium dusts → superconductor dust. Electric Blast Furnace → hot ingot → Vacuum Freezer.
   > Tip: the fusion chambers alone eat 30 superconductor coils (240 cables). Run several furnaces.

28. **A Breath of Noble Gas**: 64x any of `or(item(chemlib:helium)item(chemlib:neon)item(chemlib:argon)item(chemlib:krypton)item(chemlib:xenon)item(chemlib:radon))` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: any 64 noble gas items from ChemLib, in any mix.
   > Chemistry: noble gases have full outer electron shells, so they almost never react. Neon glows red in a discharge tube; xenon glows blue; radon is radioactive.
   > How: Alchemistry Dissolver on air-rich or gas-bearing items, or the Fusion Chamber (check JEI for which inputs give which gas).
   > Tip: helium is the lightest: fuse two hydrogen and you're there.
29. **The Rare Earths**: 64x any of `or(item(chemlib:lanthanum)item(chemlib:cerium)item(chemlib:praseodymium)item(chemlib:neodymium)item(chemlib:promethium)item(chemlib:samarium)item(chemlib:europium)item(chemlib:gadolinium)item(chemlib:terbium)item(chemlib:dysprosium)item(chemlib:holmium)item(chemlib:erbium)item(chemlib:thulium)item(chemlib:ytterbium)item(chemlib:lutetium))` *(after: A Breath of Noble Gas)*
   > What: any 64 lanthanide items from ChemLib: lanthanum through lutetium.
   > Chemistry: the lanthanides fill the 4f electron shell, which sits deep inside the atom. That's why they're so alike and so hard to separate.
   > How: Fusion Chamber (pairs that add up to 57-71) or the Dissolver on rare-earth-bearing items (check JEI).
   > Tip: neodymium makes the strongest permanent magnets; europium makes red phosphors in screens.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why 'rare' earths?
   > They aren't rare. Cerium is about as common as copper in the Earth's crust. They're 'rare' because they never form rich deposits on their own.
   > Separating them took chemists over a century. Their outer electrons are nearly the same, so their chemistry is nearly the same; only the slow shrinking of the atoms across the row (the lanthanide contraction) tells them apart.
   > Industry separates them by solvent extraction, hundreds of stages long. Your Fusion Chamber skips all that.
30. **Island of Stability**: 64x any of `or(item(chemlib:oganesson)item(chemlib:tennessine)item(chemlib:livermorium)item(chemlib:moscovium)item(chemlib:flerovium)item(chemlib:nihonium))` *(after: The Actinides)*
   > What: any 64 of the six newest elements: nihonium, flerovium, moscovium, livermorium, tennessine and oganesson.
   > Chemistry: all six were made in the last 25 years, a few atoms at a time, and decay within seconds or less.
   > How: Alchemistry Fusion Chamber. Automate the inputs and let it run.
   > Tip: physicists predict an 'island of stability' near 114 protons and 184 neutrons, where superheavy nuclei might last much longer. No one has reached it yet.
31. **Demigod**: checkmark *(after: The Terraformer, Quantum Armour, Shining Alloy, Your First Singularity, Other Skies, Island of Stability, Echoes)*
   > You don't remember being this any more. You simply are.
   > What: you've planted the Seed, walked every world, built armour from a collapsed star, and held the whole periodic table.
   > Now: build. A city, a garden on Mars, a pocket world for every friend on the server. The tools are yours.
   > The new world is waiting. It's whatever you make it.
32. **Pressure Not Required**: 64x `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Nucleosynthesis)*
   > What: the Nucleosynthesizer turns coal into diamond with 4 mB of antimatter. You found it.
   > Chemistry: both are carbon. Graphite and diamond differ only in how the atoms bond: sheets of rings versus a rigid 3D lattice. Nature needs about 50,000 atmospheres to make the change.
   > Tip: 64 diamonds from 64 coal. Your younger self, swinging an iron pickaxe, would be furious.
33. **Where It Began**: find biome `biomesoplenty:origin_valley` *(after: Rare Ground)*
   > What: Biomes O' Plenty's Origin Valley, built to look like the very first versions of Minecraft.
   > Bright grass, roses, plain old trees. You remember a world this simple. It was the first one you made.
   > Tip: it's rare. If you found it by chance, consider it a gift.
34. **Ultradense Metal Ball**: `modern_industrialization:ultradense_metal_ball` *(after: Tungsten Large Plates)*
   > What: the core that 64 nukes crush into a singularity.
   > Chemistry: tungsten, lead and iridium are among the densest metals there are. Iridium and osmium tie for the record at about 22.6 g/cm³, twice as dense as lead.
   > How: Assembler: 4 tungsten large plates, 4 lead plates and 1 iridium plate.
35. **Quantum Sword**: checkmark *(after: Quantum Upgrade)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Quantum Sword" on the Gear and Comfort page. Click to dismiss.
36. **Two Charged Cores**: 2x `kubejs:energy_core` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: the Terraformer is built around 2 charged Energy Cores, and every 9 chunks it reshapes burns one more.
   > How: empty core (4 stainless plates, 4 polonium pellets, a processing unit) → MI Assembler at 512 EU/t for 6000 ticks.
   > Tip: keep the charging Assembler running for the rest of the game.
37. **A Stack of Industrial TNT**: 64x `modern_industrialization:industrial_tnt` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: 32 nuke crafts take 192 Industrial TNT. Start with a stack.
   > Chemistry: nitrogen compounds store energy because the N≡N triple bond they release is so stable. Making N₂ again sets it all free at once.
   > How: Mixer: 4 sand + 3 flint + 250 mB toluene + 1000 mB nitrogen → 4 TNT.
38. **Plutonium Ingots**: 16x `modern_industrialization:plutonium_ingot` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: 32 nuke crafts take 128 plutonium ingots. This is the first eighth.
   > Chemistry: plutonium metal has six different crystal forms between room temperature and its melting point, more than any other element.
   > How: Electric Blast Furnace (128 EU/t): 1 plutonium dust → 1 ingot. The dust comes from centrifuging depleted fuel rods.
39. **Deuterium and Tritium**: `modern_industrialization:deuterium_bucket`; `modern_industrialization:tritium_bucket` *(after: A New World)*
   > What: every nuke craft takes 100 mB deuterium and 50 mB tritium; the fusion reactor burns both by the bucket.
   > Chemistry: deuterium has one neutron, tritium two. Tritium is radioactive (half-life about 12 years), so nature has almost none.
   > How: Centrifuge hydrogen, or let the Nuclear Reactor's fluid hatches turn hydrogen and deuterium into heavier isotopes (check JEI).
40. **The First Two**: 2x `modern_industrialization:nuke` *(after: A Stack of Industrial TNT, Plutonium Ingots, Deuterium and Tritium)*
   > What: one Assembler run of MI's nuke recipe.
   > How: Assembler at 32 EU/t: 6 industrial TNT, 4 plutonium ingots, 2 processing units, 4 nuclear alloy plates, 100 mB deuterium and 50 mB tritium → 2 nukes.
   > Tip: 31 more runs to go. Automate the inputs before you start.

   > What: the ultradense metal ball is wrapped in 4 tungsten large plates.

   > How: Implosion Compressor makes tungsten ingots; Compressor → plates; 4 plates → 1 large plate.

### Market: Blocks, Food and Wild Goods

*Buy more of the blocks, food and wild goods you've already gathered.*

1. **The World Stall**: checkmark *(after: The Demigod's Market)*
   > You remember the harvest festivals held in your name. The world still sends its gifts.
   > What: this stall sells building blocks, food, crops, saplings, mob drops and the stone and plants of other worlds.
   > How: an item appears here only after the quest where you first got it. Hand in the tokens and claim the bundle; the entry resets so you can buy again.
   > Tip: tokens save gathering, never exploring. Each world's goods only appear once you've been there.
   > Tip: the space stall costs Greater Demigod Tokens (1 Greater = 9 tokens; craft them in a grid).

## Tools and Gear

### Gear and Comfort

*Better tools from better materials, and a soft place to land.*

1. **Repair Kits**: `silentgear:crude_repair_kit` *(after: Tools from Parts)*
   > You remember tools that never wore out. These will, but you can mend them.
   > What: Silent Gear tools don't break for good; at zero durability they just stop working until repaired.
   > How: craft a Crude Repair Kit, load it with matching material, then combine it with the tool in a crafting grid.
   > Tip: a better kit (Sturdy, then Crimson and Azure) holds more material and repairs more per use.
2. **Blaze Gold**: 4x `silentgear:blaze_gold_ingot` *(after: Repair Kits, Into the Fire)*
   > What: Silent Gear's first magic alloy. It's a key ingredient of the Material Grader and the Starlight Charger.
   > Chemistry: gold (Au) is a noble metal: it barely reacts with anything, which is why it's found as native nuggets. Blaze gold is fictional; the blaze powder does the work.
   > How: gold ingot + 2 blaze powder in the Alloy Forge, or check JEI for the early crafting route.
   > Tip: keep a stack spare. Blaze gold blocks also go into the Starlight Charger.
3. **Material Grader**: checkmark *(after: Blaze Gold)*
   > What: this quest moved to the Silent Gear page, which covers the same item. Click the check to clear it here.
4. **Salvager**: checkmark *(after: Material Grader)*
   > What: this quest moved to the Silent Gear page, which covers the same item. Click the check to clear it here.
5. **Crimson Iron**: 8x `silentgear:crimson_iron_ingot` *(after: Repair Kits, Into the Fire)*
   > What: crimson iron ore generates in Nether biomes. It's the base of crimson steel and the Alloy Forge.
   > How: mine crimson iron ore in the Nether (Jade shows the name), then smelt the raw ore.
   > Tip: run a few through the Alchemistry Dissolver and see which real elements it gives back.
6. **Crimson Steel**: 4x `silentgear:crimson_steel_ingot` *(after: Crimson Iron)*
   > What: a tough, heat-loving alloy for tool heads and the Alloy Forge frame.
   > Chemistry: real steel is iron with a little carbon (under about 2%); the carbon atoms jam the iron lattice so it can't slip. Crimson steel is the fictional cousin.
   > How: the first ingots are a shaped craft (crimson iron, blaze rods, magma cream); check JEI.
7. **The Alloy Forge**: checkmark *(after: Crimson Steel)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Alloy Forge" on the Silent Gear page. Click to dismiss.
8. **Azure Electrum**: 4x `silentgear:azure_electrum_ingot` *(after: Alloy Forge, The End)*
   > What: azure silver ore generates in the End. Alloyed with gold it becomes azure electrum, a fast, enchantable metal.
   > Chemistry: real electrum is a natural gold–silver alloy (Au–Ag); the ancient Lydians struck the first coins from it.
   > How: azure silver ore needs a netherite-tier pickaxe (netherite, refined obsidian, crimson steel or better; see the Harvest Tiers chapter). Then Alloy Forge: an azure silver block, 2 gold ingots and an ender pearl.
9. **Tyrian Steel**: 4x `silentgear:tyrian_steel_ingot` *(after: Azure Electrum)*
   > What: the top Silent Gear alloy: crimson steel, azure electrum, crushed shulker shell and netherite scrap.
   > Chemistry: Tyrian purple was a real dye made from sea snails, once worth its weight in silver. The steel just borrowed the colour.
   > How: Alloy Forge (check JEI). Crush shulker shells first.
10. **The Paxel**: `mekanismtools:iron_paxel` *(after: Iron Tools)*
   > What: A paxel is a pickaxe, axe and shovel in one tool. Mekanism Tools adds them for every material, from wood to refined obsidian.
   > How: Craft an iron pickaxe, axe and shovel together with 2 sticks (check JEI).
   > Tip: One tool slot instead of three leaves more room for ore.
11. **Paxel Collector**: `mekanismtools:wood_paxel`; `mekanismtools:stone_paxel`; `mekanismtools:gold_paxel`; `mekanismtools:diamond_paxel` *(after: The Paxel)*
   > What: Craft the early paxels you skipped, plus a diamond one for the long haul.
   > Chemistry: Gold is soft because its atoms slide past each other easily. Diamond is the hardest natural material because every carbon atom is locked to four neighbours.
   > How: Same recipe as the iron paxel: pickaxe, axe and shovel of one material, plus 2 sticks.
12. **Osmium Paxel**: `mekanismtools:osmium_paxel` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: Mekanism's signature metal as a paxel: more durability and speed than bronze, iron tier for mining.
   > Chemistry: osmium (Os) is the densest natural element at about 22.6 g/cm³, twice as dense as lead.
   > How: osmium ore generates in the Overworld; smelt or process it, then craft the pickaxe, axe and shovel and combine them with a stick (check JEI).
   > Tip: your steel paxel from T1 already mines at diamond tier. This one is about durability and speed.
13. **The Ultimate Paxel**: `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_paxel` *(after: Osmium Paxel)*
   > You remember a hammer that could split mountains. This is a start.
   > What: refined obsidian is Mekanism's toughest material, and its paxel is the best of the line (netherite tier).
   > How: infuse obsidian dust with diamond in the Metallurgic Infuser, then press the refined obsidian dust in the Osmium Compressor (check JEI).
   > Tip: the same ingots make the Atomic Disassembler and much of Mekanism's late gear.
14. **Atomic Disassembler**: checkmark *(after: The Ultimate Paxel)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Atomic Disassembler" on the Mekanism: Power page. Click to dismiss.
15. **Bottled Oxygen**: `mekanism:scuba_mask`; `mekanism:scuba_tank` *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: the Scuba Mask and Tank let you breathe underwater for as long as the tank has oxygen.
   > Chemistry: the Electrolytic Separator splits water: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. The O₂ fills the tank; the H₂ is fuel.
   > How: steel, a control circuit and a chemical tank (check JEI). Fill the tank from a Chemical Tank or the separator's oxygen output.
   > Tip: great for ocean monuments and underwater prospecting.
16. **Free Runners**: checkmark *(after: Bottled Oxygen)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Free Runners" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
17. **MekaSuit**: `mekanism:mekasuit_helmet`; `mekanism:mekasuit_bodyarmor` *(after: Bottled Oxygen, EV: Processing Units)*
   > You remember armour that was never armour, only certainty. This is the closest a mortal gets.
   > What: Mekanism's modular power armour. Add modules for flight, night vision, magnet, radiation shielding and more.
   > Chemistry: it needs HDPE sheets (polyethylene: long C₂H₄ chains) and polonium pellets. Real ²¹⁰Po is made by hitting bismuth-209 with neutrons; Mekanism makes it from nuclear waste in the Solar Neutron Activator.
   > How: netherite armour, HDPE sheets, ultimate control circuits, polonium pellets and induction cells (check JEI). Install modules in the Modification Station.
18. **Hazmat Gear**: `mekanism:hazmat_mask` *(after: Bottled Oxygen)*
   > What: the full hazmat suit stops Mekanism radiation from building up in you. Cheap and worth having before fission.
   > Chemistry: lead (Pb) is dense and has many electrons, so it absorbs gamma rays well.
   > How: lead ingots and orange dye for each piece (check JEI).
19. **Hydrogen Jetpack**: checkmark *(after: Bottled Oxygen)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Jetpack" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
20. **Jetpacks**: `ironjetpacks:basic_coil`; `ironjetpacks:jetpack` *(after: Analog Circuit)*

41. **Every Tool Starts Here**: `minecraft:stick`
   > You remember holding a hammer that had no handle, because it didn't need one. Mortal tools do.
   > What: this page is a tour of tools: a short ladder of ores, then one quest for each pickaxe and sword family in the pack.
   > Chemistry: a stick is wood, a composite of cellulose fibres in a lignin glue: stiff along the grain, light, and easy to replace.
   > How: two planks stacked make four sticks. Only the ore ladder is required; the collections are optional.
   > Tip: the Harvest Tiers page explains which pick mines what; this page is about owning them.
42. **Cobblestone**: `minecraft:cobblestone` *(after: Every Tool Starts Here)*
   > What: the rock under every Overworld biome. A wooden pick breaks stone into cobblestone.
   > Chemistry: Overworld stone stands in for real crustal rock: mostly silicate minerals, feldspars and quartz, built on SiO₄ tetrahedra.
   > How: mine any stone with a wooden pickaxe.
   > Tip: keep a stack: furnaces, stone tools and many early machines eat it.
43. **Raw Iron**: `minecraft:raw_iron` *(after: Cobblestone)*
   > What: iron ore needs a stone pick. Raw iron smelts into the metal most of your early gear is made of.
   > Chemistry: iron ores are oxides such as haematite, Fe₂O₃. Smelting strips the oxygen with carbon: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
   > How: mine iron ore with a stone pickaxe or better.
   > Tip: ore processing multiplies it later; don't smelt your whole stock on day one.
44. **Diamond**: `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Raw Iron)*
   > What: diamond ore needs an iron pick and sits deep in the deepslate.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon with each atom bonded to four others in a rigid 3D network. Graphite is the same element in flat sheets.
   > How: branch-mine near the bottom of the world with an iron pickaxe.
   > Tip: Fortune works on diamond ore. Save one good pick for it.
45. **Ancient Debris**: `minecraft:ancient_debris` *(after: Diamond)*
   > What: ancient debris hides low in the Nether and needs a diamond-tier pick. It smelts into netherite scrap.
   > Chemistry: netherite is fiction, but its trick is real: some alloys keep their strength far above the temperature where steel softens.
   > How: dig tunnels around Y 15 in the Nether with a diamond (or steel) pick. It ignores explosions, so beds and TNT work.
   > Tip: it doesn't burn in lava either. Neither does anything made from it.

### Armour and Harvest Tiers

*Every armour set in the pack, trims and their materials, and which pickaxe mines what.*

1. **The Hardness of Things**: checkmark *(after: Sticks and a Wooden Pick)*
   > Once you could split a mountain with a look. Now you need the right pick. You remember why: everything has a hardness.
   > What: every ore needs a pickaxe of a certain tier: wood, stone, iron, diamond, netherite. Too weak a pick breaks the block slowly and drops nothing.
   > Chemistry: hardness is resistance to scratching and denting; toughness is resistance to cracking. A good tool needs both, and they pull against each other.
   > How: look at a block: Jade shows the tool it needs and turns red when yours is too weak. This page walks up the tiers.
   > Tip: this pack raises some tiers: MI titanium, tungsten, platinum and iridium ores need iron, and the rocket metals climb from iron to netherite.
2. **Flint**: 4x `minecraft:flint` *(after: The Hardness of Things)*
   > What: flint drops from gravel. Silent Gear makes tool heads from it, and it lights the Nether portal.
   > Chemistry: flint and chert are microcrystalline quartz, SiO₂, about 7 on the Mohs scale: harder than steel. It breaks with a curved, shell-like (conchoidal) fracture that leaves a razor edge.
   > How: dig gravel with a shovel; each block has a small chance to drop flint instead.
   > Tip: a Silent Gear pickaxe with a flint head mines like stone, but you can repair and upgrade it.
3. **Stone Tier**: 8x `minecraft:raw_iron`; 8x `minecraft:raw_copper` *(after: The Hardness of Things, Stone Age)*
   > What: a stone pickaxe (or better) opens iron, copper and lapis, plus almost every Modern Industrialization and Mekanism ore: tin, lead, nickel, antimony, bauxite, salt, monazite, uranium, osmium and fluorite.
   > Chemistry: a stone pick is a rock hitting a rock. It works on iron ore because the iron minerals (haematite Fe₂O₃, magnetite Fe₃O₄) are softer than the granite-like stone of the head... roughly.
   > How: mine 8 raw iron and 8 raw copper with any stone-tier pick.
   > Tip: you can't mine gold, redstone or diamond yet. Mark where you saw them and come back with iron.
4. **Bronze Age**: 8x `modern_industrialization:raw_tin` *(after: Stone Tier, The First Alloy)*
   > What: bronze tools are iron tier (Mekanism bronze, Silent Gear bronze): more durable than stone, and they reach gold, redstone and diamond.
   > Chemistry: pure copper is soft, about Mohs 3. Add roughly 12% tin and the bigger tin atoms sit in the copper lattice and pin the defects (dislocations) that let metal bend. That is solid-solution strengthening, and it started an age.
   > How: mine 8 raw tin. Tin ore needs only a stone pick; its mineral, cassiterite (SnO₂), is actually harder than iron ore.
   > Tip: the bronze paxel (Bronze Age on the T0 page) is a pick, axe and shovel in one.
5. **Iron Tier**: 4x `minecraft:raw_gold`; 8x `minecraft:redstone`; `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Stone Tier, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > Iron rings against stone, and something in you rings back. You remember iron.
   > What: an iron-tier pick opens gold, redstone, diamond and emerald, Create zinc, AE2 sky stone, Silent Gear crimson iron, and in this pack the hard MI ores: titanium, tungsten, platinum and iridium.
   > Chemistry: pure iron is soft (about Mohs 4). Iron from a blast furnace (pig iron) carries about 4% carbon as brittle iron carbide, so it shatters. Useful iron sits between the two.
   > How: mine 4 raw gold, 8 redstone and a diamond with an iron pickaxe, iron paxel, bronze or osmium tools.
   > Tip: diamonds sit deep (near Y -58). Branch-mine in deepslate.
6. **Hard Ores**: 4x `modern_industrialization:raw_tungsten` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: in this pack MI titanium, tungsten, platinum and iridium ores need an iron-tier pick. The metals inside still need the chemistry lines.
   > Chemistry: their real minerals are hard: wolframite ((Fe,Mn)WO₄) about 4-4.5, ilmenite (FeTiO₃) 5-6, sperrylite (PtAs₂) 6-7. Tungsten itself melts at 3422 °C, higher than any other metal.
   > How: mine 4 raw tungsten. Rich tungsten deposits sit at their own depth; check the ore pages in JEI.
   > Tip: a stone pick on these ores gets you nothing but a broken block. Bring iron.
7. **Lapis Tools**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_paxel))` *(after: Stone Tier)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools makes a lapis pickaxe and paxel. They mine at stone tier but enchant very well.
   > Chemistry: lapis lazuli is a rock, not one mineral: mostly lazurite (a sodium aluminosilicate with sulfur) about Mohs 5-5.5. The blue comes from S₃⁻ radical ions trapped in the crystal.
   > How: lapis and sticks, shaped like any pick (check JEI).
   > Tip: ground lapis was ultramarine, once worth more than gold to painters.
8. **Iron-Tier Cousins**: 1x any of `or(item(justdirethings:ferricore_pickaxe)item(twilightforest:ironwood_pickaxe)item(undergarden:cloggrum_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:bronze_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:osmium_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:osmium_paxel))` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: each of these mines exactly what an iron pick does: ferricore (Just Dire Things), ironwood (Twilight), cloggrum (Undergarden), bronze and osmium (Mekanism Tools).
   > Chemistry: osmium is the densest element (22.6 g/cm³) and quite hard, but brittle: real osmium is almost never used for tools, only for tiny wear-proof tips like old pen nibs.
   > How: craft any one of them; their mods' pages show the recipes.
   > Tip: durability and speed differ a lot between them even at the same tier. Check the tooltip.
9. **Diamond Pickaxe**: `minecraft:diamond_pickaxe` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: the vanilla road to diamond tier: obsidian, crying obsidian and ancient debris. Also the base for Mystical Agriculture tools.
   > Chemistry: diamond is carbon with every atom bonded to four neighbours in a 3D network (sp³). It's Mohs 10, the hardest natural material, but it cleaves along flat planes: a sharp knock in the right direction splits it.
   > How: three diamonds and two sticks.
   > Tip: a steel paxel (T1) is already diamond tier. Spend early diamonds on machines, not picks, if you're short.
10. **A Grown Pickaxe**: 1x any of `or(item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:prudentium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:tertium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:imperium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:supremium_pickaxe))` *(after: Diamond Pickaxe)*
   > What: Mystical Agriculture tools have no 'can't mine' list: even an inferium pick breaks azure silver, naquadah and dreadrock.
   > How: a diamond pickaxe with two inferium ingots and two inferium gemstones around it (check JEI). Higher essences make it faster, not 'higher tier'.
   > Tip: it still can't give you the metal: the ores need the same chemistry lines as ever.
11. **Fast and Useless**: checkmark *(after: Stone Tier)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Golden Pickaxe" on the Gear and Comfort page. Click to dismiss.
12. **The Scratch Test**: `minecraft:calcite`; `chemlib:calcium_sulfate`; `mekanism:fluorite_gem`; `chemlib:hydroxylapatite`; `minecraft:quartz`; `chemlib:aluminum_oxide`; `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: in 1812 Friedrich Mohs ranked ten minerals by which scratches which. Seven of them exist here.
   > Chemistry: gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O (2), calcite CaCO₃ (3), fluorite CaF₂ (4), apatite Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH) (5), quartz SiO₂ (7), corundum Al₂O₃ (9), diamond C (10). Talc (1), orthoclase (6) and topaz (8) are missing.
   > How: calcite in dripstone caves and amethyst geodes; fluorite from Mekanism ore; nether quartz; diamond. Calcium sulfate, hydroxylapatite and aluminium oxide come from the Alchemistry machines (check JEI).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Chemistry: the scale only ranks, it doesn't measure. Diamond (10) is about four times harder than corundum (9), while corundum is only a bit harder than topaz (8).
   > Tip: a fingernail is about 2.5, a copper coin 3.5, a steel knife 5.5, window glass 5.5. That's the field geologist's whole kit.
13. **Hard Rock, Soft Ore**: checkmark *(after: The Scratch Test)*
   > What: the ores you mine have real hardnesses, and they don't line up with the game's tiers at all.
   > Chemistry: galena (PbS, lead ore) 2.5; bauxite 1-3; fluorite 4; wolframite 4-4.5; uraninite (UO₂) 5-6; ilmenite 5-6; cassiterite (SnO₂) 6-7; sperrylite (PtAs₂) 6-7. Tin ore is harder than iron ore, yet the game puts it lower.
   > How: read it, then click the check.
   > Tip: real miners don't pick ore apart by hand: they blast the rock and crush it, then separate by density and froth flotation.
14. **Green Beryl**: checkmark *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Emerald" on this page. Click to dismiss.
15. **Tungsten Carbide**: 2x `modern_industrialization:tungsten_dust` *(after: Hard Ores)*
   > What: the real material that nearly every drill bit and cutting insert on Earth is made of.
   > Chemistry: heat tungsten powder with carbon at 1400-2000 °C: W + C → WC. Tungsten carbide is about Mohs 9 and keeps its hardness when red hot. Pressed with 6-12% cobalt as a binder it becomes 'cemented carbide', hard and tough at once.
   > How: macerate raw tungsten into 2 tungsten dust.
   > Tip: tungsten carbide is about twice as dense as steel. Pick up a carbide drill bit and it feels wrong.
16. **Wooden Tools**: `minecraft:wooden_sword`; `minecraft:wooden_axe`; `minecraft:wooden_shovel` *(after: The Hardness of Things)*
   > What: the full wooden set: weak, cheap, and a fine fuel once it wears out.
   > Chemistry: wood is a natural composite: long cellulose fibres, (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ chains of glucose, glued together by lignin. It's strong along the grain and splits easily across it.
   > How: planks and sticks, shaped like any tool.
   > Tip: a broken wooden tool burns in a furnace for as long as a plank. Nothing goes to waste.
17. **Soft Gold**: 8x `minecraft:gold_ingot`; `minecraft:golden_sword` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: a golden sword hits about as hard as a wooden one and wears out faster. Piglins like it, though.
   > Chemistry: gold is the most malleable metal: one gram can be beaten into a leaf about a square metre wide and a few hundred atoms thick. Great for leaf, useless for an edge.
   > How: smelt 8 gold ingots from raw gold (needs an iron-tier pick), then craft the sword.
   > Tip: wearing one piece of gold armour keeps most piglins calm in the Nether.
18. **Diamond Sword and Shovel**: `minecraft:diamond_sword`; `minecraft:diamond_shovel` *(after: Diamond Pickaxe)*
   > What: the diamond sword is the vanilla weapon to beat until netherite; the shovel digs sand and gravel at speed.
   > Chemistry: real diamond blades exist: diamond scalpels cut with an edge only a few nanometres wide. They're kept for eye surgery because one sideways knock can chip them.
   > How: two diamonds and a stick for the sword, one diamond and two sticks for the shovel.
   > Tip: enchant before you upgrade to netherite: the enchantments carry over.
19. **Mekanism Blades**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:bronze_sword)item(mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_sword)item(mekanismtools:osmium_sword)item(mekanismtools:steel_sword)item(mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_sword)item(mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_sword))` *(after: Bronze Age)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools makes a sword in every one of its metals: bronze, lapis, osmium, steel, refined glowstone and refined obsidian. Any one counts.
   > Chemistry: a good sword is a compromise. Hard steel keeps an edge; soft steel bends instead of snapping. Japanese smiths welded both into one blade and quenched it with clay on the spine.
   > How: two ingots (or gems) of the metal and a stick, like any sword (check JEI).
   > Tip: refined obsidian is the best of the set; steel is the cheapest one worth carrying.

### Armour: Steel and Obsidian

*The diamond tier without diamonds, and beyond*

1. **Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds**: 4x `minecraft:obsidian`; `minecraft:crying_obsidian` *(after: Iron Tier, Steel Paxel)*
   > You remember quenching a blade in a cold river, and the hiss of it.
   > What: Mekanism steel tools are diamond tier. Your steel paxel already mines obsidian, crying obsidian and ancient debris, long before you own a diamond pick.
   > Chemistry: steel is iron with 0.2-2% carbon. Heat it red hot and quench it in water and it becomes martensite: very hard, but brittle. Temper it (reheat to 200-600 °C) and it trades a little hardness for toughness.
   > How: mine 4 obsidian and a crying obsidian with the steel paxel (or any diamond-tier tool). Obsidian forms where water meets lava.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Chemistry: obsidian isn't actually hard: it's volcanic glass, mostly SiO₂ that cooled too fast to crystallise, about Mohs 5.5. It snaps to edges sharper than steel, which is why surgeons still sometimes use obsidian blades.
   > Tip: the game makes obsidian slow to mine for its blast resistance, not its hardness. Real obsidian shatters under a hammer.
2. **Netherite Tier**: 4x `minecraft:netherite_scrap`; `minecraft:netherite_upgrade_smithing_template` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds, Into the Fire)*
   > What: a netherite-tier tool opens Silent Gear azure silver ore (the End), Mekanism Extras naquadah ore and, much later, Ad Astra calorite.
   > Chemistry: netherite is fiction. The real champion of hard tools is tungsten carbide (WC, Mohs about 9), cemented with a little cobalt so it doesn't shatter: a ceramic-metal composite, or cermet.
   > How: smelt ancient debris into scrap; four scrap and four gold make a netherite ingot. The upgrade template comes from bastion chests.
   > Tip: copy a template with 7 diamonds and a netherrack before you use your last one.
3. **Azure Silver**: 4x `silentgear:raw_azure_silver` *(after: Netherite Tier, The End)*
   > What: azure silver ore grows on End islands and needs a netherite-tier tool. It's the base of Silent Gear's azure electrum.
   > How: mine 4 raw azure silver in the End with a netherite, refined obsidian or eclipse alloy pick.
   > Tip: a diamond pick just bounces off it; check the Jade tooltip first.
4. **Refined Obsidian**: 2x `mekanism:ingot_refined_obsidian` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: refined obsidian tools are netherite tier, no Nether trip needed. They're also Mekanism Tools' strongest set.
   > Chemistry: infusing osmium into obsidian dust is invented, but the idea is real: cermets (ceramic grains in a metal binder) are what drill bits and cutting inserts are made of.
   > How: Metallurgic Infuser: obsidian dust + diamond infusion → refined obsidian dust, then the Osmium Compressor (check JEI).
   > Tip: the refined obsidian paxel is on the Tools page; the armour is on the Mekanism page.
5. **Beyond Netherite**: 16x `undergarden:dreadrock` *(after: Netherite Tier, The Undergarden, Forgotten Tools)*
   > Harder was never the whole answer. You remember a stone that only its own metal could cut.
   > What: dreadrock and its utherium and rogdorium ores need a Forgotten tool. Netherite fails here: dreadrock is on its 'can't mine' list.
   > Chemistry: 'harder' is not one number. A cutting edge has to out-scratch the mineral, survive the impact and not wear or react away. A diamond bit cuts granite but dissolves into hot steel, because carbon diffuses into iron.
   > How: mine 16 dreadrock at the bottom of the Undergarden with a Forgotten pickaxe.
   > Tip: warden and resonarium tools (Deeper and Darker) also mine it.
6. **Ores of Other Worlds**: checkmark *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds, One Small Step)*
   > What: in this pack the rocket metals climb the ladder: Moon desh needs an iron pick, Mars ostrum a diamond-tier pick, Venus calorite a netherite-tier pick.
   > Chemistry: the three are fiction, but real space mining would face the same problem: unknown minerals, unknown hardness. Geologists still carry a steel knife and a glass plate to test them.
   > How: bring a netherite-tier tool on every trip past the Moon. The desh, ostrum and calorite quests are on the T7 and Space pages.
   > Tip: a refined obsidian paxel covers all three and doesn't need the Nether.
7. **Every Block**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:atomic_disassembler)item(mekanism:meka_tool)item(deeperdarker:warden_pickaxe))` *(after: Refined Obsidian)*
   > No block refuses you now. You remember this: not strength, but understanding.
   > What: the Atomic Disassembler, the Meka-Tool and the warden pickaxe have no 'can't mine' list. They break every block in the pack, dreadrock included.
   > Chemistry: an energy tool doesn't scratch. It's closer to a laser or plasma cutter: put enough energy into a spot and the bonds break whatever the hardness.
   > How: the Atomic Disassembler is on the Tools page, the Meka-Tool on the Mekanism page, the warden pickaxe on the Deeper and Darker page. Any one of them counts.
   > Tip: energy tools need charging; keep a charger or an Energy Cube near your base.
8. **Diamond-Tier Cousins**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:steel_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_paxel)item(justdirethings:blazegold_pickaxe)item(justdirethings:celestigem_pickaxe)item(twilightforest:steeleaf_pickaxe)item(twilightforest:knightmetal_pickaxe)item(undergarden:utherium_pickaxe)item(modern_industrialization:steam_mining_drill))` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds)*
   > What: all of these are diamond tier: Mekanism steel and refined glowstone, JDT blazegold and celestigem, Twilight steeleaf and knightmetal, Undergarden utherium, and MI's Steam Mining Drill.
   > Chemistry: the Steam Mining Drill is honest engineering: a hardened bit turned by a steam engine. Real drill bits use tungsten carbide or industrial diamond tips on a tough steel body.
   > How: craft any one of them; each mod page and JEI have the recipe.
   > Tip: the steam drill burns fuel instead of wearing out, and digs 3x3. Its tooltip lists the modes.
9. **Netherite Pickaxe**: `minecraft:netherite_pickaxe` *(after: Netherite Tier, Diamond Pickaxe)*
   > What: the vanilla netherite-tier pick. Upgrading keeps every enchantment on your diamond pick.
   > How: smithing table: netherite upgrade template + diamond pickaxe + netherite ingot.
   > Tip: netherite items float in lava and don't burn. Drop one in the Nether and it can be fished back out.
10. **Netherite-Tier Cousins**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_pickaxe)item(mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_paxel)item(mekanismtools:netherite_paxel)item(justdirethings:eclipsealloy_pickaxe)item(justdirethings:eclipsealloy_paxel)item(twilightforest:fiery_pickaxe)item(modern_industrialization:diesel_mining_drill))` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > What: all netherite tier: Mekanism refined obsidian and netherite paxel, JDT eclipse alloy, Twilight fiery, MI's Diesel Mining Drill. A Silent Gear pick with a crimson steel, azure electrum or tyrian steel head counts too (its tier comes from the head).
   > Chemistry: fiery metal is 'quenched' in fiery blood; real metallurgists do the same with oil, brine or polymer baths to control how fast the steel cools.
   > How: craft any one of the listed tools (check JEI).
   > Tip: the diesel drill is listed on the T5 page as part of Diesel Toys.
11. **Bronze Armour**: `mekanismtools:bronze_helmet`; `mekanismtools:bronze_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:bronze_leggings`; `mekanismtools:bronze_boots` *(after: Bronze Age)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools bronze armour is a touch better than iron, and it saves your iron for machines.
   > Chemistry: Bronze Age armour really was bronze, often hammered cold: working the metal (work hardening) piles up dislocations and makes it harder still.
   > How: 24 bronze ingots, shaped like any armour set. MI bronze counts (it's a c:ingots/bronze ingot).
12. **Steel Armour**: `mekanismtools:steel_helmet`; `mekanismtools:steel_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:steel_leggings`; `mekanismtools:steel_boots` *(after: Diamond Tier, Without Diamonds)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools steel armour: better than iron, from the steel you already make in MI.
   > Chemistry: real plate armour was hardened on the outside and left soft inside (case hardening): a hard face to stop blades, a tough core so it dents instead of cracking.
   > How: 24 steel ingots, shaped like any armour set (any c:ingots/steel counts).
13. **Diamond Armour**: `minecraft:diamond_helmet`; `minecraft:diamond_chestplate`; `minecraft:diamond_leggings`; `minecraft:diamond_boots` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: the full vanilla diamond set: the step before netherite, and the base you'll upgrade.
   > Chemistry: real diamond armour would be a disaster: diamond is hard but brittle, and a solid plate would crack on the first heavy blow. Real body armour stacks hard ceramic plates (boron carbide, B₄C) on tough fibres.
   > How: 24 diamonds. If that hurts, make the steel set first and come back.
14. **Netherite Armour**: `minecraft:netherite_helmet`; `minecraft:netherite_chestplate`; `minecraft:netherite_leggings`; `minecraft:netherite_boots` *(after: Netherite Tier, Diamond Armour)*
   > Your skin is mortal now, so you wear the strongest shell the world allows. You remember not needing one.
   > What: the full vanilla netherite set: the best plain armour, with knockback resistance and immunity to burning up in lava as an item.
   > How: smithing table, one piece at a time: template + diamond piece + netherite ingot. Four templates, four ingots.
   > Tip: copy templates with diamonds and netherrack so you never run out.
15. **Bastion Remnant**: find structure `minecraft:bastion_remnant` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > What: every bastion has a netherite upgrade template in its chests, often gold blocks and ancient debris too.
   > How: find a bastion in the Nether (anywhere except basalt deltas) and step inside.
   > Tip: piglin brutes don't care about gold armour. Bring a shield and a bow.
16. **Netherite Sword**: checkmark *(after: Netherite Tier, Diamond Sword and Shovel)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Netherite Sword" on the Gear and Comfort page. Click to dismiss.
17. **Lapis Armour**: `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_helmet`; `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_leggings`; `mekanismtools:lapis_lazuli_boots` *(after: Lapis Tools)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools lapis armour protects about as well as chainmail but takes enchantments very well.
   > Chemistry: the blue of lapis is the S₃⁻ radical ion caged in lazurite. Grind it, wash out the grey minerals, and you have ultramarine pigment.
   > How: 24 lapis lazuli, shaped like any armour set (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cheap set to practise enchanting on while your diamonds go into machines.
18. **A Full Leather Set**: `minecraft:leather_helmet`; `minecraft:leather_chestplate`; `minecraft:leather_leggings`; `minecraft:leather_boots` *(after: Leather Armour)*
   > What: the whole leather set: cap, tunic, trousers and boots. Getting Started asked for two of them; this is all four. Leather can be dyed any colour.
   > Chemistry: leather is tanned hide: tannins (plant polyphenols) or chromium(III) salts cross-link the collagen protein chains, so the skin stops rotting and stays flexible.
   > How: 24 leather for the set (5, 8, 7 and 4). Craft a piece with dye to colour it; a water cauldron washes the dye out.
   > Tip: leather boots let you walk on powder snow without sinking.
19. **Armour for a Friend**: `minecraft:wolf_armor`; 2x `minecraft:armadillo_scute` *(after: A Full Leather Set)*
   > What: wolf armour soaks up damage for a tamed wolf. When it cracks, repair it with scutes.
   > Chemistry: scutes are keratin plates, the same protein as hair, horn and nails. Disulfide (S–S) bridges between the chains make keratin tough; that's also why burning hair smells of sulfur.
   > How: brush an armadillo (savanna and badlands) with a brush for scutes. 6 scutes make the armour; keep 2 for repairs.
   > Tip: right-click a tamed wolf with the armour to put it on. Dye it if you like.
20. **Barding**: 1x any of `or(item(minecraft:leather_horse_armor)item(minecraft:iron_horse_armor)item(minecraft:golden_horse_armor)item(minecraft:diamond_horse_armor))` *(after: A Full Leather Set)*
   > What: horse armour, any kind. Leather horse armour can be crafted and dyed; iron, gold and diamond only turn up in chests.
   > How: 7 leather for the leather one, or loot dungeons, temples, villages and Ancient Cities for the metal ones.
   > Tip: Farmer's Delight Horse Feed heals a horse and speeds it up (Farming page).
21. **Smithing Table**: `minecraft:smithing_table` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember armour that reshaped itself to fit. A smithing table is the mortal answer: upgrade, don't start over.
   > What: the smithing table upgrades tools and armour in place (diamond to netherite) and paints armour trims. Every set on this page meets it sooner or later.
   > How: 2 iron ingots over 4 planks.
   > Tip: Apotheosis adds smithing recipes too, such as upgrading chainmail to iron (check JEI).
22. **Chainmail**: `minecraft:chainmail_helmet`; `minecraft:chainmail_chestplate`; `minecraft:chainmail_leggings`; `minecraft:chainmail_boots`
   > What: the chainmail set sits between leather and iron, and it can't be crafted in vanilla.
   > How: trade with an armourer villager, or loot it from mobs that spawn wearing it (check JEI for any pack recipe).
   > Tip: real mail is thousands of riveted iron rings: flexible, and hard to cut, but a blunt blow goes straight through.

54. **Steeleaf Armour**: `twilightforest:steeleaf_helmet`; `twilightforest:steeleaf_chestplate`; `twilightforest:steeleaf_leggings`; `twilightforest:steeleaf_boots`
   > What: steeleaf armour from the Twilight Forest.
   > How: steeleaf ingots (check JEI).
   > Tip: a full set beats mixed pieces only when the set has a bonus; check the tooltips.
55. **Knightmetal Armour**: `twilightforest:knightmetal_helmet`; `twilightforest:knightmetal_chestplate`; `twilightforest:knightmetal_leggings`; `twilightforest:knightmetal_boots`
   > What: knightmetal armour, made from what the Goblin Knights and phantoms guard.
   > How: knightmetal ingots (see the Twilight Forest page).
   > Tip: a full set beats mixed pieces only when the set has a bonus; check the tooltips.
56. **Fiery Armour**: `twilightforest:fiery_helmet`; `twilightforest:fiery_chestplate`; `twilightforest:fiery_leggings`; `twilightforest:fiery_boots`
   > What: fiery armour: hot to the touch, and it sets attackers alight.
   > How: fiery ingots (see the Twilight Forest page).
   > Tip: a full set beats mixed pieces only when the set has a bonus; check the tooltips.
57. **Arctic Armour**: `twilightforest:arctic_helmet`; `twilightforest:arctic_chestplate`; `twilightforest:arctic_leggings`; `twilightforest:arctic_boots`
   > What: arctic fur armour, dyeable, from the Twilight Forest's snowy biomes.
   > How: arctic fur (check JEI).
   > Tip: a full set beats mixed pieces only when the set has a bonus; check the tooltips.
58. **Yeti Armour**: `twilightforest:yeti_helmet`; `twilightforest:yeti_chestplate`; `twilightforest:yeti_leggings`; `twilightforest:yeti_boots`
   > What: yeti armour, from the Alpha Yeti's fur.
   > How: alpha yeti fur (see the Twilight Forest page).
   > Tip: a full set beats mixed pieces only when the set has a bonus; check the tooltips.

### Apotheosis

*Affix loot, gems, sigils, world tiers, spawners and Gateways.*

1. **A Gem in the Rough**: `apotheosis:gem` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember gear that remembered you back. Mortal gear can learn, if you teach it.
   > What: Apotheosis gems drop from monsters and chests. Each one carries a bonus that you can set into a socket on your gear.
   > How: fight, loot and read the tooltip of anything that glitters. Any gem completes this quest.
   > Tip: gems come in purities, from cracked to perfect. Better purity, bigger bonus.
2. **Gem Dust**: 4x `apotheosis:gem_dust` *(after: A Gem in the Rough)*
   > What: gem dust builds almost every Apotheosis table, sigil and rune.
   > How: crush spare gems into gem dust (JEI shows how).
   > Tip: keep good gems for sockets and crush the rest.
3. **Setting a Gem**: `minecraft:smithing_table` *(after: Gem Dust)*
   > What: the smithing table is where Apotheosis puts gems into sockets and applies sigils to gear.
   > How: 4 planks and 2 iron ingots. Put the gear in, then the gem or sigil.
   > Tip: a socketed gem is locked in until a Sigil of Withdrawal pulls it out.
4. **Gem Cutting**: `apotheosis:gem_cutting_table` *(after: Gem Dust)*
   > What: the Gem Cutting Table upgrades gems to higher purity using matching gems and dust.
   > Chemistry: real gems are cut along cleavage planes, flat directions where the crystal's bonds are weakest.
   > How: smooth stone, shears, planks and gem dust.
5. **Gem-Fused Slate**: 8x `apotheosis:gem_fused_slate` *(after: Gem Dust)*
   > What: gem-fused slate is the backing for sigils and spawner runes.
   > Chemistry: deepslate is metamorphic rock: older stone squeezed and heated deep underground until its minerals recrystallised.
   > How: 8 deepslate around 1 gem dust makes 8.
6. **Sigil of Socketing**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_socketing` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: adds a socket to gear in a smithing table, so you can slot in a gem.
   > How: gem-fused slate, an amethyst shard, gunpowder and gem dust (makes 3).
   > Tip: a Sigil of Withdrawal pulls gems back out later.
7. **Sigil of Unnaming**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_unnaming` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: removes the long generated name from an affixed item, so it goes back to its plain name.
   > How: 6 slate around 3 flint makes 6. Apply it at the smithing table.
   > Tip: a name tag afterwards lets you call the sword whatever you like.
8. **Sigil of Withdrawal**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_withdrawal` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: pulls every gem out of an item without destroying them, so a good gem can move to new gear.
   > How: gem-fused slate, blaze rods, ender pearls, a lava bucket and gem dust (makes 4).
   > Tip: withdraw gems before salvaging or reforging old gear.
9. **Sigil of Enhancement**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_enhancement` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: upgrades a socketed gem to the next rarity at the Reforging Table.
   > How: gem-fused slate, gem dust and a godforged pearl (makes 4). Godforged pearls come from salvaging mythic gear.
   > Tip: save these for gems you'll keep: a mythic gem in endgame gear is worth it.
10. **Sigil of Rebirth**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_rebirth` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: the Sigil of Rebirth is spent at the Reforging Table each time you reroll an item.
   > How: 6 slate around 3 gem dust makes 6.
   > Tip: make them in bulk before a long reforging session.
11. **Sigil of Malice**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_malice` *(after: Gem-Fused Slate)*
   > What: a sigil with no crafting recipe. It feeds the highest gateway and spawner upgrade recipes.
   > How: Apothic Invaders (named bosses from World Tier: Frontier on) sometimes drop one. Check JEI for its uses.
   > Tip: invaders hit very hard. Fight them where you can retreat.
12. **Salvaging**: `apotheosis:salvaging_table` *(after: Setting a Gem)*
   > What: the Salvaging Table breaks affixed gear into materials of its rarity.
   > How: a smithing table, an iron pickaxe and axe, copper, a lava bucket and gem dust.
   > Tip: every affixed sword you don't want is a reforge for one you do.
13. **Mysterious Scrap Metal**: `apotheosis:mysterious_scrap_metal` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: the salvage of common (grey) affix gear, used in common-tier reforging.
   > How: salvage any common affixed item.
   > Tip: common gear drops everywhere, so this piles up first.
14. **Timeworn Fabric**: `apotheosis:timeworn_fabric` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: the salvage of uncommon (green) gear. The Frontiersman's spawner upgrade rune uses it too.
   > How: salvage uncommon affixed gear.
   > Tip: sort loot by colour before salvaging; each rarity has its own material.
15. **Luminous Crystal**: 4x `apotheosis:luminous_crystal_shard` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: luminous crystal shards are the salvage of rare (blue) gear.
   > How: salvage rare gear in the Salvaging Table until you have 4 shards.
   > Tip: the Wayfarer's spawner upgrade rune is built on these.
16. **Godforged Pearl**: `apotheosis:godforged_pearl` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: the salvage of mythic gear, the rarest material: augmenting, enhancement sigils and the top runes need it.
   > How: salvage mythic gear. It drops in high world tiers, from tiered gateways and from the toughest elites.
   > Tip: never salvage a mythic item you would rather wear; check its affixes first.
17. **Arcane Sands**: `apotheosis:arcane_sands` *(after: Salvaging)*
   > What: the salvage of epic (purple) gear. The full Reforging Table needs it.
   > How: salvage epic affixed gear.
   > Tip: keep a few stacks; reforging epic gear spends them fast.
18. **Simple Reforging**: `apotheosis:simple_reforging_table` *(after: Gem Dust)*
   > What: the Simple Reforging Table rerolls affixes on gear of lower rarities.
   > How: an enchanting table, iron, smooth stone and gem dust.
   > Tip: reforging costs rarity materials; salvage junk gear to get them.
19. **Divine Reforging**: `apotheosis:reforging_table` *(after: Arcane Sands, Simple Reforging, Into the Fire)*
   > You remember weapons that chose their wielders. These at least choose good affixes.
   > What: the full Reforging Table handles every rarity, up to mythic gear.
   > How: the Simple Reforging Table, a netherite ingot, nether bricks and arcane sands.
20. **Augmenting**: `apotheosis:augmenting_table` *(after: Sigil of Enhancement, Godforged Pearl)*
   > What: the Augmenting Table improves or rerolls one affix at a time.
   > How: an enchanting table, a Nether Star, 2 godforged pearls and polished blackstone.
   > Tip: save it for gear you plan to keep for the rest of the game.
21. **World Tiers**: checkmark *(after: A Gem in the Rough)*
   > What: Apotheosis splits the game into five world tiers: Haven, Frontier, Ascent, Summit and Pinnacle. Higher tiers make monsters stronger and loot better, and raise the cap on enchanting power.
   > How: press CTRL+T to open the World Tier screen. Hover a tier to see what unlocks it; activate it once unlocked. Click the checkmark when you've looked.
   > Tip: you can step back down to an easier tier at any time.
22. **Haven**: checkmark *(after: World Tiers)*
   > What: Haven is the starting tier. It unlocks when you pick up any affixed item. Enchanting power is capped at 30 Eterna here.
   > How: find an affixed item (a coloured name). Click the checkmark when the advancement pops.
   > Tip: Haven is the tier to learn the systems in.
23. **Frontier**: checkmark *(after: Haven)*
   > What: Frontier unlocks when you wear affixed armour in all four slots and hold an affixed weapon. Apothic Invaders start to appear, and the Eterna cap rises to 45.
   > How: equip any affixed helmet, chestplate, leggings, boots and weapon, then activate Frontier (CTRL+T). Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: 45 Eterna is what the infused shelves need (Apothic Enchanting page).
24. **Ascent**: checkmark *(after: Frontier)*
   > What: Ascent needs a full set of uncommon (green) or better gear and one Apothic Invader killed. The Eterna cap rises to 60.
   > How: upgrade every slot to uncommon or better, kill an invader, then activate Ascent. Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: invaders announce themselves; fight them near a bed.
25. **Summit**: checkmark *(after: Ascent)*
   > What: Summit needs a full set of rare (blue) or better gear and a dead Wither. The Eterna cap rises to 75.
   > How: gear up in rare affixes, summon and kill the Wither, then activate Summit. Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: fight the Wither underground or in a bunker: it breaks most blocks around it.
26. **Pinnacle**: checkmark *(after: Summit)*
   > What: Pinnacle, the top tier, needs a full set of epic (purple) gear and the Ender Dragon killed. Enchanting power is uncapped (100 Eterna).
   > How: wear epic or better in every slot, beat the dragon, then activate Pinnacle. Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: this is where mythic gear and godforged pearls start to flow.
27. **Tiered Gateways**: checkmark *(after: Frontier, Gate Pearl)*
   > What: Apotheosis adds one gateway per world tier (Frontier, Ascent, Summit, Pinnacle). Each opens only in its own tier and pays out affix gear.
