   > How: the Frontier pearl is spider eyes, iron, bones, an ender pearl and rotten flesh. JEI lists the others. Open and close one, then click the checkmark.
   > Tip: the Pinnacle gate needs Sigils of Malice and a Warden Tendril.
28. **The Endless Gateway**: checkmark *(after: Tiered Gateways, Pinnacle)*
   > What: the Endless Gateway of Apothic Invaders sends wave after wave of invaders until you fall or walk away.
   > How: its pearl is a reward from the Pinnacle gateway. Open it, survive as long as you can, then click the checkmark.
   > Tip: the deeper you go, the better the payout. Bring totems.
29. **Sigil of Supremacy**: `apotheosis:sigil_of_supremacy` *(after: The Endless Gateway)*
   > You remember standing where nothing could follow. It was lonely, and you liked it.
   > What: the rarest sigil, paid out deep in the Endless Gateway. Check JEI for what it unlocks.
   > How: keep the endless gate going until it drops.
   > Tip: the gateway's reward list in JEI shows which wave it starts at.
30. **Elite Hunting**: kill 50x `minecraft:zombie` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Apotheosis gives some monsters affixed gear and makes rare elites with a coloured name. Their drops can roll affixes and sockets.
   > How: kill 50 zombies. Pick up any named or glowing item they drop and read its tooltip.
   > Tip: elites hit hard. Gear up before poking one with a stick.
31. **Potion Charm**: checkmark *(after: Gem Dust, The Brewer's Art)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Unbreakable Charms" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
32. **Gate Pearl**: `gateways:gate_pearl` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: a Gate Pearl opens a Gateway that releases waves of a chosen mob. Beat every wave for rewards.
   > How: the Blaze gate is five blaze rods, an ender pearl and three nether bricks. Apotheosis adds tiered gates (Frontier and up); JEI shows them all.
   > Tip: a gate is a controlled mob farm: blaze rods, ender pearls and XP on demand.
33. **Close a Gateway**: checkmark *(after: Gate Pearl)*
   > What: the gateway closes when every wave is defeated and pays out its reward.
   > How: throw the pearl in an open area, stay close (leaving fails the gate) and kill each wave. Click the checkmark when it closes.
   > Tip: tiered Apotheosis gates hand out affix gear and rarity materials.
34. **Gem Case**: checkmark *(after: Gem Cutting)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Gem Case" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
35. **Every Rarity**: `apotheosis:mysterious_scrap_metal`; `apotheosis:timeworn_fabric`; `apotheosis:arcane_sands`; `apotheosis:godforged_pearl` *(after: Luminous Crystal)*
   > What: one material of each other rarity: common scrap metal, uncommon timeworn fabric, epic arcane sands and a mythic godforged pearl.
   > How: salvage gear of each colour. The pearl only comes from mythic gear: tiered Gateways and the toughest elites.
   > Tip: Divine Reforging, upgrade runes and the strongest sigils all spend these.
36. **Bottled Monsters**: `minecraft:spawner` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember making monsters to order. Today you'll settle for moving one.
   > What: with Apothic Spawners a monster spawner can be picked up with a Silk Touch pickaxe and moved home.
   > How: find one in a dungeon or mineshaft, light it up, then mine it with Silk Touch (it costs the pick 100 durability).
   > Tip: spawners are mob farms for drops you can't make chemically: bones, string, ender pearls, blaze rods.
37. **Spawner Chains**: `apotheosis:spawner_chain`; `minecraft:tnt` *(after: Bottled Monsters)*
   > What: spawner chains are the binding for spawner runes. They only come from a monster spawner destroyed by an explosion.
   > Chemistry: TNT (C₇H₅N₃O₆) carries its own oxygen in its nitro groups, so it burns in microseconds and makes a shock wave.
   > How: find a spawner you don't want to keep and blow it up with TNT. Pick up the chains, and bring a spare TNT for the quest.
   > Tip: keep the good spawners: Silk Touch them home instead.
38. **Spawner Runes**: `apotheosis:spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Chains)*
   > What: a blank Spawner Rune. Crafted with one more ingredient it becomes a rune that rewrites a spawner's rules when you right-click the spawner with it.
   > How: gem dust, gem-fused slate and spawner chains (makes 2).
   > Tip: hold Shift over a placed spawner's tooltip, or look at it with Jade, to see its current stats.
39. **Rune of Immolation**: `apotheosis:burning_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: spawned mobs are set alight, so they drop cooked meat and die faster.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 campfires around it.
   > Tip: useless on Nether mobs, which don't burn.
40. **Rune of Debilitation**: `apotheosis:initial_health_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: lowers the starting health of spawned mobs, so one hit finishes them.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 pointed dripstone around it.
   > Tip: stack it a few times for a one-punch farm.
41. **Rune of Youth**: `apotheosis:youthful_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: spawned mobs are babies wherever the mob has a baby form.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 turtle eggs around it.
   > Tip: baby zombies are fast. You were warned.
42. **Rune of Spawning Range**: `apotheosis:spawn_range_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: widens the area a spawner may place mobs in.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 pistons around it.
   > Tip: use quartz in the off hand to shrink it again (see Opposite Day).
43. **Rune of Perpetual Twilight**: `apotheosis:ignore_light_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the spawner ignores light levels, so a well-lit farm still runs.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 soul lanterns around it.
   > Tip: light your farm fully: the spawner works, wild mobs don't spawn.
44. **Rune of Control**: `apotheosis:redstone_control_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the spawner only runs while it gets a redstone signal.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 comparators around it.
   > Tip: put it on every farm first, so you can switch it off.
45. **Opposite Day**: `minecraft:quartz` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: with nether quartz in your off hand, using a rune or modifier on a spawner reverses its effect (turn Silence off, shrink the range, and so on).
   > Chemistry: quartz is silicon dioxide, SiO₂: the same compound as most sand and glass.
   > How: hold quartz in the off hand and the modifier in the main hand, then right-click the spawner.
   > Tip: JEI's spawner page lists every modifier and its inverse.
46. **Rune of Silence**: `apotheosis:silent_spawner_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: spawned mobs make no sound.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with 4 wool around it.
   > Tip: your ears will thank you.
47. **Frontiersman's Upgrade**: `apotheosis:frontier_spawner_upgrade_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the first of four upgrade runes: faster spawns and more mobs per spawn. The others are Wayfarer's, Mountaineer's and Thundering.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with timeworn fabric, clocks and flint.
   > Tip: upgrade runes match the world tiers, so each new tier opens the next rune.
48. **Wayfarer's Upgrade**: `apotheosis:ascent_spawner_upgrade_rune` *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the second upgrade rune: a bigger step in spawn speed and count.
   > How: a Spawner Rune with luminous crystal shards, quartz, a spawn egg and a Sigil of Socketing (check JEI).
   > Tip: spawn eggs come from the Capturing enchantment (Choosing the Mob).
49. **Infused Spawner Rune**: checkmark *(after: Spawner Runes)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Infusing Spawner Runes" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
50. **Mountaineer's Upgrade**: `apotheosis:summit_spawner_upgrade_rune` *(after: Infusing Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the third upgrade rune: a large boost to the spawner.
   > How: an Infused Spawner Rune with arcane sands, phantom membranes, a Sigil of Malice and a Warden Tendril.
   > Tip: the tendril drops from the Warden. Plan that fight.
51. **Thundering Upgrade**: `apotheosis:pinnacle_spawner_upgrade_rune` *(after: Infusing Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the last upgrade rune: the spawner reaches its maximum.
   > How: an Infused Spawner Rune with godforged pearls, Infused Breath, a Nether Star and a perfect Endersurge gem.
   > Tip: save Nether Stars: the Seed of a New World needs them too.
52. **Rune of Stupor**: `apotheosis:no_ai_spawner_rune` *(after: Infusing Spawner Runes)*
   > What: spawned mobs have no AI: they don't move, attack or flee.
   > How: an Infused Spawner Rune with chorus fruit and a Potion of Fatigue.
   > Tip: a farm that can't fight back. Mobs without AI also don't despawn on their own.
53. **Rune of Solitude**: `apotheosis:ignore_players_spawner_rune` *(after: Infusing Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the spawner no longer needs a player nearby (the chunk still has to be loaded).
   > How: an Infused Spawner Rune with a Nether Star, phantom membranes and an eye of ender.
   > Tip: pair it with FTB Chunks chunk loading for an always-on farm.
54. **Rune of Defiance**: `apotheosis:ignore_conditions_spawner_rune` *(after: Infusing Spawner Runes)*
   > What: the spawner ignores the mob's spawn conditions entirely (light, block, biome).
   > How: an Infused Spawner Rune with a conduit and ender pearls.
   > Tip: useful for mobs with fussy rules, like slimes or guardians.
55. **Rune of Echoes**: `apotheosis:echoing_spawner_rune` *(after: Infusing Spawner Runes)*
   > What: spawned mobs drop extra copies of their loot. It stacks up to three times.
   > How: an Infused Spawner Rune ringed with 8 echo shards.
   > Tip: echo shards come from Ancient City chests, or from infusing one into four.
56. **Choosing the Mob**: checkmark *(after: Bottled Monsters)*
   > What: right-click a placed spawner with a spawn egg and it spawns that mob from then on.
   > How: spawn eggs don't drop by themselves. The quests here show three ways to get one. Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: the egg is used up, so change the mob only when you mean it.
57. **Capturing**: checkmark *(after: Choosing the Mob)*
   > What: Capturing is a weapon enchantment from Apothic Spawners: each kill has a small chance per level to drop the mob's spawn egg.
   > How: roll it at an enchanting table or find the book, and put it on a sword. Click the checkmark when you have it.
   > Tip: the chance is low (half a percent per level), so use it on a farm, not on a hunt.
58. **Eggs from Fragments**: checkmark *(after: Choosing the Mob)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Reliquary" on the Relics page. Click to dismiss.
59. **Occult Ender Lead**: checkmark *(after: Choosing the Mob)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Occult Ender Lead" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
60. **Other Spawners**: checkmark *(after: Bottled Monsters)*
   > What: two other mods in the pack make their own spawners: Ars Additions and Mystical Agriculture.
   > How: read on below. Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: unlike a monster spawner, both are crafted, so you never have to go looking for one.
61. **Source Spawner**: checkmark *(after: Other Spawners)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Source Spawner" on the Ars Nouveau page. Click to dismiss.
62. **Soulium Spawner**: checkmark *(after: Other Spawners)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Soulium Spawner" on the Mystical Agriculture page. Click to dismiss.
63. **Better Bookshelves**: checkmark *(after: Gem Dust, Into the Fire)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Hellshelves" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
64. **Infusion**: checkmark *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Infused Hellshelves" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
65. **Enchantment Library**: checkmark *(after: Infusion)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Enchantment Library" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
66. **Endshelves**: checkmark *(after: Infusion, The End)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Endshelves" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
67. **Scrap Tome**: checkmark *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Tome of Scrapping" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
68. **House Fabergé**: checkmark *(after: Gem Case, Infusion)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Gem Case of House Fabergé" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
69. **God-Fused Pearl**: checkmark *(after: Every Rarity, Infusion)*
   > Moved: this step is now "God-Fused Pearl" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
70. **Enchanting Table of the Raven**: checkmark *(after: God-Fused Pearl)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Enchanting Table of the Raven" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
71. **Curious Shelves**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:stoneshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:beeshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:melonshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:geode_shelf)item(apothic_enchanting:basic_bookshelf))` *(after: Hellshelves)*
   > What: the Stoneshelf, Beeshelf, Melonshelf, Geode shelf and Basic Bookshelf each nudge the table's stats in an odd direction.
   > Chemistry: a geode's calcite rind is CaCO₃, the same compound as chalk and limestone.
   > How: Stoneshelf: polished andesite and books. Geode shelf: calcite around a bookshelf and a budding amethyst. JEI has the rest.
   > Tip: every shelf's tooltip lists its Eterna, Quanta and Arcana: read them before you build.
72. **Hellshelf Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:blazing_hellshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:glowing_hellshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:sightshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:sightshelf_t2))` *(after: Infused Hellshelves)*
   > What: the Infused Hellshelf upgrades into Blazing (fire charges), Glowing (glowstone) or the Hellshelf of Sight, which shows more enchantment clues.
   > How: an Infused Hellshelf in the grid with the upgrade items (check JEI). Masterful Sight needs netherite and emerald blocks.
   > Tip: one Sightshelf shows much more of what the table will roll.
73. **Seashelves**: checkmark *(after: Better Bookshelves)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Seashelves" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
74. **Seashelf Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:infused_seashelf)item(apothic_enchanting:crystal_seashelf)item(apothic_enchanting:heart_seashelf)item(apothic_enchanting:filtering_shelf))` *(after: Seashelves, Infused Hellshelves)*
   > What: an Infused Seashelf, then Crystalline, Heart-Forged or the Seashelf of Aquatic Filtration, which keeps chosen enchantments out of the pool.
   > How: infuse a seashelf at the table, then craft it with prismarine crystals, a heart of the sea, or prismarine bricks and slabs (check JEI).
   > Tip: the filtering shelf is how you stop a table rolling the enchantment you never want.
75. **Deepshelves**: `apothic_enchanting:dormant_deepshelf`; `apothic_enchanting:deepshelf` *(after: Infused Hellshelves)*
   > What: the deepshelf family pushes the stats high. It starts dormant and wakes with infusion.
   > How: Dormant Deepshelf: cracked deepslate tiles and books. Infuse it at 60 Eterna (World Tier: Ascent) to wake it.
   > Tip: upgrade it with echo shards or soul lanterns; the Deepshelf of Arcane Treasures allows treasure enchantments.
76. **Deepshelf Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:echoing_deepshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:soul_touched_deepshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:treasure_shelf))` *(after: Deepshelves)*
   > What: Echoing and Soul-Touched deepshelves raise the stats further; the treasure shelf lets the table roll treasure enchantments.
   > How: a Deepshelf with an echo shard and candles, or a soul lantern and sculk. Treasure: 2 deepshelves, gold blocks, diamonds and an emerald block.
   > Tip: echo shards come from Ancient City chests.
77. **Sculkshelves**: `apothic_enchanting:warden_tendril`; 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:echoing_sculkshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:soul_touched_sculkshelf))` *(after: Deepshelf Upgrades)*
   > What: the strongest deepshelves need a Warden Tendril, which drops from a Warden.
   > How: kill a Warden (Ancient City; don't make a sound), then craft the tendril over an upgraded deepshelf with sculk and a sculk catalyst.
   > Tip: a Warden has 500 health and its sonic boom ignores armor. Plan the fight, or plan the escape.
78. **Endshelf Upgrades**: `apothic_enchanting:infused_breath`; 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:pearl_endshelf)item(apothic_enchanting:draconic_endshelf))` *(after: Endshelves)*
   > What: the top of the shelf ladder. The Pearlescent Endshelf adds end rods; the Draconic one is crowned with a dragon head.
   > How: infuse dragon's breath for Infused Breath (3 per bottle), then craft an Endshelf with end rods and ender pearls, or a dragon head and pearls.
   > Tip: dragon heads hang on End Ship bows. Bring the elytra home too.
79. **Better Tomes**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:other_tome)item(apothic_enchanting:improved_scrap_tome)item(apothic_enchanting:extraction_tome))` *(after: Tome of Scrapping, Infused Hellshelves)*
   > What: the Tome of the Others enchants like a tool no other tome covers; Superior Scrapping and Extraction strip enchantments more gently (Extraction keeps the item).
   > How: Tome of the Others: 6 books and a blaze rod (makes 6). Infuse a Scrap Tome for Superior Scrapping, and that for Extraction.
   > Tip: Extraction tomes are the cleanest way to move a good enchantment to new gear.
80. **Library of Alexandria**: checkmark *(after: Enchantment Library)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Library of Alexandria" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.
81. **Ender Leads**: 1x any of `or(item(apothic_enchanting:flimsy_ender_lead)item(apothic_enchanting:ender_lead)item(apothic_enchanting:occult_ender_lead))` *(after: Hellshelves)*
   > What: the Flimsy Ender Lead captures animals; the infused Ender Lead captures most mobs; the Occult one can bind a mob to a spawner.
   > How: flimsy: an ender pearl, a lead and a gold ingot (shapeless). Infuse it for the Ender Lead; infuse that holding a witch for the Occult lead.
   > Tip: the easy way to move a villager across the world.
82. **Inert Trident**: checkmark *(after: Infusion)*
   > Moved: this step is now "A Real Trident" on the Apothic Enchanting page. Click to dismiss.

### Relics

*Found treasures that grow with you: Relics, plus the old Reliquary curios.*

1. **Things Mortals Didn't Make**: checkmark
   > What: Relics are curios you find, never craft. Each has abilities that level up as you use them, and a research screen to spend those levels.
   > How: open a relic's tooltip for its abilities and the key that opens its upgrade screen. Click the checkmark when you have read it.
   > Tip: relics never drop from the sky: they sit in structure chests, split by dimension as the three hubs below show.
2. **A True Relic**: 1x any of `or(item(relics:chorus_staff)item(relics:experience_disperser)item(relics:ghostly_mantle)item(relics:glitchy_mantle)item(relics:hunting_belt)item(relics:jellyfish_necklace)item(relics:kinetic_belt)item(relics:leafy_mantle)item(relics:midnight_mantle)item(relics:pet_bone)item(relics:piglin_mask)item(relics:reflective_necklace)item(relics:rider_flute)item(relics:ring_of_the_seven_deadly_sins)item(relics:roller_skate)item(relics:shield_of_retaliation)item(relics:sphere_of_self_sacrifice)item(relics:springy_boot)item(relics:chef_hat)item(relics:clot_of_time)item(relics:cut_glass_boot))` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember owning things no mortal smith made. A few of them seem to have survived.
   > What: Relics are found, never crafted: mantles, belts, necklaces, boots, a chef's hat, a ring of the seven deadly sins. Each has abilities that grow with use.
   > How: loot chests in dungeons, mineshafts, temples, villages and modded structures. Any one relic completes this quest.
   > Tip: read the tooltip: each relic says what it does and how it gains experience.
3. **Overworld Chests**: visit `minecraft:overworld` *(after: A True Relic)*
   > What: the relics below come from Overworld loot: village chests, mineshafts, jungle and desert temples, shipwrecks and the odd ruin.
   > How: you are already here. Loot every chest you pass; relics are rare rolls, so volume matters.
   > Tip: an Explorer's Compass points to the nearest structure of the kind you pick; JourneyMap marks the ones you've found.
4. **Nether Chests**: visit `minecraft:the_nether` *(after: A True Relic)*
   > What: bastion remnants, nether fortresses and ruined portals hold the Nether's relics.
   > How: light a Nether portal (Chapter II) and raid a bastion. Its treasure room has the best chests and the angriest piglins.
   > Tip: gold armour keeps piglins calm until you open a chest; after that they come anyway.
5. **End Chests**: visit `minecraft:the_end` *(after: A True Relic)*
   > What: End city towers and the ships moored to them carry the rarest relics.
   > How: beat the dragon, take the gateway, find a city. Shulkers guard every chest; bring blocks for levitation falls.
   > Tip: the ship's chest sits behind the elytra frame. Take both.
6. **Roller Skates**: `relics:roller_skate` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: skates that build up movement speed while you keep running, at the cost of grip: the faster you go, the more you slide.
   > How: Overworld chests. Equip them in the feet curio slot and keep sprinting.
   > Tip: stop before corners. Levelled skates reach their top speed sooner.
7. **Jellyfish Necklace**: `relics:jellyfish_necklace` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: a necklace that raises your health and regeneration while you are in water or rain, and stores electric arcs that shock whatever you touch.
   > How: Overworld chests, often in shipwrecks and ocean ruins.
   > Tip: pair it with Flippers or Aqua Dashers for ocean monuments.
8. **Hunting Belt**: `relics:hunting_belt` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: a belt that adds charm slots and makes your tamed animals hit harder while they fight beside you.
   > How: Overworld chests. Wear it in the belt curio slot.
   > Tip: a belt full of charms turns a pack of wolves into a real escort.
9. **Cut-Glass Boot**: `relics:cut_glass_boot` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: held in hand, this boot works as a bucket that stores several liquids at once; its tooltip shows which one is selected.
   > How: Overworld chests.
   > Tip: it fills the gap between buckets and tanks when you're moving lava or water for the chemistry lines.
10. **Chef's Hat**: `relics:chef_hat` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: a hat whose kills have a chance to drop a meatball, which eats like raw beef and cooks into something better.
   > How: Overworld chests, mostly in villages.
   > Tip: its abilities level with your cooking and eating, so wear it while you farm.
11. **Leafy Mantle**: `relics:leafy_mantle` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: a cloak that lets you move freely through leaves, land on them without damage and heal while you stand in foliage; it can even absorb leaves to save you from a killing blow.
   > How: Overworld chests in forests and jungles.
   > Tip: a jungle treetop is the safest bed in the pack while you wear it.
12. **Springy Boot**: `relics:springy_boot` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: a boot that launches you backwards off a crouch-jump and keeps bouncing on every landing until you come to a stop.
   > How: Overworld chests.
   > Tip: level the Bounce ability before trying anything near lava.
13. **Rider's Flute**: `relics:rider_flute` *(after: Overworld Chests)*
   > What: a flute that stores a tamed mount and releases it where you stand, so your horse comes with you through portals and across oceans.
   > How: Overworld chests. Right-click a tamed mount to store it, right-click again to release it.
   > Tip: the stored animal is safe in the flute; a horse left outside is not.
14. **Sphere of Self-Sacrifice**: `relics:sphere_of_self_sacrifice` *(after: Nether Chests)*
   > What: an orb that burns a third of your maximum health on use and restores twice as much over ten seconds; each active restoration also reduces incoming damage, and crouching fires them off as homing blood bolts.
   > How: bastion and fortress chests.
   > Tip: it rewards being hit: resisted damage levels the relic.
15. **Piglin Mask**: `relics:piglin_mask` *(after: Nether Chests)*
   > What: a mask that stops piglins attacking you first and turns nearby piglins on anyone who attacks you; its looting ability drops golden teeth.
   > How: bastion chests. The piglins guarding them don't see the irony.
   > Tip: the golden teeth are the quest below.
16. **Reflective Necklace**: `relics:reflective_necklace` *(after: Nether Chests)*
   > What: a necklace with a chance to turn damage you take into orbs that hold part of it, and release every orb at the next thing you hit.
   > How: fortress chests.
   > Tip: take a few hits on purpose, then swing at a wither skeleton.
17. **Ring of the Seven Deadly Sins**: `relics:ring_of_the_seven_deadly_sins` *(after: Nether Chests)*
   > What: a ring whose abilities are named for the sins: Pride adds damage for height above a target, Envy for a target with more health than you, Wrath for a quick follow-up strike, and so on.
   > How: bastion chests.
   > Tip: each sin levels on its own, so the ring rewards the way you already fight.
18. **Ghostly Mantle**: `relics:ghostly_mantle` *(after: Nether Chests)*
   > What: a cloak that trails a mist which drains the air of anything standing in it, and takes less damage from targets that keep staring at you.
   > How: fortress and bastion chests.
   > Tip: run circles around a brute and let the mist do the work.
19. **Shield of Retaliation**: `relics:shield_of_retaliation` *(after: Nether Chests)*
   > What: a shield with a short parry window: hold it and damage from in front is blocked, stored, and returned.
   > How: bastion chests.
   > Tip: it blocks a blaze volley cleanly if you raise it as the first fireball leaves.
20. **Gold Teeth**: `relics:golden_tooth` *(after: Piglin Mask)*
   > What: with the Piglin Mask's looting ability, kills drop golden teeth: bigger mobs, more teeth. They also feed the mask's rank.
   > How: find a Piglin Mask, level its looting ability and fight. Teeth craft into gold ingots, or trade them to piglins.
   > Tip: it's mob-drop gold, like a zombified piglin farm: handy, but not ore.
21. **Chorus Staff**: `relics:chorus_staff` *(after: End Chests)*
   > What: a staff that teleports you a few blocks forward from a small buffer of charges that refills on its own.
   > How: End city chests.
   > Tip: it crosses the gaps between End islands that an ender pearl would miss.
22. **Clot of Time**: `relics:clot_of_time` *(after: End Chests)*
   > What: hold it and you slide back along the path you just walked, several seconds into the past, then it needs a rest.
   > How: End city and ship chests.
   > Tip: a shulker bullet lifted you off the edge? Rewind.
23. **Kinetic Belt**: `relics:kinetic_belt` *(after: End Chests)*
   > What: a belt that adds charm slots and, while you hold jump, lowers your gravity and air resistance so your momentum carries you; falls while gliding hurt less.
   > How: End city chests.
   > Tip: with Roller Skates for the run-up it is nearly an elytra.
24. **Midnight Mantle**: `relics:midnight_mantle` *(after: End Chests)*
   > What: a cloak that boosts damage near a full moon, health and regeneration near a new moon, and hides you in deep darkness.
   > How: End city chests.
   > Tip: check the moon phase before a boss fight; the mantle does.
25. **Glitchy Mantle**: `relics:glitchy_mantle` *(after: End Chests)*
   > What: a cloak that gives attacks against you a chance to miss and leaves glitchy copies of you behind that detonate on contact.
   > How: End ship chests.
   > Tip: wear it into the dragon fight: endermen hit the copies instead.
26. **Experience Disperser**: `relics:experience_disperser` *(after: A True Relic)*
   > What: when any of your relics gains experience, every other equipped relic receives a share of it.
   > How: chests in any dimension; it has no favourite.
   > Tip: it makes a full curio bar level together instead of one relic at a time.
27. **Reliquary**: `reliquary:mob_charm_fragment` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember a treasury. Most of it is scattered now, in chests and in the hands of monsters.
   > What: Reliquary items are crafted from mob parts: hearts, glands, pearls and charm fragments.
   > How: mob charm fragments drop from mobs. JEI shows the charm they build.
   > Tip: a Mob Charm stops that mob type attacking you.
28. **Alkahestry Tome**: `reliquary:alkahestry_tome` *(after: Reliquary)*
   > What: charged with redstone, the tome duplicates common items in a crafting grid.
   > Chemistry: alchemists searched for alkahest, a universal solvent. None exists (what would you keep it in?), but aqua regia, HCl + HNO₃, dissolves even gold.
   > How: check JEI for the tome and its recipes. Recharge it with redstone.
29. **Relic Hunter**: checkmark *(after: Reliquary)*
   > What: find any Relics or Artifacts item: a cloud in a bottle, running shoes, a leafy mantle, a mimic's treasure.
   > How: loot chests in dungeons, mineshafts and towers, and beware chests that bite. Click the checkmark when you have one.
   > Tip: Relics items level up as you use them; check their tooltips.
30. **Fortune Coin**: `reliquary:fortune_coin` *(after: Alkahestry Tome)*
   > What: pulls nearby items and XP toward you while active.
   > How: check JEI. Right-click to toggle it.
   > Tip: turn it off near your sorting system or it'll grab the items.
31. **Relic Growth**: checkmark *(after: A True Relic)*
   > What: relics earn experience when you use their abilities, and their levels make those abilities stronger.
   > How: keep the relic equipped and use it. Open its ability screen (the tooltip names the key) to spend levels. Click the checkmark after your first upgrade.
   > Tip: one well-levelled relic beats a drawer full of new ones.
32. **An Artifact**: 1x any of `or(item(artifacts:anglers_hat)item(artifacts:antidote_vessel)item(artifacts:aqua_dashers)item(artifacts:bunny_hoppers)item(artifacts:charm_of_shrinking)item(artifacts:charm_of_sinking)item(artifacts:chorus_totem)item(artifacts:cloud_in_a_bottle)item(artifacts:cowboy_hat)item(artifacts:cross_necklace)item(artifacts:crystal_heart)item(artifacts:digging_claws)item(artifacts:eternal_steak)item(artifacts:everlasting_beef)item(artifacts:feral_claws)item(artifacts:fire_gauntlet)item(artifacts:flame_pendant)item(artifacts:flippers)item(artifacts:golden_hook)item(artifacts:helium_flamingo)item(artifacts:kitty_slippers)item(artifacts:lucky_scarf)item(artifacts:night_vision_goggles)item(artifacts:novelty_drinking_hat)item(artifacts:obsidian_skull)item(artifacts:onion_ring)item(artifacts:panic_necklace)item(artifacts:pickaxe_heater)item(artifacts:plastic_drinking_hat)item(artifacts:pocket_piston)item(artifacts:power_glove)item(artifacts:rooted_boots)item(artifacts:running_shoes)item(artifacts:scarf_of_invisibility)item(artifacts:shock_pendant)item(artifacts:snorkel)item(artifacts:snowshoes)item(artifacts:steadfast_spikes)item(artifacts:strider_shoes)item(artifacts:superstitious_hat)item(artifacts:thorn_pendant)item(artifacts:umbrella)item(artifacts:universal_attractor)item(artifacts:vampiric_glove)item(artifacts:villager_hat)item(artifacts:warp_drive)item(artifacts:whoopee_cushion)item(artifacts:withered_bracelet))` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Artifacts are simple, always-on curios: Running Shoes, Cloud in a Bottle, Digging Claws, a Lucky Scarf and many more.
   > How: found in chests underground and in structures, and dropped by Mimics. Any one artifact completes this quest.
   > Tip: the full list, one quest per artifact, is the Artifacts page under Tools and Gear.
33. **That Chest Has Teeth**: checkmark *(after: An Artifact)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Lid and Teeth" on the Artifacts page. Click to dismiss.
34. **Divine Comedy**: checkmark *(after: An Artifact)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Whoopee Cushion" on the Artifacts page. Click to dismiss.
35. **Mob Ingredients**: 2x `reliquary:zombie_heart` *(after: Reliquary)*
   > What: Reliquary items are built from rare mob parts: zombie hearts, rib bones, catalyzing glands, slime pearls, molten cores and more.
   > How: they drop from their mobs (zombies drop zombie hearts). In this pack they can also be crafted: a zombie heart is rotten flesh in a ring of iron ingots.
   > Tip: a Looting sword makes the drops much more common than the iron recipe.
36. **Mob Charm Belt**: `reliquary:mob_charm_belt` *(after: Mob Ingredients)*
   > What: the belt holds Mob Charms, so you can be ignored by several mob types at once.
   > How: three leather and five mob charm fragments (check JEI). Each fragment is made from that mob's drops.
   > Tip: creeper and enderman charms are the most valuable around a base.
37. **Void Tear**: `reliquary:void_tear` *(after: Mob Ingredients, Ghast Tears)*
   > What: a Void Tear stores a huge stack of one item, and pulls more of it from your inventory.
   > How: a ghast tear, a nebulous heart, a slime pearl and lapis (shapeless).
   > Tip: it's also an ingredient for the Infernal Tear, Emperor's Chalice and Midas Touchstone.
38. **Lantern of Paranoia**: `reliquary:lantern_of_paranoia` *(after: Mob Ingredients)*
   > What: the lantern places torches from your inventory wherever it's dark enough for mobs to spawn.
   > How: iron ingots, glass, a slime pearl and a molten core (check JEI).
   > Tip: carry a stack of torches when caving and let it do the lighting.
39. **The Handgun**: `reliquary:handgun` *(after: Mob Ingredients)*
   > What: a pistol that fires magazines of special bullets: neutral, exorcism, blaze, ender, storm, seeker and more.
   > How: barrel, grip and hammer assemblies plus iron and a slime pearl. Bullets and magazines have their own recipes (check JEI).
   > Tip: Seeker bullets home in on targets; good against flying mobs.
40. **Phoenix Down**: `reliquary:phoenix_down` *(after: Mob Ingredients, Into the Fire)*
   > What: saves you from death, heals you, and gives you a few seconds of protection. It has several charges.
   > How: three Angelheart Vials and an Angelic Feather. Vials need milk, glass, fertile essence and an infernal claw (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep it in your inventory before boss fights and Nether trips.

### Artifacts

*Simple, always-on curios from chests, ruins and Mimics.*

1. **Trinkets in the Dirt**: checkmark *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember leaving little gifts around the world for mortals to find. Some of them are still here.
   > What: Artifacts are curios with one or two fixed, always-on effects: no levels, no fuel, no upkeep. Wear them in the matching curio slot.
   > How: they turn up in structure chests (mineshafts, dungeons, temples, villages, bastions, End cities), in archaeology loot, on rare mobs that spawn wearing one, and inside Mimics.
   > Tip: a zombie in a cowboy hat is worth chasing: mobs that spawn wearing an artifact can drop it. Click the checkmark when you have read this.
2. **Lid and Teeth**: kill 1x `artifacts:mimic` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a Mimic is a chest that bites. Each one drops a random artifact, so it is the closest thing to an artifact farm.
   > How: they hide underground, in mineshafts and in the mod's small campsites. If a chest sits somewhere odd, hit it before you open it.
   > Tip: they jump and hit hard for their size. Bring armour, not a wooden sword.
3. **Strider Shoes**: `artifacts:strider_shoes` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: shoes that let you walk on lava like a strider, and spare you the burn from magma and other hot floors.
   > How: Nether fortress chests, ruined portals, dungeon chests, warm ocean ruins (brushing), or a piglin brute wearing them.
   > Tip: they don't stop fire damage from falling in sideways. Keep a fire-resistance source too.
4. **Rooted Boots**: `artifacts:rooted_boots` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: boots that slowly refill your hunger while you walk on grass, and make nearby plants grow after you eat.
   > How: jungle temples, ancient cities, pillager outposts, strongholds, trail ruins (brushing), or a bogged wearing them.
   > Tip: stand on the grass in your farm while you eat, and the crops get a free bonemeal.
5. **Flippers**: `artifacts:flippers` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: flippers that make you much faster and more agile in water.
   > How: buried treasure, shipwrecks, big ocean ruins, or a drowned wearing them.
   > Tip: with a Snorkel, an ocean monument becomes an afternoon job.
6. **Steadfast Spikes**: `artifacts:steadfast_spikes` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: spiked boots that make you immune to knockback.
   > How: bastion treasure, pillager outposts, shipwrecks, armourer chests in villages, trail ruins, or a stray wearing them.
   > Tip: no more being punched off a ledge by a ravager or into lava by a blaze.
7. **Snowshoes**: `artifacts:snowshoes` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: shoes that let you walk on powder snow, move faster on snow and keep your grip on ice.
   > How: igloos, snowy and taiga village houses, an ancient city's ice box, trail ruins, or a stray wearing them.
   > Tip: powder snow traps are a classic grave in frozen peaks; these remove the risk.
8. **Running Shoes**: `artifacts:running_shoes` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: shoes that boost your sprint speed and let you step up full blocks while sprinting.
   > How: village armourers, shipwrecks, Nether fortresses, warm ocean ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: the step-up means you can sprint over rough ground without jumping.
9. **Kitty Slippers**: `artifacts:kitty_slippers` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: slippers that make creepers avoid you and hiss at phantoms that try to swoop on you.
   > How: jungle temples, buried treasure, village tanneries, desert pyramids (brushing).
   > Tip: wear them while building: a creeper near a half-finished wall is the worst kind of surprise.
10. **Bunny Hoppers**: `artifacts:bunny_hoppers` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: hoppers that raise your jump height and cut your fall damage.
   > How: jungle temples, buried treasure, bastion hoglin stables, village tanneries, warm ocean ruins, or a zombie wearing them.
   > Tip: with a Cloud in a Bottle you can clear most walls in two jumps.
11. **Aqua-Dashers**: `artifacts:aqua_dashers` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: shoes that let you run across water and other fluids while sprinting.
   > How: mineshafts, ancient cities, strongholds, buried treasure, warm ocean ruins and trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: stop sprinting and you sink, so don't try a lake while hungry.
12. **Withered Bracelet**: `artifacts:withered_bracelet` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a bracelet whose melee attacks can inflict the wither effect.
   > How: dungeon chests, Nether fortresses, bastion hoglin stables, cold ocean ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: wither damage keeps ticking through a mob's regeneration.
13. **Pickaxe Heater**: `artifacts:pickaxe_heater` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hand curio that smelts the ores you mine as they drop.
   > How: mineshafts, ancient cities, strongholds, bastion hoglin stables, trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: it saves furnace time only. Raw ore through the processing lines gives more metal per block.
14. **Pocket Piston**: `artifacts:pocket_piston` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a piston on your hand that adds knockback to your attacks.
   > How: village toolsmiths, Nether fortresses, pillager outposts, trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: great on a ledge, terrible in a cave where the mob lands just out of reach.
15. **Power Glove**: `artifacts:power_glove` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a glove that raises your attack damage.
   > How: pillager outposts, ruined portals, strongholds, big ocean ruins, desert pyramids (brushing).
   > Tip: pair it with Feral Claws for more hits that each land harder.
16. **Feral Claws**: `artifacts:feral_claws` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: claws that raise your attack speed, so your weapon recharges sooner.
   > How: buried treasure, shipwrecks, village weaponsmiths, trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: a slow heavy weapon gains the most from them.
17. **Onion Ring**: `artifacts:onion_ring` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a ring you can't eat that gives you Haste for a while after you eat food.
   > How: mineshafts, ancient cities, desert pyramids, warm ocean ruins, or a piglin brute wearing it.
   > Tip: eat a cheap snack right before a long mining run.
18. **Golden Hook**: `artifacts:golden_hook` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hook that makes creatures drop more experience.
   > How: buried treasure, shipwrecks, bastion treasure, or a piglin or zombified piglin wearing it.
   > Tip: wear it at your mob farm; enchanting and repairs cost a lot of levels.
19. **Vampiric Glove**: `artifacts:vampiric_glove` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a glove whose melee attacks give you back part of the damage dealt as health.
   > How: mineshafts, desert pyramids, village armourers, warm ocean ruins, or a husk wearing it.
   > Tip: it rewards staying in the fight: the more you hit, the less food you burn healing.
20. **Fire Gauntlet**: `artifacts:fire_gauntlet` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a gauntlet whose melee attacks set the target on fire.
   > How: bastion treasure, ruined portals, big ocean ruins, cold ocean ruins (brushing), or a wither skeleton wearing it.
   > Tip: fire-immune Nether mobs shrug it off; it shines in the Overworld.
21. **Digging Claws**: `artifacts:digging_claws` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: claws that raise your mining speed (the tooltip also lists the tool tier your bare hands reach).
   > How: mineshafts, buried treasure, village toolsmiths, cold ocean ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: they stack with your pickaxe's own speed, so they help long after your first tools.
22. **Warp Drive**: `artifacts:warp_drive` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a belt curio that stops ender pearls being used up when thrown (they cost hunger instead) and stops pearl damage.
   > How: dungeon chests, ancient cities, End cities, village temples, desert wells (brushing).
   > Tip: one stack of one pearl becomes a teleporter. Carry food.
23. **Chorus Totem**: `artifacts:chorus_totem` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: when a hit would kill you, the totem may teleport you somewhere nearby instead.
   > How: End city treasure and woodland mansions.
   > Tip: read its tooltip for the chance and cooldown, and don't count on two saves in one fight.
24. **Helium Flamingo**: `artifacts:helium_flamingo` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a pool float that lets you swim through the air for a short time; press its key while airborne.
   > How: ancient cities, strongholds and End city treasure.
   > Tip: helium (He) is about seven times less dense than air, which is why a real float filled with it would rise. This one just bends the rules.
25. **Crystal Heart**: `artifacts:crystal_heart` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a heart that raises your maximum health.
   > How: bastion treasure, pillager outposts and End city treasure.
   > Tip: more health means more room for everything else to go wrong.
26. **Antidote Vessel**: `artifacts:antidote_vessel` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a flask that greatly shortens poison, wither, slowness and other harmful effects on you.
   > How: bastion treasure, strongholds, village temples, cold ocean ruins, or a bogged or wither skeleton wearing it.
   > Tip: real antidotes work by binding or neutralising the poison; this one is more polite and just shortens it.
27. **Universal Attractor**: `artifacts:universal_attractor` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a magnet that pulls nearby items towards you (its tooltip names the toggle key).
   > How: desert pyramids, ruined portals, shipwrecks, desert wells (brushing), or a piglin or zombified piglin wearing it.
   > Tip: switch it off near your sorting system, or it pulls items out of the floor and into your pockets.
28. **Obsidian Skull**: `artifacts:obsidian_skull` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a skull that gives you fire resistance for a while after you take fire damage.
   > How: mineshafts, ruined portals, shipwrecks, desert pyramids (brushing), or a piglin or zombified piglin wearing it.
   > Tip: it reacts to the first burn, so it saves you from the second. Still bring a potion to the Nether.
29. **Cloud in a Bottle**: `artifacts:cloud_in_a_bottle` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a bottled cloud that lets you double jump.
   > How: mineshafts, pillager outposts, big ocean ruins, End city treasure, trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: the second jump also resets a fall, so a late double jump can save you from a long drop.
30. **Charm of Shrinking**: `artifacts:charm_of_shrinking` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a charm that shrinks you while worn.
   > How: dungeon chests, Nether fortresses, ruined portals, village weaponsmiths, trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: small players fit through one-block gaps. Great for sneaking, odd for building.
31. **Charm of Sinking**: `artifacts:charm_of_sinking` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a charm that lets you move freely underwater, as if on land.
   > How: ancient cities, desert pyramids, shipwrecks, village temples, desert wells (brushing).
   > Tip: you still need air. Bring a Snorkel or water breathing.
32. **Thorn Pendant**: `artifacts:thorn_pendant` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a pendant with a chance to damage anything that attacks you.
   > How: desert pyramids, ruined portals, trail ruins (brushing), or a husk wearing it.
   > Tip: it stacks with the Thorns enchantment on your armour.
33. **Flame Pendant**: `artifacts:flame_pendant` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a pendant with a chance to set attackers on fire, and to give you fire resistance when it does.
   > How: desert pyramids, bastion hoglin stables, trail ruins (brushing), or a skeleton wearing it.
   > Tip: it does nothing to fire-immune Nether mobs; it shines in the Overworld.
34. **Shock Pendant**: `artifacts:shock_pendant` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a pendant with a chance to strike attackers with lightning, and that protects you from lightning yourself.
   > How: ancient cities and desert pyramids (chests and brushing).
   > Tip: lightning that hits a creeper charges it. Be careful who you anger.
35. **Panic Necklace**: `artifacts:panic_necklace` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a necklace that gives you a burst of speed after you take damage.
   > How: mineshafts, bastion treasure and pillager outposts.
   > Tip: it turns a bad fight into a quick escape; use it.
36. **Cross Necklace**: `artifacts:cross_necklace` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a necklace that lengthens the short invulnerable moment after you take damage.
   > How: bastion treasure, Nether fortresses, pillager outposts, big ocean ruins, village temples.
   > Tip: it shines against many weak hits at once, like a swarm or a skeleton volley.
37. **Lucky Scarf**: `artifacts:lucky_scarf` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a scarf that adds a level of Fortune to the blocks you mine.
   > How: igloos, ruined portals, strongholds, buried treasure, big and cold ocean ruins.
   > Tip: it stacks with a Fortune pickaxe, which makes it best on diamonds, coal and other gem ores.
38. **Scarf of Invisibility**: `artifacts:scarf_of_invisibility` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a scarf that turns you invisible while worn.
   > How: desert pyramids, pillager outposts, shipwrecks, village tanneries, or a zombie wearing it.
   > Tip: armour still shows. Take it off for the full effect.
39. **Angler's Hat**: `artifacts:anglers_hat` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hat that adds a level of Luck of the Sea and of Lure to your fishing.
   > How: jungle temples, buried treasure, big ocean ruins, village tanneries, cold ocean ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: with a good rod, treasure from fishing becomes a real income.
40. **Cowboy Hat**: `artifacts:cowboy_hat` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hat that makes whatever you ride faster.
   > How: Nether fortresses, ruined portals, bastion hoglin stables, desert pyramids (brushing), or a zombie wearing it.
   > Tip: it works on horses, pigs and striders alike.
41. **Superstitious Hat**: `artifacts:superstitious_hat` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hat that adds a level of Looting to your kills.
   > How: mineshafts, pillager outposts, strongholds, big ocean ruins, village armourers, desert wells (brushing).
   > Tip: stack it with a Looting sword at your mob farm.
42. **Villager Hat**: `artifacts:villager_hat` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hat that lowers the prices villagers ask you.
   > How: village houses in every biome, igloos and trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: wear it before you open the trade window; prices update as you look.
43. **Night Vision Goggles**: `artifacts:night_vision_goggles` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: goggles that give you night vision while worn.
   > How: mineshafts, Nether fortresses, ruined portals, shipwrecks, desert pyramids (brushing), or a skeleton wearing them.
   > Tip: spotting ore in a dark cave gets much easier; mobs still spawn there.
44. **Snorkel**: `artifacts:snorkel` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a snorkel that lets you breathe underwater for a while.
   > How: buried treasure, shipwrecks, big ocean ruins, desert pyramids (brushing), or a drowned wearing it.
   > Tip: its tooltip says how long; pair it with the Charm of Sinking for long dives.
45. **Novelty Drinking Hat**: `artifacts:novelty_drinking_hat` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: the grand version of the drinking hat: potions and food go down much faster.
   > How: the same loot as the plastic hat (mineshafts, buried treasure, Nether fortresses, desert wells), only rarer, or a skeleton wearing it.
   > Tip: a fast potion in a boss fight is worth more than it sounds.
46. **Plastic Drinking Hat**: `artifacts:plastic_drinking_hat` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a hat with two cans and a straw: potions and food go down faster.
   > How: mineshafts, buried treasure, Nether fortresses, desert wells (brushing), or a skeleton wearing it.
   > Tip: real plastic is a polymer: long chains of small molecules such as ethylene, which the pack teaches you to make later.
47. **Whoopee Cushion**: `artifacts:whoopee_cushion` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a cushion that makes a rude noise when you crouch. That's all it does.
   > How: spawn bonus chests, desert pyramids, village tanneries, trail ruins (brushing).
   > Tip: the relics page has a secret for this one too.
48. **Everlasting Beef**: `artifacts:everlasting_beef` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: a piece of raw beef you can eat forever: it isn't used up.
   > How: rarely dropped by cows and mooshrooms, or from village butchers and bastion hoglin stables.
   > Tip: cook it to get the Eternal Steak, a better meal that also never runs out.
49. **Eternal Steak**: `artifacts:eternal_steak` *(after: Everlasting Beef)*
   > What: the cooked Everlasting Beef: a full steak's food that is never used up.
   > How: cook Everlasting Beef in a furnace, smoker or on a campfire.
   > Tip: cooking browns meat by the Maillard reaction: amino acids and sugars react at about 140 °C into hundreds of flavour compounds.
50. **Umbrella**: `artifacts:umbrella` *(after: Trinkets in the Dirt)*
   > What: held in your hand, the umbrella slows your fall and can block like a shield.
   > How: buried treasure, desert pyramids, village tanneries, desert wells (brushing).
   > Tip: keep it in hand while building high up: a slip becomes a slow drift.

### Silent Gear

*Gear built part by part: the material decides the stats.*

1. **Every Part a Choice**: checkmark *(after: Tools from Parts)*
   > You remember weapons shaped to the hand that held them. Here you get to shape your own again.
   > What: every Silent Gear item is assembled from parts (head, rod, binding, grip, tip, coating), and each part takes the stats and traits of its material.
   > How: make a blueprint or template for a part, craft the part from a material, then put the parts together in a crafting grid. JEI and the Material Book show every material's stats.
   > Tip: click the checkmark when you have read this. The quests below are one per gear type.
2. **Metal and Fuel**: `minecraft:iron_ingot`; `minecraft:coal` *(after: Every Part a Choice)*
   > What: iron is the first good head material for Silent Gear parts, and coal fuels the smelting (and later the Alloy Forge).
   > Chemistry: in a furnace, coal burns to carbon monoxide, which strips the oxygen from iron oxide: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
   > How: smelt raw iron with coal. Hold one of each.
   > Tip: every quest on this page hangs from here: pick the gear types you want and ignore the rest until you need them.
3. **Sword**: `silentgear:sword` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a sword: a blade and a rod, plus optional binding, grip and coating.
   > How: sword blueprint (blueprint paper and a stick), a sword blade from your material, then the blade and a rod in a crafting grid.
   > Tip: the blade's material sets damage and durability; the rod mostly adds traits.
4. **Katana**: `silentgear:katana` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a katana: a long single-edged blade that swings faster than a sword.
   > How: katana blueprint and a katana blade, then assemble with a rod (check JEI).
   > Tip: light, fast weapons suit materials with high attack speed.
5. **Machete**: `silentgear:machete` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a machete: a heavy blade that also clears leaves and plants quickly.
   > How: machete blueprint and blade, then assemble with a rod (check JEI).
   > Tip: the right tool for clearing a jungle around a base.
6. **Knife**: `silentgear:knife` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a knife: a quick little blade, and Silent Gear's tool for cutting logs into template boards.
   > How: knife blueprint and blade, then assemble with a rod (check JEI).
   > Tip: a knife cuts one log into six template boards (a tool action; check JEI).
7. **Dagger**: `silentgear:dagger` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a dagger: very fast attacks with low damage per hit.
   > How: dagger blueprint and blade, then assemble with a rod (check JEI).
   > Tip: a dagger built from a material with an on-hit trait triggers that trait often.
8. **Trident**: `silentgear:trident` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a Silent Gear trident built from prongs of your chosen material.
   > How: the trident blueprint needs a vanilla trident and a heart of the sea (check JEI); then make the prongs and assemble.
   > Tip: drowned holding a trident are the only source of the vanilla one; fight them in the rain-free shallows.
9. **Mace Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:mace_blueprint)item(silentgear:mace_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the blueprint for Silent Gear's mace, a heavy weapon with a mace core of your material.
   > How: blueprint paper and a breeze rod (from breezes in trial chambers); check JEI.
   > Tip: like the vanilla mace, it rewards hitting from a height.
10. **Spear**: `silentgear:spear` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a spear: a tipped weapon that reaches further than a sword.
   > How: spear blueprint and a spear tip, then assemble with a rod (check JEI).
   > Tip: the extra reach keeps creepers a step further away.
11. **Bow**: `silentgear:bow` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a bow whose limbs set draw speed, damage and range.
   > How: bow blueprint, bow limbs and a bowstring (cord) of string or flax, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: flax string from Silent Gear's flax plant makes a decent cord.
12. **Crossbow**: `silentgear:crossbow` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a crossbow built from crossbow limbs and a cord.
   > How: crossbow blueprint, limbs and a cord, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: load it before a fight; the first shot is free.
13. **Slingshot**: `silentgear:slingshot` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a slingshot that fires pebbles and other small shot.
   > How: slingshot blueprint, limbs and a cord, then assemble (check JEI). It shoots Silent Gear pebbles.
   > Tip: cheap ammunition makes it a good way to pull mobs out of a group.
14. **Arrows**: `silentgear:arrow` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: Silent Gear arrows: arrow heads, a shaft and fletching, built as one stack-like item.
   > How: arrow blueprint and arrow heads, then assemble with a rod and fletching (check JEI).
   > Tip: heads of a heavy material hit harder; fletching changes how straight they fly.
15. **Fletching Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:fletching_blueprint)item(silentgear:fletching_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the blueprint for fletching, the feather part of Silent Gear arrows.
   > How: two blueprint paper and a feather (check JEI).
   > Tip: Silent Gear's fluffy feathers work as a fletching material too.
16. **Pickaxe**: `silentgear:pickaxe` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a Silent Gear pickaxe, the first part-built tool you made.
   > How: pickaxe blueprint and head, then assemble with a rod (check JEI). You made one on the main path.
   > Tip: upgrade the head material first; it decides mining tier and speed.
17. **Shovel**: `silentgear:shovel` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a shovel built from a shovel head and a rod.
   > How: shovel blueprint and head, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: a fast shovel makes clay and sand runs for glassmaking painless.
18. **Axe**: `silentgear:axe` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: an axe built from an axe head and a rod: a woodcutter and a slow, heavy weapon.
   > How: axe blueprint and head, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also strips logs for charcoal and building.
19. **Paxel**: `silentgear:paxel` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a Silent Gear paxel: pickaxe, axe and shovel in one head.
   > How: paxel blueprint and a paxel head (it needs more material than a pickaxe), then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: one tool slot freed on long trips.
20. **Hammer**: `silentgear:hammer` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a hammer that breaks a 3x3 area of stone and ore at once.
   > How: hammer blueprint and head, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also crushes Silent Gear ingots into dust; the dust quests below need it.
21. **Excavator**: `silentgear:excavator` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the shovel's version of the hammer: dirt, sand and gravel in 3x3.
   > How: excavator blueprint and head, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: perfect for clearing space for a big build.
22. **Mattock**: `silentgear:mattock` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a mattock: a farming tool that tills, chops and digs.
   > How: mattock blueprint and head, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: one tool for the whole farm.
23. **Sickle**: `silentgear:sickle` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a sickle that cuts and harvests plants over an area.
   > How: sickle blueprint and blade, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: a quick harvest for wide crop fields.
24. **Shears**: `silentgear:shears` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: Silent Gear shears with stats from their blades.
   > How: shears blueprint and shear blades, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: durable shears are worth it for a wool farm.
25. **Fishing Rod**: `silentgear:fishing_rod` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a fishing rod with a hook of your chosen material.
   > How: fishing rod blueprint, a fishing hook and a cord, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: the hook's material sets the rod's durability and traits.
26. **Prospector Hammer**: `silentgear:prospector_hammer` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a hammer that scans for ores near the block you strike.
   > How: prospector hammer blueprint and head, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: pair it with the Spectrometer from the main path to plan a dig before you start.
27. **Shield**: `silentgear:shield` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a shield built from a shield plate of any material.
   > How: shield blueprint and plate, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: a tough material means fewer repairs between fights.
28. **Helmet**: `silentgear:helmet` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a helmet built from helmet plates of your material.
   > How: helmet blueprint and plates, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: armour from parts can carry traits that vanilla armour never has.
29. **Chestplate**: `silentgear:chestplate` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a chestplate built from chestplate plates.
   > How: chestplate blueprint and plates, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: it carries the most armour, so give it your best material.
30. **Leggings**: `silentgear:leggings` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: leggings built from legging plates.
   > How: leggings blueprint and plates, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: a lining (the blueprint below) adds a second material's traits.
31. **Boots**: `silentgear:boots` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: boots built from boot plates.
   > How: boots blueprint and plates, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: linings work on boots too; check the Material Book for useful traits.
32. **Elytra Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:elytra_blueprint)item(silentgear:elytra_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel, The End)*
   > What: the blueprint for Silent Gear's elytra, whose wings take stats from their material.
   > How: blueprint paper, gold, phantom membrane and a real elytra from an End ship (check JEI).
   > Tip: you need one vanilla elytra to make the blueprint, then can build wings from better materials.
33. **Ring**: `silentgear:ring` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a ring: a shank and an optional gem setting, worn as a curio.
   > How: ring blueprint and shank, then assemble with a setting (check JEI).
   > Tip: jewellery gives you its material's traits while worn, so pick a material for its trait.
34. **Bracelet**: `silentgear:bracelet` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a bracelet: a band and an optional setting, worn as a curio.
   > How: bracelet blueprint and band, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: a second jewellery slot for a second trait.
35. **Necklace**: `silentgear:necklace` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a necklace: a chain and an optional setting, worn as a curio.
   > How: necklace blueprint and chain, then assemble (check JEI).
   > Tip: the third jewellery piece; together they can carry three different traits.
36. **Lining Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:lining_blueprint)item(silentgear:lining_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the blueprint for armour linings, an extra material layer inside a piece of armour.
   > How: three blueprint paper, two wool and two string (check JEI).
   > Tip: a lining adds its material's traits without changing the armour plates.
37. **Tips**: `silentgear:tip` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a tip: an upgrade part that caps a tool or weapon with another material.
   > How: tip blueprint (two blueprint paper, paper and stone), then a tip from your material; add it to a tool in a crafting grid.
   > Tip: a diamond or quartz tip is a cheap upgrade for an iron tool.
38. **Coating Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:coating_blueprint)item(silentgear:coating_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the blueprint for coatings, a layer of a better material over a tool's main part.
   > How: four blueprint paper, a diamond and an emerald (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Coatings quest on the Gear and Comfort page covers the smithing template route.
39. **Grip Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:grip_blueprint)item(silentgear:grip_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the blueprint for grips, a handle wrap that adds its material's traits.
   > How: two blueprint paper and a grip material such as leather or wool (check JEI).
   > Tip: grips are cheap, so try different ones.
40. **Binding Blueprint**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:binding_blueprint)item(silentgear:binding_template))` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: the blueprint for bindings, which tie a head to its rod and add their own traits.
   > How: blueprint paper and two binding materials such as string or vines (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Material Book shows which bindings add which traits.
41. **Rods**: `silentgear:rod` *(after: Metal and Fuel)*
   > What: a rod: the handle part of nearly every Silent Gear tool and weapon.
   > How: rod blueprint (blueprint paper and sticks), then rods from wood, bone, blaze rods, metal and more.
   > Tip: the rod's material adds traits; a blaze rod handle is a classic.
42. **Salvager**: `silentgear:salvager` *(after: Metal and Fuel, Crimson Iron)*
   > What: a machine that breaks old Silent Gear items back into their parts.
   > How: a piston, crimson iron ingots, an iron block and obsidian (check JEI). Crimson iron ore is in the Nether.
   > Tip: salvage before upgrading; some material is lost, most comes back.
43. **Material Grader**: `silentgear:material_grader` *(after: Salvager, Into the Fire)*
   > What: a machine that grades materials; a higher grade adds bonus stats to every part made from it.
   > How: quartz, iron, three blaze gold ingots and an Advanced Upgrade Base (check JEI).
   > Tip: grade the material you use for heads; that's where the stats live.
44. **Glowing Dust**: `silentgear:glowing_dust` *(after: Material Grader)*
   > What: the tier 1 catalyst for the Material Grader, spent on each try.
   > How: a stick, two glowstone dust and a quartz make four (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep a stack by the grader.
45. **Blazing Dust**: `silentgear:blazing_dust` *(after: Material Grader)*
   > What: the tier 2 Grader catalyst, for higher grades.
   > How: blaze gold dust and two glowstone dust make four. Crush blaze gold with a hammer first (check JEI).
   > Tip: a better catalyst raises the highest grade you can reach.
46. **Glittery Dust**: `silentgear:glittery_dust` *(after: Material Grader, The End)*
   > What: the tier 3 Grader catalyst, for the best grades.
   > How: popped chorus fruit, emerald nuggets, glowstone dust and a nether banana make eight (check JEI).
   > Tip: chorus grows in the End; nether bananas grow on netherwood trees.
47. **Recrystallizer**: `silentgear:recrystallizer` *(after: Salvager, The End)*
   > What: a machine that fuses gems into hybrid gem materials with mixed stats.
   > How: azure electrum ingots, an emerald, a diamond, purpur blocks and a gold block (check JEI).
   > Tip: experiment with cheap gems before feeding it diamonds.
48. **Alloy Forge**: `silentgear:alloy_forge` *(after: Material Grader, Crimson Steel)*
   > What: the forge that makes Silent Gear's alloys: blaze gold, crimson steel, azure electrum and tyrian steel.
   > How: crimson steel ingots, blackstone and an iron block (check JEI). Fuel it like a furnace.
   > Tip: the forge gives more ingots per batch than the crafting routes.
49. **Starlight Charger**: `silentgear:starlight_charger` *(after: Alloy Forge)*
   > What: a block that collects starlight at night and charges Silent Gear materials for a bonus.
   > How: quartz blocks, glass, polished blackstone and a blaze gold block (check JEI). Place it under open sky.
   > Tip: the catalyst's tier caps how strong the charge gets.
50. **Crimson Steel Block**: `silentgear:crimson_steel_block` *(after: Starlight Charger)*
   > What: a storage block of crimson steel.
   > How: nine crimson steel ingots from the Alloy Forge.
   > Tip: it decorates as well as it stores.
51. **Azure Electrum Block**: `silentgear:azure_electrum_block` *(after: Starlight Charger, The End)*
   > What: a storage block of azure electrum.
   > How: nine azure electrum ingots; azure silver ore is in the End and needs a netherite-tier pick.
   > Tip: electrum is a real gold-silver alloy; the azure part is Silent Gear's.
52. **Tyrian Steel Block**: `silentgear:tyrian_steel_block` *(after: Starlight Charger, The End)*
   > What: a storage block of tyrian steel, Silent Gear's top alloy.
   > How: nine tyrian steel ingots from the Alloy Forge (crimson steel, azure electrum, crushed shulker shell, netherite scrap; check JEI).
   > Tip: make sure you have enough ingots for your gear first.
53. **Blaze Gold Dust**: `silentgear:blaze_gold_dust` *(after: Starlight Charger)*
   > What: blaze gold crushed into dust: the tier 1 Starlight Charger catalyst and the base of blazing dust.
   > How: crush a blaze gold ingot with a hammer (a tool action; check JEI).
   > Tip: crushing a metal hugely increases its surface area, which is why fine powders react so much faster than bars.
54. **Azure Silver Dust**: `silentgear:azure_silver_dust` *(after: Starlight Charger, The End)*
   > What: azure silver crushed into dust, for the charger and for starmetal.
   > How: crush an azure silver ingot with a hammer (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep two for the starmetal recipe.
55. **Starmetal Dust**: `silentgear:starmetal_dust` *(after: Starlight Charger, The End, The Wither)*
   > What: starmetal dust, a late Silent Gear material and charger catalyst.
   > How: azure electrum dust, two azure silver dust, blaze gold dust and a nether star fragment make three (check JEI).
   > Tip: one Nether Star crafts into nine fragments.
56. **Any Repair Kit**: 1x any of `or(item(silentgear:very_crude_repair_kit)item(silentgear:crude_repair_kit)item(silentgear:sturdy_repair_kit)item(silentgear:crimson_repair_kit)item(silentgear:azure_repair_kit))` *(after: Repair Kits)*
   > What: a repair kit holds repair materials and mends Silent Gear in a crafting grid. Five tiers, each holding more.
   > How: very crude (template boards, a stick and stone), crude (iron), sturdy (iron and a diamond), crimson (crimson steel and blaze gold), azure (azure electrum and an emerald). Check JEI.
   > Tip: better kits hold more material and repair more per use (check the tooltip).

### Quality of Life

*Small things that make a big difference.*

1. **Comfort First**: checkmark *(after: Planks and a Workbench)*
   > You remember never wasting a motion. These small things feel familiar.
   > What: this page collects the mods that save time and clicks: guidebooks, backpacks, waystones, maps, keybinds and the Utilitarian shortcuts.
   > How: each row is one topic. Nearly everything here is optional, so pick what helps you. Click the checkmark to open the page.
   > Tip: none of this is needed for the main path, but most of it pays for itself within an hour.
2. **One Book to Rule Them All**: `akashictome:tome` *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: the Akashic Tome merges every mod's guidebook into one item.
   > How: craft it, then right-click it with other guidebooks to add them.
   > Tip: right-click the tome to choose which book to open.
3. **Find Anything**: `naturescompass:naturescompass`; `explorerscompass:explorerscompass` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: Nature's Compass finds biomes; Explorer's Compass finds structures (Nether Fortresses, Ancient Cities, villages).
   > How: craft both (check JEI), right-click to pick a target, then follow the needle.
   > Tip: the Explorer's Compass is the fastest way to find an Ancient City for the Deeper and Darker quests.
4. **No More Mob Spawns**: `torchmaster:megatorch` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: the Mega Torch stops hostile mobs spawning naturally in a huge radius.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe and place it near the middle of your base.
   > Tip: it blocks natural spawns only. Spawners and Simulation Chambers still work.
5. **Graves**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: if you die, Corail Tombstone keeps your items in a grave where you fell.
   > How: walk back and open the grave to recover everything. Click the checkmark once you've read this.
   > Tip: JourneyMap drops a waypoint where you died, so the grave is easy to find.
6. **Backups**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: Simple Backups saves your world automatically.
   > How: on a server, backups live in the server's backups folder. In single player, look in your instance folder.
   > Tip: copy a backup somewhere else before trying risky reactor builds.
7. **Dread Lamp**: `torchmaster:dreadlamp` *(after: No More Mob Spawns, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Dread Lamp blocks Nether mob spawns in a large radius, the way the Mega Torch does for Overworld mobs.
   > How: check JEI. Place it at your Nether base or portal hub.
   > Tip: place it before building in the Nether so your base stays quiet.
8. **Rest Anywhere**: 1x any of `item_tag(comforts:sleeping_bags)` *(after: Comfort First, A Bed)*
   > What: A sleeping bag from Comforts skips the night without moving your spawn point, so it's ideal while exploring.
   > How: 3 wool of one colour in a vertical column. Any colour of sleeping bag counts.
   > Tip: Hammocks skip the day instead (Gear and Comfort page).
9. **Crafting on a Stick**: `crafting_on_a_stick:crafting_table` *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: a crafting table you carry around. Right-click it to open a 3x3 grid anywhere: in a mine, out exploring, mid-build.
   > How: craft it from a crafting table and a stick (check JEI). The same mod makes pocket versions of the stonecutter, smithing table, anvil, grindstone, loom and cartography table.
   > Tip: it saves a hotbar slot over placing and breaking tables. The pocket stonecutter is great for building with Create Deco and Rechiseled blocks.
10. **A Whole Workshop**: `crafting_on_a_stick:stonecutter`; `crafting_on_a_stick:smithing_table` *(after: Crafting on a Stick)*
   > What: optional: the pocket stonecutter and smithing table.
   > How: each one is its block plus a stick (check JEI).
   > Tip: the smithing table is how netherite and Apotheosis upgrades are applied, so it's handy to carry.
11. **Backpack Upgrades**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:pickup_upgrade`; `sophisticatedbackpacks:magnet_upgrade` *(after: Comfort First, A Backpack)*
   > What: pickup and magnet upgrades pull items straight into your backpack.
   > How: craft an Upgrade Base, then the upgrades (check JEI). Put them in the backpack's upgrade slots.
   > Tip: set a filter on the pickup upgrade so it only grabs ores and drops you actually want.
12. **Iron Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:iron_backpack` *(after: Comfort First, A Backpack)*
   > What: each backpack tier adds inventory rows and upgrade slots: iron, gold, diamond, netherite.
   > How: surround your backpack with iron ingots (check JEI). It keeps everything inside.
   > Tip: stack upgrades multiply how many items fit in each slot.
13. **Feeding Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:feeding_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrades)*
   > What: eats food from the backpack automatically when you're hungry.
   > How: check JEI. Farmer's Delight meals restore a lot per bite.
   > Tip: set a filter so it doesn't eat your golden apples.
14. **Netherite Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:netherite_backpack` *(after: Iron Backpack)*
   > What: the top tier: the most inventory slots and upgrade space.
   > How: ring the backpack with gold, then diamonds, then smith in a netherite ingot with a netherite upgrade template.
   > Tip: a netherite backpack has room for several stack upgrades at once.
15. **Waystones**: `waystones:waystone` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: waystones are teleport points. Activate one by right-clicking it, then warp between any you've activated.
   > How: found in villages, or craft one (check JEI). Place them at your base, mines and portals.
   > Tip: warping costs a little XP depending on distance; check the config if it seems steep.
16. **Warp Scrolls**: 4x `waystones:warp_scroll` *(after: Waystones)*
   > What: a single-use warp to any activated waystone, handy before you can afford a Warp Stone.
   > How: paper, an ender pearl, gold nuggets and an ink sac (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep one in your backpack for emergencies.
17. **Maps**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: JourneyMap draws a minimap and a full world map as you explore, with waypoints.
   > How: press J for the full JourneyMap. FTB Chunks has its own map for claims (check Controls for its key). Click the checkmark when you've tried them.
   > Tip: drop a waypoint at every rich ore deposit you find. Deposits are rare, so note the depth too.
18. **Inventory Tricks**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: small mods that save hours: Mouse Tweaks (drag and scroll to move stacks), Inventory Tweaks (sorting) and TrashSlot (a trash can in your inventory).
   > How: try a scroll-wheel drag over stacks, the sort button, and the trash slot by your hotbar. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: Polymorph shows a button when two recipes share a grid; click it to pick the one you want.
19. **Feral Flare Lantern**: `torchmaster:feral_flare_lantern` *(after: No More Mob Spawns, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the lantern places invisible light sources in the dark spots around it, so a cave or a big hall lights up without a single torch.
   > How: gold ingots, glass and glowstone dust (check JEI). Place it in the middle of the room.
   > Tip: great for a clean-looking factory floor. It still lets mobs spawn in spots it can't reach.
20. **Grave Tricks**: checkmark *(after: Graves)*
   > What: Corail Tombstone does more than store your items: it adds scrolls, tablets and the Ankh of Prayer, plus a book that makes items soulbound.
   > How: search 'tombstone' in JEI to browse them. Click the checkmark when you've had a look.
   > Tip: by default only you can open your grave, so a death on a server doesn't mean losing your gear to someone else.
21. **Loot for Everyone**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: with Lootr, structure chests (dungeons, temples, villages, mineshafts) hold separate loot for each player.
   > How: open any generated chest. You get your own roll; your friends still get theirs. Click the checkmark when you've seen one.
   > Tip: on a server, nobody has to race to a dungeon first.
22. **Stack Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_1` *(after: Iron Backpack)*
   > What: a stack upgrade multiplies how many items each backpack slot holds. Higher tiers multiply more.
   > How: check JEI; each tier is built from the one before it.
   > Tip: stack upgrades make a backpack the best place to carry dust and ingots between machines.
23. **Tool Swapper**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:tool_swapper_upgrade` *(after: Stack Upgrade)*
   > What: swaps the tool in your hand for the best one in your backpack when you start mining a block or hitting a mob.
   > How: check JEI, then put it in an upgrade slot and fill the backpack with tools.
   > Tip: pairs well with a paxel; it switches to shears or a sword only when needed.
24. **Refill Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:refill_upgrade` *(after: Stack Upgrade)*
   > What: keeps chosen hotbar items topped up from the backpack: torches, blocks, food.
   > How: check JEI. Set the items to refill in the upgrade's tab.
   > Tip: refill building blocks while bridging and you'll never stop to open your inventory.
25. **Pocket Anvil**: `crafting_on_a_stick:anvil`; `crafting_on_a_stick:grindstone` *(after: A Whole Workshop)*
