   > What: pocket versions of the anvil and grindstone, opened with right-click.
   > How: each one is its block plus a stick (check JEI).
   > Tip: the pocket anvil wears down like a placed one, so carry a spare for long trips.
26. **FTB Ultimine**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First, Stone Age)*
   > What: Ultimine breaks every connected matching block at once: a full ore vein, a tree, a strip of stone.
   > How: hold the Ultimine key (default `, the key left of 1) and break a block. Arrow keys up and down change the shape. Click the checkmark when you've tried it.
   > Tip: it can cost extra hunger, so eat first. Shapes include tunnels and flat planes for clearing space.
27. **Form a Team**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: FTB Teams groups players into a party. Teammates share quest progress and claimed chunks.
   > How: open the Teams screen from the button on your inventory screen (or use /ftbteams) and create a party, then invite friends. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: playing alone? A solo party still lets you set chunk permissions for visitors.
28. **Homes and /back**: checkmark *(after: Form a Team)*
   > What: FTB Essentials adds /sethome and /home (one home by default), /back to return to where you died or last teleported, /spawn, and /tpa to ask to teleport to a friend.
   > How: stand at your base and type /sethome, then try /home from somewhere else. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: each command has a short cooldown. /back after a death walks you straight to your grave.
29. **Just Zoom**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: Just Zoom lets you zoom in on the distance with a key, no item needed.
   > How: find its key under Options → Controls, and hold it to zoom (its options are in the Mods menu). Click the checkmark when you've tried it.
   > Tip: handy for spotting structures, meteorites and villages from a hilltop.
30. **Ping Wheel**: checkmark *(after: Form a Team)*
   > What: Ping Wheel puts a marker on the spot you look at, visible to the other players nearby.
   > How: find its keys under Options → Controls. Look at something and ping it. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: ping an ore deposit or a dangerous mob instead of typing coordinates.
31. **Chat Heads**: checkmark *(after: Form a Team)*
   > What: Chat Heads shows each player's face next to their messages in chat.
   > How: nothing to set up; it works as soon as someone talks. Click the checkmark when you've seen it.
   > Tip: its options are in the Mods menu if you want to change how heads are shown.
32. **Trade Cycling**: 16x `minecraft:emerald` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: Trade Cycling adds a button to the villager trade screen that rerolls the offers of a villager nobody has traded with yet.
   > How: give a villager a job block, open its trades and press the cycle button until the offer you want appears. Earn 16 emeralds by trading.
   > Tip: once you trade, the offers lock. Cycle a librarian until it sells the enchanted book you need.
33. **Merchant Prince**: 4x `minecraft:emerald_block` *(after: Trade Cycling)*
   > What: four emerald blocks: 36 emeralds. The villagers have noticed you.
   > Chemistry: emerald is beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, coloured green by traces of chromium.
   > Tip: every Warp Stone needs an emerald, so a good trading hall pays for your travel network.
34. **Tool Belt**: `toolbelt:belt` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: the Tool Belt holds tools outside your hotbar and opens as a radial menu so you can swap fast.
   > How: leather and string (check JEI). Keep it in your inventory; find its key under Options → Controls.
   > Tip: put the wrench, the config card and your paxel on the belt.
35. **Belt Pouches**: 2x `toolbelt:pouch` *(after: Tool Belt)*
   > What: each pouch adds a slot to your tool belt.
   > How: craft pouches, then craft them together with the belt (check JEI).
   > Tip: a full belt keeps your hotbar free for blocks and food.
36. **A Waystone Network**: 4x any of `or(item(waystones:waystone)item(waystones:mossy_waystone)item(waystones:sandy_waystone)item(waystones:deepslate_waystone)item(waystones:blackstone_waystone)item(waystones:end_stone_waystone))` *(after: Waystones)*
   > What: one waystone is a landmark; four make a network. Base, mine, Nether portal and a far-off biome.
   > How: any four waystones of any style (check JEI for the variants), or bring back ones found in villages.
   > Tip: name each one clearly ('Bauxite Mine -40') so the list stays readable.
37. **Warp Stone**: `waystones:warp_stone` *(after: A Waystone Network)*
   > What: a reusable item that opens the waystone menu wherever you stand. It recharges after each use.
   > How: amethyst shards, ender pearls and an emerald (check JEI). It's also in the Demigod Token shop.
   > Tip: with a Warp Stone, warp scrolls become backup only.
38. **Waypoints**: checkmark *(after: Maps)*
   > What: JourneyMap waypoints mark places on the minimap and in the world, with distance shown on screen.
   > How: open the full map (J) and right-click a spot to add a waypoint, or use JourneyMap's waypoint key (see Controls). Click the checkmark when you've made one.
   > Tip: JourneyMap makes a death waypoint for you; share waypoints with teammates in chat.
39. **Utilitarian Shortcuts**: checkmark *(after: Comfort First)*
   > What: the Utilitarian mod adds bulk recipes that skip the planks step (two logs in a column make 16 sticks), plus small handy blocks: tiny coal, the Trowel, the Angel Block, Snad and more. This row is its catalogue.
   > How: press U on any log in JEI to see every log shortcut. Click the checkmark when you've had a look.
   > Tip: the bulk recipes give the same items as the vanilla ones, just with fewer clicks and no waste.
40. **Chests and Ladders**: 4x `minecraft:chest`; 24x `minecraft:ladder` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts)*
   > What: logs in a chest ring make 4 chests at once. Seven logs in a ladder shape make 24 ladders.
   > How: the same shapes as the plank recipes, but with logs (check JEI).
   > Tip: three logs in a V make 12 bowls, and logs between iron make a hopper without a chest.
41. **Slabs and Stairs**: 24x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_slabs)`; 16x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_stairs)` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts)*
   > What: three logs in a row make 24 slabs; six logs in a stair shape make 16 stairs.
   > How: use logs of one wood type in the usual slab or stair shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: two slabs placed diagonally in the grid turn back into a plank, so leftover slabs are never wasted.
42. **Doors and Trapdoors**: 12x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_doors)`; 12x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wooden_trapdoors)` *(after: Slabs and Stairs)*
   > What: six logs in a door shape make 12 doors; six logs in a trapdoor shape make 12 trapdoors.
   > How: one wood type per craft (check JEI). Two logs side by side also make 4 pressure plates.
   > Tip: doors placed side by side open together, so a double door needs only one click.
43. **Re-Dyeing**: 8x any of `item_tag(c:concretes)` *(after: Doors and Trapdoors)*
   > What: Utilitarian lets you re-dye concrete, concrete powder, terracotta, stained glass, glass panes and candles that already have a colour.
   > Chemistry: real pigments are chemicals too: concrete's colours come from metal oxides, like iron oxide (Fe₂O₃) for red and brown.
   > How: eight coloured blocks around one dye re-colours all eight, or one block plus one dye does a single block (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also mixes blue and yellow dye into green, so cactus isn't the only green.
44. **Tiny Coal**: 8x `utilitarian:tiny_coal`; 8x `utilitarian:tiny_charcoal` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts, Coal)*
   > What: one coal or charcoal makes 8 tiny pieces. Each burns for 10 seconds, so you don't waste a whole coal on one item.
   > Chemistry: charcoal is wood heated without air (pyrolysis): water and volatile compounds are driven off, leaving mostly carbon.
   > How: put one coal or charcoal in the crafting grid. Eight tiny pieces craft back into one.
   > Tip: this pack's furnaces cook faster than vanilla, so one tiny coal covers more than one item.
45. **The Trowel**: `utilitarian:trowel` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts, Iron)*
   > What: the Trowel places a random block from your hotbar each time you use it. Great for natural-looking walls and paths.
   > How: two iron ingots and a stick (check JEI). Sneak-use it to switch between hotbar only and your whole inventory.
   > Tip: fill the hotbar with stone, cobblestone, andesite and tuff, and a plain wall looks weathered in seconds.
46. **Angel Block**: 4x `utilitarian:angel_block` *(after: Utilitarian Shortcuts, Iron)*
   > What: the Angel Block can be placed in empty air, with nothing next to it. It's the start of any sky bridge or floating build.
   > How: two feathers, two gold ingots and obsidian (check JEI). Use it while looking at empty air.
   > Tip: it's a building block, not flight. Flying in this pack is a chemistry milestone (see the Nether chapter).
47. **Snad**: 4x `utilitarian:snad` *(after: Tiny Coal)*
   > What: cactus, sugar cane, kelp and bamboo grow taller and faster on Snad. Soul Snad does the same for nether wart.
   > Chemistry: sand is mostly quartz grains, SiO₂, the same compound as the Nether quartz and certus you'll meet later.
   > How: two sand make one Snad (red sand makes Red Snad, soul sand makes Soul Snad).
   > Tip: a column of sugar cane on Snad is the fastest paper source for Sophisticated upgrades and Iron Furnace augments.
48. **Block Magnet**: `utilitarian:magnet` *(after: The Trowel)*
   > What: with a redstone signal, the Block Magnet pulls iron blocks, steel blocks and anvils below it up towards it.
   > Chemistry: iron is ferromagnetic: its atoms' tiny magnetic moments line up in domains. The recipe is an electromagnet, an iron core with copper on each side.
   > How: copper ingot, iron block, copper ingot in a row. Place it, put an iron block somewhere below, and power the magnet.
   > Tip: a magnet and a lever make a simple lift for iron blocks: power it to pull them up, cut the power to let them fall.
49. **Fluid Hopper**: `utilitarian:fluid_hopper` *(after: The Trowel, Water)*
   > What: the Fluid Hopper moves fluids the way a hopper moves items: it collects fluid from above and passes it on, the way a hopper does with items (check its JEI page).
   > How: iron ingots around a bucket, with white dye on top (check JEI).
   > Tip: under an infinite water source it fills a tank for your first steam boiler without any pump.
50. **Well Behaved Dropper**: `utilitarian:well_behaved_dropper` *(after: The Trowel)*
   > What: a dropper that drops items neatly in front of itself instead of flinging them in random directions.
   > How: a dropper with a gold nugget on each side (check JEI).
   > Tip: drop items onto a pressure plate or into water streams and they land exactly where you planned.
51. **Redstone Clock**: `utilitarian:redstone_clock` *(after: Snad)*
   > What: the Redstone Clock pulses a redstone signal on its own, with no repeater loop.
   > How: chiseled stone bricks with redstone on four sides (check JEI). Right-click it with an empty hand to change the speed; sneak to change it faster.
   > Tip: a slow clock on a dispenser or a Well Behaved Dropper makes a simple timed feeder.
52. **TPS Meter**: `utilitarian:tps_meter` *(after: Redstone Clock)*
   > What: the TPS Meter gives a redstone signal based on the dimension's ticks per second. A healthy server runs at 20.
   > How: four comparators around obsidian (check JEI).
   > Tip: wire it to a lamp in your factory: if it dims, something you built is lagging the server.
53. **Sound Muffler**: `utilitarian:sound_muffler` *(after: Redstone Clock)*
   > What: the Sound Muffler mutes sounds in a radius around it. Your crushers, pumps and boilers go quiet.
   > Chemistry: real soundproofing works the same way: soft, porous fibres like wool turn sound energy into a tiny amount of heat.
   > How: any wool plus a note block, shapeless.
   > Tip: one in the middle of a machine row is usually enough. Its tooltip shows the radius.
54. **Trader Carpet**: 1x any of `or(item(utilitarian:white_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:orange_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:magenta_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:light_blue_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:yellow_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:lime_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:pink_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:gray_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:light_gray_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:cyan_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:purple_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:blue_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:brown_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:green_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:red_soliciting_carpet)item(utilitarian:black_soliciting_carpet))` *(after: Redstone Clock)*
   > What: a wandering trader arriving nearby appears on a Trader Carpet instead of right in your face.
   > How: any carpet plus a small flower, shapeless. Each colour has its own carpet.
   > Tip: put it in a little market stall by your base. JEI also shows a trapped version, if you're feeling unkind.
55. **No Soliciting**: `utilitarian:no_soliciting_banner` *(after: Trader Carpet)*
   > What: the No Soliciting Banner stops wandering traders from spawning in the chunks around it.
   > How: wool, a lead and a stick, in a banner shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: use either the carpet or the banner: carpet if you like the trader's goods, banner if you don't.
56. **Outpost Claim**: `utilitarian:no_raider_block` *(after: No Soliciting)*
   > What: place the Raider Outpost Claim Block inside a pillager outpost and raiders stop coming back to it.
   > How: the recipe uses an ominous (illager) banner, which a pillager captain drops (check JEI).
   > Tip: claim the outpost before building there; it makes a fine tower base.
57. **Un-Name Tag**: `utilitarian:unname_tag` *(after: No Soliciting)*
   > What: the Un-Name Tag removes a mob's custom name.
   > How: a name tag plus white dye, shapeless. Use it on the named mob.
   > Tip: useful when a pet name typo has been bothering you for weeks.
58. **Slime in a Bucket**: `utilitarian:slime_bucket` *(after: Un-Name Tag)*
   > You remember finding hidden things by feel. The slime remembers too.
   > What: you scooped a small slime into a bucket. It gets visibly excited when you carry it into a slime chunk.
   > How: use an empty bucket on a small slime. Place it again by using the bucket on the ground.
   > Tip: slime chunks spawn slimes underground at any light level, which makes them the best spot for a slime farm.
59. **The Enchanting Table**: `minecraft:enchanting_table`; 15x `minecraft:bookshelf`; 3x `minecraft:book` *(after: Comfort First, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: the enchanting table, with the 15 bookshelves it needs for level 30 enchantments. Apotheosis makes it much deeper (Magic group).
   > Chemistry: paper is pressed cellulose fibre; old books yellow because acids left in the paper slowly break those chains (and lignin oxidises).
   > How: table: a book, 2 diamonds and 4 obsidian. Bookshelf: 6 planks and 3 books. Book: 3 paper and a leather.
   > Tip: leave one block of air between the table and the shelves, or they don't count.
60. **Anvil**: `minecraft:anvil` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: the anvil joins enchanted books to tools, repairs gear with its own material, and renames items.
   > Chemistry: a real anvil is a block of hardened steel on a softer body: the hard face doesn't dent, the soft body doesn't crack.
   > How: 3 iron blocks and 4 iron ingots: 31 iron in all.
   > Tip: every repair raises the 'too expensive' cost. Combine books first, then put them on the tool in one go.
61. **Map, Compass and Clock**: `minecraft:map`; `minecraft:compass`; `minecraft:clock` *(after: Comfort First, Iron)*
   > What: a map draws the land as you walk; a compass points to world spawn (or a lodestone); a clock shows the time of day, even underground.
   > Chemistry: a real compass needle is magnetised iron. The first ones (China, about 1,000 years ago) used lodestone, naturally magnetic magnetite, Fe₃O₄.
   > How: map: paper around a compass. Compass: 4 iron around redstone. Clock: 4 gold around redstone.
   > Tip: JourneyMap does the mapping for you; a framed map on the wall is still a nice trophy.
62. **Redstone Basics**: `minecraft:lever`; 4x `minecraft:redstone_torch`; 2x `minecraft:repeater` *(after: Comfort First, Iron Pickaxe)*
   > What: the three parts of most redstone builds: a lever (a switch), a redstone torch (a NOT gate) and a repeater (a delay and a booster).
   > Chemistry: redstone is fiction, but the logic is real: a torch is an inverter, exactly like a transistor wired as a NOT gate in every chip you own.
   > How: lever: a stick on cobblestone. Torch: redstone on a stick. Repeater: 2 torches and redstone on stone.
   > Tip: MI and Mekanism machines can be switched off with redstone; a lever by your machines saves power at night.
63. **Daylight Detector**: `minecraft:daylight_detector` *(after: Redstone Basics, Nether Quartz)*
   > What: it outputs a signal that follows the sun. Right-click it to invert, so it fires at night instead.
   > Chemistry: a real light sensor is a photodiode: light knocks electrons loose in a semiconductor and a current flows. Same physics as a solar panel, just smaller.
   > How: glass, Nether quartz and wooden slabs (check JEI).
   > Tip: inverted, it switches on street lamps at dusk.
64. **Conduit Power**: `minecraft:conduit` *(after: Comfort First, Buried Treasure)*
   > What: an activated conduit gives Conduit Power to players in the water nearby: no drowning, night vision underwater and faster mining. A bigger frame also attacks hostile mobs.
   > Chemistry: nautilus shells are aragonite, a form of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) with a different crystal packing from calcite. The pearly sheen is layers of it thinner than a wavelength of light.
   > How: a heart of the sea (buried treasure) in 8 nautilus shells (drowned and fishing). Place it in water inside a frame of prismarine (check the wiki shape in JEI's info tab).
   > Tip: perfect for an underwater base, or for clearing an ocean monument.
65. **Harvester Pylon**: checkmark *(after: Wings of a God, Animal Husbandry)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Harvester Pylon" on the Pylons page. Click to dismiss.
66. **Interdiction Pylon**: checkmark *(after: Wings of a God, Ancient Debris)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Interdiction Pylon" on the Pylons page. Click to dismiss.
67. **Guard Pylons**: checkmark *(after: Wings of a God, Form a Team)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Protection Pylon" on the Pylons page. Click to dismiss.

## Storage

### Storage and Logistics

*A god needs somewhere to keep things.*

1. **Somewhere for Everything**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:chests)` *(after: Somewhere to Put Things)*
   > You remember vaults that held the stars. Today it's a box of planks, and that's fine.
   > What: this page is every way the pack stores things: vanilla containers, Functional Storage drawers, Sophisticated chests and backpacks, and a few extras of our own.
   > How: any chest counts: vanilla, Sophisticated, archwood, whatever you have.
   > Tip: the god's archive (AE2) has its own page. Build a drawer wall first; it'll feed the archive later.
2. **Note: Items With Data**: checkmark *(after: Somewhere for Everything)*
   > What: some items carry data: enchanted books, damaged tools, filled backpacks, named things. Digital storage (AE2) spends a whole item type on each variant, so a thousand odd books eat a cell's 63 types fast.
   > How: keep data-heavy items in plain chests, drawers or a Sophisticated chest. Put only bulk, identical items (ores, dusts, ingots) in cells.
   > Tip: a storage bus on a chest full of books gives AE2 a window into it without wasting cell types.
3. **Note: Sort As You Go**: checkmark *(after: Somewhere for Everything)*
   > What: a chest named 'stuff' is where ingredients go to be forgotten. Pick a home for each kind of thing early: one wall for ores and metals, one for chemicals, one for building blocks.
   > How: drawers for bulk items, chests for odds and ends, a backpack with a void filter for junk.
   > Tip: every mod on this page can feed a controller, and a controller is what AE2 will read later.
4. **Vanilla Storage**: 1x any of `or(item(minecraft:chest)item(ars_nouveau:archwood_chest))` *(after: Somewhere for Everything)*
   > What: chests, barrels, trapped chests, ender chests, chest boats and minecarts. Simple, cheap, and still useful late game.
   > How: a chest from 8 planks, or an archwood chest from Ars Nouveau's archwood.
   > Tip: two chests side by side make a double chest; a barrel opens even with a block on top.
5. **Trapped Chest**: `minecraft:trapped_chest` *(after: Vanilla Storage)*
   > What: a trapped chest gives a redstone signal while someone has it open.
   > How: a chest and a tripwire hook (check JEI).
   > Tip: a trapped chest next to a door makes a cheap 'is anyone in my lab?' alarm.
6. **Barrel**: `minecraft:barrel` *(after: Vanilla Storage)*
   > What: a barrel holds as much as a chest and opens with any block on top, so you can stack them in a wall.
   > How: planks and slabs (check JEI).
   > Tip: a wall of barrels with item frames is a fine early sorting room.
7. **Ender Chest**: `minecraft:ender_chest` *(after: Vanilla Storage, A Door of Fire)*
   > What: every Ender Chest you open shows the same 27 slots, and only you can see yours.
   > How: 8 obsidian around an eye of ender.
   > Tip: keep spare tools and a water bucket in it; any Ender Chest becomes an emergency kit.
8. **Chest Minecart**: `minecraft:chest_minecart` *(after: Vanilla Storage)*
   > What: a chest on wheels: a minecart that carries 27 stacks along rails. A hopper under the track at home empties it as it rolls by.
   > Chemistry: steel wheels on steel rails have very low rolling resistance, which is why one locomotive can pull thousands of tonnes.
   > How: a minecart (5 iron) plus a chest (check JEI). Powered rails keep it moving.
   > Tip: a hopper minecart (also in JEI) loads itself from containers it passes under.
9. **Chest Boat**: 1x any of `item_tag(minecraft:chest_boats)` *(after: Vanilla Storage)*
   > What: a boat with a chest in it. Any wood works.
   > How: a boat plus a chest, shapeless (check JEI).
   > Tip: rivers run a long way in this pack's biomes; a chest boat is the cheapest long-distance freight before rails.
10. **Hoppers**: 2x `minecraft:hopper` *(after: Vanilla Storage, Iron)*
   > What: a hopper pulls items from the container above it and pushes them into the one it points at.
   > How: 5 iron ingots around a chest (Utilitarian also has a log recipe; check JEI).
   > Tip: a redstone signal locks a hopper, which makes simple item gates.
11. **Functional Storage**: `minecraft:chest` *(after: Somewhere for Everything)*
   > You remember shelves that went on forever. Drawers are the closest thing to them.
   > What: Functional Storage drawers hold a lot of a single item and show it on the front. They're the backbone of a bulk store: cobblestone, dusts, ingots, salts.
   > How: every drawer starts with a chest in the middle of its recipe, so bring one. The first drawer is the next quest.
   > Tip: a drawer wall behind a Storage Controller is one inventory for pipes, and later for AE2.
12. **Your First Drawer**: 1x any of `item_tag(functionalstorage:drawer)` *(after: Functional Storage)*
   > What: a drawer of any wood with 1, 2 or 4 slots. Right-click to insert, left-click to take one, sneak-left-click for a stack.
   > How: planks and a chest in the drawer shape (check JEI).
   > Tip: double-right-click with an item to pour in every matching stack from your inventory.
13. **Linking Tool**: `functionalstorage:linking_tool` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: the Linking Tool adds drawers that aren't touching a Storage Controller to its network, and pairs Ender Drawers.
   > How: check JEI. Right-click the controller to start, then right-click each drawer. Holding the tool shows what's linked.
   > Tip: link a drawer at your mine entrance so ore pours straight into the wall at home.
14. **Drawer Controller**: 1x any of `or(item(functionalstorage:storage_controller)item(functionalstorage:framed_storage_controller))` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: the Storage Controller links nearby drawers into one inventory you (and pipes, hoppers and AE2 storage buses) can use.
   > How: place it among your drawers (check JEI). Drawers touching it or linked with the Linking Tool join the network.
   > Tip: one pipe into the controller is a sorting system: each item goes to the drawer that already holds it.
15. **Controller Extension**: `functionalstorage:controller_extension` *(after: Drawer Controller)*
   > What: an extension works like the controller itself: pipes and players reach the whole drawer network through it.
   > How: check JEI, then link it with the Linking Tool.
   > Tip: one by the smelters, one by the crafting bench.
16. **Simple Compacting Drawer**: `functionalstorage:simple_compacting_drawer` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: stores two forms of one item (ingot and block, say) as a single pool and hands out whichever you ask for.
   > How: check JEI. Insert the item you want it to track.
   > Tip: good for things with no nugget form, like coal and coal blocks.
17. **Compacting Drawer**: `functionalstorage:compacting_drawer` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: a compacting drawer stores nuggets, ingots and blocks of one metal as a single pool.
   > Chemistry: a block holds the same metal atoms as 9 ingots; only the packing changes, so nothing is lost either way.
   > How: craft it (check JEI), then insert the item you want to track.
   > Tip: perfect for copper and tin next to your bronze setup.
18. **Framed Drawers**: 1x any of `or(item(functionalstorage:framed_1)item(functionalstorage:framed_2)item(functionalstorage:framed_4)item(functionalstorage:compacting_framed_drawer)item(functionalstorage:framed_storage_controller)item(functionalstorage:framed_controller_extension)item(functionalstorage:framed_simple_compacting_drawer))` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: framed drawers and controllers take on the texture of blocks you give them, so a drawer wall can match your lab.
   > How: craft the framed version (check JEI), then sneak-right-click it with the blocks you want for its frame and face.
   > Tip: framed drawers work exactly like normal ones, upgrades included.
19. **Configuration Tool**: `functionalstorage:configuration_tool` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: the Configuration Tool locks drawers to their item, toggles the count and item display, and more.
   > How: check JEI. Sneak-use cycles its mode; the mode shows on the item.
   > Tip: lock every drawer in a sorting wall, so an empty drawer still only accepts its own item.
20. **Fluid Drawers**: 1x any of `or(item(functionalstorage:fluid_1)item(functionalstorage:fluid_2)item(functionalstorage:fluid_4))` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: fluid drawers store a fluid instead of items, and show it on the front.
   > Chemistry: handy for small stocks of acids: one drawer of H₂SO₄, one of HCl, one of HNO₃. A real lab keeps acids in separate, labelled containers too.
   > How: check JEI for the 1, 2 and 4 slot versions. Pipes and MI fluid pipes fill and drain them; storage upgrades work on them.
21. **Ender Drawer**: `functionalstorage:ender_drawer` *(after: Linking Tool)*
   > What: every Ender Drawer with the same frequency shares one inventory, wherever it is.
   > How: check JEI. Pair drawers with the Linking Tool.
   > Tip: put one at your mine and one at your smelters to send ore home.
22. **Collector Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:collector_upgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: a drawer with a Collector Upgrade pulls in matching items dropped nearby.
   > How: check JEI. Right-click the drawer to open its upgrade slots.
   > Tip: under a cobblestone generator or a mob farm's drop point it replaces a hopper line.
23. **Redstone Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:redstone_upgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: the Redstone Upgrade makes a drawer emit a signal based on how full it is (or full / empty, by mode).
   > How: check JEI. Put it in the drawer's utility slot and cycle its mode.
   > Tip: wire it to a machine so a cobblestone drawer that's full switches the generator off.
24. **Copper Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:copper_upgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: storage upgrades multiply how much a drawer holds. Copper is the first and cheapest.
   > Chemistry: copper (8.96 g/cm³) is soft and malleable, which is why it was the first metal people worked.
   > How: copper ingots and blocks, chests and a drawer (check JEI). Right-click the drawer to open its upgrade slots.
25. **Gold Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:gold_upgrade` *(after: Copper Upgrade)*
   > What: the gold upgrade multiplies a drawer's capacity more than copper.
   > Chemistry: gold is the most malleable metal there is: one gram beats into a square metre of leaf.
   > How: builds on the copper upgrade (check JEI).
26. **Diamond Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:diamond_upgrade` *(after: Gold Upgrade)*
   > What: the diamond upgrade is the big step: one drawer holds a serious stockpile.
   > How: builds on the gold upgrade (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Iron Downgrade does the reverse, limiting a drawer to a single stack per slot.
27. **Netherite Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:netherite_upgrade` *(after: Diamond Upgrade, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the top drawer upgrade. One drawer holds an absurd amount of a single item.
   > How: smithing table: netherite upgrade template + diamond upgrade + netherite ingot.
   > Tip: save it for cobblestone, raw ore or dust, the things you have tens of thousands of.
28. **Iron Downgrade**: `functionalstorage:iron_downgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: the Iron Downgrade limits a drawer to one stack per slot.
   > How: check JEI.
   > Tip: useful for a drawer that feeds a machine: it keeps a small buffer instead of swallowing your whole stock.
29. **Void Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:void_upgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: a drawer with a Void Upgrade destroys whatever doesn't fit, so a full drawer never backs up a pipe.
   > Chemistry: real matter can't vanish (mass is conserved in every chemical reaction). In Minecraft, it can.
   > How: check JEI.
   > Tip: a void-upgraded cobblestone drawer at the end of a quarry line keeps everything flowing.
30. **Pusher Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:pusher_upgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: the Pusher pushes the drawer's items into the block it faces. No pipes needed.
   > How: check JEI. Put it in the drawer's utility slot and set its direction in the drawer's menu.
   > Tip: a drawer of coal with a Pusher behind a row of furnaces keeps them fuelled.
31. **Puller Upgrade**: `functionalstorage:puller_upgrade` *(after: Your First Drawer)*
   > What: the Puller pulls items from the block it faces into the drawer.
   > How: check JEI. Utility slot, set the direction in the drawer's menu.
   > Tip: a drawer with a Puller behind a macerator collects all the dust without a single pipe.
32. **Sophisticated Storage**: 1x any of `item_tag(sophisticatedstorage:base_tier_wooden_storage)` *(after: Somewhere for Everything)*
   > You remember vaults that answered to a word. These answer to upgrade cards, which is nearly as good.
   > What: Sophisticated Storage chests, barrels, limited barrels and shulker boxes take upgrade cards (stack, compacting, hopper, filters) and tier upgrades, just like your backpack.
   > How: craft any wooden chest or barrel of the mod (check JEI).
   > Tip: barrels keep their contents when broken, so moving a full one is easy.
33. **Copper Tier**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedstorage:copper_chest)item(sophisticatedstorage:copper_barrel))` *(after: Sophisticated Storage)*
   > What: the copper tier sits between wood and iron: a few more slots for a little copper.
   > Chemistry: copper tarnishes green: over years it forms a patina of basic copper carbonate, Cu₂CO₃(OH)₂, which then protects the metal underneath.
   > How: a copper chest or barrel from JEI, or a basic-to-copper tier upgrade right-clicked on a placed wooden one.
34. **Iron Tier**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedstorage:iron_chest)item(sophisticatedstorage:iron_barrel))` *(after: Sophisticated Storage)*
   > What: the iron tier: more slots and more upgrade slots.
   > How: craft an iron chest or barrel, or use a tier upgrade (basic → iron skips copper) on the placed container: nothing inside moves.
   > Tip: the Decoration Table re-skins chests and barrels with any wood or block, so your storage room can match your base.
35. **Gold Tier**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedstorage:gold_chest)item(sophisticatedstorage:gold_barrel))` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: the gold tier, with more slots and upgrade slots again.
   > How: check JEI, or an iron-to-gold tier upgrade on the placed chest or barrel.
   > Tip: upgrade the barrel your ore line feeds first; it fills fastest.
36. **Diamond Tier**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedstorage:diamond_chest)item(sophisticatedstorage:diamond_barrel))` *(after: Gold Tier)*
   > What: the diamond tier. Enough upgrade slots for stack upgrades, a hopper and a filter at once.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon, the same element as the coal in your furnace, arranged in a lattice where every atom bonds to four others.
   > How: check JEI, or a gold-to-diamond tier upgrade on the placed container.
37. **Netherite Tier**: 1x any of `or(item(sophisticatedstorage:netherite_barrel)item(sophisticatedstorage:netherite_chest))` *(after: Diamond Tier, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the netherite tier has the most slots and upgrade slots of any Sophisticated container.
   > How: check JEI, or a diamond-to-netherite tier upgrade on a placed diamond chest or barrel.
   > Tip: a netherite barrel full of stack upgrades holds a staggering amount.
38. **Upgrade Base**: `sophisticatedstorage:upgrade_base` *(after: Sophisticated Storage)*
   > What: every Sophisticated Storage upgrade card starts from an upgrade base.
   > How: planks and iron ingots in a checker pattern. The backpack mod has its own base; JEI shows both.
   > Tip: make a few at a time; you'll want stack, hopper and compacting upgrades soon.
39. **Storage Controller**: `sophisticatedstorage:controller` *(after: Sophisticated Storage)*
   > What: the Controller joins touching Sophisticated containers into one inventory. Right-click it with an item and it goes to the container that already holds that item.
   > How: place it next to your chests and barrels (check JEI). Pipes into the controller reach every connected container.
   > Tip: one pipe into the controller is a sorting system; a storage bus on it later gives AE2 the whole room.
40. **Storage Tool**: `sophisticatedstorage:storage_tool` *(after: Storage Controller)*
   > What: the Storage Tool links containers to a controller without touching it and toggles settings like locks and displays.
   > How: an ender pearl, iron, sticks and a redstone torch (check JEI). Its tooltip lists each mode.
   > Tip: locked slots keep their item type even when empty, so a sorting system never fills them with junk.
41. **Storage Link**: `sophisticatedstorage:storage_link` *(after: Storage Tool)*
   > What: a Storage Link joins containers that aren't touching the controller's group, within the controller's range.
   > How: check JEI. Place it against the far container (or group) and link it with the Storage Tool.
   > Tip: a link under the floor joins a second storage room without a wall of cables.
42. **Sophisticated Chest**: `sophisticatedstorage:chest` *(after: Sophisticated Storage)*
   > What: Sophisticated chests take the same tier upgrades and upgrade cards as the barrels, and show their contents in a double-chest layout.
   > How: a wooden chest version (check JEI).
   > Tip: chests connect to the controller the same way barrels do.
43. **Limited Barrels**: `sophisticatedstorage:limited_barrel_1`; `sophisticatedstorage:limited_barrel_4` *(after: Sophisticated Storage)*
   > What: limited barrels have one to four big slots and show their items on the front, like drawers, but take Sophisticated upgrades.
   > How: check JEI for each size. They use the same tier upgrades as normal barrels.
   > Tip: a four-slot limited barrel per metal (ore, dust, ingot, block) makes a tidy wall.
44. **Sophisticated Shulker Box**: `sophisticatedstorage:shulker_box` *(after: Sophisticated Chest, The End)*
   > What: a shulker box that takes tier upgrades and upgrade cards, and keeps everything inside when you pick it up.
   > How: a chest, two shulker shells and a lever (check JEI). Shulkers live in End cities.
   > Tip: a shulker box with a compacting upgrade is a portable ore bank for long mining trips.
45. **Tier Upgrade Kits**: `sophisticatedstorage:diamond_to_netherite_tier_upgrade` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > What: tier upgrades turn a placed chest or barrel into the next tier without moving a thing. This one is the last step, diamond to netherite.
   > How: a lever and a netherite ingot, shapeless (check JEI for the other steps).
   > Tip: every item and upgrade card inside stays where it was.
46. **Stack Upgrades**: `sophisticatedstorage:stack_upgrade_tier_1` *(after: Upgrade Base)*
   > What: stack upgrades multiply how many items fit in each slot of a chest or barrel. Higher tiers multiply more.
   > How: an upgrade base and storage blocks (check JEI). Insert it in an upgrade slot.
   > Tip: a barrel with a few stack upgrades holds a whole mine's worth of cobblestone or raw ore.
47. **Compacting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedstorage:compacting_upgrade` *(after: Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Compacting Upgrade squeezes 9 nuggets into an ingot and 9 ingots into a block as items arrive.
   > Chemistry: a block holds the same metal atoms as 9 ingots; only the packing changes, so no mass is lost either way.
   > How: craft it (check JEI) and put it in an upgrade slot. Add a filter so it only compacts what you choose.
48. **Compression Upgrade**: `sophisticatedstorage:compression_upgrade` *(after: Compacting Upgrade)*
   > What: the Compression Upgrade links a few slots so nuggets, ingots and blocks of one material count as a single stock.
   > How: an upgrade base, pistons, iron and redstone (check JEI). Choose which slots it uses in the upgrade tab.
   > Tip: take out exactly the form you need: blocks for storage, ingots for crafting, nuggets for small recipes.
49. **Hopper Upgrade**: `sophisticatedstorage:hopper_upgrade` *(after: Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Hopper Upgrade pulls items from one side and pushes them out another, with filters.
   > How: an upgrade base, a hopper, iron and redstone (check JEI). Set directions and filters in the container's upgrade tab.
   > Tip: a barrel with a hopper upgrade under a machine's output collects everything without pipes.
50. **Storage Input and Output**: `sophisticatedstorage:storage_input`; `sophisticatedstorage:storage_output` *(after: Storage Controller)*
   > What: Storage Input only accepts items into the controller's containers; Storage Output only lets them out. Pipes and hoppers use them like any inventory.
   > How: a wooden storage block, gold, planks and a repeater (check JEI). Place them touching the controller's group.
   > Tip: put an Input at the end of your ore line and an Output by your crafting area, so the two never mix.
51. **Storage in Motion**: `sophisticatedstorageinmotion:storage_minecart` *(after: Iron Tier)*
   > What: Sophisticated Storage in Motion puts upgradeable chests and barrels on minecarts, boats and rafts, upgrades and all.
   > How: combine a minecart with a Sophisticated chest or barrel (check JEI). Boats and rafts work the same way.
   > Tip: a hopper upgrade on a storage minecart makes a simple ore train between your mine and base.
52. **An Early Network**: `toms_storage:storage_terminal`; `toms_storage:inventory_connector` *(after: Drawer Controller)*
   > What: Tom's Simple Storage connects your chests into one searchable terminal. It's your network until AE2.
   > How: place an Inventory Connector touching your chests (or link them with Inventory Cables), and a Storage Terminal on it.
   > Tip: point it at a drawer controller and every drawer shows up in the terminal.
53. **Crafting Terminal**: `toms_storage:crafting_terminal` *(after: An Early Network)*
   > What: a terminal with a crafting grid that pulls ingredients from the network. JEI's + button fills it for you.
   > How: upgrade a Storage Terminal (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Wireless Terminal (also in JEI) lets you use it from across the base.
54. **Inventory Cables**: 16x `toms_storage:inventory_cable`; `toms_storage:inventory_cable_connector` *(after: An Early Network)*
   > What: inventory cables carry the Inventory Connector's reach to chests that aren't touching it.
   > How: run cables from the connector and put a Cable Connector on each chest or drawer (check JEI).
   > Tip: framed cables can wear any block's texture, so they hide in walls.
55. **Wireless Terminal**: `toms_storage:adv_wireless_terminal` *(after: Crafting Terminal)*
   > What: the Advanced Wireless Terminal opens your Tom's network from a long way off.
   > How: check JEI, then right-click it on a Storage Terminal to bind it.
   > Tip: it's the cheapest remote storage access until AE2.
56. **Pipez**: checkmark *(after: Hoppers)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Item Pipes" on the Automation and Logic page. Click to dismiss.
57. **LaserIO**: checkmark *(after: Pipez, LV Machine Hull)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Laser Nodes" on the Automation and Logic page. Click to dismiss.
58. **Entangled**: checkmark *(after: Ender Chest)*
   > What: an Entangled Block is a window into another inventory: bind it to a chest or machine, and anything put in the Entangled Block goes into the bound block, even across dimensions.
   > How: ender pearls, obsidian and a wooden chest (check JEI). Right-click the target with the Entangled Binder (pearls, obsidian and a diamond), then right-click the Entangled Block. Click the checkmark when one is working.
   > Tip: put one next to a remote ore processor and pipe the output straight home. Both chunks must be loaded.

### Storage: Sophisticated Backpacks

*Storage and Logistics, continued: Sophisticated Backpacks*

1. **A Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:backpack` *(after: Leather Armour, Somewhere to Put Things, Somewhere for Everything)*
   > You remember carrying whole worlds. For now, a leather bag will do.
   > What: more inventory, and it can be upgraded later (pickup, magnet, feeding and more).
   > How: leather, string and a chest (check JEI for the shape). Wear it in the chest slot or keep it in your inventory.
   > Tip: take it on your first mining trip. The upgrade base is also sold in the Demigod Token shop.
2. **Copper Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:copper_backpack` *(after: A Backpack)*
   > What: the copper backpack sits between leather and iron: a few more slots and an extra upgrade slot.
   > How: surround your backpack with copper ingots (check JEI). Everything inside stays put.
   > Tip: copper is plentiful early, so this is the cheapest upgrade in the line.
3. **Gold Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:gold_backpack` *(after: Iron Backpack)*
   > What: the gold backpack adds inventory rows and upgrade slots over the iron one.
   > How: surround an iron backpack with eight gold ingots. Everything inside stays put.
   > Tip: spend the new upgrade slot on a stack upgrade; it multiplies every slot at once.
4. **Diamond Backpack**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:diamond_backpack` *(after: Gold Backpack)*
   > What: the diamond backpack is the tier before netherite: even more rows and upgrade slots.
   > How: surround a gold backpack with eight diamonds.
   > Tip: netherite comes after it (the Netherite Backpack quest, on the Quality of Life page).
5. **Backpack Upgrade Base**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:upgrade_base` *(after: A Backpack)*
   > What: every backpack upgrade starts from this base. The upgrades below each add one thing the pack does by itself.
   > How: leather, string and iron (check JEI). It's also in the Demigod Token shop.
   > Tip: upgrades go in the slots on the left of the backpack screen; sneak-right-click the slot to open an upgrade's settings.
6. **Tank Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:tank_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Tank Upgrade stores fluid inside the backpack. Fill and empty it with buckets or tanks from its upgrade tab.
   > Chemistry: a real acid needs the right container: HF eats glass, so it's kept in PTFE; concentrated H₂SO₄ can sit in steel. A backpack tank isn't fussy.
   > How: an upgrade base surrounded by glass (check JEI).
   > Tip: a tank of water means you're never stuck in a lava cave without a way to cool it into obsidian.
7. **Advanced Pickup**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_pickup_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrades)*
   > What: the advanced pickup upgrade has more filter slots and can filter by tag, mod or durability.
   > How: the basic pickup upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: a tag filter for 'c:raw_materials' picks up every raw ore in the pack with one entry.
8. **Advanced Magnet**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_magnet_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrades)*
   > What: the advanced magnet pulls drops from further away, with the advanced filter slots.
   > Chemistry: a real magnet only pulls iron, nickel, cobalt and a few alloys. This one is less picky.
   > How: the basic magnet upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
9. **Smelting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:smelting_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Smelting Upgrade is a furnace in the backpack screen, burning fuel from the backpack.
   > Chemistry: smelting iron ore is a reduction: carbon monoxide strips the oxygen off the ore, Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
   > How: an upgrade base and a furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: smelt your raw ore on the walk home.
10. **Auto-Smelting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:auto_smelting_upgrade` *(after: Smelting Upgrade)*
   > What: the Auto-Smelting Upgrade smelts matching items inside the backpack on its own, using fuel from the backpack.
   > How: the smelting upgrade with a hopper, gold, redstone and a diamond (check JEI).
   > Tip: filter it to raw ores only, or it will smelt your logs into charcoal too.
11. **Pump Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:pump_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Pump Upgrade fills and empties the backpack's tank from blocks in the world or from tanks you click on.
   > How: an upgrade base with buckets, glass, a piston and a sticky piston (check JEI). It needs a Tank Upgrade to work with.
   > Tip: set it to 'fill' on a water source and the tank is never empty.
12. **Advanced Pump**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_pump_upgrade` *(after: Pump Upgrade)*
   > What: the advanced pump moves fluid faster and filters which fluids it touches.
   > How: the pump upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
13. **Experience Pump**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:xp_pump_upgrade` *(after: Advanced Pump)*
   > What: the XP Pump stores your experience as fluid in the backpack's tank and gives it back on demand.
   > How: an advanced pump upgrade with ender eyes, bottles o' enchanting and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: bank your levels before a risky fight; a grave keeps items, not levels.
14. **Battery Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:battery_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base, Forge Energy)*
   > What: stores Forge Energy in the backpack, which other upgrades and charging tools can use.
   > Chemistry: a battery stores energy as chemistry: two electrodes with different appetites for electrons, kept apart by an electrolyte.
   > How: an upgrade base with gold ingots and redstone blocks (check JEI).
   > Tip: charge it at home, then top up your jetpack or Mining Gadget in the field.
15. **Deposit Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:deposit_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: with a Deposit Upgrade, sneak-right-clicking a container with the backpack puts matching items into it.
   > How: an upgrade base, a chest, iron, redstone and a piston (check JEI).
   > Tip: deposit ores into your processing chest in one click when you get home.
16. **Advanced Deposit**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_deposit_upgrade` *(after: Deposit Upgrade)*
   > What: the advanced version with more filter slots and tag filters.
   > How: the deposit upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
17. **Blasting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:blasting_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Blasting Upgrade smelts ores and metal at double speed, like a blast furnace, from the backpack screen.
   > Chemistry: a blast furnace forces air through the fuel so it burns hotter: C + O₂ → CO₂, then CO₂ + C → 2CO, and the CO reduces the ore.
   > How: an upgrade base with a blast furnace, iron and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: one furnace-type upgrade is enough: they share the backpack's fuel.
18. **Auto-Blasting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:auto_blasting_upgrade` *(after: Blasting Upgrade)*
   > What: the automatic version: it blasts matching items inside the backpack by itself.
   > How: the blasting upgrade with a hopper, gold, redstone and a diamond (check JEI).
19. **Stonecutter Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stonecutter_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Stonecutter Upgrade adds a stonecutter to the backpack screen.
   > How: an upgrade base with a stonecutter, iron and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: perfect for Create Deco, Rechiseled and laboratory blocks on a building trip.
20. **Filter Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:filter_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Filter Upgrade decides what pipes and hoppers may put into or take out of the backpack.
   > How: an upgrade base with string and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: a backpack in a hopper line with a filter is a cheap sorter.
21. **Advanced Filter**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_filter_upgrade` *(after: Filter Upgrade)*
   > What: more filter slots, plus filters by tag, mod or durability.
   > How: the filter upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
22. **Smoking Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:smoking_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Smoking Upgrade is a smoker in the backpack screen: food only, at double speed.
   > Chemistry: smoking preserves meat: phenols and other compounds in wood smoke kill microbes and slow the fats going rancid.
   > How: an upgrade base with a smoker, iron and redstone (check JEI).
23. **Auto-Smoking Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:auto_smoking_upgrade` *(after: Smoking Upgrade)*
   > What: the automatic version: raw food in the backpack is smoked by itself.
   > How: the smoking upgrade with a hopper, gold, redstone and a diamond (check JEI).
24. **Mixtape**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:jukebox_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > You remember a time when the spheres sang to you. A jukebox in a backpack will have to do.
   > What: the Jukebox Upgrade plays music discs from inside your backpack, wherever you walk.
   > Tip: it plays to everyone nearby. Choose your disc with care.
25. **Advanced Tool Swapper**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_tool_swapper_upgrade` *(after: Tool Swapper)*
   > What: the advanced tool swapper also swaps to the right weapon for the mob in front of you, with more filter slots.
   > How: the tool swapper upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
26. **Stack Upgrade II**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_2` *(after: Stack Upgrade)*
   > What: each stack tier multiplies how many items fit in every backpack slot. Tier 2 multiplies more than tier 1.
   > How: the tier 1 upgrade with better materials (check JEI).
   > Tip: a backpack full of stacked dust is the cheapest way to move a day's mining to your machines.
27. **Stack Upgrade III**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_3` *(after: Stack Upgrade II)*
   > What: tier 3 of the stack upgrade.
   > How: the tier 2 upgrade with diamonds (check JEI).
28. **Stack Upgrade IV**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:stack_upgrade_tier_4` *(after: Stack Upgrade III, Ancient Debris)*
   > What: tier 4, the biggest stack multiplier a backpack takes.
   > How: the tier 3 upgrade with netherite (check JEI).
   > Tip: two of these in a netherite backpack and you can carry a quarry's output.
29. **Crafting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:crafting_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: adds a 3x3 crafting grid to the backpack screen that can use the backpack's own items.
   > How: an upgrade base, a crafting table, iron and a chest (check JEI).
   > Tip: JEI's + button fills the backpack grid straight from the backpack.
30. **Advanced Feeding**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_feeding_upgrade` *(after: Feeding Upgrade)*
   > What: the advanced feeding upgrade has more food slots and can be set to eat only when no hunger would be wasted.
   > How: the feeding upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
31. **Void Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:void_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Void Upgrade destroys chosen items as they enter the backpack: cobblestone, dirt, gravel, rotten flesh.
   > Chemistry: real matter can't vanish (mass is conserved in every chemical reaction). In Minecraft, it can.
   > How: an upgrade base, ender pearls, obsidian and redstone (check JEI). Set the filter carefully.
   > Tip: keep a stack of cobblestone out of the filter. You'll want it for building and for the Matter Condenser later.
32. **Advanced Void**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_void_upgrade` *(after: Void Upgrade)*
   > What: more filter slots, tag filters, and an 'overflow only' mode that keeps one stack and deletes the rest.
   > How: the void upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
33. **Inception**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:inception_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base, The Wither)*
   > What: with the Inception Upgrade, backpacks stored inside your backpack keep using their own upgrades, and you can open them from the outer one.
   > How: an upgrade base with ender eyes, diamonds and a Nether Star (check JEI).
   > Tip: a small 'mining' backpack inside your main one keeps its magnet and void settings separate.
34. **Compacting Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:compacting_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: the Compacting Upgrade squeezes 9 of something into its block as you pick it up.
   > How: an upgrade base with pistons, iron and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: compact redstone, lapis and coal while mining; whole blocks take a ninth of the space.
35. **Advanced Compacting**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_compacting_upgrade` *(after: Compacting Upgrade)*
   > What: the advanced version compacts more item types at once and can uncraft blocks back into pieces.
   > How: the compacting upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
36. **Restock Upgrade**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:restock_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base)*
   > What: a Restock Upgrade tops the backpack up from a container you sneak-right-click: torches, food, whatever it already holds.
   > How: an upgrade base, a chest, iron, redstone and a sticky piston (check JEI).
   > Tip: restock torches and food from your supply chest on the way out, every time.
37. **Advanced Restock**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_restock_upgrade` *(after: Restock Upgrade)*
   > What: the advanced version with more filter slots and tag filters.
   > How: the restock upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
38. **Everlasting**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:everlasting_upgrade` *(after: Backpack Upgrade Base, The Wither, The End)*
   > What: with the Everlasting Upgrade, a dropped backpack can't burn, explode or despawn.
   > How: an upgrade base, nether stars and end crystals (check JEI). That means beating the Wither and visiting the End.
   > Tip: worth it before reactor work or deep Nether trips, where a lost pack hurts most.
39. **Advanced Refill**: `sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_refill_upgrade` *(after: Refill Upgrade)*
   > What: the advanced refill upgrade keeps more hotbar items topped up from the backpack, with a target slot for each.
   > How: the refill upgrade with gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
40. **Fully Advanced**: 4x any of `or(item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_feeding_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_refill_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_restock_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_deposit_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_void_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_tool_swapper_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_compacting_upgrade)item(sophisticatedbackpacks:advanced_pump_upgrade))` *(after: Advanced Pickup)*
   > What: a collection: any four advanced upgrades (feeding, refill, restock, deposit, void, tool swapper, compacting, pump).
   > How: each is its basic upgrade plus gold, diamonds and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: a diamond backpack has the slots for all of them at once.
