### Applied Energistics

*The archive of a god: every item as data, every recipe on demand.*

1. **Before the Archive**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:chests)` *(after: HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > You remember a library with no shelves, where every book answered when you thought of it.
   > What: Applied Energistics 2 turns items into data. A network of cables, drives and terminals holds everything you own and can craft on demand.
   > How: show any chest to begin. Soon a single terminal will replace rooms of them.
   > Tip: AE2 opens in the HV tier here: the Inscriber needs an MI Turbo hull and the Controller a digital circuit.
2. **Note: Read the Guide**: checkmark *(after: Before the Archive)*
   > What: AE2's in-game guide explains every block, with pictures. Hold G over an AE2 item in JEI or your inventory to open its page.
   > Tip: the guide's 'Getting Started' pages cover channels better than any quest text could.
3. **Note: Channels and Power**: checkmark; checkmark *(after: Before the Archive)*
   > What: almost every AE2 problem is one of two things: the network has no power, or a device has no channel.
   > How: a device whose light is off has no channel; a dark terminal means no power. Tick one box for each once you've read it.
   > Tip: the Network Tool (later in this chapter) shows both at a glance.
4. **Quartz Wrench**: 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:quartz_wrench)` *(after: Before the Archive)*
   > What: the wrench rotates AE2 blocks and sneak-click picks them up, parts included.
   > How: certus or nether quartz with iron (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also removes a single cable part without breaking the cable.
5. **Charger and Inscriber**: `ae2:charger`; `ae2:inscriber` *(after: Before the Archive)*
   > What: the Charger puts energy into certus crystals; the Inscriber presses processors and grinds crystals into dust.
   > Chemistry: real quartz is piezoelectric: squeeze it and it makes a voltage, push a voltage into it and it flexes. AE2 imagines it can store the charge.
   > How: the Charger is iron and copper (check JEI). The Inscriber is gated here: it needs an MI Turbo hull.
   > Tip: a Crank on top of the Charger works too, slowly, if your power isn't up yet.
6. **Dowsing Rod**: `ars_nouveau:dowsing_rod` *(after: Charger and Inscriber)*
   > What: Ars Nouveau's Dowsing Rod highlights nearby blocks of interest. It's a second way into the meteor hunt.
   > How: check JEI (it needs source from Ars Nouveau).
   > Tip: the compass is faster for meteorites; the rod is handy for everything else.
7. **Meteorite Compass**: `ae2:meteorite_compass` *(after: Charger and Inscriber)*
   > What: the compass needle swings towards the nearest meteorite, where certus and the Inscriber presses wait.
   > How: charged certus and iron (check JEI).
   > Tip: each meteorite holds one press in its mysterious cube. You need four.
8. **Certus Quartz**: `ae2:certus_quartz_crystal`; `ae2:certus_quartz_dust` *(after: Meteorite Compass)*
   > You remember crystals that sang when you touched them. These still hum, faintly.
   > What: certus quartz goes into almost every AE2 recipe: processors, glass, cells and cards.
   > Chemistry: certus is fictional, but it behaves like real quartz (SiO₂), which is piezoelectric: squeeze it and it makes a small voltage.
   > How: mine certus from meteorite craters and budding certus. Grind crystals into dust in the Inscriber with no press.
   > Tip: charged certus plus certus dust dropped in water makes two new crystals. Grow it once you have a little.
9. **Fluix**: `ae2:fluix_dust`; `ae2:fluix_crystal` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: fluix crystals carry AE2's channels: every cable, core and most parts need fluix.
   > Chemistry: a reaction in solution: charged certus, nether quartz and redstone dropped together in water fuse into fluix. Real crystals also grow fastest from a seed in solution.
   > How: throw charged certus, nether quartz and redstone into a water block: you get two fluix crystals. Grind fluix in the Inscriber for dust.
   > Tip: four crystals make a fluix block, which is where ExtendedAE's entro grows (see its own page).
10. **The Three Processors**: `ae2:logic_processor`; `ae2:calculation_processor`; `ae2:engineering_processor` *(after: Meteorite Compass)*
   > What: AE2's three processors: logic (gold), calculation (certus) and engineering (diamond). You'll want hundreds of each.
   > Chemistry: gold barely reacts with air or water, so it never corrodes; real chips use it for contacts. Diamond spreads heat better than any metal.
   > How: press the material with its press, press MI silicon with the Silicon Press, then inscribe the print, redstone and printed silicon together.
   > Tip: one Inscriber per processor type, each fed by pipes, keeps all three in stock.
11. **Cables**: 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:glass_cable)`; 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:covered_cable)`; 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:covered_dense_cable)` *(after: Fluix)*
   > What: each ME device uses one channel. Glass and covered cables carry 8 channels, dense cables 32. Any colour counts.
   > How: fluix crystals and quartz make glass cable; wool covers it; four covered cables and redstone make a dense one (check JEI).
   > Tip: build a dense-cable backbone from the controller and branch normal cables off it.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: if a device's light is off, it has no channel. Count devices on each normal cable (max 8). Drives, terminals, buses and interfaces all count. Plain cables, quartz fibre and energy cells don't.
12. **Smart Cables**: 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:smart_cable)`; 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:smart_dense_cable)` *(after: Cables)*
   > What: smart cables light up one stripe per channel in use, so you can see where a branch runs out.
   > How: a covered cable plus redstone and glowstone (check JEI); the dense version from dense cable.
   > Tip: use smart cable on the busy branches and plain cable everywhere else.
13. **Note: Count Your Channels**: checkmark *(after: Cables)*
   > What: a controller sends 32 channels out of each face. A normal cable carries 8 of them, a dense cable all 32.
   > How: plan one dense line per face, then branch. Click to continue.
   > Tip: a subnetwork behind an interface spends only one channel on the main network.
14. **Knife, Anchor and Name Press**: 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:knife)`; `ae2:cable_anchor`; `ae2:name_press` *(after: Cables)*
   > What: the cutting knife makes Cable Anchors (they keep two neighbouring cables from joining) and the Inscriber Name Press, which labels items.
   > How: a knife from certus or nether quartz and iron; cut any metal ingot for 4 anchors, or iron for the press (check JEI).
   > Tip: rename the press in an anvil, then press anything with it to give it that name. Every chemist labels their bottles.
15. **Color Applicator**: `ae2:color_applicator` *(after: Cables)*
   > What: the Color Applicator paints cables. Cables of different colours don't connect, so two networks can run side by side.
   > Chemistry: dyes work by absorbing some wavelengths of light and reflecting the rest; the colour you see is what's left over.
   > How: an energy cell, a 4k component and processors (check JEI). Load dye into it and charge it.
16. **Sky Stone**: 16x `ae2:sky_stone_block`; 4x `ae2:smooth_sky_stone_block` *(after: Meteorite Compass)*
   > What: sky stone is the rock of AE2 meteorites. The ME Controller in this pack needs smooth sky stone.
   > Chemistry: real stony meteorites are mostly silicate minerals like olivine and pyroxene; iron meteorites are an iron-nickel alloy.
   > How: mine the crater shell (iron pickaxe or better), then smelt sky stone into smooth sky stone.
   > Tip: the Inscriber grinds sky stone into sky dust, which ExtendedAE and AdvancedAE recipes ask for.
17. **All Four Presses**: `ae2:logic_processor_press`; `ae2:calculation_processor_press` *(after: Meteorite Compass)*
   > What: the Inscriber has four presses: silicon, logic, calculation and engineering. You need all four for the processors.
   > How: each meteorite's mysterious cube holds one press. Keep finding meteorites until you have the set.
   > Tip: never use your only copy in a long automation line. Make a spare in the Inscriber with an iron block first (check JEI).
18. **Printed Silicon**: 8x `modern_industrialization:silicon_ingot`; 4x `ae2:printed_silicon` *(after: All Four Presses)*
   > What: printed silicon is the base layer of every AE2 processor.
   > Chemistry: industry makes silicon by heating quartz with carbon to about 2000 °C: SiO₂ + 2C → Si + 2CO. Chips need it purer than 99.9999999%.
   > How: press MI silicon ingots in the Inscriber with the Silicon Press. They come from the Electric Blast Furnace (quartz dust + coke dust).
   > Tip: in this pack certus and sand don't smelt into silicon: carbothermic reduction is the only way, as in the real world.
19. **Calculation Prints**: 4x `ae2:printed_calculation_processor`; 4x `ae2:calculation_processor` *(after: Printed Silicon)*
   > What: calculation processors go into crafting units, cards, bigger cell components and wireless parts.
   > Chemistry: a real quartz crystal vibrates at a precise frequency when a voltage drives it. Watches count 32,768 vibrations a second to keep time.
   > How: press a certus crystal with the Calculation Press, then combine it with redstone and printed silicon.
20. **Cell Housings**: 2x `ae2:item_cell_housing`; 2x `ae2:fluid_cell_housing` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: a storage cell is a housing plus a component. Item housings take iron; fluid housings take copper.
   > How: quartz glass, redstone and metal in a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: sneak-use an empty cell in the air to split it back into housing and component, for upgrading to a bigger one.
21. **Annihilation and Formation**: 2x `ae2:annihilation_core`; 2x `ae2:formation_core` *(after: The Three Processors)*
   > What: annihilation cores take things into the network; formation cores put things out. Interfaces, providers, planes and assemblers all need both.
   > How: nether quartz (annihilation) or certus (formation), plus fluix dust and a logic processor, two at a time.
   > Tip: make a stack of each. Autocrafting eats them fast.
22. **Budding Certus by Hand**: `ae2:damaged_budding_quartz`; `ae2:chipped_budding_quartz` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: a certus quartz block dropped in water with charged certus becomes Damaged Budding Certus; repeat to climb to Chipped and better.
   > How: throw a certus block and a charged crystal into water together (JEI's transform tab).
   > Tip: lower-grade budding blocks decay as they grow. Keep charged certus to remake them.
23. **Ender Dust**: 8x `ae2:ender_dust` *(after: Charger and Inscriber)*
   > What: ender pearls ground into dust in the Inscriber. Entangled singularities, entro seeds and wireless parts use it.
   > How: put an ender pearl in the Inscriber with no press.
   > Tip: an enderman model in a Simulation Chamber keeps the pearls coming.
24. **Fluix Sword**: checkmark *(after: Fluix)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Fluix Sword" on the Gear and Comfort page. Click to dismiss.
25. **Energy Acceptor**: `ae2:energy_acceptor` *(after: Certus Quartz)*
   > What: the ME network turns FE into its own AE energy. The Energy Acceptor does the converting.
   > How: connect it to any FE source (an energy cube, a Powah cell, a Flux Point) and to your cables (check JEI).
   > Tip: a controller face can't take power directly from FE; always go through an acceptor.
26. **Energy Cells**: `ae2:energy_cell`; `ae2:dense_energy_cell` *(after: Energy Acceptor)*
   > What: Energy Cells store AE; a Dense Energy Cell stores eight times more.
   > How: the dense cell is eight Energy Cells around a calculation processor (check JEI). Put them anywhere on the network.
   > Tip: when a network flickers during autocrafting, more buffer is usually the cure, not more power input.
27. **Energy Card**: `ae2:energy_card` *(after: Energy Cells)*
   > What: an Energy Card raises how much AE a portable terminal, cell or tool holds.
   > Chemistry: a battery's capacity depends on how much reactant it holds; adding cells in parallel adds capacity, as this card does.
   > How: an advanced card plus a dense energy cell (check JEI). Slot it into the item in a Cell Workbench.
28. **Terminals**: `ae2:terminal`; `ae2:crafting_terminal` *(after: The Three Processors)*
   > What: the ME Terminal shows and searches everything the network stores. The Crafting Terminal adds a crafting grid that pulls from storage.
   > How: an illuminated panel plus processors; the crafting version adds a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: JEI's + button fills the crafting terminal's grid straight from the network.
29. **ME Controller**: `ae2:controller` *(after: Terminals, Cables)*
   > What: the Controller hands out channels: 32 from each face. Without one, a network is limited to 8 devices.
   > How: in this pack it takes smooth sky stone, fluix, an engineering processor and an MI digital circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: controller blocks can be joined into a bigger box, but never into a cross or a loop.
30. **Network Tool**: `ae2:network_tool` *(after: Terminals)*
   > What: right-click any cable or device with the Network Tool to see its channels, power use and status. It also holds spare upgrade cards.
   > How: a quartz wrench, a chest and a calculation processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: when something's dark, this is the first tool to reach for.
31. **ME Chest and Drive**: `ae2:chest`; `ae2:drive` *(after: ME Controller)*
   > You remember a mind that held every name of every thing. The archive is waking.
   > What: the ME Chest is a one-cell drive with its own terminal. The ME Drive holds ten cells for the whole network.
   > How: both from iron, quartz glass, fluix cable and processors (check JEI). Connect the drive to the controller with cable.
   > Tip: keep power stable: an Energy Cell buffers the network.
32. **Cell Workbench**: `ae2:cell_workbench` *(after: ME Chest and Drive)*
   > What: the Cell Workbench sets which items a cell accepts (partitioning) and adds cards to cells.
   > How: wool, iron, a chest and a calculation processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cell partitioned to one dust keeps that stock in one place.
33. **IO Port**: `ae2:io_port` *(after: ME Chest and Drive)*
   > What: the IO Port empties a cell into the network, or fills a cell from it.
   > How: glass, two drives, fluix cable, iron and a logic processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: upgrading 4k cells to 64k? Run the old cells through an IO Port first.
34. **Equal Distribution Card**: `ae2:equal_distribution_card` *(after: Cell Workbench)*
   > What: with this card a partitioned cell keeps the same room for each of its items, so one item can't crowd out the others.
   > How: a basic card plus a few items (check JEI). Slot it in through the Cell Workbench.
35. **Overflow Destruction Card**: `ae2:void_card` *(after: Cell Workbench)*
   > What: a cell with this card destroys items of its partitioned types once it's full, instead of refusing them.
   > Chemistry: real matter can't vanish: mass is conserved in every chemical reaction. In Minecraft it can.
   > How: a basic card plus a few items (check JEI). Use it with a partition, or it will delete everything.
   > Tip: a void card on a cobblestone cell stops a generator from filling your whole network.
36. **ME Interface**: 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:interface)` *(after: Cables)*
   > What: an interface keeps chosen items stocked in itself for pipes and machines to pull. A storage bus on an interface lets one network see into another. Block or cable-part version.
   > How: iron, glass, an annihilation core and a formation core (check JEI). Set the items to keep in its top row.
   > Tip: a subnetwork for one chemical line, joined to the main network through an interface, keeps channels free.
37. **Import Bus**: `ae2:import_bus` *(after: ME Interface)*
   > What: an Import Bus pulls items out of the inventory it faces and into storage.
   > How: an annihilation core, iron and a sticky piston (check JEI). Put it on a cable facing a machine's output.
   > Tip: add a filter and Acceleration Cards to pull only products, faster.
38. **Export Bus**: `ae2:export_bus` *(after: ME Interface)*
   > What: an Export Bus pushes chosen items from storage into the inventory it faces.
   > How: a formation core, iron and a piston (check JEI). Set what it exports in its slots.
   > Tip: an export bus feeding coal coke to a boiler keeps it lit forever.
39. **Annihilation Plane**: `ae2:annihilation_plane` *(after: Import Bus)*
   > What: the Annihilation Plane breaks the block in front of it, or picks up items that land there, and stores them.
   > How: fluix crystals and an annihilation core (check JEI). It takes enchantments like a pickaxe.
   > Tip: an annihilation plane in front of a cobblestone generator feeds the Matter Condenser with no pipes.
40. **Formation Plane**: `ae2:formation_plane` *(after: Export Bus)*
   > What: the Formation Plane places blocks (or drops items) from the network into the space in front of it.
   > How: fluix crystals and a formation core (check JEI). Filter it, or it places anything you store.
41. **P2P Tunnels**: `ae2:me_p2p_tunnel` *(after: ME Interface)*
   > What: a pair of P2P tunnels carries 32 channels (or items, fluids, FE and redstone) through a single cable.
   > How: iron, an engineering processor and fluix (check JEI). Place both ends, then link them with a Memory Card.
   > Tip: right-click a P2P tunnel with a bucket, redstone dust or an FE item to change what it carries.
42. **Storage Bus**: `ae2:storage_bus` *(after: ME Interface)*
   > What: a Storage Bus on a chest, drawer controller or tank lets the network read and fill it as if it were a cell.
   > How: an interface, a piston and a sticky piston (check JEI).
   > Tip: a storage bus on your Functional Storage controller gives AE2 the whole drawer wall, without spending cell types.
43. **Memory Card**: `ae2:memory_card` *(after: P2P Tunnels)*
   > What: the Memory Card copies a part's settings and filters to another, and links P2P tunnels.
   > How: a calculation processor, iron, gold and redstone (check JEI). Sneak-use it on the source, then use it on the target.
44. **Capacity Card**: `ae2:capacity_card` *(after: Storage Bus)*
   > What: a Capacity Card adds filter slots to buses and other parts.
   > How: a basic card plus certus (check JEI). Slot it into the part's upgrade slots.
45. **Fuzzy and Inverter Cards**: `ae2:fuzzy_card`; `ae2:inverter_card` *(after: Capacity Card)*
   > What: Fuzzy matches items by damage or ignores their data; Inverter turns a whitelist into a blacklist.
   > How: an advanced card plus one extra item each (check JEI).
   > Tip: an inverted storage bus on a junk chest takes everything except what you list.
46. **Quartz Fiber**: `ae2:quartz_fiber` *(after: ME Interface)*
   > What: Quartz Fiber passes power between two networks without joining them.
   > Chemistry: glass made from pure SiO₂ (fused silica) is what real optical fibre is made of: so clear that light travels kilometres inside it.
   > How: glass and quartz dust (check JEI).
47. **Tunnels for Everything**: 2x `ae2:fe_p2p_tunnel`; 2x `ae2:fluid_p2p_tunnel` *(after: P2P Tunnels)*
   > What: P2P tunnels can carry FE, fluids, items, light or redstone instead of channels.
   > How: right-click an ME P2P tunnel with what it should carry, like a bucket or an FE item (check JEI for the full list).
   > Tip: FE tunnels move power through one cable instead of a bundle of power lines.
48. **Spatial IO Port**: `ae2:spatial_io_port` *(after: IO Port)*
   > What: the Spatial IO Port stores everything inside a frame of Spatial Pylons in a spatial cell, and can put it back elsewhere.
   > How: glass, an IO Port and an engineering processor (check JEI and the AE2 guide).
   > Tip: the stored room becomes a real dimension you can visit. Ask before you move someone else's base.
49. **Spatial Pylon**: `ae2:spatial_pylon` *(after: Spatial IO Port)*
   > What: pylons outline the space to be stored, along three edges of a box.
   > How: fluix and quartz glass (check JEI). Each pylon row also takes a channel.
50. **Spatial Anchor**: `ae2:spatial_anchor` *(after: Spatial Pylon)*
   > What: the Spatial Anchor keeps every chunk its network touches loaded.
   > How: check JEI.
   > Tip: one anchor keeps both ends of a quantum bridge alive.
51. **Spatial Cell**: 1x any of `or(item(ae2:spatial_storage_cell_2)item(ae2:spatial_storage_cell_16)item(ae2:spatial_storage_cell_128))` *(after: Spatial Pylon)*
   > What: spatial cells hold the stored space: 2, 16 or 128 blocks to a side.
   > How: a spatial component in a housing (check JEI).

### AE2: Autocrafting

*Applied Energistics, continued: Autocrafting*

1. **1k Component**: `ae2:cell_component_1k` *(after: ME Chest and Drive)*
   > What: components are the memory inside every storage cell. The 1k is the smallest.
   > Chemistry: certus and fluix are fictional, but the logic processors behind them echo real chips: doped silicon (Si).
   > How: certus, redstone and a logic processor (check JEI).
2. **4k Component**: `ae2:cell_component_4k` *(after: 1k Component)*
   > What: the first step up: a 4k component holds four times as many bytes as a 1k.
   > How: three 1k components around quartz glass, with redstone and a calculation processor (check JEI).
3. **16k Component**: `ae2:cell_component_16k` *(after: 4k Component)*
   > What: each tier combines three of the last with a calculation processor and quartz glass.
   > How: 16k from three 4k (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cell holds up to 63 item types whatever its size, so use small cells for odd items and big cells for bulk.
4. **64k Component**: `ae2:cell_component_64k` *(after: 16k Component)*
   > What: the 64k component, also what the Matter Condenser needs to make singularities.
   > How: three 16k components around quartz glass, with a calculation processor (check JEI).
5. **256k Component**: `ae2:cell_component_256k` *(after: 64k Component)*
   > What: the top AE2 component: 256 kilobytes for a single cell.
   > How: three 64k components around quartz glass, with sky stone dust and a calculation processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: a cell spends bytes on every new item type, so put bulk stock here and rare items elsewhere.
6. **1M Component**: `megacells:cell_component_1m` *(after: 256k Component)*
   > What: MEGA Cells continues the ladder past 256k: 1M, 4M, 16M, 64M, 256M.
   > How: 256k components, sky steel and accumulation processors (check JEI; the MEGA Cells section has both).
   > Tip: MEGA components need MEGA cell housings; AE2's won't take them.
7. **4M Component**: `megacells:cell_component_4m` *(after: 1M Component)*
   > What: the 4M component, four times the 1M.
   > How: 1M components, accumulation processors, ender dust and vibrant quartz glass (check JEI).
8. **16M Component**: `megacells:cell_component_16m` *(after: 4M Component)*
   > What: the next MEGA step.
   > How: three 4M components with accumulation processors (check JEI).
9. **64M Component**: `megacells:cell_component_64m` *(after: 16M Component)*
   > What: one step from the top.
   > How: three 16M components with accumulation processors (check JEI).
10. **256M Component**: `megacells:cell_component_256m` *(after: 64M Component)*
   > Every name of every thing, and room to spare. You remember this kind of memory.
   > What: the 256M MEGA component, the top of AE2 storage in this pack.
   > How: three 64M components with accumulation processors (check JEI).
11. **Item Storage Cell**: `ae2:item_storage_cell_1k` *(after: 1k Component)*
   > What: the 1k item cell: the thing you actually put in a drive.
   > How: a 1k component in an item cell housing (check JEI).
   > Tip: sneak-use an empty cell in the air to split it back into housing and component.
12. **Fluid Storage Cell**: 1x any of `or(item(ae2:fluid_storage_cell_1k)item(ae2:fluid_storage_cell_4k)item(ae2:fluid_storage_cell_16k)item(ae2:fluid_storage_cell_64k)item(ae2:fluid_storage_cell_256k))` *(after: Item Storage Cell)*
   > What: fluid cells store fluids the same way item cells store items. Any size counts.
   > Chemistry: H₂SO₄, HCl and HNO₃ each eat through different metals, so a real lab needs a different container for each. A fluid cell doesn't care.
   > How: a component in a fluid cell housing (check JEI).
13. **Portable Cell**: 1x any of `or(item(ae2:portable_item_cell_1k)item(ae2:portable_item_cell_4k)item(ae2:portable_item_cell_16k)item(ae2:portable_item_cell_64k)item(ae2:portable_item_cell_256k)item(ae2:portable_fluid_cell_1k)item(ae2:portable_fluid_cell_4k)item(ae2:portable_fluid_cell_16k)item(ae2:portable_fluid_cell_64k)item(ae2:portable_fluid_cell_256k))` *(after: Item Storage Cell)*
   > What: a portable cell is a storage cell with its own terminal and battery. Any size, item or fluid.
   > How: a component, a chest, a terminal and an energy cell (check JEI). Charge it in the Charger.
   > Tip: a portable cell on a mining trip holds far more than a backpack.
14. **Bulk Item Cell**: `megacells:bulk_item_cell` *(after: Item Storage Cell)*
   > What: a Bulk Item Cell holds a single item type in near-unlimited amounts.
   > How: the bulk component needs a 1M component and accumulation processors (check JEI). Partition it in a Cell Workbench.
   > Tip: perfect for cobblestone (condenser feed), salt dust or coal coke. A Compression Card stores nuggets, ingots and blocks as one pool.
15. **AE2 Powered Tools**: `ae2:charged_staff`; `ae2:entropy_manipulator`; `ae2:matter_cannon` *(after: 1k Component)*
   > What: the Charged Staff zaps mobs; the Entropy Manipulator heats or cools blocks; the Matter Cannon fires matter balls or nuggets.
   > Chemistry: the manipulator follows real phase changes: removing heat freezes water, and lava cools into obsidian when it loses heat too fast to crystallise.
   > How: each uses an energy cell and processors; the cannon also takes a 4k component (check JEI). Charge them in the Charger.
16. **Sky Steel**: 4x `megacells:sky_steel_ingot`; `megacells:item_storage_cell_1m` *(after: 256k Component)*
   > What: sky steel goes into every MEGA part. The 1M item cell is the first MEGA cell you can put in a drive.
   > Chemistry: sky steel is made by dropping charged certus, iron and sky stone into lava: heat drives the alloying, like a tiny smelter.
   > How: throw the ingredients into a lava pool for sky steel, then build the 1M cell (check JEI).
17. **Sky Bronze and Sky Osmium**: 4x `megacells:sky_bronze_ingot`; 4x `megacells:sky_osmium_ingot` *(after: Sky Steel)*
   > What: the same lava trick with copper gives sky bronze, and with osmium gives sky osmium. Both go into MEGA's larger parts.
   > Chemistry: real bronze is copper plus tin (Cu + Sn); here the sky stone plays the tin. Osmium (Os) is the densest natural element, 22.6 g/cm³.
   > How: drop charged certus, the ingot and a sky stone block into lava together.
18. **Accumulation Processors**: 4x `megacells:accumulation_processor` *(after: Sky Steel, Matter Condenser)*
   > What: the accumulation processor is MEGA's fourth processor, needed for every 1M+ part.
   > How: inscribe a singularity between the calculation and engineering presses to make the Accumulation Press, then print sky steel with it (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep the press. The Inscriber can copy it with an iron block, like the other presses.
19. **MEGA Crafting CPU**: `megacells:1m_crafting_storage`; 4x `megacells:mega_crafting_unit` *(after: Accumulation Processors)*
   > What: MEGA crafting storage and units build a separate, much larger crafting CPU.
   > How: check JEI. MEGA blocks only join other MEGA blocks, so build it as its own multiblock.
   > Tip: the Seed of a New World chain is huge. One big CPU saves splitting the job by hand.
20. **MEGA Pattern Provider**: `megacells:mega_pattern_provider` *(after: MEGA Crafting CPU)*
   > What: a pattern provider with many more pattern slots than the normal one.
   > How: made as a cable part and turned into a block in the crafting grid (check JEI).
   > Tip: put one on each multi-input MI machine, like the Chemical Reactor.
21. **MEGA Energy**: `megacells:mega_energy_cell`; `megacells:greater_energy_card` *(after: Accumulation Processors)*
   > What: the MEGA Energy Cell is eight dense cells around an accumulation processor. The Greater Energy Card gives portable tools far more charge.
   > How: both in a crafting table (check JEI).
22. **A Pocket Archive**: `megacells:portable_item_cell_256m` *(after: 256M Component)*
   > What: a portable cell with a 256M component: a whole storage network you carry, no drive needed.
   > How: a 256M component in a portable cell housing with an energy cell (check JEI). Charge it first.
   > Tip: perfect for a long trip to another planet.
23. **Pattern Providers**: 1x any of `item_tag(ae2:pattern_provider)`; `ae2:pattern_access_terminal` *(after: Cables)*
   > What: a Pattern Provider holds crafting patterns and sends their inputs to the machine it faces. The Pattern Access Terminal shows every provider on one screen.
   > How: iron, a crafting table and cores for the provider; an illuminated panel, an engineering processor and a provider for the terminal (check JEI).
   > Tip: processing patterns can drive MI machines too: send the inputs, wait for the outputs. The Automation and Logic page walks through a full sulfuric acid line.
24. **Encoding Patterns**: `ae2:pattern_encoding_terminal`; `ae2:blank_pattern` *(after: Pattern Providers)*
   > What: the Pattern Encoding Terminal writes crafting or processing recipes onto blank patterns.
   > How: a crafting terminal plus an engineering processor; blank patterns from quartz glass, glowstone and iron (check JEI).
   > Tip: JEI's + button fills the encoder with any recipe you look up.
25. **Molecular Assembler**: `ae2:molecular_assembler` *(after: Encoding Patterns)*
   > What: a Molecular Assembler next to a pattern provider crafts crafting-table recipes for the network.
   > How: iron, quartz glass, cores and a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: one provider can feed up to six assemblers, one on each face.
26. **Acceleration Card**: `ae2:speed_card` *(after: Molecular Assembler)*
   > What: Acceleration Cards speed up buses, Inscribers and Molecular Assemblers.
   > How: an advanced card plus fluix (check JEI). Up to five in an assembler.
27. **Level Emitter**: `ae2:level_emitter` *(after: Pattern Providers)*
   > What: the Level Emitter gives a redstone signal when the network holds more (or less) of an item than you set.
   > How: a redstone torch and a calculation processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: wire one to an MI Electrolyzer so it only runs while hydrogen stock is low.
28. **Redstone Card and Toggle Bus**: `ae2:redstone_card`; `ae2:toggle_bus` *(after: Level Emitter)*
   > What: a Redstone Card makes a bus work only with (or without) a signal. A Toggle Bus connects or cuts a cable branch by redstone.
   > How: a basic card plus a redstone torch; the toggle bus is fluix cable, redstone and a lever (check JEI).
   > Tip: put a toggle bus in front of a subnetwork you only want running sometimes.
29. **Crafting Card**: `ae2:crafting_card` *(after: Redstone Card and Toggle Bus)*
   > What: with a Crafting Card, an export bus or interface asks autocrafting for items the network doesn't have.
   > How: a basic card plus a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Crafting Card and a Redstone Card together make items only when a machine asks for them.
30. **Growth Accelerator**: `ae2:growth_accelerator` *(after: Pattern Providers)*
   > What: Growth Accelerators speed up certus buds growing on budding certus blocks.
   > Chemistry: real quartz crystals grow from silica-rich water over thousands of years. The idea of a seed crystal pulling material out of solution is real.
   > How: iron, fluix cable, quartz glass and a fluix block (check JEI). Place them touching budding certus and power them.
   > Tip: flawless budding certus never decays. Never break it with a normal pickaxe.
31. **Crafting Storage**: 1x any of `or(item(ae2:1k_crafting_storage)item(ae2:4k_crafting_storage)item(ae2:16k_crafting_storage)item(ae2:64k_crafting_storage)item(ae2:256k_crafting_storage))` *(after: Pattern Providers)*
   > What: crafting storage blocks make a crafting CPU: the bigger the storage, the bigger the job it can plan.
   > How: a crafting unit plus a cell component of the matching size (check JEI). Build a solid box of crafting blocks.
   > Tip: two CPUs beat one huge one: a long job then doesn't block a quick request.
32. **Co-Processor**: `ae2:crafting_accelerator` *(after: Crafting Storage)*
   > What: each Crafting Co-Processing Unit lets a CPU run one more step at the same time.
   > How: a crafting unit plus an engineering processor (check JEI).
   > Tip: co-processors only help if the machines keep up. Ten acid patterns on one Chemical Reactor still run one at a time.
33. **Crafting Monitor**: `ae2:crafting_monitor` *(after: Co-Processor)*
   > What: the Crafting Monitor shows the item a CPU is working on, right on its face.
   > How: a crafting unit plus a storage monitor (check JEI). Part of the CPU's box.
34. **A Bigger Plan**: 2x `ae2:16k_crafting_storage`; `ae2:64k_crafting_storage` *(after: Crafting Storage)*
   > What: long chemical chains need far more crafting storage than 1k.
   > How: a crafting unit plus a 16k or 64k component (check JEI). Add them to the CPU's box.
35. **ME Requester**: `merequester:requester` *(after: Crafting Storage)*
   > What: the ME Requester keeps a set amount of an item in stock by ordering crafts automatically.
   > How: check JEI. Set "keep 64 HDPE" and it never runs out.
   > Tip: it needs autocrafting patterns for whatever it keeps in stock.
36. **Requester Terminal**: `merequester:requester_terminal` *(after: ME Requester)*
   > What: the Requester Terminal lists every ME Requester on the network.
   > How: an illuminated panel, a logic processor and a Requester, shapeless (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep a stock rule for each acid: H₂SO₄, HCl and HNO₃ feed almost everything late game.
37. **Packaged Extended Crafting**: `packagedexcrafting:basic_crafter` *(after: Packaged Automation, Crystaltine)*
   > What: Packaged ExCrafting adds crafters that run Extended Crafting recipes from packages.
   > How: an auto table of the right size, an ME package component, crystaltine components, black iron and a redstone catalyst (check JEI).
   > Tip: encode the recipe in the Packaged Auto encoder, just like normal packages.
38. **The Ultimate Crafter**: `packagedexcrafting:ultimate_crafter` *(after: Packaged Extended Crafting, 9x9: Ultimate Table)*
   > What: the Ultimate Crafter runs 9x9 Ultimate Table recipes automatically from the network.
   > How: same recipe as the basic crafter, with an Ultimate Auto Table in the middle (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Seed of a New World is a 9x9 recipe. Feed it from the network and the capstone crafts itself.
39. **Matter Condenser**: `ae2:condenser`; `ae2:matter_ball` *(after: 1k Component)*
   > What: the Matter Condenser destroys items. With a component inside, it squeezes them into Matter Balls (or, with a 64k, a Singularity).
   > How: craft it (check JEI), put a component in, set the mode and feed it cobblestone from a pipe.
   > Tip: matter balls are Matter Cannon ammo; singularities unlock MEGA's press and every AdvancedAE machine.
40. **Singularity, Dust and a Small Bang**: `ae2:singularity`; `ae2:ender_dust`; `ae2:tiny_tnt` *(after: Matter Condenser)*
   > What: a singularity from the condenser, ender dust from the Inscriber and Tiny TNT: together they make entangled singularities.
   > Chemistry: gunpowder is potassium nitrate, charcoal and sulfur: 2KNO₃ + S + 3C → K₂S + N₂ + 3CO₂. The gases expanding all at once are the bang.
   > How: drop a singularity and ender dust together, then set off Tiny TNT next to them: you get a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities.
   > Tip: set it off away from anything you care about. It is still TNT.
41. **Quantum Bridge**: 16x `ae2:quantum_ring`; 2x `ae2:quantum_link`; 2x `ae2:quantum_entangled_singularity` *(after: Singularity, Dust and a Small Bang)*
   > What: two Quantum Network Bridges joined by entangled singularities act like one cable, even across dimensions.
   > How: build a 3x3 ring of 8 Quantum Rings around a Quantum Link Chamber at each end, then put one of a pair of entangled singularities in each chamber.
   > Tip: both ends must be chunk-loaded. Use FTB Chunks to force-load them.
42. **Spooky Action**: 2x `ae2:quantum_entangled_singularity` *(after: Singularity, Dust and a Small Bang)*
   > You remember being in two places at once. It felt exactly like this.
   > What: you made a pair of Quantum Entangled Singularities by blowing up a singularity with ender dust.
   > Chemistry: real entangled particles share one quantum state: measure one and you know the other, however far apart. Sadly it can't send messages faster than light; AE2 is kinder.
43. **Loaded Cannon**: `ae2:matter_cannon`; 16x `ae2:matter_ball` *(after: Matter Condenser)*
   > What: the Matter Cannon fires matter balls or metal nuggets from a cell inside it.
   > Chemistry: AE2 rates each nugget by its element's real atomic mass: iron 55.8, osmium 190.2, uranium 238. Heavier atoms carry more momentum at the same speed.
   > How: a condenser on Matter Ball mode makes ammo; the cannon's tooltip shows how to load it.
   > Tip: osmium and uranium nuggets are the best ammo you'll have spare.
44. **Wireless Access Point**: `ae2:wireless_access_point`; `ae2:wireless_booster` *(after: ME Controller)*
   > What: the Wireless Access Point sends your network a short distance through the air. Boosters raise its range.
   > How: a wireless receiver over a calculation processor and fluix cable; boosters from fluix dust, certus, ender dust and iron (check JEI).
   > Tip: put the access point near the middle of your base for the best coverage.
45. **Wireless Terminals**: `ae2:wireless_terminal`; `ae2:wireless_crafting_terminal` *(after: Wireless Access Point)*
   > What: reach your ME network from anywhere in range of a Wireless Access Point. The crafting version has a grid too.
   > How: check JEI. Link the terminal by putting it in the access point, and charge it in the Charger.
46. **Infinite Range**: `aeinfinitybooster:infinity_card`; `aeinfinitybooster:dimension_card` *(after: Wireless Terminals)*
   > What: the Infinity Booster Card removes the access point's range limit in one dimension; the Dimension Card reaches every dimension.
   > How: both need Nether Stars, so the Wither comes first (check JEI). The dimension card takes four infinity cards.
   > Tip: put the card in the Wireless Access Point, not the terminal, and keep that chunk loaded.
47. **Quantum Bridge Card**: `ae2wtlib:quantum_bridge_card` *(after: Quantum Bridge, Wireless Terminals)*
   > What: this AE2 Wireless Terminals card lets a terminal reach the network through quantum entanglement, from any distance or dimension.
   > How: quantum rings, a Quantum Link Chamber and an advanced card (check JEI). Its tooltip explains how to pair it.
   > Tip: the network's end must stay chunk-loaded.
48. **Universal Terminal**: `ae2wtlib:wireless_universal_terminal` *(after: Wireless Terminals)*
   > What: AE2 Wireless Terminals merges the crafting, pattern access and pattern encoding terminals into one Universal Terminal.
   > How: combine two wireless terminals in a crafting grid (check JEI); add more by crafting them in again.
   > Tip: a Magnet Card from the same mod pulls nearby drops straight into your network.
49. **A Spare Dimension Card**: 2x `aeinfinitybooster:dimension_card` *(after: Infinite Range)*
   > What: a second Dimension Card, for a second network or an outpost's access point.
   > How: four Infinity Cards, four Nether Stars and an eye of ender (check JEI).
50. **Import and Export Cards**: `ae2importexportcard:import_card`; `ae2importexportcard:export_card` *(after: Wireless Terminals)*
   > What: these cards go in a wireless terminal. The Import Card pushes chosen items from your inventory into the network; the Export Card keeps chosen items stocked in your inventory.
   > How: an import (or export) bus, redstone blocks, an advanced card and processors (check JEI).
   > Tip: set the Import Card to cobblestone, dirt and raw ores, and mining trips never fill your inventory.
51. **Gas in the Network**: `appmek:chemical_storage_cell_1k` *(after: Item Storage Cell)*
   > What: Applied Mekanistics lets AE2 store and move Mekanism chemicals: H₂, O₂, Cl₂, HCl, SO₂ and the rest.
   > Chemistry: a 1k cell holds a lot of gas because the network stores amounts, not tanks. Real gases need pressure vessels.
   > How: a chemical cell housing (osmium, quartz glass, redstone) + a 1k component. Import buses on chemical tanks fill it.
   > Tip: processing patterns can pull stored SO₂ and O₂ straight from the cell to feed your sulfuric acid line.
52. **A Tank Farm in a Cell**: `appmek:chemical_storage_cell_64k` *(after: Gas in the Network)*
   > What: a 64k chemical cell replaces a room full of chemical tanks.
   > Chemistry: one mole of any ideal gas fills about 22.4 L at 0 °C and 1 atm. Stored as data, it fills nothing at all.
   > How: chemical housing plus a 64k component (check JEI).
53. **Shielded Storage**: `megacells:radioactive_chemical_cell` *(after: A Tank Farm in a Cell, Fission)*
   > What: normal chemical cells refuse radioactive chemicals. MEGA's Radioactive Chemical Cell holds one, like nuclear waste or plutonium.
   > Chemistry: spent fuel stays dangerous because unstable nuclei keep decaying, giving off α, β and γ radiation for years.
   > How: check JEI for the radioactive component and cell.
54. **Energy in a Cell**: 4x `appflux:charged_redstone`; `appflux:fe_1k_cell` *(after: Item Storage Cell)*
   > What: Applied Flux stores FE in AE2 cells and moves it through the network with Flux Accessors.
   > How: redstone crystal (redstone block, fluix and glowstone dropped in water) → charge it in the Charger → FE cell core and housing (check JEI).
   > Tip: the housing needs insulating resin, which needs silicon: a little chemistry even here.
55. **Flux Accessor**: `appflux:flux_accessor`; `appflux:induction_card` *(after: Energy in a Cell)*
   > What: a Flux Accessor pushes FE from your FE cells into any machine it touches. An Induction Card lets an I/O bus or interface do the same.
   > How: an energy acceptor, energy processors, copper and glowstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: one FE cell plus accessors can replace a tangle of power cables.

### Extended and Advanced AE

*Bigger providers, faster crafters, and a computer that thinks in parallel.*

1. **Beyond the Basics**: `ae2:fluix_crystal` *(after: Fluix)*
   > You remember the archive was never big enough. It can grow.
   > What: ExtendedAE adds bigger versions of AE2's blocks and a new crystal, entro. AdvancedAE adds a reaction chamber, quantum alloy and a multiblock crafting computer.
   > How: any fluix crystal opens this page. Both halves start from it.
   > Tip: the Assembler Matrix and the Quantum Computer are the two big builds here; everything else feeds them.
2. **Note: Two Mods, One Page**: checkmark *(after: Beyond the Basics)*
   > What: the top half of this page is ExtendedAE (entro, the Crystal Assembler, extended blocks). The bottom half is AdvancedAE (the Reaction Chamber and everything quantum).
   > Tip: ExtendedAE changes a few AdvancedAE recipes to use its own parts, so check JEI rather than an online wiki.
3. **Fluix Block**: `ae2:fluix_block` *(after: Beyond the Basics)*
   > What: four fluix crystals make a fluix block. Planted with an entro seed, it becomes budding entro.
   > How: four fluix crystals in a square (check JEI).
4. **Entro Crystals**: `extendedae:entro_seed`; `extendedae:entro_crystal` *(after: Fluix Block)*
   > What: entro crystals feed every ExtendedAE machine. They grow like certus, from Budding Entroized Fluix.
   > How: craft Entro Seeds (sand, ender dust, redstone, glowstone, sky dust), then right-click a placed Fluix Block with a seed to make it budding. Harvest the clusters.
   > Tip: Growth Accelerators work on budding entro too.
5. **Note: Cells That Aren't Storage**: checkmark *(after: Fluix Block)*
   > What: ExtendedAE has cells that don't store anything: one that destroys what it's sent, and ones that supply water or cobblestone without end.
   > How: both go in an ordinary ME Drive. Click to continue.
6. **ME Void Cell**: `extendedae:void_cell` *(after: Note: Cells That Aren't Storage)*
   > What: a cell that destroys what you send it. Its modes delete items, turn them into Matter Balls, or compress them into Singularities.
   > Chemistry: in the real world matter is never destroyed in a chemical reaction; it only rearranges. This cell ignores that law.
   > How: check JEI. Partition it to cobblestone in a Cell Workbench and put it in a drive.
   > Tip: on Singularity mode it replaces the Matter Condenser for AdvancedAE and MEGA's singularity needs.
7. **Infinity Cell**: 1x any of `or(item(extendedae:infinity_water_cell)item(extendedae:infinity_cobblestone_cell))` *(after: Note: Cells That Aren't Storage)*
   > What: an infinity cell reports an endless stock of water or cobblestone to the network. Either one counts.
   > Chemistry: water (H₂O) is the most-used solvent in this pack: electrolysis, the Bayer process, acid dilution. Never running out of it is a quiet luxury.
   > How: check JEI. Put it in a drive; autocrafting pulls from it like any cell.
8. **Crystal Assembler**: `extendedae:crystal_assembler` *(after: Entro Crystals)*
   > What: the Crystal Assembler makes ExtendedAE's blocks from several items (and sometimes a fluid) at once.
   > How: crush entro to dust in the Inscriber, drop it in water with a gold ingot and lapis for an entro ingot, then build a Machine Frame and the Assembler (check JEI).
   > Tip: it accepts pipes and patterns, so the network can drive it like any other machine.
9. **Extended Blocks**: 1x any of `or(item(extendedae:ex_import_bus_part)item(extendedae:ex_export_bus_part)item(extendedae:ex_charger)item(extendedae:ex_inscriber)item(extendedae:ex_molecular_assembler)item(extendedae:ex_drive)item(extendedae:ex_io_port)item(extendedae:ex_interface)item(extendedae:ex_pattern_provider))` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: ExtendedAE's 'Ex' blocks are larger versions of AE2's: the Extended Pattern Provider holds many more patterns, the Extended Drive many more cells, and so on.
   > How: made in the Crystal Assembler from the normal block plus concurrent processors (check JEI). Any one of them counts.
   > Tip: one extended provider can feed a whole row of chemical reactors.
10. **Extended Pattern Access**: `extendedae:ex_pattern_access_part` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: the Extended Pattern Access Terminal lists every pattern provider on the network with search and filters.
   > How: a Pattern Access Terminal upgraded in the Crystal Assembler (check JEI). A wireless version exists too.
   > Tip: name your pattern providers in an anvil (Sulfuric Acid, Polyethylene) and the terminal groups them by name.
11. **Circuit Slicer**: `extendedae:circuit_cutter` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: the Circuit Slicer cuts a whole block (gold, diamond, silicon, certus) into nine printed circuits at once.
   > How: made in the Crystal Assembler (check JEI). Put the matching press in and feed it blocks.
   > Tip: a silicon block becomes nine printed silicon. That's an MI ingot line feeding AE2 nine at a time.
12. **ME Canner**: `extendedae:caner` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: the ME Canner fills buckets, cells and other containers from the network, or empties them back in.
   > Chemistry: many recipes still ask for a bucket of acid. The canner means the network can hand over 1,000 mB of H₂SO₄ in a bucket without you.
   > How: made in the Crystal Assembler (check JEI). Set Fill or Empty mode in its GUI and give it patterns through a provider.
13. **Wireless Connectors**: 2x `extendedae:wireless_connect`; `extendedae:wireless_tool` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: a pair of Wireless Connectors links two parts of your network without a cable between them. The Setup Kit binds them.
   > How: connectors come two at a time from the Crystal Assembler; the kit too (check JEI). Use the kit on one end, then the other.
   > Tip: great for reaching a reactor room behind thick shielding.
14. **Wireless Hub**: `extendedae:wireless_hub` *(after: Wireless Connectors)*
   > What: the ME Wireless Hub takes many wireless links at one point.
   > How: from the Crystal Assembler (check JEI). Bind each connector to it with the Setup Kit.
   > Tip: one hub in the middle of your base, linked out to every outpost room.
15. **Crystal Fixer**: `extendedae:crystal_fixer` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: budding entro and certus decay as they grow clusters. The Crystal Fixer restores them with fresh material.
   > How: from the Crystal Assembler (check JEI). Put it next to a budding block and give it what its GUI asks for.
   > Tip: one fixer keeps both farms alive.
16. **Active Formation Plane**: `extendedae:active_formation_plane` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: ExtendedAE's plane inserts items straight into the inventory it faces instead of dropping them.
   > How: a formation plane upgraded with ExtendedAE parts (check JEI).
   > Tip: handy for filling machines that don't accept a storage bus.
17. **Concurrent Processors**: 4x `extendedae:concurrent_processor` *(after: Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: concurrent processors go into nearly every Extended block: drives, providers, interfaces, inscribers and chargers.
   > How: build the Concurrent Press in the Crystal Assembler, inscribe entro crystals with it, then assemble the prints with printed silicon and redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Crystal Assembler can also make AE2's normal processors from their prints.
18. **Extended Inscriber and Charger**: `extendedae:ex_inscriber`; `extendedae:ex_charger` *(after: Concurrent Processors)*
   > What: the Extended Inscriber and Extended Charger work on several items in parallel, so processors and charged certus stop being a bottleneck.
   > How: a normal Inscriber or Charger plus capacity cards and a concurrent processor, in the Crystal Assembler (check JEI).
19. **Extended Interface and IO Port**: `extendedae:ex_interface`; `extendedae:ex_io_port` *(after: Extended Blocks)*
   > What: the Extended Interface stocks many more item types than a normal one. The Extended IO Port empties and fills cells far faster.
   > How: both from the Crystal Assembler (check JEI).
   > Tip: an Extended Interface next to an MI machine can hold every input that machine needs.
20. **Smarter Buses**: `extendedae:tag_storage_bus`; `extendedae:threshold_level_emitter` *(after: Extended Blocks)*
   > What: the Tag Storage Bus filters by item tag, so one bus can accept every dust or every ingot. The Threshold Level Emitter turns on at one amount and off at another.
   > How: a storage bus or level emitter plus processors (check JEI).
   > Tip: a threshold emitter on an MI Electrolyzer stops it flickering: on below 10,000 mB of hydrogen, off above 50,000 mB.
21. **Assembler Matrix Shell**: 43x `extendedae:assembler_matrix_frame`; 125x any of `or(item(extendedae:assembler_matrix_wall)item(extendedae:assembler_matrix_glass))` *(after: Extended Blocks)*
   > What: the Assembler Matrix is a multiblock that replaces walls of molecular assemblers. This is its shell: frames on the edges, walls or glass on the faces.
   > How: both from the Crystal Assembler (check JEI). The counts here are enough for a full-size shell.
   > Tip: glass faces let you watch the crafters work; walls are cheaper.
22. **Filling the Matrix**: 35x `extendedae:assembler_matrix_pattern`; 35x `extendedae:assembler_matrix_crafter`; 5x `extendedae:assembler_matrix_speed` *(after: Assembler Matrix Shell)*
   > Thirty-five hands working as one. You remember having more, but this is a start.
   > What: pattern cores hold the patterns, crafter cores do the work in parallel, and speed cores make each job finish sooner.
   > How: all from the Crystal Assembler with concurrent processors and entro (check JEI). They go inside the shell.
   > Tip: it's for crafting-table recipes only. Processing patterns for MI machines still need pattern providers.
23. **Into AdvancedAE**: `ae2:logic_processor` *(after: Beyond the Basics)*
   > What: AdvancedAE's first machines and its pattern provider all need logic processors. Bring one to begin.
   > How: the Inscriber, as on the Applied Energistics page.
24. **Reaction Chamber**: `advanced_ae:reaction_chamber` *(after: Into AdvancedAE)*
   > What: AdvancedAE's Reaction Chamber combines items and a fluid with lots of energy. Its first job: shattering singularities.
   > How: a matter condenser, a vibration chamber, fluix dust, glowstone and a bucket (check JEI). Feed it a singularity, ender dust, sky dust and lava.
   > Tip: it uses a lot of power per craft. Put it on its own Energy Acceptor.
25. **Directional Providers**: 1x any of `item_tag(advanced_ae:adv_pattern_provider)`; `advanced_ae:adv_pattern_encoder` *(after: Into AdvancedAE)*
   > What: the Advanced Pattern Provider lets a processing pattern send each input to a chosen side of the machine. The Advanced Pattern Encoder writes the sides onto the pattern.
   > How: an Extended Pattern Provider, a logic processor, an ender pearl and redstone for the provider (check JEI for both).
   > Tip: a Mekanism PRC takes items, a fluid and a gas on different sides: perfect for this.
26. **Quantum Materials**: `advanced_ae:shattered_singularity`; `advanced_ae:quantum_alloy`; `advanced_ae:quantum_processor` *(after: Reaction Chamber)*
   > What: the three materials behind everything quantum: a shattered singularity, quantum alloy, and the quantum processor printed on it.
   > Chemistry: copper is the alloy's base for a reason: after silver it's the best electrical conductor of any metal.
   > How: shatter a singularity in the Reaction Chamber; react quantum infusion with copper ingots and singularities for the alloy; press it with the Quantum Press (check JEI).
   > Tip: copy the Quantum Press before you use it in automation, like the other presses.
27. **Encoding Directions**: `advanced_ae:adv_pattern_encoder` *(after: Directional Providers)*
   > What: the encoder adds side information to a processing pattern.
   > How: put a pattern in, set each input's side, and take it out. Click JEI for the recipe.
   > Tip: keep one next to your Pattern Encoding Terminal.
28. **A Stack of Quantum Processors**: 4x `advanced_ae:quantum_processor` *(after: Quantum Materials)*
   > What: quantum processors go into the Quantum Computer's parts, quantum gear and AdvancedAE's best buses.
   > How: inscribe quantum alloy with the Quantum Press, then add redstone and printed silicon (check JEI).
29. **Quantum Unit and Structure**: `advanced_ae:quantum_unit`; `advanced_ae:quantum_structure` *(after: Quantum Materials)*
   > What: Quantum Structure blocks make the computer's shell; Quantum Crafting Units fill its inside.
   > How: both need quantum alloy and shattered singularities (check JEI).
30. **Quantum Storage**: 2x `advanced_ae:quantum_storage_128`; `advanced_ae:quantum_storage_256` *(after: Quantum Unit and Structure)*
   > What: quantum storage blocks set how big a crafting job the computer can hold in mind.
   > How: a quantum unit plus storage components (check JEI; ExtendedAE changes a few recipes).
   > Tip: storage first: a long chemical chain fails to plan long before it runs short of threads.
31. **Quantum Accelerator**: `advanced_ae:quantum_accelerator` *(after: Quantum Unit and Structure)*
   > What: each Quantum Accelerator lets the computer run more crafting steps at once.
   > How: a quantum unit, quantum processors and shattered singularities (check JEI).
32. **Quantum Core**: `advanced_ae:quantum_core` *(after: Quantum Accelerator, Quantum Storage)*
   > You remember thinking a thousand thoughts at once. The machine remembers how, too.
   > What: the Quantum Core is the heart of the Quantum Computer: a multiblock crafting CPU with huge storage and many parallel jobs.
   > How: the core goes inside a shell of Quantum Structure, with units, accelerators and storage around it (check JEI for size limits).
   > Tip: build it next to your main pattern providers so every chemical line can run at once.
33. **Multi-Threader**: `advanced_ae:quantum_multi_threader` *(after: Quantum Core, Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: the Multi-Threader multiplies what each accelerator in the computer adds.
   > How: quantum parts and ExtendedAE's components (check JEI). Only a few fit in one computer.
34. **Data Entangler**: `advanced_ae:data_entangler` *(after: Quantum Core, Crystal Assembler)*
   > What: the Quantum Data Entangler multiplies the whole computer's storage. Only a few fit in one multiblock.
   > How: quantum storage, quantum units and shattered singularities (check JEI).
   > Tip: one entangler is usually enough for the Seed of a New World chain.
35. **Quantum Crafter**: `advanced_ae:quantum_crafter` *(after: Quantum Accelerator)*
   > What: the Quantum Crafter crafts patterns over and over with no CPU, keeping a set amount in stock.
   > How: quantum accelerators, a quantum unit, 64k components and shattered singularities (check JEI).
   > Tip: set it to keep plates and wires in stock; the CPU stays free for the long chains.
36. **The Full Quantum Computer**: 200x `advanced_ae:quantum_structure`; 100x `advanced_ae:quantum_accelerator`; `advanced_ae:quantum_core`; `advanced_ae:quantum_multi_threader` *(after: Multi-Threader)*
   > Every reaction you ever learned, planned at once. You remember being this.
   > What: the materials for a maximum-size Quantum Computer: a full shell, a hundred accelerators, the core and a multi-threader.
   > How: it's a lot of shattered singularities. Automate the Reaction Chamber and the Condenser (or a Void Cell on Singularity mode) first.
   > Tip: you don't need the full size to finish the pack. This is for the archive's own sake.
37. **Quantum Armour**: `advanced_ae:quantum_helmet`; `advanced_ae:quantum_chestplate`; `advanced_ae:quantum_leggings`; `advanced_ae:quantum_boots` *(after: Quantum Materials)*
   > What: quantum armour is netherite armour rebuilt around quantum processors, with slots for AdvancedAE's armour cards.
   > How: each piece needs its netherite piece, quantum alloy plates, quantum processors and a quantum storage component (check JEI).
   > Tip: flight in this pack comes from chemistry (pylons, jetpacks, the Angel Ring), not from AE2, so no quest asks for the Flight Card.
