## Logistics

### Automation and Logic

*Make the factory run itself.*

1. **Moving Things Around**: 1x any of `or(item(pipez:wrench)item(integrateddynamics:wrench)item(laserio:laser_wrench)item(mekanism:configurator)item(powah:wrench)item(modern_industrialization:wrench))` *(after: Iron)*
   > You never carried your own buckets. You remember things flowing to where you wanted them.
   > What: this page is every way the pack moves items, fluids, gases and power: Pipez, Mekanism transmitters, Integrated Dynamics, LaserIO, and a few extras.
   > How: any of the logistics wrenches counts: Pipez, Integrated Dynamics, LaserIO, the Mekanism Configurator, Powah or Modern Industrialization.
   > Tip: start with Pipez. It is cheap, it works early, and you can swap it for something cleverer later.
2. **Pipez**: `pipez:wrench` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: Pipez has a pipe for each thing that moves, and the Pipe Wrench to cut and rejoin pipe sides.
   > How: check JEI for the wrench. Sneak-click where a pipe meets a machine to make that end extract.
   > Tip: Pipez only pulls from ends you set to extract, so connecting a pipe to a machine never drains it by accident.
3. **Item Pipes**: `pipez:item_pipe` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: the item pipe moves stacks between inventories.
   > How: iron and redstone (check JEI). Set the machine end to extract with the wrench or by sneak-clicking.
   > Tip: one pipe line can feed a whole row of furnaces; items go to the nearest free one first.
4. **Fluid Pipes**: `pipez:fluid_pipe` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: the fluid pipe moves liquids: water to boilers, acid to reactors, fuel to generators.
   > Chemistry: a pipe of sulfuric acid in real life is lined with PTFE or glass, because H₂SO₄ eats most metals. Pipez is kinder.
   > How: iron and redstone with a bucket (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep one fluid per pipe line, or the first fluid in blocks the rest.
5. **Energy Pipes**: `pipez:energy_pipe` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: the energy pipe carries FE (Forge Energy), the power most mods share.
   > How: iron and redstone with a redstone block (check JEI). Extract from the generator side.
   > Tip: MI machines run on EU, not FE. Use MI cables for those.
6. **Universal Pipe**: `pipez:universal_pipe` *(after: Item Pipes, Fluid Pipes, Energy Pipes)*
   > What: the Universal Pipe carries several kinds of thing at once in one line (its tooltip lists which).
   > How: item, fluid and energy pipes with iron and a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: set each side's mode per type in its GUI, so one pipe can feed a machine items and power together.
7. **Gas Pipes**: `pipez:gas_pipe` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: the gas pipe moves Mekanism chemicals: hydrogen, oxygen, chlorine, SO₂ and the rest.
   > Chemistry: keep H₂ and Cl₂ in separate lines: mixed and lit, they react explosively (H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl).
   > How: iron and redstone with infused alloy (check JEI).
8. **Filter Destination Tool**: `pipez:filter_destination_tool` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: this tool picks the one inventory a filter sends its items to.
   > How: right-click the target block with the tool, then click the filter entry in the pipe's GUI (check JEI for the recipe).
   > Tip: useful when two furnaces sit on one line but only one should get the coal.
9. **Pipe Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(pipez:basic_upgrade)item(pipez:improved_upgrade)item(pipez:advanced_upgrade)item(pipez:ultimate_upgrade))` *(after: Pipez)*
   > What: upgrades raise a pipe end's speed and unlock filters, redstone modes and round-robin. Any tier counts.
   > How: each tier is the one before plus better materials (check JEI). Put it in the extracting end.
   > Tip: round-robin spreads ore evenly across a row of machines.
10. **Mekanism Transport**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Configurator" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
11. **Mechanical Pipes**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism Transport)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Mechanical Pipes" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
12. **Universal Cables**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism Transport)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Universal Cable" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
13. **Logistical Transporters**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism Transport)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Logistical Transporters" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
14. **Thermodynamic Conductors**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism Transport)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Thermodynamic Conductors" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
15. **Pressurized Tubes**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism Transport)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Pressurized Tubes" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
16. **Integrated Dynamics**: `integrateddynamics:wrench` *(after: Crystalized Menril)*
   > What: Integrated Dynamics reads values from the world (tank levels, item counts), applies logic, and acts on them. Integrated Tunnels uses the same cables to move things. The Menril wrench rotates and removes ID blocks and parts.
   > How: Menril chunks and redstone (check JEI). The mod's own book, On the Dynamics of Integration, has worked examples.
   > Tip: the resin line that makes Menril chunks is on the Integrated Dynamics page.
17. **Logic Cables**: 10x `integrateddynamics:cable` *(after: Integrated Dynamics)*
   > What: logic cables join readers, writers, importers and exporters into one network.
   > How: crystalized Menril chunks and redstone (check JEI). Parts go on the side of a cable.
   > Tip: use the wrench on a cable side to cut it, so two networks next to each other stay apart.
18. **Variable Cards**: `integrateddynamics:variable` *(after: Integrated Dynamics)*
   > What: a variable card stores one thing: a number, a yes/no, an item, or a rule built in the Logic Programmer.
   > How: Menril chunks around redstone (check JEI).
   > Tip: make a stack. Every reader value and every exporter rule wants its own card.
19. **Items by Logic**: `integratedtunnels:part_importer_item`; `integratedtunnels:part_interface_item` *(after: Logic Cables, Variable Cards)*
   > What: an Item Importer pulls items into the network; an Item Interface lets the network's items be reached from a chest or machine.
   > How: put both on cables (check JEI for the parts). The importer takes a variable card that says what to move.
   > Tip: with no card, an importer moves everything. Add a card when you want it picky.
20. **Fluids by Logic**: `integratedtunnels:part_importer_fluid`; `integratedtunnels:part_interface_fluid` *(after: Logic Cables, Variable Cards)*
   > What: the fluid versions of the importer and interface.
   > Chemistry: an exporter that only runs while a tank reader says 'below 50%' is a simple feedback loop, the same idea as a float valve in a cistern.
   > How: check JEI for both parts; place them on cables against tanks and machines.
21. **Energy by Logic**: `integratedtunnels:part_importer_energy`; `integratedtunnels:part_interface_energy` *(after: Logic Cables, Variable Cards)*
   > What: energy importers and interfaces move FE through logic cables.
   > How: check JEI. Pull from a generator or battery, push out at a machine.
   > Tip: a redstone variable can switch power to a whole wing of the base on and off.
22. **LaserIO**: `laserio:logic_chip` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: LaserIO nodes sit on machines and pass items, fluids, chemicals, power and redstone along lasers. Logic chips go into every node and card.
   > How: raw logic chips are a quartz block, clay, gold nuggets and redstone (4 at a time); smelt them.
   > Tip: one node can serve all six sides of the block it touches.
23. **Laser Wrench**: `laserio:laser_wrench` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: the Laser Wrench links nodes together.
   > How: iron and a logic chip (check JEI). Click the first node, then the second.
   > Tip: sneak-click a node with the wrench to unlink it.
24. **Laser Nodes**: `laserio:laser_node` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: a node sits against a machine and holds the cards for each of its sides.
   > How: glass, iron, redstone and a logic chip (check JEI).
   > Tip: right-click a node to open its six side slots.
25. **Basic Filter**: `laserio:filter_basic` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: filters go inside cards. The basic filter matches the items you list.
   > How: put the filter in a card's filter slot and set it up.
   > Tip: flip it to deny mode to send everything except the listed items.
26. **Item Cards**: `laserio:card_item` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: cards tell each node what to move and in which direction.
   > How: put a card in a node's side slot. Set it to Extract on the source and Insert on the destination.
   > Tip: right-click with a card in your hand to open its settings.
27. **Fluid Cards**: `laserio:card_fluid` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: fluid cards move liquids between nodes.
   > How: same as item cards: Extract on the tank, Insert on the machine.
   > Tip: one node can run several cards on one side.
28. **Energy Cards**: `laserio:card_energy` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: energy cards move FE between nodes.
   > How: a logic chip with quartz, gold nuggets and a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: a node on your battery and one on each machine replaces a whole cable run.
29. **Redstone Cards**: `laserio:card_redstone` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: redstone cards read a signal at one node and send it out at another.
   > How: a logic chip with redstone (check JEI). Set channels to pair senders and receivers.
   > Tip: switch a separator on only while the sulfur chest has stock.
30. **Chemical Cards**: `laserio:card_chemical` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: chemical cards move Mekanism chemicals: hydrogen, oxygen, SO₂, slurries.
   > Chemistry: a separator splits water 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂. Two chemical cards on one node carry both gases off to different machines.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe; set Extract and Insert like any card.
31. **Card Holder**: `laserio:card_holder` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: the Card Holder carries spare cards and filters and fills nodes from your inventory.
   > How: a logic chip in iron with a chest (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep one of each card type in it while you wire a new line.
32. **Card Cloner**: `laserio:card_cloner` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: the Card Cloner copies one card's settings onto others.
   > How: a logic chip in iron with paper (check JEI). Sneak-click a card to copy, click another to paste.
   > Tip: clone one tuned acid card to every reactor in the line.
33. **Laser Connector**: `laserio:laser_connector` *(after: Laser Nodes)*
   > What: a connector relays lasers between nodes without holding cards.
   > How: glass, redstone, iron and a logic chip (check JEI).
   > Tip: nodes link up to a set range; connectors let you go round corners and through walls.
34. **Count Filter**: `laserio:filter_count` *(after: Basic Filter)*
   > What: the count filter tops a machine up to a set number and stops.
   > How: a basic filter with a comparator (check JEI).
   > Tip: 64 sulfur in the oxidizer and no more: the rest stays in storage for other lines.
35. **Tag Filter**: `laserio:filter_tag` *(after: Basic Filter)*
   > What: the tag filter matches whole tags, like c:dusts or c:ores.
   > How: a basic filter with a name tag or paper (check JEI). Type the tag in its screen.
   > Tip: one tag filter on c:raw_materials sends every raw ore to your processing line.
36. **Mod Filter**: `laserio:filter_mod` *(after: Basic Filter)*
   > What: the mod filter matches every item from the mod of the item you show it.
   > How: a basic filter plus a book (check JEI).
   > Tip: route all ChemLib items to the lab store with one card.
37. **Card Overclocker**: `laserio:overclocker_card` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: card overclockers raise how much one card moves per trip.
   > How: check JEI; it goes in a card's upgrade slot.
   > Tip: most lines don't need it. Add it when a machine starves.
38. **Node Overclocker**: `laserio:overclocker_node` *(after: LaserIO)*
   > What: node overclockers make a node act more often.
   > How: check JEI; it goes in the node's upgrade slot.
   > Tip: pair a fast node with an overclocked card for the busiest machine in a line.
39. **A Computer**: `computercraft:computer_normal` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > You never did your own chores. You remember having things that did them for you.
   > What: CC: Tweaked computers run Lua programs: monitor tanks, balance chemical lines, build a base dashboard.
   > How: place it and right-click. Type help, or edit startup to write a program that runs on boot.
   > Tip: Mekanism machines can be read by computers directly. Put a computer next to one and try peripheral.getNames().
40. **Monitors**: 4x `computercraft:monitor_advanced` *(after: A Computer)*
   > What: monitors show program output on a wall. Placed together, they join into one big screen.
   > How: put monitors next to the computer and run monitor <side> <program> to send output to them.
   > Tip: advanced monitors show colour and accept clicks, so you can make touch buttons.
41. **Wired Networks**: 2x `computercraft:wired_modem`; 16x `computercraft:cable` *(after: Monitors)*
   > What: wired modems and networking cable connect a computer to machines that aren't touching it.
   > How: put a modem on the machine, run cable back to a modem on the computer, and right-click the machine's modem to attach it.
   > Tip: each attached peripheral gets a name. List them with peripheral.getNames().
42. **Ender Modem**: `computercraft:wireless_modem_advanced`; `computercraft:pocket_computer_advanced` *(after: Wired Networks)*
   > What: the Ender Modem sends messages with no range limit, even between dimensions. A pocket computer carries a terminal with you.
   > How: use rednet on both ends: one computer broadcasts tank levels, your pocket computer reads them.
   > Tip: a remote alarm for your reactor is a very good idea.
43. **Turtles**: `computercraft:turtle_normal` *(after: A Computer)*
   > What: turtles are programmable robots that mine, build and farm.
   > How: craft one with a tool (a pickaxe makes a mining turtle) and fuel it with coal.
   > Tip: try the built-in excavate and tunnel programs first.
44. **Advanced Peripherals**: `advancedperipherals:energy_detector`; `advancedperipherals:me_bridge` *(after: Wired Networks, The God's Archive)*
   > What: extra peripherals: the Energy Detector measures power flow; the ME Bridge reads (and requests crafts from) your whole AE2 network.
   > How: place them on your wired network like any other peripheral.
   > Tip: an ME Bridge program can keep your stock of every intermediate topped up.
45. **Base Dashboard**: `advancedperipherals:fluid_detector`; 8x `computercraft:monitor_advanced` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: a wall screen that shows your chemical stocks, power and flow rates at a glance.
   > How: the Fluid Detector measures flow through a pipe. Combine it with tank readings and the energy detector in one program.
   > Tip: colour lines red when a tank drops below 20%. You'll spot problems from across the room.
46. **Printers and Disks**: `computercraft:printer`; `computercraft:disk_drive` *(after: A Computer)*
   > What: a Disk Drive lets you save programs on floppy disks and carry them between computers. A Printer prints text onto paper.
   > How: check JEI. Put a disk in the drive and it appears as disk/ in the computer's files.
   > Tip: print a list of your reactions and their inputs and bind the pages into a book: a real lab notebook.
47. **Advanced Turtle**: `computercraft:turtle_advanced` *(after: Turtles)*
   > What: advanced turtles have colour screens and can be clicked, which makes menus easy.
   > How: an advanced computer with gold instead of iron around it (check JEI). Give it a pickaxe to make a Mining Turtle.
   > Tip: run excavate 16 on a mining turtle and it digs a 16x16 hole down to bedrock, bringing everything back.
48. **Geo Scanner**: `advancedperipherals:geo_scanner` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: the Geo Scanner lists every block around it within a radius, including ores, for your computer to read.
   > Chemistry: real geologists find ore bodies by measuring gravity, magnetism and how rocks conduct electricity, rather than digging blind.
   > How: check JEI. Put it next to a computer (or in a pocket computer) and call scan(8).
   > Tip: write a program that counts ore blocks by type: it's a quick way to check a deposit before setting up a mine.
49. **Chat Box and Player Detector**: `advancedperipherals:chat_box`; `advancedperipherals:player_detector` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: the Chat Box lets a computer send chat messages; the Player Detector tells it who is nearby.
   > How: check JEI. Place them next to a computer.
   > Tip: have the base warn everyone in chat when a tank of hydrogen is nearly full or an induction matrix is running low.
50. **Inventory Manager**: `advancedperipherals:inventory_manager`; `advancedperipherals:memory_card` *(after: Advanced Peripherals)*
   > What: the Inventory Manager lets a computer move items into and out of your own inventory, once you bind it with a Memory Card.
   > How: right-click the Memory Card to bind it to yourself, then put it in the manager (check JEI).
   > Tip: a button that refills your hotbar with torches and food from storage is a classic first program.
51. **Buses**: `ae2:import_bus`; `ae2:export_bus`; `ae2:storage_bus` *(after: The God's Archive)*
   > What: an import bus pulls items out of a machine, an export bus pushes them in, and a storage bus lets ME see inside a chest or tank.
   > How: place them on cable facing the machine. Set filters in each bus's GUI.
   > Tip: Applied Mekanistics is in the pack, so buses and storage also handle Mekanism gases like hydrogen and SO₂.
52. **Crafting CPU**: 2x `ae2:crafting_unit`; `ae2:1k_crafting_storage` *(after: Buses)*
   > What: a crafting CPU is a multiblock that works out and tracks autocrafting jobs.
   > How: build a solid box of crafting units with at least one crafting storage, and connect it to your network.
   > Tip: more storage lets it plan bigger jobs; co-processing units run more steps at once.
53. **Encoding Patterns**: `ae2:pattern_encoding_terminal`; 8x `ae2:blank_pattern` *(after: Crafting CPU)*
   > What: a pattern is a recipe card: these inputs make that output.
   > How: in the Pattern Encoding Terminal, switch to Processing mode for machine recipes and fill in the inputs and outputs.
   > Tip: processing patterns work for any machine: MI, Mekanism or the Combiner.
54. **Autocraft a Chemical Line**: `ae2:pattern_provider`; `ae2:molecular_assembler` *(after: Encoding Patterns)*
   > What: pattern providers push ingredients into machines; molecular assemblers do crafting-table recipes.
   > How: put a provider against an MI or Mekanism machine, load a processing pattern, and send the output back into the network.
   > Tip: chain patterns (sulfur → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄) and one request runs the whole line.
55. **Level Emitters**: checkmark *(after: Buses)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Level Emitter" on the Applied Energistics page. Click to dismiss.
56. **Fully Automated Sulfuric Acid**: 16x `modern_industrialization:sulfuric_acid_bucket`; checkmark *(after: Autocraft a Chemical Line, Level Emitter)*
   > The factory hums without you. You remember this kind of quiet.
   > What: a line that makes sulfuric acid on its own and stops when the tanks are full.
   > Chemistry: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃ (industry uses a vanadium oxide catalyst), then SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄.
   > How: Separator (O₂) → Oxidizer (S → SO₂) → Infuser (SO₃) → Rotary Condensentrator (water vapour) → Infuser (H₂SO₄). Feed sulfur with a bus or LaserIO and gate it with a level emitter.
   > Tip: when it runs a full day with no help, fill 16 buckets and click the checkmark.
57. **Super Factory Manager**: `sfm:manager`; 8x `sfm:cable`; `sfm:disk` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: one Manager block runs a short program that moves items, fluids and energy between everything on its cables.
   > How: put the disk in the Manager and write a program, e.g. EVERY 20 TICKS DO INPUT FROM a OUTPUT TO b END.
   > Tip: the in-game editor has examples. Start with one input and one output.
58. **Labels**: `sfm:labelgun`; `sfm:network_tool` *(after: Super Factory Manager)*
   > What: the Label Gun tags inventories with names (like a and b above) for your programs.
   > How: set a label in the gun, then right-click each machine. The Network Tool shows what's connected.
   > Tip: label by job ('sulfur_in', 'acid_out'), not by machine type.
59. **Your First SFM Program**: checkmark *(after: Super Factory Manager)*
   > What: Super Factory Manager runs small text programs written on a disk. Labels name the blocks it talks to.
   > How: label a chest a and a furnace b with the Label Gun, then write this program on the disk and put it in the manager. Click the checkmark when items start moving.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Program:
   > EVERY 20 TICKS DO
   >     INPUT FROM a
   >     OUTPUT TO b
   > END
   > Tip: add a side, like OUTPUT TO b TOP SIDE, to choose which face of the block is used. The manager's built-in examples cover fluids and energy too.
60. **Logistics Network**: 2x `logisticsnetworks:logistics_node` *(after: Labels)*
   > What: Logistics Network nodes sit on machines and chests and move items, fluids and energy between every node in the same named network, with no cables.
   > How: obsidian, a redstone block, hoppers, an eye of ender and a redstone torch for a node (check JEI). Open a node to create or join a network, then set what it imports and exports.
   > Tip: the Wrench has a copy-paste mode: set up one node, then paste its settings onto the rest.
61. **Logistics Filters**: `logisticsnetworks:tag_filter`; `logisticsnetworks:amount_filter` *(after: Logistics Network)*
   > What: filters narrow what a node moves: by tag, by amount and more.
   > How: put a filter in a node's slot and set it up in its GUI (check JEI for all the filter types).
   > Tip: a tag filter for 'c:dusts' sends every dust to one chest.
62. **Node Upgrades**: `logisticsnetworks:iron_upgrade`; `logisticsnetworks:gold_upgrade` *(after: Logistics Network)*
   > What: upgrades raise how much a node moves per batch and how often. Iron, gold, diamond and netherite tiers each do more.
   > How: the tier's metal, hoppers, chests and smooth stone (check JEI). Put them in the node's upgrade slots.
   > Tip: the upgrade's tooltip lists its exact items, fluid and energy per batch.
63. **Moving Chemicals**: `logisticsnetworks:mekanism_chemical_upgrade` *(after: Node Upgrades, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: the Mekanism Chemical Upgrade lets nodes move Mekanism chemicals: H₂, O₂, Cl₂, SO₂ and the rest.
   > Chemistry: the contact process needs SO₂ and O₂ in the same place: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃. Nodes can bring both to one Chemical Infuser.
   > How: basic chemical tanks, infused alloy, chests and an Iron Upgrade (check JEI).
   > Tip: one network for gases and another for items keeps the settings easy to read.
64. **Network Manager**: `logisticsnetworks:computer` *(after: Logistics Network)*
   > What: the Computer opens a Network Manager that lists your networks, their nodes and how much each channel moves.
   > How: iron, glass and a comparator (check JEI).
   > Tip: when a line stops, look here first: a channel with no flow shows where the jam is.

### Integrated Dynamics

*Logic networks grown from resin.*

1. **Menril Trees**: `integrateddynamics:menril_log` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > Thought made solid, growing on a tree. You remember building minds out of stranger things.
   > What: Menril trees are where Integrated Dynamics starts: logs for resin, and berries from the leaves.
   > Chemistry: real tree resins are mixtures of terpenes, small hydrocarbons that plants build from isoprene units (C₅H₈). Amber is resin that hardened over millions of years.
   > How: find a Menril tree in the Overworld (Jade names it) and plant its saplings near your base.
2. **Menril Berries**: `integrateddynamics:menril_berries` *(after: Menril Trees)*
   > What: berries drop from Menril leaves.
   > How: break or wait for Menril leaves to decay.
   > Tip: read the berries' tooltip before you eat a stack.
3. **Menril Seeds**: `mysticalagriculture:menril_seeds` *(after: Menril Berries)*
   > What: Mystical Agriculture can grow Menril essence, which crafts into Menril logs, so you never chase trees again.
   > How: check JEI for the seed; its tier sets which Mystical Agriculture essence and circuit it needs.
   > Tip: the Mystical Agriculture page covers seed tiers.
4. **Squeezer**: `integrateddynamics:squeezer` *(after: Menril Trees)*
   > What: the Squeezer presses Menril logs into liquid resin.
   > How: an iron block, iron, planks and sticks (check JEI). Put a Menril log in and jump on it a few times.
   > Tip: it presses other things too. Ores give 2 raw ores in this pack, like every early processor.
5. **Drying Basin**: `integrateddynamics:drying_basin` *(after: Squeezer)*
   > What: the Drying Basin dries Menril resin into crystalized Menril chunks.
   > Chemistry: drying is evaporation: the solvent leaves and the dissolved solids stay, just as salt is left when brine dries.
   > How: logs, iron and black dye (check JEI). Place the Squeezer on top of the basin and the resin flows straight in.
6. **Crystalized Menril**: 10x `integrateddynamics:crystalized_menril_chunk` *(after: Drying Basin)*
   > What: crystalized Menril chunks make every cable, card and part of Integrated Dynamics.
   > How: dry resin in the basin, a bucket at a time.
   > Tip: nine chunks make a block, and some recipes want the block.
7. **Energy Battery**: `integrateddynamics:energy_battery` *(after: Crystalized Menril)*
   > What: the Energy Battery stores FE and can feed a network through its cables.
   > How: crystalized Menril chunks and blocks around a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: any FE source works; link a cable to your main grid instead if you have one.
8. **ID Generator**: `integrateddynamics:coal_generator` *(after: Energy Battery)*
   > What: Integrated Dynamics' own Generator burns furnace fuel for FE.
   > Chemistry: burning charcoal is C + O₂ → CO₂, about 33 kJ of heat for every gram of carbon.
   > How: an Energy Battery plus a furnace (check JEI).
9. **Mechanical Squeezer**: `integrateddynamics:mechanical_squeezer` *(after: Energy Battery)*
   > What: the powered Squeezer: faster and pipe-friendly.
   > How: the Squeezer with Energy Batteries, a diamond and obsidian (check JEI). Feed it FE.
   > Tip: ore output is capped at 2 raw ores in this pack, the same as the hand-powered one.
10. **Mechanical Drying Basin**: `integrateddynamics:mechanical_drying_basin` *(after: Energy Battery)*
   > What: the powered Drying Basin: it dries resin much faster.
   > How: the Drying Basin with Energy Batteries and more (check JEI).
   > Tip: press U on it in JEI to see what else it dries.
11. **Input Transformer**: `integrateddynamics:variable_transformer_input` *(after: Variable Cards)*
   > What: input variable transformers are the crafting parts of readers and importers.
   > How: variable cards, Menril chunks and a sticky piston (check JEI). Craft extra before a big build.
   > Tip: one transformer per part, so a dozen goes quickly.
12. **Output Transformer**: `integrateddynamics:variable_transformer_output` *(after: Variable Cards)*
   > What: output variable transformers are the crafting parts of writers and exporters.
   > How: like the input one, mirrored (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep both kinds in a chest next to your crafting table.
13. **Importers**: 1x any of `or(item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_energy)item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_world_energy)item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_item)item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_world_item)item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_fluid)item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_world_fluid)item(integratedtunnels:part_importer_world_block))` *(after: Input Transformer)*
   > What: importers pull items, fluids or energy into the network. World importers take straight from the world: they break blocks, pick up items, or drain fluid.
   > How: an input transformer and a few extras per part (check JEI). Any importer counts.
   > Tip: a world block importer with a filter is a tidy quarry face.
14. **Exporters**: 1x any of `or(item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_energy)item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_world_energy)item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_item)item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_world_item)item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_fluid)item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_world_fluid)item(integratedtunnels:part_exporter_world_block))` *(after: Output Transformer)*
   > What: exporters push items, fluids or energy out of the network. World exporters place blocks, drop items or pour fluid.
   > How: an output transformer and a few extras per part (check JEI). Any exporter counts.
   > Tip: a world block exporter is an automatic block placer for a cobble or basalt generator.
15. **Integrated Tunnels**: checkmark *(after: Importers, Exporters, Items by Logic)*
   > What: importers, exporters and interfaces together move anything along the logic cables, controlled by variables.
   > How: put an Item Importer on a chest and an Item Exporter on a machine, and give the exporter a variable card that says what to move. Click the checkmark when it works.
   > Tip: a fluid exporter with a yes/no variable from a tank reader only fills the reactor when it's below half.
16. **Logic Programmer**: `integrateddynamics:logic_programmer` *(after: Integrated Tunnels)*
   > What: the Logic Programmer writes values and rules onto variable cards: 'tank above 90%', 'more than 64 sulfur', and so on.
   > How: Menril chunks and a few extras (check JEI). Pick an operator on the left, fill in its inputs, and write it onto a blank card.
   > Tip: a Redstone Writer turns a yes/no card into a signal: perfect for stopping a separator when its tank is full.
17. **Portable Programmer**: `integrateddynamics:portable_logic_programmer` *(after: Logic Programmer)*
   > What: the same Logic Programmer, as an item.
   > How: a Logic Programmer and Menril chunks (check JEI).
   > Tip: carry it while wiring up a factory, so you can fix a card on the spot.
18. **Challenge: The Self-Stopping Separator**: checkmark *(after: Integrated Tunnels)*
   > What: make a Mekanism Electrolytic Separator turn itself off when its hydrogen tank is 90% full, and back on below 50%.
   > How: a Reader on the tank → a comparison in the Logic Programmer → a Redstone Writer on the separator (set it to redstone control in its GUI).
   > Tip: the gap between 50% and 90% (hysteresis) stops it flickering on and off.
   > Click the checkmark once it works.
19. **Note: Readers and Aspects**: checkmark *(after: Integrated Tunnels)*
   > What: every Reader part (inventory, fluid, energy, redstone, world and more) offers a list of aspects: single values it can read, like 'fill ratio' or 'item count'.
   > How: right-click a placed reader to see its aspects, and drag one onto a blank card to save it. Display Panels show a card's value live.
   > Tip: a Display Panel on every main tank is a cheap base dashboard. Click the checkmark when you've read one value.
20. **Integrated Crafting**: `integratedcrafting:part_interface_crafting` *(after: Logic Programmer)*
   > What: the Crafting Interface crafts on demand through the ID network, much like AE2 patterns.
   > How: write recipes onto variable cards with the Logic Programmer and put them in the interface on a machine (check JEI for the part).
   > Tip: it's a cheaper autocrafter than AE2 for small chains, like rubber sheets or redstone batteries.
21. **Variable Store**: `integrateddynamics:variablestore` *(after: Logic Programmer)*
   > What: the Variable Store holds variable cards so the whole network can use them.
   > How: check JEI. Put cards in the store and reference them from any writer or display panel on the network.
   > Tip: name cards with the Labeller after what they measure ('H2 tank %'). You'll thank yourself later.
22. **Crafting Job Terminal**: `integratedterminals:part_terminal_crafting_job` *(after: Integrated Crafting)*
   > What: Integrated Terminals' Crafting Job Terminal shows what Integrated Crafting is working on and what it's waiting for.
   > How: check JEI; it's a part, so it goes on a cable.
   > Tip: the Storage Terminal part (and its portable version) shows everything on the network, like an ME terminal.

### Pylons

*Standing stones that bend the rules of a chunk.*

1. **Pylons**: `minecraft:polished_blackstone` *(after: The Pylon's Frame)*
   > You remember marking ground as yours with a single stone. These are close enough.
   > What: Pylons are blocks that change the rules in an area: give you an effect, farm for you, keep mobs out, keep players out, or protect what you've built.
   > How: every pylon is the pylon frame (quartz slabs, iron bars and polished blackstone) around a core block. Most take a filter to tell them what to act on.
   > Tip: polished blackstone comes from the Nether: smelt or stonecut blackstone, then polish it.
2. **Expulsion Pylon**: `pylons:expulsion_pylon` *(after: Player Filter)*
   > What: the Expulsion Pylon sends other players out of the chunks around it. Whitelist friends with a Player Filter.
   > How: the pylon frame (quartz slabs, iron bars and polished blackstone) around a diamond block (check JEI).
   > Tip: with FTB Teams, your team is whitelisted automatically.
3. **Interdiction Pylon**: `pylons:interdiction_pylon` *(after: Mob Filter, Lifeless Filter)*
   > What: stops chosen mobs spawning around it. A Mob Filter names the mob; a Lifeless Filter blocks all natural spawns.
   > How: the pylon frame (quartz slabs, iron bars and polished blackstone) around a netherite block (check JEI). Put the filter inside.
   > Tip: a phantom filter over your base means sleepless nights are only a figure of speech.
4. **Harvester Pylon**: `pylons:harvester_pylon` *(after: A Spare Hoe)*
   > What: harvests ripe crops in a square around it and puts them in a chest above it, wearing down a hoe as it goes.
   > Chemistry: every harvest carries nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium out of the soil. Real farms put it back with fertiliser; this one forgives you.
   > How: the pylon frame (quartz slabs, iron bars and polished blackstone) around a hay bale. Put it level with the crops, a hoe inside and a chest on top.
   > Tip: an Unbreaking hoe lasts far longer; a Mending one never runs out.
5. **Infusion Pylon**: `pylons:infusion_pylon` *(after: Potion Filter, Lighter than Air)*
   > What: the Infusion Pylon applies a potion filter's effect to its owner, anywhere. With a Flying filter, that's flight.
   > Chemistry: its core needs hydrogen, the lightest element: the gas that lifted the first balloons.
   > How: in this pack: 2 quartz slabs, 2 iron bars, a block of emerald, 3 polished blackstone and 1 hydrogen from your Dissolver (check JEI).
   > Tip: the main path's Wings of a God quest walks through the flight filter step by step.
6. **Protection Pylon**: `pylons:protection_pylon` *(after: Mob Filter, Block Filter)*
   > What: stops chosen blocks being broken, or chosen mobs being hurt, in its range. A pet or a showpiece is safe even from your own sword.
   > How: the pylon frame (quartz slabs, iron bars and polished blackstone) around a honeycomb block (check JEI). Add a Block Filter or a Mob Filter.
   > Tip: protect the glass of your evaporation tower before the first creeper finds it.
7. **Player Filter**: `pylons:player_filter` *(after: Pylons)*
   > What: a Player Filter lists players for the Expulsion Pylon to let through.
   > How: cyan terracotta, green dye and glass around a diamond (check JEI). Right-click a player with it to add them.
   > Tip: one filter holds several names.
8. **Mob Filter**: `pylons:mob_filter` *(after: Pylons)*
   > What: a Mob Filter names a mob type for the Interdiction or Protection Pylon.
   > How: cyan terracotta, green dye and glass around netherite (check JEI). Use it on the mob to set it.
   > Tip: one filter per mob type; a pylon takes several.
9. **Potion Filter**: `pylons:potion_filter` *(after: Pylons)*
   > What: a Potion Filter stores a potion effect for the Infusion Pylon.
   > How: 2 cyan terracotta, green dye, an emerald and 5 glass. Drink a potion, then right-click the filter to store the effect.
   > Tip: it only works once it holds an hour of the effect, so brew Long or Extra Long potions.
10. **A Spare Hoe**: 1x any of `item_tag(minecraft:hoes)` *(after: Pylons)*
   > What: the Harvester Pylon needs a hoe to work, and wears it down by one point per harvest.
   > How: any hoe counts: wood, iron, diamond or a modded one.
   > Tip: the better the hoe, the longer between refills.
11. **Lifeless Filter**: `pylons:lifeless_filter` *(after: Pylons)*
   > What: the Lifeless Filter makes an Interdiction Pylon block every natural spawn over a much larger area.
   > How: cyan terracotta, green dye and glass around a Nether Star (check JEI).
   > Tip: spawners and breeding still work, so farms inside the area keep running.
12. **Block Filter**: `pylons:block_filter` *(after: Pylons)*
   > What: a Block Filter lists blocks the Protection Pylon keeps from being broken.
   > How: cyan terracotta, green dye and glass around a honeycomb (check JEI). Use it on a block to add it.
   > Tip: list the glass and casings of a multiblock so a slip of the pickaxe can't break it.

## Resources

### Farming and Food

*Grow what you need, cook it well, feed it back to the soil.*

1. **Knife and Board**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:tools/knife)`; `farmersdelight:cutting_board` *(after: Something to Eat)*
   > You remember feasts that lasted a week. Start with something smaller.
   > What: Farmer's Delight adds crops, meals and kitchen blocks. The knife harvests straw and cuts ingredients.
   > How: craft a knife (flint is the cheapest; any knife counts) and a Cutting Board. Place items on the board and use the knife on them.
   > Tip: a knife on tall grass gives straw; wild crops (tomatoes, onions, cabbage, rice) grow in the wild.
2. **Cooking Pot**: `farmersdelight:cooking_pot` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: the Cooking Pot turns several ingredients into one meal. It needs heat underneath.
   > Chemistry: browning meat is the Maillard reaction: amino acids and sugars react above about 140 °C, making hundreds of flavour compounds.
   > How: iron, bricks, a wooden shovel and a water bucket (check JEI). Place it over a fire, campfire or Stove.
3. **A Proper Meal**: 2x `farmersdelight:vegetable_soup` *(after: Cooking Pot)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight meals restore a lot of hunger and give long effects like Nourishment (hunger stops dropping) and Comfort.
   > How: cook vegetable soup in the Cooking Pot (check JEI), then bowl it.
   > Tip: a Feeding Upgrade in your backpack eats these for you.
4. **Pasta with Meatballs**: 2x `farmersdelight:pasta_with_meatballs` *(after: A Proper Meal, The New Crops)*
   > What: a hearty meal that chains every kitchen tool: knife (minced beef), board (raw pasta from dough) and pot (tomato sauce).
   > Chemistry: dough is starch and gluten proteins; water lets gluten chains cross-link into the stretchy network that holds pasta together.
   > How: follow the tree in JEI: wheat dough → raw pasta, beef → minced beef, tomatoes → tomato sauce, then the pot.
   > Tip: press U on any ingredient in JEI to see every meal that uses it.
5. **A Varied Diet**: 6x any of `item_tag(farmersdelight:meals)` *(after: Pasta with Meatballs)*
   > What: collect six bowls or plates of any Farmer's Delight meal: stews, soups, rice dishes, ratatouille, you choose.
   > How: anything in the 'meals' tag counts. Mix and match, they don't have to be different.
   > Tip: meals stack to 16; keep a stack in the backpack for long mining trips.
6. **Rich Soil**: `farmersdelight:organic_compost`; 4x `farmersdelight:rich_soil` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: organic compost slowly turns into Rich Soil, which grows crops faster and mushrooms into colonies.
   > Chemistry: composting is microbes breaking down organic matter with oxygen. They release CO₂ and heat, and leave humus rich in nitrogen.
   > How: craft compost from dirt, straw and bone meal plus rotten flesh or tree bark (check JEI), place it and wait.
   > Tip: till Rich Soil with a hoe to get rich farmland for crops.
7. **The Stove**: `farmersdelight:stove` *(after: Cooking Pot)*
   > What: the Stove heats a Cooking Pot or Skillet on top and can grill up to six items on its own surface.
   > How: iron ingots, bricks and a campfire (check JEI). Light it with flint and steel.
   > Tip: unlike a campfire it doesn't need logs, and it looks right in a kitchen.
8. **A Feast**: `farmersdelight:honey_glazed_ham_block` *(after: A Proper Meal)*
   > What: feasts are placed as blocks and served with a bowl, several portions each.
   > How: cook a Honey Glazed Ham (check JEI). Place it on a table and right-click with bowls.
   > Tip: a feast is the easiest way to feed a whole team before a boss fight.
9. **Banquet**: `farmersdelight:roast_chicken_block`; `farmersdelight:shepherds_pie_block` *(after: A Feast)*
   > What: two more feasts for the table: a whole Roast Chicken and a Shepherd's Pie.
   > How: both come from the Cooking Pot (check JEI). Each needs a container, often a bowl, to serve.
   > Tip: place feasts where everyone passes, like next to the team's waystone.
10. **Mushroom Colonies**: 2x any of `item_tag(farmersdelight:mushroom_colonies)` *(after: Rich Soil)*
   > What: a mushroom on Rich Soil grows into a colony that you can harvest again and again.
   > Chemistry: fungi don't photosynthesise. They digest organic matter with enzymes, which is why rich, dark soil suits them.
   > How: plant a brown or red mushroom on Rich Soil in low light, wait, then harvest it with shears; the colony stays and regrows.
   > Tip: mushroom colonies are the steady source of mushrooms for stews and rice dishes.
11. **Skillet**: `farmersdelight:skillet` *(after: The Stove)*
   > What: a frying pan that cooks one item at a time over heat, and doubles as a surprisingly good weapon.
   > How: iron ingots and a brick (check JEI). Place it on the Stove or a campfire, or check its tooltip for cooking in hand.
   > Tip: Fire Aspect on a skillet sounds silly; it works.
12. **Breakfast**: 4x `farmersdelight:fried_egg`; 4x `farmersdelight:cooked_bacon` *(after: Skillet)*
   > What: the start of most Farmer's Delight breakfasts: fried eggs and cooked bacon.
   > Chemistry: egg white turns opaque as heat unfolds its proteins (denaturation) and they tangle together; it can't go back.
   > How: cut raw porkchop into bacon on the Cutting Board, then fry it and the eggs on the Skillet or Stove.
   > Tip: combine them into Bacon and Eggs in the Cooking Pot (check JEI).
13. **The New Crops**: 4x `farmersdelight:tomato`; 4x `farmersdelight:onion`; 4x `farmersdelight:cabbage`; 4x `farmersdelight:rice` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight crops are the base of nearly every meal.
   > How: find wild tomatoes, onions, cabbages and rice in the world (rice grows in shallow water). Break them for seeds and replant.
   > Tip: rice must be planted in water one block deep, like in a real paddy.
14. **Tomatoes on a Rope**: 16x `farmersdelight:rope` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: tomato vines climb rope, so a single plant grows several blocks tall and fruits all the way up.
   > How: craft rope from straw (check JEI), hang it above a tomato plant, and let the vine climb.
   > Tip: rope also lets you climb down mineshafts; right-click a placed rope to extend it downward.
15. **Harvest Festival**: 128x any of `item_tag(c:crops)` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: a full harvest: any 128 items from the shared crops tag (wheat, carrots, potatoes, tomatoes, rice and more).
   > How: a large field, Hopper Botany Pots, or an MI Farmer all count. Carry them in one go.
   > Tip: crop storage blocks (crates and bags) pack 9 crops each; you need the loose crops here.
16. **Hopper Botany Pots**: 1x any of    > How: place one on a chest, add soil (dirt) and a seed.
   > Tip: Rich Soil or farmland grows faster than dirt, and Mystical Agriculture seeds work in pots too.
17. **Animal Husbandry**: `minecraft:lead`
   > What: cows, sheep, pigs and chickens give food, leather, wool and eggs. Two adults fed their favourite food make a baby.
   > How: lead two animals into a pen and feed them. Just Enough Breeding adds a JEI page per animal: look up any mob egg or food to see what it eats and what it drops.
   > Tip: babies take about 20 minutes to grow; feeding them their breeding food speeds that up.
18. **Pet Food**: `farmersdelight:horse_feed`; `farmersdelight:dog_food` *(after: Animal Husbandry, Knife and Board)*
   > What: Horse Feed heals and speeds up horses; Dog Food heals tamed wolves and gives them buffs.
   > How: both are Farmer's Delight crafting recipes (check JEI).
   > Tip: a well-fed wolf is a decent bodyguard in the early Twilight Forest.
19. **N, P and K**: `chemlib:urea`; `chemlib:diammonium_phosphate`; `chemlib:potassium_nitrate` *(after: The Combiner)*
   > What: plants need nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) more than anything else from the soil. These three compounds deliver them.
   > Chemistry: urea CO(NH₂)₂ is 46% nitrogen; diammonium phosphate (NH₄)₂HPO₄ carries N and P; potassium nitrate KNO₃ carries K and N.
   > How: make all three in the Alchemistry Combiner (check JEI for the element recipe of each).
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why nitrogen is the hard one.
   > Air is 78% nitrogen, but N₂ has a triple bond that plants can't break. Only some soil bacteria (and lightning) can 'fix' it.
   > In 1909 Fritz Haber found how to force N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃ with a metal catalyst, high pressure and heat; Carl Bosch scaled it up.
   > Today about half the nitrogen in your body passed through a Haber-Bosch plant. Ammonia is turned into urea, ammonium nitrate and phosphates.
   > You'll build that same reaction in the main quests (Haber-Bosch, HV tier). Phosphorus comes from mined phosphate rock, and potassium from potash salts like KCl.
20. **NPK Fertilizer**: `extended_industrialization:npk_fertilizer_bucket` *(after: N, P and K, The Chemical Reactor, Sulfuric Acid)*
   > What: Extended Industrialization's NPK Fertilizer is a fluid the MI Farmer can spread to grow crops faster.
   > Chemistry: bone meal is calcium phosphate; sulfuric acid frees phosphoric acid, H₃PO₄, just like the real 'wet process' for phosphate rock.
   > How: Chemical Reactor, three steps (check JEI): bone meal + H₂SO₄ → phosphoric acid; potato/carrot/beetroot + water + HCl → potassium chloride, then KCl + H₂ + O₂ → potassium hydroxide; finally nitrogen + phosphoric acid + KOH → NPK Fertilizer.
   > Tip: real NPK plants start from ammonia, not raw nitrogen. Here the recipe takes the shortcut.
21. **The Steam Farmer**: `extended_industrialization:steam_farmer` *(after: Analog Circuit, Electric Motor)*
   > What: Extended Industrialization's Farmer is a multiblock that tills, plants, harvests and (with fertiliser) speeds up a whole field.
   > How: analog circuits, a motor, bronze plated bricks, a steel combine and a bronze pipe casing (check JEI). Its layout is in JEI and the MI guidebook.
   > Tip: the Electric Farmer is the upgrade. JEI has a fertiliser page that shows which fluids speed up a Farmer.
22. **Food Fight**: 8x `farmersdelight:rotten_tomato` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: you found a use for spoiled tomatoes: rotten tomatoes can be thrown.
   > Chemistry: rotting is bacteria and fungi breaking sugars into acids, alcohols and gases. Don't eat it.
   > Tip: they're also good compost material. Probably better than throwing them at the team.
23. **Kitchen Garden**: 16x `minecraft:wheat_seeds`; 8x `minecraft:potato`; 8x `minecraft:carrot`; 8x `minecraft:melon_slice`; 8x `minecraft:sweet_berries` *(after: A First Field)*
   > What: the vanilla crops beyond wheat: potatoes and carrots from village farms, melons from jungles, sweet berries from taiga.
   > Chemistry: a potato is mostly starch, long chains of glucose packed into grains. Cooking swells and bursts the grains (gelatinisation), which is why a baked potato is soft.
   > How: break grass for seeds, raid a village farm for potatoes and carrots, and replant everything.
   > Tip: sweet berry bushes hurt to walk through. Plant a row as a mob fence.
24. **Barnyard Goods**: 16x any of `or(item(minecraft:beef)item(minecraft:porkchop)item(minecraft:mutton)item(minecraft:chicken)item(minecraft:rabbit))`; 4x `minecraft:leather`; 4x `minecraft:feather`; 4x `minecraft:egg` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: 16 raw meat of any kind, plus leather, feathers and eggs: the steady output of a few animal pens.
   > Chemistry: an eggshell is about 95% calcium carbonate, CaCO₃: the same compound as chalk and limestone. Drop one in vinegar and it fizzes away as CO₂.
   > How: breed cows, pigs, sheep, chickens or rabbits and harvest the adults. Chickens lay eggs on their own.
   > Tip: cook meat before eating; raw chicken can give you Hunger.
25. **Milk**: `minecraft:milk_bucket` *(after: Leather)*
   > What: drinking milk clears every potion effect, good and bad. It's also a baking ingredient.
   > Chemistry: milk is an emulsion: fat droplets held in water by proteins (casein). Add acid and the casein clumps into curds, which is the first step of every cheese.
   > How: use an empty bucket on a cow (or a goat).
   > Tip: carry one into the Deep Dark or the Wither fight to wipe Darkness or Wither in one gulp.
26. **Sugar**: 3x `minecraft:sugar` *(after: Sugar Cane)*
   > What: sugar goes into cakes, pies, fermented spider eyes and speed potions.
   > Chemistry: table sugar is sucrose, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁: a glucose and a fructose joined together. Heat it past about 160 °C and it breaks down into hundreds of brown, bitter-sweet compounds: caramel.
   > How: one sugar cane makes one sugar. A row of cane on Snad (Quality of Life page) grows fast.
   > Tip: the Alchemistry Dissolver splits sucrose into carbon, hydrogen and oxygen if you need the elements.
27. **Bake Sale**: `minecraft:cake` *(after: Sugar, Wheat)*
   > Wheat, sugar, milk and eggs from your own field and pasture. You remember feasts; this is a good start.
   > What: a cake, placed and eaten a slice at a time. It needs something from every part of this page.
   > Chemistry: baking is chemistry you can eat: egg proteins set the structure, sugar caramelises, and the Maillard reaction between sugars and proteins browns the crust.
   > How: 3 milk buckets, 2 sugar, an egg and 3 wheat (you keep the buckets).
   > Tip: a cake on the table in your base means nobody ever starves between trips.
28. **Honey and Wax**: 6x `minecraft:honeycomb`; 4x `minecraft:honey_bottle` *(after: Campfire)*
   > What: shears on a full bee nest give honeycomb; a glass bottle gives honey. Honeycomb waxes copper so it never tarnishes.
   > Chemistry: beeswax is mostly long esters (fatty acids joined to long alcohols). Wax on copper keeps out the air and water that would turn it green.
   > How: put a campfire under the nest first: the smoke keeps the bees calm. Then shear it or bottle it when it's dripping.
   > Tip: honey bottles cure poison and can be crafted into sugar.
29. **An Apiary**: `minecraft:beehive`; 2x `minecraft:honey_block`; 2x `minecraft:honeycomb_block` *(after: Honey and Wax)*
   > What: a beehive you can place where you like, plus the two honey blocks: sticky honey blocks and decorative honeycomb blocks.
   > Chemistry: honey is a supersaturated sugar solution, about 80% sugar in 17% water. That's why it slowly crystallises, and why bacteria can't live in it: the sugar pulls the water out of them.
   > How: a beehive is planks and honeycomb. A honey block is 4 honey bottles; a honeycomb block is 4 honeycomb. Lead bees home with flowers.
   > Tip: honey blocks slow anything on them and stop pistons pulling other blocks; great for flying machines.
30. **Wildflowers**: 16x any of `or(item(minecraft:dandelion)item(minecraft:poppy)item(minecraft:cornflower)item(minecraft:blue_orchid)item(minecraft:allium)item(minecraft:azure_bluet)item(minecraft:oxeye_daisy)item(minecraft:lily_of_the_valley)item(minecraft:red_tulip)item(minecraft:orange_tulip)item(minecraft:white_tulip)item(minecraft:pink_tulip)item(minecraft:torchflower))` *(after: Knife and Board)*
   > What: flowers make dyes, feed bees and decorate. Any 16 count.
   > Chemistry: many flower colours are anthocyanins, pigments that change colour with pH: the same molecule is red in acid and blue in alkali, like red cabbage indicator.
   > How: pick them in meadows and flower forests, or bone meal grass to grow more.
   > Tip: cornflower gives blue dye without lapis.
31. **Bone Meal**: 32x `minecraft:bone_meal` *(after: Rich Soil)*
   > What: bone meal makes crops, saplings and flowers grow instantly.
   > Chemistry: bone is mostly hydroxyapatite, Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH). Ground bone was one of the first phosphate fertilisers, before mined phosphate rock took over.
   > How: one bone makes 3 bone meal; a composter also turns plant scraps into it.
   > Tip: the NPK quests further along this page start from bone meal.
32. **Hay Bales**: 4x `minecraft:hay_block` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: a hay bale is 9 wheat. Horses and llamas eat it, and landing on one cuts fall damage by 80%.
   > How: 9 wheat in the crafting grid.
   > Tip: a hay bale under a campfire makes the smoke rise much higher: a signal for friends.
33. **Crates and Bags**: 4x any of `or(item(farmersdelight:cabbage_crate)item(farmersdelight:onion_crate)item(farmersdelight:tomato_crate)item(farmersdelight:carrot_crate)item(farmersdelight:potato_crate)item(farmersdelight:beetroot_crate)item(farmersdelight:rice_bag))` *(after: The New Crops)*
   > What: Farmer's Delight crates and bags hold 9 crops each and look good in a pantry. Any four.
   > How: 9 of the crop in the crafting grid (check JEI). Break one back into crops any time.
   > Tip: a wall of crates is a kitchen store that doubles as decoration.
34. **From the Sea**: 16x `minecraft:kelp`; 16x `minecraft:dried_kelp`; `minecraft:tropical_fish` *(after: Gone Fishing)*
   > What: kelp grows fast underwater; dried, it's a snack and (as a block) a good furnace fuel. Tropical fish come from fishing or warm oceans.
   > Chemistry: burnt kelp ash was the world's first source of iodine: Bernard Courtois found it in 1811 when sulfuric acid on seaweed ash gave off violet I₂ vapour. The ash was also a source of soda for glass.
   > How: harvest kelp, smelt it into dried kelp, and catch or bucket a tropical fish.
   > Tip: 9 dried kelp make a block that burns for 20 items in a furnace.
35. **Nether Fungi**: 4x `minecraft:crimson_fungus`; 4x `minecraft:warped_fungus` *(after: Into the Fire, Bone Meal)*
   > What: crimson and warped fungi grow into huge Nether trees when bone-mealed on matching nylium. Warped fungus on a stick steers a strider.
   > Chemistry: real fungi aren't plants: their cell walls are chitin, the same polymer as insect shells, not cellulose.
   > How: pick them in the crimson and warped forests. Bone meal on nylium grows more.
   > Tip: hoglins run from warped fungus. Plant some around your Nether base.
36. **Chorus Orchard**: 16x `minecraft:chorus_fruit`; 8x `minecraft:popped_chorus_fruit` *(after: The End)*
   > What: chorus fruit teleports you a short way when eaten. Smelted, it becomes popped chorus fruit for purpur blocks, end rods and Silent Gear's glittery dust.
   > How: break chorus plants on the outer End islands, or plant a chorus flower on end stone and grow your own.
   > Tip: in this pack the Potion of Flying uses hydrogen, not chorus, so this crop is for building and Silent Gear.
37. **Flax String**: 3x `silentgear:flax_string` *(after: Flax Seeds)*
   > What: Silent Gear's flax gives fibre for string, so bows and bindings don't depend on spider hunts.
   > Chemistry: flax fibre is nearly pure cellulose. Linen, made from it, is one of the oldest textiles, woven for over 30,000 years.
   > How: grow flax and craft its fibre into flax string (check JEI for the recipe).
   > Tip: flax flowers make blue dye too.
38. **Overqualified**: `minecraft:netherite_hoe` *(after: Netherite Tier)*
   > You remember making forests grow with a word. Now you're upgrading a hoe with netherite. Priorities.
   > What: a netherite hoe. It tills, it harvests leaves and sculk fast, and it cost you a netherite ingot.
   > Tip: hoes are the fastest tool for leaves, hay, moss and sculk. So it isn't entirely a joke.
39. **Something That Grows**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:crops)` *(after: A First Field)*
   > You remember fields that ripened when you walked past them. Now you'll have to wait for the sun, like everyone else.
   > What: this page covers food: the vanilla field and pasture, Farmer's Delight's kitchen, fertiliser chemistry and the sea.
   > Chemistry: every crop is stored sunlight: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, powered by light and run by chlorophyll.
   > How: pick up any crop (wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, Farmer's Delight crops and more all count).
   > Tip: village farms are a free first harvest.
40. **A Hoe**: 1x any of `item_tag(minecraft:hoes)`
   > What: a hoe tills dirt and grass into farmland, the only block most crops grow on.
   > How: 2 of any tool material and 2 sticks. Any hoe counts.
   > Tip: farmland within 4 blocks of water stays wet and grows crops faster.
41. **Seeds**: 8x `minecraft:wheat_seeds` *(after: A Hoe)*
   > What: wheat seeds come from breaking grass, and every harvest gives more back.
   > How: break tall grass, then plant on tilled farmland.
   > Tip: seeds also feed chickens; keep a few spare.
42. **Wheat**: 3x `minecraft:wheat` *(after: Seeds)*
   > What: wheat is bread, cake and animal feed.
   > Chemistry: a wheat grain is mostly starch plus gluten proteins, the proteins that make dough stretch.
   > How: grow seeds until the stalks turn gold, then break them.
   > Tip: a composter turns spare seeds into bone meal.
43. **Bread**: 3x `minecraft:bread` *(after: Wheat)*
   > What: the simplest real meal: three wheat make a loaf.
   > Chemistry: real bread rises because yeast ferments sugar into CO₂ and ethanol; the gas gets trapped in the gluten network.
   > How: 3 wheat in a row on a crafting table.
   > Tip: bread stacks to 64 and never spoils. Carry a stack.
44. **Sugar Cane**: `minecraft:sugar_cane` *(after: Seeds)*
   > What: sugar cane gives sugar and paper.
   > How: find it on sand or dirt next to water and replant it by water.
   > Tip: break the top blocks and leave the bottom one: it regrows.
45. **Flax Seeds**: `silentgear:flax_seeds` *(after: Seeds)*
   > What: Silent Gear's flax is grown for its fibre, which becomes string.
   > How: check JEI for where flax seeds drop, then plant them on farmland.
   > Tip: one seed is enough to start; replant the extras.
46. **Fishing Rod**: `minecraft:fishing_rod`
   > What: fishing gives fish, and sometimes treasure: saddles, name tags, enchanted books.
   > How: 3 sticks and 2 string.
   > Tip: Luck of the Sea and Lure enchantments make it far better.
47. **Shears**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:tools/shear)` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: shears take wool from sheep (they regrow it by eating grass), and collect leaves, vines and cobwebs.
   > How: 2 iron ingots diagonally. Any shears count.
   > Tip: dye a sheep and it grows coloured wool forever.
48. **Wool**: 3x any of `item_tag(minecraft:wool)` *(after: Shears)*
   > What: wool makes beds, carpets and banners.
   > Chemistry: wool is keratin, a protein held together by sulfur bridges between its chains.
   > How: shear sheep; each one gives 1 to 3 wool.
   > Tip: three wool and three planks make a bed: set your spawn early.
49. **Leather**: 3x `minecraft:leather` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: leather goes into books, item frames, armour and backpacks.
   > Chemistry: tanning cross-links the collagen in hide so it stops rotting; plant tannins or chromium salts do the job.
   > How: cows drop 0 to 2 leather each.
   > Tip: rabbit hide also crafts into leather (4 hides make 1).
50. **Eggs**: 3x `minecraft:egg` *(after: Animal Husbandry)*
   > What: chickens lay eggs by themselves about every 5 to 10 minutes.
   > Chemistry: the shell is about 95% calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, the same compound as limestone.
   > How: keep a few chickens penned and pick up what they drop.
   > Tip: throwing an egg sometimes hatches a chick.
51. **Feathers and Chicken**: 10x `minecraft:feather`; 5x `minecraft:chicken` *(after: Eggs)*
   > What: feathers make arrows and quills; raw chicken cooks into a decent meal.
   > How: breed chickens with seeds, then harvest the adults.
   > Tip: cook the chicken; raw chicken can make you hungry.

### Mystical Agriculture

*Resource crops, within the rules of chemistry.*

1. **Mystical Agriculture**: `mysticalagriculture:infusion_altar`; 8x `mysticalagriculture:infusion_pedestal` *(after: Prosperity Seed Base, Iron)*
   > You remember coaxing metal out of the ground like wheat. Some of that still works.
   > What: resource crops grow essence that crafts into real materials. Seeds are made on the Infusion Altar with Infusion Pedestals around it.
   > How: the altar is gold, stone and red wool; 8 Infusion Pedestals stand around it (check JEI for both and the layout).
   > Tip: Tier 3/4/5 seeds need MI LV/MV/HV circuits, and crops for chemistry milestones can't be grown at all. Farming is a convenience here, not a shortcut.
2. **Prosperity**: 4x `mysticalagriculture:prosperity_shard` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: prosperity shards come from prosperity ore. They make seed bases (the core of every resource seed) and infusion crystals.
   > How: mine prosperity ore (an iron pick is enough).
   > Tip: Ultimine the veins; you'll want a lot of shards.
3. **Infusion Crystal**: `mysticalagriculture:infusion_crystal` *(after: Inferium Essence)*
   > What: a crystal that combines lower essence into higher tiers. It wears out with use.
   > How: a diamond, prosperity shards and inferium essence (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Master Infusion Crystal never wears out; it comes much later, from supremium.
4. **Prudentium**: `mysticalagriculture:prudentium_essence` *(after: Infusion Crystal)*
   > What: the second essence tier, for tier 2 seeds (JEI lists every crop and its tier).
   > How: 4 inferium essence around an infusion crystal make 1 prudentium (check JEI).
   > Tip: it uncrafts back to inferium if you overshoot (check JEI).
5. **Tertium: LV Seeds**: `mysticalagriculture:tertium_essence` *(after: Prudentium, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: tier 3 seeds (iron, copper, redstone, nether quartz, tin, lead and more) need Tertium essence and an MI analog circuit.
   > Chemistry: the analog circuit stands on steel, and steel stands on coke: coal baked without air until only carbon is left.
   > How: 4 prudentium around an infusion crystal make 1 tertium. Each seed type costs its circuit once; planted seeds multiply.
6. **Imperium: MV Seeds**: `mysticalagriculture:imperium_essence` *(after: Tertium: LV Seeds, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: tier 4 seeds (gold, lapis, nickel, blaze, enderman and more) need Imperium essence and an MI electronic circuit.
   > Chemistry: the electronic circuit needs aluminum, which only electrolysis can free from its oxide: 2Al₂O₃ → 4Al + 3O₂.
   > How: 4 tertium around an infusion crystal make 1 imperium.
7. **Supremium: HV Seeds**: `mysticalagriculture:supremium_essence` *(after: Imperium: MV Seeds, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > You remember gardens that grew gold. These come close, and they still answer to chemistry.
   > What: tier 5 seeds (diamond, emerald, netherite and more) need Supremium essence and an MI digital circuit.
   > Chemistry: the digital circuit needs polyethylene: thousands of ethylene units, C₂H₄, linked into one chain.
   > How: 4 imperium around an infusion crystal make 1 supremium.
8. **Growth Accelerators**: `mysticalagriculture:inferium_growth_accelerator` *(after: Inferium Essence)*
   > What: growth accelerators placed below farmland speed up the crops above them. Stack several for more effect.
   > How: check JEI for each tier's recipe.
   > Tip: put them under the floor of your crop room so they're out of the way.
9. **Awakening**: `mysticalagriculture:awakened_supremium_essence` *(after: Awakening Rig, Cognizant Dust)*
   > What: the Awakening Altar turns supremium into awakened supremium for the strongest Mystical Agriculture gear.
   > How: JEI shows the altar, its Awakening Pedestals, the Essence Vessels and the awakening recipe.
   > Tip: awakened supremium makes the best Mystical Agriculture tools and armour.
10. **Master Infusion Crystal**: `mysticalagriculture:master_infusion_crystal` *(after: Supremium: HV Seeds)*
   > What: an infusion crystal with no durability, so essence upgrades stop costing crystals.
   > How: a supremium gemstone, supremium essence and prosperity shards (check JEI).
   > Tip: worth it once you are mass-producing tertium and imperium for seeds.
11. **Inferium Seeds**: 4x any of `item_tag(mysticalagriculture:seeds)` *(after: Mystical Agriculture)*
   > What: Inferium Seeds grow inferium essence, the fuel for every higher tier. Any 4 Mystical Agriculture seeds complete this.
   > How: 8 inferium essence around wheat seeds in a crafting grid (no altar needed). Plant them on farmland and replant the extra seeds.
   > Tip: every other resource seed starts from a seed base on the altar, so build a big inferium field first.
12. **Essence Farmland**: `mysticalagriculture:inferium_farmland`; `mysticalagriculture:inferium_seeds` *(after: Inferium Essence)*
   > What: farmland infused with essence. Inferium crops drop more essence on higher-tier farmland.
   > How: one inferium essence plus one farmland, shapeless (check JEI). Higher tiers use their own essence.
   > Tip: upgrade the farmland under your inferium field as each new essence tier arrives.
13. **Mystical Fertilizer**: `mysticalagriculture:mystical_fertilizer` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: instantly grows a crop or sapling, including resource crops that bone meal can't push.
   > How: bone meal, inferium essence and a diamond make 4 (check JEI).
   > Tip: save it for slow, expensive crops rather than wheat.
14. **Agglomeratio**: `mysticalagriculture:nature_agglomeratio`; `mysticalagriculture:earth_agglomeratio` *(after: Prosperity)*
   > What: some crops (nature, the four elements, dye, nether, coral and others) don't map to one item. Their seed recipes use an agglomeratio instead.
   > How: Nature Agglomeratio is pumpkin, potato, cactus and sugar cane; JEI shows the rest.
   > Tip: the elemental crops (air, earth, water, fire) feed many other recipes, so they're good early picks.
15. **Why Chemistry Won't Grow**: checkmark *(after: Tertium: LV Seeds)*
   > What: seeds for uranium, uraninite, osmium, fluorite, silicon, steel, aluminum, graphite, platinum, iridium, refined obsidian and refined glowstone don't exist in this pack. Click the checkmark when you've read why.
   > How: if JEI shows no altar recipe for a crop, it's one of these. Get them from ore processing and the reactors in the main quests.
   > Tip: iron, copper, tin, lead, gold and other everyday metals are still farmable, behind their circuit gates.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Deep dive: why these metals?
   > Each blocked resource is the reason a tier exists. Steel needs carbon from coke and an oxygen-controlled furnace; aluminum needs electrolysis of molten alumina (Hall-Héroult, 2Al₂O₃ → 4Al + 3O₂).
   > Silicon is reduced from quartz with carbon at about 2000 °C (SiO₂ + 2C → Si + 2CO). Fluorite is the fluorine source for uranium enrichment; uranium and uraninite are the nuclear chain.
   > Platinum and iridium come from the PGM line: anode sludge, aqua regia, ammonium hexachloroplatinate, calcining. Graphite and osmium gate Mekanism and MI steps.
   > Growing them on a plant would skip the chemistry those tiers teach. Everything else stays farmable, so farming saves time without replacing a single reaction.
16. **Watering Can**: `mysticalagriculture:watering_can` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: right-click to water crops in an area, which makes them grow faster while you hold it.
   > How: iron ingots, a bowl and bone meal (check JEI). Fill it from any water source.
   > Tip: stand in the middle of the field and hold right-click.
17. **Inferium Ingots**: 4x `mysticalagriculture:inferium_ingot` *(after: Prosperity)*
   > What: essence-infused ingots for tools, armour and the better watering cans.
   > How: a prosperity ingot plus 2 inferium essence (check JEI for the prosperity ingot).
   > Tip: each essence tier has its own ingot; JEI shows the upgrade path.
18. **Inferium Watering Can**: `mysticalagriculture:inferium_watering_can` *(after: Watering Can, Inferium Ingots, Mystical Fertilizer)*
   > What: a tiered watering can covers a larger area and works faster.
   > How: your watering can, inferium ingots and mystical fertilizer (check JEI). The higher tiers repeat the pattern.
   > Tip: the can keeps its contents when upgraded.
19. **A Lucky Harvest**: `mysticalagriculture:fertilized_essence` *(after: Inferium Seeds)*
   > What: crops sometimes drop Fertilized Essence. You found one.
   > How: it crafts into mystical fertilizer (check JEI).
   > Tip: more crops means more chances; a big inferium field pays for itself.
20. **Soulstone**: 4x `mysticalagriculture:soulium_dust`; 8x `mysticalagriculture:soulstone` *(after: Mystical Agriculture, Into the Fire)*
   > What: soulstone clusters generate in the Nether. A few of their blocks are soulium ore, the source of soulium dust.
   > How: mine soulstone in the Nether and watch for soulium ore (check JEI for its drops).
   > Tip: a soulium ingot is a prosperity ingot plus 2 soulium dust; soul dust (for soul glass) comes from smelting smooth soulstone.
21. **Machine Frame**: `mysticalagriculture:machine_frame` *(after: Soulstone)*
   > What: the shared frame for the Harvester, Soul Extractor, Seed Reprocessor and other MA machines.
   > How: iron, redstone and stone (check JEI).
   > Tip: MA machines run on Forge Energy, so they plug into any FE cable.
22. **Harvester**: `mysticalagriculture:harvester` *(after: A Scythe)*
   > What: the Harvester picks mature crops in an area in front of it and replants them, pushing drops into its inventory.
   > How: machine frame, soulium ingots, iron and two diamond scythes (check JEI). Power it with FE.
   > Tip: pipe its output into storage and the field runs itself.
23. **Soul Extractor**: `mysticalagriculture:soul_extractor` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: fills Soul Jars from mob drops (rotten flesh, bones, string and more) instead of kills.
   > How: machine frame, soulium ingots, iron and a soulium dagger (check JEI). Power it with FE.
   > Tip: feed it drops from an HNN Simulation Chamber for a fully passive soul supply.
24. **A Pot Farm**: 8x any of 8x any of `item_tag(mysticalagriculture:seeds)` *(after: Hopper Botany Pots, Inferium Seeds)*
   > What: Mystical Agriculture seeds grow in Hopper Botany Pots, which harvest by themselves into a chest below.
   > How: put each pot on a hopper, pipe or chest, add dirt or farmland and a seed. Hold any MA seed in JEI to see its pot growth time.
   > Tip: a column of pots over one shared item pipe is a compact essence farm for every tier.
25. **Infusion Pedestals**: 8x `mysticalagriculture:infusion_pedestal` *(after: Mystical Agriculture)*
   > What: the altar takes its eight side ingredients from the pedestals around it. Every seed recipe uses all eight.
   > How: each pedestal is gold, red wool and stone (check JEI). Place them as JEI shows around the altar.
   > Tip: a hopper or pipe into the altar's centre makes repeat seeds easier.
26. **Better Farmland**: `mysticalagriculture:prudentium_farmland` *(after: Prudentium)*
   > What: higher-tier farmland makes inferium crops drop more essence: prudentium, tertium, imperium or supremium.
   > How: one essence of the tier plus farmland (shapeless), or till dirt with a hoe and the essence.
   > Tip: it only boosts inferium crops; resource crops grow the same on any farmland.
27. **Stronger Accelerators**: `mysticalagriculture:prudentium_growth_accelerator` *(after: Prudentium)*
   > What: higher-tier growth accelerators reach further and tick crops more often.
   > How: essence of the tier around stone and that tier's gemstone (makes 3; check JEI).
   > Tip: stack them in a column under the crop; each tier adds range.
28. **Inferium Armour**: `mysticalagriculture:inferium_helmet`; `mysticalagriculture:inferium_chestplate`; `mysticalagriculture:inferium_leggings`; `mysticalagriculture:inferium_boots` *(after: Inferium Essence)*
   > What: Mystical Agriculture armor in six tiers, from inferium to awakened supremium. Higher tiers hold augments.
   > How: a diamond armor piece with two ingots and two gemstones of the tier (it keeps the item's enchantments). Each tier upgrades the last.
   > Tip: higher tiers also take augments; see the Augments quest.
29. **Inferium Tools**: 1x any of `or(item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_sword)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_pickaxe)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_axe)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_shovel)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_hoe)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_watering_can)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_bow)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_crossbow)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_shears)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_sickle)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_scythe)item(mysticalagriculture:inferium_fishing_rod))` *(after: Inferium Essence)*
   > What: essence swords, bows, crossbows and fishing rods, upgraded tier by tier like the armor.
   > How: the diamond (or plain) item with two ingots and two gemstones of the tier (check JEI).
   > Tip: a sword with the Mystical Enlightenment enchantment can collect Cognizant Dust from bosses.
30. **Augments**: `mysticalagriculture:unattuned_augment` *(after: Inferium Tools, Inferium Armour)*
   > What: augments add effects to essence tools and armor (speed, night vision, mining area and more). The Tinkering Table fits them.
   > How: an Unattuned Augment is prosperity shards and iron; attune it on the altar (check JEI). The Tinkering Table fits it.
   > Tip: higher gear tiers have more augment slots.
31. **Seed Reprocessor**: `mysticalagriculture:seed_reprocessor` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: grinds surplus resource seeds back into the essence they're made of, powered by FE.
   > How: a machine frame with soulium ingots, iron and 2 iron hoes.
   > Tip: feed it the extra seeds from a pot farm and nothing goes to waste.
32. **Essence Furnace**: `mysticalagriculture:furnace` *(after: Prosperity)*
   > What: a powered furnace that smelts with FE instead of burning fuel.
   > Chemistry: an electric furnace heats by resistance: current through a wire, P = I²R. No combustion, no CO₂ at the furnace.
   > How: a machine frame with iron, prosperity ingots and 2 furnaces.
33. **Essence Enchanter**: `mysticalagriculture:enchanter` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: applies the enchantment you pick, paid for with experience essence plus an item for each enchantment (check JEI for the costs).
   > How: an enchanting table on a soulium ingot over 3 soulstone.
   > Tip: it's the easy way to put Mystical Enlightenment on a sword.
34. **Soulium Spawner**: `mysticalagriculture:soulium_spawner` *(after: Seeds of Something)*
   > What: a powered spawner that turns mob essence into living mobs (JEI's Soulium Spawner page lists what each costs).
   > How: a machine frame with iron, soulium ingots and 2 wither skeleton skulls.
   > Tip: pair it with a mob grinder for drops crops can't grow, like XP.
35. **Awakening Rig**: `mysticalagriculture:awakening_altar`; 4x `mysticalagriculture:awakening_pedestal`; 4x `mysticalagriculture:essence_vessel` *(after: Supremium: HV Seeds)*
   > What: the Awakening Altar is fed by 4 Awakening Pedestals and 4 Essence Vessels holding air, earth, water and fire essence.
   > How: both are gold and soulstone, with orange wool (pedestal) or glass (vessel). JEI shows the layout.
   > Tip: fill the vessels before you start; awakening drains a lot of elemental essence.
36. **Witherproof Bricks**: 1x any of `or(item(mysticalagriculture:witherproof_block)item(mysticalagriculture:witherproof_bricks)item(mysticalagriculture:witherproof_glass))` *(after: Wither Skeleton Seeds)*
   > What: bricks the Wither's skulls can't destroy: build a box and fight it on your terms.
   > How: a witherproof block is soulstone in wither skeleton essence (a tier 5 crop); 4 blocks make 4 bricks.
   > Tip: the Seed of a New World needs Nether Stars, so a safe Wither arena pays for itself.
37. **Cognizant Dust**: 4x `mysticalagriculture:cognizant_dust` *(after: Supremium: HV Seeds)*
   > You remember learning from the strongest things you fought. Some of it is still on the floor.
   > What: Cognizant Dust drops from the Wither and the Ender Dragon when they die to an essence weapon with Mystical Enlightenment.
   > How: enchant an essence sword in the Essence Enchanter, then land the last hit on a boss with it.
   > Tip: it goes into awakened supremium: JEI shows the awakening recipe.
38. **Seeds of Something**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:seeds)`
   > You remember coaxing metal out of the ground like wheat. Some of that still works.
   > What: Mystical Agriculture grows resources as crops. This page climbs its five essence tiers and lists every seed this pack allows.
   > Chemistry: a real plant only builds itself from CO₂, water and a few soil minerals. Growing iron from a seed is the magic part; the circuit gates are the chemistry part.
   > How: pick up any seed. Wheat seeds from grass are fine.
   > Tip: seeds for uranium, osmium, fluorite and the other chemistry milestones don't exist here, by design.

   > What: every resource seed is crafted around a seed base on the Infusion Altar.

   > What: the first essence. Everything on this page is built from it, and every higher essence is made from four of the tier below.
   > How: mine inferium ore (or kill mobs, which drop a little). 8 essence around wheat seeds make Inferium Seeds.
   > Tip: a big inferium field is the engine of the whole page.
