### Mystical Agriculture: Tier 1 Crops

*Mystical Agriculture, continued: Tier 1 Crops*

1. **Soulium Dagger**: `mysticalagriculture:soulium_dagger`; 4x `mysticalagriculture:soul_jar`; `mysticalagriculture:soul_extractor` *(after: Prudentium, Soulstone)*
   > What: kills with this dagger capture the mob's soul into a Soul Jar in your inventory.
   > How: a golden sword, soulium ingots and soulium dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: carry 4 Soul Jars for four mob types; the Soul Extractor fills jars from drops instead of kills.
2. **Soul Jars**: 2x `mysticalagriculture:soul_jar` *(after: Soulium Dagger)*
   > What: each jar stores souls of one mob type. Full jars are the material for mob seeds.
   > How: soul glass (soul dust around glass) and a soulium ingot (check JEI).
   > Tip: carry one empty jar per mob type you're hunting.
3. **Fill a Jar**: kill 20x `minecraft:zombie` *(after: Soul Jars)*
   > What: fill a Soul Jar with zombie souls for zombie seeds (rotten flesh).
   > How: keep an empty Soul Jar in your inventory and kill zombies with the Soulium Dagger.
   > Tip: the Soul Extractor can also pull souls out of mob drops like rotten flesh (check JEI).
4. **Mob Seeds**: `mysticalagriculture:soulium_seed_base` *(after: Fill a Jar, Tertium: LV Seeds)*
   > What: mob seeds start from a Soulium Seed Base and grow drops like rotten flesh, bones and string.
   > How: a prosperity seed base plus 2 soulium dust. On the altar, put it in the middle and the full jars and essence on the pedestals (check JEI).
   > Tip: zombie, skeleton, spider and creeper are tier 3, so they also need an analog circuit.
5. **Experience Capsule**: `mysticalagriculture:experience_capsule` *(after: Soul Jars)*
   > What: stores experience points picked up while it's in your inventory, to spend later.
   > How: 2 soulium ingots and 2 soul glass.
6. **Ice Seeds**: `mysticalagriculture:ice_seeds` *(after: Essence Farmland, Mystical Agriculture)*
   > What: ice seeds grow ice essence, which crafts back into ice and snow.
   > How: a prosperity seed base on the Infusion Altar, with inferium essence and the crop's materials on the pedestals (check JEI).
   > Chemistry: ice is water whose molecules have locked into a hexagonal lattice held by hydrogen bonds; that open lattice is why ice floats.
   > Tip: one seed is enough: plant it and every harvest has a chance to drop another.

### Mob Data and Big Crafting

*Monifactory-inspired machinery: simulate mobs, craft on giant tables, and fold whole factories into a block.*

1. **Deep Learning**: `hostilenetworks:deep_learner` *(after: Neural Networks)*
   > You remember knowing every creature by name. You can learn them again, one fight at a time.
   > What: Hostile Neural Networks records mobs into data models. Trained models later make mob drops without the mob.
   > How: craft the Deep Learner (check JEI). Put models in the Deep Learner and keep it in your inventory while you fight.
   > Tip: start with a mob whose drops you'll need in bulk, like blazes, slimes or endermen.
2. **Your First Model**: `hostilenetworks:data_model` *(after: Deep Learning, Model Framework)*
   > What: a data model attuned to one mob type. It starts at Faulty and levels up as you kill that mob.
   > How: right-click a mob with a Blank Data Model, or craft a specific model (check JEI). Then hunt with the Deep Learner.
   > Tip: tiers go Faulty, Basic, Advanced, Superior, Self Aware. Higher tiers are more accurate, so fewer simulations fail.
3. **Simulation**: `hostilenetworks:sim_chamber`; `hostilenetworks:prediction_matrix` *(after: Deep Learning, Model Framework, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Simulation Chamber runs a trained model on FE and prediction matrices to make predictions and mob drops.
   > How: it needs an MV electronic circuit (aluminum chemistry). Insert a model of Basic tier or better, matrices and power.
   > Tip: pipe matrices in and drops out; one chamber per model keeps things simple.
4. **Loot Fabricator**: `hostilenetworks:loot_fabricator` *(after: Simulation)*
   > You remember making things appear from nothing. This is the mortal version: data, power and patience.
   > What: turns predictions into the specific drop you pick (blaze rods, ender pearls, slime balls and more).
   > How: also needs an MV electronic circuit. Feed it predictions from the chamber and select the output in its GUI.
   > Tip: simulated blazes are a cheap blaze-rod source for Silent Gear alloys and brewing.
5. **Self Aware**: checkmark *(after: Simulation)*
   > What: train one data model all the way to Self Aware, the top tier.
   > How: keep killing that mob with the model in your Deep Learner, or let the Simulation Chamber train it. Click the checkmark when you've done it.
   > Tip: a Self Aware model almost never fails a simulation.
6. **Twilight Predictions**: `hostilenetworks:twilight_prediction` *(after: Simulation, The Twilight Forest)*
   > What: Twilight Forest mobs give their own prediction type.
   > How: train a model on a Twilight mob and run it in the Simulation Chamber.
   > Tip: the Loot Fabricator shows which drops each prediction can become.
7. **Black Iron Parts**: `extendedcrafting:black_iron_slate`; `extendedcrafting:basic_component`; `extendedcrafting:basic_catalyst` *(after: Steel)*
   > What: Extended Crafting tables are built from black iron slates plus a component and a catalyst of matching tier.
   > How: black iron ingot = iron ingot + black dye (shapeless). Two ingots make a slate. A component takes a slate, luminessence (glowstone, redstone, gunpowder) and iron; four components ring a black iron ingot for the catalyst.
   > Tip: make extra black iron; every table tier and the Crafting Core need more.
8. **Extended Crafting**: 8x `extendedcrafting:black_iron_ingot`; `extendedcrafting:basic_table` *(after: Black Iron Parts)*
   > What: the Basic Table is a 3x3 table for Extended Crafting recipes, and the base of every bigger table.
   > How: black iron slate, basic component and catalyst, an iron block and a crafting table.
   > Tip: each bigger table is crafted from the one before it, so don't use this one up as decoration.
9. **5x5: Advanced Table**: `extendedcrafting:advanced_table` *(after: Extended Crafting, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: a 5x5 crafting grid for mid-game recipes.
   > Chemistry: its MI electronic circuit rests on aluminum, won by electrolysis of alumina: 2Al₂O₃ → 4Al + 3O₂.
   > How: the Basic Table, gold blocks, advanced component and catalyst, plus the electronic circuit (check JEI).
10. **7x7: Elite Table**: `extendedcrafting:elite_table` *(after: 5x5: Advanced Table, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: a 7x7 grid. Crystaltine and many late parts are crafted here.
   > Chemistry: the MI digital circuit needs polyethylene, chains of ethylene (C₂H₄) from cracking oil.
   > How: the Advanced Table, diamond blocks, elite component and catalyst, plus the digital circuit.
11. **9x9: Ultimate Table**: `extendedcrafting:ultimate_table` *(after: 7x7: Elite Table, EV: Processing Units)*
   > You remember building worlds on a table far bigger than this. Nine by nine will do for now.
   > What: the endgame's biggest crafts happen here, including the Seed of a New World.
   > Chemistry: the MI processing unit needs PVC: polyvinyl chloride, (C₂H₃Cl)ₙ, made from ethylene and chlorine.
   > How: the Elite Table, emerald blocks, ultimate component and catalyst, plus the processing unit.
12. **Packaged Automation**: `packagedauto:packager`; `packagedauto:unpackager` *(after: The God's Archive, 5x5: Advanced Table)*
   > What: Packaged Auto lets AE2 autocraft with Extended Crafting tables, through the PackagedExCrafting addon.
   > How: encode recipes in the Encoder, then set up a Packager, a PackagedExCrafting crafter and an Unpackager by your ME network (tooltips and JEI explain each block).
   > Tip: one setup per table size handles every recipe of that size.
13. **Ender Crafting**: `extendedcrafting:ender_crafter`; 2x `extendedcrafting:ender_alternator` *(after: Black Iron Parts, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the Ender Crafter finishes its recipes over time, faster with more Ender Alternators nearby.
   > How: ender ingots (iron + ender pearl), eyes of ender and a crafting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: a ring of alternators around the crafter speeds it up a lot.
14. **Combination Crafting**: `extendedcrafting:crafting_core`; 4x `extendedcrafting:pedestal` *(after: 7x7: Elite Table)*
   > What: put the main item on the Crafting Core and the extras on Pedestals around it. The core uses FE to fuse them.
   > How: elite components and catalysts, a frame and black iron (check JEI). JEI shows every combination recipe.
   > Tip: pipe FE into the core; it won't start without power.
15. **Crystaltine**: 4x `extendedcrafting:crystaltine_ingot` *(after: 7x7: Elite Table)*
   > What: a late crafting metal made on the Elite Table.
   > Chemistry: lapis lazuli's blue comes from lazurite, a sodium aluminosilicate with trapped sulfur ions (S₃⁻).
   > How: diamonds, lapis, iron, gold and a Nether Star in a 7x4 pattern (check JEI).
16. **Compact Machines**: `compactmachines:personal_shrinking_device` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: fold an entire factory into a single block. The Personal Shrinking Device lets you walk inside it.
   > How: shrinking and enlarging modules, an eye of ender, copper, iron and glass panes (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also shows you which machine room you're in and takes you back out.
17. **Machine Walls**: 16x `compactmachines:wall` *(after: Compact Machines)*
   > What: Compact Machine Walls frame every machine block.
   > How: crafted from polished deepslate (check JEI).
   > Tip: inside a room the walls are unbreakable; these crafted ones aren't.
18. **Atom Modules**: 2x `compactmachines:shrinking_module`; 2x `compactmachines:enlarging_module` *(after: Machine Walls)*
   > What: every Compact Machine needs one Atom Shrinking Module and one Atom Enlarging Module.
   > How: an eye of ender, a light pressure plate, a stone button and a piston (sticky for shrinking).
   > Tip: make spares; each new machine eats a pair.
19. **Step Inside**: visit `compactmachines:compact_world` *(after: Atom Modules)*
   > You remember holding a world in your palm. This one is smaller, but it's yours.
   > What: craft a Compact Machine, place it, and right-click it with the Personal Shrinking Device to enter its room.
   > How: walls + both modules + a metal sets the size: copper = tiny, iron = small, gold = normal, obsidian = giant, netherite = colossal (check JEI for the rest).
   > Tip: tunnels carry items, fluids and power through the walls; perfect for a compact chemical line.
20. **Hide the Cables**: `cable_facades:facade_wrench` *(after: LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: Cable Facades disguise cables and pipes as any block. Tidy factories, same throughput.
   > How: craft the Facade Wrench, then apply blocks to cables (check JEI).
   > Tip: facades on MI pipes make chemical lines much easier to look at.
21. **Teleporting Cake**: `telepastries:overworld_cake` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: TelePastries cakes teleport you to their dimension when you eat a slice.
   > How: the Overworld Cake brings you home. Refill it with saplings; the Nether Cake takes obsidian.
   > Tip: place the Overworld Cake in your Nether hub for a quick ride home.
22. **Cake at the End**: `telepastries:end_cake` *(after: Teleporting Cake, The End)*
   > What: a cake that sends you to the End.
   > How: a cake surrounded by eyes of ender. Refill it with eyes of ender.
   > Tip: leave it in your base so the End is one bite away.
23. **Training Data: Blazes**: kill 30x `minecraft:blaze` *(after: Your First Model, Into the Fire)*
   > What: every kill with a matching model in your Deep Learner adds data. Blaze models are worth it: blaze rods feed brewing, Powah and Create's Blaze Burners.
   > How: put a blaze data model in the Deep Learner, keep it in your inventory, and hunt blazes at a Nether Fortress.
   > Tip: a blaze model at a high tier turns the Simulation Chamber into an endless rod farm.
24. **Training Data: Endermen**: kill 30x `minecraft:enderman` *(after: Your First Model)*
   > What: ender pearls go into Entangled blocks, AE2 seeds, Powah ender cells and teleporting. An enderman model makes them renewable.
   > How: load an enderman data model and hunt them at night, in warped forests, or in the End.
   > Tip: wear a carved pumpkin, or look at their feet, so they don't attack you first.
25. **Overworld Predictions**: `hostilenetworks:overworld_prediction` *(after: Simulation)*
   > What: each simulation gives a prediction for the mob's home dimension as well as the drop. Overworld, Nether and End predictions are used in recipes and Fabrication Directives.
   > How: simulate any Overworld mob, such as a zombie or a cow. The Nether and End ones are their own quests.
   > Tip: predictions stack up fast; send them to storage with a pipe.
26. **The Data Center**: `hostilenetworks:data_center`; 1x any of `item_tag(c:obsidians)`; `minecraft:black_stained_glass`; `hostilenetworks:data_center_io_port` *(after: Loot Fabricator)*
   > You remember watching a million lives at once. This is a pale copy, but a useful one.
   > What: the Data Center runs up to 25 Self Aware data models at the same time, each making one drop per cycle.
   > How: a Sim Chamber, a Loot Fabricator, a Nether Star, echo shards and obsidian. Build a 7x7x7 hollow shell: obsidian floor, black stained glass walls and ceiling, with the controller in a bottom wall facing out (JEI shows the rules).
   > Tip: IO ports in the shell let pipes feed inputs and pull the drops. A Fabrication Directive picks which drop each slot makes.
27. **Flux Crafting**: `extendedcrafting:flux_crafter`; 2x `extendedcrafting:flux_alternator` *(after: Extended Crafting)*
   > What: the Flux Crafter runs special recipes using FE delivered by nearby Flux Alternators, like the Flux Star.
   > How: gold and redstone ingots (check JEI). Place alternators around the crafter and power them.
   > Tip: JEI's Flux Crafter tab lists every recipe and the FE each one needs.
28. **Auto Tables**: `extendedcrafting:basic_auto_table` *(after: Crystaltine)*
   > What: Auto Tables remember a recipe and craft it with FE whenever the ingredients are inside. Each table size has its own.
   > How: a crafting table of the same size plus crystaltine components (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Ultimate Auto Table is also the heart of Packaged ExCrafting's Ultimate Crafter (see the Applied Energistics page).
29. **A Room for Every Line**: 4x `compactmachines:machine` *(after: Step Inside)*
   > What: one compact machine per chemical line keeps your base tidy: a sulfuric acid room, a chlorine room, a petrochemical room.
   > How: craft more machines (check JEI for the sizes) and enter each with the Personal Shrinking Device.
   > Tip: a room only runs while the chunk with its machine block is loaded, so claim and force-load your factory.
30. **Multiblock Builder**: `industrialization_overdrive:terminal` *(after: MV: Aluminum, Electric Blast Furnace)*
   > What: Industrialization Overdrive's Multiblock Builder places every missing block of an MI multiblock from your inventory (or a linked ME network). Other modes copy and paste a formed one, or tear it down.
   > How: steel plates, glass panes and an MI electronic circuit (MV). Look at the controller and press the key combination its tooltip shows; another key cycles the modes.
   > Tip: carry the casings, hatches and coils first: it only places what you have.

   > Chemistry: redstone stands in for real conductors. Real circuits run on copper traces and doped silicon.
   > How: pick up any redstone. The learner and models below need it.
   > Tip: the Simulation Chamber and Loot Fabricator need an MV electronic circuit in this pack.

## Tech

### The Mechanical Age

*Create: rotation, presses and mixers. An early mechanical age that runs alongside steam and feeds into Modern Industrialization.*

1. **Andesite Alloy**: `create:andesite_alloy` *(after: Andesite)*
   > Gears and shafts. You remember a world that ran on clockwork, and you liked it.
   > What: andesite alloy, Create's first building material.
   > How: craft andesite with iron nuggets (zinc nuggets work too). Later a Mechanical Mixer makes it in bulk.
   > Tip: hold W over almost any Create block to watch its Ponder tutorial.
2. **Andesite Casing**: `create:andesite_casing` *(after: Andesite Alloy)*
   > What: casing blocks are the shell for gearboxes, deployers and more.
   > How: right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with andesite alloy. That's 'item application', and Create uses it a lot.
   > Tip: strip logs with an axe first. Any wood type works.
3. **Belts**: `create:belt_connector` *(after: Andesite)*
   > What: a belt links two shafts: it carries rotation between them and moves items along its top.
   > How: dried kelp makes belt connectors. Click one shaft with it, then a second shaft up to 20 blocks away in a straight line.
   > Tip: a belt past a press, a fan or a deployer is the simplest Create production line.
4. **Mechanical Press**: `create:mechanical_press` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: the Mechanical Press flattens ingots into plates and compacts items in a basin.
   > How: put the press over a depot, a belt or a basin, and power it.
   > Tip: plates are shared with MI in this pack, so pressed plates work in MI recipes too.
5. **Mechanical Mixer**: `create:mechanical_mixer` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: a mixer over a basin, heated by a Blaze Burner, makes alloys and fluids.
   > Chemistry: heat speeds up reactions and melts metals so they can mix into alloys.
   > How: catch a blaze in an Empty Blaze Burner (iron plates around netherrack), put it under the basin, feed it fuel, and put the mixer above.
   > Tip: feed the burner with a deployer or a mechanical arm so it never goes cold.
6. **Brass**: 8x `create:zinc_ingot`; 8x `create:brass_ingot` *(after: Mechanical Mixer, Blaze Burner)*
   > A golden metal, mixed in a basin. The old skill comes back to your hands.
   > What: brass, the key metal of Create's second age.
   > Chemistry: brass is a copper-zinc alloy, usually about two-thirds copper. Zinc makes it harder and gives the gold colour.
   > How: 1 copper + 1 zinc in a heated mixer gives 2 brass. Zinc ore generates in the world.
7. **Brass Casing**: `create:brass_casing` *(after: Brass)*
   > What: brass casing, for mechanical crafters, arms and brass tunnels.
   > How: right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with a brass ingot.
   > Tip: a deployer holding brass ingots can apply it automatically.
8. **Precision**: `create:precision_mechanism` *(after: Deployer)*
   > Each step in its place, every time. You used to build worlds this way.
   > What: the precision mechanism, made by sequenced assembly: one item passes the same stations several times. Mechanical Crafters join into a big grid for recipes too large for a crafting table.
   > How: start with a gold plate, then deploy a cogwheel, a large cogwheel and an iron nugget onto it, 5 loops. JEI shows the sequence. Crafters are an electron tube, brass casing and crafting table.
   > Tip: some outputs are scrap. Sort them off the end of the belt and recycle them.
9. **Engineer's Goggles**: `create:goggles` *(after: Andesite)*
   > What: Engineer's Goggles show speed and stress when you look at a machine; the wrench rotates and picks up Create blocks.
   > How: wear the goggles in your helmet slot and look at a shaft or generator.
   > Tip: sneak-right-click with the wrench to pick a block up instantly.
10. **Create Deco**: 8x `createdeco:brass_catwalk`; 8x `createdeco:andesite_sheet_metal` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: catwalks, sheet metal, cage lamps and other industrial building blocks.
   > How: check JEI for Create Deco recipes. Many use a press or the stonecutter.
   > Tip: catwalks over your machine lines make maintenance much easier.
11. **Millstone**: `create:millstone` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: the Millstone grinds cobblestone to gravel, wheat to flour, flowers to dye, bones to bone meal and more.
   > Chemistry: grinding raises surface area: a powder reacts, dissolves and mixes much faster than a lump.
   > How: a cogwheel, an andesite casing and stone. Power it from the side or below and drop items in on top.
   > Tip: it doesn't take ores here. Ore crushing needs Crushing Wheels later.
12. **Copper Casing**: `create:copper_casing` *(after: Copper)*
   > What: copper casing is the base for spouts, item drains and hose pulleys.
   > How: right-click a stripped log or stripped wood with a copper ingot.
   > Tip: press a stack of copper sheets while you're at it. Pipes need them next.
13. **Fluid Pipes**: `create:fluid_pipe` *(after: Copper)*
   > What: fluid pipes carry liquids, but only while a Mechanical Pump pushes them along.
   > Chemistry: a pump makes a pressure difference, and fluid always flows from high pressure to low.
   > How: copper sheets around a copper ingot make 4 pipes; a pipe and a cogwheel make a pump. The arrow on the pump shows the flow direction.
   > Tip: reverse the pump's rotation to reverse the flow.
14. **Hose Pulley**: `create:hose_pulley` *(after: Copper Casing)*
   > What: the Hose Pulley lowers a hose into a pool and sucks the fluid up, or fills an area from your pipes.
   > How: a copper casing, a dried kelp block and a copper plate. Power it and pipe its output away with a pump.
   > Tip: a big enough body of water or lava counts as endless (check the Ponder), so it's a free fluid source.
15. **Bioethanol**: `createaddition:seed_oil_bucket`; `createaddition:bioethanol_bucket` *(after: Fluid Pipes)*
   > What: Crafts and Additions makes liquid fuel from plants: seed oil, then biomass, then bioethanol, which burns in a Liquid Blaze Burner.
   > Chemistry: real bioethanol comes from yeast fermenting sugar: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2 C₂H₅OH + 2 CO₂. Plant oils are triglycerides, long carbon chains that store a lot of energy.
   > How: compact seeds in a press and basin for seed oil; mix crops with seed oil over heat for biomass; mix biomass, sugar and cinder flour for bioethanol (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's a renewable fuel for Create steam engines that never touches your oil wells.
16. **Spout**: `create:spout` *(after: Copper Casing)*
   > What: the Spout pours fluid into items below it on a depot or belt: water bottles, buckets, honey, lava cakes and more.
   > How: a copper casing over dried kelp. Pipe fluid into it and put a depot underneath.
   > Tip: spouts are a station in many sequenced assembly recipes, so you'll use them again.
17. **Item Drain**: `create:item_drain` *(after: Copper Casing)*
   > What: the Item Drain empties fluid containers that roll over it and holds the fluid for your pipes.
   > How: iron bars over a copper casing. Put it in a belt line and pull the fluid out with a pump.
   > Tip: it's the easy way to turn buckets from another mod into piped fluid.
18. **Blaze Cake**: `create:blaze_cake` *(after: Spout)*
   > What: feeding a Blaze Cake to a burner makes it superheated for a while, hotter than any normal fuel.
   > How: compact an egg, sugar and cinder flour into a cake base, then spout 250 mB of lava into it.
   > Tip: some recipes need superheat (New Age's blank circuits, for one). Check the heat icon in JEI.
19. **Encased Fan**: `create:encased_fan` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: an Encased Fan blows items along and processes them depending on what the air passes through.
   > How: a shaft, an andesite casing and a propeller (iron plates around alloy). Water in front washes, fire smokes, lava blasts, soul fire haunts.
   > Tip: items on a belt or depot in the air stream are processed; loose items on the ground are too.
20. **Smoking and Blasting**: `minecraft:campfire`; `minecraft:lava_bucket` *(after: Encased Fan)*
   > What: a fan blowing through fire or a campfire cooks food (smoking); through lava it smelts like a blast furnace (blasting).
   > Chemistry: hot air carries heat by convection, which is why a fan oven cooks faster than a still one.
   > How: put a lit campfire or a lava source block a block or two in front of the fan and send items through the stream.
   > Tip: one lava block never runs out, so bulk blasting costs nothing but rotation.
21. **Haunting**: `minecraft:soul_campfire`; 16x `minecraft:soul_sand` *(after: Smoking and Blasting)*
   > What: air blown through soul fire 'haunts' items: sand becomes soul sand, stone bricks infested, fungi swap Nether types.
   > How: a soul campfire or soul fire in front of a fan. Pass sand through it for soul sand. JEI lists every haunting recipe.
   > Tip: it's a renewable source of soul sand and soul soil, handy for Nether wart and soul torches.
22. **Fan Catalysts**: `create_connected:empty_fan_catalyst` *(after: Haunting)*
   > What: Create: Connected's fan catalysts hold the 'fire' or 'water' for a fan in one tidy block.
   > How: brass and iron bars make the empty catalyst; fill it to pick its processing type (check JEI).
   > Tip: no more flowing water flooding your belt line.
23. **Depots**: `create:depot` *(after: Belts)*
   > What: a Depot holds one stack of items for a press, fan, spout or deployer to work on.
   > How: andesite alloy and an andesite casing. Right-click to put items on it.
   > Tip: a depot under a press is the cheapest plate maker in the game.
24. **Andesite Funnel**: `create:andesite_funnel` *(after: Belts)*
   > What: funnels pull items out of chests and machines onto belts, or insert items from a belt; tunnels split a belt line evenly.
   > How: andesite alloy over dried kelp makes 2 funnels. Place them on a chest face or at the end of a belt (check JEI for tunnels).
   > Tip: a redstone signal shuts a funnel off, which is an easy on/off switch.
25. **Weighted Ejector**: `create:weighted_ejector` *(after: Depots)*
   > What: the Weighted Ejector flings items (or you) to a target block in an arc.
   > How: a gold plate, a depot and a cogwheel. Hold it and click the target before you place it.
   > Tip: stand on it for a free launch pad. The landing is your problem.
26. **Chutes**: `create:chute` *(after: Belts)*
   > What: chutes drop items straight down between machines and chests; a fan under or over one blows items upward.
   > How: iron plates and an iron ingot make 4 chutes.
   > Tip: a chute into a crushing wheel or basin is the simplest feeder there is.
27. **Item Vaults**: `create:item_vault` *(after: Belts)*
   > What: Item Vaults merge into one big storage block when placed together.
   > How: iron plates around a barrel. Place several side by side; funnels and pipes reach the whole vault.
   > Tip: vaults also go into frogports, so make a few extra.
28. **Brass Funnel**: `create:brass_funnel` *(after: Belts, Brass)*
   > What: brass funnels, tunnels and smart chutes take a filter, so you choose exactly which items pass and how many.
   > How: each uses an electron tube and brass (check JEI). Put an item or a Create Filter in the slot on the block.
   > Tip: a brass tunnel set to 'synchronise' only lets items through when every lane has one: perfect for 1:1 recipes.
29. **Rose Quartz**: 4x `create:rose_quartz`; 4x `create:polished_rose_quartz` *(after: Mechanical Mixer)*
   > What: rose quartz, for electron tubes.
   > How: craft 1 Nether quartz with 8 redstone, then polish it: hold sandpaper with the rose quartz in your off-hand and use it (a deployer can do this too).
   > Tip: washing crushed iron makes redstone as a byproduct, so a later ore line can feed this.
30. **Electron Tubes**: 4x `create:electron_tube` *(after: Rose Quartz)*
   > What: electron tubes go into deployers, mechanical crafters and other smart machines.
   > How: polished rose quartz on top of an iron plate.
   > Tip: make a stack. You'll need more than you think.
31. **Deployer**: `create:deployer` *(after: Electron Tubes, Brass)*
   > What: a deployer acts like a player's hand: it places, uses and applies items.
   > How: an andesite casing, an electron tube and a brass hand (pressed brass sheets).
   > Tip: deployers over a belt are how Create builds things in steps: that's sequenced assembly.
32. **Mechanical Arm**: `create:mechanical_arm` *(after: Precision, Brass Casing)*
   > What: the mechanical arm moves items between depots, belts, basins and machines in its reach.
   > How: hold the arm and click inputs and outputs before you place it. Check the Ponder.
   > Tip: one arm can feed a whole ring of depots around it.
33. **Crushing Wheels**: 2x `create:crushing_wheel` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: two Crushing Wheels spinning toward each other grind ore blocks into crushed ore, obsidian into powder, and stone into gravel and sand.
   > How: each wheel is a mechanical crafting recipe (check JEI). Place them side by side, spin them inward, and drop items in from above.
   > How: yields: an ore block gives 1 crushed ore plus a 75% chance of a second; deepslate and modded ores are capped at 2 in this pack. Raw ore gives just 1 crushed ore (no gain), plus an XP nugget chance.
   > Tip: crush ore blocks (silk touch), not raw ore. Even so it's the same 2x ceiling as every route before acids; Mekanism's acid chain is where 3x and up begins.
34. **Bulk Washing**: `create:encased_fan`; 8x `create:crushed_raw_iron` *(after: Crushing Wheels)*
   > What: an encased fan blowing through water washes crushed ore into nuggets plus a byproduct.
   > How: put flowing water in front of the fan and pass items through the air stream (a belt works).
   > Tip: washed crushed iron gives 9 nuggets (one ingot's worth) and a 75% chance of redstone. The byproduct is the bonus, not extra iron.
35. **Sturdy Sheets**: 4x `create:powdered_obsidian`; 4x `create:sturdy_sheet` *(after: Crushing Wheels)*
   > What: sturdy sheets, the armour plate for train casings and schedules.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass: lava cooled so fast that its silica never formed crystals.
   > How: crush obsidian into powder, then a sequenced assembly: spout 500 mB of lava onto it, press, press. JEI shows the loop.
   > Tip: the crushing wheels give the obsidian back 75% of the time, so feed it in until it's all powder.
36. **Rotation to Electricity**: `createaddition:alternator` *(after: Precision, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: Crafts and Additions' Alternator turns rotation into FE.
   > Chemistry: a coil turning in a magnetic field pushes electrons along the wire: electromagnetic induction.
   > How: in this pack its core is an MI analog circuit (LV), so electricity from rotation waits for the LV age. Feed it fast rotation.
37. **Electricity to Rotation**: `createaddition:electric_motor` *(after: Rotation to Electricity)*
   > What: the Electric Motor turns FE back into rotation, with a speed you set.
   > How: give it FE from your MI or Mekanism grid and set the speed in its GUI.
   > Tip: motors free you from water wheels and windmills. Put a Create line anywhere.
38. **Wires and Connectors**: `createaddition:rolling_mill`; 4x `createaddition:connector`; `createaddition:copper_spool` *(after: Rotation to Electricity)*
   > What: the Rolling Mill turns ingots into rods and plates into wire. Spools of wire link connectors into power lines.
   > How: roll copper plates into wire, wind it onto a spool, then click two connectors with the spool to string a wire.
   > Tip: connectors carry power over long gaps without cables on the ground.
39. **Accumulators**: 2x `createaddition:capacitor`; `createaddition:modular_accumulator` *(after: Wires and Connectors)*
   > What: the Modular Accumulator stores FE, and several placed together merge into one bigger battery.
   > Chemistry: the capacitor here is zinc over copper, the same pair Volta used in the first battery in 1800.
   > How: needs brass casing, capacitors, copper rods and electrum wire. Electrum is gold + silver mixed hot.
   > Tip: put it between your alternators and your machines to smooth out spikes.
40. **Tesla Coil**: `createaddition:tesla_coil` *(after: Accumulators)*
   > What: the Tesla Coil charges FE items on belts or depots below it, and zaps anything that walks under it.
   > How: a mechanical crafting recipe with brass, a capacitor, electron tubes and a copper spool (check JEI). Power it with FE.
   > Tip: put a belt of jetpacks or gadgets under it for an automatic charging station.
41. **Create: New Age**: `create_new_age:generator_coil`; `create_new_age:basic_energiser` *(after: Rotation to Electricity)*
   > What: magnet-and-coil generators, and Energisers that charge items with electricity.
   > How: the Generator Coil's core is an MI analog circuit (LV) in this pack. Spin it among magnets; the Ponder shows the layout.
   > Tip: the Basic Energiser is just an andesite casing and a lightning rod.
42. **New Age Motors**: `create_new_age:basic_motor`; `create_new_age:carbon_brushes` *(after: Create: New Age)*
   > What: New Age's Basic Motor runs on FE and spins a shaft; carbon brushes and motor extensions tune it.
   > Chemistry: a motor is a generator run backwards: current in a coil inside a magnetic field feels a force and turns.
   > How: an andesite casing, a magnetite block, a shaft and iron nuggets (check JEI for magnetite). Brushes are alloy, coal and a shaft.
43. **Heat Engines**: `create_new_age:stirling_engine`; `create_new_age:basic_solar_heating_plate` *(after: Create: New Age)*
   > What: New Age moves heat through heat pipes. Solar heating plates collect it from sunlight; a Stirling Engine turns it into slow rotation, and a Boiler Heater uses it in place of a blaze burner.
   > Chemistry: a real Stirling engine heats and cools a sealed gas. Hot gas expands and pushes a piston; cooled gas contracts and pulls it back. No fuel burns inside it.
   > How: heat pipes, iron and glass for the plate; a copper block, heat pipes and a shaft for the engine (check JEI and the Ponder scenes).
44. **Charging Metal**: 4x `create_new_age:overcharged_iron` *(after: Create: New Age)*
   > What: overcharged iron, made by charging an iron ingot in an Energiser.
   > How: power the Energiser with FE and put iron underneath it (on a depot or belt). Each ingot takes 1,000 FE.
   > Tip: overcharged metals make better wire and magnets.
45. **New Age Circuits**: 4x `create_new_age:blank_circuit`; `create_new_age:copper_circuit` *(after: Charging Metal)*
   > What: New Age's own circuit boards, used in its better machines (check JEI for uses).
   > Chemistry: real boards are an insulating base with copper traces; here quartz, stone, iron and redstone fuse into the base.
   > How: compact stone, redstone, iron and quartz over a superheated burner (blaze cake) for 4 blanks, then deploy copper wire onto one.
46. **Layered Magnets**: 4x `create_new_age:layered_magnet` *(after: Charging Metal)*
   > What: stronger magnets for New Age generators.
   > How: overcharged iron and overcharged gold in layers (check JEI).
   > Tip: a stronger field induces more current in the same coil.
47. **Thorium Reactor**: 8x `create_new_age:thorium`; `create_new_age:reactor_rod` *(after: Charging Metal, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: New Age's nuclear reactor, fuelled by thorium.
   > Chemistry: thorium-232 isn't fissile itself; it absorbs a neutron and becomes uranium-233, which is.
   > How: the rods need MI processing units (EV) in this pack, so it arrives alongside Mekanism fission. Check JEI and the Ponder for the build.
   > Tip: treat it like any reactor: cooling first, then power.
48. **Liquid Experience**: `create_enchantment_industry:mechanical_grindstone`; `create_enchantment_industry:experience_bucket` *(after: Precision)*
   > What: Enchantment Industry turns experience into a fluid you can store and pipe.
   > How: the Mechanical Grindstone strips enchantments off items; a Grindstone Drain collects the XP as fluid. Check JEI.
   > Tip: feed it the enchanted junk from your mob farm.
49. **Automated Enchanting**: `create_enchantment_industry:blaze_enchanter` *(after: Liquid Experience)*
   > What: the Blaze Enchanter spends liquid XP to enchant items automatically.
   > How: it's a smithing upgrade of a Blaze Burner with an enchanting table (check JEI). Give it an enchanting template and XP.
   > Tip: put it beside a belt and a deployer for a hands-free enchanting line.
50. **The Printer**: `create_enchantment_industry:printer` *(after: Automated Enchanting)*
   > What: the Printer copies written and enchanted books, paid for in liquid XP.
   > How: check JEI and the Ponder for the setup.
   > Tip: find a good enchanted book once, then print it as often as your XP lasts.
51. **Experience Lantern**: `create_enchantment_industry:experience_lantern` *(after: Liquid Experience)*
   > What: the Experience Lantern pulls nearby experience orbs in and stores them as liquid XP.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe. Hang it over a mob farm's kill zone and pipe its XP away.
   > Tip: pair it with the Blaze Enchanter and your farm pays for its own enchanting.
52. **Spare Burners**: 2x `create:empty_blaze_burner`; `create:blaze_cake_base` *(after: Mechanical Mixer)*
   > What: empty Blaze Burners to catch more blazes, and a Blaze Cake base ready to fill with lava.
   > Chemistry: a superheated burner runs hotter because the cake gives it richer fuel; as a rule of thumb, many reactions run about twice as fast for every 10 °C hotter.
   > How: burners are iron plates around netherrack; right-click a blaze with one, or use it on a monster spawner. The cake base is compacted egg, sugar and cinder flour (check JEI).
   > Tip: a big steam boiler wants nine or more burners. Catch them early.
53. **Fluid Valve**: `create:fluid_valve` *(after: Fluid Pipes)*
   > What: a Fluid Valve opens or closes a pipe when rotation turns it; a valve handle turns it by hand.
   > How: an iron plate and a fluid pipe (check JEI).
   > Tip: a clutch on the valve's shaft gives you a redstone-controlled pipe.
54. **Nozzle**: `create:nozzle` *(after: Encased Fan)*
   > What: a Nozzle on the front of an Encased Fan spreads its air all around instead of in a line, and pushes or pulls mobs in range.
   > How: andesite alloy and wool (check JEI).
   > Tip: a fan, a nozzle and a fire behind it make a warm room. A water source behind it, a mob wash.
55. **Take a Seat**: 1x any of `item_tag(create:seats)` *(after: Andesite Casing)*
   > What: Create seats. You can sit on them, mobs sit on them, and a seated mob (or you) is what drives a train or moving contraption.
   > How: a wooden slab and wool of any colour. Dye one seat to recolour it.
   > Tip: a villager in a seat behind train controls becomes your conductor.
56. **Andesite**: `minecraft:andesite` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: andesite is the stone Create is built on: alloy, casings and every early machine start with it.
   > How: find it in the hills or underground, or mix diorite with cobblestone.
   > Tip: andesite is a real volcanic rock, rich in plagioclase feldspar. Mine a stack.
57. **Blaze Burner**: `create:blaze_burner` *(after: Blaze Rods)*
   > What: a Blaze Burner heats a basin from below, for mixing alloys and some fluids.
   > How: make an Empty Blaze Burner (iron plates around netherrack) and right-click a blaze with it. Feed it fuel.
   > Tip: a blaze cake makes it superheated for the hottest recipes.
58. **Basin**: `create:basin` *(after: Fluid Pipes, Belts)*
   > What: the basin holds items and fluids for a press or mixer above it.
   > How: an andesite alloy (check JEI). Put it under the machine; output comes out its sides.
   > Tip: a funnel or spout on it automates the inputs.
59. **Mechanical Crafter**: `create:mechanical_crafter` *(after: Brass Casing)*
   > What: crafters join into grids for recipes too big for a crafting table, and craft by themselves.
   > How: an electron tube, brass casing and a crafting table.
   > Tip: the precision mechanism and Create's big recipes need these.
60. **Andesite Tunnel**: `create:andesite_tunnel` *(after: Belts)*
   > What: a tunnel on a belt splits items evenly to the sides and to belts beside it.
   > How: andesite alloy and dried kelp.
61. **Brass Tunnel**: `create:brass_tunnel` *(after: Belts, Brass)*
   > What: a brass tunnel splits by filter and by rule (round robin, prefer nearest and so on).
   > How: brass, dried kelp and an electron tube (check JEI).
62. **Smart Chute**: `create:smart_chute` *(after: Chutes)*
   > What: a smart chute only lets the filtered items fall.
   > How: a chute with brass and an electron tube (check JEI).
63. **Copper**: `minecraft:copper_ingot` *(after: Andesite)*
   > What: copper makes Create's pipes, tanks, spouts and casings.
   > How: smelt raw copper. Copper sheets come from a press.
   > Tip: copper oxidises green in air (a copper carbonate patina); wax it with honeycomb to stop it.
64. **Mechanical Pump**: `create:mechanical_pump` *(after: Fluid Pipes)*
   > What: a pump pushes fluid along pipes in the direction of its arrow.
   > How: a fluid pipe and a cogwheel.
   > Tip: faster rotation pumps faster.
65. **Smart Fluid Pipe**: `create:smart_fluid_pipe` *(after: Fluid Pipes)*
   > What: a smart pipe lets only the fluid you set pass.
   > How: a pipe with a brass plate and an electron tube (check JEI).
66. **Fluid Tank**: `create:fluid_tank` *(after: Copper)*
   > What: fluid tanks join into large tanks when placed next to and on top of each other.
   > How: copper sheets and a barrel (check JEI).
   > Tip: a tank is also the boiler for steam engines.
67. **Wrench**: `create:wrench` *(after: Andesite)*
   > What: the wrench rotates Create blocks, and sneak-click picks them up instantly.
   > How: gold plate, a cogwheel and a stick (check JEI).

### Create: Contraptions

*Bearings, pistons, pulleys and drills*

1. **Shafts**: `create:shaft` *(after: Andesite Alloy)*
   > What: Create runs on rotation, not electricity. Shafts carry it in a straight line from a source to the machines.
   > Chemistry: it's mechanics, not chemistry: power = torque x angular speed. Create shows the load as stress units (SU).
   > How: andesite alloy, 4 shafts per craft. Place them end to end.
   > Tip: hold W over any Create block to watch its Ponder.
2. **Gear Ratios**: `create:large_cogwheel`; `create:cogwheel` *(after: Cogwheels)*
   > What: a large cogwheel meshed with a small one doubles the speed (or halves it the other way).
   > Chemistry: physics, really: power is torque times speed. Gearing trades one for the other, and Create shows the trade as stress: a machine's SU cost grows with its speed.
   > How: a shaft and two planks make a large cogwheel. Place it diagonally next to a small one so the teeth mesh.
   > Tip: run slow machines (like mixers you don't need fast) at low speed to save stress.
3. **Windmills**: `create:windmill_bearing`; 8x any of `or(item(create:white_sail)item(create:sail_frame))` *(after: Cogwheels)*
   > What: a windmill bearing with sails attached spins without water.
   > How: place the bearing, build at least 8 sails onto the front of it (the Ponder shows how), and right-click the bearing.
   > Tip: more sails means more stress capacity but slower speed. Check the numbers with your goggles.
4. **Hand Crank**: `create:hand_crank` *(after: Cogwheels)*
   > What: the simplest power source: you turn it yourself.
   > How: three planks over an andesite alloy. Hold right-click on it to spin whatever it's attached to.
   > Tip: handy for testing a contraption before you build a real generator for it.
5. **Speedometer**: `create:speedometer` *(after: Gear Ratios, Andesite Casing)*
   > What: the Speedometer reads RPM; the Stressometer shows how much of your network's capacity is in use.
   > How: a compass on an andesite casing makes the speedometer (check JEI for the stressometer). Put them inline on a shaft.
   > Tip: both give a comparator signal, so a nearly full network can switch things off by redstone.
6. **Clutch**: `create:clutch` *(after: Shafts)*
   > What: a powered Clutch stops the rotation passing through it; unpowered, it passes rotation like a shaft.
   > How: andesite casing, a shaft and redstone.
   > Tip: a clutch on a lever is the off switch every machine line needs.
7. **Chain Drives**: `create:encased_chain_drive` *(after: Shafts)*
   > What: encased chain drives pass rotation between each other in a line, in any direction, like a bike chain.
   > How: an andesite casing and three iron nuggets. The Adjustable Chain Gearshift version changes speed with a redstone signal (check JEI).
   > Tip: a neat way to bring power up a wall without shafts sticking out.
8. **Create: Connected**: `create_connected:brass_gearbox`; `create_connected:kinetic_bridge` *(after: Windmills)*
   > What: Create: Connected adds small conveniences: compact gearboxes, a kinetic bridge that carries rotation across gaps, and more.
   > How: check JEI for everything the mod adds.
   > Tip: the kinetic bridge saves long runs of shafts.
9. **Kinetic Battery**: `create_connected:kinetic_battery` *(after: Create: Connected)*
   > What: the Kinetic Battery charges from rotation and gives it back later, so a windmill's power isn't wasted when nothing is running.
   > How: check JEI and its Ponder scene (hold W over it). Put it on a shaft line to charge it.
   > Tip: a charged battery can be picked up and moved, like a wind-up spring.
10. **Mechanical Bearing**: `create:mechanical_bearing` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a bearing turns the blocks attached to its face into a moving 'contraption': doors, rotors, fans, ferris wheels.
   > How: a wooden slab, an andesite casing and a shaft. Build onto its face, power it, and right-click to start.
   > Tip: moving blocks keep working: a spinning contraption can carry drills, harvesters and seats.
11. **Clockwork Bearing**: `create:clockwork_bearing` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: the Clockwork Bearing points its contraption at the current in-game time, like the hands of a clock.
   > How: a wooden slab, a brass casing and an electron tube. Build an hour hand on it, and a second layer for the minute hand.
   > Tip: a giant clock tower is a classic Create build.
12. **Super Glue**: `create:super_glue` *(after: Andesite)*
   > What: Super Glue marks blocks that should move together when a piston, bearing or gantry moves them.
   > How: slime, an iron plate and an iron nugget. Click two corners to glue the whole box between them.
   > Tip: glue is reusable: a glued area costs no extra glue to resize.
13. **Rope Pulley**: `create:rope_pulley` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: the Rope Pulley lowers and raises a contraption on a rope, which makes a simple lift.
   > How: an andesite casing, wool and an iron plate. Glue a platform under it and power it.
   > Tip: the brass Elevator Pulley (check JEI) adds floor buttons and stops at contacts.
14. **Mechanical Piston**: 1x any of `or(item(create:mechanical_piston)item(create:sticky_mechanical_piston))` *(after: Piston Poles)*
   > What: a mechanical piston pushes and pulls glued blocks along a straight line, as far as its poles reach.
   > How: a wooden slab, an andesite casing and an extension pole. Put poles behind the piston head; each pole adds one block of travel.
   > Tip: rotation direction decides push or pull, so a gearshift reverses it.
15. **Mechanical Drill**: `create:mechanical_drill` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a moving Drill breaks the blocks in front of it and drops them.
   > How: andesite casing, alloy and iron (check JEI). Mount it on a piston, bearing or gantry.
   > Tip: a drill on a slow bearing makes a cobblestone or tree farm.
16. **Gantries**: `create:gantry_carriage`; `create:gantry_shaft` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a Gantry Carriage runs along a powered gantry shaft, carrying its contraption with it, with no length limit.
   > How: gantry shafts are alloy and redstone; the carriage is a slab, a casing and a cogwheel. Power the shaft and the carriage moves.
   > Tip: gantries can carry other gantries, which makes an X-Y frame for a big drill or quarry.
17. **Minecart Contraptions**: `create:cart_assembler` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a Cart Assembler on a rail turns a passing minecart and the blocks glued to it into a moving contraption.
   > How: andesite alloy, redstone and logs. Place it as a rail, build on top, then send a minecart through with the assembler powered.
   > Tip: a minecart contraption with a drill digs its own tunnel along the track.
18. **Mechanical Saw**: `create:mechanical_saw` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a still saw over a belt cuts logs into planks and acts as a stonecutter; on a contraption it fells whole trees.
   > How: iron plates, an iron ingot and an andesite casing. Set its target recipe with a filter if it has several.
   > Tip: a row of saws on a bearing makes a tree farm that never misses a log.
19. **Steam Engines**: `create:steam_engine`; `create:fluid_tank`; `create:shaft` *(after: Cogwheels)*
   > What: Create's boiler: a fluid tank full of water, heated by Blaze Burners, drives steam engines on its sides.
   > Chemistry: water expands about 1,600 times when it boils. That pressure pushes the pistons.
   > How: pump water into the tank, put fuelled Blaze Burners underneath, and place engines on its sides with a shaft in front. Check the Ponder.
   > Tip: a bigger tank and more burners raise the boiler level. Goggles show what's limiting it.
20. **Cardboard**: `create:cardboard` *(after: Belts, Mechanical Mixer)*
   > What: cardboard, for Create's package logistics.
   > Chemistry: paper and card are mats of cellulose fibres; water lets the fibres bond as it dries, which is why pulp holds together.
   > How: mix 4 pulpable items (like sticks or sugar cane; check JEI) with 250 mB of water for pulp, then press the pulp into cardboard.
21. **Packagers**: `create:packager` *(after: Cardboard)*
   > What: a Packager boxes items from the inventory behind it into a package with an address, or unpacks packages addressed to it.
   > How: a cardboard block, iron ingots and redstone. Put a sign or name on it for its address (see the Ponder).
   > Tip: packages ride belts, chutes and chain conveyors like any other item.
22. **Package Frogport**: `create:package_frogport` *(after: Chain Conveyor)*
   > What: chain conveyors carry packages through the air; a Package Frogport tongues them off the chain at the right stop.
   > How: a frogport is a slimeball, an item vault and andesite alloy; a chain conveyor is a large cogwheel in andesite casings. Link chains with iron chains.
   > Tip: a chain network with frogports at each base is a whole-base mail system.
23. **Stock Link**: `create:stock_link` *(after: A Package)*
   > What: a Stock Link reports what a packager can reach; a Stock Ticker lets you browse that stock and order items to be packed and sent.
   > How: a transmitter (lightning rod, copper plates, redstone) on an item vault makes the link; add glass and gold for the ticker.
   > Tip: put the ticker by your workbench and order ingredients without walking to storage.
24. **Factory Gauges**: 2x `create:factory_gauge` *(after: Stock Link)*
   > What: Factory Gauges watch your stock and request ingredients for a recipe whenever a target amount runs low.
   > How: a stock link and a precision mechanism make 2. Place them on a packager and link them in their panel (see the Ponder).
   > Tip: chain gauges together and one order can run a whole production line.
25. **Speed Controller**: `create:rotation_speed_controller` *(after: Speedometer, Precision, Brass Casing)*
   > What: the Rotation Speed Controller sets the speed of the cogwheel on top of it to any RPM you choose.
   > How: a precision mechanism over a brass casing. Power it from below and set the speed on its face.
   > Tip: faster costs more stress, so only speed up what needs it.
26. **Train Casing**: `create:railway_casing` *(after: Brass Casing, Sturdy Sheets)*
   > What: train casing is the base block for stations, controls, signals and bogeys.
   > How: right-click a brass casing with a sturdy sheet.
   > Tip: right-clicking a track with train casing places a bogey: the wheels your train sits on.
27. **Train Track**: 16x `create:track` *(after: Deployer)*
   > What: Create's train track, which can curve, slope and cross.
   > How: sequenced assembly on stone slabs (the 'sleepers'): deploy an iron or zinc nugget, deploy another, then press. Check JEI.
   > Tip: click one track end, then another, to lay a curve or slope between them.
28. **Train Station**: `create:track_station` *(after: Train Casing, Train Track)*
   > What: a Train Station assembles a train from the casing, bogeys and blocks on the track beside it; Train Controls let you drive it.
   > How: a station is train casing and a compass; controls are a lever, train casing and a precision mechanism.
   > Tip: stand at the station's GUI and press assemble once the controls face the way you want to go.
29. **Your First Train**: `create:schedule`; 1x any of `item_tag(create:seats)` *(after: Building a Train)*
   > A machine that carries itself across the world. You used to move whole mountains like this.
   > What: a Train Schedule tells a train where to stop and when to leave, so it runs by itself.
   > How: a sturdy sheet and paper make 4. Write stops in it and give it to the conductor (a mob in a seat behind the controls).
   > Tip: a train with portable storage interfaces at each station moves ore and goods on its own.
30. **Signals**: `create:track_signal` *(after: Building a Train)*
   > What: signals split a line into sections so two trains never share one. Real railways use the same 'block' idea.
   > How: train casing and an electron tube make 4. Place them on the track at each junction.
   > Tip: check the Ponder for chain signals at crossings.
31. **Water Wheels**: 1x any of `or(item(create:water_wheel)item(create:large_water_wheel))` *(after: Cogwheels)*
   > What: a 3x3 water wheel. It turns at half the speed of the small one but gives more stress capacity in total (check with goggles).
   > Chemistry: physics again: a bigger wheel catches the flow further from its axle, so the same water gives more torque.
   > How: a water wheel ringed with planks. Give it flowing water across the whole face.
   > Tip: follow it with a large cogwheel to get the speed back.
32. **Adjustable Chain Gearshift**: `create:adjustable_chain_gearshift` *(after: Chain Drives)*
   > What: a chain drive that changes its speed ratio with the strength of a redstone signal.
   > How: an encased chain drive with an electron tube (check JEI).
   > Tip: a comparator on a chest makes a line speed up as the chest fills.
33. **Mechanical Plough**: `create:mechanical_plough` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: the Mechanical Plough tills dirt and breaks small blocks as a contraption moves; Radial Chassis grabs blocks around it in a ring, for bearing contraptions.
   > How: plough: iron plates, andesite alloy and a casing. Radial chassis: logs and andesite alloy, three at a time (check JEI).
   > Tip: a plough leading a row of harvesters and seed deployers is a field that farms itself.
34. **Portable Interfaces**: `create:portable_fluid_interface`; `create:portable_storage_interface` *(after: Copper Casing, Contraptions)*
   > What: a pair of Portable Storage (or Fluid) Interfaces, one on the contraption and one on the ground, swap items or fluids whenever they line up.
   > How: an andesite casing (items) or copper casing (fluids) with a chute (check JEI).
   > Tip: a train with fluid interfaces can haul acid from a remote plant without a single pipe.
35. **Display Links and Nixie Tubes**: `create:display_link`; 4x `create:nixie_tube` *(after: Stock Link, Electron Tubes)*
   > What: a Display Link reads a block (a stockpile, a tank, a station, a speedometer) and writes it onto Nixie Tubes, signs or display boards.
   > How: a transmitter on brass casing makes the link; two electron tubes make four nixie tubes (check JEI).
   > Tip: link a tank of seed oil to a nixie row and you'll see the level from across the room.
36. **Re-Packager**: `create:repackager` *(after: Packagers)*
   > What: a Re-Packager opens incoming packages and repacks their contents, so a recipe's ingredients arrive at a machine in one box.
   > How: a Packager converted in the crafting grid (check JEI).
   > Tip: use it in front of a mechanical crafter that needs many different items at once.
37. **Train Fittings**: `create:track_observer`; 2x `create:train_door` *(after: Building a Train)*
   > What: Train Doors and Trapdoors open only when the train is stopped at a station. A Train Observer gives a redstone signal when a train passes over it.
   > How: a wooden door or trapdoor with train casing; the observer is train casing and a pressure plate (check JEI).
   > Tip: a train observer before a station can open a loading gate in time.
38. **Cogwheels**: 1x any of `or(item(create:cogwheel)item(create:large_cogwheel))` *(after: Shafts)*
   > What: cogwheels hand rotation to the cogs next to them, so it can turn corners.
   > How: a shaft and planks. Large cogs mesh diagonally with small ones.
   > Tip: any cog counts here.
39. **Gearbox**: `create:gearbox` *(after: Shafts)*
   > What: a gearbox passes rotation out of all four of its side faces.
   > How: four cogwheels around an andesite casing.
   > Tip: it reverses the direction on opposite sides; check with goggles.
40. **Gearshift**: `create:gearshift` *(after: Shafts)*
   > What: a powered Gearshift reverses the rotation passing through it.
   > How: andesite casing, a cogwheel and redstone.
   > Tip: pistons and gantries need it to come back home.
41. **Sequenced Gearshift**: `create:sequenced_gearshift` *(after: Gearshift)*
   > What: runs a list of steps: turn so many degrees, wait, reverse, repeat.
   > How: brass casing, a cogwheel and an electron tube (check JEI).
   > Tip: perfect for doors and drawbridges.
42. **Vertical Gearbox**: `create:vertical_gearbox` *(after: Shafts)*
   > What: a gearbox turned on its side, passing rotation up and down.
   > How: a gearbox in the crafting grid.
43. **Stressometer**: `create:stressometer` *(after: Gear Ratios, Andesite Casing)*
   > What: shows how much of your network's stress capacity is in use.
   > How: check JEI. Put it inline on a shaft.
   > Tip: it gives a comparator signal: switch things off before the network stalls.
44. **Building a Train**: `create:controls`; `create:super_glue`; `create:railway_casing` *(after: Train Station)*
   > What: a train is glued blocks on bogeys, with controls at the front.
   > How: put a railway casing on the track to make a bogey, build on it, glue it, place the controls and click the station to assemble.
   > Tip: see the Ponder on the station for each step.
45. **Train Controls**: `create:controls` *(after: Building a Train)*
   > What: the controls let you drive a train by hand, or seat a conductor for a schedule.
   > How: check JEI.
46. **More Glue**: `create:super_glue` *(after: Building a Train)*
   > What: each carriage of a train is glued on its own bogeys.
   > How: glue each carriage before you assemble it.
47. **Contraptions**: `create:super_glue`; `create:andesite_casing` *(after: Andesite Casing, Super Glue)*
   > What: a contraption is a group of glued blocks moved by a piston, bearing, gantry, pulley or cart.
   > How: glue the blocks to each other and to the mover's face, then power the mover.
   > Tip: drills, saws and harvesters on a contraption work as it moves.
48. **Linear Chassis**: `create:linear_chassis` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a chassis pulls in the blocks next to it in a line, without glue.
   > How: andesite alloy and logs. Use slime on a face to make it sticky.
49. **Radial Chassis**: `create:radial_chassis` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a radial chassis pulls in a circle of blocks around it: windmill sails, doors, platforms.
   > How: andesite alloy and logs (check JEI).
50. **Mechanical Harvester**: `create:mechanical_harvester` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: a moving Harvester picks grown crops and leaves the plant to regrow.
   > How: andesite casing, alloy and iron plates (check JEI).
   > Tip: a slow piston sweep over a field is a full farm.
51. **Piston Poles**: `create:piston_extension_pole` *(after: Contraptions)*
   > What: extension poles behind a mechanical piston set how far it pushes.
   > How: andesite alloy and planks (check JEI).
52. **A Package**: 1x any of `item_tag(create:packages)` *(after: Packagers)*
   > What: a package is a box of items with an address on it.
   > How: a Packager boxes whatever is in the inventory behind it.
53. **Chain Conveyor**: `create:chain_conveyor` *(after: A Package)*
   > What: chain conveyors carry packages between them on a chain.
   > How: a large cogwheel in andesite casing; link two with iron chains.
54. **Postbox**: 1x any of `item_tag(create:postboxes)` *(after: A Package)*
   > What: a postbox sends and receives packages by train.
   > How: check JEI. Put it next to a station.
55. **Stock Ticker**: `create:stock_ticker` *(after: Stock Link)*
   > What: the ticker shows what your linked packagers can reach and lets you order items to be packed and sent.
   > How: a stock link with glass and gold (check JEI).
56. **Table Cloth**: 1x any of `item_tag(create:table_cloths)` *(after: Stock Ticker)*
   > What: a table cloth on a table shows items for sale; a stock ticker behind it fills the orders.
   > How: wool and an item (check JEI).
   > Tip: on a shared server, it's a real shop.

### Mekanism

*Osmium, infusion and gases: Mekanism's machines, factories, circuits and logistics. Reactors and add-ons are on the next page.*

1. **The Mekanism Way**: checkmark *(after: Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > Osmium hums in your hand. You remember metals that drank other substances and grew stronger.
   > What: Mekanism is a machine mod built on infusion and gases: soak a metal in carbon, redstone, diamond or refined obsidian and it becomes an alloy; pipe gases between machines and they become chemistry.
   > How: every machine comes in tiers (basic, advanced, elite, ultimate). In this pack each tier's control circuit needs the matching MI circuit.
   > Tip: this page is a side path. The main-path Mekanism quests are linked on the left; click one to jump there. Reactors, More Machine and Mekanism Extras are on the next page, Power and Beyond.
2. **Energy Tablet**: `mekanism:energy_tablet` *(after: Infused Alloy)*
   > What: a portable FE store. It is also a crafting part in the Robit, the Wind Generator, lasers, Free Runners and the Portable Teleporter.
   > How: gold ingots, redstone and Infused Alloy (check JEI).
   > Tip: make a few at once; you'll keep needing them.
3. **Reinforced Alloy**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_reinforced` *(after: The Mekanism Way, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: the second Mekanism alloy, used in elite circuits, lasers and the Solar Neutron Activator.
   > Chemistry: real alloys work the same way: a few percent of a second element (carbon in steel, chromium in stainless) changes the metal's properties.
   > How: Metallurgic Infuser: Infused Alloy + diamond infusion (from diamonds or diamond dust; check JEI).
4. **Atomic Alloy**: 4x `mekanism:alloy_atomic` *(after: Reinforced Alloy)*
   > What: the top Mekanism alloy, needed for ultimate circuits, teleportation cores and the Robit.
   > How: first infuse obsidian dust with diamond to get refined obsidian dust, then infuse Reinforced Alloy with refined obsidian.
   > Tip: crush obsidian in the Crusher or an MI macerator for obsidian dust.
5. **Universal Cable**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_universal_cable)item(mekanism:advanced_universal_cable)item(mekanism:elite_universal_cable)item(mekanism:ultimate_universal_cable))` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: Universal Cable carries FE between generators, cubes and machines. Any tier counts here.
   > Chemistry: a cable is a conductor: electrons drift through the metal, and its resistance turns a little of the power into heat (P = I²R).
   > How: steel with redstone, 8 per craft. Higher tiers wrap 8 of the tier below around an alloy (check JEI).
   > Tip: cables of one type join into one network. Colour them with a Configurator to keep two networks apart.
6. **Seismic Survey**: `mekanism:seismic_vibrator`; `mekanism:seismic_reader` *(after: Universal Cable)*
   > What: the Seismic Vibrator shakes the ground beneath it; the Seismic Reader then shows every block straight down to bedrock.
   > Chemistry: real prospectors use reflection seismology: sound waves bounce off layers of different density, and the echo times map oil and ore bodies.
   > How: vibrator: tin, lapis, Basic Control Circuits and a steel casing; reader: steel, lapis and an Energy Tablet (check JEI).
   > Tip: rich ore deposits sit at metal-specific depths. Survey before you dig.
7. **Nutritional Paste**: `mekanism:nutritional_liquifier`; `mekanism:canteen` *(after: Universal Cable)*
   > What: the Nutritional Liquifier turns food into nutritional paste; a Canteen carries it and feeds you when you drink.
   > Chemistry: food energy is chemical energy in carbohydrates, fats and proteins. Mashing food changes its form, not its calories.
   > How: liquifier: redstone, bowls, Basic Control Circuits and a steel casing. Canteen: tin and a bowl (check JEI). The MekaSuit has a module that drinks paste for you.
8. **Chargepad**: `mekanism:chargepad` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: the Chargepad charges the FE items in your inventory (and a Robit) while you stand on it.
   > How: polished blackstone pressure plates over steel and an Energy Tablet (check JEI). Feed it power from below.
   > Tip: put one in front of your storage. Every visit tops up your tools.
9. **Osmium Armour**: `mekanismtools:osmium_helmet`; `mekanismtools:osmium_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:osmium_leggings`; `mekanismtools:osmium_boots` *(after: The Mekanism Way)*
   > What: Mekanism Tools adds a full armour set for each of its metals. Osmium is the first, and tougher than iron.
   > Chemistry: osmium is the densest natural element (22.6 g/cm³). Real osmium is brittle and its oxide, OsO₄, is volatile and very toxic, so nobody actually wears it.
   > How: osmium ingots in the usual armour shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: bronze, steel and lapis sets exist too; see JEI for their stats.
10. **Refined Obsidian Armour**: `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_helmet`; `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_leggings`; `mekanismtools:refined_obsidian_boots` *(after: Osmium Armour, The Ultimate Paxel)*
   > What: the strongest Mekanism Tools armour: high protection and toughness, good until the MekaSuit.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass: lava cooled too fast for crystals to form. Infusing it with diamond and pressing it with osmium makes Mekanism's refined form.
   > How: refined obsidian ingots from the Osmium Compressor, in armour shapes (check JEI).
11. **Refined Glowstone Armour**: `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_helmet`; `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_chestplate`; `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_leggings`; `mekanismtools:refined_glowstone_boots` *(after: Refined Obsidian Armour)*
   > What: the other Osmium Compressor metal as an armour set. Check JEI for how it compares with refined obsidian.
   > Chemistry: real glow-in-the-dark materials store energy in their crystal and release it as light (phosphorescence); glowstone is Minecraft's version.
   > How: Osmium Compressor: glowstone dust + osmium → refined glowstone ingots, then armour shapes.
12. **Osmium**: `mekanism:ingot_osmium` *(after: The Mekanism Way)*
   > What: osmium is the metal in almost every Mekanism machine, cable and upgrade.
   > Chemistry: osmium (Os, element 76) is a platinum-group metal and the densest element known, about 22.6 g/cm³.
   > How: mine osmium ore underground and smelt it, or run it through your ore line for more per ore.
   > Tip: you will want stacks of it. Put osmium at the top of your ore processing list.
13. **Reading a Machine**: checkmark *(after: The Mekanism Way)*
   > What: every Mekanism machine has a side configuration tab. Each colour is a slot or tank, and each side of the block can be set to one of them.
   > How: open a machine and click the side tab on its GUI, or use the Configurator in the world. Multiblock layouts are in Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI.
   > Tip: auto-eject on the output side saves you a pump or a transporter.
14. **Metallurgic Infuser**: `mekanism:metallurgic_infuser` *(after: Osmium)*
   > A furnace that adds rather than burns. Your hands remember this kind of patience.
   > What: the Metallurgic Infuser pushes carbon, redstone, diamond or refined obsidian into a metal. It is how every Mekanism alloy and steel starts.
   > Chemistry: carburising is real: hot iron soaks up carbon from its surroundings and becomes steel. Mekanism uses the same idea for every alloy.
   > How: iron, osmium, redstone and a furnace (check JEI). Put the infuse material in the left slot and the metal in the middle.
15. **Infused Alloy**: `mekanism:alloy_infused` *(after: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: the first Mekanism alloy. It goes into energy tablets, advanced circuits, upgrades and the second tier of everything.
   > How: Metallurgic Infuser: iron ingot + redstone infusion.
   > Tip: enriched redstone from the Enrichment Chamber gives far more infuse per item.
16. **Basic Control Circuit**: `mekanism:basic_control_circuit` *(after: Metallurgic Infuser, Mekanism Circuits)*
   > What: the circuit inside every basic Mekanism machine.
   > How: in this pack it needs an MI analog circuit (LV) with osmium and Basic Alloy (check JEI). The infuser shortcut is removed.
   > Tip: make a stack. Almost every quest on this page eats a few.
17. **Steel**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:ingots/steel)` *(after: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: steel ingots: the frame of every Mekanism casing, cable and tank.
   > Chemistry: steel is iron with about 0.2-2% carbon. The carbon atoms sit between the iron atoms and stop the layers from sliding, which makes it harder.
   > How: infuse iron with carbon to get enriched iron, infuse that again into steel dust and smelt it. Steel from your MI line works too.
   > Tip: any steel ingot counts: the pack unifies them.
18. **The Basic Tier**: `minecraft:redstone`; `mekanism:basic_control_circuit` *(after: Basic Control Circuit, Infused Alloy)*
   > What: every Mekanism block comes in four tiers: basic, advanced, elite and ultimate. Each tier pairs an alloy with a control circuit.
   > How: the basic tier runs on redstone and Basic Control Circuits.
   > Tip: the tier of a factory, cube or tank shows in its name and its colour stripe.
19. **The Advanced Tier**: `mekanism:alloy_infused`; `mekanism:advanced_control_circuit` *(after: The Basic Tier, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the advanced tier pairs Infused Alloy with the Advanced Control Circuit.
   > How: the circuit needs an MI electronic circuit (MV) in this pack.
   > Tip: advanced cables, tanks and factories all use this pair.
20. **The Elite Tier**: `mekanism:alloy_reinforced`; `mekanism:elite_control_circuit` *(after: The Advanced Tier, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the elite tier pairs Reinforced Alloy (diamond infusion) with the Elite Control Circuit.
   > How: the circuit needs an MI digital circuit (HV) in this pack.
   > Tip: diamond infuse comes from diamonds or diamond dust; enrich it first for more per diamond.
21. **The Ultimate Tier**: `mekanism:alloy_atomic`; `mekanism:ultimate_control_circuit` *(after: The Elite Tier, EV: Processing Units)*
   > The top of the ladder. You remember when four steps felt like a long climb.
   > What: the ultimate tier pairs Atomic Alloy (refined obsidian infusion) with the Ultimate Control Circuit.
   > How: the circuit needs an MI processing unit (EV) in this pack.
22. **Solar Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:solar_generator` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: a small generator that makes FE in daylight under open sky.
   > Chemistry: a photovoltaic cell is a silicon junction: light knocks electrons loose and the junction pushes them one way, making a current.
   > How: solar panels, an Energy Tablet and osmium (check JEI).
23. **Advanced Solar Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:advanced_solar_generator` *(after: Solar Generator)*
   > What: four solar generators on a frame, with much more output.
   > How: solar generators, Infused Alloy and iron (check JEI).
   > Tip: it works in the rain too, just slower.
24. **Heat Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:heat_generator` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: burns fuel or sits by lava and turns heat into FE.
   > Chemistry: a heat engine needs a hot side and a cold side; the bigger the difference, the more work it can do.
   > How: iron, wood, copper and a furnace (check JEI).
25. **Bio-Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:bio_generator` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: burns bio fuel (crushed plants) for FE.
   > Chemistry: plants store sunlight as sugars: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. Burning them gives that energy back.
   > How: redstone, bio fuel and an Energy Tablet (check JEI).
26. **Wind Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:wind_generator` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: a turbine that makes more FE the higher you build it.
   > Chemistry: a turbine's power grows with the cube of wind speed, so a little more wind gives a lot more power.
   > How: an Energy Tablet, osmium and circuits (check JEI). Put it on a tall tower.
27. **Energy Cube**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_energy_cube)item(mekanism:advanced_energy_cube)item(mekanism:elite_energy_cube)item(mekanism:ultimate_energy_cube))` *(after: Energy Tablet)*
   > What: a block battery that stores FE and keeps it when broken. Any tier counts.
   > How: redstone, iron, Energy Tablets and a steel casing (check JEI).
   > Tip: set its sides in the GUI: one input, the rest output.

### Mekanism: Machines

*Mekanism, continued: Machines*

1. **Refined Obsidian**: `mekanism:ingot_refined_obsidian` *(after: Osmium Compressor, Obsidian Dusts)*
   > What: refined obsidian ingots: very hard, blast-proof metal for teleporters, the Robit and endgame tools.
   > How: the Osmium Compressor presses refined obsidian dust with liquid osmium into ingots. It needs an Advanced Control Circuit (MV).
   > Tip: refined glowstone ingots come from the same machine: glowstone dust plus osmium.
2. **Advanced Control Circuit**: `mekanism:advanced_control_circuit` *(after: Steel Casing, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the circuit for every advanced-tier Mekanism block: factories, cubes, tanks, the Purification Chamber, and in this pack the whole 4x/5x ore line (injection, dissolution, washer, crystallizer).
   > How: an MI electronic circuit above two Infused Alloys and a Basic Control Circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: the old infuser shortcut for circuits is removed in this pack. Circuits follow MI's voltage tiers.
3. **Elite Control Circuit**: `mekanism:elite_control_circuit` *(after: Advanced Control Circuit, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the circuit for elite-tier blocks, the Combiner, the Security Desk and the Solar Neutron Activator.
   > How: an MI digital circuit above two Reinforced Alloys and an Advanced Control Circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: HV comes with polyethylene on the main path. Make a stack of these before upgrading factories.
4. **Ultimate Control Circuit**: `mekanism:ultimate_control_circuit` *(after: Elite Control Circuit, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: the circuit behind Mekanism's best blocks: the Isotopic Centrifuge, QIO, the Quantum Entangloporter, the Dimensional Stabilizer, the MekaSuit and the Meka-Tool.
   > How: an MI processing unit above two Atomic Alloys and an Elite Control Circuit (check JEI).
   > Tip: this unlocks the rest of the page: ultimate factories, QIO, More Machine's big machines and Mekanism Extras.
5. **Teleportation Core**: 2x `mekanism:teleportation_core` *(after: Refined Obsidian, Atomic Alloy)*
   > What: the part inside teleporters, the Digital Miner, QIO drive arrays and the Quantum Entangloporter.
   > How: Atomic Alloy, gold ingots, a diamond and ender pearls (check JEI).
   > Tip: you'll need at least four of these for this page alone. Automate Atomic Alloy early.
6. **Teleporter**: `mekanism:teleporter`; 9x `mekanism:teleporter_frame` *(after: Teleportation Core)*
   > What: a frame-and-controller portal that links to other teleporters, even across dimensions.
   > How: the controller is a Teleportation Core in steel casings with basic circuits. Frames are refined obsidian around refined glowstone. Build a 3x4 frame with the controller in it (check JEI).
   > Tip: set both ends to the same frequency, and give the sending end plenty of power.
7. **Dimensional Stabilizer**: `mekanism:dimensional_stabilizer` *(after: Refined Obsidian, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: Mekanism's chunk loader. It keeps chunks around it running while you're away, so your factories never pause.
   > How: refined obsidian, Atomic Alloy, Ultimate Control Circuits (EV) and a diamond block (check JEI). Pick the chunks in its GUI.
   > Tip: load only what you need. Every loaded chunk costs server time.
8. **Quantum Entangloporter**: 2x `mekanism:quantum_entangloporter` *(after: Teleportation Core, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: two Entangloporters on the same frequency act as one block: energy, items, fluids, chemicals and heat go in one and out the other, across any distance or dimension.
   > Chemistry: real quantum entanglement can't carry information or matter faster than light (the no-communication theorem). Mekanism takes a little artistic licence.
   > How: refined obsidian, Atomic Alloy, Ultimate Control Circuits (EV) and a Teleportation Core (check JEI).
   > Tip: a pair is the easiest way to pipe uranium hexafluoride or D-T fuel from a remote plant to your base.
9. **Energized Smelter**: `mekanism:energized_smelter` *(after: Steel Casing)*
   > What: Mekanism's electric furnace. It smelts anything a furnace can, takes upgrades, and is the base of the smelting factory.
   > Chemistry: electric heating is Joule heating: current through a resistance makes heat (P = I²R). No fuel, no smoke.
   > How: Basic Alloy, glass, a Basic Control Circuit and a steel casing (check JEI).
10. **Basic Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_smelting_factory)item(mekanism:basic_enriching_factory)item(mekanism:basic_crushing_factory)item(mekanism:basic_compressing_factory)item(mekanism:basic_combining_factory)item(mekanism:basic_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:basic_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:basic_infusing_factory)item(mekanism:basic_sawing_factory))` *(after: Energized Smelter)*
   > What: a factory is a machine with several slots that work in parallel. A basic factory runs 3 operations at once.
   > How: craft any single machine (Energized Smelter, Enrichment Chamber, Crusher...) with Basic Control Circuits and Basic Alloy. Any factory type counts.
   > Tip: factories sort their own inputs with auto-sort in the GUI, so one input pipe is enough.
11. **Advanced Factory**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:advanced_smelting_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_enriching_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_crushing_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_compressing_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_combining_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_purifying_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_injecting_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_infusing_factory)item(mekanism:advanced_sawing_factory))` *(after: Basic Factory)*
   > What: 5 parallel slots, and faster with upgrades.
   > How: upgrade a basic factory in the crafting grid with Advanced Control Circuits, Infused Alloy and osmium, or use a Tier Installer on a placed one.
