## Chemistry

### The Periodic Table

*Rebuild the table, group by group. Each column shares a chemistry, because each shares an outer-electron arrangement.*

1. **Reading the Table**: checkmark *(after: First Entries in the Periodic Table)*
   > You remember this chart. You used to know every box by heart.
   > What: the periodic table orders the elements by proton number. Rows are periods; columns are groups.
   > Chemistry: elements in the same group have the same number of outer (valence) electrons, so they react alike.
   > How: press U on any element in JEI to see which blocks the Dissolver turns into it.
   > Tip: this chapter is a side path. Nothing in the main story waits on it, but it pays well.
2. **Alkali Metals**: 8x `chemlib:lithium`; 8x `chemlib:sodium`; 8x `chemlib:potassium` *(after: Reading the Table)*
   > What: lithium, sodium and potassium, the softest and most reactive metals.
   > Chemistry: one valence electron, easily lost. Sodium fizzes on water (2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂); potassium burns lilac.
   > How: end stone gives lithium; lapis lazuli gives sodium (the mineral lazurite is a sodium aluminosilicate). Plants give potassium.
   > Tip: check JEI with U on each element. Many common blocks hide small amounts.
3. **Alkaline Earth Metals**: 4x `chemlib:beryllium`; 8x `chemlib:magnesium`; 8x `chemlib:calcium` *(after: Alkali Metals)*
   > What: beryllium, magnesium and calcium: lighter structural metals and the stuff of bones and limestone.
   > Chemistry: two valence electrons, so they form 2+ ions. Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is limestone; magnesium burns blinding white.
   > How: andesite and bone give calcium (bone via hydroxylapatite, the mineral in teeth). Beryllium and magnesium come out of their compounds: check JEI.
4. **Transition Metals**: 16x `chemlib:iron`; 16x `chemlib:copper`; 8x `chemlib:nickel`; 8x `chemlib:zinc`; 4x `chemlib:gold` *(after: Alkaline Earth Metals)*
   > What: the hard, conductive metals behind every machine you've built.
   > Chemistry: their d-orbitals fill across the row. That's why they form coloured compounds and make good catalysts.
   > How: dissolve ingots, nuggets or dusts of each metal.
   > Tip: ore you already process gives nuggets and dust. Dissolve the spares, not your ingots.
5. **Post-Transition Metals**: 8x `chemlib:aluminum`; 8x `chemlib:tin`; 8x `chemlib:lead`; 4x `chemlib:indium` *(after: Transition Metals)*
   > What: aluminum, tin, lead and indium: softer, lower-melting metals just right of the transition block.
   > Chemistry: indium tin oxide is the clear conductor in every touchscreen. Lead is dense enough to stop X-rays.
   > How: diorite dissolves into tin and indium. Aluminum and lead come from their ingots, dusts and minerals (check JEI).
   > Perk: hold one of each of these four elements and your body remembers them: +2 armor toughness, permanently. Soft metals bend instead of breaking.
   > Tip: type /warbucks elements to see which Periodic Table perks you've unlocked and what's still missing.
6. **Liquid Metals**: 4x `chemlib:mercury`; 4x `chemlib:gallium` *(after: Transition Metals)*
   > What: mercury and gallium, the two metals you can pour (almost) at room temperature.
   > Chemistry: mercury melts at −38.8 °C; gallium at 29.8 °C, below body temperature.
   > How: ender pearls and end stone dissolve into mercury. Cobblestone gives a little gallium.
7. **Challenge: The First Twenty**: `chemlib:hydrogen`; `chemlib:helium`; `chemlib:lithium`; `chemlib:beryllium`; `chemlib:boron`; `chemlib:carbon`; `chemlib:nitrogen`; `chemlib:oxygen`; `chemlib:fluorine`; `chemlib:neon`; `chemlib:sodium`; `chemlib:magnesium`; `chemlib:aluminum`; `chemlib:silicon`; `chemlib:phosphorus`; `chemlib:sulfur`; `chemlib:chlorine`; `chemlib:argon`; `chemlib:potassium`; `chemlib:calcium` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: one of each of elements 1 to 20, the four shortest rows of the table.
   > Chemistry: these twenty make up almost all of your body, the oceans and the air.
   > How: most come from the groups in this chapter. Boron and the noble gases need the Fusion Chamber (boron is 5: try H + Be).
   > Tip: an optional collection. Keep one of each in a chest as you go.
8. **The Coinage Metals**: 8x `chemlib:copper`; 8x `chemlib:silver`; 8x `chemlib:gold` *(after: Transition Metals)*
   > What: the three metals humans have minted into money for thousands of years.
   > Chemistry: they're unreactive enough to keep their shine. Silver is the best electrical conductor of any element.
   > How: deepslate dissolves into a little silver. Check JEI for richer sources.
9. **Metalloids**: 4x `chemlib:germanium`; 16x `chemlib:silicon`; 4x `chemlib:arsenic` *(after: Reading the Table)*
   > What: germanium, silicon and arsenic sit on the staircase between metals and non-metals.
   > Chemistry: silicon conducts a little, and a trace of arsenic (doping) controls how much. The first transistor (1947) was germanium.
   > How: sand dissolves into silicon dioxide, which dissolves again into silicon and oxygen. Blaze powder and Nether bricks give germanium.
   > Tip: you'll need a lot of silicon later, for circuits and AE2.
10. **Non-Metals**: 16x `chemlib:nitrogen`; 8x `chemlib:phosphorus`; 16x `chemlib:sulfur` *(after: Metalloids)*
   > What: nitrogen, phosphorus and sulfur. Life and industry both run on them.
   > Chemistry: nitrogen and phosphorus feed every crop; sulfur becomes sulfuric acid, the most-made chemical on Earth.
   > How: check JEI with U. Nether blocks are a good place to look for sulfur.
11. **Chalcogens**: 16x `chemlib:oxygen`; 16x `chemlib:sulfur`; 4x `chemlib:selenium` *(after: Non-Metals)*
   > What: oxygen, sulfur and selenium. 'Chalcogen' means 'ore-former'.
   > Chemistry: two electrons short of a full shell, so they grab metals: most ores are oxides or sulfides (Fe₂O₃, ZnS, PbS).
   > How: fish and crimson fungus dissolve into selenium. Oxygen comes from nearly everything.
   > Tip: selenium is a trace nutrient: you need a little, and too much is poisonous.
12. **Halogens**: 4x `chemlib:fluorine`; 8x `chemlib:chlorine`; 4x `chemlib:bromine`; 4x `chemlib:iodine` *(after: Chalcogens)*
   > What: fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine, the most reactive non-metals.
   > Chemistry: one electron short of full. 'Halogen' means 'salt-maker': Na + Cl → NaCl, table salt.
   > How: magma blocks give fluorine and bromine. Horn coral gives iodine (via lead iodide). Chlorine comes out of salts: check JEI.
13. **Noble Gases**: 8x `chemlib:helium`; 8x `chemlib:neon`; 8x `chemlib:argon` *(after: Halogens, Post-Transition Metals, EV: Processing Units)*
   > Two halves of the table, joined. More of the old knowledge settles into place.
   > What: helium, neon and argon, the gases that refuse to react.
   > Chemistry: a full outer shell means nothing to gain or lose. Argon shields welds from air; neon glows red in a discharge tube.
   > How: nothing dissolves into them, so build them: the Alchemistry Fusion Chamber (EV) adds proton numbers, so H + H → He. Check JEI for neon and argon.
   > Tip: real stars fuse hydrogen into helium too, though it takes them four protons, not two.
14. **Heavy Noble Gases**: 2x `chemlib:xenon`; 2x `chemlib:radon` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: xenon and radon, the heaviest natural noble gases.
   > Chemistry: in 1962 xenon was made to react (with platinum hexafluoride), ending the idea that noble gases never react. Radon is radioactive.
   > How: dragon's breath dissolves into both. That means a trip to the End.
15. **Rare Earths**: 4x `chemlib:lanthanum`; 4x `chemlib:cerium`; 4x `chemlib:neodymium` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: the lanthanides: lanthanum, cerium, neodymium and their near-identical neighbours.
   > Chemistry: they differ only in an inner (4f) shell, so their chemistry is almost the same. Neodymium makes the strongest permanent magnets.
   > How: check JEI for sources. The Alchemistry Fusion Chamber can also build them from lighter elements.
16. **Actinides**: 4x `chemlib:thorium`; 8x `chemlib:uranium`; 4x `chemlib:plutonium` *(after: Noble Gases, Transmutation by Neutron)*
   > What: thorium, uranium and plutonium, the fuels of the nuclear age.
   > Chemistry: every actinide is radioactive. Plutonium barely exists in nature: you made it by firing neutrons at uranium.
   > How: dissolve uranium and thorium materials. Plutonium comes from your fission reactor's waste.
17. **Isotopes: Heavy Water**: `mekanism:electric_pump`; `mekanism:upgrade_filter`; `mekanism:heavy_water_bucket` *(after: Alkali Metals, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: heavy water, D₂O: water made with deuterium, hydrogen with an extra neutron.
   > Chemistry: isotopes have the same protons (so the same chemistry) but different neutrons. About 1 in 6,400 hydrogen atoms is deuterium.
   > How: put a Filter Upgrade in a Mekanism Electric Pump and pump from water. It pulls out heavy water instead.
   > Tip: deuterium is half of fusion fuel. You'll want this again in the Power chapter.
18. **Superheavy Elements**: `chemlib:tennessine` *(after: Rare Earths, Actinides)*
   > What: tennessine, element 117. Nothing in the world dissolves into it; you have to build it.
   > Chemistry: real labs make superheavy elements by smashing nuclei together; only a handful of atoms have ever existed.
   > How: the Alchemistry Fusion Chamber joins two elements, adding their proton numbers. Check JEI for the pairs that reach 117.
   > Tip: one more step after this: add hydrogen (1) to tennessine (117) and you get 118.
19. **Element 118**: `chemlib:oganesson` *(after: Superheavy Elements, The Complete Periodic Table)*
   > The last box on the table. You remember now: you once named these.
   > What: oganesson, the heaviest element ever made.
   > Chemistry: in reality it lasts under a millisecond. Here it sits in your inventory, which is the kind of thing demigods can do.
   > How: fuse tennessine with hydrogen (or any pair adding to 118) in the Fusion Chamber.
20. **Covalent Bonds: CO₂**: 4x `chemlib:carbon_dioxide` *(after: Non-Metals)*
   > What: carbon dioxide, your first compound in this chapter.
   > Chemistry: C + O₂ → CO₂. Non-metals don't hand electrons over; they share them in covalent bonds (O=C=O).
   > How: in the Combiner, pick Carbon Dioxide and supply 1 carbon + 2 oxygen.
   > Tip: the Combiner GUI shows each recipe once you select its output.
21. **Hydrocarbons**: 4x `chemlib:methane`; 4x `chemlib:ethylene` *(after: Covalent Bonds: CO₂)*
   > What: methane (natural gas) and ethylene (the building block of polyethylene).
   > Chemistry: CH₄ has four single bonds. C₂H₄ has a C=C double bond, which is what lets it link into plastic chains.
   > How: Combiner: methane = 1 C + 4 H; ethylene = 2 C + 4 H.
22. **Ammonia**: 4x `chemlib:ammonia` *(after: Hydrocarbons)*
   > What: ammonia, NH₃, the base of nearly all fertiliser.
   > Chemistry: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. Breaking nitrogen's triple bond is hard; the Haber-Bosch process needs heat, pressure and an iron catalyst.
   > How: Combiner: 1 nitrogen + 3 hydrogen. Later you'll run real Haber-Bosch in an MI machine.
23. **Ionic Bonds: Salt**: 8x `chemlib:sodium_chloride` *(after: Ammonia)*
   > What: sodium chloride, NaCl: table salt.
   > Chemistry: sodium gives its one electron to chlorine. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ then hold together in a cubic crystal: an ionic bond.
   > How: Combiner: 1 sodium + 1 chlorine.
   > Tip: a reactive metal plus a poisonous gas makes something you sprinkle on food. Chemistry is strange.
24. **Strong Acids**: 4x `chemlib:hydrochloric_acid`; 4x `chemlib:nitric_acid` *(after: Ionic Bonds: Salt)*
   > What: hydrochloric acid (HCl) and nitric acid (HNO₃).
   > Chemistry: acids give up H⁺ ions in water. Mixed 3:1, HCl and HNO₃ make aqua regia, which dissolves gold and platinum.
   > How: Combiner: HCl = 1 H + 1 Cl; HNO₃ = 1 H + 1 N + 3 O.
25. **King of Chemicals**: 8x `chemlib:sulfuric_acid` *(after: Strong Acids)*
   > Built atom by atom. The old craft is coming back faster now.
   > What: sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, built straight from elements.
   > Chemistry: industry makes it by the contact process: S → SO₂ → SO₃ → H₂SO₄. Here you skip the plant and place the atoms yourself.
   > How: Combiner: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulfur + 4 oxygen.
26. **Sugar and Wood**: 2x `chemlib:sucrose`; 2x `chemlib:cellulose` *(after: Covalent Bonds: CO₂)*
   > What: sucrose (table sugar) and cellulose (what wood and paper are made of).
   > Chemistry: plants make both from CO₂ and water using sunlight. Cellulose is a chain of glucose rings: C₆H₁₀O₅ per unit.
   > How: Combiner: sucrose = 12 C + 22 H + 11 O; cellulose = 6 C + 10 H + 5 O.
   > Tip: that's a lot of atoms. Stock up on carbon, hydrogen and oxygen first.
27. **Alcohol**: 4x `chemlib:hydroxide`; 2x `chemlib:ethanol` *(after: Hydrocarbons)*
   > What: ethanol, C₂H₅OH, made by attaching a hydroxide (OH) group to a two-carbon chain.
   > Chemistry: the -OH group is what makes it an alcohol and lets it mix with water.
   > How: Combiner: hydroxide = 1 O + 1 H, then ethanol = 2 C + 5 H + 1 hydroxide.
28. **Lye**: 4x `chemlib:sodium_hydroxide` *(after: Ionic Bonds: Salt)*
   > What: sodium hydroxide, NaOH: lye, a strong base.
   > Chemistry: industry makes it by electrolysing salt water: 2NaCl + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂. Acid + base → salt + water.
   > How: Combiner: 1 sodium + 1 hydroxide (make hydroxide from 1 O + 1 H).
29. **Rust**: 4x `chemlib:iron_oxide` *(after: Strong Acids)*
   > What: iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃: rust, and also hematite, the most common iron ore.
   > Chemistry: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃. A blast furnace runs this backwards, using carbon to pull the oxygen off.
   > How: Combiner: 2 iron + 3 oxygen.
30. **Group 1, Complete**: `chemlib:lithium`; `chemlib:sodium`; `chemlib:potassium`; `chemlib:rubidium`; `chemlib:cesium`; `chemlib:francium` *(after: Noble Gases)*
   > What: all six alkali metals: Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs and Fr.
   > Chemistry: reactivity climbs down the group: the outer electron sits further from the nucleus and is lost more easily. Caesium explodes in water.
   > How: press U on rubidium and caesium in JEI for Dissolver sources. Francium is rare in both reality and here; the Fusion Chamber can build it.
   > Tip: real francium has a half-life of about 22 minutes. Yours keeps.
31. **Group 2, Complete**: `chemlib:beryllium`; `chemlib:magnesium`; `chemlib:calcium`; `chemlib:strontium`; `chemlib:barium`; `chemlib:radium` *(after: Group 1, Complete)*
   > What: all six alkaline earth metals: Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba and Ra.
   > Chemistry: strontium salts burn red and barium salts green: that's how fireworks get their colours. Radium glows from its own radioactivity.
   > How: JEI (U) shows Dissolver sources for strontium, barium and radium; the Fusion Chamber fills any gaps.
32. **The Boron Group**: `chemlib:boron`; `chemlib:aluminum`; `chemlib:gallium`; `chemlib:indium`; `chemlib:thallium` *(after: Group 2, Complete)*
   > What: boron, aluminum, gallium, indium and thallium.
   > Chemistry: boron is a metalloid; the rest are metals. Borosilicate glass (with B₂O₃) survives sudden heat, which is why lab glassware uses it.
   > How: boron needs the Fusion Chamber (5 = 1 + 4: hydrogen + beryllium). Check JEI for thallium.
   > Tip: thallium is very toxic in reality. In a chest it's harmless.
33. **The Carbon Group**: `chemlib:carbon`; `chemlib:silicon`; `chemlib:germanium`; `chemlib:tin`; `chemlib:lead` *(after: Post-Transition Metals)*
   > What: carbon, silicon, germanium, tin and lead, all with four valence electrons.
   > Chemistry: the group runs from a non-metal (carbon) through metalloids (Si, Ge) to metals (Sn, Pb). Same outer shell, very different behaviour.
   > How: all five come from the Dissolver: coal or graphite, sand, Nether bricks, diorite and lead ingots (check JEI).
34. **The Pnictogens**: `chemlib:nitrogen`; `chemlib:phosphorus`; `chemlib:arsenic`; `chemlib:antimony`; `chemlib:bismuth` *(after: Non-Metals)*
   > What: nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony and bismuth.
   > Chemistry: five valence electrons, so they often form three bonds (NH₃, PH₃). Bismuth crystals grow in stepped 'hopper' shapes with a rainbow oxide film.
   > How: JEI (U) shows Dissolver sources for antimony and bismuth.
35. **Group 17, Complete**: `chemlib:fluorine`; `chemlib:chlorine`; `chemlib:bromine`; `chemlib:iodine`; `chemlib:astatine` *(after: The Boron Group)*
   > What: the four common halogens plus astatine, one of the rarest natural elements on Earth.
   > Chemistry: down the group the halogens go from gas (F₂, Cl₂) to liquid (Br₂) to solid (I₂): bigger molecules attract each other more strongly.
   > How: astatine has a few Dissolver sources (press U in JEI), or build it in the Fusion Chamber.
36. **Group 18, Complete**: `chemlib:helium`; `chemlib:neon`; `chemlib:argon`; `chemlib:krypton`; `chemlib:xenon`; `chemlib:radon` *(after: Heavy Noble Gases)*
   > What: helium through radon, the whole right-hand column.
   > Chemistry: from 1960 to 1983 the metre was defined by the orange light of krypton-86. Xenon lights car headlamps and drives ion engines in spacecraft.
   > How: nothing dissolves into the light ones: fuse them in the Fusion Chamber (krypton is 36: try neon + iron). Xenon and radon come from dragon's breath.
37. **All Fifteen Lanthanides**: `chemlib:lanthanum`; `chemlib:cerium`; `chemlib:praseodymium`; `chemlib:neodymium`; `chemlib:promethium`; `chemlib:samarium`; `chemlib:europium`; `chemlib:gadolinium`; `chemlib:terbium`; `chemlib:dysprosium`; `chemlib:holmium`; `chemlib:erbium`; `chemlib:thulium`; `chemlib:ytterbium`; `chemlib:lutetium` *(after: Rare Earths)*
   > What: the full lanthanide row, the first line of the f-block.
   > Chemistry: europium makes the red in old TV screens and the anti-forgery glow in euro notes. Promethium has no stable isotope at all.
   > How: a few have Dissolver sources (press U); the Fusion Chamber builds the rest by adding proton numbers.
   > Tip: a challenge, not a requirement. Work through them as spare elements pile up.
38. **All Fifteen Actinides**: `chemlib:actinium`; `chemlib:thorium`; `chemlib:protactinium`; `chemlib:uranium`; `chemlib:neptunium`; `chemlib:plutonium`; `chemlib:americium`; `chemlib:curium`; `chemlib:berkelium`; `chemlib:californium`; `chemlib:einsteinium`; `chemlib:fermium`; `chemlib:mendelevium`; `chemlib:nobelium`; `chemlib:lawrencium` *(after: Actinides)*
   > What: the full actinide row. Everything past uranium is man-made.
   > Chemistry: einsteinium and fermium were first found in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb test in 1952. Americium sits in household smoke detectors.
   > How: the Fusion Chamber: gold (79) plus a light element reaches actinium and beyond (check JEI for the pairs).
39. **Limestone**: 4x `chemlib:calcium_carbonate` *(after: Covalent Bonds: CO₂)*
   > What: calcium carbonate, the mineral in limestone, chalk, marble and seashells.
   > Chemistry: heat it and it splits: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. That quicklime is the start of cement and mortar.
   > How: Combiner: first carbonate (1 carbon + 3 oxygen), then 1 calcium + 1 carbonate.
40. **Saltpeter**: 4x `chemlib:potassium_nitrate` *(after: Ammonia)*
   > What: potassium nitrate, the oxidiser in gunpowder and a classic fertiliser.
   > Chemistry: black powder is roughly 75% KNO₃, 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur. The nitrate brings its own oxygen, so it burns without air.
   > How: Combiner: nitrate (1 nitrogen + 3 oxygen), then 1 potassium + 1 nitrate.
   > Tip: the Combiner also turns potassium nitrate, sulfur and graphite into gunpowder (check JEI).
41. **Aspirin**: 2x `chemlib:acetylsalicylic_acid` *(after: Alcohol)*
   > What: acetylsalicylic acid, the world's best-known painkiller.
   > Chemistry: willow bark contains salicin, used against pain for thousands of years. Adding an acetyl group (1897) made it gentler on the stomach.
   > How: Combiner: 9 carbon + 8 hydrogen + 4 oxygen.
42. **Permanganate**: 2x `chemlib:potassium_permanganate` *(after: Lye)*
   > What: potassium permanganate, deep purple crystals and a strong oxidiser.
   > Chemistry: manganese here is in its +7 oxidation state and eager to take electrons back. The purple fades as it reacts, so chemists use it as its own indicator.
   > How: Combiner: 1 potassium + 1 manganese + 4 oxygen.
43. **Morning Coffee**: `chemlib:caffeine` *(after: Ammonia)*
   > Even a demigod likes a cup in the morning. You remember that much without trying.
   > What: caffeine, built atom by atom: 8 carbon, 10 hydrogen, 4 nitrogen, 2 oxygen.
   > Chemistry: it blocks adenosine receptors in the brain, the signal that tells you you're tired.
   > Tip: plants make caffeine as an insecticide. You drink it on purpose.
44. **Han Purple**: `chemlib:han_purple` *(after: Ionic Bonds: Salt)*
   > What: han purple, BaCuSi₂O₆, a barium copper silicate.
   > Chemistry: Chinese artisans made it more than 2,000 years ago by firing barium, copper and silica minerals together. It colours figures in the Terracotta Army.
   > How: Combiner: 1 barium + 1 copper + 2 silicon + 6 oxygen.
   > Tip: one of the first synthetic pigments in history. You just repeated an ancient experiment.

## Energy

### Power

*Energy is chemistry too: combustion, gas burning, fission and fusion.*

1. **Choosing Your Power**: `minecraft:redstone` *(after: Forge Energy)*
   > You remember holding lightning. For now, the generator you built in T1 will do.
   > What: this page lists the pack's power options by stage: early burners, moving power, storing it, mid-game and end-game plants. Furnaces and Generator Galore have their own page, Generators.
   > Chemistry: every generator turns some stored energy into current: chemical bonds (C + O₂ → CO₂), sunlight, wind, heat, or the nucleus itself.
   > How: a little redstone opens the page. Most lines are optional; pick the ones that suit your base.
   > Tip: MI machines run on EU, Modern Industrialization's own electricity. Most other mods run on FE (Forge Energy).
2. **Early Power**: `minecraft:coal` *(after: Choosing Your Power)*
   > What: early power comes from burning fuel or catching heat and light.
   > Chemistry: coal is mostly carbon; burning it releases about 33 kJ per gram as it becomes CO₂.
   > How: a lump of coal starts this section. Charcoal works in every burner too.
3. **Heat Generator**: `mekanismgenerators:heat_generator` *(after: Early Power, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: Mekanism's first generator. It burns fuel and turns heat into FE.
   > How: place lava next to it for a passive bonus, and feed it fuel for more.
   > Tip: lava from a pump makes this a decent passive generator early on.
4. **Coal Generators**: 1x any of `or(item(justdirethings:generatort1)item(integrateddynamics:coal_generator)item(generatorgalore:iron_generator))` *(after: Early Power)*
   > What: a plain fuel-burning generator from any mod: Just Dire Things, Integrated Dynamics or Generator Galore.
   > How: check JEI for each. Feed it coal, charcoal or coke.
   > Tip: coke from your coke oven burns twice as long as coal in most burners.
5. **Renewables**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanismgenerators:solar_generator)item(mekanismgenerators:advanced_solar_generator)item(mekanismgenerators:wind_generator))` *(after: Early Power, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: Mekanism's solar panels and wind generator: free power once built. Any one counts.
   > Chemistry: silicon solar cells use a p-n junction: a photon knocks an electron loose and the junction pushes it into a current.
   > How: solar under open sky; wind as high as you can build it (check JEI).
   > Tip: pair them with an energy cube to cover the night or a calm spell.
6. **Advanced Solar**: checkmark *(after: Renewables)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Advanced Solar Generator" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
7. **Wind Power**: checkmark *(after: Renewables)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Wind Generator" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
8. **Bio Fuel**: checkmark *(after: Heat Generator)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Bio-Generator" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
9. **Moving Power**: `minecraft:iron_ingot` *(after: Choosing Your Power)*
   > What: power is useless where it's made. This section is cables, pipes and the ways to skip them.
   > Chemistry: copper and aluminium carry real grids because their electrons move freely; iron conducts about six times worse than copper.
   > How: an iron ingot opens the section.
10. **Energy Pipes**: `pipez:energy_pipe`; `pipez:wrench` *(after: Moving Power)*
   > What: Pipez energy pipes carry FE, and the Pipe Wrench sets which ends pull.
   > How: iron and redstone with a redstone block for the pipe (check JEI). Sneak-click the generator end to extract.
   > Tip: the Automation and Logic page has the rest of Pipez.
11. **Pipe Upgrades**: 1x any of `or(item(pipez:basic_upgrade)item(pipez:improved_upgrade)item(pipez:advanced_upgrade)item(pipez:ultimate_upgrade))` *(after: Energy Pipes)*
   > What: an upgrade in the extracting end raises how much a pipe moves. Any tier counts.
   > How: each tier is the one before plus better materials (check JEI).
   > Tip: one upgrade at the generator end is enough for the whole line.
12. **Universal Cables**: checkmark *(after: Moving Power, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Universal Cable" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
13. **Quantum Entangloporter**: checkmark *(after: Moving Power, EV: Processing Units)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Quantum Entangloporter" on the Mekanism page. Click to dismiss.
14. **Flux Networks**: 4x `fluxnetworks:flux_dust` *(after: Moving Power, Into the Fire)*
   > What: flux dust is the base of every Flux Networks device.
   > Chemistry: real redstone doesn't exist, but pressure really does change minerals: graphite squeezed hard enough becomes diamond, and that's the idea here.
   > How: its tooltip says it: redstone compressed with bedrock and obsidian. JEI's Flux Networks page shows the setup. Bedrock is easy to reach at the Nether's floor or roof.
   > Tip: make a big batch now. The Flux Core needs an MI processing unit (EV), but the dust doesn't.
15. **Flux Cores**: 4x `fluxnetworks:flux_core`; `fluxnetworks:flux_block` *(after: Flux Networks, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: Flux Cores are the heart of every flux device; nine flux dust make a Flux Block.
   > How: in this pack: flux dust and obsidian around an MI processing unit (EV). Check JEI.
   > Tip: a plug, a point and a storage block each eat cores. Make four at once.
16. **Flux Plug**: `fluxnetworks:flux_plug` *(after: Flux Cores)*
   > What: a Flux Plug takes power from whatever it touches and puts it on a flux network.
   > How: flux blocks and a flux core (check JEI). Open it and create a network.
   > Tip: put one on your biggest battery's output.
17. **Set Up a Network**: checkmark *(after: Flux Plug)*
   > What: every flux device joins one named network. The network decides who may connect.
   > How: open the plug, make a network, give it a colour and set its security (public, encrypted or private). Click the checkmark when it's set.
   > Tip: private networks stop a teammate's machine draining your reactor by accident.
18. **Flux Point**: `fluxnetworks:flux_point` *(after: Set Up a Network)*
   > What: a Flux Point gives network power to whatever it touches.
   > How: like the plug (check JEI). Join it to the same network.
   > Tip: set a priority so the most important machines fill first.
19. **Flux Storage**: `fluxnetworks:basic_flux_storage` *(after: Set Up a Network)*
   > What: Basic Flux Storage buffers energy for the network.
   > How: flux blocks and glass around a flux core (check JEI).
   > Tip: flux storage keeps its energy when broken, so you can carry charged batteries to a new base.
20. **Note: Priorities**: checkmark *(after: Set Up a Network)*
   > What: each plug and point has a priority and a transfer limit. High-priority points fill first; storage fills last.
   > How: open a point, set its priority and limit. Click the checkmark when you've set one.
   > Tip: give the reactor coolant pumps the top priority. Everything else can wait a tick.
21. **Flux Controller**: `fluxnetworks:flux_controller` *(after: Set Up a Network)*
   > What: the Flux Controller sends network energy wirelessly into players' inventories.
   > How: flux blocks, a flux core and flux dust (check JEI).
   > Tip: turn charging off for your armour slots if it fights with other chargers. The Flux Configurator copies settings between devices.
22. **Herculean Storage**: `fluxnetworks:herculean_flux_storage` *(after: Flux Storage)*
   > What: Herculean (and then Gargantuan) Flux Storage holds far more energy in one block, shared with the whole network.
   > How: Basic Flux Storage blocks around glass panes (check JEI). Gargantuan is the same with Herculean blocks.
   > Tip: one Herculean block can carry a small base through a night with no solar.
23. **Storing Power**: `minecraft:iron_ingot` *(after: Choosing Your Power)*
   > What: a battery keeps machines running when the generator stalls, and catches power you'd otherwise waste.
   > Chemistry: a lead-acid battery stores energy in a reversible reaction: Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ ⇌ 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O.
   > How: an iron ingot opens the section.
24. **Energy Cubes**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_energy_cube)item(mekanism:advanced_energy_cube)item(mekanism:elite_energy_cube)item(mekanism:ultimate_energy_cube))` *(after: Storing Power, Mekanism: Metallurgic Infuser)*
   > What: energy cubes hold FE so short spikes don't stall your machines. Any tier counts.
   > How: put one between your generators and machines. Configure its sides with the Configurator.
   > Tip: cubes upgrade in place: craft the next tier around the old one.
25. **Energy Battery**: `integrateddynamics:energy_battery` *(after: Storing Power)*
   > What: a small FE battery made of crystalized Menril. It stacks power with others placed next to it.
   > How: Menril chunks and blocks around a redstone block (check JEI). The resin line is on the Automation and Logic page.
   > Tip: it fits on a logic network, where cables can carry its power.
26. **Induction Matrix**: 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_induction_provider)item(mekanism:advanced_induction_provider)item(mekanism:elite_induction_provider)item(mekanism:ultimate_induction_provider))`; 1x any of `or(item(mekanism:basic_induction_cell)item(mekanism:advanced_induction_cell)item(mekanism:elite_induction_cell)item(mekanism:ultimate_induction_cell))` *(after: Lithium)*
   > Power stored, waiting, obedient. This feels familiar.
   > What: a hollow multiblock battery. Cells inside set how much it stores; providers set how fast it charges and discharges.
   > How: casings form the shell (Structural Glass works for the walls), ports move energy in and out. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
   > Tip: switch one port to output with the Configurator. Start small; you can rebuild it larger later.
27. **Mid-Game Power**: `minecraft:diamond` *(after: Choosing Your Power)*
   > What: the mid game is about chemistry you've built yourself: burning hydrogen, and fission fuel.
   > Chemistry: diamond is carbon too, but burning one for power would be a terrible trade.
   > How: a diamond opens the section.
28. **Burning Hydrogen**: `mekanismgenerators:gas_burning_generator` *(after: Mid-Game Power, Mekanism Gases)*
   > What: the Gas-Burning Generator turns flammable gas into FE.
   > Chemistry: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O + energy. The only exhaust is water.
   > How: pipe hydrogen from your Electrolytic Separator in with pressurized tubes.
   > Tip: electrolysis costs more energy than burning hydrogen returns. Use it to store spare power, not to make it.
29. **More Powah**: `powah:uraninite` *(after: Mid-Game Power, Uranium Dioxide)*
   > What: uraninite fuels Powah's reactors. The Powah! page has the whole mod, tier by tier.
   > Chemistry: uraninite is UO₂. In this pack you make it the real way: uranium dust oxidised in MI's Chemical Reactor.
   > How: uranium dust and oxygen in the Chemical Reactor (MV). Powah's own shortcut is removed.
   > Tip: a Powah reactor takes uraninite, coolant, and carbon or redstone to boost it.
30. **End-Game Power**: `minecraft:netherite_ingot` *(after: Choosing Your Power, Into the Fire)*
   > What: end-game power means fusion: more energy than everything else on this page together.
   > How: a netherite ingot opens the section.
   > Tip: the Mekanism: Power page walks through fission and fusion step by step.
31. **Fusion**: `mekanismgenerators:fusion_reactor_controller` *(after: End-Game Power, D-T Fuel, Transmutation by Neutron)*
   > The power of a star, in a box you built. This is what you were.
   > What: Mekanism's fusion reactor, the top of the power tree.
   > Chemistry: D + T → ⁴He + n + 17.6 MeV, millions of times more energy per kilogram than any chemical reaction.
   > How: a filled Hohlraum in the controller, then a burst from a Laser through a Laser Amplifier to ignite it. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
32. **Bigger Cubes**: `mekanism:advanced_energy_cube` *(after: Energy Cubes, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: the Advanced Energy Cube holds and moves much more energy.
   > How: a basic cube with infused alloy, osmium ingots and energy tablets around it (check JEI). Upgrading in place keeps the stored energy.
   > Tip: Elite and Ultimate cubes follow the same pattern with reinforced and atomic alloys.
33. **Evaporation Ponds**: `mekanism:thermal_evaporation_controller`; `mekanism:brine_bucket` *(after: Bigger Cubes)*
   > What: the Thermal Evaporation Plant boils water down into brine, and brine down into liquid lithium.
   > Chemistry: real lithium comes from salt flats: brine sits in ponds until the water evaporates and the salts concentrate.
   > How: a multiblock tower of Thermal Evaporation Blocks, Valves and one Controller. See Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks in JEI.
   > Tip: taller towers and more heat run faster. Feed it plain water.
34. **Lithium**: 8x `mekanism:dust_lithium` *(after: Evaporation Ponds)*
   > What: lithium dust, for induction cells (and later, tritium).
   > Chemistry: lithium is the lightest metal and gives up its electron easily, which is why lithium-ion batteries store so much energy for their weight.
   > How: run brine through the plant again for liquid lithium. Turn it into gas in a Rotary Condensentrator, then crystallise it in a Chemical Crystallizer.
   > Tip: check JEI with R on Lithium Dust to confirm each step.
35. **Reactor Safety**: checkmark *(after: Mid-Game Power, Fission)*
   > Moved: this step is now "Fission Logic Adapter" on the Mekanism: Power page. Click to dismiss.
36. **Industrial Turbine**: 16x `mekanismgenerators:turbine_casing` *(after: Fission Logic Adapter)*
   > What: Mekanism's multiblock turbine. Feed it steam from fission or a boiler and it makes huge amounts of FE.
   > How: casings, valves, vents, rotors with blades, a rotational complex, a pressure disperser and electromagnetic coils. Layout: Just Enough Mekanism Multiblocks.
   > Tip: a Saturating Condenser turns spent steam back into water, closing the loop.
37. **D-T Fuel**: `mekanism:solar_neutron_activator`; `mekanismgenerators:hohlraum` *(after: Industrial Turbine, Lithium)*
   > What: fusion fuel: deuterium and tritium, the two heavy isotopes of hydrogen.
   > Chemistry: deuterium comes from heavy water (D₂O). Tritium is bred from lithium by neutrons: ⁶Li + n → ³H + ⁴He.
   > How: electrolyse heavy water for deuterium; put lithium in the Solar Neutron Activator for tritium. Combine them into D-T fuel in the Chemical Infuser, then fill a Hohlraum with it (a chemical tank's item slot works; see its tooltip).
   > Tip: heavy water comes from a Mekanism Electric Pump with a Filter Upgrade.
38. **EU Storage**: `modern_industrialization:lv_storage_unit` *(after: Storing Power, LV Machine Hull)*
   > What: MI's storage unit holds EU, Modern Industrialization's electricity.
   > How: built from redstone batteries, battery alloy plates and an LV hull. Put it between your turbine and your machines.
   > Tip: a buffer lets your steam turbine keep running while machines are idle.
39. **MV Steam Turbine**: `modern_industrialization:mv_steam_turbine` *(after: EU Storage, MV: Aluminum)*
   > What: a bigger steam turbine that outputs MV power.
   > Chemistry: a turbine converts the energy of hot, expanding steam into rotation, then a generator turns rotation into current.
   > How: assemble it from an MV hull, aluminum rotors and large motors (check JEI).
40. **Transformers**: `modern_industrialization:lv_mv_transformer` *(after: MV Steam Turbine)*
   > What: a transformer moves energy between two neighbouring voltage tiers (LV and MV here).
   > How: place it between an MV cable and your LV machines (or the other way round). Check which face is which in its tooltip.
   > Tip: real grids do the same: high voltage for transmission, low voltage at the socket.
41. **HV Steam Turbine**: `modern_industrialization:hv_steam_turbine` *(after: Transformers, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: the HV steam turbine, for HV machine lines.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe. Feed it from a large boiler.
   > Tip: more steam than one turbine can eat? Add a second turbine on the same steam line.
42. **Large Steam Turbine**: `modern_industrialization:large_steam_turbine` *(after: HV Steam Turbine, EV: Processing Units)*
   > What: MI's multiblock steam turbine. It eats steam by the thousands of mB and makes serious EU.
   > How: the controller needs an HV steam turbine, a processing unit (EV) and a highly advanced hull. Layout: JEI or the MI guidebook.
   > Tip: pair it with a large boiler or a reactor's steam output.
43. **Diesel Generators**: `modern_industrialization:mv_diesel_generator` *(after: Mid-Game Power, Diesel Power)*
   > What: MI generators that burn the fuels from your distillation tower.
   > Chemistry: diesel is a mix of hydrocarbons around C₁₂ to C₂₀. Long chains pack lots of C-H bonds, and lots of energy.
   > How: pipe diesel into the generator and cable it to your machines.
44. **Large Diesel Generator**: `modern_industrialization:large_diesel_generator` *(after: Diesel Generators, HV: Digital Circuits)*
   > What: a multiblock diesel generator for real factories.
   > How: the 3D layout is in JEI and the MI guidebook. It needs fluid input and energy output hatches.
   > Tip: refined fuels (like boosted diesel) burn for more EU per bucket. Check JEI.

### Generators

*Faster furnaces and a burner for every fuel.*

1. **Furnaces and Generators**: `minecraft:furnace` *(after: Fire, Choosing Your Power)*
   > Fire was the first thing you ever gave anyone. You remember that much.
   > What: Iron Furnaces makes faster furnaces, tier by tier; Generator Galore makes burners for every odd fuel. Both start from the humble furnace.
   > Chemistry: a furnace is a controlled oxidation: fuel + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + heat. Better furnaces just waste less of that heat.
   > How: any vanilla furnace opens the section.
2. **Copper Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:copper_furnace` *(after: Furnaces and Generators)*
   > What: a faster furnace from copper, and the start of the silver branch.
   > How: copper ingots around a vanilla furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: every furnace tier can upgrade in place with an upgrade kit, keeping its contents.
3. **Iron Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:iron_furnace` *(after: Furnaces and Generators)*
   > What: the first real step up: smelts noticeably faster than vanilla.
   > How: iron ingots around a vanilla furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: 4x vanilla cooking is on in this pack, so even this one is quick.
4. **Silver Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:silver_furnace` *(after: Copper Furnace, Iron Furnace)*
   > What: the silver tier, between iron and gold.
   > Chemistry: silver has the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any metal (about 6% better than copper).
   > How: silver ingots and glass around an iron furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: silver comes from MI ore processing and the Mining dimension's veins.
5. **Gold Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:gold_furnace` *(after: Silver Furnace)*
   > What: the gold tier: faster again.
   > How: gold ingots and a block of gold around an iron furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: a gold furnace on your ore line pays for itself quickly.
6. **Diamond Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:diamond_furnace` *(after: Gold Furnace)*
   > What: the diamond tier.
   > How: diamonds and glass around a gold furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: from here the tree splits into emerald and crystal.
7. **Emerald Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:emerald_furnace` *(after: Diamond Furnace)*
   > What: the emerald tier.
   > Chemistry: emerald is the mineral beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, coloured green by a trace of chromium.
   > How: emeralds around a diamond furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: a villager trading hall makes emeralds cheap.
8. **Crystal Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:crystal_furnace` *(after: Diamond Furnace)*
   > What: the crystal tier, built with Nether quartz and glass.
   > Chemistry: window glass is mostly SiO₂ with soda and lime. Unlike quartz, its atoms have no regular lattice: it is a frozen liquid, not a crystal.
   > How: glass and an eye of ender around a diamond furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: obsidian next needs both the emerald and the crystal furnace.
9. **Obsidian Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:obsidian_furnace` *(after: Crystal Furnace, Emerald Furnace)*
   > What: the obsidian tier: very fast, and blast-proof.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass: lava that cooled too fast to form crystals.
   > How: obsidian and blaze rods around an emerald furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: it's the base for the netherite tier.
10. **Netherite Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:netherite_furnace` *(after: Obsidian Furnace, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the top standard tier.
   > How: netherite ingots, magma cream and a soul sand or soul soil block around an obsidian furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Rainbow Core needs one of these.
11. **Allthemodium Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:allthemodium_furnace` *(after: Netherite Furnace)*
   > What: a furnace from Allthemodium, beyond netherite.
   > How: Allthemodium ingots and blocks around a netherite furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: the Allthemodium page covers where the metal comes from.
12. **Vibranium Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:vibranium_furnace` *(after: Allthemodium Furnace)*
   > What: the vibranium tier.
   > How: vibranium around an Allthemodium furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: vibranium comes from the Other dimension.
13. **Unobtainium Furnace**: `ironfurnaces:unobtainium_furnace` *(after: Vibranium Furnace)*
   > What: the fastest furnace in the mod.
   > How: unobtainium around a vibranium furnace (check JEI).
   > Tip: worth it only if you smelt by the hundred thousand.
14. **Rainbow Core**: `ironfurnaces:rainbow_core` *(after: Netherite Furnace)*
   > What: the core of the Rainbow Generator.
   > Chemistry: stained glass gets its colour from metal ions in the glass: cobalt for blue, chromium for green, gold for ruby red.
   > How: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple and magenta stained glass around two netherite furnaces (check JEI).
15. **Rainbow Plating**: 8x `ironfurnaces:rainbow_plating` *(after: Obsidian Furnace)*
   > What: eight plating, from one each of the copper, iron, silver, gold, diamond, emerald, crystal and obsidian furnaces.
   > How: shapeless, all eight furnaces together (check JEI).
   > Tip: upgrade kits make the furnaces cheaper than building each from scratch.
16. **The Rainbow Generator**: `ironfurnaces:million_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:copper_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:iron_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:silver_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:gold_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:diamond_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:emerald_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:crystal_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:obsidian_furnace`; `ironfurnaces:netherite_furnace` *(after: Rainbow Plating, Rainbow Core)*
   > What: the Rainbow Furnace, plus one furnace of every other tier. When every tier runs as a generator, it makes a great deal of FE.
   > How: 8 rainbow plating around a rainbow core. Put a Generator augment in one furnace of each tier and keep them all burning; the tooltip explains the rest.
   > Tip: you can only have one Rainbow Generator, so pick its spot with care.
17. **Rainbow Coal**: `ironfurnaces:rainbow_coal` *(after: The Rainbow Generator)*
   > What: a fuel that burns for a very long time. It has no crafting recipe.
   > How: read the Rainbow Furnace's tooltip carefully. It hints at what to do.
   > Tip: try it far from anything you love.
18. **Augments**: `minecraft:paper` *(after: Copper Furnace, Iron Furnace)*
   > What: augments go in a furnace's side slots and change how it works: blasting, smoking, more slots, speed, efficiency or power.
   > How: every augment starts with paper (check JEI). A furnace takes one of each type.
   > Tip: speed and fuel efficiency pull in opposite directions; pick one per furnace.
19. **Blasting Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_blasting` *(after: Augments)*
   > What: makes the furnace act as a blast furnace: faster on ores and metal, no food.
   > How: check JEI for its recipe, then put it in one of the furnace's augment slots.
   > Tip: put it on the furnace your ore line feeds.
20. **Smoking Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_smoking` *(after: Augments)*
   > What: makes the furnace act as a smoker: fast on food only.
   > How: check JEI for its recipe, then put it in one of the furnace's augment slots.
   > Tip: one smoking furnace next to the kitchen is plenty.
21. **Factory Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_factory` *(after: Augments)*
   > What: turns the furnace into a factory with several input and output slots that smelt side by side.
   > How: check JEI for its recipe, then put it in one of the furnace's augment slots.
   > Tip: a factory furnace plus a pipe to storage is a whole smelting room in one block.
22. **Generator Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_generator` *(after: Augments)*
   > What: turns the furnace into a generator that burns fuel for FE instead of smelting.
   > How: check JEI for its recipe, then put it in one of the furnace's augment slots.
   > Tip: the Rainbow Generator needs one of these in a furnace of every tier.
23. **Speed Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_speed` *(after: Augments)*
   > What: makes the furnace smelt faster at the cost of more fuel.
   > How: check JEI for its recipe, then put it in one of the furnace's augment slots.
   > Tip: good on furnaces fed by a steady fuel line.
24. **Efficiency Augment**: `ironfurnaces:augment_fuel` *(after: Augments)*
   > What: makes fuel last longer at the cost of speed.
   > How: check JEI for its recipe, then put it in one of the furnace's augment slots.
   > Tip: good on furnaces you fill by hand.
25. **Wireless Heating**: `ironfurnaces:heater`; `ironfurnaces:item_heater` *(after: Copper Furnace, Iron Furnace)*
   > What: the Heater stores FE; a Heater card links a furnace to it, so the furnace burns electricity instead of fuel.
   > How: check JEI for both. Right-click the heater with the card, then put the card in a furnace.
   > Tip: one heater can feed a whole row of furnaces.
26. **Configuration Copier**: `ironfurnaces:item_copy` *(after: Copper Furnace, Iron Furnace)*
   > What: copies a furnace's side settings and pastes them onto another.
   > How: check JEI. Sneak-click to copy, click to paste.
   > Tip: set one furnace's input, output and fuel faces, then paste it down the row.
27. **Furnace Spooka-lator**: `ironfurnaces:item_spooky` *(after: Copper Furnace, Iron Furnace)*
   > What: a purely cosmetic trick: right-click a furnace and it takes on a spooky look.
   > How: a carved pumpkin and a furnace, shapeless.
   > Tip: sneak-right-click the furnace to undo it.
28. **Furnace Wrapping Paper**: `ironfurnaces:item_xmas` *(after: Copper Furnace, Iron Furnace)*
   > What: another cosmetic: right-click a furnace to wrap it like a present.
   > How: check JEI for the recipe.
   > Tip: sneak-right-click to unwrap it again.
29. **Copper Generator**: `generatorgalore:copper_generator` *(after: Furnaces and Generators)*
   > What: Generator Galore's first generator: slow, but very cheap.
   > How: copper ingots around a furnace, with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: the iron generator from your T1 power quest is the next step up.
30. **Iron Generator**: `generatorgalore:iron_generator` *(after: Copper Generator)*
   > What: a steady fuel burner and the root of the Generator Galore tree.
   > How: iron ingots around a copper generator, with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: every later generator is built from this one or its children.
31. **Gold Generator**: `generatorgalore:gold_generator` *(after: Iron Generator)*
   > What: it burns fuel faster and makes more FE per tick.
   > How: upgrade from the iron generator (check JEI), or use the iron-to-gold upgrade kit on a placed one.
   > Tip: a faster burn needs a steadier fuel supply. Pipe in charcoal from a tree farm.
32. **Culinary Generator**: `generatorgalore:culinary_generator` *(after: Gold Generator)*
   > What: burns food; better food burns longer.
   > Chemistry: food energy is chemical energy: a kilocalorie is about 4.2 kJ, whether your body or a generator releases it.
   > How: crops, a cake and eggs around a gold generator, with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: hook it to a farm's overflow.
33. **Diamond Generator**: `generatorgalore:diamond_generator` *(after: Gold Generator)*
   > What: a much stronger fuel burner, and the start of the gem branch.
   > How: a gold generator in diamonds with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: feed it coal blocks; loose coal won't keep up.
34. **Netherite Generator**: `generatorgalore:netherite_generator` *(after: Diamond Generator, Into the Fire)*
   > What: the netherite generator burns ordinary fuel at a very high rate.
   > How: smithing table: template, diamond generator and a netherite ingot (check JEI).
   > Tip: it leads to the Nether Star generator.
35. **Emerald Generator**: `generatorgalore:emerald_generator` *(after: Diamond Generator)*
   > What: a step past diamond on the same fuel.
   > Chemistry: emerald is beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈. The beryllium in it is one of the lightest metals there is.
   > How: a diamond generator in emeralds with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: villagers are the cheapest emerald source.
36. **Obsidian Generator**: `generatorgalore:obsidian_generator` *(after: Diamond Generator, A Door of Fire)*
   > What: a stronger burner, and the base for the ender, enchantment and magmatic generators.
   > How: a diamond generator in obsidian with a redstone block (or the diamond-to-obsidian upgrade kit).
   > Tip: JEI shows the whole tree.
37. **Honey Generator**: `generatorgalore:honey_generator` *(after: Culinary Generator)*
   > What: burns honey.
   > Chemistry: honey is about 80% sugars (fructose and glucose). Sugar burns well: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O.
   > How: a culinary generator in honey blocks with buckets and a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: a few beehives with campfires underneath keep it running.
38. **Potion Generator**: `generatorgalore:potion_generator` *(after: Culinary Generator)*
   > What: burns potions; stronger potions burn longer.
   > How: pink dye around a culinary generator, with brewing stands and a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: every failed brew finally has a use.
39. **Enchantment Generator**: `generatorgalore:enchantment_generator` *(after: Obsidian Generator)*
   > What: burns enchanted books and items.
   > How: an obsidian generator in enchanted books with an enchanting table (check JEI).
   > Tip: fishing junk books finally have a use.
40. **Magmatic Generator**: `generatorgalore:magmatic_generator` *(after: Obsidian Generator)*
   > What: burns lava, a bucket at a time or by pipe.
   > Chemistry: lava is molten silicate rock at roughly 700 to 1,200 °C.
   > How: gold ingots around an obsidian generator, with a lava bucket (check JEI).
   > Tip: a Nether lava lake and a pump give endless fuel.
41. **Ender Generator**: `generatorgalore:ender_generator` *(after: Obsidian Generator)*
   > What: burns ender pearls.
   > How: an obsidian generator in ender pearls with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: an enderman farm feeds it for ever.
42. **Netherstar Generator**: `generatorgalore:netherstar_generator` *(after: Netherite Generator)*
   > What: the Nether Star Generator burns Nether Stars for an enormous amount of FE.
   > Chemistry: real stars run on fusion: four hydrogen nuclei become one helium nucleus, and a little mass becomes a lot of energy, E = mc².
   > How: wither skeleton skulls around a netherite generator, with a redstone block (check JEI).
   > Tip: save most stars for Powah's nitro crystals.
43. **Halitosis Generator**: `generatorgalore:halitosis_generator` *(after: Ender Generator)*
   > What: burns dragon's breath, bottled from the dragon's attacks in the End.
   > How: amethyst around an ender generator, with an end rod (check JEI).
   > Tip: plan an End trip and bring empty bottles.
44. **Eight Times the Burn**: 1x any of `or(item(generatorgalore:copper_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:diamond_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:emerald_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:enchantment_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:ender_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:gold_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:halitosis_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:honey_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:iron_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:magmatic_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:netherite_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:netherstar_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:obsidian_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:potion_generator_8x)item(generatorgalore:culinary_generator_8x))` *(after: Copper Generator, An Ancient City)*
   > What: 8x generators burn fuel eight times as fast and make eight times the FE in one block. Any 8x generator counts.
   > How: eight generators of a tier around an echo shard (check JEI). Echo shards come from Ancient City chests.
   > Tip: make sure the fuel line can keep up first.
45. **Sixty-Four Times**: 1x any of `or(item(generatorgalore:culinary_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:enchantment_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:ender_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:halitosis_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:honey_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:magmatic_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:netherite_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:netherstar_generator_64x)item(generatorgalore:potion_generator_64x))` *(after: Eight Times the Burn)*
   > What: 64x generators: eight 8x generators in one block. Any one counts.
   > How: eight 8x generators around a conduit (check JEI).
   > Tip: a 64x generator eats fuel 64 times as fast. Feed it from storage, not a chest.
46. **Upgrade in Place**: `generatorgalore:iron_to_gold_upgrade` *(after: Gold Generator)*
   > What: Generator Galore upgrade kits turn a placed generator into the next tier, keeping its fuel and connections.
   > How: gold ingots, an item frame and a redstone block for iron → gold (check JEI for the others). Right-click the placed generator.
   > Tip: the tree branches: gold leads to diamond or to the food-burning Culinary Generator.
47. **Upgrade Kits**: `ironfurnaces:upgrade_gold`; `ironfurnaces:upgrade_diamond` *(after: Gold Furnace)*
   > What: upgrade kits turn a placed furnace into the next tier and keep its contents, augment and settings.
   > How: each kit is the next tier's materials around a block (check JEI). Right-click the placed furnace with it.
   > Tip: kits are cheaper than crafting a new furnace when you have a whole row to upgrade.
48. **Every Kit**: 2x any of `or(item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_copper)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_iron)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_iron2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_gold2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_silver)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_silver2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_emerald)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_crystal)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_obsidian)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_obsidian2)item(ironfurnaces:upgrade_netherite))` *(after: Upgrade Kits)*
   > What: there's a kit for every step: vanilla to copper or iron, copper to iron, iron to gold or silver, diamond to emerald or crystal, up to netherite. Any two.
   > How: each is the next tier's material around a stone tool material or gem (check JEI).
   > Tip: kits keep the furnace's augment, so upgrade a generator furnace without losing its setup.

### Powah!

*Powah: dielectric parts, the Energizing Orb, crystal tiers, generators, cells and wireless power. The starter and basic tiers are open early; the Orb needs an MI electronic circuit (MV).*

1. **Powah!**: checkmark *(after: Forge Energy)*
   > Insulators and conductors. You remember that power is mostly about where it is not allowed to go.
   > What: Powah builds every block in seven tiers: starter, basic, hardened, blazing, niotic, spirited and nitro. Each row of this page is one tier; each column is one kind of block.
   > How: the starter and basic rows need only dielectric parts and capacitors. Everything from hardened up goes through the Energizing Orb, which needs an MI electronic circuit (MV) in this pack.
   > Tip: click the checkmark to start. You don't need every block: pick the columns you'll use.
2. **Dielectric Parts**: 16x `powah:dielectric_paste`; `powah:dielectric_casing` *(after: Powah!)*
   > What: dielectric paste goes into rods, casings, capacitors and cables; the casing is the frame inside almost every Powah block.
   > Chemistry: a dielectric is an insulator that polarises in an electric field. Fired clay (aluminosilicates such as kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄) is the porcelain on real power-line insulators.
   > How: paste, shapeless: 3 coal or charcoal + 2 clay balls + a lava bucket makes 24. Casing: 4 iron ingots in the corners, horizontal rods top and bottom, upright rods in the middle row (check JEI).
   > Tip: the lava recipe gives more per craft and keeps the bucket. Make a stack.
3. **The Energizing Orb**: `powah:energizing_orb`; 1x any of `or(item(powah:energy_cable_starter)item(powah:energy_cable_basic))`; 1x any of `or(item(powah:energizing_rod_starter)item(powah:energizing_rod_basic))` *(after: Dielectric Parts, Electronic Circuit)*
   > A glass sphere that fills with light. You remember charging things just by holding them.
   > What: the Orb turns FE into new materials: energized steel, crystals, ender cores. Every Powah tier above basic needs it.
   > How: in this pack: glass on top and sides, an MI electronic circuit on each side of a dielectric casing in the middle, and 3 horizontal rods on the bottom. Bring a rod and a cable too.
   > How: place the orb, aim Energizing Rods at it from nearby, feed the rods FE through cables and put the ingredients in the orb. JEI's Energizing tab shows each recipe and its FE cost.
   > Tip: the first jobs are energized steel and the Ender Core.
4. **Tiny Capacitor**: `powah:capacitor_basic_tiny` *(after: Dielectric Parts)*
   > What: tiny capacitors set a block's tier to starter.
   > Chemistry: a capacitor is two conductors separated by a dielectric. It stores E = ½CV², and a better dielectric raises the capacitance C.
   > How: one basic capacitor splits into 2 tiny ones (check JEI).
5. **Basic Capacitor**: `powah:capacitor_basic` *(after: Dielectric Parts)*
   > What: basic capacitors set a block's tier to basic, and split into tiny ones.
   > How: iron ingots, paste and a redstone block make 4 basic capacitors.
   > Tip: two basic capacitors combine into a large one, which the hardened and crystal tiers need later.
6. **Energized Steel**: `powah:steel_energized` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: Powah's basic alloy, made by the Energizing Orb. It opens the hardened tier.
   > How: put 1 iron + 1 gold in the Orb for 2 Energized Steel (check JEI for the FE cost).
   > Tip: hardened capacitors are a large capacitor in energized steel and paste.
7. **Thermo Generator**: `powah:thermo_generator_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: a generator that needs a hot block underneath and a coolant fed in.
   > Chemistry: thermoelectric plates make current from a temperature difference (the Seebeck effect). Hotter below and colder inside means more power.
   > How: thermo plates, tiny capacitors and a casing (check JEI). Place it on lava or magma and pipe water in.
8. **Furnator**: `powah:furnator_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: a Powah generator that burns furnace fuel for FE. It's an early way to run the Dissolver.
   > Chemistry: burning oxidises carbon. Coke burns cleaner and longer than coal because its volatile tars were already driven off.
   > How: paste, 2 tiny capacitors, a dielectric casing and a furnace.
   > Tip: feed it coke from your coke ovens for long runs.
9. **Starter Solar Panel**: `powah:solar_panel_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: Powah's solar panel. It makes FE from daylight with no fuel at all.
   > Chemistry: light can knock electrons out of a material (the photoelectric effect, explained by Einstein in 1905). Solar cells collect them as current.
   > How: photoelectric panes, tiny capacitors and a casing (check JEI). Place it under open sky.
   > Tip: it stops at night; pair it with a cell.
10. **Magmator**: `powah:magmator_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: a generator that burns lava (and other hot fluids) instead of solid fuel.
   > Chemistry: lava is molten silicate rock at roughly 700 to 1,200 °C. The Magmator draws that stored heat off as FE.
   > How: like the Furnator, but with a bucket in place of the furnace. JEI's Magmatic Fluids list shows what it accepts.
   > Tip: a Nether lava lake and a pump give endless fuel.
11. **Starter Reactor**: 36x `powah:reactor_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor, Uranium Dioxide)*
   > What: 36 starter reactor blocks: enough for a full, if weak, reactor. Every better reactor block is crafted from these.
   > Chemistry: uranium dioxide is a ceramic: it melts near 2,865 °C, which is why real fuel pellets are UO₂ and not uranium metal.
   > How: 4 uraninite, 4 tiny capacitors and a dielectric casing make 4. Uraninite comes from MI's Chemical Reactor (uranium dust + oxygen).
   > Tip: all blocks in one stack must be the same tier, or they won't form one reactor.
12. **Starter Ender Gate**: `powah:ender_gate_starter` *(after: Energy Cables, The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: the Ender Gate taps the ender network wherever you place it, without storing much itself.
   > How: tiny capacitors and a dielectric casing, plus the block's own parts (check JEI).
   > Tip: its Ender Core is made in the Energizing Orb, so this one waits for the Orb.
13. **Energy Cables**: `powah:energy_cable_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: Powah's cables. Each tier carries more FE per tick.
   > How: 6 horizontal rods, 2 iron nuggets and a tiny capacitor make 12 starter cables.
   > Tip: cables connect to any FE block, not just Powah ones. Use the Powah wrench to configure sides.
14. **Player Transmitter**: `powah:player_transmitter_starter`; 1x any of `or(item(powah:binding_card)item(powah:binding_card_dim))` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: a block that charges the FE items carried by the player bound to it.
   > How: Player Aerial Pearl on top, tiny capacitors and a casing in the middle, an upright rod below. The Binding Card is a blank card with redstone and rotten flesh; right-click to bind it to yourself.
   > Tip: either Binding Card counts here: the plain one or the dimensional one.
15. **Starter Energy Hopper**: `powah:energy_hopper_starter` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: the Energy Hopper charges the FE items in the container it faces.
   > How: tiny capacitors and a dielectric casing, plus the block's own parts (check JEI).
   > Tip: starter blocks need no Energizing Orb, so they work from your first day of power.

47. **Basic Energizing Rod**: `powah:energizing_rod_basic` *(after: Starter Energizing Rod, Basic Capacitor)*
   > What: higher-tier rods pour FE into the Orb faster.
   > Chemistry: quartz is crystalline SiO₂ and is piezoelectric: squeeze it and it makes a voltage. Every quartz watch keeps time with a vibrating crystal.
   > How: a block of quartz on top, basic capacitors and a casing in the middle, a starter rod below.
   > Tip: crystals cost hundreds of thousands of FE. More and better rods matter more than anything else here.

49. **Powah's Manual**: `powah:book` *(after: Dielectric Parts)*
   > What: Powah's in-game book, with a page and a picture for every block on this chapter.
   > How: a book and a dielectric paste, shapeless.
   > Tip: add it to your Akashic Tome (Quality of Life page) so it doesn't take a slot.
50. **Dielectric Rods**: 8x `powah:dielectric_rod`; 8x `powah:dielectric_rod_horizontal` *(after: Dielectric Parts)*
   > What: insulated rods, upright and horizontal. Both go into casings, the Orb, cables and cards.
   > How: 6 paste around 3 iron bars: a vertical line of bars for the upright rod, a horizontal line for the horizontal one. 8 per craft.
   > Tip: you'll need far more horizontal rods than upright ones; every cable craft eats six.
51. **Spare Casings**: 2x `powah:dielectric_casing` *(after: Dielectric Rods)*
   > What: the frame inside almost every Powah machine, cell and generator.
   > How: 4 iron ingots in the corners, horizontal rods top and bottom, upright rods in the middle row (check JEI).
   > Tip: craft a stack of casings before a big upgrade session.
52. **Powah Wrench**: `powah:wrench` *(after: Dielectric Parts)*
   > What: Powah's wrench. It has Rotate, Config and Link modes; the mode shows on the item.
   > How: iron ingots and dielectric paste (check JEI).
   > Tip: Config mode sets which sides of a cell or generator push or take power.
53. **Player Aerial Pearl**: `powah:player_aerial_pearl` *(after: Dielectric Parts)*
   > What: the core of the Player Transmitter.
   > How: craft an Aerial Pearl (an ender pearl in iron bars and paste), then use it on a Zombie or a Husk.
   > Tip: trap a zombie near your base so you can make more later.
54. **Panes and Plates**: 3x `powah:photoelectric_pane`; 3x `powah:thermoelectric_plate` *(after: Tiny Capacitor)*
   > What: photoelectric panes go into solar panels; thermo plates go into thermo generators.
   > Chemistry: lapis gets its blue from trisulfur radical ions (S₃⁻) trapped in the mineral lazurite.
   > How: pane: a glass pane in lapis and paste. Plate: a tiny capacitor in redstone and blaze powder.
   > Tip: blaze powder means a trip to the Nether first.
55. **Dimensional Binding Card**: `powah:binding_card_dim` *(after: Player Transmitter)*
   > What: the dimensional version of the Binding Card, for transmitters and other Powah blocks that take a card.
   > How: use a Binding Card on an Enderman or an Endermite.
   > Tip: read its tooltip to see what it does differently from the plain card.
56. **Charged Snowball**: 4x `powah:charged_snowball` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: a snowball charged with 500,000 FE. Throw it and lightning strikes where it lands.
   > Chemistry: a lightning channel heats air to around 30,000 K, hotter than the Sun's surface. It splits N₂ and O₂, and the nitrogen oxides it makes fertilise the soil.
   > How: one snowball in the Energizing Orb.
   > Tip: lightning turns a pig into a zombified piglin and a villager into a witch. Aim carefully.
57. **Large and Hardened Capacitors**: 2x `powah:capacitor_basic_large`; 2x `powah:capacitor_hardened` *(after: Energized Steel)*
   > What: hardened capacitors unlock the hardened tier of everything.
   > How: 2 basic capacitors make a large one. A large capacitor in energized steel and paste makes 2 hardened capacitors.
   > Tip: large capacitors go into every crystal capacitor too. Craft spares.
58. **Ender Core**: 2x `powah:ender_core` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: the heart of Ender Cells and Ender Gates.
   > How: Energizing Orb: an eye of ender, a dielectric casing and a tiny capacitor, 50,000 FE.
   > Tip: one core per ender block, at every tier.
59. **Dry Ice**: 4x `powah:dry_ice` *(after: Basic Reactor)*
   > What: a strong solid coolant for the Powah reactor. Cooler reactors waste less fuel.
   > Chemistry: real dry ice is solid CO₂, which sublimes straight to gas at -78.5 °C. Powah's is made from energized blue ice, which is H₂O, so take the name loosely.
   > How: Energizing Orb: 2 blue ice, 10,000 FE. JEI's Coolants and Solid Coolants tabs list every option and its strength.
   > Tip: the reactor also takes carbon and redstone to boost it. Check its GUI slots.
60. **A Block of Nitro**: `powah:nitro_crystal_block` *(after: Nitro Crystal)*
   > Nine crystals, each a star's worth of charge, pressed into one block. You remember holding that much. You used to call it Tuesday.
   > What: a storage block of nitro crystals. It does nothing; it's just very, very expensive.
   > Tip: you can always break it back into crystals.

### Powah: Blazing Tier

*Powah!, continued: Blazing Tier*

1. **Blazing Crystal**: `powah:crystal_blazing` *(after: The Energizing Orb, Blaze Rods)*
   > What: every Powah tier past hardened is built from a crystal made in the Orb. Blazing crystals open the blazing tier.
   > How: energize a blaze rod (or four blaze powder) with 120,000 FE (check JEI).
   > Tip: a blaze farm (or a Hostile Neural Networks blaze model) keeps the crystals coming.
2. **Niotic Crystal**: `powah:crystal_niotic` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: the niotic tier. Reactors and generators get much stronger.
   > Chemistry: diamond is pure carbon in a rigid lattice where every atom bonds to four others. It insulates electricity but carries heat better than any metal.
   > How: energize a diamond with 300,000 FE (check JEI).
3. **Spirited Crystal**: `powah:crystal_spirited` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > What: the spirited tier, one step below the top.
   > Chemistry: emerald is the mineral beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈. A trace of chromium (Cr³⁺) replacing some aluminium gives it its green colour.
   > How: energize an emerald with 1,000,000 FE (check JEI). A villager trading hall pays off here.
4. **Nitro Crystal**: `powah:crystal_nitro` *(after: The Energizing Orb)*
   > Twenty million FE poured into a star. You remember power like this; it used to be yours.
   > What: nitro crystals build the strongest Powah blocks.
   > How: energize a Nether Star, two redstone blocks and a blazing crystal block with 20,000,000 FE. One craft makes sixteen.
   > Tip: save your Nether Stars for this; the Wither is the only reliable source.

## Magic

### Ars Nouveau

*Spellcraft, Source, rituals and the Wilden: magic that runs on stored energy.*

1. **Words with Weight**: `minecraft:book` *(after: Whispers of Magic)*
   > You remember that a word, said the right way, was once enough. A book will have to do for now.
   > What: Ars Nouveau is spellcraft you design yourself: glyphs written into a book, powered by mana, plus Source, a stored magic that runs machines and rituals.
   > How: hold a plain book (paper and leather). The Worn Notebook from Chapter II explains every block and glyph.
   > Tip: this page runs book, archwood, Scribe's Table, Source, Apparatus, rituals. Glyphs fill the three tiers above.
2. **Novice Spell Book**: `ars_nouveau:novice_spell_book` *(after: Words with Weight)*
   > What: the Novice Spell Book holds spells built from glyphs: a form (how it's cast), effects, then augments. It can use tier 1 glyphs.
   > How: a book with an iron shovel, pickaxe, axe and sword (shapeless). Open it to combine glyphs, e.g. Projectile + Break to mine at range.
   > Tip: the Worn Notebook explains every glyph. Mana regenerates over time.
3. **Building a Spell**: checkmark *(after: Novice Spell Book)*
   > What: a spell is a row of glyphs read left to right: one form first (Projectile, Touch, Self, Underfoot...), then effects, each followed by the augments that change it.
   > How: open the book's spell screen (the key is in Controls, C by default), drag glyphs into a slot, name it and save. Click the checkmark when you have saved one.
   > Tip: augments only touch the glyph right before them: Break, Amplify mines harder; Amplify, Break does nothing.
4. **Mana**: checkmark *(after: Novice Spell Book)*
   > What: every cast spends mana from the bar above your hotbar; it refills on its own. Longer spells cost more.
   > How: raise your maximum and regeneration with better spell books, mage armor, mana amulets and threads. Click the checkmark when you've read this.
   > Tip: mana is personal. Source is the separate, stored energy that machines and rituals use.
5. **Archwood Logs**: 16x any of `item_tag(c:logs/archwood)` *(after: Novice Spell Book)*
   > What: archwood is the wood Ars Nouveau builds with: the Scribe's Table, Source Jars, the Imbuement Chamber and every ritual tablet.
   > How: find the bright red, blue, green or purple trees in archwood forests and cut any 16 logs. Bring saplings home too.
   > Tip: ritual tablets ask for a specific colour (purple for Flight and Binding, green for farming rituals), so plant all four.
6. **Dowsing Rod**: `ars_nouveau:dowsing_rod` *(after: Archwood Logs)*
   > What: a short burst of Scrying for budding amethyst, and magical creatures within 75 blocks start to glow. It has limited uses.
   > Chemistry: a geode is a hollow rock where silica-rich water slowly deposited SiO₂ crystals inward, layer by layer.
   > How: a gold ingot above two archwood planks.
   > Tip: a budding amethyst near home means endless source gems.
7. **Apprentice Spell Book**: `ars_nouveau:apprentice_spell_book` *(after: Novice Spell Book)*
   > What: the second spell book tier: more mana, more slots and access to tier 2 glyphs.
   > How: a crafting-grid upgrade: your Novice book with obsidian, 3 diamonds, 2 quartz blocks and 2 blaze rods (keeps your spells).
   > Tip: more mana means longer spells and more casts between rests.
8. **Scribe's Table**: `ars_nouveau:scribes_table` *(after: Archwood Logs)*
   > You remember an alphabet older than any language. Each letter you recover is a new glyph.
   > What: the Scribe's Table crafts new glyphs, which unlock more spell parts.
   > How: archwood slabs, gold nuggets and archwood logs. Use your spell book on it, pick a glyph, then throw the items on the table; each glyph also costs experience.
   > Tip: it pulls ingredients from nearby chests, which saves a lot of throwing.
9. **Tier 1 Glyphs**: checkmark *(after: Scribe's Table)*
   > What: tier 1 glyphs are the basics: Break, Harm, Ignite, Light, Harvest, Leap, Freeze and more, plus augments like Amplify and Delay. The Novice book can hold them.
   > How: scribe them at the Scribe's Table. Each costs a few common items plus 27 experience points; the quests around this one list each recipe.
   > Tip: a Touch + Break + Amplify spell is a magic pickaxe. Click the checkmark to open the tier.
10. **Ignite**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_ignite` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: sets blocks and creatures on fire for a short time. With Sensitive it makes Mage Fire, which never spreads or burns blocks.
   > Chemistry: fire needs three things at once: fuel, oxygen and heat. Take any one away and it goes out.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a flint and steel and 3 coal or charcoal, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Ignite then Flare (tier 2) is a classic fire combo.
11. **Craft**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_craft` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: opens a crafting grid wherever you are.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a crafting table, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a Self + Craft spell on a spare slot saves carrying a table.
12. **Rune**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_rune` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: places a temporary rune that casts the rest of the spell on whatever steps on it.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, runic chalk and a tripwire hook, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Runic Chalk makes permanent runes that can be recharged; this glyph's runes fade.
13. **Snare**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_snare` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: roots a creature in place so it can neither walk nor jump. Extend Time makes it last longer.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: earth essence and 4 cobwebs, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: snare a creeper, then walk away.
14. **Freeze**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_freeze` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: freezes water or lava in a small area and slows creatures. Ice becomes packed ice, packed ice becomes blue ice.
   > Chemistry: when water touches lava, the lava loses heat fast and solidifies into obsidian or cobblestone.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: water essence and 2 snow blocks, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Touch + Freeze makes a path across a lava lake.
15. **Delay**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_delay` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: pauses the spell for a moment before the glyphs to its right resolve.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, a repeater and a clock, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Extend Time lengthens the wait; Duration Down shortens it.
16. **Light**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_light` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: on a block it leaves a permanent light; on yourself it gives Night Vision. Amplify and Dampen change the brightness.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a lantern and a torch, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Projectile + Light lights a cave ceiling you can't reach.
17. **Place Block**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_place_block` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: places blocks from your hotbar where the spell lands.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and a dispenser, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: with AOE it lays a whole floor in one cast.
18. **Cut**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_cut` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: shears blocks and creatures (sheep, leaves, vines), or nicks anything that can't be sheared. Amplify uses an axe instead.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, shears and an iron sword, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: it costs no mana at all.
19. **Harm**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_harm` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: damages the target. Amplify hits harder; a time augment turns it into poison.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: earth essence and 3 iron swords, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: two Harms in a row do nothing extra: the target is briefly immune after a hit.
20. **Interact**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_interact` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: uses blocks and creatures as if you clicked them: levers, chests, animals.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, a lever, a wooden pressure plate and a button, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Projectile + Interact flips a lever across a chasm.
21. **Amplify**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_amplify` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: makes most effects stronger: more damage, and a higher mining level for Break.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a diamond pickaxe, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: stack it: each Amplify adds a little more power and mana cost.
22. **Phantom Block**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_phantom_block` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: creates a block that vanishes after a short while. Amplify makes it permanent.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: 8 glass blocks, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
