   > Tip: Underfoot + Phantom Block is an emergency bridge.
23. **Fell**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_fell` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: harvests entire trees, mushrooms, cactus and other plants. AOE raises how many blocks it takes.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: earth essence and a diamond axe, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: aim at the bottom log of a big archwood tree.
24. **Leap**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_leap` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: launches the target in the direction it faces. Amplify throws it further.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence and 3 Wilden Wings, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: pair it with Slowfall for a safe landing.
25. **Redstone Signal**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_redstone_signal` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: places a temporary redstone power source. Amplify and Dampen set its strength.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and 3 redstone blocks, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Touch + Redstone Signal opens an iron door with no button.
26. **Harvest**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_harvest` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: takes the produce of grown crops and leaves the plant in place.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: earth essence and an iron hoe, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: with AOE it clears a field in one cast.
27. **Break**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_break` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: breaks blocks of normal hardness. Amplify raises the mining level; Sensitive mines as if with shears.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: an iron pickaxe, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Touch + Break + Amplify is a magic pickaxe.
28. **Pick Up**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_pickup` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: pulls in item drops around where the spell lands. AOE widens the radius.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: 2 hoppers, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: end every mining spell with it so nothing is left behind.
29. **Launch**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_launch` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: throws a creature or block into the air.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence and 3 rabbit hides, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: on yourself it climbs a cliff; on a skeleton it ends the fight.
30. **Dispel**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_dispel` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: removes potion effects from the target and sends tamed summons back into their charm. A witch at half health vanishes and leaves Wixie shards.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence and 3 milk buckets, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: this is how you get a Wixie.
31. **Pull**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_pull` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: drags the target towards you; blocks hit by it fall towards you.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a fishing rod, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Sensitive stops it moving blocks.
32. **Gust**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_gust` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: pushes a target or block a short distance away from you.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence and 3 pistons, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: it clears a ledge of zombies in one cast.
33. **Toss**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_toss` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: places items from your inventory where the spell lands, or into a container it hits.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and a dropper, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Dampen halves the stack it throws; Amplify doubles it.
34. **Summon Steed**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_summon_steed` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons a saddled horse that leaves after a while. Summoning makes you sick for a bit, so no other summon until it wears off.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: 4 leather, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a fast way across the Overworld before you have flight.
35. **Summon Wolves**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_summon_wolves` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons two wolves that fight beside you for a while.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: conjuration essence, 3 bones and 4 Wilden Wings, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Extend Time keeps them around longer.
36. **Underfoot**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_underfoot` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: a form that casts the spell on the block beneath you.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: iron boots and a wooden pressure plate, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Underfoot + Break digs straight down; mind the lava.
37. **Sensitive**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_sensitive` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: lets forms target things they normally pass through (grass, fluids, air) and changes how several effects behave.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: scaffolding, a poppy and a water bucket, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: read each glyph's tooltip for what Sensitive changes.
38. **Evaporate**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_evaporate` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: deletes fluids in an area. AOE makes the area bigger.
   > Chemistry: real evaporation needs energy: about 2,260 joules for every gram of water boiled off.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and 3 sponges, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: drains a flooded cave in seconds.
39. **Bounce**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_bounce` *(after: Tier 1 Glyphs)*
   > What: gives the Bounce effect: you spring back up when you hit the ground. Amplify keeps more forward speed.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence and 3 slime balls, plus 27 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: it turns a long fall into a hop.
40. **Imbuement Chamber**: `ars_nouveau:imbuement_chamber` *(after: Archwood Logs)*
   > What: the Imbuement Chamber turns amethyst or lapis into source gems, and source gems into essences.
   > How: archwood planks and gold (check JEI). It slowly gathers Source by itself; Source Jars within 2 blocks make it much faster.
   > Tip: essence recipes want Arcane Pedestals with items right next to the chamber.
41. **Source Gems**: 16x `ars_nouveau:source_gem` *(after: Imbuement Chamber)*
   > What: source gems are the currency of Ars Nouveau: sourcestone, pedestals, relays, essences and charms all need them.
   > Chemistry: amethyst is quartz (SiO₂) tinted purple by iron impurities; lapis owes its blue to lazurite, an aluminosilicate holding sulfur radicals.
   > How: put an amethyst shard or a lapis lazuli in the Imbuement Chamber and wait; Source Jars nearby speed it up.
   > Tip: a budding amethyst geode or an amethyst farm turns into an endless gem supply.
42. **Source Jar**: `ars_nouveau:source_jar` *(after: Source Gems)*
   > You remember power you could pour from one vessel to another. Here it is again, in a jar.
   > What: Source is Ars Nouveau's stored magical energy. Jars hold it, and machines, rituals and helpers draw from jars nearby.
   > How: glass and archwood slabs. Place jars next to whatever spends Source; a comparator reads how full they are.
   > Tip: empty jars do nothing. The next step is a Sourcelink to fill them.
43. **Volcanic Sourcelink**: `ars_nouveau:volcanic_sourcelink` *(after: Source Jar)*
   > What: the Volcanic Sourcelink burns fuel and pushes the Source into nearby jars.
   > Chemistry: burning is fast oxidation: C + O₂ → CO₂ plus heat. The sourcelink claims that energy as Source.
   > How: two source gems, two gold ingots and a lava bucket. Feed it logs or coal with a hopper or pipe.
   > Tip: the other sourcelinks feed on crops (Agronomic), food (Mycelial), mob deaths (Vitalic) and potions (Alchemical).
44. **Vitalic Sourcelink**: `ars_nouveau:vitalic_sourcelink` *(after: Source Jar)*
   > What: the Vitalic Sourcelink gathers Source when creatures nearby die or age.
   > How: 2 source gems, 2 gold ingots and a glistering melon slice.
   > Tip: put it beside a mob farm's kill floor.
45. **Mycelial Sourcelink**: `ars_nouveau:mycelial_sourcelink` *(after: Source Jar)*
   > What: the Mycelial Sourcelink consumes food dropped nearby and turns it into Source; richer food gives more.
   > Chemistry: food energy is chemical energy: respiration runs C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O, slowly instead of in a flame.
   > How: 2 source gems, 2 gold ingots and a bowl of mushroom stew.
   > Tip: feed it from a crop farm's surplus with a hopper.
46. **Agronomic Sourcelink**: `ars_nouveau:agronomic_sourcelink` *(after: Source Jar)*
   > What: the Agronomic Sourcelink makes Source whenever plants around it grow.
   > Chemistry: plants store sunlight as sugar: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. The sourcelink sips some of that energy.
   > How: 2 source gems, 2 gold ingots and wheat.
   > Tip: an Agronomic Sourcelink next to a crop farm is free Source forever.
47. **Source Relays**: 2x `ars_nouveau:relay` *(after: Source Gems)*
   > What: relays carry Source from one jar to another, so your sourcelinks don't have to sit next to the machines that spend it.
   > How: gold ingots around a source gem block. Link them with a Dominion Wand (the Worn Notebook shows how). A Relay Splitter shares one input between many outputs.
   > Tip: put noisy sourcelink farms out of sight and relay the Source in.
48. **Four Archwoods**: `ars_nouveau:red_archwood_sapling`; `ars_nouveau:blue_archwood_sapling`; `ars_nouveau:green_archwood_sapling`; `ars_nouveau:purple_archwood_sapling` *(after: Archwood Logs)*
   > What: Blazing (red), Cascading (blue), Flourishing (green) and Vexing (purple) archwood. Each colour feeds different rituals.
   > How: break archwood leaves in the four kinds of archwood forest. Plant a few of each at home.
   > Tip: the Ritual of Awakening needs all four saplings at once.

### Ars Nouveau: Tier 2 Glyphs

*Ars Nouveau, continued: Tier 2 Glyphs*

1. **Archmage Spell Book**: `ars_nouveau:archmage_spell_book` *(after: Apprentice Spell Book, The Wilden Chimera)*
   > You remember when every word you spoke was a spell. This book is a reminder.
   > What: the last book tier, with tier 3 glyphs and the most mana.
   > How: crafting grid: the Apprentice book with 3 ender pearls, 2 emeralds, a Totem of Undying, a Nether Star and a Wilden Tribute.
   > Tip: the Wither and the Wilden Chimera both stand between you and this book.
2. **Tier 2 Glyphs**: checkmark *(after: Scribe's Table, Apprentice Spell Book)*
   > What: tier 2 adds the AOE, Pierce, Fortune, Extract, Extend Time and Dampen augments, and effects like Smelt, Crush, Grow, Exchange, Explosion and Heal.
   > How: scribe them with the Apprentice book (a Novice book can't hold them). Most want an essence from the Imbuement Chamber and 55 experience points.
   > Tip: Crush + AOE grinds cobble to sand and gravel in bulk. Click the checkmark to open the tier.
3. **Tier 3 Glyphs**: checkmark *(after: Scribe's Table, Archmage Spell Book)*
   > What: tier 3 glyphs are the strongest: Blink (teleport), Lightning, Fangs, Linger (a lasting zone), Split, Glide and the bigger summons.
   > How: scribe them with the Archmage book; each costs 160 experience points and rare items.
   > Tip: Glide works like an elytra, not like flight. Click the checkmark to open the tier.
4. **Flare**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_flare` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: a target that is already on fire bursts into cinders that hurt everything nearby and leave short-lived Mage Fire.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: fire essence, 2 flint and steels, 2 fire charges and a blaze rod, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: cast Ignite first, then Flare.
5. **Cold Snap**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_cold_snap` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: a wet, slowed or freezing target takes a burst of damage and sprays falling ice that slows its neighbours.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: water essence, a powder snow bucket and ice, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Conjure Water first makes any target 'wet'.
6. **Slowfall**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_slowfall` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: gives Slow Falling.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence, a Wilden Wing, 3 feathers, a blaze rod and nether wart, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Leap + Slowfall crosses a ravine.
7. **Crush**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_crush` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: grinds stone into gravel and gravel into sand, and flowers into extra dye; it also hurts creatures, more so when they swim.
   > Chemistry: real sand is mostly quartz grains, SiO₂, worn off rock by water and ice over a very long time.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: earth essence, a grindstone and a piston, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Sensitive makes it work on dropped items (JEI lists every recipe).
8. **Smelt**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_smelt` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: smelts blocks and dropped items where it lands. AOE does more at once; Dampen uses smoker recipes.
   > Chemistry: smelting an oxide ore means removing oxygen: carbon pulls it off, e.g. Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: fire essence, 4 blast furnaces and a blaze rod, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Break + Smelt mines sand straight into glass.
9. **Accelerate**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_accelerate` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: makes Projectile spells fly faster.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a powered rail, sugar and a clock, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: fast projectiles are easier to aim at moving targets.
10. **Grow**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_grow` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: makes plants grow as if bone-mealed.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: earth essence, 5 bone blocks and 3 seeds, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: AOE turns it into a field-wide fertiliser.
11. **Dampen**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_dampen` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: weakens most effects. Useful when a spell is too strong for the job.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a nether brick, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Dampen on Explosion makes a small, tidy blast.
12. **Invisibility**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_invisibility` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: turns the target invisible for a short time.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence, a fermented spider eye and a blaze rod, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: armour still shows; take it off to truly hide.
13. **Extract**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_extract` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: gives Break a silk-touch effect and stops Explosion destroying blocks. It can't be combined with Fortune.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: an emerald, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: pick up ores whole to process them in your machines for more yield.
14. **Duration Down**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_duration_down` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: shortens timed effects such as potions, Delay and Redstone Signal.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a clock and glowstone dust, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a short Redstone Signal is a one-tick pulse.
15. **Exchange**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_exchange` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: on blocks it swaps them for the block in your hotbar, as if silk-touched; on a creature it swaps your positions.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, an emerald block and 2 ender pearls, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: AOE + Exchange re-floors a room in one cast.
16. **Conjure Water**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_conjure_water` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: places water or puts out burning creatures; with Extend Time it keeps them wet.
   > Chemistry: water is H₂O: each molecule is bent, with the oxygen end slightly negative. That polarity is why it dissolves salts so well.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: water essence and a water bucket, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: it sets up Cold Snap and Lightning.
17. **Extend Time**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_extend_time` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: lengthens timed effects: buffs, Fangs, summons and more.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a clock and a redstone block, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: two Extend Times on Night Vision cover a whole caving trip.
18. **Heal**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_heal` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: restores a little health at the cost of some hunger. Undead take that amount as damage instead.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence, 4 glistering melon slices and a golden apple, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Projectile + Heal is an anti-zombie bolt.
19. **Pierce**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_pierce` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: lets projectiles pass through a target and keep going, and makes effects like Break also hit the block behind.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: an arrow and a Wilden Spike, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Break + Pierce + AOE digs a tunnel 3 wide and several deep.
20. **Fortune**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_fortune` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: raises drops from creatures killed by Harm and blocks broken by Break. It can't be combined with Extract.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a rabbit's foot, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: the same idea as the enchantment, in spell form.
21. **Ender Inventory**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_ender_inventory` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: opens your ender chest wherever you are.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and an ender chest, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a spare inventory on every expedition.
22. **AOE**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_aoe` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: makes the spell hit a wider area around the block it targets.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a firework star, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: every AOE adds one block of radius, and mana cost.
23. **Gravity**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_gravity` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: makes blocks and creatures fall. With Extend Time it stops players flying and doubles their fall damage.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence, 2 anvils and 3 feathers, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a useful counter to flying enemies.
24. **Decelerate**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_decelerate` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: makes Projectile spells fly slower.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: soul sand, a cobweb and a clock, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: slow projectiles are easier to follow with Linger or Orbit.
25. **Wind Shear**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_wind_shear` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: hurts targets that are off the ground, more the higher they are (up to 10 blocks). Grounded targets take nothing.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence and 3 iron swords, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Launch first, then Wind Shear.
26. **Sense Magic**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_sense_magic` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: gives Magic Find: magical creatures within 75 blocks glow, and spells on runes show.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence, a Dowsing Rod and Starbuncle shards, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: it finds Starbuncles and Whirlisprigs for their shards.
27. **Name**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_name` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: names a creature, a container or your off-hand item after the spell's name.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and a name tag, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a name tag in your hotbar overrides the spell's name.
28. **Firework**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_firework` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: launches a firework at the target. Amplify adds stars; Extend Time adds flight time.
   > Chemistry: firework colours come from metal ions: strontium burns red, copper blue-green, sodium yellow, barium green.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: fire essence, 2 firework rockets and a firework star, plus 55 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: carry a firework and the spell copies it.
29. **Explosion**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_explosion` *(after: Tier 2 Glyphs)*
   > What: causes an explosion where the spell lands. Amplify makes it a bit bigger and harder; AOE makes it much wider but not harder.
   > Chemistry: TNT is trinitrotoluene, C₇H₅N₃O₆: toluene nitrated with HNO₃ and H₂SO₄, the same acids your Ostwald and contact plants make.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: fire essence, 3 TNT and a fire charge, plus 55 experience points.
   > Tip: add Extract and the blast stops destroying the blocks it breaks.
30. **Intangible**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_intangible` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: turns blocks into air for a short time, then puts them back.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, 3 phantom membranes and 2 ender pearls, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: a temporary door into someone else's sealed base.
31. **Split**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_split` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: fires several projectiles at once, each carrying the effects.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a Relay Splitter, a Wilden Spike and a stonecutter, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Split + Break mines a row of blocks.
32. **Summon Vex**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_summon_vex` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons three vexes that attack hostile creatures until they take enough damage.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: conjuration essence and a Totem of Undying, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Extend Time keeps them fighting longer.
33. **Lightning**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_lightning` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: strikes lightning. Struck targets are Shocked and take more from the next bolt; wet targets and those wearing powered gear take extra.
   > Chemistry: a bolt heats the air to around 30,000 K; the expanding air is the thunder. It also joins N₂ and O₂ into NO: nature's own nitrogen fixation.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence, 3 lightning rods and a Heart of the Sea, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Conjure Water first, then Lightning.
34. **Blink**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_blink` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: teleports you where the spell lands; on Self it blinks you forward. With a Warp Scroll in your off hand it sends a hit creature to the scroll's spot.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence and 4 ender pearls, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Projectile + Blink is the fastest way across a valley.
35. **Fangs**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_fangs` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons evoker fangs towards the target; on Self they ring you.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: conjuration essence, 2 prismarine shards and a Totem of Undying, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Extend Time adds more fangs.
36. **Wither**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_wither` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: applies the Wither effect.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence and 3 wither skeleton skulls, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: pair it with Hex for heavy damage over time.
37. **Summon Decoy**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_summon_decoy` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons a copy of you that draws every nearby enemy.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: conjuration essence and 4 armor stands, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: cast it, step back, then use your AOE spells.
38. **Hex**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_hex` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: applies Hex: more damage while the target is poisoned, withering, burning or frozen, and half the healing and mana regeneration.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: abjuration essence, a fermented spider eye, 3 blaze rods and a wither rose, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Ignite + Hex is a strong opener.
39. **Orbit**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_orbit` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons three projectiles orbiting the target that cast the spell on anything they touch.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: a compass, an eye of ender and a blaze rod, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Self + Orbit + Harm is a spinning shield.
40. **Glide**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_glide` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: gives the Glide effect: you glide like an elytra wearer. It is not flight.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: air essence, an elytra and 3 diamonds, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: it still costs an elytra, so it's a convenience, not a shortcut.
41. **Summon Undead**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_summon_undead` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: summons skeleton allies that fight hostile creatures for a while. Augments change their weapons.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: conjuration essence, a bone and a wither skeleton skull, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Amplify gives them better weapons.
42. **Linger**: `ars_nouveau:glyph_linger` *(after: Tier 3 Glyphs)*
   > What: creates a field that keeps applying the spell to everything inside it for a while.
   > How: at the Scribe's Table: manipulation essence, dragon's breath, a diamond block and 2 blaze rods, plus 160 experience points. Learn it into your book afterwards.
   > Tip: Linger + Heal is a healing circle for a team.
43. **Ritual Brazier**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_brazier` *(after: Arcane Pedestals)*
   > You remember rites that changed the weather and the seasons. The brazier remembers them too.
   > What: rituals are area effects: sunrise, cloudshaping, overgrowth, flight and more. Each needs a brazier and a ritual tablet.
   > How: an Arcane Pedestal, a source gem block and three gold ingots (shapeless). Place it and right-click it with a ritual tablet.
   > Tip: most rituals draw Source from nearby jars, so build next to your source room.
44. **Ritual of Sunrise**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_sunrise` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: skips the night to sunrise.
   > How: a red archwood log, 3 dandelions and a clock (shapeless).
   > Tip: on a server it saves waiting for everyone to sleep.
45. **Ritual of Warping**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_warping` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: teleports everything around the brazier to the spot stored in a Warp Scroll.
   > How: a purple archwood log and a Warp Scroll (shapeless). The scroll is blank parchment with lapis and source gems (check JEI).
   > Tip: a team trip to a far base in one step.
46. **Ritual of Overgrowth**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_overgrowth` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: makes plants around the brazier grow, again and again, as if bone-mealed.
   > How: a green archwood log, 3 magebloom and 2 earth essences (shapeless).
   > Tip: the farming rituals Harvest, Forestation and Flowering also start from a green log (check JEI).
47. **Ritual of Moonfall**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_moonfall` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: skips the day to nightfall.
   > How: a blue archwood log, an ink sac, a coal block and a clock (shapeless).
   > Tip: night on demand is a quick way to hunt Wilden.
48. **Ritual of Fertility**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_fertility` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: breeds the animals around the brazier without feeding them by hand.
   > How: a green archwood log, 3 wheat, a golden apple and 2 blaze powder (shapeless).
   > Tip: cap your pens; it doesn't know when to stop.
49. **Ritual of Burrowing**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_burrowing` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: digs holes straight down from the brazier.
   > How: a green archwood log, an iron pickaxe and a coal block (shapeless).
   > Tip: ore it digs comes out as ore: it saves digging, not processing.
50. **Ritual of Challenge**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_challenge` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: calls a raid to the brazier, the way Bad Omen does.
   > How: a purple archwood log, an emerald block and an ink sac (shapeless).
   > Tip: a raid farm without hunting pillager captains.
51. **Ritual of Cloudshaping**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_cloudshaping` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: clears the sky, or starts rain or a storm.
   > How: a blue archwood log, a feather and a source gem block (shapeless).
   > Chemistry: rain forms when water vapour condenses on tiny particles; cloud seeding uses silver iodide, AgI, for the same job.
   > Tip: a storm on demand makes charged creepers and tridents easier.
52. **Ritual of Disintegration**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_disintegration` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: destroys hostile creatures near the brazier and leaves extra experience.
   > How: a red archwood log, 3 golden swords and 3 books (shapeless).
   > Tip: useful for glyph experience, which adds up fast in tier 3.
53. **Ritual of Restoration**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_restoration` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: heals and cures the creatures near the brazier, zombie villagers included.
   > How: a green archwood log, a golden apple and abjuration essence (shapeless).
   > Tip: curing zombie villagers gives you the best trade prices.
54. **Ritual of Awakening**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_awakening` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > You remember forests that stood up when you called. Some of them still do.
   > What: awakens nearby archwood trees into Weald Walkers that guard an area, and budding amethyst into an Amethyst Golem charm.
   > How: a green archwood log, one sapling of each colour and 4 source gems (shapeless). Run it next to the tree base or the budding amethyst.
   > Tip: add Book and Quills to the ritual and it makes Bookwyrm charms instead.
55. **Ritual of Flight**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_flight` *(after: Ritual Brazier, Wings of a God)*
   > You already remember the sky. Now your home remembers it too.
   > What: gives creative flight to players near the brazier, paid for with Source. It's base flight, not world flight.
   > Chemistry: hydrogen (H₂) is the lightest gas there is, 14 times less dense than air. It lifted the first balloons in 1783.
   > How: a purple archwood log, 3 Wilden Wings, 2 diamonds, an ender pearl and 2 hydrogen from the Dissolver (this pack's recipe). Put the tablet in the Ritual Brazier and keep the jars topped up.
   > Tip: this opens after the Infusion Pylon on purpose: real flight is a chemistry milestone.
56. **Ritual of Wilden Summoning**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_wilden_summon` *(after: Ritual Brazier, Wilden Hunt)*
   > What: summons the Wilden Chimera, Ars Nouveau's boss, at the brazier.
   > How: a purple archwood log, 3 Wilden drops (horns, spikes or wings, mixed is fine) and a lapis block (shapeless).
   > Tip: build a separate brazier away from your base for this one.
57. **Ritual of Scrying**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_scrying` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: Scrying highlights a chosen block (usually an ore) through walls for a while.
   > How: a purple archwood log, 3 spider eyes, glowstone and a source gem block. The Worn Notebook shows how to pick which block it reveals.
   > Tip: combine it with the spectrometer and the pack's deposit depths to find rich veins faster.
58. **Ritual of Binding**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_binding` *(after: Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: the Ritual of Binding turns a creature charm into its familiar form, a companion that rides along and grants a bonus.
   > How: a purple archwood log, blank parchment, an ender pearl and 3 source gems. Run it in the brazier with the charm nearby.
   > Tip: the Worn Notebook lists what each familiar gives.
59. **A Familiar**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:familiar_starbuncle)item(ars_nouveau:familiar_wixie)item(ars_nouveau:familiar_drygmy)item(ars_nouveau:familiar_whirlisprig)item(ars_nouveau:familiar_bookwyrm)item(ars_nouveau:familiar_amethyst_golem)item(ars_elemental:firenando_familiar)item(ars_elemental:flashjack_familiar)item(ars_elemental:siren_familiar))` *(after: Ritual of Binding)*
   > What: a familiar is a bound creature that rides along and gives a passive bonus: Starbuncles speed you up, Wixies boost potions, Bookwyrms cut spell costs.
   > How: run the Ritual of Binding with the creature's charm nearby to turn it into a familiar item. Use the item to call your familiar.
   > Tip: Ars Elemental adds elemental familiars (Firenando, Flashjack, Siren) that boost that school of magic.
60. **Ritual of Chunk Loading**: `ars_additions:ritual_chunk_loading` *(after: Ritual of Scrying)*
   > What: an Ars Additions ritual that keeps its chunk loaded while it has Source.
   > How: craft the tablet (check JEI) and run it in a Ritual Brazier next to your Source Jars.
   > Tip: FTB Chunks can also force-load claimed chunks; use whichever you prefer.
61. **The Wilden Chimera**: kill 1x `ars_nouveau:wilden_boss` *(after: Conjuration Essence, Ritual of Wilden Summoning)*
   > You remember beasts that were many beasts at once. You remember winning.
   > What: the Wilden Chimera combines all three Wilden. It drops Wilden Tribute, used for the Archmage book and Ars Elemental's Mark of Mastery.
   > How: run the Ritual of Wilden Summoning (quest above) in a brazier away from your base, and fight.
   > Tip: it has phases and calls spikes from the ground. Keep moving and bring healing.
62. **Two Roads to the Sky**: checkmark *(after: Ritual of Flight)*
   > What: a note on the Ritual of Flight and the pack's other flight sources.
   > How: read the second page, then click the checkmark.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > Ritual of Flight: the tablet is a purple archwood log, 3 Wilden Wings, 2 diamonds, an ender pearl and 2 hydrogen. The hydrogen is this pack's addition: no chemistry, no wings.
   > Range: the ritual only grants flight near its brazier and drains Source while you fly. It's base flight, not world flight.
   > Not flight: the Belt of Levitation, the Jump Ring and the Glide glyph help you move, but none of them is true flight.
   > Elsewhere: the Infusion Pylon with a Potion of Flying (hydrogen from the Dissolver), Iron Jetpacks (MI circuits) and the Angel Ring (digital circuit) all work anywhere. See Tools and Comfort.

### Ars Nouveau: Elemental Essences

*Fire, earth, water and the caster's tools*

1. **Potion Jar**: `ars_nouveau:potion_jar` *(after: Source Jar, Abjuration Essence)*
   > What: a Potion Jar stores a large amount of one potion, and pours it back into bottles.
   > How: a Source Jar and abjuration essence (shapeless).
   > Tip: a brewing Wixie can fill it for you.
2. **Alchemical Sourcelink**: `ars_nouveau:alchemical_sourcelink` *(after: Potion Jar)*
   > What: the Alchemical Sourcelink drinks potions from nearby Potion Jars and turns them into Source; stronger potions give more.
   > How: 2 source gems, 2 gold ingots and a brewing stand.
   > Tip: a Wixie brewing into a jar beside it makes a hands-free Source line.
3. **Sourcestone**: 32x `ars_nouveau:sourcestone` *(after: Source Gems)*
   > What: sourcestone is the building block of the Arcane Core, the Arcane Pedestals and the Enchanting Apparatus.
   > How: eight stone around one source gem gives eight sourcestone (any c:stones work). A stonecutter turns it into bricks and tiles.
   > Tip: make extra; it's a handsome building stone for your magic room.
4. **Arcane Pedestals**: 8x `ars_nouveau:arcane_pedestal` *(after: Sourcestone)*
   > What: pedestals hold the side ingredients for the Apparatus, the Imbuement Chamber and the Ritual Brazier.
   > How: sourcestone, gold nuggets and a source gem each (check JEI). Set them around the Apparatus, within a few blocks.
   > Tip: a hopper under a pedestal won't pull from it; load pedestals by hand or with a Starbuncle.
5. **Enchanting Apparatus**: `ars_nouveau:enchanting_apparatus`; `ars_nouveau:arcane_core` *(after: Arcane Pedestals)*
   > You remember forging with more hands than two. The pedestals will have to stand in for them.
   > What: the Apparatus sits on an Arcane Core and fuses items from the surrounding Arcane Pedestals, using Source.
   > How: the core is sourcestone, gold and a source gem; the Apparatus is sourcestone, gold and a diamond. Core first, Apparatus on top, then put the main item in it and right-click (check JEI).
   > Tip: it also applies enchantments to gear: more ways to make divine equipment.
6. **Magebloom Seeds**: 3x `ars_nouveau:magebloom_crop` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: magebloom is a flower crop; each flower gives 4 magebloom fiber for robes, threads, parchment and runic chalk.
   > How: in the Apparatus: any seeds in the middle, 4 source gems on the pedestals. Plant them like wheat.
   > Tip: a small magebloom field early saves a lot of waiting later.
7. **Magebloom Fiber**: 16x `ars_nouveau:magebloom_fiber` *(after: Magebloom Seeds)*
   > What: magebloom fiber is the cloth of Ars Nouveau: robes, threads, the Alteration Table, parchment and runic chalk.
   > Chemistry: real fibres like cotton are cellulose: long chains of glucose (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ held together by hydrogen bonds.
   > How: each magebloom flower crafts into 4 fiber. Keep some seeds back so the field keeps growing.
   > Tip: a Harvest ritual or a Whirlisprig keeps the field going without you.
8. **Spell Parchment**: `ars_nouveau:spell_parchment` *(after: Magebloom Fiber)*
   > What: Spell Parchment carries one spell. Turrets, runes and other casters read their spell from it.
   > How: Blank Parchment is paper ringed with magebloom fiber. Put it on the Scribe's Table, pick the spell in your book, then sneak and use the book on the table.
   > Tip: label your parchments with the spell's name; they all look alike.
9. **Runic Chalk**: `ars_nouveau:runic_chalk` *(after: Spell Parchment, Manipulation Essence)*
   > What: Runic Chalk draws permanent runes that cast a spell on whatever walks over them; they can be recharged.
   > How: manipulation essence, bone meal and magebloom fiber (shapeless). Draw a rune, then use parchment or your book on it to give it a spell.
   > Tip: Mirrorweave (magebloom blocks around conjuration essence) hides a rune or a secret door; Sense Magic reveals both.
10. **Dominion Wand**: `ars_nouveau:dominion_wand` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: the Dominion Wand links blocks and creatures: relays to jars, Starbuncles to chests, golems and Weald Walkers to their homes.
   > How: a stick in the Enchanting Apparatus with 2 source gems and a gold ingot on the pedestals.
   > Tip: click the first thing, then the second. Sneak-click shows what is already linked.
11. **Starbuncle**: `ars_nouveau:starbuncle_charm` *(after: Dominion Wand)*
   > What: a Starbuncle carries items from one chest to another. Cute logistics.
   > How: befriend a wild Starbuncle for its shards (the Worn Notebook explains how), then put the shards in the Apparatus with 4 gold ingots.
   > Tip: use a Dominion Wand to set where it picks up and where it drops off.
12. **Too Cool for Logistics**: `ars_nouveau:starbuncle_shades` *(after: Starbuncle)*
   > You remember having servants who took themselves very seriously. This one does not.
   > What: Starbuncle Shades: tinted glass and a source gem. Give them to a Starbuncle.
   > Tip: they do nothing useful. That is the point.
13. **Wixie**: `ars_nouveau:wixie_charm` *(after: Dominion Wand)*
   > What: a Wixie works a cauldron: it repeats a crafting recipe or brews potions from nearby chests.
   > How: cast a Dispel spell on a witch at half health or less for Wixie Shards, then the Apparatus with a sapling, an emerald, a crafting table and a brewing stand.
   > Tip: pair a brewing Wixie with a Potion Jar to keep your favourite potion stocked.
14. **Whirlisprig**: `ars_nouveau:whirlisprig_charm` *(after: Dominion Wand)*
   > What: a Whirlisprig speeds up plant growth around it and makes Source from a varied garden.
   > How: Whirlisprig shards in the Apparatus with a source gem, magebloom (seed and flower), a diamond, three saplings and wheat seeds.
   > Tip: the more different plants nearby, the happier it is.
15. **Drygmy**: `ars_nouveau:drygmy_charm` *(after: Dominion Wand)*
   > What: a Drygmy at its henge collects drops from nearby mobs without hurting them.
   > How: Drygmy shards (the Worn Notebook explains how to befriend one) in the Apparatus with fish, wheat, an apple, a carrot, seeds and 3 source gems.
   > Tip: the Worn Notebook shows the henge layout and what the Drygmy needs nearby.
16. **Amethyst Golem**: `ars_nouveau:amethyst_golem_charm` *(after: Dominion Wand, Ritual of Awakening)*
   > What: the Amethyst Golem grows and harvests amethyst near its home, turns amethyst blocks into budding amethyst and stores the shards.
   > Chemistry: amethyst is quartz, SiO₂, coloured purple by Fe³⁺ ions that natural radiation has changed in the crystal.
   > How: run the Ritual of Awakening near budding amethyst. Place the charm, then give the golem a home with the Dominion Wand (a chest makes it store shards).
   > Tip: golem shards in an Imbuement Chamber are a hands-free source gem line.
17. **Enchanter's Sword**: `ars_nouveau:enchanters_sword` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: the Enchanter's Sword casts its stored spell on whatever it hits, as if by Touch, and boosts your spell damage.
   > How: a diamond sword in the Apparatus with a diamond, 2 gold blocks and 2 source gem blocks. Inscribe it at the Scribe's Table with a spell that has no form (e.g. Ignite, Extend Time).
   > Tip: a short Hex or Snare spell makes every hit count.
18. **Enchanter's Shield**: `ars_nouveau:enchanters_shield` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: blocking a hit gives you a short burst of Mana Regeneration and Spell Damage, and the shield slowly repairs itself with your mana.
   > How: a shield in the Apparatus with 2 gold blocks and 2 source gem blocks.
   > Tip: it keeps enchantments from the shield you put in.
19. **Enchanter's Mirror**: `ars_nouveau:enchanters_mirror` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus, Manipulation Essence)*
   > What: the mirror casts one spell on you, cheaper and longer than from the book.
   > How: a source gem block in the Apparatus with 2 glass, 2 manipulation essences, 2 archwood logs and 2 gold ingots.
   > Tip: inscribe it with a spell that has no form, such as Night Vision (Light) with Extend Time.
20. **Enchanter's Bow**: `ars_nouveau:spell_bow` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus, Manipulation Essence)*
   > What: with enough mana, the Enchanter's Bow turns your arrows into spell arrows that carry its stored spell; with no arrows it fires a harmless spell arrow.
   > How: a bow in the Apparatus with a source gem block, a gold block and manipulation essence.
   > Tip: a Snare or Hex spell on the bow sets up every melee fight.
21. **Light and Void**: `ars_nouveau:jar_of_light`; `ars_nouveau:void_jar` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: the Jar of Light summons a light that follows you; the Jar of Voiding deletes chosen items as you pick them up, for a little mana.
   > Chemistry: real 'cold light' exists: in a glow stick, a peroxide reaction excites a dye that gives off light instead of heat.
   > How: both are a glass bottle in the Apparatus. Light: 4 glowstone, 2 redstone lamps and 2 glass. Voiding: a lava bucket, a bucket, an Allow Scroll and an ender pearl.
   > Tip: a Void Jar set to cobblestone and dirt keeps your inventory clean while mining.
22. **Rings of Discount**: `ars_nouveau:ring_of_lesser_discount`; `ars_nouveau:ring_of_greater_discount` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: discount rings cut the mana cost of every spell you cast. You have two ring slots.
   > How: a Ring of Potential (iron nuggets and a source gem) in the Apparatus with 4 diamonds, 2 ender pearls and 2 source gems. The Greater ring is the lesser one with 4 diamonds, 2 blaze rods and 2 source gems.
   > Tip: make the lesser ring twice and upgrade one; the two stack.
23. **Belt of Unstable Gifts**: `ars_nouveau:belt_of_unstable_gifts` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: the belt hands you a random helpful potion effect every so often.
   > How: a Mundane Belt in the Apparatus with sugar, nether wart, a blaze rod, glowstone dust, a fermented spider eye, redstone, a brewing stand and a feather.
   > Tip: you can't choose the effect; it's a bonus, not a plan.
24. **Belt of Levitation**: `ars_nouveau:belt_of_levitation` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus, Air Essence)*
   > What: the Belt of Levitation lets you rise by sneaking in mid-air. It is climbing, not flight.
   > How: a Mundane Belt in the Apparatus with 4 gold ingots, 3 feathers and air essence.
   > Tip: it also softens falls a little; real flight is still a chemistry milestone.
25. **Mana Amulets**: `ars_nouveau:amulet_of_mana_boost`; `ars_nouveau:amulet_of_mana_regen` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: amulets are curios that raise your maximum mana (Boost) or how fast it comes back (Regen). You wear one at a time.
   > How: a Dull Trinket (iron nuggets and a source gem) in the Apparatus. Boost: 3 diamonds and 5 source gems. Regen: 2 diamonds, 2 gold and 4 source gems.
   > Tip: Regen suits short, frequent spells; Boost suits big ones.
26. **Enchanter's Wand**: `ars_nouveau:wand` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus, Manipulation Essence, Air Essence)*
   > What: the wand fires its one stored spell as an accelerated projectile.
   > How: an archwood log in the Apparatus with 4 source gems, 2 gold ingots, air essence and manipulation essence.
   > Tip: inscribe it with a spell that has no form of its own, e.g. just Break, or Harm + Amplify.
27. **Ender Source Jar**: `ars_additions:ender_source_jar` *(after: Storage Lectern)*
   > What: an Ars Additions jar whose Source is shared with your other Ender Source Jars, wherever they are.
   > How: a Source Jar in the Apparatus with 4 ender pearls and 4 popped chorus fruit.
   > Tip: one at home and one at an outpost makes a Source network without relays.
28. **Storage Lectern**: `ars_nouveau:storage_lectern`; 2x `ars_nouveau:repository` *(after: Enchanting Apparatus)*
   > What: the Storage Lectern shows the contents of linked Repositories and chests in one searchable screen.
   > How: a lectern with 4 chests in the Apparatus; Repositories are archwood logs and gold nuggets. Link them with a Dominion Wand.
   > Tip: it's small and cheap; AE2 or Occultism storage scale further.
29. **Spell Turret**: `ars_nouveau:spell_turret` *(after: Storage Lectern)*
   > What: a turret casts the spell you inscribe into it whenever it gets a redstone signal, using Source from nearby jars.
   > How: the Basic Spell Turret is source gems, gold and a redstone block; upgrade it in the Apparatus with a source gem block and 2 blaze rods.
   > Tip: a turret with Break or Harvest on a clock is a simple farm.
30. **Ars Additions Charms**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_additions:undying_charm)item(ars_additions:fall_prevention_charm)item(ars_additions:fire_resistance_charm)item(ars_additions:night_vision_charm)item(ars_additions:water_breathing_charm)item(ars_additions:void_protection_charm))` *(after: Rings of Discount)*
   > What: Ars Additions charms save you once from a specific danger: falling, fire, drowning, the void, or death itself.
   > How: made in the Enchanting Apparatus around a glass bottle (the Undying Charm takes a Totem of Undying, crying obsidian and glowstone). Recharge them in the Imbuement Chamber.
   > Tip: a Void Protection Charm (stable warp scroll and end stone bricks) is cheap insurance in the End.
31. **Handy Haversack**: `ars_additions:handy_haversack` *(after: Storage Lectern)*
   > What: the Handy Haversack links to a container so items you pick up go straight there.
   > How: craft it (check JEI), then bind it to a chest or your storage as its tooltip says.
   > Tip: bind it to your AE2 or Occultism storage interface for a bottomless pocket.
32. **Warp Scrolls**: `ars_nouveau:stable_warp_scroll` *(after: Ender Source Jar)*
   > What: a Warp Scroll remembers a spot and takes you back once; the Stable Warp Scroll can be reused.
   > How: Warp Scroll: blank parchment, 4 lapis and 4 source gems. Stabilize it in the Apparatus with 4 blaze powder and 2 ender pearls.
   > Tip: a Ritual of Warping (purple log + warp scroll) does the same for creatures around the brazier.
33. **Fire Essence**: 2x `ars_nouveau:fire_essence` *(after: Source Gems)*
   > What: essences are source gems imbued with one idea. Fire essence goes into fire glyphs, threads and Ars Elemental gear.
   > Chemistry: gunpowder is about 75% saltpetre (KNO₃), 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur: the nitrate supplies the oxygen, so it burns without air.
   > How: Imbuement Chamber: a source gem, with flint and steel, a torch and gunpowder on nearby pedestals (2,000 Source).
   > Tip: Arcane Pedestals next to the chamber hold the extra ingredients.
34. **Earth and Water**: `ars_nouveau:earth_essence`; `ars_nouveau:water_essence` *(after: Fire Essence)*
   > What: earth essence feeds growth rituals and earth spells; water essence makes Sanctuary, the Everfull Urn and water foci.
   > Chemistry: burned kelp was once Europe's source of soda ash (Na₂CO₃), and in 1811 the first iodine was isolated from seaweed ash.
   > How: earth: an iron ingot, seeds and dirt on pedestals. Water: a water bucket, a snow block and kelp. Both 2,000 Source.
   > Tip: keep a stack of source gems ready; essences go fast.
35. **Abjuration Essence**: `ars_nouveau:abjuration_essence` *(after: Earth and Water)*
   > What: abjuration essence makes Potion Jars, the Potion Melder, Potion Flasks and Restoration.
   > How: Imbuement Chamber: a source gem, with a fermented spider eye, sugar and a milk bucket on pedestals (2,000 Source).
   > Tip: a Source Jar plus abjuration essence makes a Potion Jar, which stores potions by the litre.
36. **Manipulation Essence**: `ars_nouveau:manipulation_essence` *(after: Abjuration Essence)*
   > What: manipulation essence goes into the Enchanter's Wand, Spell Bow, Repairing thread, runic chalk and Containment.
   > How: Imbuement Chamber: a source gem, with a stone button, redstone and a clock on pedestals (2,000 Source).
   > Tip: it also converts some blocks into others, such as stone into granite or tuff (check JEI).
37. **Anima Essence**: `sauce:anima_essence` *(after: Manipulation Essence)*
   > What: anima essence is the eighth essence, used for the Mark of Mastery and necromantic gear.
   > Chemistry: bone meal comes from bone, which is mostly hydroxyapatite, a calcium phosphate (Ca₅(PO₄)₃OH).
   > How: Imbuement Chamber: a source gem, with a wither skeleton skull, bone meal and a golden apple on pedestals (3,000 Source).
   > Tip: the skulls come from Nether fortresses, or Occultism's Wild Hunt.
38. **Air Essence**: `ars_nouveau:air_essence` *(after: Wilden Wings)*
   > What: air essence makes the Jump Ring, the Belt of Levitation, air foci and several threads.
   > How: Imbuement Chamber: a source gem, with a feather, a Wilden Wing and arrows on pedestals (2,000 Source).
   > Tip: save a few wings for the Ritual of Flight before spending them here.
39. **Conjuration Essence**: `ars_nouveau:conjuration_essence` *(after: Air Essence)*
   > What: conjuration essence feeds summoning glyphs and can also make end stone or soul sand (check JEI).
   > How: Imbuement Chamber: a source gem, with a Wilden Horn, Starbuncle shards and a book on pedestals (2,000 Source).
   > Tip: the Mark of Mastery needs one of every essence, so make this one early.
40. **Wilden Hunt**: kill 5x `ars_nouveau:wilden_hunter` *(after: Novice Spell Book)*
   > What: Wilden are Ars Nouveau's wild magical beasts. Hunters charge, Stalkers fly, Guardians throw spikes.
   > How: they roam the Overworld at night, more often near archwood forests and Wilden dens. Bring a shield.
   > Tip: keep every horn, spike and wing they drop. Rituals need them.
41. **Wilden Wings**: 3x `ars_nouveau:wilden_wing` *(after: Wilden Hunt)*
   > What: Wilden Wings drop from Wilden Stalkers, the flying ones.
   > How: hunt Stalkers at night. The Ritual of Flight tablet needs three wings (purple archwood log, 3 wings, 2 diamonds, an ender pearl).
   > Tip: a Ritual of Wilden Summoning will need three more Wilden drops, so keep hunting.
42. **Mark of Mastery**: `ars_elemental:mark_of_mastery` *(after: The Wilden Chimera, Anima Essence)*
   > What: the Mark of Mastery upgrades elemental foci and turns Arcanist armor into elemental mage armor.
   > How: imbue a Wilden Tribute with all seven essences plus anima essence on the pedestals (check JEI). One tribute gives five marks.
   > Tip: five marks is a focus plus most of an armor set; plan before you spend them.
43. **Lesser Elemental Focus**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:lesser_fire_focus)item(ars_elemental:lesser_water_focus)item(ars_elemental:lesser_earth_focus)item(ars_elemental:lesser_air_focus))` *(after: Anima Essence)*
   > What: an Ars Elemental focus is a curio that strengthens one school of spells (fire, water, earth or air) and lowers its cost.
   > Chemistry: the four classical elements were the first attempt at a periodic table. You know there are 118, but the spells don't.
   > How: in the Imbuement Chamber: an amethyst shard with 3 matching essences and 3 gold ingots on pedestals (5,000 Source).
   > Tip: choose the school your favourite spell uses most.
44. **Greater Elemental Focus**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:fire_focus)item(ars_elemental:water_focus)item(ars_elemental:earth_focus)item(ars_elemental:air_focus))` *(after: Lesser Elemental Focus, Mark of Mastery)*
   > What: the full focus gives a much bigger bonus to its school and protects you from matching hazards.
   > How: put the lesser focus in the Enchanting Apparatus with a Mark of Mastery on a pedestal (5,000 Source).
   > Tip: a fire focus pairs well with Ignite and Flare; a water focus with Watery Grave.
45. **Elemental Mage Armor**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:fire_hat)item(ars_elemental:aqua_hat)item(ars_elemental:earth_hat)item(ars_elemental:air_hat)item(ars_elemental:fire_robes)item(ars_elemental:aqua_robes)item(ars_elemental:earth_robes)item(ars_elemental:air_robes))` *(after: Mark of Mastery)*
   > What: Ars Elemental turns Arcanist armor into fire, water, earth or air armor, each with resistances and a spell bonus.
   > How: in the Enchanting Apparatus: an Arcanist piece plus a Mark of Mastery, a netherite ingot and two matching essences (7,000 Source).
   > Tip: a full set matching your focus makes that school very cheap to cast.
46. **Everfull Urn**: `ars_elemental:everfull_urn` *(after: Earth and Water)*
   > What: the Everfull Urn pushes water into adjacent tanks and machines for free.
   > Chemistry: water is the feedstock for half your chemistry: electrolysis splits 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
   > How: a flower pot in the Apparatus with a source gem, 2 water essences and 2 prismarine shards.
   > Tip: one next to an electrolyzer saves a pump.
47. **Caster's Bag**: `ars_elemental:caster_bag` *(after: Manipulation Essence)*
   > What: the Curio Bag holds trinkets and charms; the Caster's Bag is its upgrade that also takes spell books and caster tomes.
   > How: Curio Bag: a chest in magebloom fiber. Then the Apparatus with 2 manipulation essences, 2 blaze powder and 2 gold blocks.
   > Tip: it frees hotbar slots for tools.
48. **Mage Armor**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:sorcerer_robes)item(ars_nouveau:arcanist_robes)item(ars_nouveau:battlemage_robes))` *(after: Magebloom Fiber)*
   > What: Ars Nouveau armor comes in three styles (Sorcerer, Arcanist, Battlemage). Each piece adds mana and mana regeneration.
   > How: made in the Enchanting Apparatus around a golden armor piece with 4 magebloom fiber (check JEI for each style).
   > Tip: grow magebloom early; every piece needs fiber.
49. **Armor Tiers**: checkmark *(after: Mage Armor)*
   > What: mage armor has three tiers. Each tier raises mana and opens more thread slots.
   > How: put the armor in the Apparatus: tier 2 needs 2 blaze rods (2,500 Source), tier 3 needs 2 ender pearls and a chorus fruit (5,000 Source).
   > Tip: click the checkmark once you've upgraded a piece.
50. **Alteration Table**: `ars_nouveau:alteration_table`; 2x `ars_nouveau:blank_thread` *(after: Mage Armor)*
   > What: the Alteration Table holds a piece of mage armor and lets you put threads (perks) into its slots.
   > How: the table is a Scribe's Table with magebloom fiber; blank threads are magebloom fiber and gold nuggets.
   > Tip: right-click the table with armor, then with threads.
51. **Threads**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:thread_spellpower)item(ars_nouveau:thread_magic_capacity)item(ars_nouveau:thread_repairing)item(ars_nouveau:thread_warding)item(ars_nouveau:thread_feather)item(ars_nouveau:thread_high_step))` *(after: Alteration Table)*
   > What: threads add perks: Spellpower, Magic Capacity, Repairing, Warding, Feather Falling, Step Height and more.
   > How: a blank thread in the Apparatus with the thread's ingredients (Repairing: an anvil and 2 manipulation essences; check JEI for the rest).
   > Tip: Spellpower takes one of every essence; it's worth it for a main spell set.
52. **Containment**: `ars_nouveau:mob_jar`; `ars_nouveau:ritual_containment` *(after: Manipulation Essence, Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: Containment Jars hold a living mob. Chickens still lay, cows can be milked, sheep sheared, and a jarred blaze lights the room.
   > How: the jar is glass and archwood slabs. The Ritual of Containment (purple log, manipulation essence, 3 glass bottles) puts a mob within 3 blocks into a nearby jar.
   > Tip: a Drygmy counts jarred mobs as if they were roaming free.
53. **Source Spawner**: `ars_additions:source_spawner` *(after: Containment, Drygmy)*
   > What: an Ars Additions spawner that reads nearby Containment Jars to decide what to spawn and pays Source for each mob. A redstone signal turns it off.
   > How: a Drygmy charm in the Apparatus with a summon focus and conjuration essence.
   > Tip: it spawns mobs without their guaranteed drops, so it's for farms of normal drops, not boss loot.
54. **A Full Mage Set**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:sorcerer_hood)item(ars_nouveau:arcanist_hood)item(ars_nouveau:battlemage_hood))`; 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:sorcerer_robes)item(ars_nouveau:arcanist_robes)item(ars_nouveau:battlemage_robes))`; 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:sorcerer_leggings)item(ars_nouveau:arcanist_leggings)item(ars_nouveau:battlemage_leggings))`; 1x any of `or(item(ars_nouveau:sorcerer_boots)item(ars_nouveau:arcanist_boots)item(ars_nouveau:battlemage_boots))` *(after: Mage Armor)*
   > What: four pieces of mage armor, any style mixed: every piece adds mana and regeneration, and each one is a thread slot.
   > How: each piece is the matching golden armor piece in the Apparatus with magebloom fiber (check JEI per style).
   > Tip: Arcanist pieces are needed later for Ars Elemental's elemental armor.
55. **A Full Elemental Set**: 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:fire_hat)item(ars_elemental:aqua_hat)item(ars_elemental:earth_hat)item(ars_elemental:air_hat))`; 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:fire_robes)item(ars_elemental:aqua_robes)item(ars_elemental:earth_robes)item(ars_elemental:air_robes))`; 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:fire_leggings)item(ars_elemental:aqua_leggings)item(ars_elemental:earth_leggings)item(ars_elemental:air_leggings))`; 1x any of `or(item(ars_elemental:fire_boots)item(ars_elemental:aqua_boots)item(ars_elemental:earth_boots)item(ars_elemental:air_boots))` *(after: Elemental Mage Armor)*
   > You remember wearing a single element like a cloak. Now you wear it like a lab coat.
   > What: all four slots in Ars Elemental armor. Matching pieces stack their school bonus and resistances.
   > How: each Arcanist piece in the Apparatus with a Mark of Mastery, a netherite ingot and two matching essences.
   > Tip: that's four marks and four netherite: plan it with your Wilden Tribute.
56. **Two Ring Slots**: checkmark *(after: Rings of Discount)*
   > What: you can wear two rings at once, and their discounts add up.
   > How: wear a Greater and a Lesser ring together, or two Greater rings once you can afford them. Click the checkmark when both slots are full.
   > Tip: the rings quest above asks for one of each; this is the reminder to wear both.

### Occultism

*Spirits, pentacles, otherworld storage and miners that dig where you can't.*

1. **Before You Summon**: checkmark; checkmark
   > What: Occultism is ritual magic: chalk circles, bowls of ingredients and spirits bound by name. Each spirit rank (foliot, djinni, afrit, marid) opens the next.
   > How: the Dictionary of Spirits explains every ritual and shows each pentacle in 3D. Tick both boxes once you have it.
   > Tip: pack gates: miners can't dig the chemistry-milestone ores, and every crusher spirit gives 2 dust per ore.
2. **Demon's Dream Seeds**: `occultism:datura_seeds` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember seeing everything at once. A strange seed in the grass promises some of it back.
   > What: Demon's Dream is the plant every Occultism path starts from: its fruit opens the Third Eye, its seeds make the Dictionary.
   > How: break grass until a Demon's Dream seed drops. Plant it on farmland.
   > Tip: replant the first seeds; you'll want a small field.
3. **Dictionary of Spirits**: `occultism:dictionary_of_spirits` *(after: Demon's Dream Seeds)*
   > What: the Dictionary of Spirits is Occultism's guide: rituals, pentacles in 3D, spirits and their jobs.
   > How: a book and a Demon's Dream seed, shapeless.
   > Tip: its pentacle pages can project the circle into the world for you to trace.
4. **Demon's Dream**: 4x `occultism:datura` *(after: Demon's Dream Seeds)*
   > What: eating Demon's Dream Fruit gives the Third Eye: you see Otherworld blocks hidden behind normal ones.
   > How: grow the seeds and harvest the fruit. Eat one when you want to look.
   > Tip: with the Third Eye active, otherworld trees appear among normal oaks.
5. **Strike a Spark**: `minecraft:flint_and_steel` *(after: Demon's Dream, Dictionary of Spirits)*
   > What: spiritfire is lit from Demon's Dream Fruit, and flint and steel is the match.
   > Chemistry: flint and steel sparks are tiny shavings of iron that oxidise so fast in air they glow: 4Fe + 3O₂ → 2Fe₂O₃.
   > How: an iron ingot and a flint.
   > Tip: the same lighter starts the unbound afrit ritual much later.
6. **Spiritfire**: 16x `occultism:otherstone`; `occultism:otherworld_sapling_natural`; `occultism:spirit_attuned_gem` *(after: Strike a Spark)*
   > What: spiritfire doesn't hurt you and doesn't destroy items: things thrown into it come out converted.
   > Chemistry: andesite, the input for otherstone, is a grey volcanic rock made mostly of plagioclase feldspar.
   > How: throw a Demon's Dream Fruit on the ground and light it. Then throw in andesite (otherstone), an oak sapling (otherworld sapling) and a diamond (spirit-attuned gem).
   > Tip: books, feathers and black dye also go in: they come out as taboo books, awakened feathers and purified ink.
7. **Divination Rod**: `occultism:divination_rod` *(after: Spiritfire)*
   > What: the rod points toward otherworld blocks such as otherstone and otherworld trees.
   > How: gold ingots, glass and a spirit-attuned gem. Use it as the Dictionary explains to pick a target.
   > Tip: handy for finding an otherworld grove before you have saplings.
8. **Spirit-Attuned Gems**: 4x `occultism:spirit_attuned_gem` *(after: Spiritfire)*
   > What: spirit-attuned gems are in almost every spirit tool: magic lamps, lenses, the infused pickaxe, stabilizers and crystals.
   > Chemistry: a diamond is pure carbon in a rigid tetrahedral lattice, which is why it survives spiritfire unchanged in substance.
   > How: throw diamonds into spiritfire. Four gems make a Spirit-Attuned Crystal, which the mineshaft and bigger pentacles need.
   > Tip: keep a few diamonds aside for this from the start.
9. **Silver**: 8x any of `item_tag(c:ingots/silver)` *(after: Demon's Dream)*
   > What: silver goes into magic lamps, lens frames, satchels, the infused pickaxe and storage remotes.
   > Chemistry: silver (Ag) is the best electrical conductor of all metals. It tarnishes black when traces of H₂S turn its surface into Ag₂S.
   > How: mine and smelt silver ore; any silver ingot counts (they're unified).
   > Tip: MI's ore processing gives silver as a byproduct too.
10. **Otherworld Trees**: 8x `occultism:otherworld_log`; 3x `occultism:otherworld_ashes` *(after: Spiritfire)*
   > What: otherworld trees look like oaks unless you have the Third Eye. Their logs burn in spiritfire to otherworld ashes, half of white chalk.
   > Chemistry: real wood ash is mostly calcium and potassium carbonates. Potash (K₂CO₃ leached from 'pot ash') gave potassium its name.
   > How: grow the otherworld sapling from spiritfire and cut it while under the Third Eye. Burn logs for ashes.
   > Tip: a foliot sapling trader later sells stable saplings that don't need the Third Eye.
11. **Burnt Otherstone**: 3x `occultism:burnt_otherstone` *(after: Spiritfire)*
   > What: burnt otherstone counts as otherstone dust, the base of every chalk.
   > How: cut or craft otherstone into polished otherstone, then smelt it in a furnace.
   > Tip: make a stack; every new chalk colour starts from white impure chalk.
12. **How a Ritual Works**: checkmark *(after: Spiritfire)*
   > What: a ritual needs a chalk pentacle, a Golden Sacrificial Bowl in the middle, ingredients in plain bowls around it, and an activation item (usually a bound book).
   > How: put the ingredients in the bowls, then right-click the golden bowl with the activation item. Some rituals also want a sacrifice killed nearby, or an item used. Tick the box when you've read this.
   > Tip: the Dictionary's ritual pages list all of that per ritual, and JEI shows every ritual recipe.
13. **Familiars**: checkmark *(after: How a Ritual Works)*
   > What: familiars are small spirits that stay with you and help: the greedy familiar picks up items, the bat gives night vision, the blacksmith repairs.
   > How: each has its own summoning ritual (the Dictionary lists them). Tick the box when you've read this.
   > Tip: a Familiar Ring, later, lets you wear one.
14. **The Butcher Knife**: `occultism:butcher_knife` *(after: How a Ritual Works)*
   > What: animals killed with the Butcher Knife drop tallow, the wax of Occultism's large candles.
   > Chemistry: tallow is rendered animal fat: triglycerides of stearic, palmitic and oleic acid, the stuff of the first candles.
   > How: iron and sticks. Kill pigs, cows or sheep with it.
   > Tip: a small animal pen pays for a lot of candles.
15. **Candles and a Crystal**: 4x any of `item_tag(minecraft:candles)`; `occultism:spirit_attuned_crystal` *(after: The Butcher Knife, Spirit-Attuned Gems)*
   > What: candles in a pentacle steady it, so summoned spirits last longer. The Spirit-Attuned Crystal anchors bigger pentacles and goes into the mineshaft and miners.
   > Chemistry: a real crystal is a lattice that repeats in three dimensions; four small gems pressed together would only be a polycrystal.
   > How: a large candle is string over tallow (any candle counts here). The crystal is four spirit-attuned gems in a 2×2 grid.
   > Tip: the Dictionary's pentacle pages show where candles and crystals go.
16. **White Chalk and a Brush**: `occultism:chalk_white_impure`; `occultism:chalk_white`; `occultism:brush` *(after: How a Ritual Works, Otherworld Trees, Burnt Otherstone)*
   > What: white chalk draws the basic pentacle glyphs. The brush wipes glyphs away again much faster than breaking them.
   > Chemistry: real chalk is calcium carbonate, CaCO₃, which fizzes away in acid: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂.
   > How: burnt otherstone and otherworld ashes make impure white chalk; purify it in spiritfire. Brush: three planks over two wool and a string.
   > Tip: chalk wears out with use, so make a few.
17. **Sacrificial Bowls**: `occultism:golden_sacrificial_bowl`; 4x `occultism:sacrificial_bowl` *(after: How a Ritual Works)*
   > What: the Golden Sacrificial Bowl is the centre of every ritual; plain Sacrificial Bowls hold the ingredients.
   > How: bowls are otherstone; the golden one adds gold. Dark versions (from otherrock) work the same.
   > Tip: ingredient bowls can stand anywhere within 8 blocks of the golden bowl.
18. **A Book of Binding**: `occultism:purified_ink`; `occultism:book_of_binding_foliot` *(after: How a Ritual Works)*
   > What: a Book of Binding waits for a spirit's name. Bound, it becomes the key that starts that spirit's rituals.
   > How: spiritfire turns black dye into purified ink, a book into a taboo book and a feather into an awakened feather. Add blue dye for the foliot book.
   > Tip: the colour of dye picks the spirit rank: blue foliot, purple djinni, yellow afrit, green marid.
19. **Bind a Foliot**: `occultism:book_of_binding_bound_foliot`; `minecraft:iron_ingot`; 1x any of `item_tag(c:ingots/silver)`; `minecraft:gold_ingot`; `minecraft:copper_ingot` *(after: Candles and a Crystal, A Book of Binding, Sacrificial Bowls, White Chalk and a Brush)*
   > You remember names that made things kneel. The smallest of them comes back first.
   > What: a bound Book of Binding holds a spirit's name and starts its rituals. Foliots are the weakest spirits, and their first job is crushing ore.
   > How: bind the foliot book with a name as the Dictionary describes (check JEI). The four ingots are the Foliot Crusher's ritual ingredients.
   > Tip: Aviar's Circle, the foliot summoning pentacle, uses only white chalk.
20. **Spirits in a Jar**: `ars_nouveau:ritual_containment`; `ars_nouveau:ritual_brazier`; `ars_nouveau:mob_jar` *(after: Bind a Foliot, Ritual Brazier)*
   > What: Ars Nouveau's Containment Jar holds a living creature, and many keep working inside it. Summoned spirits can be stored the same way.
   > How: place jars near a Ritual Brazier and run the Ritual of Containment; it pulls a nearby creature (within 3 blocks) into a jar.
   > Tip: a jar is a tidy way to move a worker spirit to a new base.
21. **Reading a Pentacle**: checkmark *(after: Bind a Foliot)*
   > What: a pentacle's colours say what it does: white is the base, gold possesses, purple infuses, lime calls djinn, red binds afrits, blue binds marids.
   > How: every new colour is impure white chalk plus a special ingredient, purified in spiritfire. Tick the box when you've read this.
   > Tip: the Dictionary's Pentacles section is a table: each tier upgrades the pentacle you drew before.
22. **Foliot Crusher**: 4x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/gold)`; 2x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/obsidian)` *(after: Bind a Foliot)*
   > What: a crusher spirit picks up ores and gems and drops dusts. New chalks need gold, silver, iron, emerald, calcite and obsidian dust.
   > How: Summon Foliot Crusher: iron, gold, copper and silver ingots in the bowls, a white-chalk circle. Feed it items; any gold and obsidian dust counts for this quest.
   > Tip: a foliot gives 2 dusts per ore, the pack's normal cap. Bigger crushers are only faster; use the MI and Mekanism ore lines for real ore yield.
23. **Golden Chalk**: `occultism:chalk_gold` *(after: Foliot Crusher)*
   > What: golden (yellow) chalk turns a summoning into a possession: the spirit takes over a creature's body.
   > How: impure white chalk with glowstone dust and 2 gold dust, purified in spiritfire.
   > Tip: Hedyrin's Lure (white + gold) is the foliot possession pentacle.
24. **Possessed Endermite**: kill 1x `occultism:possessed_endermite` *(after: Golden Chalk)*
   > What: a possessed endermite has a high chance to drop end stone, which purple chalk needs.
   > How: foliot possession ritual with 2 dirt and 2 stone (the Dictionary shows the extra step). Kill what appears.
   > Tip: run it a few times; crushed end stone goes into every purple chalk.
25. **Possessed Skeleton**: 4x `minecraft:skeleton_skull` *(after: Golden Chalk)*
   > What: skeleton skulls raise a pentacle's calling power. Every djinni, afrit and marid pentacle places them.
   > How: foliot possession ritual with 4 bones and a chicken as the sacrifice. The possessed skeleton drops skulls.
   > Tip: check each pentacle in the Dictionary for how many skulls it wants.
26. **Three New Colours**: `occultism:chalk_yellow_impure`; `occultism:chalk_purple_impure`; `occultism:chalk_light_gray_impure` *(after: Reading a Pentacle, Possessed Endermite)*
   > What: the first coloured chalks: yellow (possession), purple (infusion) and light gray (a stronger foundation).
   > Chemistry: calcite, in light gray chalk, is CaCO₃, exactly the compound real chalk and limestone are made of.
   > How: impure white chalk plus: glowstone and 2 gold dust (yellow); crushed end stone and 2 obsidian dust (purple); silver dust, iron dust and crushed calcite (light gray).
   > Tip: your foliot crusher makes every one of those dusts.
27. **Purple Chalk**: `occultism:chalk_purple` *(after: Possessed Endermite)*
   > What: purple chalk binds spirits into objects. Every crafting ritual (satchels, storage, miners) needs it.
   > Chemistry: obsidian is volcanic glass, about 70% SiO₂ that cooled too fast to crystallise.
   > How: impure white chalk with crushed end stone and 2 obsidian dust, purified in spiritfire.
   > Tip: Eziveus' Spectral Compulsion (white + purple) is the foliot crafting pentacle.
28. **Light Gray Chalk**: `occultism:chalk_light_gray` *(after: Foliot Crusher, Silver)*
   > What: light gray chalk strengthens a pentacle's foundation; djinni pentacles need it.
   > Chemistry: calcite is CaCO₃, exactly the compound real chalk and limestone are made of.
   > How: impure white chalk with silver dust, iron dust and crushed calcite, purified in spiritfire.
   > Tip: calcite lines amethyst geodes, so collect it while you farm source gems.
29. **Foliot Workers**: 1x any of `or(item(occultism:book_of_calling_foliot_lumberjack)item(occultism:book_of_calling_foliot_farmer)item(occultism:book_of_calling_foliot_cleaner)item(occultism:book_of_calling_foliot_transport_items))` *(after: Bind a Foliot)*
   > What: summoned foliots can work: Lumberjack cuts trees, Farmer tends crops, Janitor picks up items, Transporter moves items between chests.
   > How: each is a foliot summoning ritual (Lumberjack: an otherworld sapling, 3 saplings and an axe). The Book of Calling it gives lets you set its work area.
   > Tip: a Transporter feeding a Crusher and a Janitor collecting the dust is a whole processing line.
30. **Surprisingly Large Bag**: `occultism:satchel` *(after: Purple Chalk)*
   > What: a satchel with a bound foliot inside that keeps it bigger on the inside.
   > How: a foliot crafting ritual: a chest, two leather, string and a silver ingot around the golden bowl, on a white and purple pentacle.
   > Tip: the djinni version, the Ender Satchel, opens your ender chest.
31. **The Crafting Circle**: 2x `minecraft:experience_bottle`; 1x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/emerald)` *(after: Three New Colours, Purple Chalk)*
   > What: the foliot crafting pentacle (white and purple) binds a foliot into an object. Its first useful product is research fragment dust.
   > Chemistry: emerald is beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈, coloured green by traces of chromium.
   > How: draw the pentacle from the Dictionary. These are the dust's ingredients: 2 bottles o' enchanting and emerald dust (crush an emerald).
   > Tip: bottles o' enchanting come from villager clerics, or from a Tome of Peritia's stored XP.
32. **Research Fragment Dust**: `occultism:research_fragment_dust`; `occultism:chalk_lime_impure` *(after: The Crafting Circle)*
   > What: research fragment dust is the special ingredient of lime chalk and knowledge tablets.
   > How: the foliot crafting ritual with emerald dust and 2 bottles o' enchanting. Then impure white chalk with the dust, emerald dust and a slime ball makes impure lime chalk.
   > Tip: lime is the colour that calls djinn; make extra.
33. **Lime Chalk**: `occultism:chalk_lime` *(after: Research Fragment Dust)*
   > What: lime chalk attracts spirits stronger than foliots. Every djinni pentacle and up uses it.
   > How: purify impure lime chalk in spiritfire.
   > Tip: make several; afrit and marid pentacles still use lime.
34. **Otherworld Goggles**: `occultism:otherworld_goggles` *(after: The Crafting Circle)*
   > What: the goggles give a permanent Third Eye, and show even more hidden blocks than Demon's Dream does, iesnium ore among them.
   > How: lenses (glass panes and an attuned gem) become infused lenses in a foliot ritual with 2 silver and gold; add a lens frame (otherstone and silver) and leather.
   > Tip: goggles let you see, not harvest: you still need the infused or iesnium pickaxe.
35. **Bind a Djinni**: `occultism:book_of_binding_bound_djinni` *(after: Lime Chalk, Light Gray Chalk, Possessed Skeleton)*
   > You remember spirits who bowed when you passed. This one only negotiates.
   > What: djinn are the second rank of spirits. Their rituals make storage, soul gems, the infused pickaxe and better miners.
   > How: a Book of Binding with purple dye, bound with a name like the foliot one. Djinni pentacles add light gray and lime chalk and skeleton skulls.
   > Tip: the Dictionary's Pentacles section is a table: each tier upgrades the pentacle you drew before.
36. **The Djinni's Workshop**: `minecraft:phantom_membrane`; `minecraft:gunpowder`; `minecraft:gray_dye`; `minecraft:clay_ball` *(after: Bind a Djinni)*
   > What: the djinni crafting pentacle makes most of Occultism's mid-game: the infused pickaxe, soul gems, storage, gray paste.
   > Chemistry: gunpowder is KNO₃, sulfur and charcoal; clay is mostly kaolinite, Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄. Together with a phantom membrane and gray dye they make gray paste.
   > How: draw the pentacle from the Dictionary, then run the gray paste ritual with these four ingredients and your djinni book.
   > Tip: this one pentacle covers more recipes than any other; build it somewhere permanent.
37. **Gray Chalk**: `occultism:gray_paste`; `occultism:chalk_gray` *(after: The Djinni's Workshop)*
   > What: gray chalk is the foundation colour of afrit pentacles.
   > How: impure white chalk with gray paste, purified in spiritfire.
   > Tip: gray, light gray and black chalk can stand in for white in most pentacles.
38. **Apprentice Ritual Satchel**: `occultism:ritual_satchel_t1` *(after: The Djinni's Workshop)*
   > What: fill the satchel with chalks, candles, skulls and crystals; preview a pentacle in the Dictionary and the foliot places the pieces for you.
   > How: a foliot crafting ritual: a hopper, a dispenser, 2 wool, 2 leather, string and a silver ingot.
   > Tip: chalks are used up by durability, so keep spares inside.
39. **Mending Chalk**: checkmark *(after: The Djinni's Workshop)*
   > What: worn-out chalk can be fully repaired by infusing it with a djinni instead of crafting a new one.
