   > How: on the djinni crafting pentacle: 3 otherworld essence and a spirit-attuned gem, started with the chalk itself. Otherworld essence is Demon's Dream essence burned in spiritfire. Tick the box when you've read this.
   > Tip: it's worth it for the expensive colours: red, blue and anything rainbow.
40. **Soul Gem**: `occultism:soul_gem` *(after: The Djinni's Workshop)*
   > What: a Soul Gem traps a living creature so you can move it and release it elsewhere.
   > How: a djinni ritual: a diamond, copper, silver and gold ingots, a fragile soul gem and 3 soul sand or soil.
   > Tip: it's the easy way to move villagers or animals to your base.
41. **Familiar Ring**: `occultism:familiar_ring` *(after: Soul Gem)*
   > What: familiars are summoned with rituals (greedy, bat, beaver, deer, blacksmith...). The ring stores one so it travels with you.
   > How: a djinni ritual with a soul gem, two gold and two silver ingots. Capture your familiar with it.
   > Tip: the Greedy Familiar picks up items for you. The Dictionary lists what each familiar does.
42. **Machine Operator**: `occultism:book_of_calling_djinni_manage_machine` *(after: Bind a Djinni)*
   > What: the djinni Machine Operator keeps a linked machine fed from your Storage Actuator and returns the results.
   > How: djinni summoning ritual with a coal block, gold, iron and a furnace. Use its Book of Calling on the storage and the machine.
   > Tip: it's a light autocrafting option before AE2.
43. **A Djinni Crusher**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/iron)`; 1x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/silver)`; 1x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/gold)`; 1x any of `item_tag(c:dusts/copper)` *(after: Bind a Djinni)*
   > What: the djinni summoning pentacle calls a djinni crusher. It's faster than a foliot, and it can crush ice, which a foliot can't.
   > How: the djinni crusher ritual takes one each of iron, silver, gold and copper dust. Feed it ice, packed ice and blue ice for light blue chalk.
   > Tip: like every crusher here, it gives 2 dust per ore; it's only faster.
44. **Dimensional Matrix**: `occultism:dimensional_matrix` *(after: Bind a Djinni)*
   > What: the Dimensional Matrix binds a djinni to hold items in a pocket dimension.

### Neo Vitae

*Blood magic: an altar that drinks, orbs that remember, and rituals carved in stone.*

1. **Before You Bleed**: checkmark; checkmark
   > What: Neo Vitae spends your life, and later your mobs', as a fuel called Essentia Vitae (EV). Everything on this page follows from the altar.
   > How: the guide book Scriptura Vitae (a book and 4 redstone) shows every altar tier, ritual and array in 3D. Tick both boxes once you've made it.
   > Tip: the big pack gates are noted on the quests they touch: the Athanor (LV circuits), Tenebrae ink and flight (hydrogen and MV).
2. **Ara Vitae**: `neovitae:ara_vitae` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember that every power has a price, and that the oldest price was always blood.
   > What: the Ara Vitae is the heart of Neo Vitae. It turns life into Essentia Vitae (EV) and uses it to transmute items placed on top.
   > Chemistry: blood is about 55% plasma (mostly water, salts and proteins) and 45% cells. Its red comes from haemoglobin, an iron(II) complex that carries O₂.
   > How: a furnace, 3 gold ingots and 4 deepslate (the mod's 'vitae stone') in a crafting table.
   > Tip: the guide book, Scriptura Vitae, is a book with 4 redstone; it shows every multiblock.
3. **Novicius Orb**: `neovitae:blood_orb_weak` *(after: Ara Vitae)*
   > What: an Orb of Vitae is your personal EV network. Right-click it to bleed into it; machines and sigils draw from it anywhere.
   > Chemistry: the orb starts as a diamond: pure carbon in a tetrahedral lattice, hard enough to hold whatever the altar pours into it.
   > How: place a diamond on the empty altar and stand close. With no blood of its own, the altar draws from anyone nearby.
   > Tip: watch your hearts while bleeding. Eat well first; regeneration is your fuel.
4. **Tabula Rasa**: 8x `neovitae:tabula_rasa` *(after: Ara Vitae)*
   > What: Tabula Rasa is the blank slate in almost every Neo Vitae recipe: runes, sigils, tables and fuel cells.
   > Chemistry: deepslate is metamorphosed rock: heat and pressure deep underground recrystallised it into dense, layered stone.
   > How: put deepslate on the altar with blood in it. Cobblestone on the altar also turns into cobbled deepslate for 50 EV.
   > Tip: make a stack; you will use them faster than you expect.
5. **Tabula Vitae**: `neovitae:tabula_vitae` *(after: Tabula Rasa)*
   > What: the Tabula Vitae combines up to six items with EV from the orb inside it: reagents, catalysts, cutting fluids, anointments.
   > Chemistry: its gunpowder recipe is real: sulfur, saltpetre (KNO₃) and charcoal, about 10:75:15 by mass in classic black powder.
   > How: deepslate, planks, iron and gold ingots and a Tabula Rasa. Put your orb in its orb slot.
   > Tip: it also grinds an ore block into 2 dust, the pack's normal pre-acid yield.
6. **Throwing Daggers**: 16x `neovitae:throwing_dagger`; `neovitae:base_spiritus_soul_raw` *(after: Tabula Vitae)*
   > What: creatures killed with throwing daggers drop Spiritus Essence, the residue of a soul. The Hellfire Forge burns it.
   > How: 2 iron ingots and a string in the Tabula Vitae make 16 daggers. Throw them at mobs and pick up what's left.
   > Tip: a Sentient Sword collects Spiritus much faster once you have one.
7. **Hellfire Forge**: `neovitae:hellfire_forge`; `neovitae:spiritus_gem_petty` *(after: Throwing Daggers)*
   > What: the Hellfire Forge combines items using Spiritus in its gem slot instead of fuel. Its first job is a gem to hold that Spiritus.
   > How: iron ingots, an iron block, deepslate and a Tabula Rasa. Then forge a Petty Spiritus Gem (redstone, gold, glass, lapis).
   > Tip: a recipe only starts if the gem holds at least its minimum Spiritus. JEI shows both numbers.
8. **Petty Spiritus Gem**: `neovitae:spiritus_gem_petty` *(after: Hellfire Forge)*
   > What: Spiritus gems store Spiritus and soak up any you pick up, so it stops cluttering your inventory.
   > Chemistry: lapis lazuli is mostly lazurite, a sodium aluminium silicate whose blue comes from trapped S₃⁻ radical ions.
   > How: redstone, a gold ingot, glass and lapis in the Hellfire Forge.
   > Tip: bigger gems come later from the same forge; each holds much more.
9. **Sentient Sword**: `neovitae:sentient_sword` *(after: Petty Spiritus Gem)*
   > What: the Sentient Sword collects Spiritus from every kill and hits harder the more Spiritus you carry.
   > How: an iron sword in the Hellfire Forge with a Petty Spiritus Gem as catalyst (the gem stays).
   > Tip: the axe, pickaxe, shovel and scythe work the same way.
10. **Spike Trap**: `neovitae:spike_trap` *(after: Hellfire Forge)*
   > What: a redstone-triggered block of blades. Kills it makes within 16 blocks of an Ara Vitae feed the altar directly.
   > How: dungeon stone around a dispenser and spikes (spikes are made on the altar). Dungeon stone comes from the Demon Realm, so this waits until you've been there.
   > Tip: a mob farm that ends on spike traps is an EV farm.
11. **Routing Conduits**: 4x `neovitae:routing_conduit`; `neovitae:input_routing_node`; `neovitae:output_routing_node` *(after: Hellfire Forge)*
   > What: Neo Vitae has its own item routing: conduits link input nodes (which pull from inventories) to output nodes (which push into them).
   > How: conduits are 2 deepslate, iron and glass in the Hellfire Forge; a conduit and a hopper make an input node. Input and output nodes craft into each other.
   > Tip: check Scriptura Vitae for how the network is linked and filtered.
12. **Node Router**: `neovitae:node_router`; checkmark *(after: Routing Conduits)*
   > What: the Node Router connects routing nodes to each other.
   > How: 2 deepslate, an iron ingot and redstone in the Hellfire Forge. Tick the box once you've linked a node pair.
   > Tip: link in a line or a star; long chains are easier to fix later than tangles.
13. **Routing Upgrades**: `neovitae:master_core`; `neovitae:master_core_speed` *(after: Routing Conduits)*
   > What: the Routing Stack Upgrade and Routing Speed Upgrade make a routing network move more items, more often.
   > How: stack: 2 iron, glass and a lapis block in the Hellfire Forge. Speed: 2 gold, glass and a redstone block.
   > Tip: JEI and Scriptura Vitae show where the upgrades go.
14. **Arcane Scribe Tool**: `neovitae:arcane_scribe_tool` *(after: Tabula Vitae)*
   > What: the Arcane Scribe Tool draws an Alchemy Array. Drop two items into an array and it crafts a sigil or casts an effect.
   > Chemistry: it is made of redstone, white dye, gunpowder and coal: a pigment, a binder and a little fire.
   > How: Tabula Vitae, then right-click the ground with the tool.
   > Tip: JEI lists every array recipe under the Alchemy Array category.
15. **Arrays: Base and Catalyst**: checkmark *(after: Arcane Scribe Tool)*
   > What: every array recipe has a base item, dropped in first, and a catalyst, dropped in second. Swap them and nothing happens.
   > How: draw an array, drop the base, then the catalyst. Tick the box when you've read this.
   > Tip: sigils are reagent first, slate second; JEI shows which is which.
16. **Divination and Seer's Sigils**: `neovitae:sigil_divination`; `neovitae:sigil_seer` *(after: Arrays: Base and Catalyst, Stronger Slates)*
   > What: the Divination Sigil shows the EV in your network and in an altar. The Seer's Sigil adds the altar's tier, rates and a ritual's working area.
   > How: Divination: an array with redstone first, then a Tabula Rasa. Seer's: the Sight Reagent (Tabula Vitae) first, then a Tabula Robur.
   > Tip: keep one handy while you build up the altar; it tells you when a craft has enough EV.
17. **Utility Sigils**: `neovitae:sigil_water`; `neovitae:sigil_lava`; `neovitae:sigil_void`; `neovitae:sigil_green_grove`; `neovitae:sigil_fast_miner`; `neovitae:sigil_magnetism` *(after: Arrays: Base and Catalyst, Stronger Slates)*
   > What: Water and Lava place fluids, Void deletes them, Green Grove speeds crops, Fast Miner gives haste and Magnetism pulls items to you.
   > Chemistry: lava plus cobblestone in the Tabula Vitae gives sulfur: volcanoes really do deposit sulfur where their gases (H₂S, SO₂) cool at vents.
   > How: each is its reagent (Tabula Vitae) in an array with a slate: Tabula Rasa or Robur for most, Tabula Animata for Magnetism.
   > Tip: a Sigil of Holding keeps them in one slot.
18. **Blank Runes**: 8x `neovitae:rune_blank` *(after: Novicius Orb, Tabula Rasa)*
   > What: runes around the altar raise its tier. Tier II is a ring of 8 runes one block below the altar.
   > How: deepslate, a Tabula Rasa and your orb in a crafting table (the orb is not used up). Scriptura Vitae shows each tier's layout.
   > Tip: blank runes count for the structure; upgraded runes add their effect on top.
19. **The First Ring**: `neovitae:blood_orb_apprentice` *(after: Blank Runes)*
   > What: eight runes in a ring under the altar make it Tier II: a bigger basin and new recipes.
   > How: place the ring as Scriptura Vitae shows; the Divination or Seer's sigil confirms the tier. This completes with the orb the new tier makes.
   > Tip: the altar only checks its shape; you can rebuild it with better runes later without losing anything.
20. **Discipulus Orb**: `neovitae:blood_orb_apprentice` *(after: The First Ring)*
   > You remember the weight of a bigger vessel, and how much more it could hold.
   > What: a bigger orb holds more EV and unlocks tier-2 recipes, including the Sacrifice rune and Tabula Robur.
   > How: a block of redstone on a Tier II altar (8 runes), 5,000 EV.
   > Tip: keep the old orb; Tabula recipes that need a lower orb accept a higher one.
21. **Alchemy Flask**: `neovitae:alchemy_flask` *(after: Discipulus Orb)*
   > What: the Alchemy Flask holds potion effects you can add to, lengthen and strengthen, and drink several times.
   > Chemistry: a glass bottle is mostly SiO₂ with soda and lime: about as unreactive a container as you can make cheaply.
   > How: a glass bottle on a Tier I altar or better, 4,000 EV. Rinse it with a water bucket to empty it.
   > Tip: the Flight effect is fused in a flask too; in this pack it needs 2 hydrogen.
22. **Tipped Daggers**: `neovitae:tipped_throwing_dagger` *(after: Alchemy Flask)*
   > What: throwing daggers coated with a lingering flask's effect, so every hit applies it.
   > How: amethyst throwing daggers in the Athanor with a lingering flask as the tool make 8 (check JEI).
   > Tip: weakness or slowness on a dagger makes the Demon Realm a lot friendlier.
23. **Sacrifice and Speed**: `neovitae:rune_sacrifice`; `neovitae:rune_speed` *(after: Blank Runes)*
   > What: Runes of Sacrifice give more EV per creature killed near the altar; Speed Runes make it craft faster.
   > How: both start from a blank rune. Sacrifice needs a Tabula Robur, gold and an Apprentice orb or better; Speed needs Tabula Rasa and sugar.
   > Tip: a mob farm next to a ring of Sacrifice runes feeds the altar while you're away.
24. **Stronger Slates**: 4x `neovitae:tabula_robur`; 2x `neovitae:tabula_animata` *(after: Discipulus Orb)*
   > What: Tabula Robur and Tabula Animata are the next slates: runes, sigils, casings and the Athanor need them.
   > How: a Tabula Rasa on the altar becomes Robur (2,000 EV); Robur on a Tier III altar becomes Animata.
   > Tip: slates are where most of your EV goes early on. Upgrade the altar before mass-producing them.
25. **Sigil of Holding**: `neovitae:sigil_holding` *(after: Stronger Slates)*
   > What: the Sigil of Holding stores other sigils and lets you switch between them.
   > How: Reagent Holding (chest, leather, 2 string) in an array with a Tabula Animata.
   > Tip: put your Water, Lava and Divination sigils in it to free hotbar slots.
26. **The Second Ring**: `neovitae:blood_orb_magician` *(after: Discipulus Orb)*
   > What: Tier III adds a wider ring of runes a level further down, with pillars and caps at the corners.
   > How: Scriptura Vitae shows the layout block by block. This completes with the Veneficus orb that the new tier makes.
   > Tip: Runes of Capacity and Charging help the altar hold enough EV for the orb.
27. **Veneficus Orb**: `neovitae:blood_orb_magician` *(after: The Second Ring, Stronger Slates)*
   > What: the third orb. With it come ritual stones, the Master Ritual Stone and activation crystals.
   > Chemistry: gold is the input: it barely reacts with anything, which is why it lasts in the ground as native metal.
   > How: a block of gold on a Tier III altar, 25,000 EV. Scriptura Vitae shows the Tier III layout.
   > Tip: Runes of Capacity and Charging help the altar hold enough EV for this craft.
28. **Tome of Peritia**: `neovitae:experience_tome` *(after: Veneficus Orb)*
   > What: the Tome of Peritia stores experience levels so you can spend them later.
   > How: an enchanted book, lapis blocks, gold, string, 2 Tabula Animata and a Veneficus orb.
   > Tip: the Array of Liquified Experience moves stored XP into a tank as fluid.
29. **Master Ritual Stone**: `neovitae:master_ritual_stone`; 8x `neovitae:ritual_stone`; `neovitae:activation_crystal_weak` *(after: Veneficus Orb)*
   > What: a ritual is a Master Ritual Stone surrounded by inscribed ritual stones in a fixed pattern, started with an activation crystal.
   > How: ritual stones from obsidian, Tabula Robur and a Discipulus orb; the master stone needs the Veneficus orb. The crystal is a Lava Crystal on the altar.
   > Tip: the Ritual Diviner places a whole ritual's stones for you, already inscribed.
30. **Ritual Diviner**: `neovitae:ritual_diviner` *(after: Master Ritual Stone)*
   > What: the Ritual Diviner builds a chosen ritual around a Master Ritual Stone, stone by stone, from your inventory.
   > How: the four elemental inscription tools (ghast tear, obsidian, magma cream, lapis block on the altar) with diamonds and a stick.
   > Tip: useful early rites: Green Grove (crops), Harvest, Well of Suffering (EV from mobs) and Magnetism (ores, like a slow quarry).
31. **Sentient Armour**: `neovitae:sentient_helmet`; `neovitae:sentient_plate`; `neovitae:sentient_leggings`; `neovitae:sentient_boots` *(after: Master Ritual Stone)*
   > What: Sentient Armour gains upgrades from what you do while wearing it: running, taking hits, mining, eating.
   > How: an Alchemy Array with Reagent Binding (glowstone, redstone, gunpowder, gold nugget) and an iron armour piece, one array per piece.
   > Tip: a ritual can push the armour's upgrade capacity further; Scriptura Vitae lists it under rituals.
32. **Upgrade Tomes**: `neovitae:upgrade_tome` *(after: Sentient Armour)*
   > What: an Upgrade Tome adds one upgrade to Sentient Armour without earning it the slow way.
   > How: some are Tabula Vitae recipes around a written book (Curios Sockets: shulker shell, ender pearl, gold); others, like Elytra, only come from Demon Realm loot.
   > Tip: bad upgrades exist too (Limp Leg, Dulled Blade): read a tome before you use it.
33. **Tau Fruit**: 4x `neovitae:weak_tau`; `neovitae:strong_tau` *(after: Master Ritual Stone)*
   > What: Tau is a fruit from the Demon Realm. Saturated (Strong) Tau feeds the Athanor's blood shards.
   > How: the ritual Breaching the Edge of Demon Realm builds a small dungeon whose chests and farms hold Tau. Replant it; a creature standing on the plant while it ripens makes Strong Tau.
   > Tip: bring armour and food; the dungeon is not empty.
34. **Athanor**: `neovitae:athanor` *(after: Tau Fruit, Analog Circuit)*
   > What: the Athanor is Neo Vitae's reaction chamber: ore processing, sulfur from netherrack, blood shards and the late gems.
   > Chemistry: a medieval athanor was a furnace that fed itself charcoal to hold one steady heat. Holding a temperature is a control problem, so here it needs analog circuits.
   > How: deepslate, 2 Tabula Animata, a furnace, a Veneficus orb and 2 MI analog circuits (LV). Tools go in its tool slot: cutting fluid, resonator, hydration cell.
   > Tip: it runs at half speed with no Raw Spiritus in the chunk and up to double speed when the chunk is full.
35. **Basic Cutting Fluid**: `neovitae:basic_cutting_fluid` *(after: Athanor)*
   > What: cutting fluid is the Athanor's tool for breaking ore apart.
   > Chemistry: real cutting fluids are oil emulsions that cool and lubricate a cut; this one is plant oil, sugar, coal dust and water with redstone and gunpowder.
   > How: plant oil, redstone, gunpowder, sugar, coal dust and a water bottle (or Water Sigil) in the Tabula Vitae.
   > Tip: in this pack an ore block gives 2 fragments here, the normal pre-acid cap.
36. **Blood and Ore**: 8x any of `or(item(neovitae:iron_dust)item(neovitae:gold_dust)item(neovitae:copper_dust))` *(after: Basic Cutting Fluid)*
   > What: with Cutting Fluid as its tool, the Athanor breaks an ore block into 2 fragments, then gravel, then dust.
   > Chemistry: in this pack the big ore multipliers belong to acids (HCl, H₂SO₄ in Mekanism): dissolving ore frees metal that crushing leaves behind.
   > How: put ore and cutting fluid in the Athanor. Raw ore goes straight to 1 dust with a small bonus chance.
   > Tip: this is a magic route at the normal 2x cap, not a shortcut past the acid lines.
37. **Gravel and Corruption**: `neovitae:corrupted_dust`; `neovitae:iron_gravel` *(after: Athanor)*
   > What: Athanor ore processing goes ore, fragment, gravel, dust. Corrupted Dust is a by-product of the later steps.
   > How: follow an iron ore through the Athanor and keep the gravel; four tiny piles of corrupted dust craft into one (JEI lists its sources).
   > Tip: the mod's 'fragment plus corrupted dust makes more gravel' recipe is removed here: no doubling past 2x.
38. **Sanguine Reverter**: `minecraft:enchanted_book`; `neovitae:sanguine_reverter` *(after: Athanor)*
   > What: with the Sanguine Reverter as its tool, the Athanor takes things apart again: orbs back to their parts, enchantments off books and gear.
   > How: shears, deepslate, a Tabula Animata and an iron ingot in the Hellfire Forge.
   > Tip: JEI lists everything it can unmake.
39. **Weak Blood Shard**: `neovitae:weak_blood_shard`; 4x `neovitae:bloodstone` *(after: Athanor)*
   > What: Weak Blood Shards open Tier IV: the Magus orb, stronger anointments and potion catalysts. Tier IV's pillars are capped with bloodstone.
   > How: Strong Tau in the Athanor with a hydration cell as the tool and 3,200 mB of Essentia Vitae. Bloodstone is 8 stone around a bucket of Essentia Vitae.
   > Tip: the Primitive Hydration Cell is cobblestone, a water bucket, a Tabula Rasa and a Veneficus orb.
40. **Magus Orb**: `neovitae:blood_orb_master` *(after: Weak Blood Shard)*
   > You remember the altar answering before you asked. Your blood and the stone keep the same time now.
   > What: the fourth orb, for Tier IV recipes and the Awakened Activation Crystal.
   > How: a Weak Blood Shard on a Tier IV altar, 40,000 EV.
   > Tip: stock up EV first; the altar drains fast on big crafts.
41. **Tenebrae Ink**: `neovitae:tenebrae_scribe_tool` *(after: Magus Orb, Electronic Circuit, Lighter than Air)*
   > What: the Tenebrae inscription tool carves the dark ritual stones of the big rites: Condor (flight in an area), Torment Nexus, Enchanted Vitae.
   > Chemistry: soot (carbon black) is the oldest ink there is. Here a coal block is made into ink with 2 hydrogen (chemlib:hydrogen) and an MI electronic circuit (MV).
   > How: Tabula Vitae with a Magus-level setup. The Flight elixir (Suspended + Levitation fused with a Combinational Catalyst) also needs 2 hydrogen.
   > Tip: flight in this pack is always a chemistry milestone. The Ritual of Meteo has no catalysts here: ore comes from the ground and from chemistry.
42. **Ritual Diviner [Tenebrae]**: `neovitae:ritual_diviner_tenebrae` *(after: Tenebrae Ink, Ritual Diviner)*
   > What: the Tenebrae diviner can place every Tier IV ritual, including the Ritual of the Condor.
   > How: your Ritual Diviner, 2 Tenebrae tools and 2 Tabula Spiritus.
   > Tip: the Ritual Configurator changes a ritual's area and options.
43. **The Demon Realm**: visit `neovitae:dungeon` *(after: Magus Orb)*
   > What: the Demon Realm is Neo Vitae's own dimension of dungeons: farms, crypts, libraries and, deeper down, the mines.
   > How: a dungeon ritual on a Master Ritual Stone opens the way (the Diviner lists the dungeon rites). Step through.
   > Tip: the realm's chests hold keys; every locked door further in wants one.
44. **Highway to the Deep**: 2x `neovitae:standard_key`; visit `neovitae:dungeon` *(after: Magus Orb)*
   > What: Standard Dungeon Keys open the locked rooms of the Demon Realm's larger dungeons.
   > How: loot Demon Realm chests until you have two. The Highway to Hell ritual leads into the Endless dungeon beyond.
   > Tip: keys stack; take every one you see.
45. **Mine Entrance Key**: `neovitae:mine_entrance_key` *(after: Highway to the Deep)*
   > What: the mines are the Demon Realm level where demonite ore lies. Their entrance key is forged, not found.
   > How: a Tabula Animata, an echo shard, a diamond and a Simple Key (from the first dungeon) in the Hellfire Forge.
   > Tip: echo shards come from Ancient City chests in the Deep Dark.
46. **Mine Dungeon Key**: `neovitae:mine_key` *(after: Mine Entrance Key)*
   > What: Mine Dungeon Keys open the locked rooms inside the mines.
   > How: found in Demon Realm chests (the standard dungeon has a chest for them, and the mines hold more).
   > Tip: ore rooms and the smithy are worth a key each.
47. **Raw Demonite**: `neovitae:raw_demonite` *(after: Mine Dungeon Key)*
   > What: demonite is Neo Vitae's magic metal ore, found only in the Demon Realm's mines.
   > How: mine demonite ore in the mines; it drops raw demonite.
   > Tip: demonite isn't a chemistry metal, so its processing isn't capped like real ores are.
48. **Hellforged Metal**: 9x `neovitae:ingot_hellforged` *(after: Raw Demonite)*
   > What: Hellforged metal makes the Dominus orb and the reinforced runes.
   > How: smelt or blast raw demonite into Hellforged Ingots.
   > Tip: Hellforged Dust, which better cutting fluids need, comes from ingots in the Athanor.
49. **Dominus Orb**: `neovitae:blood_orb_archmage`; `neovitae:hellforged_block` *(after: Hellforged Metal)*
   > What: the fifth orb, made from a block of Hellforged metal.
   > How: a Hellforged Block on a Tier V altar, 80,000 EV. Tier V needs upgraded runes and capstones (see Scriptura Vitae).
   > Tip: Reinforced runes (Hellforged Parts) double a rune's effect.
50. **Divinus Orb**: `neovitae:blood_orb_transcendent`; `neovitae:crystal_cluster` *(after: Dominus Orb)*
   > You remember the last altar: not a tool any more, but a promise kept in stone.
   > What: the sixth and final orb. It opens the Deus rites and the top of Vitaemancy.
   > How: a Crystal Cluster (sculk, Tabula Aetherea, a Weak Blood Shard and a Nether Star in the Hellfire Forge) on a Tier VI altar, 200,000 EV.
   > Tip: Nether Stars only come from the Wither here; a diamond can't be turned into one.
51. **Deeper Locks**: `neovitae:mine_key` *(after: The Demon Realm)*
   > What: the mines have more locked rooms than one key opens.
   > How: keep looting Demon Realm chests for Mine Dungeon Keys.
   > Tip: the smithy room is where Hellforged Parts tend to turn up.
52. **Hellforged Parts**: `neovitae:hellforged_parts` *(after: Deeper Locks)*
   > What: Hellforged Parts turn a rune into a reinforced rune with double the effect.
   > How: loot from the mines' chests (the foreman's treasure and the smithy especially).
   > Tip: reinforce your Sacrifice and Capacity runes first.
53. **Tau Oil**: `neovitae:tau_oil`; 4x `neovitae:weak_tau` *(after: Magus Orb)*
   > What: Tau Oil makes any anointment last four times longer and goes into better cutting fluids.
   > Chemistry: pressing fruit for oil is old chemistry: most plant oils are triglycerides, three fatty acids on a glycerol backbone.
   > How: 3 Weak Tau and bone meal in the Tabula Vitae.
   > Tip: keep a Tau farm running; the oil and the shards both eat fruit.
54. **Raw Crystal Catalyst**: `neovitae:raw_spiritus_catalyst` *(after: Tau Oil)*
   > What: the Raw Crystal Catalyst helps Spiritus crystals form.
   > Chemistry: one ingredient is sulfur dust (S): the same element the Athanor bakes out of netherrack and the pack's acid lines are built on.
   > How: nether wart, Tau Oil, sulfur dust and a potato in the Hellfire Forge.
   > Tip: MI and the Athanor both make sulfur; you'll have spare by now.
55. **Spiritus Crucible**: `neovitae:vas_maleficum` *(after: Magus Orb)*
   > What: every chunk has a Spiritus aura. The Crucible burns Spiritus crystals into it, so the chunk runs thick with one aspect.
   > How: a cauldron, deepslate, lapis and a diamond in the Hellfire Forge.
   > Tip: a chunk thick with an aspect is how you fill a gem with that aspect.
56. **Spiritus Aura Gauge**: `neovitae:spiritus_gauge` *(after: Spiritus Crucible)*
   > What: the gauge shows how much Spiritus, and of which aspect, hangs over the chunk you stand in.
   > How: gold, redstone, glass and a demon (aspect) crystal in the Hellfire Forge.
   > Tip: check it before you start a ritual that draws on the aura.
57. **Crystallarium**: `neovitae:crystallarium_maleficum`; `neovitae:raw_spiritus_crystal` *(after: Spiritus Aura Gauge)*
   > What: the Crystallarium grows Spiritus crystal clusters from the aura around it.
   > Chemistry: real crystals grow the same way in principle: from a saturated medium, onto a seed, one layer at a time.
   > How: a Hellfire Forge, deepslate, lapis and glass in the Hellfire Forge. A Raw Crystal Cluster is 4 raw crystal shards, also forged.
   > Tip: Fortune on the harvest scales with how thick the chunk's aura is.
58. **An Aspected Crystal**: 1x any of `or(item(neovitae:spiritus_ruina_shard)item(neovitae:spiritus_nihilum_shard)item(neovitae:spiritus_vindicta_shard)item(neovitae:spiritus_invictus_shard))` *(after: Crystallarium)*
   > What: Spiritus has four aspects: Ruina, Nihilum, Vindicta and Invictus. Each crystal carries one, and each fuels different recipes and rites.
   > How: grow crystals in an aspected aura; JEI shows how each aspect's crystal is made. Any one completes this quest.
   > Tip: one chunk per aspect keeps the auras from mixing.
59. **Crystallum Fractura**: checkmark *(after: Crystallarium)*
   > What: the Crystallum Fractura ritual harvests grown Spiritus crystals (and amethyst) around it and speeds their growth.
   > How: its stones are easiest to place with the Tenebrae Ritual Diviner. Tick the box once it's running.
   > Tip: attune it to one aspect with the Ritual Configurator for better yields of that aspect.

### Apothic Enchanting

*Enchanting past level 30: shelves, infusion, tomes and libraries.*

1. **Apothic Enchanting**: 1x any of `or(item(minecraft:enchanting_table)item(apothic_enchanting:apothic_enchanting_table))` *(after: Carbon Under Pressure)*
   > You remember words that could bind power into iron. Mortals kept a few of them, in books.
   > What: Apothic Enchanting rebuilds enchanting around three stats, Eterna, Quanta and Arcana, set by the shelves around the table.
   > How: a vanilla table is a book, 2 diamonds and 4 obsidian. The Apothic table swaps the book for any tome. Either one completes this quest.
   > Tip: the table's screen shows all three stats, so you can see what each new shelf does.
2. **Fifteen Shelves**: 15x any of `item_tag(c:bookshelves)` *(after: Apothic Enchanting)*
   > What: 15 plain bookshelves give 15 Eterna, enough for vanilla's level 30 enchantments. Every better shelf on this page goes further.
   > How: 6 planks and 3 books per shelf. Place them one block away from the table, up to two blocks high.
   > Tip: leave the air gap clear: a torch or carpet between table and shelf blocks it.
3. **Infusion**: checkmark *(after: Fifteen Shelves)*
   > What: besides enchanting gear, the table can infuse: put certain items in, and if all three stats sit inside the recipe's window you get a new item.
   > How: enchant anything once, then open JEI's Infusion page to see every recipe and its window. Click the checkmark.
   > Tip: an infusion needs the stats inside a window, not just above a minimum. Too much Quanta can spoil it.
4. **Lapis for Infusing**: 3x `minecraft:lapis_lazuli` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: infusions spend lapis and experience like normal enchanting. Below are the useful infusions that aren't shelves.
   > Chemistry: lapis lazuli's blue comes from lazurite, a sodium aluminosilicate holding sulfur ions (S₃⁻) in its cage.
   > How: mine lapis (deepslate levels are richest) or grow it.
   > Tip: keep a stack of lapis in the table; it stays there between uses.
5. **Eterna**: 1x any of `item_tag(c:bookshelves)` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: Eterna is enchanting power. It sets the maximum level the table offers. Most shelves add some; the world tier caps it.
   > How: every bookshelf adds 1. Hold one and read its tooltip.
   > Tip: Eterna is capped per shelf type too: plain shelves stop counting at 15.
6. **Quanta**: `apothic_enchanting:hellshelf` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: Quanta is randomness. More Quanta means each enchantment's power can land well above or below the average.
   > How: hellshelves are the first shelf that adds Quanta.
   > Tip: high Quanta is a gamble; Rectification (a stat on some shelves) only lets it swing upwards.
7. **Arcana**: `apothic_enchanting:seashelf` *(after: Infusion)*
   > What: Arcana raises the chance of rare enchantments and of extra enchantments on one item.
   > How: seashelves are the first shelf that adds Arcana.

### Equivalent Exchange

*A builder's toy for a demigod who has already mastered the elements.*

1. **The Philosopher's Stone**: `projecte:philosophers_stone` *(after: The Complete Periodic Table)*
   > You remember turning one thing into another with a thought. Now you know what it really costs.
   > What: the Philosopher's Stone transmutes blocks in the world and is the key to every ProjectE item.
   > Chemistry: alchemists spent centuries looking for a stone that turns lead into gold. Real transmutation needs a nuclear reaction, and you've already done that: it's how you made oganesson.
   > How: redstone dust and glowstone dust in a ring around one oganesson (this pack's recipe).
   > Tip: it isn't used up in crafting recipes, so one stone lasts forever.
2. **World Transmutation**: checkmark *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: right-click a block with the stone to turn it into a related block: stone and cobblestone, dirt, grass and sand, one wood or flower type into the next.
   > How: an outline shows what will change before you click; sneak-click for the reverse direction. ProjectE's keybinds change the area size and shape.
   > Tip: a whole hillside of stone into cobblestone (or back) takes seconds. Click the checkmark once you've tried it.
3. **Transmutation Table**: `projecte:transmutation_table` *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: the Transmutation Table turns items into EMC and EMC back into any item you've learned.
   > How: four obsidian in the corners, four stone on the sides, the Philosopher's Stone in the centre.
   > Tip: your EMC and your learned items belong to you, not the table: every table you open shows the same list.
4. **Burn to Learn**: checkmark *(after: Transmutation Table)*
   > What: placing an item in the table's burn slot destroys it, adds its EMC to your total and teaches you that item.
   > How: burn a stack of something cheap (cobblestone, logs, sand), then try to burn an iron ingot. The ingot has no EMC, so it can't be learned.
   > Tip: stone, wood, glass, terracotta, wool and other building materials all work. Click the checkmark when you understand the rule.
5. **Covalence Dust**: 8x `projecte:low_covalence_dust`; 8x `projecte:medium_covalence_dust`; 8x `projecte:high_covalence_dust` *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: three dusts used for ProjectE storage and repairs.
   > Chemistry: a covalent bond is two atoms sharing electrons. The name fits: these dusts bind items together.
   > How: low: charcoal and 8 cobblestone. Medium: an iron ingot and redstone. High: a diamond and coal. Each recipe makes 40.
   > Tip: covalence dust repairs tools in a crafting grid: the matching dust for the tool's material.
6. **Alchemical Chest**: `projecte:alchemical_chest` *(after: Covalence Dust)*
   > What: a large chest, and the base of the Alchemical Bag.
   > How: one of each covalence dust on top, stone, a diamond and stone in the middle, iron, a chest and iron on the bottom.
7. **Alchemical Bag**: 1x any of `or(item(projecte:white_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:orange_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:magenta_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:light_blue_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:yellow_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:lime_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:pink_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:gray_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:light_gray_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:cyan_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:purple_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:blue_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:brown_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:green_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:red_alchemical_bag)item(projecte:black_alchemical_bag))` *(after: Alchemical Chest)*
   > What: an Alchemical Bag shares its inventory with every bag of the same colour you own.
   > How: three high covalence dust on top, wool on each side of an Alchemical Chest, and three wool below. Dye the wool for a different colour.
   > Tip: keep one colour for building blocks so your supplies follow you between builds.
8. **Repair Talisman**: `projecte:repair_talisman` *(after: Covalence Dust)*
   > What: while it's in your inventory it slowly repairs your damaged tools and armor.
   > How: covalence dusts, string and paper (check JEI for the pattern).
9. **Transmutation Tablet**: `projecte:transmutation_tablet` *(after: Transmutation Table, Dark Matter)*
   > What: a portable Transmutation Table.
   > How: four Dark Matter blocks, four stone and a Transmutation Table. That's sixteen Dark Matter: a real project.
   > Tip: worth it for big builds far from home.
10. **The Law of Conservation**: checkmark *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: in this pack, EMC works on building blocks only. Metals, gems, dusts, ores and plates have no EMC.
   > How: read the second page, then click the checkmark.
   > {@pagebreak}
   > The rule: ProjectE normally gives every item an EMC value, so a pile of cobblestone can become diamonds. In a chemistry pack that would skip everything you've built.
   > Chemistry: matter isn't created or destroyed in a chemical reaction (Lavoisier, 1789). Iron comes from iron oxide, Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Copper comes from its ores. Gold comes from anode sludge and aqua regia. You can rearrange atoms; you can't conjure them.
   > So: ingots, nuggets, raw ores, dusts, gems, plates, gears, rods, wires and storage blocks are set to EMC 0. Nether Stars, the Dragon Egg and the Beacon are 0 too, because the Seed of a New World needs them.
   > Also removed: Energy Condensers, Collectors and Relays. They turn EMC into unlimited items or power.
   > What's left: a terraforming and building tool. Stone, wood, glass, sand, dirt and decoration are what a demigod reshapes the world with, and those still have EMC.
11. **Alchemical Coal**: 4x `projecte:alchemical_coal` *(after: The Philosopher's Stone)*
   > What: a dense fuel and the first step toward Dark Matter.
   > Chemistry: coal is mostly carbon. Packing more energy into less mass is what refining fuel is all about.
   > How: the Philosopher's Stone and four coal (shapeless). It must be real coal, not charcoal.
   > Tip: it also burns far longer than coal in a furnace.
12. **Mobius Fuel**: 4x `projecte:mobius_fuel` *(after: Alchemical Coal)*
   > What: the next fuel tier.
   > How: the Philosopher's Stone and four alchemical coal. That's 16 coal per Mobius Fuel.
   > Tip: automate coal now (Create crushing, MI quarries or a coal farm); the next steps need a lot.
13. **Aeternalis Fuel**: 8x `projecte:aeternalis_fuel` *(after: Mobius Fuel)*
   > What: the top fuel, and the main ingredient of Dark Matter.
   > How: the Philosopher's Stone and four Mobius Fuel. Each one is 64 coal; this quest asks for eight (512 coal).
   > Tip: packaged autocrafting (PackagedAuto or AE2) can do the whole chain while you build.
14. **Dark Matter**: `projecte:dark_matter` *(after: Aeternalis Fuel)*
   > You remember materials no forge could make. This one you made from coal and patience.
   > What: Dark Matter is ProjectE's strongest crafting material: tools, armor and rings.
   > How: eight Aeternalis Fuel around a diamond block. The diamonds come from real mining or synthesis; EMC can't make them here.
   > Tip: four Dark Matter make a Dark Matter Block, used by the tablet and the Dark Matter Furnace.
15. **Dark Matter Tools**: 1x any of `or(item(projecte:dm_pick)item(projecte:dm_axe)item(projecte:dm_shovel)item(projecte:dm_sword)item(projecte:dm_hoe)item(projecte:dm_shears)item(projecte:dm_hammer))` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: Dark Matter tools never break and dig very fast. Their charge key widens what they mine.
   > How: like diamond tools, but Dark Matter replaces the head and diamonds the handle (the pickaxe is 3 Dark Matter and 2 diamonds).
   > Tip: charge the Dark Matter Hammer to mine a wider area: great for clearing land.
16. **Dark Matter Armor**: `projecte:dm_helmet`; `projecte:dm_chestplate`; `projecte:dm_leggings`; `projecte:dm_boots` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: very strong armor that doesn't wear out.
   > How: shaped like diamond armor, all Dark Matter: helmet 5, chestplate 8, leggings 7, boots 4.
   > Tip: that's 24 Dark Matter. Automate the fuel chain first.
17. **Black Hole Band**: `projecte:black_hole_band` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: while active, it draws nearby items toward you.
   > How: an Iron Band (eight iron around a lava bucket) between two Dark Matter, with string above and below.
   > Tip: switch it off near your storage system.
18. **Red Matter**: `projecte:red_matter` *(after: Dark Matter)*
   > What: the strongest ProjectE material, for Red Matter tools and armor.
   > How: three Dark Matter in the middle row with three Aeternalis Fuel above and three below.
   > Tip: each one is three Dark Matter plus 384 coal of fuel. Only for the truly committed.
19. **Rapid Reorganisation**: `projecte:nova_catalyst` *(after: Mobius Fuel)*
   > You remember reshaping mountains. The quick way was never the tidy way.
   > What: a Nova Catalyst: TNT and Mobius Fuel. A much bigger blast.
   > Chemistry: TNT is trinitrotoluene, C₇H₅N₃O₆. It carries its own oxygen, which is why it burns so fast.
   > Tip: never near your base. Ever.

## Exploration

### The End

*The End: the dragon, its cities and its ships.*

1. **The End**: visit `minecraft:the_end` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > You remember the edge of the world. It's closer than it used to be.
   > What: the End holds the dragon, End Cities, shulkers and azure silver ore. End Crystals power Just Dire Things' flight upgrade.
   > How: throw eyes of ender to find a stronghold, fill the portal frame and jump in.
   > Tip: bring blocks, a bow and slow-falling potions. YUNG's Better Strongholds make the hunt more interesting.
2. **Slay the Dragon**: kill 1x `minecraft:ender_dragon` *(after: The End)*
   > What: the Ender Dragon guards the End's central island. Beating it opens the gateways to the outer islands.
   > How: shoot or climb to the End Crystals on the obsidian pillars and destroy them first (the caged ones need a climb), then fight the dragon when it perches on the portal.
   > Tip: stay out of its purple breath and never look an enderman in the eye mid-fight. A bow and a stack of arrows do most of the work.
3. **The Dragon's Breath**: 4x `minecraft:dragon_breath` *(after: Slay the Dragon)*
   > What: the dragon's purple breath can be bottled and makes lingering potions.
   > Chemistry: the Dissolver splits one bottle into 8 xenon and 8 radon, two heavy noble gases. It gives no oganesson in this pack: element 118 has never been found in nature, so here it only comes from the Fusion Chamber.
   > How: catch the purple breath cloud in glass bottles during the fight, or respawn the dragon for another go.
   > Tip: crystals respawn the dragon when placed on the exit portal, if you need it again.
4. **An End City**: find structure `minecraft:end_city` *(after: Slay the Dragon)*
   > What: End Cities are tall purpur towers on the outer islands, guarded by shulkers. Some have an End Ship moored alongside.
   > How: throw an ender pearl into an End Gateway near the main island, then search the outer islands. The Explorer's Compass can find one.
   > Tip: shulker bullets make you float; carry milk or slow falling.
5. **End City Loot**: `minecraft:elytra`; 4x `minecraft:shulker_shell` *(after: The Dragon's Breath, An End City)*
   > What: End Cities hold elytra (on the end ships) and shulkers whose shells make shulker boxes.
   > How: take an End Gateway from the main island, then search the outer islands for purple towers.
   > Tip: the Angel Ring needs an elytra; shulker shells feed Silent Gear's tyrian steel.
6. **Rocket Boost**: 32x `minecraft:firework_rocket` *(after: End City Loot)*
   > What: firework rockets boost elytra flight. Thirty-two is a good start for a long trip.
   > Chemistry: gunpowder is black powder: about 75% potassium nitrate (KNO₃, the oxidiser), 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur. The nitrate supplies its own oxygen, so it burns fast even in a sealed tube.
   > How: paper + gunpowder (1–3 for longer flight) in the crafting grid. Creepers and the hunting page give gunpowder.
   > Tip: rockets with a firework star explode and hurt you; use plain ones for flying.
7. **The Egg**: `minecraft:dragon_egg` *(after: Slay the Dragon)*
   > One egg, one dragon, one world. You remember having a whole shelf of these.
   > What: the dragon leaves a single egg on top of the exit portal the first time it dies.
   > Tip: it teleports when you hit it. Push it off with a piston, or let it fall onto a torch to pick it up.

### Exploration

*Go and see what the world has made without you.*

1. **A Plains Village**: find structure `minecraft:village_plains` *(after: Iron)*
   > You remember knowing every corner of this world by heart. For now, a compass will do.
   > What: villagers trade emeralds for crops, tools and enchanted books, and their beds and fields are free for the taking (politely).
   > How: plains villages generate in plains and a few grassy modded biomes. Walk into one. Nature's Compass and Explorer's Compass (the Find Anything quest, linked on the left) point you to any biome or structure on this page.
   > Tip: Towns and Towers adds a village style for most biomes (the optional villages next to this one), and villages often have a waystone. A cartographer villager sells maps to ocean monuments and woodland mansions.
2. **A Forest Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_forest` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: Towns and Towers builds a village style for each biome. The forest village is timber and cobblestone.
   > How: find one in a forest biome (Explorer's Compass: Towns and Towers) and walk in.
   > Tip: each biome style has its own loot chests.
3. **A Meadow Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_meadow` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: high meadows below the peaks get their own village style.
   > How: find a meadow biome on a mountainside and the village in it.
   > Tip: meadows are where bees and wildflowers are thickest.
4. **A Snowy Taiga Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_snowy_taiga` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: a village built for the cold, in the snowy taiga.
   > How: find a snowy taiga and the village in it.
   > Tip: bring leather boots for powder snow.
5. **A Swamp Village**: find structure `towns_and_towers:village_swamp` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: vanilla never put villages in swamps. Towns and Towers does.
   > How: find a swamp and the village in it.
   > Tip: witches love swamps too; keep a milk bucket handy.
6. **A Desert Village**: find structure `minecraft:village_desert` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: a sandstone village in the desert.
   > Chemistry: sandstone is sand grains (mostly quartz, SiO₂) cemented by minerals like calcite or iron oxides that precipitated from groundwater.
   > How: find a desert village (Explorer's Compass) and walk in.
7. **A Pillager Outpost**: find structure `towns_and_towers:pillager_outpost_forest` *(after: A Plains Village)*
   > What: pillagers build watchtowers. Towns and Towers gives each biome its own design.
   > How: find a forest outpost and walk in. Expect crossbow fire.
   > Tip: killing a pillager captain gives Bad Omen; in 1.21 you drink the ominous bottle it drops to start a raid.
8. **A Woodland Mansion**: find structure `minecraft:mansion` *(after: A Pillager Outpost)*
   > What: huge dark-oak mansions, very rare, deep in dark forests. Vindicators and evokers live inside.
   > How: a cartographer's woodland explorer map or the Explorer's Compass. Step inside.
   > Tip: evokers drop totems of undying; vindicators hit very hard.
9. **Better Dungeons**: checkmark *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's Better Dungeons adds catacombs, fortresses and spider caves underground.
   > How: find one (the Explorer's Compass lists them), clear it and loot it. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: some dungeon chests hold Relics and Artifacts items.
10. **Zombie Catacombs**: find structure `betterdungeons:zombie_dungeon` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's zombie dungeon: a tomb with spawners, coffins and loot.
   > How: find it with the Explorer's Compass (Better Dungeons) and step inside.
   > Tip: break or torch the spawners first; then loot at your leisure.
11. **Skeleton Fortress**: find structure `betterdungeons:skeleton_dungeon` *(after: Zombie Catacombs)*
   > What: YUNG's skeleton dungeon is a sprawling underground fort.
   > How: find it and step inside. Bring a shield.
   > Tip: torches on every spawner; skeletons will pick you off from the dark otherwise.
12. **Spider Caves**: find structure `betterdungeons:spider_dungeon` *(after: Skeleton Fortress)*
   > What: a natural-looking cave full of webs, cave spiders and their spawners.
   > Chemistry: real spider silk is a protein (spidroin) with crystalline β-sheets that make it, weight for weight, stronger than steel.
   > How: find one and step inside. A sword or shears cut webs fast.
   > Tip: cave spiders poison; carry milk.
13. **A Better Stronghold**: find structure `betterstrongholds:stronghold` *(after: Spider Caves)*
   > What: YUNG's Better Strongholds replaces the vanilla stronghold with a much larger, trapped maze. The End portal room is inside.
   > How: throw eyes of ender, or use the Explorer's Compass. Step inside.
   > Tip: mark your path with torches on one side; the halls all look alike.
14. **Better Mineshafts**: checkmark *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's Better Mineshafts are longer, with ore deposits, carts and loot.
   > How: explore one and loot a chest. Click the checkmark when done.
   > Tip: look for minecarts with chests along the tracks.
15. **An Old Mineshaft**: find structure `bettermineshafts:mineshaft_oak` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: YUNG's mineshafts come in styles for each biome. The oak style is the common one.
   > How: find one under a forest or plains (Explorer's Compass) and walk in.
   > Tip: the rails and planks are free building material.
16. **Mineshafts of the Caves**: find structure `bettermineshafts:mineshaft_dripstone`; find structure `bettermineshafts:mineshaft_lush` *(after: An Old Mineshaft)*
   > What: two mineshafts built into cave biomes: one among dripstone, one among moss and glow berries.
   > Chemistry: dripstone is calcium carbonate: water carrying dissolved Ca(HCO₃)₂ drips, loses CO₂, and leaves CaCO₃ behind, a millimetre at a time.
   > How: find a mineshaft under dripstone caves and one under lush caves.
17. **Trail Ruins**: find structure `minecraft:trail_ruins`; `minecraft:brush` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: half-buried ruins of an old people. Suspicious gravel hides pottery sherds and armour trims.
   > How: find the ruins (Explorer's Compass) and bring a brush (feather, copper ingot, stick).
   > Tip: brush slowly; breaking suspicious blocks destroys the loot.
18. **Trial Chambers**: find structure `minecraft:trial_chambers`; `minecraft:trial_key` *(after: A Better Stronghold)*
   > What: copper and tuff vaults deep underground. Trial spawners give keys; keys open vaults.
   > Chemistry: the halls show copper's patina: Cu weathers to green basic copper carbonate, Cu₂CO₃(OH)₂, unless you wax it.
   > How: find a chamber, beat a trial spawner's wave and take the key.
   > Tip: breezes deflect arrows; fight them up close.
19. **Temples**: find structure `minecraft:desert_pyramid`; find structure `minecraft:jungle_pyramid` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: a desert pyramid and a jungle temple, each with treasure and a trap.
   > Chemistry: the desert trap is TNT: trinitrotoluene, C₇H₅N₃O₆, which carries its oxygen inside the molecule.
   > How: find one of each. Don't stand on the pressure plate in the desert.
20. **Odd Little Houses**: find structure `minecraft:swamp_hut`; find structure `minecraft:igloo` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: a witch's hut in the swamp and an igloo on the snow. Some igloos hide a basement.
   > How: find one of each and step inside.
   > Tip: the igloo basement has a brewing stand and a golden apple for curing a zombie villager.
21. **A Ruined Portal**: find structure `minecraft:ruined_portal` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: broken Nether portals, with crying obsidian and a chest of gold.
   > Chemistry: obsidian forms when lava (molten silicate) cools so fast it can't crystallise: it's volcanic glass.
   > How: find one and stand inside it. Fill the missing blocks to repair the portal.
22. **A Shipwreck**: find structure `minecraft:shipwreck` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: sunken ships with supply, treasure and map chests. The map leads to buried treasure.
   > How: find a wreck (Explorer's Compass) and swim inside.
   > Tip: a potion of water breathing or a turtle shell helmet makes this easy.
23. **Buried Treasure**: find structure `minecraft:buried_treasure`; `minecraft:heart_of_the_sea` *(after: A Shipwreck)*
   > What: buried chests on beaches, each with a Heart of the Sea for a conduit.
   > How: follow a shipwreck's treasure map to the X and dig down.
   > Tip: the chest is usually right under the X, a few blocks down.
24. **Ocean Ruins**: find structure `minecraft:ocean_ruin_warm`; find structure `minecraft:ocean_ruin_cold` *(after: A Shipwreck)*
   > What: ruins on the sea floor: sandstone ones in warm water, stone bricks in cold.
   > Chemistry: warm-water coral reefs are calcium carbonate skeletons; more dissolved CO₂ makes seawater more acidic and dissolves them.
   > How: find one of each. Drowned guard them.
25. **Wreckage**: find structure `towns_and_towers:wreckage_ocean` *(after: A Shipwreck)*
   > What: Towns and Towers scatters its own wreckage across the oceans.
   > How: find it with the Explorer's Compass (Towns and Towers) and swim in.
   > Tip: boats are faster than swimming between ocean structures.
26. **An Ocean Monument**: find structure `minecraft:monument`; 4x `minecraft:wet_sponge` *(after: Buried Treasure)*
   > What: a prismarine temple guarded by guardians and three elder guardians. Its sponge rooms and gold block vault are the prize.
   > Chemistry: a sponge holds water by capillary action in its pores; dry it in a furnace to drive the water off.
   > How: find it with a cartographer's map or the Explorer's Compass. Bring water breathing and Respiration.
   > Tip: elder guardians give Mining Fatigue; kill all three to lift it (see the hunting page).
27. **A Nether Fortress**: find structure `minecraft:fortress` *(after: Into the Fire)*
   > What: dark nether-brick bridges and halls. Blazes give blaze rods; wither skeletons drop skulls for the Wither.
   > How: fortresses run in long lines across the Nether; the Explorer's Compass finds them quickly.
   > Tip: nether wart grows in the fortress stairwells; take some for brewing.
28. **A Bastion Remnant**: find structure `minecraft:bastion_remnant` *(after: A Nether Fortress)*
   > What: blackstone castles full of piglins and gold. Some hide netherite upgrade templates and ancient debris.
   > Chemistry: gold doesn't tarnish because it's the least reactive metal: it won't oxidise in air, even at high temperatures.
   > How: wear one piece of gold armour so piglins stay calm, then step inside.
   > Tip: opening chests angers piglins anyway; piglin brutes ignore gold entirely.
29. **Nether Fossils**: find structure `minecraft:nether_fossil` *(after: A Nether Fortress)*
   > What: giant bone fossils in the soul sand valleys.
   > Chemistry: bone is mostly hydroxyapatite, Ca₅(PO₄)₃(OH): a calcium phosphate mineral, the same family as phosphate rock for fertiliser.
   > How: find a soul sand valley and walk into one of the bone arches.
30. **A Nether Dungeon**: find structure `betterdungeons:small_nether_dungeon` *(after: A Nether Fortress)*
   > What: Better Dungeons adds small dungeons to the Nether too, with spawners and loot.
   > How: find one with the Explorer's Compass and step inside.
   > Tip: fire resistance first; everything here burns.
31. **Ruins in the Fire**: find structure `minecraft:ruined_portal_nether` *(after: A Bastion Remnant)*
   > What: ruined portals turn up in the Nether as well, with the same gold chest.
   > How: find one in the Nether and stand inside it.
   > Tip: crying obsidian makes respawn anchors, which let you respawn in the Nether.
32. **Erupting Inferno**: find biome `biomesoplenty:erupting_inferno` *(after: A Bastion Remnant)*
   > What: a Nether biome of lava, ash and erupting vents.
   > Chemistry: volcanic gas is mostly water vapour, CO₂ and SO₂; the SO₂ is what makes volcanic air sting.
   > How: Nature's Compass finds it. Fire resistance is a must.
33. **Cliffs of Chalk**: find biome `regions_unexplored:chalk_cliffs`; find biome `regions_unexplored:towering_cliffs` *(after: Iron)*
   > What: two Regions Unexplored cliff biomes: white chalk and towering stone.
   > Chemistry: chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) made of the shells of tiny sea plankton. Heat it and it gives quicklime: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.
   > How: Nature's Compass finds each one. Visit both.
34. **Hot Ground**: find biome `biomesoplenty:hot_springs`; find biome `biomesoplenty:volcanic_plains` *(after: Cliffs of Chalk)*
   > What: two Biomes O' Plenty biomes warmed from below.
   > Chemistry: hot springs carry dissolved minerals; when the water cools at the surface, silica and carbonates precipitate as terraces.
   > How: visit both (Nature's Compass).
35. **Wetlands**: find biome `biomesoplenty:bog`; find biome `biomesoplenty:marsh`; find biome `regions_unexplored:fen` *(after: Hot Ground)*
   > What: three kinds of wetland from the two biome mods.
   > Chemistry: waterlogged peat has almost no oxygen, so it barely rots; microbes there make methane (CH₄), the original "marsh gas".
   > How: visit all three. Bring a boat.
36. **Caves That Glow**: find biome `regions_unexplored:redstone_caves`; find biome `regions_unexplored:bioshroom_caves`; find biome `biomesoplenty:glowing_grotto` *(after: Wetlands)*
   > What: cave biomes lit by redstone, giant glowing mushrooms and glowing fungi.
   > Chemistry: real glowing fungi use the same chemistry as fireflies: luciferin oxidised by O₂ with the help of an enzyme, luciferase.
   > How: these are underground; Nature's Compass gives the location, then dig down.
37. **Useful Forests**: find biome `biomesoplenty:maple_woods`; find biome `regions_unexplored:eucalyptus_forest`; find biome `biomesoplenty:orchard` *(after: Cliffs of Chalk)*
   > What: three forests whose real trees give us chemicals.
   > Chemistry: maple sap is about 2% sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁), boiled down 40:1 into syrup. Eucalyptus oil is mostly eucalyptol (C₁₀H₁₈O).
   > How: visit all three.
38. **Dry Country**: find biome `regions_unexplored:joshua_desert`; find biome `regions_unexplored:saguaro_desert`; find biome `regions_unexplored:outback` *(after: Hot Ground)*
   > What: Joshua trees, saguaro cacti and the red outback.
   > Chemistry: red desert soil is coloured by a thin coat of iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃, on every grain: the same rust that colours Mars.
   > How: visit all three. Carry water.
39. **Cold Places**: find biome `biomesoplenty:tundra`; find biome `regions_unexplored:icy_heights`; find biome `biomesoplenty:snowblossom_grove` *(after: Wetlands)*
   > What: three cold biomes from the biome mods.
   > Chemistry: ice floats because water expands about 9% when it freezes: hydrogen bonds lock the molecules into an open hexagonal lattice.
   > How: visit all three. Warm clothes not required, but recommended.
40. **Colour Fields**: find biome `regions_unexplored:poppy_fields`; find biome `biomesoplenty:jacaranda_glade`; find biome `regions_unexplored:wisteria_grove` *(after: Caves That Glow)*
   > What: biomes full of flowers: poppies, jacarandas and wisteria.
   > Chemistry: most red, purple and blue petals owe their colour to anthocyanins, pigments that change colour with pH (red in acid, blue in base).
   > How: visit all three. Collect the flowers for dyes.
41. **Strange Heights**: find biome `regions_unexplored:spires`; find biome `biomesoplenty:crag` *(after: Caves That Glow)*
   > What: tall rock spires and broken crags: two of the most dramatic landscapes in the pack.
   > Chemistry: rock spires are what's left when softer rock around them is weathered away by water, frost and slow acid rain (H₂CO₃ from dissolved CO₂).
   > How: visit both. Bring a water bucket for the way down.
42. **Dead Lands**: find biome `biomesoplenty:wasteland`; find biome `biomesoplenty:dead_forest` *(after: Caves That Glow)*
   > What: cracked wasteland and grey dead forest.
   > Chemistry: soil dies when it loses organic matter and nitrogen; your Haber-Bosch ammonia (N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃) is how real farms put nitrogen back.
   > How: visit both. A demigod might one day make them green again.
43. **The Origin Valley**: find biome `biomesoplenty:origin_valley` *(after: Strange Heights)*
   > Blocky trees, bright grass, a sky of old. You remember the world looking exactly like this, once.
   > What: a rare Biomes O' Plenty biome styled after Minecraft's earliest days.
   > Tip: there's a snowy version too, the wintry origin valley.

### The Undergarden

*A forgotten land under the world, opened with acid.*

1. **The Catalyst**: `undergarden:catalyst` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > Acid opened the way, and the dark below remembers you. You were the one who sealed it.
   > What: the Catalyst lights an Undergarden portal: a stone-brick frame, like a Nether portal's.
   > How: copper ingots, stone, an ender pearl and a bucket of sulfuric acid (MI, Mekanism or ChemLib; this pack's recipe, check JEI).
   > Tip: keep it: the Catalyst isn't used up, so one lights every portal you build.
2. **Before You Go Down**: checkmark
   > What: the Undergarden is a whole world under the Overworld: its own biomes, metals, food and rotting monsters.
   > How: the creatures, biomes and plants on this page are one quick task each. The metals below them build into the gear you'll want down there.
   > Tip: click the checkmark once you've read this.
3. **The Undergarden**: visit `undergarden:undergarden` *(after: The Catalyst)*
   > No sun, no sky, and still the place feels like home. You remember why you hid it so well.
   > What: a dimension beneath the world: depthrock caverns, sunless forests, seas and the rotspawn infection.
   > How: build the stone-brick frame, light it with the Catalyst and step through.
   > Tip: the Undergarden has no sun. Bring a stack of torches and mark your portal.
4. **The Catacombs**: find structure `undergarden:catacombs` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: the catacombs are a buried tomb of the Undergarden's old builders. The Forgotten Guardian, a hulking armoured giant, still stands watch.
   > How: the Explorer's Compass can find one. Step inside.
   > Tip: the chests hold Forgotten upgrade templates and regalium.
5. **The Forgotten Guardian**: kill 1x `undergarden:forgotten_guardian` *(after: The Catacombs)*
   > You remember the old guardians and the oaths they swore. This one has forgotten its own.
   > What: the Undergarden's boss. It drops Forgotten nuggets, the only source of Forgotten metal.
   > How: clear the catacomb halls, then fight the guardian.
   > Tip: it's slow; hit it, step back out of its swing, and repeat.
6. **A Forgotten Vestige**: find structure `undergarden:forgotten_vestige` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: forgotten vestiges are ruins left by the Undergarden's builders, guarded by the Forgotten and full of pots.
   > How: explore until you find one (the Explorer's Compass helps) and step inside.
   > Tip: Denizen camps are the other settlement down here; they belong to the hostile Denizens who live there now.
7. **The Forgotten**: kill 3x `undergarden:forgotten` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: the Forgotten are armoured undead that guard the catacombs and vestiges. Some carry a cloggrum battleaxe or ancient armour.
   > How: kill three Forgotten in a catacomb or vestige.
   > Tip: they hit hard but slowly. Shield up, then strike.
8. **A Minion of Your Own**: kill 1x `undergarden:forgotten_guardian`; `undergarden:forgotten_block` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: stack a carved gloomgourd on a block of Forgotten metal and it wakes as a Forgotten Minion that fights for you.
   > How: a block of Forgotten metal is nine Forgotten Ingots, so beat the guardian until you have enough nuggets.
   > Tip: the mod has an advancement for building one; the minion fires at your enemies.
9. **The Rotbelcher**: kill 1x `undergarden:rotbelcher`; 8x `undergarden:utheric_shard` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: a bloated rotspawn that hurls rot from a distance. Like rotbeasts, it drops utheric shards.
   > How: close the distance fast, or fight it with a bow or slingshot from cover. Collect 8 shards from it and its kin.
   > Tip: a shard torch nearby softens it up while you fight.
10. **Brutes**: kill 1x `undergarden:brute`; 2x `undergarden:brute_tusk` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: brutes are tusked beasts that leave you alone until you hit them. Their tusks grind into bone meal.
   > Chemistry: tusks, teeth and bone are mostly hydroxyapatite, Ca₅(PO₄)₃OH, which is why bone meal feeds plants phosphorus.
   > How: one brute tusk crafts into four bone meal.
11. **The Denizens**: kill 1x `undergarden:denizen` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: Denizens live in camps around campfires. They drop mysterious masks, and their camp chests hold more.
   > How: find a denizen camp and fight. Breaking their campfire angers the whole camp.
   > Tip: draw them out one at a time.
12. **You Monster**: kill 1x `undergarden:scintling` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: you killed a scintling, a harmless glowing snail. It dropped a goo ball.
   > Chemistry: real snail slime is a mix of glycoproteins and water that thickens under stress, letting the snail glue itself to walls.
   > Tip: goo balls make sticky pistons, so at least it wasn't for nothing.
13. **Rotling**: kill 1x `undergarden:rotling` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: rotlings are the small, quick rotspawn: the infection's first wave.
   > How: they gather in the dark caverns. Light an area and they come to you.
   > Tip: utherium weapons deal extra damage to every rotspawn.
14. **Rotwalker**: kill 1x `undergarden:rotwalker` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: rotwalkers are the tall rotspawn: slower than rotlings, much tougher.
   > How: they wander the caverns in the dark. Fight in the open.
   > Tip: a shard torch nearby softens them up.
15. **Rotbeast**: kill 1x `undergarden:rotbeast` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: the rotbeast is the heaviest rotspawn, with a lot of health and a hard hit. It drops utheric shards.
   > How: find one in the deeper caverns and fight it where you have room to back off.
   > Tip: its shards make shard torches, which hurt its kin.
16. **Muncher**: kill 1x `undergarden:muncher` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: munchers are one of the Undergarden's hostile hunters.
   > How: you'll meet them in the caverns soon enough. Check JEI for what they drop.
   > Tip: keep your armour up when you explore new caverns.
17. **Stoneborn**: kill 1x `undergarden:stoneborn` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: stoneborn are the stony folk of the Undergarden. They drop depthrock pebbles, among other things.
   > How: find one in the caverns and bring it down. Check JEI for its drops.
   > Tip: pebbles are slingshot ammo.
18. **Gloomper**: kill 1x `undergarden:gloomper` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: gloompers are hopping toads, one of the Undergarden's game animals. They drop meat and leather.
   > How: hunt them in the forests and fields.
   > Tip: they hop away fast; a slingshot or bow helps.
19. **Nargoyle**: kill 1x `undergarden:nargoyle` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: nargoyles are among the Undergarden's nastier predators.
   > How: they turn up as you explore. Fight with your back to a wall.
   > Tip: the Bounty Board has a bigger hunt for nargoyles and munchers.
20. **Sploogie**: kill 1x `undergarden:sploogie` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: sploogies are one of the odder creatures of the Undergarden's caverns.
   > How: find one and bring it down. Check JEI for what it drops.
   > Tip: every creature down here is worth a look in JEI's mob drops.
21. **Gwibling**: kill 1x `undergarden:gwibling` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: gwiblings are the little fish of the Undergarden's seas, and they cook into a decent meal.
   > How: find one in an Undergarden sea and catch it with a weapon (or a bucket, for a live one).
   > Tip: the full-grown gwib in the same waters is not friendly.
22. **Gwib**: kill 1x `undergarden:gwib` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: the gwib is the gwibling all grown up: a hostile fish that goes after swimmers.
   > How: fight it from the shore, or from a block above the water.
   > Tip: Respiration and Depth Strider help if you must fight in the water.
23. **Mog**: kill 1x `undergarden:mog` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: mogs are mossy burrowers. They drop mogmoss and depthrock pebbles.
   > How: find them digging in the depthrock forests.
   > Tip: mogmoss makes rugs and slop bowls.
24. **Smog Mog**: kill 1x `undergarden:smog_mog` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: smog mogs are the mogs of the smog spires. They drop blue mogmoss.
   > How: visit the smog spires and find one.
   > Tip: you need the smog spires for the biome quest anyway.
25. **Dweller**: kill 1x `undergarden:dweller` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: dwellers are big rideable grazers. They drop meat and leather.
   > How: hunt them in the forests and fields; an underbean on a stick steers one you ride.
   > Tip: keep one alive and saddled for long cavern trips.
26. **Greater Dweller**: kill 1x `undergarden:greater_dweller` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: the greater dweller is a much bigger relative of the dweller.
   > How: it lives in the Undergarden's open caverns. Check JEI for what it drops.
   > Tip: bring a bow: it has plenty of health.
27. **A Pot That Moves**: kill 1x `undergarden:mysterious_pot` *(after: A Forgotten Vestige)*
   > What: some of the pots in a forgotten vestige are creatures pretending to be pots.
   > How: break pots in a vestige until one fights back, then finish it.
   > Tip: keep your sword out while you loot the ruins.
28. **Cloggrum**: `undergarden:cloggrum_ingot` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: cloggrum is the first Undergarden metal: about as good as iron, and the base for every Forgotten tool later.
   > How: mine cloggrum ore in depthrock (stone pickaxe or better) and smelt the raw cloggrum.
   > Tip: run a spare through the Alchemistry Dissolver: what is this strange metal made of?
29. **Cloggrum Tools**: `undergarden:cloggrum_pickaxe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_axe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_shovel`; `undergarden:cloggrum_hoe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_sword` *(after: Cloggrum)*
   > What: the full cloggrum toolset.
   > How: cloggrum ingots in the usual tool shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: keep them once you replace them: cloggrum tools are what the Forgotten template upgrades.
30. **Battleaxe and Shield**: `undergarden:cloggrum_battleaxe`; `undergarden:cloggrum_shield` *(after: Cloggrum)*
   > What: a cloggrum battleaxe and shield. The shield holds off the Forgotten's heavy swings.
   > Chemistry: a shield spreads a blow over a large area: the same force over more area means less pressure (P = F / A) on your arm.
   > How: the battleaxe can't be crafted: a Forgotten carrying one drops it. The shield is cloggrum and planks (check JEI).
   > Tip: the battleaxe is what the Forgotten template turns into the Forgotten Battleaxe.
31. **Cloggrum Armour**: `undergarden:cloggrum_helmet`; `undergarden:cloggrum_chestplate`; `undergarden:cloggrum_leggings`; `undergarden:cloggrum_boots` *(after: Cloggrum)*
   > What: a full set of cloggrum armour. The boots have a perk: scintling goo no longer slows you.
   > How: 24 cloggrum ingots for the set. Raw cloggrum also turns up in depleted mines.
   > Tip: scintlings leave sticky goo trails across whole caverns; the boots pay for themselves fast.
32. **Froststeel**: `undergarden:froststeel_ingot` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: froststeel weapons give targets the Chilly effect, which slows them.
   > Chemistry: real steel gets brittle in deep cold: below its ductile-to-brittle transition temperature it cracks instead of bending, which is why ships' hulls once split in icy seas.
   > How: froststeel ore only forms in shiverstone, in the frozen biomes. It needs an iron pickaxe; smelt the raw froststeel.
   > Tip: raw froststeel has a blast furnace recipe, so smelt it there at double speed.
33. **Froststeel Tools**: `undergarden:froststeel_sword`; `undergarden:froststeel_pickaxe`; `undergarden:froststeel_axe`; `undergarden:froststeel_shovel`; `undergarden:froststeel_hoe` *(after: Froststeel)*
   > What: sword, pickaxe, axe, shovel and hoe of froststeel.
   > Chemistry: cold slows chemistry down: as a rule of thumb, many reactions run about half as fast for every 10 °C cooler. That's why a fridge keeps food.
   > How: froststeel ingots in the usual tool shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: a froststeel sword is great against fast rotspawn; slowed foes can't close the gap.
34. **Froststeel Armour**: `undergarden:froststeel_helmet`; `undergarden:froststeel_chestplate`; `undergarden:froststeel_leggings`; `undergarden:froststeel_boots` *(after: Froststeel)*
   > What: the full froststeel armour set.
   > How: froststeel ingots in the usual armour shapes (check JEI).
   > Tip: compare it with cloggrum in your inventory before you commit: pick the set whose perks suit how you fight.
35. **Regalium**: `undergarden:regalium_crystal` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: regalium is the Undergarden's treasure: a rare crystal in depthrock and shiverstone.
   > How: smelt regalium ore. It also turns up in catacomb chests.
   > Tip: catacombs are also where the Forgotten Guardian waits.
36. **Slingshot**: `undergarden:slingshot` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: a ranged weapon that fires pebbles, goo balls, gronglets or rotten blisterberries.
   > How: twistytwigs (two wigglewood planks make four) and sticks. Pebbles drop from mogs and stoneborn, or stonecut depthrock.
   > Tip: it takes its own enchantments: Ricochet bounces shots off walls, Self Sling launches you instead.
37. **Things That Burst**: `undergarden:blisterbomb`; `undergarden:boomgourd` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: a blisterbomb is a throwable of rotten blisterberries that bursts into a harmful cloud; a boomgourd is a gloomgourd packed with them, and explodes.
   > Chemistry: real rotting fruit ferments: yeast turns its sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide (C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂), and sealed fruit can split from the gas.
   > How: a twistytwig over six rotten blisterberries makes blisterbombs; eight around a gloomgourd make a boomgourd (check JEI).
   > Tip: treat the boomgourd like TNT: place it, light it, step back.
38. **Ancient Armour**: `undergarden:ancient_helmet`; `undergarden:ancient_chestplate`; `undergarden:ancient_leggings` *(after: The Forgotten)*
   > What: the Forgotten wear ancient armour. It has no recipe: the only way to get a piece is from a Forgotten when it falls.
   > How: keep fighting Forgotten in catacombs and vestiges until you have the helmet, chestplate and leggings. Looting helps.
   > Tip: drops are rare; a vestige full of Forgotten is the best hunting ground.
39. **Mysterious Mask**: `undergarden:denizen_mask` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: the carved masks the Denizens wear.
   > How: Denizens drop them, and their camp chests hold more.
   > Tip: wear one to the next camp and see who notices.
40. **Blood Mushroom**: `undergarden:blood_mushroom` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: a small blood mushroom, the seed of the bloody stew.
   > Chemistry: real ink caps (Coprinus) digest their own gills into a black liquid as they ripen, and people once wrote with it. The Undergarden's ink mushroom is a nod to them.
   > How: they grow on the ground in the bogs and forests; the blood mushroom bog has the most.
41. **Blisterberries**: `undergarden:blisterberry` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: blisterberry bushes drop both fresh and rotten berries. The rotten ones are slingshot ammo and the base of blisterbombs.
   > Chemistry: rotting is chemistry by microbes: yeasts and bacteria break sugars into ethanol, acids and gas, which is why spoiled fruit fizzes and smells sour.
   > How: harvest blisterberry bushes in the forests.
   > Tip: don't eat the rotten ones.
42. **Gloomgourds**: `undergarden:gloomgourd`; `undergarden:gloomgourd_seeds` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: a dark gourd that grows like a pumpkin. Carve it for lanterns and minions, or bake it into pie.
   > How: find a wild gloomgourd; one gourd crafts into four seeds. Plant them on deepsoil farmland.
   > Tip: a carved gloomgourd over a torch makes a gloom-o-lantern; over a shard torch, a shard-o-lantern.
43. **Underbeans**: `undergarden:underbeans` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: underbean bushes grow on the forest floors. Their beans are the Undergarden's first food.
   > Chemistry: beans are protein-rich because legumes host bacteria that fix nitrogen from the air: N₂ becomes ammonia (NH₃), and the plant builds amino acids from it.
   > How: right-click a ripe underbean bush to pick it.
   > Tip: raw beans are edible, but roasted ones are far better.
44. **Glitterkelp**: `undergarden:glitterkelp` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: glitterkelp grows in the Undergarden's seas. It's edible and smelts into dried kelp.
   > Chemistry: real kelp is where iodine was discovered: in 1811 Bernard Courtois added sulfuric acid to seaweed ash and saw violet I₂ vapour rise.
   > How: harvest it from the water.
   > Tip: the gloomgourd pie needs a glitterkelp.
45. **Gronglet**: `undergarden:gronglet` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: small glowing growths that hang on grongle trees in the gronglegrowth. The Infuser can purify or corrupt them.
   > How: break a wild gronglet to pick it up.
   > Tip: keep two: a side quest later wants one of each Infuser kind.
46. **Depthrock**: 32x `undergarden:depthrock` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: depthrock is the Undergarden's stone, the way deepslate is the Overworld's. Its ores (cloggrum, froststeel, utherium, regalium) all sit in it or in icy shiverstone.
   > Chemistry: dissolve depthrock in the Alchemistry Dissolver and it gives silicon dioxide (SiO₂), iron and aluminium, with rare traces of zirconium, gallium, dysprosium and tungsten.
   > How: mine it anywhere below.
   > Tip: depthrock stonecuts into pebbles for the slingshot.
47. **Woods Without Sun**: 8x `undergarden:smogstem_log`; 8x `undergarden:wigglewood_log`; 8x `undergarden:grongle_log` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: three kinds of tree that grow with no daylight at all.
   > How: smogstem forests, wigglewood forests and the gronglegrowth each have their own tree.
   > Tip: wigglewood planks make the twistytwigs for the slingshot.
48. **Shard Torches**: 8x `undergarden:shard_torch` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: a torch tipped with an utheric shard. It lights the dark and hurts rotspawn that come close.
   > How: one utheric shard on a stick. Shards drop from rotbeasts and rotbelchers and sit in catacomb chests.
   > Tip: ring your portal and your base with them.
49. **A Depleted Mine**: find structure `undergarden:depleted_mine` *(after: The Undergarden)*
   > What: old mines left by the Undergarden's builders. The chests still hold raw cloggrum, raw froststeel and cloggrum tools.
   > How: explore depthrock caverns until you find timber supports and rails; step inside.
   > Tip: a quick way to an early cloggrum pickaxe.
50. **Mogmoss**: 4x `undergarden:mogmoss`; 4x `undergarden:blue_mogmoss` *(after: Mog)*
   > What: mogs drop mogmoss; the smog mogs of the smog spires drop the blue kind.
   > How: hunt mogs in the depthrock forests and smog mogs in the smog spires. Mogmoss makes rugs and slop bowls.
